studies.design: Observational multicenter real-world noninferiority implementation study
studies.ai_system: AI system for mammography screening support
studies.finding: In population mammography screening of 463,094 women, AI-supported double reading achieved a breast cancer detection rate of 6.7 per 1,000 vs 5.7 per 1,000 without AI (17.6% higher, 95% CI +5.7%, +30.8%). Recall rate was 37.4 vs 38.3 per 1,000 (noninferior), and PPV of recall was 17.9% vs 14.9%.
studies.limitation: Non-randomised: radiologists voluntarily chose whether to use AI, so selection bias is possible.
studies.title: Nationwide real-world implementation of AI for cancer detection in population-based mammography screening.

studies.design: Pragmatic multisite randomized controlled trial of AI-ECG mortality-risk alerts delivered to physicians
studies.finding: Physicians receiving AI-ECG alerts were compared with physicians without them, with 90-day all-cause mortality as the outcome. Mortality was 3.6% in the intervention group versus 4.3% in the control group (HR = 0.83, 95% CI = 0.70-0.99). In high-risk ECG patients, cardiac death was 0.2% versus 2.4% (HR = 0.07).
studies.limitation: Only 39 physicians were randomized, and the mechanism of the benefit is unclear.
studies.title: AI-enabled electrocardiography alert intervention and all-cause mortality: a pragmatic randomized clinical trial.

studies.design: Single-blind randomized clinical trial using clinical vignettes
studies.humans: Attending physicians and residents in family, internal, or emergency medicine
studies.finding: Physicians reviewed up to 6 clinical vignettes and were scored on a diagnostic reasoning rubric. The median score was 76% with the LLM vs 74% with conventional resources (adjusted difference 2 percentage points, 95% CI -4 to 8; P = .60). The LLM alone scored 16 percentage points (95% CI, 2-30; P = .03) higher than the conventional resources group.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 50 physicians working on vignettes rather than real patients.
studies.title: Large Language Model Influence on Diagnostic Reasoning: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

studies.design: Randomized double-blind crossover OSCE-style study with patient-actors
studies.finding: AMIE and 20 primary care physicians held text-based consultations with patient-actors across 159 case scenarios. AMIE showed greater diagnostic accuracy and superior performance on 30 of 32 axes rated by specialist physicians and 25 of 26 axes rated by patient-actors.
studies.limitation: Consultations used synchronous text chat with simulated patients, a format unfamiliar in clinical practice.
studies.title: Towards conversational diagnostic artificial intelligence.

studies.design: Randomized reader study on 302 published case reports
studies.finding: Clinicians generated differential diagnoses for challenging published case reports. AMIE alone had higher top-10 accuracy than unassisted clinicians (59.1% vs 33.6%, P = 0.04). Clinicians assisted by AMIE reached 51.7% top-10 accuracy, compared with 36.1% without assistance and 44.4% with search.
studies.limitation: Cases came from published case reports rather than live care, and only 20 clinicians took part.
studies.title: Towards accurate differential diagnosis with large language models.

studies.design: Blinded randomized non-inferiority trial
studies.finding: The proportion of echocardiographic studies with substantial LVEF change on cardiologist review was 16.8% for initial AI assessment versus 27.2% for sonographer assessment (difference -10.4%, P < 0.001 for superiority). The mean absolute difference from previous cardiologist assessment was 6.29% for AI versus 7.23% for sonographers.
studies.limitation: Single task (LVEF); studies with poor image quality excluded.
studies.title: Blinded, randomized trial of sonographer versus AI cardiac function assessment.

studies.design: Prospective randomized controlled trial using clinical vignettes
studies.finding: 92 physicians answered five management reasoning vignettes with GPT-4 plus conventional resources or with conventional resources alone. LLM users scored higher (mean difference 6.5%, 95% CI 2.7 to 10.2, P < 0.001) and spent more time per case (119.3 s). There was no significant difference between LLM-augmented physicians and the LLM alone (-0.9%, P = 0.8).
studies.limitation: Simulated vignettes rather than real clinical practice.
studies.title: GPT-4 assistance for improvement of physician performance on patient care tasks: a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Randomized clinical vignette survey study
studies.ai_system: Image-based AI model with/without explanations, including systematically biased versions
studies.humans: Hospitalist physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants
studies.finding: Baseline accuracy was 73.0%; standard AI increased accuracy by 2.9 percentage points and 4.4 points with explanations. Systematically biased AI decreased accuracy by 11.3 percentage points, and explanations did not mitigate this (decrease of 9.1 points).
studies.limitation: Vignette-based survey rather than live care; includes non-physician clinicians.
studies.title: Measuring the Impact of AI in the Diagnosis of Hospitalized Patients: A Randomized Clinical Vignette Survey Study.

studies.design: Pragmatic cluster-randomised controlled implementation trial, 205 UK primary care practices
studies.ai_system: AI-enabled stethoscope (heart failure, AF, valvular heart disease algorithms)
studies.finding: Practices were randomized to implement the AI stethoscope or to routine care, with new heart failure diagnoses as the primary endpoint. Heart failure detection did not differ between groups (IRR 0·94 [95% CI 0·86-1·02]). AI stethoscope use was independently associated with higher detection rates.
studies.limitation: Low uptake within intervention practices likely diluted the intention-to-treat effect; the use-associated finding is observational.
studies.title: Triple cardiovascular disease detection with an artificial intelligence-enabled stethoscope (TRICORDER) in the UK: a cluster-randomised controlled implementation trial.

studies.design: Model development with retrospective reader comparison and single-center real-world prospective deployment
studies.humans: Primary care physicians and endocrinology residents
studies.finding: For identifying referable diabetic retinopathy, the average PCP's accuracy was 81.0% unassisted and 92.3% assisted by DeepDR-Transformer. In a prospective study comparing an unassisted PCP arm (n = 397) with a PCP+DeepDR-LLM arm (n = 372), newly diagnosed patients in the assisted arm showed better self-management (P < 0.05) and patients with referral DR were more likely to adhere to referrals (P < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Single-center prospective study, apparently non-randomized; clinician numbers not stated.
studies.title: Integrated image-based deep learning and language models for primary diabetes care.

studies.design: Randomised controlled non-inferiority screening trial (safety analysis)
studies.finding: 80 033 women were randomised to AI-supported mammography screen reading or standard double reading. Cancer detection was 6·1 vs 5·1 per 1000 (ratio 1·2, p=0·052), recall rates were 2·2% vs 2·0%, and screen-reading workload fell by 44·3%.
studies.limitation: Interim safety analysis; the primary endpoint (interval cancer rate) is still pending.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-supported screen reading versus standard double reading in the Mammography Screening with Artificial Intelligence trial (MASAI): a clinical safety analysis of a randomised, controlled, non-inferiority, single-blinded, screening accuracy study.

studies.design: Multicenter prospective diagnostic validation study
studies.ai_system: Lung Guidance AI (deep learning LUS acquisition guidance)
studies.humans: Trained health care professionals (medical assistants, respiratory therapists, nurses) vs LUS experts without AI
studies.finding: Patients with dyspnea underwent lung ultrasound by AI-guided nonexperts and by experts without AI. 98.3% (95% CI, 95.1%-99.4%) of AI-guided THCP studies were of diagnostic quality, with no significant difference vs expert-acquired studies (difference, 1.7%; 95% CI, -1.6% to 5.0%).
studies.limitation: Compares AI-assisted nonexperts with experts rather than nonexperts without AI; operators were not physicians.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Lung Ultrasound by Nonexperts.

studies.design: Stepped-wedge randomized clinical trial in 9 oncology clinics
studies.ai_system: EHR machine learning 6-month mortality algorithm with behavioral nudges
studies.finding: Among high-risk encounters, SIC rates were 3.4% in control vs 13.5% in intervention periods; the intervention increased SICs (adjusted OR 2.09) and decreased end-of-life systemic therapy (adjusted OR 0.25). No effect on hospice enrollment, inpatient death or ICU use.
studies.limitation: Intervention combines ML with peer-comparison nudges, so ML effect is not isolated; clinician number not stated.
studies.title: Long-term Effect of Machine Learning-Triggered Behavioral Nudges on Serious Illness Conversations and End-of-Life Outcomes Among Patients With Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

studies.design: Pragmatic cluster-randomized trial in primary care
studies.ai_system: ECG-based machine learning model for advanced chronic liver disease
studies.finding: Primary care teams were randomized to access ECG-ML results or usual care, with new diagnoses of advanced CLD within 180 days as the outcome. The intervention increased new diagnoses (1.0% versus 0.5%; OR 2.09, 95% CI 1.22-3.55, P = 0.007), and among ECG-ML-positive patients from 1.1% to 4.4%.
studies.limitation: Diagnostic yield was below epidemiological estimates, probably reflecting variable clinician adherence.
studies.title: Detection of undiagnosed liver cirrhosis via AI-enabled electrocardiogram: a pragmatic, cluster-randomized clinical trial.

studies.design: Single-center pragmatic open-label randomized controlled trial
studies.ai_system: Commercial AI-based CAD software for chest radiographs
studies.humans: Three radiologists with 13-36 years of experience
studies.finding: Health-screening chest radiographs were read by radiologists with or without AI CAD. The detection rate of actionable nodules was higher with AI (0.59% [31 of 5238]) than without (0.25% [13 of 5238]; OR 2.4; P=.008), with similar false-referral rates (45.9% vs 56.0%; P=.14).
studies.limitation: Single center, open-label, only three radiologists.
studies.title: AI Improves Nodule Detection on Chest Radiographs in a Health Screening Population: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Prospective multicenter cohort study in a national screening program, single-read setting
studies.finding: Screening mammography in 24,543 women with 140 screen-detected cancers. Cancer detection rate was 13.8% higher for radiologists using AI-CAD (n = 140 [5.70‰]) than without AI (n = 123 [5.01‰]; p < 0.001), with no significant difference in recall rates (p = 0.564).
studies.limitation: Preliminary analysis; non-randomised design in a single country's screening program.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence for breast cancer screening in mammography (AI-STREAM): preliminary analysis of a prospective multicenter cohort study.

studies.design: Prospective 2-center diagnostic study; dermatologists before and after CNN results
studies.finding: Dermatologists classified 228 suspect melanocytic lesions in screening. With CNN results, sensitivity rose from 84.2% to 100.0%, specificity from 72.1% to 83.7%, and accuracy from 74.1% to 86.4%; the CNN alone had comparable sensitivity and higher specificity and accuracy than dermatologists alone. Unnecessary excisions of benign nevi fell by 19.2%.
studies.limitation: Sequential unblinded re-evaluation design; only 38 melanomas.
studies.title: Assessment of Diagnostic Performance of Dermatologists Cooperating With a Convolutional Neural Network in a Prospective Clinical Study: Human With Machine.

studies.design: Prospective multicentre cohort study in 18 hospitals
studies.finding: Detection of acute myocardial infarction in 8493 ED patients. AI-ECG AUROC was 0.878 (95% CI, 0.868-0.888), comparable with the HEART score and superior to the Physician AMI score.
studies.limitation: Physician AUROC not reported in abstract; single country.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence applied to electrocardiogram to rule out acute myocardial infarction: the ROMIAE multicentre study.

studies.design: Prospective single-center before-after study
studies.ai_system: Commercial AI triage system for PE on CTPA
studies.finding: Radiologist accuracy and miss rate for PE were 97.6% and 12.3% without AI vs 98.6% and 6.1% with AI, not significantly different (P = .15, P = .11). Mean wait time for positive studies fell from 21.5 to 11.3 minutes.
studies.limitation: Non-randomised sequential phases with partly different radiologists; single centre.
studies.title: Prospective Evaluation of AI Triage of Pulmonary Emboli on CT Pulmonary Angiograms.

studies.design: Single-centre randomized noninferiority trial
studies.ai_system: CADx optical diagnosis system for colorectal polyps
studies.finding: Optical diagnosis of diminutive polyps during colonoscopy, with pathology as gold standard. Accuracy was 77.2% for autonomous AI vs 72.1% for AI-assisted endoscopists (P = .86); autonomous AI had higher agreement with pathology-based surveillance intervals (91.5% vs 82.1%; P = .016).
studies.limitation: Single academic institution; comparator was AI-assisted rather than unaided endoscopists, and number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Autonomous Artificial Intelligence vs Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Human Optical Diagnosis of Colorectal Polyps: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Prospective population-based paired-reader non-inferiority study
studies.finding: Among 55,581 screened women, one radiologist plus AI detected 261 vs 250 cancers for two-radiologist double reading (relative proportion 1·04, 95% CI 1·00-1·09), non-inferior. AI single reading detected 246 vs 250 (1·04 non-inferior at 0·98), and two radiologists plus AI detected 269 (1·08).
studies.limitation: Single-centre study, partly funded by the AI vendor; outcome limited to screen-detected cancers within 3 months.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence for breast cancer detection in screening mammography in Sweden: a prospective, population-based, paired-reader, non-inferiority study.

studies.design: Cluster randomized stepped-wedge trial at 4 stroke centers
studies.ai_system: AI-enabled automated LVO detection on CT angiogram with secure messaging
studies.humans: Clinicians and radiologists at comprehensive stroke centers
studies.finding: AI LVO detection with mobile alerts was activated stepwise at 4 stroke centers, with 243 patients analysed. Implementation was associated with a reduction in door-to-groin time of 11.2 minutes (95% CI, -18.22 to -4.2) and CT-to-EVT time fell by 9.8 minutes. There was no difference in functional independence (odds ratio, 1.3; 95% CI, 0.42-4.0).
studies.limitation: Workflow time outcome rather than diagnostic accuracy; only 4 centers and number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Automated Large Vessel Occlusion Detection Software and Thrombectomy Treatment Times: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.

studies.design: Randomized crossover trial, 4 centers in China
studies.ai_system: Multimodal joint-AI model (EUS images plus clinical information)
studies.finding: Endoscopists diagnosed solid pancreatic lesions on EUS with or without AI assistance in 130 prospectively recruited patients. Novice endoscopists' diagnostic accuracy rose from 0.69 (95% CI, 0.61-0.76) without AI to 0.90 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94) with AI (P < .001). Interpretability information alleviated the skepticism of experienced endoscopists.
studies.limitation: Only 12 endoscopists; the benefit was reported mainly for novices.
studies.title: Diagnosing Solid Lesions in the Pancreas With Multimodal Artificial Intelligence: A Randomized Crossover Trial.

studies.design: Multicenter parallel randomised controlled trial
studies.finding: Advanced colorectal neoplasia detection rate did not differ (34.8% with intervention vs. 34.6% controls; aRR 1.01), nor did adenoma detection rate (64.2% vs. 62.0%). CADe increased detection of nonpolypoid lesions, proximal adenomas and lesions 5 mm or smaller.
studies.limitation: High control ADR may limit generalisability to low-detecting endoscopists; industry funded.
studies.title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Colonoscopy Detection of Advanced Neoplasias : A Randomized Trial.

studies.design: Prospective multicenter single-group study, 6 US centers
studies.finding: General endoscopists predicted histology of polyps 5 mm or less before and after CADx assistance during routine colonoscopy. Sensitivity did not differ (90.7% vs. 90.8%; P = 0.52) while specificity was higher with CADx (59.5% vs. 64.7%; P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Single-group before/after design, not randomized; industry-sponsored.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence for Real-Time Prediction of the Histology of Colorectal Polyps by General Endoscopists.

studies.design: Randomised clinical trial in a community clinic
studies.ai_system: Eleos Health AI platform for behavioural therapy
studies.finding: Patients whose therapy was supported by the AI platform had depression and anxiety reductions of 34% and 29% versus 20% and 8% for TAU, and attended more sessions (mean 5.24 vs 3.14). Therapists using the platform submitted progress notes on average 55 hours earlier.
studies.limitation: Small sample (47 patients), single site, 2-month follow-up; therapists may not be physicians.
studies.title: Effects of an Artificial Intelligence Platform for Behavioral Interventions on Depression and Anxiety Symptoms: Randomized Clinical Trial.

studies.design: Benchmark on curated MIMIC dataset of 2,400 real cases with simulated clinical framework, compared with physicians
studies.finding: LLMs were evaluated on diagnosing four common abdominal pathologies in real patient cases within a simulated clinical decision-making framework. LLMs performed significantly worse than physicians across pathologies; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives no quantitative results or physician numbers; the setting is a simulated workflow using retrospective records.
studies.title: Evaluation and mitigation of the limitations of large language models in clinical decision-making.

studies.design: Prospective reader experiment with purported AI giving correct or incorrect BI-RADS suggestions
studies.ai_system: Purported AI system suggesting BI-RADS categories
studies.finding: Radiologists read 50 mammograms assisted by a purported AI; correct ratings fell when AI was incorrect: inexperienced 79.7% vs 19.8%, moderately experienced 81.3% vs 24.8%, very experienced 82.3% vs 45.5%. Inexperienced readers showed greater degree of bias (4.0 vs 2.4 and 1.2).
studies.limitation: Experimental setting with a simulated AI and small enriched case set; no unaided control arm.
studies.title: Automation Bias in Mammography: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence BI-RADS Suggestions on Reader Performance.

studies.design: Cross-sectional masked panel evaluation
studies.humans: AAO-affiliated ophthalmologists answering forum questions; 8 ophthalmologist raters
studies.finding: For 200 patient eye care forum questions, chatbot answers were comparable to ophthalmologist answers for incorrect or inappropriate content (PR 0.92; 95% CI 0.77-1.10), likelihood of harm (PR 0.84) and extent of harm (PR 0.99). Raters distinguished AI from human answers with mean accuracy 61.3%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective online forum responses, not real clinical care; evaluated by ophthalmologists, not patients.
studies.title: Comparison of Ophthalmologist and Large Language Model Chatbot Responses to Online Patient Eye Care Questions.

studies.design: Prospective observational study with AI-aided and AI-unaided periods
studies.ai_system: Commercial AI software for chest radiographs
studies.finding: Reading times of 11 radiologists for 18,680 CXRs were compared with and without AI. Total reading times were shorter with AI (13.3 s vs. 14.8 s, p < 0.001); shorter when AI found no abnormality (10.8 s vs. 13.1 s) but not different when AI detected abnormality (18.6 s vs. 18.4 s, p = 0.452).
studies.limitation: Only reading time measured, not diagnostic accuracy; 11 radiologists, non-randomised periods.
studies.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on the reading times of radiologists for chest radiographs.

studies.design: Multicenter single-blind randomized noninferiority trial of AI insulin titration vs senior physicians
studies.ai_system: iNCDSS AI insulin clinical decision support system
studies.finding: Time in target glucose range was 76.4% with iNCDSS and 73.6% with physicians (difference 2.7%; 95% CI -2.7% to 8.0%), meeting noninferiority. No significant differences in adverse events.
studies.limitation: Short 5-day inpatient trial with 149 patients.
studies.title: Real-Time AI-Assisted Insulin Titration System for Glucose Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

studies.design: Multicenter randomized controlled trial, AI-assisted vs non-assisted EGD
studies.ai_system: Computer-aided detection device for gastric neoplasms
studies.finding: 29,514 patients were randomised to AI-assisted or non-assisted upper endoscopy. Gastric neoplasm detection after pathological review was 1.42 vs 1.25% (RR 1.13; P = .25), while AI reduced blind spots from 2.52 to 1.07 (P < .001) and prolonged procedure time.
studies.limitation: Number of endoscopists not stated; benefit seen only on original pathology and in exploratory subgroups.
studies.title: Effect of a Computer-Aided Device for Detecting Gastric Neoplasms: A Multicenter, Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Multicenter prospective randomized study
studies.ai_system: Simulated AI advice with local or global explanations
studies.finding: Chest radiograph diagnosis with simulated AI advice under different explanation types. Local explanations yielded better accuracy than global ones when the AI advice was correct (β = 0.86; Padj < .001) and reduced time (β = -0.19). Physicians placed greater simple trust in local explanations regardless of AI correctness (β = 1.32).
studies.limitation: Simulated AI advice; compares explanation types rather than no-AI reading.
studies.title: Care to Explain? AI Explanation Types Differentially Impact Chest Radiograph Diagnostic Performance and Physician Trust in AI.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial of clinician-AI collaborative diagnostic workflows
studies.finding: Clinicians diagnosed cases using AI as first opinion, AI as second opinion, or conventional resources. Both collaborative workflows improved diagnostic accuracy over conventional resources (85% and 82% vs. 75%), and were not statistically different from AI-alone accuracy (90%).
studies.limitation: Case-based evaluation with 70 clinicians; case type and real-world applicability not detailed in abstract.
studies.title: From tool to teammate in a randomized controlled trial of clinician-AI collaborative workflows for diagnosis.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial using retrospective patient data
studies.finding: Nine general cardiologists managed complex suspected genetic cardiomyopathy cases with or without AMIE, and blinded subspecialists rated the assessments. Subspecialists preferred AMIE-assisted assessments 46.7% of the time versus 32.7% for cardiologists alone (P = 0.02). Cardiologists alone had more clinically significant errors (24.3% versus 13.1%, P = 0.033) and more missing content (37.4% versus 17.8%, P = 0.0021).
studies.limitation: Only nine cardiologists, and cases were retrospective records rather than live care.
studies.title: A large language model for complex cardiology care.

studies.design: Model development with controlled evaluation against cardiologists and prospective trial
studies.finding: EchoNext detected structural heart disease from ECGs and outperformed cardiologists in a controlled evaluation. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives no quantitative results or number of cardiologists for the comparison.
studies.title: Detecting structural heart disease from electrocardiograms using AI.

studies.design: Comparative cross-sectional study of GPT-4 versus specialists on questions and deidentified cases
studies.humans: Glaucoma and retina specialists and trainees (12 attendings, 3 senior trainees)
studies.finding: On 20 questions and 20 deidentified glaucoma and retina cases, the combined mean rank for accuracy was 506.2 for the LLM chatbot versus 403.4 for glaucoma specialists (P < .001). Against retina specialists, the accuracy mean rank was 235.3 versus 216.1 (P = .17), and completeness was 258.3 versus 208.7 (P = .005).
studies.limitation: Single center, small set of questions and cases, Likert ratings by the participating clinicians.
studies.title: Assessment of a Large Language Model's Responses to Questions and Cases About Glaucoma and Retina Management.

studies.design: Single-center prospective observational study in an urban ED over one week
studies.finding: Overall ESI triage accuracy was 65.2 % for nurses, 66.5 % for ChatGPT and 61.8 % for Copilot. In recognizing high-acuity patients, ChatGPT and Copilot outperformed triage nurses (87.8 % and 85.7 % versus 32.7 %), and nurses significantly under-triaged.
studies.limitation: Single center, one week, AI given physician-written vignettes; comparators are nurses not physicians.
studies.title: Evaluating LLM-based generative AI tools in emergency triage: A comparative study of ChatGPT Plus, Copilot Pro, and triage nurses.
studies.source: The American journal of emergency medicine

studies.design: Single-center randomized trial (2:1)
studies.ai_system: AI detecting cancer progression from imaging reports triggering trial notifications
studies.finding: Effect of notifying oncologists about matched trials on therapeutic trial enrollment among 20 707 patients. Enrollment was 2.20% in the intervention arm vs 2.03% in control (difference 0.18 percentage points; P = .41).
studies.limitation: Single academic center; outcome reflects patient enrollment and number of oncologists not stated.
studies.title: Clinical Trial Notifications Triggered by Artificial Intelligence-Detected Cancer Progression: A Randomized Trial.

studies.design: Prospective observational study; dermatologists assessed lesions before and after real-time AI scores
studies.finding: In 603 biopsied lesions (95 melanomas), dermatologists' melanoma risk assessment improved after ADAE exposure (AUC 0.7798 vs. 0.8161, p = 0.042). ADAE alone had sensitivity 96.8% and specificity 37.4% at its threshold.
studies.limitation: Non-randomised before/after design; largely White population; number of dermatologists not stated.
studies.title: Prospective validation of dermoscopy-based open-source artificial intelligence for melanoma diagnosis (PROVE-AI study).

studies.design: Model development with multicenter and real-world validation
studies.ai_system: PANDA deep learning on non-contrast CT
studies.finding: For pancreatic lesion detection on non-contrast CT, PANDA achieved an AUC of 0.986-0.996 in multicenter validation across 6,239 patients. It outperformed mean radiologist performance by 34.1% in sensitivity and 6.3% in specificity for PDAC identification.
studies.limitation: Model-development study; number of radiologists not stated in the abstract.
studies.title: Large-scale pancreatic cancer detection via non-contrast CT and deep learning.

studies.design: Observational cohort model development and external validation
studies.ai_system: Machine learning ECG model for occlusion MI
studies.finding: Using 7,313 consecutive patients, the derived model for ECG diagnosis of occlusion MI outperformed practicing clinicians and commercial interpretation systems in precision and sensitivity. Combined with clinical judgment, it helped correctly reclassify one in three patients with chest pain.
studies.limitation: Abstract reports no numeric clinician comparison; model-development observational design.
studies.title: Machine learning for ECG diagnosis and risk stratification of occlusion myocardial infarction.

studies.design: Cross-sectional study of 195 Reddit r/AskDocs exchanges, blinded evaluation in triplicate
studies.humans: Verified physicians responding on a public forum
studies.finding: Licensed health care professionals compared chatbot and physician responses to 195 patient questions. Evaluators preferred chatbot responses in 78.6% (95% CI, 75.0%-81.8%) of 585 evaluations; good or very good quality was 78.5% for the chatbot vs 22.1% for physicians, and empathetic or very empathetic was 45.1% vs 4.6%.
studies.limitation: Physician answers came from a public online forum rather than clinical care, and chatbot responses were much longer.
studies.title: Comparing Physician and Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Responses to Patient Questions Posted to a Public Social Media Forum.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre observational before-after study
studies.finding: The study compared adenoma detection rate in standard, non-AI colonoscopy before and after endoscopists were exposed to AI. ADR fell from 28·4% to 22·4% (absolute difference -6·0%, 95% CI -10·5 to -1·6; p=0·0089), and AI exposure had an odds ratio of 0·69.
studies.limitation: Observational before-after design open to confounding; the number of endoscopists is not stated.
studies.title: Endoscopist deskilling risk after exposure to artificial intelligence in colonoscopy: a multicentre, observational study.

studies.design: Multicenter randomized controlled trial, AI-enhanced coaching vs self-learning
studies.finding: Novice surgeons performing laparoscopic cholecystectomy were randomised to AI-enhanced coaching or self-learning. The coaching group improved Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Rating Form scores from 31 to 40 (P=0.008) and outperformed the self-learning group at study end (40 vs 38, P=0.032); CVS achievement in the coaching group rose from 11% to 78% (P=0.021).
studies.limitation: Very small sample (22 surgeons enrolled, 18 completed); intervention combines coaching with AI so the AI's specific contribution is unclear.
studies.title: Impact of an AI-based laparoscopic cholecystectomy coaching program on the surgical performance: a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Large-scale digital experiment in simulated store-and-forward teledermatology
studies.ai_system: Fair deep learning decision support system
studies.humans: 389 board-certified dermatologists and 459 primary-care physicians from 39 countries
studies.finding: Physicians diagnosed 364 images across 46 skin diseases; specialists and generalists had accuracies of 38% and 19%, and were four percentage points less accurate on dark skin. DL decision support improved accuracy of both by more than 33%, but exacerbated the skin-tone accuracy gap among generalists.
studies.limitation: Simulated image-based setting, not live care.
studies.title: Deep learning-aided decision support for diagnosis of skin disease across skin tones.

studies.design: Prospective comparative study with random assignment of residents
studies.finding: Differential diagnosis of 48 complex critical illness cases. Top diagnosis accuracy was 60% (29/48) for the AI model, 27% (13/48) for non-AI-assisted residents and 58% (28/48) for AI-assisted residents. Diagnostic time fell with AI (median 972 s vs 1920 s).
studies.limitation: Small sample of literature cases and 32 residents, each handling about 3 cases.
studies.title: A large language model improves clinicians' diagnostic performance in complex critical illness cases.

studies.design: Model development and validation with clinician comparison
studies.finding: Models screened and diagnosed 11 CVD types with AUC 0.988 and 0.991. The diagnostic model outperformed cardiologists in diagnosing pulmonary arterial hypertension.
studies.limitation: Clinician comparison limited to one disease and not quantified in abstract.
studies.title: Screening and diagnosis of cardiovascular disease using artificial intelligence-enabled cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.

studies.design: Stepwise multicentre validation: external comparison, MRMC reader study, randomised open-label comparison, prospective deployment
studies.ai_system: Deep-learning CTA intracranial aneurysm detection model
studies.finding: In external data, AI sensitivity was 0·943 vs 0·658 for clinicians. In the MRMC study, per-patient AUC improved from 0·795 without AI to 0·878 with AI; in the randomised comparison AUC was 0·858 vs 0·789. Prospectively, clinician AUC improved from 0·787 to 0·909.
studies.limitation: Randomised stage was open-label; conducted in Chinese hospitals only.
studies.title: A deep-learning model for intracranial aneurysm detection on CT angiography images in China: a stepwise, multicentre, early-stage clinical validation study.

studies.design: Cluster randomized controlled trial in six ICUs across two hospitals
studies.finding: Adherence to delirium interventions was higher with AI-AntiDelirium than in control units (75 % vs. 58 %, P < 0.01). AI-AntiDelirium also decreased extraneous cognitive load and improved germane cognitive load (both P < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Participants were nurses rather than physicians, and the outcome was guideline adherence rather than patient outcomes.
studies.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of a clinical decision support system (AI-Antidelirium) to improve Nurses' adherence to delirium guidelines in the intensive care unit.

studies.design: Diagnostic study with prospective testing cohorts
studies.ai_system: ScolioNets deep learning model in AlignProCARE app
studies.finding: Classification of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis severity, curve type and progression from smartphone back photographs. Sensitivity for recommending follow-up was 84.88% for the model vs 44.19% (senior) and 62.79% (junior surgeon); for progression the model was comparable to the senior surgeon (sensitivity 63.33% vs 77.42%).
studies.limitation: Only two surgeons as comparators, assessing photographs alone.
studies.title: Deep Learning Model to Classify and Monitor Idiopathic Scoliosis in Adolescents Using a Single Smartphone Photograph.

studies.design: Randomised controlled crossover reader trial
studies.ai_system: AI for periapical radiolucency detection on panoramic radiographs
studies.finding: Detection of periapical radiolucencies on 50 panoramic radiographs with CBCT reference. AI assistance improved overall accuracy (91.6 % unaided vs. 93.3 % AI-aided; p < 0.001), mainly reducing false positive rate (4.3 % vs 2.0 %), with sensitivity stable (46.0 % vs 45.8 %).
studies.limitation: Small image set in an experimental reader setting; modest absolute gain.
studies.title: Impact of artificial intelligence assistance on diagnosing periapical radiolucencies: A randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Single-blind parallel-group randomized controlled trial, Hong Kong
studies.finding: Colonoscopies by endoscopists-in-training were randomized to CADe or no CADe, with adenoma detection rate as the primary outcome. ADR was 57.5% with CADe vs 44.5% without (adjusted RR 1.41; 95% CI, 1.17-1.72; P < .001). There was no significant difference in advanced ADR, and the non-neoplastic resection rate was higher with CADe (52.1% vs 35.0%).
studies.limitation: Single-region trial limited to trainees; no difference in advanced adenoma detection; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Effect of Real-Time Computer-Aided Polyp Detection System (ENDO-AID) on Adenoma Detection in Endoscopists-in-Training: A Randomized Trial.
studies.source: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

studies.design: Prospective single-center before-after study
studies.ai_system: Commercial AI triage system for intracranial hemorrhage
studies.finding: Radiologists read head NCCT for intracranial hemorrhage without (phase 1) and with (phase 2) AI triage. Accuracy (99.5% vs 99.2%), sensitivity (98.6% vs 98.9%) and NPV did not differ, specificity was higher without AI (99.8% vs 99.3%, p=.004), and turnaround time was 147.1 vs 149.9 minutes (p=.11).
studies.limitation: Non-randomized sequential phases at a single center; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Prospective Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Triage of Intracranial Hemorrhage on Noncontrast Head CT Examinations.

studies.design: Multicentre tandem double-blind randomised controlled trial at 12 hospitals in China
studies.ai_system: AI system for detecting superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions on WLE and non-magnified NBI
studies.finding: Endoscopists did tandem upper GI endoscopy with and without AI. Per-lesion miss rates were 1·7% (2/118) in the AI-first group versus 6·7% (6/90) in the routine-first group (risk ratio 0·25, 95% CI 0·06-1·08; p=0·079); per-patient miss rates were 1·9% versus 5·1% (p=0·40).
studies.limitation: Differences not statistically significant; endoscopists unmasked; per-protocol analysis.
studies.title: Effect of an artificial intelligence-assisted system on endoscopic diagnosis of superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions: a multicentre, tandem, double-blind, randomised controlled trial.

studies.design: Multicentre prospective study; each capsule read in standard mode then blinded AI-assisted mode
studies.humans: Capsule endoscopy readers at 14 European centres
studies.finding: Detection of potentially small bowel bleeding P1/P2 lesions in 133 patients. Diagnostic yield with AI-assisted reading was 98 [73·7%] of 133 versus 82 [62·4%] of 133 with standard reading (non-inferior p<0·0001, superior p=0·0213). Mean reading time was 3·8 min with AI versus 33·7 min standard.
studies.limitation: Readings were sequential rather than randomised, and the study was industry-supported; the number of readers is not stated.
studies.title: AI-assisted capsule endoscopy reading in suspected small bowel bleeding: a multicentre prospective study.

studies.design: Development and clinical validation with in vivo and external validation
studies.finding: Patient-level kidney stone type prediction during flexible ureteroscopy. AiFURS achieved diagnostic accuracy of 92.2-95.3% in in vivo validation (100 cases) and 86.8-92.2% in external validation (80 cases), outperforming expert surgeons; surgeon figures not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Surgeon comparison figures and number of surgeons not reported; small validation cohorts.
studies.title: Clinical validation of an AI-assisted system for real-time kidney stone detection during flexible ureteroscopic surgery.

studies.design: Diagnostic study of fictional cases with blinded tumor board rating
studies.humans: One expert physician; molecular tumor board raters
studies.finding: For 10 fictional advanced cancer cases, LLM treatment options reached F1 scores of 0.04, 0.17, 0.14 and 0.19 against the expert as criterion standard. LLM options were recognized as AI-generated with median 7.5 points versus 2.0 for manually annotated cases, and they did not reach the quality and credibility of human experts.
studies.limitation: Only 10 fictional cases and a single expert comparator.
studies.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Decision Support in Personalized Oncology.

studies.design: Retrospective evaluation of 10,000 ED visits' notes comparing LLM recommendations with a resident physician
studies.finding: The LLMs made admission, radiology request and antibiotic prescription recommendations from Emergency Department notes. GPT-4-turbo and GPT-3.5-turbo had accuracy scores 8% and 24% lower than the physician on average, respectively. The LLMs were overly cautious, with high sensitivity at the cost of specificity.
studies.limitation: Retrospective notes only; the human comparator appears to be a single resident.
studies.title: Evaluating the use of large language models to provide clinical recommendations in the Emergency Department.

studies.design: Multicenter randomised controlled trial in community practices
studies.finding: Adenomas per colonoscopy did not differ with vs without CADe (0.73 vs 0.67, P = 0.496); ADR was 35.9 vs 37.2%. CADe increased nonadenomatous, nonserrated polyps (0.90 vs 0.51) and withdrawal time (11.7 vs 10.7 minutes).
studies.limitation: Modest sample of 769 patients; endoscopist number not stated.
studies.title: Evaluation of Computer-Aided Detection During Colonoscopy in the Community (AI-SEE): A Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trial.

studies.design: Multicenter randomized noninferiority tandem trial, 3 hospitals in China
studies.finding: Patients were randomized to novice, AI-assisted novice or expert withdrawal, with adenoma miss rate (AMR) as primary outcome. AMR and polyp miss rate were lower with AI-assisted novices than novices alone (18.82% vs 43.69% and 21.23% vs 35.38%, P < .001). AI-assisted novices were noninferior to experts (AMR 18.82% vs 26.97%).
studies.limitation: Conducted in China only; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Effect of artificial intelligence on novice-performed colonoscopy: a multicenter randomized controlled tandem study.

studies.design: Single-center non-randomized clinical trial with biweekly allocation
studies.finding: Detection of breast cancer metastases in 190 sentinel lymph node specimens, with or without AI assistance. AI-assisted pathologists had a reduced adjusted relative risk of IHC use (0.680, 95% CI 0.347-0.878), with significant time reductions and up to 30% improved sensitivity.
studies.limitation: Non-randomized, single center, small sample, apparently a single expert pathologist.
studies.title: Clinical implementation of artificial-intelligence-assisted detection of breast cancer metastases in sentinel lymph nodes: the CONFIDENT-B single-center, non-randomized clinical trial.

studies.design: Prospective multicenter randomized trial, CADe vs human second observer during colonoscopy
studies.humans: Human second observers (trainees or experienced nurses)
studies.finding: Patients undergoing colonoscopy were randomized to CADe-assisted or human observer-assisted groups (1,261 analysed). Adenomas per colonoscopy were 0.42 vs 0.35 (P = 0.034) and PDR 47.5% vs 37.4% (P < 0.001), while ADR was 25.8% vs 24.0% (P = 0.464). CADe false detections were lower than the human observer's (122 vs 191, P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Comparator second observers were trainees or nurses rather than physicians, and the ADR difference was not significant.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence empowers the second-observer strategy for colonoscopy: a randomized clinical trial.

studies.design: Prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy comparison
studies.ai_system: ADAE open-source ensemble algorithm with real test-time augmentation
studies.finding: Melanoma diagnosis from dermoscopic images collected prospectively across eight hospitals. AI balanced accuracy was 0.798 vs 0.781 for dermatologists, with higher sensitivity (0.921 vs 0.734) but lower specificity (0.673 vs 0.828).
studies.limitation: Only melanoma-suspicious lesions included; number of dermatologists not stated.
studies.title: Prospective multicenter study using artificial intelligence to improve dermoscopic melanoma diagnosis in patient care.

studies.design: International paired non-inferiority confirmatory study with multireader multicase observer study
studies.finding: The AI system and radiologists detected clinically significant prostate cancer on 400 MRI examinations. The AI system had an AUROC of 0·91 vs 0·86 for the pool of 62 radiologists, which was statistically superior. Against routine practice readings in 1000 cases, non-inferiority was not confirmed.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design, with the comparison to routine practice not confirming non-inferiority.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence and radiologists in prostate cancer detection on MRI (PI-CAI): an international, paired, non-inferiority, confirmatory study.

studies.design: Historical controls with prospective evaluation across three workflow periods
studies.ai_system: Regulatory-cleared AI software for incidental pulmonary embolism detection and worklist prioritization
studies.finding: Across 11 736 oncology CT scans, AI-based worklist prioritization reduced median detection and notification time for IPE to 87 minutes vs 7714 minutes routine and 4973 minutes human triage. Radiologists' missed rate of IPE fell from 44.8% (47 of 105) without AI to 2.6% (one of 38) with AI (P < .001).
studies.limitation: Non-randomised sequential periods with historical controls; low event numbers; backlog setting; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Tool for Detection and Worklist Prioritization Reduces Time to Diagnosis of Incidental Pulmonary Embolism at CT.

studies.design: Retrospective analysis of 100 ED admissions
studies.finding: Diagnostic accuracy for internal medicine emergencies against discharge diagnosis in 100 patients. GPT-4 outperformed ED resident physicians (P=.01) and GPT-3.5 (P<.001), with significant superiority over physicians in cardiovascular disease (P=.03).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, single-centre, small sample of 100 patients.
studies.title: ChatGPT With GPT-4 Outperforms Emergency Department Physicians in Diagnostic Accuracy: Retrospective Analysis.

studies.design: Cross-sectional vignette study
studies.finding: On three validated clinical scenarios, ChatGPT showed indecisiveness in initial assessments, suggested unnecessary tests and modified decisions inappropriately on re-evaluation compared with expert nurses and students. It responded about 4 times faster than novices and twice as fast as experts.
studies.limitation: Only three scenarios and nurses rather than physicians; largely qualitative reporting of decision quality.
studies.title: A comparative vignette study: Evaluating the potential role of a generative AI model in enhancing clinical decision-making in nursing.

studies.design: Randomised controlled trial of AI-assisted vs conventional colonoscopy
studies.ai_system: Fujifilm CADEye and Medtronic GI Genius
studies.finding: Adenoma detection in colonoscopy among 240 analysed patients. ADR did not differ between AI-assisted and conventional colonoscopy (41% vs 43%), though sessile serrated lesion detection was higher with AI (22% vs 11%, p=0.004).
studies.limitation: Single-centre trial with modest sample, mostly experienced endoscopists.
studies.title: Impact of AI-aided colonoscopy in clinical practice: a prospective randomised controlled trial.

studies.design: Single-centre randomised clinical trial
studies.ai_system: Machine learning models predicting postoperative mortality and AKI
studies.humans: Anaesthesiologists and nurse anaesthetists providing telemedicine support
studies.finding: Clinicians predicted 30-day mortality and AKI for 5071 patients with or without ML predictions. Mortality AUROC was 0.793 assisted vs 0.780 unassisted (P=0.76); AKI AUROC was 0.734 vs 0.688 (P=0.06). Clinician performance was not improved by machine learning assistance.
studies.limitation: Single centre; clinicians were remote telemedicine reviewers rather than treating teams.
studies.title: Effect of machine learning models on clinician prediction of postoperative complications: the Perioperative ORACLE randomised clinical trial.

studies.design: Multicenter parallel-group randomized controlled trial
studies.ai_system: Cloud-based real-time CADe system for colonoscopy
studies.finding: Colorectal neoplasia detection in 841 patients randomized to CADe-assisted or standard colonoscopy. CADe improved adenomas per colonoscopy (0.82 vs. 0.62, Ratio 1.33) and adenoma detection rate (43.2% vs. 35.9%), with improved SSL and large polyp detection; PPA was non-inferior.
studies.limitation: Endoscopists unblinded to assignment; outcomes are detection rates rather than clinical outcomes.
studies.title: A novel cloud-based artificial intelligence for real-time detection of colorectal neoplasia - a randomized controlled trial (EAGLE).

studies.design: Model development with three reader studies
studies.finding: In reader studies, PanDerm outperformed clinicians by 10.2% in early-stage melanoma detection through longitudinal analysis. PanDerm assistance improved clinicians' skin cancer diagnostic accuracy by 11% on dermoscopy images and enhanced nondermatologist providers' differential diagnosis by 16.5% across 128 skin conditions.
studies.limitation: Reader studies on images within a model-development paper; reader numbers and details not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A multimodal vision foundation model for clinical dermatology.

studies.design: Clinical validation: real-time scanning, test-retest and large databases vs manual measurement
studies.ai_system: Automatic LV volume and EF AI software
studies.humans: Echocardiography readers (4 readers in reproducibility arm)
studies.finding: AI measurement of LV volumes and EF was compared with manual measurement. Real-time AI reduced total acquisition and processing time by 77% (median 5.3 min, P < 0.001); test-retest reproducibility was superior inter-observer and non-inferior intra-observer, with good agreement with reference and no decrease in accuracy compared with experts.
studies.limitation: Small real-time sample (50 patients); agreement reported qualitatively in abstract.
studies.title: Automatic measurements of left ventricular volumes and ejection fraction by artificial intelligence: clinical validation in real time and large databases.

studies.design: Single-centre randomised controlled trial of CADe-assisted vs standard colonoscopy
studies.finding: Adenoma detection rate in routine colonoscopy was compared between standard and CADe-assisted colonoscopy in 2015 participants. ADR was 33·7% (341 of 1012) in the standard group and 37·5% (376 of 1003) in the CADe group (estimated mean absolute difference 4·1 percentage points [95% CI 0·0-8·1]; p=0·051).
studies.limitation: Single centre with endoscopists unblinded; primary difference did not reach statistical significance.
studies.title: Effect of real-time computer-aided detection of colorectal adenoma in routine colonoscopy (COLO-GENIUS): a single-centre randomised controlled trial.

studies.design: International multicentre randomised tandem trial
studies.finding: In 916 screening/surveillance colonoscopies, adenomas per colonoscopy were higher with CAD (0·70 vs 0·51, p=0·015), with non-inferior adenomas per extraction (0·59 vs 0·66). Adenoma miss rate in tandem colonoscopies was 19% with CAD first vs 36% with conventional first (p=0·024).
studies.limitation: Endoscopists unblinded to assignment; tandem subset small (127 patients).
studies.title: A computer-aided polyp detection system in screening and surveillance colonoscopy: an international, multicentre, randomised, tandem trial.

studies.design: Prospective single-center randomized controlled trial
studies.ai_system: AI diagnostic support system for ESCC detection during endoscopy
studies.finding: Detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma during EGD in 320 patients. Detection rate among nonexperts was 47% with AI vs 45% control (P = 0.93), experts 87% vs 57% (P = 0.20), all endoscopists 57% vs 50% (P = 0.70).
studies.limitation: Single-center exploratory trial likely underpowered; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Randomized controlled trial of an artificial intelligence diagnostic system for the detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in clinical practice.

studies.design: Randomized blinded exploratory study of simulated telehealth consultations
studies.finding: In 105 simulated multimodal telehealth consultations assessed by 18 specialists, multimodal AMIE outperformed PCPs in diagnostic accuracy and conversation quality. It was superior on 29 of 32 evaluation axes, including seven of nine multimodal reasoning metrics.
studies.limitation: Simulated consultations with patient actors; number of PCPs not stated; developer-run study.
studies.title: Advancing conversational diagnostic AI with multimodal reasoning.

studies.design: Cross-sectional evaluation on NEJM Image Challenges
studies.finding: GPT-4V performed comparably to human physicians in multi-choice accuracy (81.6% vs. 77.8%). However, it presented flawed rationales in 35.5% of correctly answered cases.
studies.limitation: Quiz cases with aggregate physician responses; not real clinical care.
studies.title: Hidden flaws behind expert-level accuracy of multimodal GPT-4 vision in medicine.

studies.design: Cohort study with propensity matching and difference-in-difference, intervention hospital vs 3 control hospitals
studies.ai_system: Machine learning 30-day mortality prediction algorithm with physician notification
studies.finding: Patients whose physicians were notified of high ML-predicted mortality were 5 times more likely to have documented goals of care discussions (OR, 5.11) than matched controls. GOCDs occurred earlier (median 4 vs 16 days).
studies.limitation: Non-randomized observational design in one health system.
studies.title: Advanced Care Planning for Hospitalized Patients Following Clinician Notification of Patient Mortality by a Machine Learning Algorithm.

studies.design: Comparative case-file study
studies.finding: On 50 case files, all chatbots reached at least human performance, and accGPT performed best in giving ACR "usually appropriate" recommendations. Chatbots took 5 minutes and 0.19 € for all cases vs 50 minutes and 29.99 € for radiologists.
studies.limitation: Small set of 50 cases; radiologist number not stated.
studies.title: A Context-based Chatbot Surpasses Trained Radiologists and Generic ChatGPT in Following the ACR Appropriateness Guidelines.

studies.design: Comparative vignette study
studies.humans: Untrained ED doctors; professional triage raters
studies.finding: On 124 vignettes, GPT-4-based ChatGPT (κ=0.67) and untrained doctors (κ=0.68) had similar agreement with professional consensus triage. Using the LLM as second opinion gave a nonsignificant increase (κ=0.70; P=.97).
studies.limitation: Vignettes rather than live triage; number of doctors not stated.
studies.title: Triage Performance Across Large Language Models, ChatGPT, and Untrained Doctors in Emergency Medicine: Comparative Study.

studies.design: Randomized online vignette experiment comparing explainable AI CDSS prototypes against Centor Score
studies.ai_system: Explainable AI CDSS prototypes for strep throat prediction from smartphone throat images
studies.finding: Telehealth providers predicted strep throat from clinical vignettes using either the Modified Centor Score or a randomly assigned explainable AI prototype. Compared with the Centor Score, AI-based CDSS improved clinicians' predictions. Participants nonetheless reported lower trust in the AI and requested more in-person confirmatory testing.
studies.limitation: Online survey with vignettes rather than real patients; the comparator was a Centor Score aid rather than no aid, and no effect sizes are reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Explainable AI decision support improves accuracy during telehealth strep throat screening.

studies.design: Multicenter cluster randomized active-controlled trial
studies.ai_system: Deep-learning-enabled CDSS predicting antidepressant remission probabilities plus clinical algorithm (AID-ME)
studies.humans: Clinicians treating outpatient adults with moderate or greater MDD at 9 sites
studies.finding: For depression treatment selection and management, remission (MADRS <11) at study exit occurred in 12 (28.6%) patients of clinicians with the AI-CDSS versus 0% in the active-control group (P = .012). Speed of improvement was 1.26 vs 0.37 (P = .03).
studies.limitation: Small sample (61 patients analysed) and no primary care clinicians, as acknowledged by the authors.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence in Depression-Medication Enhancement (AID-ME): A Cluster Randomized Trial of a Deep-Learning-Enabled Clinical Decision Support System for Personalized Depression Treatment Selection and Management.

studies.design: Pragmatic open-label cluster randomized controlled trial at 2 hospitals
studies.ai_system: AI-enabled ECG alerts for atrial fibrillation
studies.finding: AI-ECG alerts to noncardiologists increased NOAC prescription within 90 days in AI-detected AF patients (23.3% versus 12.0%; HR 1.85) and AF diagnosis (HR 1.40). No significant differences were seen in echocardiograms, cardiologist visits, stroke or death.
studies.limitation: Open-label trial at two hospitals in Taiwan; small numbers with AI-detected AF limit outcome analyses.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled ECGs for Atrial Fibrillation Identification and Enhanced Oral Anticoagulant Adoption: A Pragmatic Randomized Clinical Trial.
studies.source: Journal of the American Heart Association

studies.design: Randomized, blinded virtual OSCE across 100 multivisit case scenarios plus RxQA medication benchmark
studies.finding: AMIE was compared with 21 PCPs on multivisit management in 100 guideline-based scenarios; AMIE was non-inferior to PCPs in management reasoning as assessed by specialists and scored better on preciseness of treatment and investigation and on guideline alignment. On the RxQA medication benchmark, AMIE outperformed PCPs on higher-difficulty questions.
studies.limitation: Simulated virtual OSCE scenarios rather than real patient care.
studies.title: Towards conversational artificial intelligence for disease management.

studies.design: Open-label randomized non-inferiority trial in an emergency department
studies.ai_system: RISK INDEX machine-learning 31-day mortality prediction tool
studies.humans: Internal medicine specialists in the ED
studies.finding: 31-day mortality risk stratification in 1303 ED patients randomized to standard care or standard care plus RISK INDEX. RISK INDEX's prognostic accuracy matched or outperformed clinical intuition (AUROC 0.84 vs. 0.73-0.76), but it did not alter treatment plans (1/644 changes; 0.16%) or clinical outcomes.
studies.limitation: Single-centre, unblinded trial; number of participating physicians not stated.
studies.title: Machine learning for risk stratification in the emergency department (MARS-ED): a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Prospective paired diagnostic accuracy study on 300 histopathology-verified oral lesion cases
studies.ai_system: Gemini Pro 2.5 with three prompting strategies
studies.finding: Diagnosis of oral lesions from clinical vignettes. Human experts achieved the highest Top-1 accuracy (61%), while Chain-of-Thought prompting led in Top-3 accuracy (82%); no AI prompt matched humans in low-difficulty cases.
studies.limitation: Number of experts not stated; vignette-based evaluation.
studies.title: Prompt-dependent performance of multimodal AI model in oral diagnosis: a comprehensive analysis of accuracy, narrative quality, calibration, and latency versus human experts.

studies.design: Comparison on 14,606 ambulatory ECG recordings with cardiologist consensus panel adjudication
studies.finding: For critical arrhythmias, the AI had mean sensitivity of 98.6% versus 80.3% for technicians, with a relative risk of missed diagnosis 14.1 times higher for technicians. The AI had a higher false-positive event rate (12 vs 5 per 1,000 patient days).
studies.limitation: The comparators were technicians, not physicians, and only a sample of events was adjudicated.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence for direct-to-physician reporting of ambulatory electrocardiography.

studies.design: Prospective multicenter study
studies.ai_system: UltraSight real-time echocardiography guidance on Lumify handheld device
studies.humans: 6 nurses and 3 medical residents (novices) vs expert sonographers without AI
studies.finding: Novices guided by AI scanned 240 patients; 99.2%, 99.6%, 92.9% and 100% of studies had sufficient quality for the key assessments. Images from novices and sonographers yielded concordant diagnostic interpretation in 83% to 96% of studies.
studies.limitation: Novices were not compared with unaided novices, only with experts; small number of operators.
studies.title: Real-Time Artificial Intelligence-Based Guidance of Echocardiographic Imaging by Novices: Image Quality and Suitability for Diagnostic Interpretation and Quantitative Analysis.

studies.design: Blinded cross-sectional comparison of ChatGPT-4.0 vs expert physician panel answers to 100 online patient questions, rated by patients and specialists
studies.humans: Expert panel of experienced physicians from a web-based platform
studies.finding: For 100 public health questions across 5 specialties, patients rated ChatGPT higher than physician answers for empathy (4.18 vs 2.7; P<.001) and usefulness (4.04 vs 2.98; P<.001). Specialist physicians also rated ChatGPT higher in correctness (4.51 vs 3.55; P<.001), though patients did not recognise potentially harmful ChatGPT responses.
studies.limitation: Written answers from a single web platform; may not generalise to clinical care.
studies.title: "Doctor ChatGPT, Can You Help Me?" The Patient's Perspective: Cross-Sectional Study.

studies.design: Large-scale prospective tandem randomised controlled trial (ChiCTR2100050654)
studies.ai_system: Computer-aided detection system for early esophageal carcinoma during NBI endoscopy
studies.finding: 3400 patients were randomised to CAD-first or routine-first NBI endoscopy for detection of esophageal neoplasia. The CAD-first group had a neoplastic lesion detection rate of 3.12% vs 1.59% in the routine-first group (relative detection ratio 1.96, P = 0.0047). Junior endoscopists benefited, with no significant difference for senior endoscopists.
studies.limitation: Number of endoscopists not stated; benefit confined to junior endoscopists in subgroup analysis.
studies.title: Effect of computer aided detection system on esophageal neoplasm diagnosis in varied levels of endoscopists.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of ChatGPT answers vs online expert answers to 115 radiation oncology patient questions
studies.humans: Online expert answers from professional society websites
studies.finding: Of 115 questions, the LLM performed the same or better than expert answers in 108 responses (94%) for relative correctness, 89 (77%) for completeness and 105 (91%) for conciseness; only 2 were rated potentially harmful. LLM readability was at a higher level (13.64 vs 10.63; P < .001).
studies.limitation: Compared against website text rather than clinicians answering directly; small rater panel.
studies.title: Quality of Large Language Model Responses to Radiation Oncology Patient Care Questions.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on 150 real brain tumor MRI reports
studies.finding: GPT-4 and five radiologists suggested diagnoses from the textual findings of 150 preoperative brain tumor MRI reports, with pathology as ground truth. GPT-4 achieved final diagnostic accuracy of 73% versus 65 to 79% for radiologists. For differential diagnoses GPT-4 reached 94% versus 73 to 89% for radiologists.
studies.limitation: Text reports only (translated from Japanese), small number of radiologists, two institutions.
studies.title: Comparative analysis of GPT-4-based ChatGPT's diagnostic performance with radiologists using real-world radiology reports of brain tumors.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic study of thyroid nodule US images comparing LLMs alone and human-LLM interaction strategies against pathology
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT 3.5, ChatGPT 4.0, Google Bard; image-to-text model + LLM; CNN
studies.humans: Two senior readers and one junior reader
studies.finding: For malignancy diagnosis of 1161 thyroid nodule US images, ChatGPT 4.0 had an accuracy of 78%-86% and sensitivity of 86%-95%. With ChatGPT 4.0, the image-to-text-LLM strategy reached AUC 0.83 and accuracy 84%, comparable to the human-LLM interaction strategy with two senior readers and one junior reader and exceeding the human-LLM strategy with one junior reader.
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective image set; no clear comparison of readers with versus without LLM reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Collaborative Enhancement of Consistency and Accuracy in US Diagnosis of Thyroid Nodules Using Large Language Models.

studies.design: Model development with prospective test set; radiologist reading time with and without AI
studies.ai_system: CNN for head and neck CT angiography stenosis/plaque
studies.finding: The algorithm's plaque classification agreed with radiologists in 85.6% of cases per vessel. AI assistance reduced radiologists' diagnosis and report-writing time from 28.8 minutes ± 5.6 to 12.4 minutes ± 2.0 (P < .001).
studies.limitation: Primarily model development; accuracy with vs without AI not reported, and reader number not stated.
studies.title: Deep Learning for Head and Neck CT Angiography: Stenosis and Plaque Classification.

studies.design: Cross-sectional study on 1226 Chinese fundus fluorescein angiography reports
studies.finding: Classification of retinal vascular disease from angiography reports. ChatGPT with English direct-diagnosis prompts reached an F1-score of 80.05% (70.47% with Chinese prompts), against 89.35% for ophthalmologists and 82.69% for interns.
studies.limitation: Single-language report set; the number of clinicians is not stated and the task is text-only.
studies.title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study.

studies.design: Pragmatic randomized controlled trial
studies.ai_system: AI-ECG low ejection fraction decision support
studies.finding: Early diagnosis of low EF among 13,631 inpatients. AI-ECG results increased newly diagnosed low EF (1.5% vs. 1.1%, HR 1.50, 95% CI: 1.11-2.03) with similar echocardiogram use (17.1% vs. 17.3%) and higher PPV (34.2% vs. 20.2%).
studies.limitation: Single academic centre; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis and prognostication in low ejection fraction using electrocardiograms in inpatient department: a pragmatic randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Randomized double-blind evaluation of therapy transcripts plus real-world deployment analysis
studies.ai_system: LLM with cognitive layer architecture for psychotherapy
studies.humans: Human clinicians delivering therapy sessions; 22 expert clinician raters
studies.finding: 227 participants generated mental well-being session transcripts with different therapy agents, rated by 22 expert clinicians. LLMs augmented with the cognitive layer architecture consistently outperformed both standalone LLMs and human clinicians across key CBT competencies.
studies.limitation: Comparison based on rated transcripts of naturalistic sessions with participants rather than clinical patients; number of human therapists not stated.
studies.title: A cognitive layer architecture to support large-language model performance in psychotherapy interactions.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on Radiology Diagnosis Please cases with image inputs
studies.finding: On 190 cases, radiologists' overall accuracy was 61%, versus 49% for GPT-4V and 39% for Gemini Pro Vision at temperature 1. Radiologists were significantly better than Gemini (P < .001), but the difference from GPT-4V was not significant after Bonferroni adjustment (P = .02).
studies.limitation: Published quiz cases rather than clinical practice.
studies.title: Comparing Diagnostic Accuracy of Radiologists versus GPT-4V and Gemini Pro Vision Using Image Inputs from Diagnosis Please Cases.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-reader crossover randomised study
studies.ai_system: Deep learning algorithm for acute intracranial haemorrhage detection on brain CT
studies.finding: Nine reviewers interpreted brain CTs from 296 patients for acute intracranial haemorrhage with and without AI assistance. Patient-wise diagnostic accuracy was 0.9703 with AI vs 0.9471 without (p < 0.0001). Non-radiologist physicians improved most; neuroradiologists showed a non-significant trend.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study with only nine readers, so it does not show effects in live care.
studies.title: Deep learning based automatic detection algorithm for acute intracranial haemorrhage: a pivotal randomized clinical trial.

studies.design: Human-computer comparison study on 75 cases
studies.finding: For rare disease differential diagnosis from EHRs, PhenoBrain achieved top-3 recall of 0.613 and top-10 recall of 0.813, surpassing 50 specialist physicians. Combining PhenoBrain's predictions with specialists increased top-3 recall to 0.768.
studies.limitation: Only 75 cases; specialists' own figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A phenotype-based AI pipeline outperforms human experts in differentially diagnosing rare diseases using EHRs.

studies.design: Model development with prospective validation against clinician predictions
studies.ai_system: POPS machine learning model using preoperative EHR data
studies.finding: POPS predicted maximum postoperative pain (0-10 NRS) on the day of surgery and four subsequent days. In prospective validation, POPS outperformed clinician predictions on all postoperative days, though with degraded calibration.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives no numerical results for the clinician comparison or the number of clinicians.
studies.title: Development and prospective validation of postoperative pain prediction from preoperative EHR data using attention-based set embeddings.

studies.design: Blinded clinician rating of AI vs human suggestions
studies.humans: Humans who generated suggestions for improving clinical decision support alerts
studies.finding: Five clinicians rated 36 AI-generated and 29 human-generated suggestions for improving 7 CDS alerts. Of the 20 highest-scoring suggestions, 9 were generated by ChatGPT, and AI suggestions were rated highly understandable and relevant but of moderate usefulness and low acceptance.
studies.limitation: Very small sample of alerts and raters, with limited quantitative comparison.
studies.title: Using AI-generated suggestions from ChatGPT to optimize clinical decision support.
studies.source: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

studies.design: Pilot vignette study
studies.finding: ChatGPT-3 and physicians produced differential diagnoses for clinical vignettes covering ten common chief complaints. Within five-item differential lists, physicians were correct more often than ChatGPT-3 (98.3% vs 83.3%, p = 0.03); the abstract also reports 53.3% vs 93.3% for the top diagnosis while stating physicians were superior.
studies.limitation: Small pilot with physician-authored vignettes, and the abstract's top-diagnosis figures are internally inconsistent.
studies.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Differential-Diagnosis Lists Generated by Generative Pretrained Transformer 3 Chatbot for Clinical Vignettes with Common Chief Complaints: A Pilot Study.
studies.source: International journal of environmental research and public health

studies.design: Test-retest study of LV GLS measurement on repeated echocardiograms, AI vs readers
studies.finding: Test-retest variability was lower with AI than interreader scenarios (dataset I: MDC 3.7 vs 5.5; dataset II: MDC 3.9 vs 5.2; all P < .05). There was bias in 13 of 24 interreader scenarios but none with AI.
studies.limitation: Small datasets (n = 40 and n = 32) measuring reproducibility rather than accuracy.
studies.title: Deep Learning for Improved Precision and Reproducibility of Left Ventricular Strain in Echocardiography: A Test-Retest Study.
studies.source: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

studies.design: International multireader diagnostic observer study, with and without AI
studies.humans: 61 readers (34 experts, 27 nonexperts) from 53 centers in 17 countries
studies.finding: Readers assessed 360 biparametric prostate MRI exams for csPCa. AUROC rose from 0.882 unassisted to 0.916 with AI (P < .001); sensitivity from 94.3% to 96.8% and specificity from 46.7% to 50.1% at PI-RADS 3 or more, with greater benefit for nonexperts.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study, not prospective clinical workflow.
studies.title: AI-Assisted vs Unassisted Identification of Prostate Cancer in Magnetic Resonance Images.

studies.design: Nonblinded parallel-group randomized controlled trial in a simulated setting
studies.ai_system: Ambu Broncho Simulator AI navigational system with augmented reality
studies.humans: Critical-care physicians trained by AI only vs by expert tutor
studies.finding: Forty critical-care physicians received 30 minutes of bronchoscopy training guided by AI only (n=19) or expert tutor feedback (n=21). AI-trained physicians had better mean intersegmental time (-7.9 s, p=0.027), procedure time (-77 s, p=0.022) and segments revisited (-7 segments, p=0.019); no significant difference for other measures.
studies.limitation: Simulated setting, small single-centre trial, nonblinded; not validated in patients.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Bronchoscopy is Superior to Human Expert Instruction for the Performance of Critical-Care Physicians: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Randomized clinical study comparing manual registrations by users of varying experience with automatic AI registration of CBCT and intraoral scans in 150 patients
studies.ai_system: AI registration tool integrated into implant planning software
studies.humans: Experienced user, inexperienced operator, post-graduate implant dentistry students
studies.finding: Accuracy of CBCT-to-intraoral scan registration was measured by linear measurements between anatomical landmarks. Fully automatic AI registration was not significantly different from conventional methods in patients without restorations; with multiple restoration artifacts, user experience was important for accurate registration.
studies.limitation: Few operators; accuracy depends on presence of restoration artifacts; numeric results not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Accuracy of manual and artificial intelligence-based superimposition of cone-beam computed tomography with digital scan data, utilizing an implant planning software: A randomized clinical study.

studies.design: International multicentre randomised controlled trial
studies.finding: Adenoma detection during colonoscopy in 430 individuals with Lynch syndrome randomised to CADe-assisted or white light endoscopy alone. Mean adenomas per colonoscopy were 0·64 in both groups (adjusted rate ratio 1·03; p=0·87).
studies.limitation: Endoscopists were not masked; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: An artificial intelligence-assisted system versus white light endoscopy alone for adenoma detection in individuals with Lynch syndrome (TIMELY): an international, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

studies.design: Prospective paired accuracy study of 100 biopsy-confirmed oral lesion cases with vignettes and photographs
studies.finding: LLMs and an oral medicine expert produced Top-5 ranked differentials for 100 biopsy-confirmed oral lesions. Top-1 accuracies were 52% (ChatGPT-5), 59% (ChatGPT-4o), and 79% (expert; p < 0.001); at Top-5, 78%, 83%, and 91%.
studies.limitation: Single expert comparator and standardized vignettes rather than live consultations.
studies.title: ChatGPT-5 vs oral medicine experts for rank-based differential diagnosis of oral lesions: a prospective, biopsy-validated comparison.

studies.design: Pilot cross-sectional question study
studies.ai_system: Nine chatbots including ChatGPT4, Bard, Claude, Llama
studies.humans: General dentists, pediatric dentists and students (n = 20/group)
studies.finding: On 30 true/false pediatric dentistry questions, pediatric dentists (96.67%) and general dentists (88.0%) were significantly more accurate than chatbots; students scored 80.8%. ChatGPT had the highest chatbot accuracy (78%).
studies.limitation: Pilot study with only 30 true/false questions.
studies.title: Accuracy and consistency of chatbots versus clinicians for answering pediatric dentistry questions: A pilot study.

studies.design: Equivalence study with blinded specialist ratings
studies.finding: Responses to 200 cancer questions from Reddit r/AskDocs rated by oncologists. The best chatbot (Claude) scored higher than physicians in quality (3.56 vs 3.00), empathy (3.62 vs 2.43) and readability (3.79 vs 3.07; all P < .001).
studies.limitation: Physician comparator responses came from an online forum, not clinical practice; pilot rating measures.
studies.title: Physician and Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Responses to Cancer Questions From Social Media.

studies.design: Single-centre RCT, 415 participants
studies.finding: Colonoscopy with versus without CADe. ADR was 59.4% in the CADe group and 47.6% in the control group (p = 0.018); rectosigmoid adenoma miss rate was 11.9% vs 26.0% (p = 0.037).
studies.limitation: Single centre; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Clinical Evaluation of Computer-Aided Colorectal Neoplasia Detection Using a Novel Endoscopic Artificial Intelligence: A Single-Center Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Prospective real-time comparison during colonoscopy, histopathology reference
studies.finding: Optical diagnosis of 423 diminutive polyps as neoplastic vs non-neoplastic. POLAR achieved 79 % accuracy, 89 % sensitivity, 38 % specificity; endoscopists achieved 83 % accuracy, 92 % sensitivity, 44 % specificity. Accuracy did not differ significantly (P = 0.10).
studies.limitation: Low specificity for both and few hyperplastic polyps; FIT-positive population only.
studies.title: Computer-aided diagnosis for optical diagnosis of diminutive colorectal polyps including sessile serrated lesions: a real-time comparison with screening endoscopists.

studies.design: Prospective single-centre diagnostic study with temporally independent test cohort
studies.finding: Detection of gallbladder cancer on ultrasound in 273 test patients. The DL model had sensitivity 92.3%, specificity 74.4% and AUC 0.887, comparable to both radiologists.
studies.limitation: Single centre; only two radiologists.
studies.title: Deep-learning enabled ultrasound based detection of gallbladder cancer in northern India: a prospective diagnostic study.
studies.source: The Lancet regional health. Southeast Asia

studies.design: Single-institution randomised trial
studies.finding: Adenoma detection in colonoscopy for 800 patients. ADR was 58.8% with LCA vs 43.5% with LCI alone (P<0.001), and APC 1.31 vs 0.94.
studies.limitation: Single institution; endoscopist number not stated; unblinded.
studies.title: Linked-color imaging with or without artificial intelligence for adenoma detection: a randomized trial.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on existing patient data set
studies.finding: ChatGPT-4 listed the correct top diagnosis in 35% vs 39% for rheumatologists (p = 0.30) and within the top 3 in 60% vs 55% (p = 0.38). It had better sensitivity for IRD at the cost of lower specificity.
