studies.limitation: Pilot study on a prior data set; number of rheumatologists not stated.
studies.title: Diagnostic accuracy of a large language model in rheumatology: comparison of physician and ChatGPT-4.

studies.design: Model development with stepwise validation including comparison with physicians and single-arm feasibility trial
studies.finding: For inpatient insulin titration in type 2 diabetes, RL-DITR showed better glycemic control performance than junior and intermediate physicians (MAE of 1.18 ± 0.09 U) on quantitative and blinded qualitative review. Physician values are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Physician comparison details and numbers not reported; feasibility trial had only 16 patients.
studies.title: Optimized glycemic control of type 2 diabetes with reinforcement learning: a proof-of-concept trial.

studies.design: Three-phase reader study comparing explainable AI vs conventional AI support
studies.ai_system: Explainable AI for melanoma vs nevi diagnosis
studies.finding: Dermatologists diagnosed melanomas and nevi with XAI versus conventional AI support. Confidence and trust significantly increased with XAI compared to conventional AI; no accuracy numbers are reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Abstract reports no quantitative accuracy results or reader numbers.
studies.title: Dermatologist-like explainable AI enhances trust and confidence in diagnosing melanoma.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic study with blinded physician rating
studies.ai_system: Multimodal generative AI chest radiograph report model
studies.humans: On-site attending radiologists and teleradiology service
studies.finding: 500 ED chest radiograph reports were rated on a 5-point Likert scale by 6 ED physicians. AI scored 3.22 and radiologist reports 3.34, not significantly different, both higher than teleradiology at 2.74; no difference in probability of no clinically significant discrepancy.
studies.limitation: Single centre retrospective; quality judged by Likert ratings rather than outcomes.
studies.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Chest Radiograph Interpretation in the Emergency Department.

studies.design: Prospective consecutive comparison of automated AI vs manual echo LVEF with CMR reference
studies.humans: Echo readers using modified biplane Simpson
studies.finding: In 229 analysed patients, Auto-Echo and MBS-Echo both correlated with CMR (R = 0.89 and 0.89) with comparable AUCs (0.93 and 0.92). Auto-Echo was closer to CMR in reduced LVEF and had lower test-retest variability (2.5% vs 7.9%).
studies.limitation: Number of human readers not stated; single study population.
studies.title: Improved assessment of left ventricular ejection fraction using artificial intelligence in echocardiography: A comparative analysis with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.

studies.design: Comparative reader study
studies.finding: On six panoramic radiographs, AI achieved a mean score of 6.12 for identifying teeth with attachment loss vs 5.43 for senior specialists, 4.58 for specialists and 3.65 for general dentists. AI performance was comparable to senior specialists.
studies.limitation: Only six images assessed.
studies.title: AI Efficiency in Dentistry: Comparing Artificial Intelligence Systems with Human Practitioners in Assessing Several Periodontal Parameters.

studies.design: Single-center pragmatic randomized controlled trial, 1100 patients
studies.finding: Patients undergoing colonoscopy were randomised to real-time CADe or traditional colonoscopy. Adenoma detection rate was 42.5% with CADe vs 34.4% without (P = .005), and mean adenomas per colonoscopy 0.89 ± 1.46 vs 0.60 ± 1.12 (P < .001). The benefit was larger in the first half of the study (47.2% vs 33.7%) than the second half (38.7% vs 34.9%; P = .33).
studies.limitation: Single community center; benefit attenuated over time and driven by diminutive adenomas.
studies.title: The Efficacy of Real-time Computer-aided Detection of Colonic Neoplasia in Community Practice: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial.
studies.source: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

studies.design: Randomised controlled trial, three arms, 171 patients analysed
studies.finding: Patients undergoing caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia were randomised to oscillometric, continuous non-invasive, or hypotension prediction index-guided haemodynamic management. Median time-weighted average hypotension was 0.89 mmHg and 0.30 mmHg vs 0.08 mmHg in the HPI group (p < 0.001). Vomiting occurred in 13/59, 6/55 and 3/57 respectively (p = 0.023).
studies.limitation: Modest sample; number of clinicians not stated and outcome is a physiological surrogate.
studies.title: Proactive haemodynamic management using the hypotension prediction index during caesarean section: a randomised controlled study.

studies.design: Prospective real-world diagnostic accuracy study of 1690 melanocytic lesions in 143 high-risk patients
studies.ai_system: 3D-Vectra WB360 and 2D-FotoFinder-ATBM total body photography CNNs
studies.finding: For melanoma detection against histopathology, the 3D-CNN had sensitivity 90.0%, specificity 64.6% and ROC-AUC 0.92. Dermatologists and augmented intelligence achieved the same sensitivity (90%) with ROC-AUC 0.91 and 0.88 but superior specificity (92.3% and 86.2%). The 2D-CNN (sensitivity 70%, specificity 40%, ROC-AUC 0.68) was outperformed by 3D-CNN and dermatologists.
studies.limitation: Small number of patients at a single high-risk population; few melanomas limit precision.
studies.title: Diagnostic performance of augmented intelligence with 2D and 3D total body photography and convolutional neural networks in a high-risk population for melanoma under real-world conditions: A new era of skin cancer screening?

studies.design: Multicenter prospective study of 1036 patients with 2296 nodules
studies.finding: For thyroid nodule diagnosis against the global 2e criteria, the AI had sensitivity, specificity, accuracy and AUC of 0.868, 0.934, 0.917 and 0.901. The AI was comparable to senior radiologists and outperformed junior radiologists (all P < 0.05). AI assistance significantly improved junior radiologists' performance, bringing it to a level comparable to senior radiologists against pathology.
studies.limitation: The number of radiologists is not stated, and pathology was available for only a subset of nodules.
studies.title: The clinical value of artificial intelligence in assisting junior radiologists in thyroid ultrasound: a multicenter prospective study from real clinical practice.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial, 150 patients
studies.ai_system: Machine learning model on preoperative CBCT
studies.finding: Dental implant planning with AI versus traditional assessment. Implant success was 92% in the AI-assisted group versus 78% in the traditional group; AI prediction accuracy was 87% versus 71% for traditional methods.
studies.limitation: Number of clinicians and methods poorly described; small single trial.
studies.title: Evaluating the Role of AI in Predicting the Success of Dental Implants Based on Preoperative CBCT Images: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Prospective randomized unblinded controlled implementation study
studies.ai_system: AI triage system for screening mammography
studies.finding: Screening participants were randomized to AI-prioritized same-visit radiologist evaluation versus standard care. Control time to additional imaging was 25.6 days and to biopsy diagnosis 55.9 days; the AI group's mean times were reduced by 25% (6.4 fewer days) and 30% (16.8 fewer days) respectively.
studies.limitation: Unblinded, operational endpoints only; diagnostic accuracy not compared; single implementation setting.
studies.title: Triaging mammography with artificial intelligence: an implementation study.

studies.design: Prospective single-center pretest/post-test randomized clinical trial
studies.humans: Endoscopists of different seniority, including junior doctors
studies.finding: AI-assisted endoscopy increased detection of intestinal metaplasia (14.23% vs 9.15%, P = 0.013), atrophy (22.76% vs 17.28%, P = 0.031) and intestinal adenomas (48.52% vs 24.58%, P < 0.001) compared with control. Gains were notable among junior doctors (e.g., adenomas 45.18% vs 29.27%, P = 0.002).
studies.limitation: Single-center study with pretest/post-test design; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence system improves the quality of digestive endoscopy: A prospective pretest and post-test single-center clinical trial.
studies.source: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver

studies.design: Prospective open-label randomized pilot trial
studies.ai_system: Generative AI virtual assistant with retrieval-augmented generation, run by nonmedical staff
studies.humans: Doctors or nurses delivering standard care
studies.finding: GDMT optimization in 60 patients with new HFrEF over 12 weeks. VA-guided care delivered by nonmedical staff achieved superior GDMT optimization across all medication classes, lower NT-proBNP and fewer hospitalizations than standard care by doctors or nurses.
studies.limitation: Small pilot (n = 60), open-label; no numeric results in abstract.
studies.title: Design and Architecture of a Generative-AI-Supported, Nonphysician-Delivered Model for GDMT Optimization in HFrEF: The ASSIST-HF Trial.

studies.design: Multicentre prospective diagnostic clinical trial
studies.ai_system: Mobile phone-powered 7-class AI algorithm and ISIC AI algorithm
studies.finding: For 172 suspicious pigmented lesions, the 7-class AI was equivalent to specialists (accuracy difference 1·2% [95% CI -6·9 to 9·2]) and superior to novices (21·5%), while the ISIC AI was inferior to specialists (-11·6%). For management decisions, the 7-class AI was significantly inferior to specialists (-0·5% scenario A; -0·4% scenario B) and mixed versus novices.
studies.limitation: Specialist tertiary settings, Fitzpatrick I-III skin only, and number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Comparison of humans versus mobile phone-powered artificial intelligence for the diagnosis and management of pigmented skin cancer in secondary care: a multicentre, prospective, diagnostic, clinical trial.

studies.design: Randomized tandem video trial, with and without AI order
studies.ai_system: AI-based clinical decision support system for Barrett's esophagus
studies.humans: 22 endoscopists from 12 centers, BE experts and nonexperts
studies.finding: Endoscopists assessed 96 videos for Barrett's esophagus-related neoplasia. AI stand-alone sensitivity, specificity and accuracy were 92.2%, 68.9% and 81.3%, versus 83.3%, 58.1% and 71.5% for BE experts without AI. With AI, BE nonexperts improved sensitivity from 69.8% to 78.0% and specificity from 67.3% to 72.7%, though experts and nonexperts remained below AI stand-alone performance.
studies.limitation: Video-based assessment rather than live endoscopy, with a modest number of endoscopists.
studies.title: Influence of artificial intelligence on the diagnostic performance of endoscopists in the assessment of Barrett's esophagus: a tandem randomized and video trial.

studies.design: Multicenter model development and testing with expert comparison
studies.finding: LLNM-Net predicted lateral lymph node metastasis in thyroid cancer from ultrasound and clinical data. In multicenter testing it achieved an AUC of 0.944 and 84.7% accuracy, outperforming human experts (64.3% accuracy).
studies.limitation: Retrospective model-development study; number and experience of human experts not stated in the abstract.
studies.title: Explainable multimodal deep learning for predicting thyroid cancer lateral lymph node metastasis using ultrasound imaging.

studies.design: Pragmatic cluster randomized trial
studies.ai_system: Machine learning mortality prediction model with notifications
studies.finding: Physicians were notified about patients at high mortality risk to prompt advance care planning. ACP documentation by the randomized physician was 34.7% vs 19.6% (OR 2.04; 95% CI 1.16-3.59); documentation by any clinician did not differ significantly (52.8% vs 42.8%).
studies.limitation: Single academic center; process outcome (documentation) rather than patient outcomes.
studies.title: Impact of Prognostic Notifications on Inpatient Advance Care Planning: A Cluster Randomized Trial.
studies.source: Journal of pain and symptom management

studies.design: Prospective cross-sectional comparison study
studies.ai_system: ResNet18 deep learning classifier on smartphone fundus images
studies.finding: Smartphone fundus images from 156 infants were graded for ROP by human graders and an AI system. Human graders detected TR-ROP with sensitivity 100% and specificity 83.49%, while the AI had TR-ROP sensitivity 100% with specificity 58.6%.
studies.limitation: Single-centre study with a small test set.
studies.title: Efficacy of Smartphone-Based Telescreening for Retinopathy of Prematurity With and Without Artificial Intelligence in India.

studies.design: Model development using data from two interventional studies, with external validation
studies.ai_system: Multimodal neural network (wound images plus PROMs)
studies.finding: The model predicted surgical site infection within 48 h from remote postoperative wound monitoring data. Its performance was comparable to clinician triage (0.762 [0.690-0.835] vs 0.777 [0.721-0.832]). Simulated use suggested an 80% reduction in staff time.
studies.limitation: Number of clinicians not stated; the staff-time saving is from simulated usage only.
studies.title: Multimodal machine learning to predict surgical site infection with healthcare workload impact assessment.

studies.design: Secondary analysis of prospective ScreenTrustCAD screening trial
studies.finding: Recall proportion and PPV by which reader flagged screening mammograms. Single flags: recall 14.2% after radiologist vs 4.6% after AI CAD, PPV 3.4% vs 22%. Double flags: two radiologists recall 57.2%, PPV 2.5% vs AI CAD plus one radiologist recall 38.6%, PPV 25.0%.
studies.limitation: Observational analysis of consensus behaviour within one trial; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Human-AI Interaction in the ScreenTrustCAD Trial: Recall Proportion and Positive Predictive Value Related to Screening Mammograms Flagged by AI CAD versus a Human Reader.

studies.design: Randomized, open-label, single-center tandem colonoscopy study
studies.finding: Patients were randomized to colonoscopy with or without CADe, followed by a tandem second colonoscopy by a different endoscopist to measure adenoma miss rate. The AMR was 17.4% in the CADe group versus 30.3% in the non-CADe group (P=0.009).
studies.limitation: Small single-center trial (48 vs 46 patients), open-label.
studies.title: Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence: Computer-aided Detection of Colorectal Polyps.
studies.source: Journal of the anus, rectum and colon

studies.design: Multicenter randomized controlled trial in seven hospitals
studies.ai_system: Endoscopy quality control assistant (EQCA), CNN with LSTM
studies.finding: Detection of upper GI cancer-related lesions during EGD, 16 012 patients with EQCA versus 16 005 controls. Detection rates were higher with EQCA for cancer-related lesions (8.00% vs. 5.55%) and cancer (1.93% vs. 1.21%; both P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Number of endoscopists not reported; longer inspection time may partly explain the effect.
studies.title: A novel artificial intelligence-based system for quality monitoring during esophagogastroduodenoscopy: a multicenter randomized controlled study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 106 published musculoskeletal quiz cases
studies.humans: A radiology resident and a board-certified radiologist
studies.finding: On 106 Skeletal Radiology 'Test Yourself' cases, GPT-4-based ChatGPT had 43% (46/106) accuracy and GPT-4V-based ChatGPT 8% (9/106). The radiology resident achieved 41% (43/106) and the board-certified radiologist 53% (56/106). GPT-4 was not significantly different from either radiologist (p = 0.78 and 0.22), while GPT-4V was significantly lower than both.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists; published quiz cases may not reflect practice.
studies.title: ChatGPT's diagnostic performance based on textual vs. visual information compared to radiologists' diagnostic performance in musculoskeletal radiology.

studies.design: Prospective diagnostic accuracy study, 100 consecutive primary care patients
studies.ai_system: Image analysis ML model screening 44 skin diseases
studies.finding: Skin lesion diagnosis in 100 consecutive primary care patients. Overall Top-1 accuracy of the ML model (39%) was lower than GPs (64%) and dermatologists (72%); on trained diagnoses the model's Top-3 (75%) was comparable to GPs' Top-3 (76%) and its Top-5 (89%) comparable to dermatologists' Top-3 (90%).
studies.limitation: Small single-region sample of 100 patients; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Exploring the potential of artificial intelligence in improving skin lesion diagnosis in primary care.

studies.design: Prospective study with randomized assignment to EUS-FNA with or without AI guidance
studies.finding: Diagnosis of malignant vs benign pancreatic masses on contrast-enhanced harmonic EUS. In the clinical trial, accuracy, sensitivity and specificity of CH-EUS MASTER were significantly better than endoscopists. AI-guided EUS-FNA had accuracy 93.8%, sensitivity 90.9%, specificity 100%, not significantly different from control, but significantly improved first-pass diagnostic yield.
studies.limitation: Small single-system trial; abstract gives no endoscopist figures or sample size.
studies.title: Contrast-enhanced harmonic endoscopic ultrasound (CH-EUS) MASTER: A novel deep learning-based system in pancreatic mass diagnosis.

studies.design: Prospective single-centre single-arm masked non-inferiority trial
studies.ai_system: AI as a medical device (CNN) on smartphone dermoscopic images
studies.humans: Consultant dermatologist / teledermatology standard of care
studies.finding: Classification of suspicious skin lesions in a teledermatology cancer pathway (789 lesions). With AI sensitivity set at 91 and 92.5%, the AIaMD had a significantly higher rate of identifying lesions not needing biopsy or urgent referral than standard of care (p = 0.001) with comparable sensitivity for skin cancer.
studies.limitation: Single centre with few melanomas (8) and few darker skin types; AI sensitivity matched to literature-defined clinician sensitivity.
studies.title: Accuracy of an artificial intelligence as a medical device as part of a UK-based skin cancer teledermatology service.

studies.design: Double-blind observational comparison
studies.finding: GPT-4 and clinicians wrote personalized knee osteoarthritis self-management guidance for 50 patient profiles. GPT-4 scored higher for accuracy (mean 5.31 vs 4.76; P=.05), personalization (54.32 vs 33.20; P<.001) and safety (median 61 vs 50; P<.001). It was also faster (530.03 vs 37.29 words per min).
studies.limitation: Single-center exploratory study with only 2 clinician authors.
studies.title: Comparing Artificial Intelligence-Generated and Clinician-Created Personalized Self-Management Guidance for Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: Blinded Observational Study.

studies.design: Three-way crossover randomised controlled reader trial (ChiCTR2100048233)
studies.ai_system: PAICS (Prenatal Ultrasound Diagnosis Artificial Intelligence Conduct System)
studies.finding: 36 sonologists read 709 fetal neurosonographic images/videos to detect intracranial malformations unassisted, with concurrent PAICS, or with PAICS as second reader. Average accuracy rose from 73% unassisted to 80% concurrent and 82% second mode (P < 0.001), and AUC from 0.85 to 0.89 and 0.90. Median read time rose from 6 s to 7 s and 11 s.
studies.limitation: Reader study on retrospective image/video data rather than live clinical scanning.
studies.title: Deep learning system improved detection efficacy of fetal intracranial malformations in a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Prospective multicenter real-time comparison
studies.finding: Real-time optical prediction of polyp histology for 661 polyps in 320 patients. CADx overall accuracy was 71.6% vs 75.2% for endoscopists (P = 0.023); sensitivity for neoplastic polyps 61.8% vs 70.3% (P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Single CADx system; number of endoscopists not stated; endoscopist prediction made before seeing CADx output.
studies.title: Real-World Validation of a Computer-Aided Diagnosis System for Prediction of Polyp Histology in Colonoscopy: A Prospective Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Prospective blinded single-centre comparison
studies.humans: Two sleep surgery experts and a senior otolaryngology resident
studies.finding: In 16 DISE cases, LLM and human ratings were compared to the clinical reference. Humans had perfect or near-perfect agreement for velum, oropharynx, tongue base and jaw thrust; the LLM matched expert performance in all domains except epiglottis, where agreement was moderate. No unsafe recommendations were identified.
studies.limitation: Single centre, only 16 patients and 3 human raters.
studies.title: AI meets sleep surgery: assessing drug-induced sleep endoscopy interpretation with a large language model.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial
studies.ai_system: Computer-aided polyp detection within an optimized technique (CADopt)
studies.finding: Adenoma detection during colonoscopy in 467 patients. ADR was 49.3% (95% CI 42.7-56.0) with CADopt vs 38.2% (95% CI 32.0-44.7) with standard colonoscopy (p = 0.016); PDR 78.2% vs 59.2%.
studies.limitation: Intervention bundled CADe with linked color imaging, water exchange and retroflexion, so the AI effect cannot be isolated.
studies.title: Optimized computer-assisted technique for increasing adenoma detection during colonoscopy: a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study, 500 radiographs, each reader reading half with and half without AI
studies.humans: 4 thoracic radiologists, 4 general radiologists, 4 radiology residents
studies.finding: Detection of five abnormalities on chest radiographs. AI raised sensitivity by an absolute 26% for pneumothorax, 14% for consolidation, 12% for nodule, 8.5% for pleural effusion and 5.9% for mediastinal and hilar mass. Specificity increased except for pneumothorax (-0.2%), and reading time fell from 81 to 56 seconds.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-hospital reader study with an enriched case mix.
studies.title: Using AI to Improve Radiologist Performance in Detection of Abnormalities on Chest Radiographs.

studies.design: Instrument validation study comparing ChatGPT and otolaryngologists on clinical cases
studies.finding: ChatGPT and physicians assessed otolaryngology records of 45 patients for differential diagnosis, management and treatment, rated with the AIPI score. The mean AIPI score of the senior otolaryngologist was significantly higher than ChatGPT's (p = 0.001).
studies.limitation: The primary aim was instrument validation; the sample was small and no scores were reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Validity and reliability of an instrument evaluating the performance of intelligent chatbot: the Artificial Intelligence Performance Instrument (AIPI).
studies.source: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre evaluation versus clinical reports
studies.finding: Sensitivity for abnormal radiographs was 99.1% for AI versus 72.3% for radiologist reports, and 99.8% vs 93.5% for critical radiographs. AI specificity was 28.0% of normal radiographs.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; AI low specificity; comparison with routine reports rather than controlled reading.
studies.title: Autonomous Chest Radiograph Reporting Using AI: Estimation of Clinical Impact.

studies.design: Prospective simulation study, 1198 abstracts
studies.finding: Screening abstracts for radiology systematic reviews. ChatGPT reached a sensitivity of 95% and an NPV of 99%, slightly outperforming the GPs' sensitive consensus, but had lower specificity and PPV than the human raters.
studies.limitation: Literature screening rather than a clinical task; the number of physicians is not stated.
studies.title: Methodological insights into ChatGPT's screening performance in systematic reviews.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to radiologists and a prospective dataset
studies.finding: Breast tumour classification. The model performed similarly to experienced radiologists at benign/malignant classification and was superior at pathology-level differential diagnosis. In the prospective set, accuracy was 90.1% for the model versus 92.7% for preliminary pathologist assessments.
studies.limitation: Model-development paper; reader numbers and detailed comparison statistics are not given in the abstract.
studies.title: A multimodal machine learning model for the stratification of breast cancer risk.

studies.design: Three-phase prospective study in an LMIC ICU
studies.ai_system: Bespoke AI tool for lung ultrasound interpretation
studies.finding: Non-expert clinicians interpreted lung ultrasound clips with and without AI. Accuracy improved from 68.9% to 82.9% on retrospective clips and from 68.1% to 93.4% in prospective real-time testing (p < 0.001); time-to-interpret fell from 12.1 s to 5.0 s.
studies.limitation: Prospective phase very small (7 patients); single resource-limited ICU.
studies.title: Clinical benefit of AI-assisted lung ultrasound in a resource-limited intensive care unit.

studies.design: Prospective feasibility study
studies.humans: Novice providers using AI vs expert sonographers without AI
studies.finding: 36 novices using AI guidance and 2 expert sonographers without AI scanned patients for rheumatic heart disease. Novice images enabled diagnostic interpretation in >90% of studies for RHD presence, MV morphology and mitral regurgitation vs 99% by experts (P ≤ .001). For aortic regurgitation novices reached 79% and for aortic stenosis 50%, vs 99% and 91% by experts.
studies.limitation: No novice-without-AI control; the comparison is with experts and is confounded by expertise.
studies.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence Guidance for Rheumatic Heart Disease Screening by Novices.
studies.source: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

studies.design: Cross-sectional blinded comparison of responses
studies.humans: Physicians answering on DXY platform; 3 chief physicians as raters
studies.finding: For 239 autism-related patient questions, 46.86% of evaluations preferred physicians versus 34.87% ChatGPT and 18.27% ERNIE Bot. Physicians scored higher on usefulness (3.54 vs 3.40 ChatGPT) while ChatGPT scored higher on empathy (3.64 vs 3.13).
studies.limitation: Only 3 raters; online platform responses; Chinese-language single context.
studies.title: Physician Versus Large Language Model Chatbot Responses to Web-Based Questions From Autistic Patients in Chinese: Cross-Sectional Comparative Analysis.

studies.design: Retrospective analysis of 58 hand fracture cases comparing LLM recommendations with actual surgeon decisions
studies.finding: The LLMs' management plans for hand fractures were scored against actual surgeon decisions. ChatGPT-4o had accuracy 98.28% (precision 58.48%), DeepSeek-V3 63.79% and Gemini 1.5 18.97%.
studies.limitation: Surgeons served as the reference standard rather than being scored themselves; small single dataset.
studies.title: Breaking Bones, Breaking Barriers: ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Gemini in Hand Fracture Management.

studies.design: Diagnostic accuracy study plus reader study of dentists without and then with AI on periapical radiographs
studies.finding: The AI's sensitivity ranged from 80.2% to 97.1% and specificity from 87% to 99.6% across conditions. Interns and specialists reading with the AI showed higher accuracy, sensitivity and specificity than without it for caries, periapical lesions, restoration, endodontic treatment, calculus and marginal bone loss.
studies.limitation: Sequential unaided-then-aided reading with only five radiographs per reader.
studies.title: Assessment of the Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence Software in Identifying Common Periodontal and Restorative Dental Conditions (Marginal Bone Loss, Periapical Lesion, Crown, Restoration, Dental Caries) in Intraoral Periapical Radiographs.

studies.design: Prospective multicenter comparison in four emergency departments
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-4o with customized prompts via voice commands
studies.finding: ED triage of 6657 patients against an EM specialist gold standard. Agreement was Cohen's kappa 0.782 for triage personnel and 0.833 for GPT-4o; F1 was 0.863 for the triage team vs 0.897 for GPT-4.
studies.limitation: Gold standard set by a single EM specialist per site; weaker AI performance for complex cases in tertiary hospitals.
studies.title: ChatGPT-supported patient triage with voice commands in the emergency department: A prospective multicenter study.
studies.source: The American journal of emergency medicine

studies.design: Prospective multicentre trial with blinded endoscopists and second observer using CADe
studies.ai_system: CADe combining convolutional and recurrent neural networks
studies.finding: Polyp detection during colonoscopy in 946 patients. CADe was not superior to human polyp detection (sensitivity 94.6% vs 96.0%) but outperformed endoscopists for adenomas; unblinding added 86 true positive polyps (1.1% ADR increase per patient) and increased procedure time by 6.6±6.5 min, changing surveillance intervals in 22/946 patients.
studies.limitation: Not randomised; number of endoscopists not stated; additional yield mostly diminutive polyps.
studies.title: Clinical consequences of computer-aided colorectal polyp detection.

studies.design: Prospective propensity score-matched non-randomized controlled study
studies.finding: In 1,758 matched colonoscopies, ENAD-assisted colonoscopy had higher ADR (45.1% vs. 38.8%, p=0.010), SSL detection rate (5.7% vs. 2.5%) and adenomas per colonoscopy (0.78±1.17 vs. 0.61±0.99). Withdrawal time was longer (9.0±3.4 vs. 8.3±3.1).
studies.limitation: Non-randomized single tertiary center study.
studies.title: Effectiveness of a novel artificial intelligence-assisted colonoscopy system for adenoma detection: a prospective, propensity score-matched, non-randomized controlled study in Korea.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to dermatologists
studies.finding: The model estimated PASI scores from psoriasis images and was compared with 43 dermatologists. It outperformed their average performance with a 33.2% performance gain in overall PASI score, with MAE of 2.05.
studies.limitation: Comparison details limited in abstract; developer-led evaluation.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Psoriasis Severity Assessment: Real-world Study and Application.

studies.design: Prospective observational study in the emergency department
studies.finding: For B-line assessment of pulmonary edema, the physician was 96.7% sensitive and 79.1% specific. The AI was 95.6% sensitive and 64.1% specific, so the physician was more specific.
studies.limitation: Single site; 71 patients.
studies.title: Comparison of artificial intelligence versus real-time physician assessment of pulmonary edema with lung ultrasound.
studies.source: The American journal of emergency medicine

studies.design: Preclinical validation comparing AI and human virtual implant planning on 50 CBCT/intraoral scan datasets
studies.humans: Implant clinicians; three implant dentistry specialists as evaluators
studies.finding: About 89% of AI-planned and 93% of human-planned implants were clinically acceptable. The AI took 187 s versus 406 s for humans, and its median surface deviation was zero versus inter-operator 0.56 mm.
studies.limitation: Preclinical study of 50 cases only.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Versus Human Intelligence in Presurgical Implant Planning: A Preclinical Validation.

studies.design: Simulation on real patient cases in sandboxed EHR
studies.finding: An autonomous AI agent managed real patient cases in a sandboxed EHR, ordering tests, generating differentials and treatment plans. The abstract reports MIRA outperformed physicians in diagnostic accuracy, without giving numbers.
studies.limitation: Simulated sandbox setting; no numbers or physician count in abstract; prospective validation needed.
studies.title: Towards autonomous medical artificial intelligence agents.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with internal test and external validation
studies.finding: For predicting coronary revascularization in ED visits, the model achieved AUROC 0.91 versus 0.65 for clinician ECG interpretation in the test cohort. Externally, AUROC was 0.81 vs 0.70 for revascularization and 0.85 vs 0.74 for Type 1 MI.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; clinician interpretation taken from records, number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Deep learning electrocardiogram model for risk stratification of coronary revascularization need in the emergency department.

studies.design: Secondary analysis of 2 randomized controlled trials
studies.finding: In unassisted colonoscopy, adenoma detection rate was higher in early than late sessions (13.73% vs 5.70%). With AI assistance, early and late sessions did not differ (22.95% vs 22.06%), and AI's assistance effect was larger in late sessions (OR 3.81 vs 1.60).
studies.limitation: This is a secondary analysis at a single center, and the number of endoscopists is not stated.
studies.title: Assessment of the Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Association Between Time of Day and Colonoscopy Quality.

studies.design: Pragmatic cluster randomised quality improvement study across Veterans Health Administration facilities
studies.humans: Endoscopists (269 at CADe sites, 547 at control sites)
studies.finding: Endoscopists at facilities given CADe devices were compared with those at control facilities on adenoma detection rate (ADR). ADR rose from 50.7% to 54.9% at CADe sites and fell from 51.8% to 51.1% at control sites. CADe availability was associated with odds ratio 1.22 (95% CI, 1.15 to 1.28) for adenoma detection.
studies.limitation: Randomisation was by facility with pre/post comparisons; effects on cancer outcomes and deskilling were not assessed.
studies.title: Impact of Availability of Computer-Aided Detection Devices on Adenoma Detection During Colonoscopy: A Cluster Randomized Study.

studies.design: Observational vignette study comparing GPT-3 with physicians and laypeople
studies.finding: On 48 synthetic vignettes, GPT-3 had the correct diagnosis in its top three for 88% (42/48) versus 96% (637/666) for physicians (p=0.012). For triage, GPT-3 was correct in 70% (34/48) versus 91% (608/666) for physicians (p<0.0001).
studies.limitation: Short synthetic vignettes and a small number of cases.
studies.title: The diagnostic and triage accuracy of the GPT-3 artificial intelligence model: an observational study.

studies.design: Prospective multicenter randomized controlled trial
studies.finding: Polyp detection during colonoscopy in 805 patients. The AI-assisted group had significantly higher polyp and adenoma detection rates than colonoscopy without AI, with an OR of 1.50 for polyp detection.
studies.limitation: Abstract does not report the actual detection rates or number of endoscopists.
studies.title: A prospective multicenter randomized controlled trial on artificial intelligence assisted colonoscopy for enhanced polyp detection.

studies.design: Prospective quasi-randomized multicenter controlled trial at four Danish centers
studies.finding: Adenoma detection rate in colonoscopy was compared between AI-assisted and conventional colonoscopy in 795 patients. ADR was 59.1% with AI vs 46.6% without (P < 0.001), significant among experts (59.9% vs 47.3%) but not non-experts. In screening colonoscopies ADR was 74.4% vs 58.1% (P = 0.003).
studies.limitation: Quasi-randomized rather than truly randomized allocation; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Improvement in adenoma detection rate by artificial intelligence-assisted colonoscopy: Multicenter quasi-randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Multisite analytical and clinical validation; assisted vs unassisted pathologist reads
studies.finding: Pathologists scored MASH liver biopsies with and without AIM-MASH assistance. AI-assisted reads were superior to unassisted reads for inflammation, ballooning, MAS ≥ 4 with ≥1 in each category and MASH resolution, and non-inferior for steatosis and fibrosis.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives no numeric results or reader numbers; clinical-trial histology context.
studies.title: Clinical validation of an AI-based pathology tool for scoring of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.

studies.design: Laboratory randomised cross-over reader study, 200 ACL MRIs
studies.ai_system: AI for ACL rupture diagnosis on MRI
studies.finding: Clinicians diagnosed ACL rupture on MRI with and without AI. AI increased accuracy from 87.2%±13.1% to 96.4%±1.9% (P < .001), but automation bias accounted for 45.5% of errors in the AI-assisted round.
studies.limitation: Laboratory setting; suppression strategy benefit only estimated.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence suppression as a strategy to mitigate artificial intelligence automation bias.
studies.source: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

studies.design: Prospective multicentre cross-over study, 750 patients, physicians reassessed after AI-QCT
studies.humans: Site physicians at 5 expert CCTA sites
studies.finding: Physicians' diagnoses and management plans were compared before and after AI-QCT results. AI-QCT changed diagnosis or management in 428 patients (57.1%; P < 0.001) and reduced need for downstream testing by 37.1% (P < 0.001), with additional statin initiation/increase in 28.1% and aspirin in 23.0%.
studies.limitation: Measures change in plans, not accuracy or patient outcomes; no reference standard reported.
studies.title: Impact of atherosclerosis imaging-quantitative computed tomography on diagnostic certainty, downstream testing, coronary revascularization, and medical therapy: the CERTAIN study.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-center multi-reader multi-case two-stage crossover study
studies.ai_system: AI-driven 3D reconstruction of pulmonary vessels and bronchi
studies.finding: Surgeons assessed 140 cases for preoperative lung surgery planning with and without the system. Assistance improved anatomical variant identification accuracy by 8% (p < 0.01), reducing errors by 41%, improved procedure selection accuracy by 8%, and cut planning time by 25%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study; ten surgeons.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence driven 3D reconstruction for enhanced lung surgery planning.

studies.design: Diagnostic study of ML on smartphone fundus videos compared with pediatric ophthalmologists
studies.ai_system: ML frame selection and ROP classifier
studies.finding: For ROP screening, the model's sensitivity at the patient level was 93.3% versus 73.3% for ophthalmologists, and at the frame level 76.7% versus 71.4%. Specificity and accuracy were higher for ophthalmologists.
studies.limitation: Ophthalmologists served as comparator panel with only three readers; specificity trade-off.
studies.title: AI-Enabled Screening for Retinopathy of Prematurity in Low-Resource Settings.

studies.design: Cluster-randomized stepped-wedge trial at physician level
studies.ai_system: Machine learning survival model with automated emails and care coaches
studies.finding: Prompting serious illness conversations in metastatic cancer. Prognosis documentation within 14 days was 2.9% in the intervention vs 1.1% in control (adjusted OR 4.3); advance care planning documentation was 7.7% vs 1.8% (adjusted OR 14.2).
studies.limitation: Intervention combined ML prompts with care coaches, so the AI effect cannot be isolated; absolute rates low.
studies.title: Automated patient selection and care coaches to increase advance care planning for patients with cancer.
studies.source: Journal of the National Cancer Institute

studies.design: Development and validation study with test cohort
studies.ai_system: AI-assisted readout for Skin Prick Automated Test
studies.finding: Wheal measurement in skin prick tests. AI showed specificity of 98·4% and sensitivity of 85·0% against physician measurements, and physicians adjusted 5·8% of AI measurements, changing interpretation in 0·5% of cases. AI-assisted readout significantly reduced inter- and intra-observer variability and readout time compared to manual physician measurements.
studies.limitation: Physician measurement served as the reference; the number of physicians is not stated.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted readout method for the evaluation of skin prick automated test results.

studies.design: Multicenter development with multinational reader studies
studies.finding: For predicting neoadjuvant therapy response, MRP had robustness comparable to breast radiologists and outperformed them in predicting pathological complete response pre-NAT (ΔAUROC 14% and 10% on in-house and external datasets).
studies.limitation: Reader numbers not stated; retrospective imaging data.
studies.title: An explainable longitudinal multi-modal fusion model for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response in women with breast cancer.

studies.design: Deep learning development with external testing and comparison to cardiologists
studies.finding: CHDdECG achieved ROC-AUC of 0.915 on a 12,000-case test set and 0.917 and 0.907 on external sets. It surpassed cardiologists in CHD detection, though cardiologist figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Comparison details and number of cardiologists not reported.
studies.title: Congenital heart disease detection by pediatric electrocardiogram based deep learning integrated with human concepts.

studies.design: Reader study: users classified 100 EEG samples with and without AI assistance
studies.humans: Eight medical professionals with relevant backgrounds
studies.finding: Users classified 100 ICU EEG samples into six ictal-interictal patterns with and without AI assistance. Mean user diagnostic accuracy improved from 47 to 71% (P<0.04) with AI.
studies.limitation: Only eight readers and 100 samples in a retrospective reader study.
studies.title: Improving Clinician Performance in Classifying EEG Patterns on the Ictal-Interictal Injury Continuum Using Interpretable Machine Learning.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective cohort with prospective randomized cohort
studies.ai_system: 2.5D CNN diagnostic model and nnU-Net contouring model
studies.finding: For detecting nasopharyngeal carcinoma recurrence, the AI model had comparable sensitivity to MRI radiologists (74.3% vs. 74.7%, P = 0.89). AI-aided MRI improved specificity (92.5% vs. 85.0%, P = 0.034) internally and sensitivity (81.9% vs. 70.8%, P = 0.021) externally. In the prospective randomized cohort of 1248 patients, sensitivity was 78.6% vs. 67.3% (P = 0.23), nonsignificant.
studies.limitation: Prospective randomized comparison was underpowered and nonsignificant; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence aided precise detection of local recurrence on MRI for nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a multicenter cohort study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of LLM SIRI-2 scores with expert suicidologists and health professionals from prior studies
studies.humans: Expert suicidologists and mental health professionals (prior study data)
studies.finding: LLMs rated clinician responses to suicidal ideation scenarios on the SIRI-2. ChatGPT scored 45.7 (roughly equivalent to master's level counselors), Claude 36.7 (exceeding mental health professionals after training), and Gemini 54.5 (equivalent to untrained K-12 staff). All LLMs showed upward bias versus expert suicidologists.
studies.limitation: Human comparison relies on historical scores from prior studies rather than a concurrent clinician sample; hypothetical scenarios.
studies.title: Competency of Large Language Models in Evaluating Appropriate Responses to Suicidal Ideation: Comparative Study.

studies.design: Multicentre single-blinded RCT
studies.finding: Detection of early upper GI neoplasms during OGD. The detection rate was 6.1% (56/914) with IQCS versus 2.3% (21/915) with routine examination (P = 0.0001), with fewer blind spots (2.3 vs. 6.2).
studies.limitation: Per-protocol analysis in Chinese centres only; the number of endoscopists is not stated.
studies.title: Efficacy of a real-time intelligent quality-control system for the detection of early upper gastrointestinal neoplasms: a multicentre, single-blinded, randomised controlled trial.

studies.design: Prospective cross-sectional study at 6 rural vision centers
studies.finding: Among referred participants, agreement with the glaucoma specialist was 80.3% for AI versus 55.3% for tele-ophthalmologists. AI had fewer false positive referrals (2 out of 10) than tele-ophthalmologists (9 out of 10).
studies.limitation: Small referred subgroup and specialist reference had extra tests; number of tele-ophthalmologists not stated.
studies.title: Diagnostic Performance of the Offline Medios Artificial Intelligence for Glaucoma Detection in a Rural Tele-Ophthalmology Setting.

studies.design: Randomized pre-post intervention vignette study
studies.finding: Physicians answered triage, risk assessment and treatment questions on chest pain video vignettes before and after GPT-4 recommendations. Accuracy improved from 47% to 65% in the white male patient group and from 63% to 80% in the Black female patient group, without introducing or exacerbating demographic bias.
studies.limitation: Pre-post design on standardized vignettes with no concurrent control arm, so order and learning effects cannot be separated from AI effect.
studies.title: Physician clinical decision modification and bias assessment in a randomized controlled trial of AI assistance.

studies.design: Pragmatic randomized clinical trial in the emergency department
studies.finding: 3576 ED patients with acute respiratory symptoms were randomized to chest radiograph interpretation with or without AI-CAD. Sensitivity was 67.2% [317/472] with AI vs. 66.0% [324/491] without (OR 1.02; P = 0.917), and false-positive rates were 19.3% vs. 18.5% (P = 0.985).
studies.limitation: Single tertiary institution with trainee readers; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Conventional Versus Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Interpretation of Chest Radiographs in Patients With Acute Respiratory Symptoms in Emergency Department: A Pragmatic Randomized Clinical Trial.

studies.design: Randomized parallel-group pilot trial
studies.finding: Sixty adults with overweight or obesity were randomized to AI-guided or physician-guided dietary-supplement prescriptions for 180 days. Mean weight loss was -12.3 % in the AI-guided group versus -7.2 % in the physician-guided group (difference -5.1 %, p < 0.01). At day 180, 25/30 (83.3 %) of AI-guided participants versus 16/30 (53.3 %) of physician-guided participants achieved ≥5 % weight reduction.
studies.limitation: Small pilot trial (n=60); the number of prescribing physicians is not stated.
studies.title: Optimizing weight loss with artificial intelligence: A randomized controlled trial of dietary-supplement prescriptions in adults with overweight and obesity.

studies.design: Pragmatic cluster-randomized trial
studies.ai_system: AI-based predictive analytics display of deterioration risk
studies.finding: In 10,422 inpatient visits on a cardiology ward, clinicians were randomized by cluster to a passive display of AI risk trajectories or to usual care. There was no change in the primary outcome of clinical deterioration events between groups.
studies.limitation: Clinicians moved 11% of patients into or out of display beds, undermining randomization; the number of clinicians is not stated.
studies.title: A randomized controlled trial of artificial intelligence-based analytics for clinical deterioration.

studies.design: Prospective single-center randomized controlled trial in real-world LDCT interpretation
studies.ai_system: Commercial AI lung nodule evaluation tool integrated into PACS
studies.finding: Among 911 individuals undergoing screening LDCT randomized to AI-assisted or unassisted interpretation, interpretation time per examination did not differ significantly (187 vs 172 seconds; p = .23). AI assistance yielded a higher detection rate of Lung-RADS-positive nodules (16.9% vs 10.3%; p = .03) and of all nodules (52.9% vs 32.6%; p = .002), and more follow-up LDCT recommendations (15.3% vs 7.4%; p = .04).
studies.limitation: Single-center open-label trial; no lung cancers diagnosed during follow-up, so the clinical value of extra detections is unknown.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Lung Nodule Evaluation on Low-Dose Chest CT in Asymptomatic Individuals: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Randomized vignette experiment (2020 assessments)
studies.finding: Radiologists reviewing cases with images received no LLM support or one of three explanation formats. Chain-of-thought explanations improved diagnostic accuracy by 12.2% versus no LLM support (P = 0.001) and outperformed standard output (+7.2%; P = 0.040) and differential diagnosis format (+9.7%; P = 0.004).
studies.limitation: Controlled vignette setting; number of radiologists not stated in abstract.
studies.title: The effect of medical explanations from large language models on diagnostic accuracy in radiology.

studies.design: Retrospective LLM evaluation plus prospective physician study
studies.ai_system: Seven commercial LLMs incl. ChatGPT-o1-preview, DeepSeek-R1
studies.finding: Diagnosis of rare hematologic diseases from real admission records, where ChatGPT-o1-preview reached a top-10 accuracy of 70.3%. In the prospective phase, 28 physicians each diagnosed 5 cases with sequential access to LLM output. LLMs significantly improved the accuracy of less-experienced physicians, with no significant benefit for specialists, and biased outputs sometimes worsened performance.
studies.limitation: Small sample of physicians, with only 5 cases each.
studies.title: Performance of Large Language Models in Diagnosing Rare Hematologic Diseases and the Impact of Their Diagnostic Outputs on Physicians: Combined Retrospective and Prospective Study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 40 multiple-choice ECG cases
studies.finding: 40 ECG cases from a textbook (20 everyday, 20 challenging) as multiple-choice questions. GPT-4 outperformed emergency medicine specialists and cardiologists on everyday questions (p < 0.001, p = 0.001) and on total accuracy (p < 0.001, p = 0.001); on challenging questions it beat emergency specialists (p < 0.001) but did not differ from cardiologists (p = 0.190).
studies.limitation: Textbook multiple-choice cases rather than real clinical ECG interpretation; small question set.
studies.title: Comparison of emergency medicine specialist, cardiologist, and chat-GPT in electrocardiography assessment.
studies.source: The American journal of emergency medicine

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison on NEJM Image Challenge cases
studies.humans: Junior faculty radiologists, clinicians, an in-training radiologist and a medical student
studies.finding: On 272 NEJM Image Challenge cases, GPT-4o had the highest LLM accuracy (59.6%), outperforming a medical student (47.1%) but not junior faculty (80.9%) or the in-training radiologist (70.2%).
studies.limitation: Published challenge cases rather than clinical practice, with possible training-data contamination.
studies.title: Comparing Large Language Model and Human Reader Accuracy with New England Journal of Medicine Image Challenge Case Image Inputs.

studies.design: Retrospective fairness analysis on five chest x-ray datasets
studies.finding: Chest x-ray diagnosis across five globally sourced datasets. Compared with board-certified radiologists, the foundation models consistently underdiagnosed marginalized groups, with higher rates in intersectional subgroups such as Black female patients.
studies.limitation: Abstract reports no quantitative results or radiologist numbers; comparison focuses on bias rather than overall accuracy.
studies.title: Demographic bias of expert-level vision-language foundation models in medical imaging.

studies.design: Model development with comparison against expert orthodontist clinical classification
studies.ai_system: Multistage neural network on intraoral photographs
studies.finding: Malocclusion classification from intraoral photographs in 248 test patients. The AI had accuracy 93.1% for molar and 89.1% for canine classification, reported as higher than orthodontists, but mean absolute error of 1.98 ± 2.11 for overjet and 1.28 ± 1.60 for overbite was not acceptable compared with expert orthodontists.
studies.limitation: Single-centre study where the expert clinician also served as reference; human performance figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Designing an artificial intelligence system for dental occlusion classification using intraoral photographs: A comparative analysis between artificial intelligence-based and clinical diagnoses.
studies.source: American journal of orthodontics and dentofacial orthopedics : official publication of the American Association of Orthodontists, its constituent societies, and the American Board of Orthodontics

studies.design: Comparison of seven LLMs and gastroenterologists on 67 offline challenging gastrointestinal cases
studies.finding: LLMs and gastroenterologists gave possible diagnoses for 67 challenging cases with primary gastrointestinal symptoms. Claude 3.5 Sonnet covered the highest proportion of instructive diagnoses (76.1%, [70.6%-80.9%]), significantly surpassing all gastroenterologists (p < 0.05 for all). Against gastroenterologists using search engines or other traditional resources, the coverage rate was 76.1% vs. 45.5% [40.7%-50.4%], p < 0.001.
studies.limitation: Small set of 67 curated challenging cases from an offline dataset rather than live care.
studies.title: Multiple large language models versus experienced physicians in diagnosing challenging cases with gastrointestinal symptoms.

studies.design: Multicenter randomized trial, CADe-assisted vs conventional colonoscopy
studies.finding: Among 497 analysed participants, adenoma detection rate was 38.4% with CADe vs 37.7% conventional (P = 0.43) and adenomas per colonoscopy 0.66 vs 0.66 (P = 0.97). Sessile serrated lesions per colonoscopy increased (0.30 vs 0.19; P = 0.049) with CADe.
studies.limitation: Control ADR exceeded sample size assumptions, so the trial may be underpowered.
studies.title: A computer-aided detection system in the everyday setting of diagnostic, screening, and surveillance colonoscopy: an international, randomized trial.

studies.design: Multicenter randomized controlled study
studies.ai_system: CNN model for endoscopic diagnosis of H. pylori infection
studies.finding: Endoscopists diagnosed H. pylori infection with or without CNN assistance. AI-assisted accuracy was 92.8% vs 75.6% unassisted, sensitivity 91.8% vs 78.6%, and specificity 93.4% vs 74.5% (all P < 0.05). The model alone had accuracy of 89.6%.
studies.limitation: Number of endoscopists not stated; developer-run trial of own system.
studies.title: Development and application of an artificial intelligence-assisted endoscopy system for diagnosis of Helicobacter pylori infection: a multicenter randomized controlled study.

studies.design: Clinical trial; participants scanned volunteer patients and re-evaluated EU-TIRADS after S-Detect analysis
studies.humans: Medical students, US novice physicians and US experienced physicians
studies.finding: Twenty participants scanned five patients with thyroid nodules and classified them by EU-TIRADS before and after S-Detect analysis. Accuracy of the biopsy recommendation outcome was 69.8% before and 69.2% after AI (p = 0.75). Mean S-Detect diagnostic accuracy was 71.3% (range 40-100%) depending on operator.
studies.limitation: Very small sample of five patients with only one malignant nodule; sequential non-randomised design.
studies.title: Human-AI collaboration for ultrasound diagnosis of thyroid nodules: a clinical trial.
studies.source: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on deidentified ED patient self-report data
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT 3.5/4.0, Ada and WebMD symptom checkers
studies.finding: Diagnosis of ED patients from self-reported symptoms. Top-1 match was 40% for ChatGPT 3.5 and 33% for ChatGPT 4.0 versus a mean 47% for physicians; top-3 was 63% and 50% versus 69% for physicians.
studies.limitation: Very small sample (30 cases for diagnosis); no statistical comparison with physicians reported.
studies.title: Comparison of Diagnostic and Triage Accuracy of Ada Health and WebMD Symptom Checkers, ChatGPT, and Physicians for Patients in an Emergency Department: Clinical Data Analysis Study.

studies.design: Model development with prospective test set and radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Multi-phase CNN for renal mass malignancy
studies.finding: For predicting renal mass malignancy on CT, the model achieved an AUC of 0.871 in the prospective test set and surpassed the average performance of seven seasoned radiologists.
studies.limitation: Radiologist metrics not quantified in the abstract.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence links CT images to pathologic features and survival outcomes of renal masses.

studies.design: Preregistered experiments comparing explainable AI (heatmaps) vs black-box AI support
studies.ai_system: Chest X-ray lung lesion AI with visual heatmaps vs black-box AI
studies.humans: Radiologists (and factory workers in separate experiment)
studies.finding: Radiologists assessed chest X-rays for lung lesions supported by either explainable or black-box AI. Explainable AI improved task performance by 4.7 percentage points (95% CI: 1.1% to 8.3%) in the medical experiment compared to black-box AI.
studies.limitation: Compares two forms of AI support rather than AI vs no AI; number of radiologists not stated in abstract.
studies.title: Explainable AI improves task performance in human-AI collaboration.

studies.design: Comparison of ChatGPT differential diagnosis lists against physicians on 52 case-report vignettes
studies.finding: On 52 complex GIM case vignettes, ChatGPT-4 correct diagnosis rates were comparable to physicians within the top 10 (43/52, 83% vs 39/52, 75%; P=.47), top 5 (42/52, 81% vs 35/52, 67%; P=.18) and top diagnosis (31/52, 60% vs 26/52, 50%; P=.43). Differences were not significant.
studies.limitation: Small set of published case reports from a single department, possibly in training data; only 3 physicians.
studies.title: ChatGPT-Generated Differential Diagnosis Lists for Complex Case-Derived Clinical Vignettes: Diagnostic Accuracy Evaluation.

studies.design: Model development with internal and external reader study
studies.finding: Radiologists diagnosed ovarian cancer on ultrasound with and without OvcaFinder assistance. Average AUCs improved from 0.927 to 0.977 internally and from 0.904 to 0.941 externally. False positive rates decreased by 13.4% and 8.3% respectively.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study; number of radiologists not stated in the abstract.
studies.title: Development and validation of an interpretable model integrating multimodal information for improving ovarian cancer diagnosis.

studies.design: Benchmark (mARC-QA) of clinical reasoning scenarios comparing LLMs with physicians
studies.ai_system: o1, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek and other LLMs
studies.finding: On mARC-QA scenarios designed to exploit the Einstellung effect, LLMs performed poorly compared to physicians, showing lack of commonsense medical reasoning, hallucination and overconfidence.
studies.limitation: Adversarially designed question set; abstract gives no numbers or physician sample size.
studies.title: Limitations of large language models in clinical problem-solving arising from inflexible reasoning.

studies.design: Large-scale empirical evaluation on real-world EHRs
studies.finding: Clinical trial matching of patients from real-world EHRs. OncoLLM outperformed GPT-3.5 and matched the performance of qualified medical doctors; no numbers reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Abstract reports no quantitative results or number of doctors.
studies.title: PRISM: Patient Records Interpretation for Semantic clinical trial Matching system using large language models.

studies.design: Retrospective case comparison
studies.finding: For 36 dermatology emergency clinic cases, ChatGPT made the correct primary diagnosis 56% of the time with dermatologist-recorded data and 39% with nonspecialist data. This was similar to nonspecialists (36%) but much lower than dermatologists (83%).
studies.limitation: Small single-clinic sample of 36 patients; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: ChatGPT versus clinician: challenging the diagnostic capabilities of artificial intelligence in dermatology.

studies.design: Randomized comparison of surgeons with vs without AI on cases from prospectively followed patients
studies.finding: Predicting 30-day outcomes after emergency general surgery in 150 cases. POTTER outperformed surgeons for mortality (AUC 0.880 vs. 0.841) and most outcomes except septic shock (0.816 vs. 0.820). Surgeons with POTTER outperformed those without for mortality (0.870 vs. 0.841), bleeding (0.811 vs. 0.735), pneumonia (0.803 vs. 0.753) but not septic shock (0.712 vs. 0.820) or ventilator dependence (0.834 vs. 0.833).
studies.limitation: Simulated case presentations from a single center; 15 surgeons per arm.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence versus surgeon gestalt in predicting risk of emergency general surgery.
studies.source: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

studies.design: International paired non-inferiority observational multi-reader multi-case study
studies.ai_system: PANORAMA AI system for PDAC detection on CT
studies.finding: On 391 patients for pancreatic cancer detection on CT, AI achieved an AUROC of 0·92 (95% CI 0·89-0·94) versus 0·88 (0·85-0·91) for the pooled 68 radiologists. This was non-inferior (p<0·0001) and superior (p=0·001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective enriched reader study subset, not prospective clinical deployment.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence and radiologists in pancreatic cancer detection using standard of care CT scans (PANORAMA): an international, paired, non-inferiority, confirmatory, observational study.

studies.design: Multicenter prospective randomized clinical trial in outpatient clinics
studies.finding: Nonradiologist physicians detected lung lesions on chest radiographs with or without AI assistance. The AUC was 0.840 vs. 0.718 at the CXR level (P = 0.017) and 0.800 vs. 0.677 at the lesion level (P = 0.011). AI did not affect clinical decisions.
studies.limitation: Only seven physicians took part; patients rather than readers were randomized.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Solution for Chest Radiographs in Respiratory Outpatient Clinics: Multicenter Prospective Randomized Clinical Trial.
studies.source: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

studies.design: Model development and validation with a crossover reader study
studies.ai_system: Multimodal CT radiomics and clinical model
studies.finding: The model predicted occult peritoneal metastasis in gastric cancer from CT radiomics and clinical factors. In crossover validation, AI assistance increased the average radiologist AUC from 0.735 to 0.872.
studies.limitation: Number of readers and details of the reader study are not given in the abstract.
studies.title: Multimodal digital biopsy for preoperative prediction of occult peritoneal metastasis in gastric cancer.

studies.design: Within-subject randomized controlled vignette study (AI CDS vs automated CDS vs no support)
studies.ai_system: Conceptual prototype AI-based clinical decision support for ASCVD risk
studies.finding: Doctors assessed 10-year ASCVD risk and management on 9 vignettes. AI-based CDS improved risk assessment by 27% versus unassisted assessment (NNT=3.7) and statin prescription by 29%, with less time (63.6 s vs 72.8 s). Aspirin, antihypertensive and referral decisions did not significantly improve.
studies.limitation: Online vignette study with a conceptual prototype, not real-world care.
studies.title: AI-Assisted Cardiovascular Risk Assessment by General Practitioners in Resource-Constrained Indonesian Settings Using a Conceptual Prototype: Randomized Controlled Study.

studies.design: Comparison of Chat-GPT and triage nurses on 30 vignettes recreated from real ED cases
studies.finding: Concordance in triage code assignment between nurses and Chat-GPT was 0.278 (unweighted Cohen's kappa). For all outcomes AUROC was higher for nurses; for 72-h mortality nurses had AUROC 0.910 vs 0.669 for Chat-GPT.
studies.limitation: Only 30 vignettes; comparators are nurses.
studies.title: Human intelligence versus Chat-GPT: who performs better in correctly classifying patients in triage?
studies.source: The American journal of emergency medicine

studies.design: Model development with man-machine comparison and multi-reader multi-case study
studies.finding: Diagnosis of early gastric neoplasms on white light endoscopy videos. AI accuracy exceeded endoscopists in internal (81.10% vs. 70.61%) and external videos (88.24% vs. 78.49%); with AI assistance endoscopist accuracy improved (70.61% vs. 79.63%, p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Video-based reader study rather than live procedures.
studies.title: Explainable artificial intelligence incorporated with domain knowledge diagnosing early gastric neoplasms under white light endoscopy.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-centre multi-scanner validation study
studies.ai_system: Pi (CE-marked deep-learning CAD for prostate MRI)
studies.finding: For detecting GG ≥ 2 prostate cancer on multiparametric MRI in 252 validation patients, Pi had an AUC of 0.91 vs 0.95 for radiologists, meeting non-inferiority. At threshold 3.5, AI sensitivity was 95% and specificity 67%, versus radiologists' 99% and 73%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; negative MRIs without biopsy assumed negative; non-inferiority margin of 10% is wide.
studies.title: AI-powered prostate cancer detection: a multi-centre, multi-scanner validation study.

studies.design: Quantitative intervention study with regression
studies.humans: 210 participants from different backgrounds including physicians
studies.finding: Automation bias was measured as agreement rate with wrong AI recommendations in a diagnostic task. Diagnostic performance, wound care training, physician profession and female gender significantly reduced false agreement, while higher perceived benefit promoted it.
studies.limitation: Mixed participants not all clinicians; no numeric agreement rates in abstract.
studies.title: Automation Bias in AI-Decision Support: Results from an Empirical Study.
studies.source: Studies in health technology and informatics

studies.design: Development with internal, external and prospective testing compared with endoscopists
studies.finding: Diagnosis of malignant biliary strictures on digital single-operator cholangioscopy. MBSDeiT achieved AUC of .976 on the prospective test set and identified 92.3% of MBSs in prospective videos, with superior performance to expert and novice endoscopists.
studies.limitation: Endoscopist performance figures and numbers not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A real-time interpretable artificial intelligence model for the cholangioscopic diagnosis of malignant biliary stricture (with videos).

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter standalone validation with reader comparison
studies.ai_system: Commercial AI products for bone age and lung nodule detection
studies.humans: 14 and 17 human readers of varying experience
studies.finding: For bone age, no RMSE difference between algorithms (0.63 and 0.57 years) and readers (0.68 years). For lung nodules on chest radiographs, four algorithms (AUC range, 0.86-0.93) outperformed readers (mean AUC, 0.81), while the rest showed no difference.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; readers read randomized subsets rather than in clinical workflow.
studies.title: Comparison of Commercial AI Software Performance for Radiograph Lung Nodule Detection and Bone Age Prediction.

studies.design: Observational study of 100 consecutive ED patients
studies.humans: Triage nurses and a senior clinician
studies.finding: ESI triage acuity was assigned by GPT-4 and human evaluators for 100 adult ED patients using the same data. GPT-4 assigned a lower median ESI score (2.0) than human evaluators (median 3.0; p < 0.001), suggesting overestimation of severity.
studies.limitation: Small single-sample study with human ESI as comparator rather than an outcome-based reference standard.
studies.title: Evaluating Large Language Model-Assisted Emergency Triage: A Comparison of Acuity Assessments by GPT-4 and Medical Experts.

studies.design: Prospective multi-site noninferiority study
studies.ai_system: Cloud-based chest X-ray TB detection AI
studies.finding: In 1910 patients, TB AI sensitivity and specificity were 87% and 70% at the high-sensitivity threshold and 78% and 82% at the balanced threshold, versus radiologists' mean sensitivity of 76% and specificity of 82%. The AI was noninferior to radiologists for TB triaging, and comparable at the balanced threshold.
studies.limitation: Radiologists read images blinded rather than in clinical workflow; high TB/HIV burden population limits generalisability.
studies.title: Prospective Multi-Site Validation of AI to Detect Tuberculosis and Chest X-Ray Abnormalities.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study, 1672 pediatric radiographs, readings before and after AI
studies.ai_system: Commercial deep learning fracture detection software
studies.finding: Fracture detection on pediatric radiographs. AI alone had sensitivity 92%, specificity 83% and accuracy 87%. AI assistance improved the residents' sensitivity from 84 to 87%, specificity from 91 to 92% and accuracy from 88 to 90%, although in 2% of cases readers wrongly discarded a correct diagnosis.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only three resident readers.
studies.title: Real-life benefit of artificial intelligence-based fracture detection in a pediatric emergency department.

studies.design: Retrospective before-after analysis of prospectively maintained database plus survey
studies.ai_system: FDA-approved real-time CADe for polyp detection
studies.humans: Endoscopists at a US tertiary center
studies.finding: Adenomas detected per colonoscopy did not differ compared with historical controls (1.08 vs 1.04, P = .65), even restricting to cases with CADe activated (1.27 vs 1.17, P = .45). ADR also did not differ.
studies.limitation: Non-randomised historical comparison; CADe activated in only 52.1% of cases.
studies.title: Performance and attitudes toward real-time computer-aided polyp detection during colonoscopy in a large tertiary referral center in the United States.

studies.design: Retrospective validation of deep learning system on chest CT against radiologist panel
studies.finding: Detection of benign nodules, primary lung cancers and metastases on non-screening chest CT. On the external test set the AI sensitivity was 94.3%, 96.9% and 92.0% respectively at 1 FP/scan, comparable to or higher than the radiologists, with a slightly higher FP/s (average difference of 0.6).
studies.limitation: Small external test set (100 scans); radiologists also defined the reference labels.
studies.title: Deep learning for the detection of benign and malignant pulmonary nodules in non-screening chest CT scans.

studies.design: Development and validation against pathologist consensus
studies.finding: Histologic scoring of MASH biopsies. Agreement with expert consensus was comparable for AIM-MASH vs average pathologists for MASH CRN scores (82% versus 81%) and fibrosis (97% versus 96%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective trial data; number of pathologists not stated.
studies.title: AI-based automation of enrollment criteria and endpoint assessment in clinical trials in liver diseases.

studies.design: Diagnostic comparison of LLMs and a junior radiologist on thyroid nodule ultrasound images against pathology
studies.finding: For benign versus malignant classification of 116 thyroid nodules, ChatGPT-4o had an AUC of 57.0% and Claude 3-Opus 52.0%, versus 72.4% for the junior radiologist. Kappa was 0.116, 0.034 and 0.450 respectively. Unnecessary biopsy rates were 41.4%, 43.1% and 12.1%.
studies.limitation: Small sample with a single junior radiologist as comparator.
studies.title: Assessing the feasibility of ChatGPT-4o and Claude 3-Opus in thyroid nodule classification based on ultrasound images.

studies.design: Model development, reader studies and real-world retrospective screening
studies.ai_system: GRAPE deep learning on noncontrast CT
studies.finding: In reader studies for gastric cancer detection on noncontrast CT, GRAPE significantly outperformed radiologists, improving sensitivity by 21.8% and specificity by 14.0%, particularly in early-stage GC. GRAPE also detected cases radiologists had initially missed.
studies.limitation: Assisted-reading results and reader numbers not detailed in abstract.
studies.title: AI-based large-scale screening of gastric cancer from noncontrast CT imaging.

studies.design: Two-stage development and multicenter diagnostic trial on cholangioscopy videos
studies.finding: On 170 cholangioscopy videos, CNN2 detected neoplasia with 90.5 % sensitivity and 68.2 % specificity. It outperformed nonexpert #2 (AUC-CRM 0.657 vs AUC-CNN2 0.794), nonexpert #4 (AUC-CRM 0.683 vs 0.791) and expert #4 (AUC-CRM 0.755 vs 0.848), all P < 0.05.
studies.limitation: Small number of endoscopists, and AI outperformed only some of them; video-based evaluation.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence for diagnosing neoplasia on digital cholangioscopy: development and multicenter validation of a convolutional neural network model.

studies.design: Retrospective single-center study
studies.ai_system: Hybrid GPT-4 plus deterministic O-RADS MRI scoring
studies.finding: The hybrid LLM model assigned O-RADS MRI scores from pelvic MRI reports. For lesions with an originally reported score, hybrid accuracy was 97% [153 of 158] vs 88% [139 of 158] for reporting radiologists (P = .004).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-center comparison against radiologists' original scores, using a reference standard derived from report interpretation.
studies.title: Accuracy of Large Language Model-based Automatic Calculation of Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System MRI Scores from Pelvic MRI Reports.

studies.design: Retrospective cohort study
studies.ai_system: AI in Cedars-Sinai Connect virtual urgent care
studies.humans: Treating physicians in virtual urgent care
studies.finding: In 461 AI-assisted virtual urgent care visits, initial AI and final physician recommendations were concordant in 262 visits (56.8%). AI recommendations were more often rated optimal (77.1%) than treating physician decisions (67.1%); quality was equal in 67.9%, better for AI in 20.8% and better for physicians in 11.3%.
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective study; adjudicators not blinded to recommendation source and unknown whether physicians viewed AI recommendations.
studies.title: Comparison of Initial Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Final Physician Recommendations in AI-Assisted Virtual Urgent Care Visits.

studies.design: Prospective two-centre study comparing autonomous AI telemedicine call decisions with supervising ophthalmologist decisions
studies.finding: In 202 patients assessed ~3 weeks after cataract surgery, Dora R1 showed overall outcome sensitivity of 94% and specificity of 86% against the supervising ophthalmologist's decisions, with kappa 0.758-0.970 across parameters. Four patients were recommended for discharge by Dora R1 but not the clinician; none required further review on callback.
studies.limitation: Clinician decision used as reference; modest sample from two UK hospitals.
studies.title: Accuracy and safety of an autonomous artificial intelligence clinical assistant conducting telemedicine follow-up assessment for cataract surgery.

studies.design: Reader study with eye-tracking comparing XAI vs standard AI support
studies.ai_system: Explainable AI with domain-specific explanations vs standard AI
studies.finding: Dermatologists diagnosed 16 dermoscopic images of melanomas and nevi with XAI or standard AI support. XAI improved diagnostic balanced accuracy by 2.8 percentage points compared to standard AI.
studies.limitation: Compares two forms of AI assistance rather than with vs without AI; only 16 images.
studies.title: Dermatologist-like explainable AI enhances melanoma diagnosis accuracy: eye-tracking study.

studies.design: Prospective comparison of automated vs manual measurement
studies.ai_system: Machine learning software for ONSD segmentation
studies.humans: Clinicians performing bedside manual ONSD measurement
studies.finding: ONSD measurement on transorbital ultrasound in TBI patients to distinguish raised ICP. Median difference between automated and manual ONSD was 0.06 mm; for ICP ≥20 mmHg AUC was 0.74 manual vs 0.83 automatic, and for ≥14 mmHg 0.70 manual vs 0.68 automatic.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 25 patients; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Noninvasive intracranial pressure assessment by optic nerve sheath diameter: Automated measurements as an alternative to clinician-performed measurements.

studies.design: Multicenter model development with prospective real-world validation
studies.finding: LungDiag classified respiratory diseases from EHRs. In real-world testing on 1142 EHRs it achieved an F1 score of 0.651 for top 1 diagnosis and outperformed human experts and ChatGPT 4.0; the experts' scores are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Human expert results and number of experts are not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: LungDiag: Empowering artificial intelligence for respiratory diseases diagnosis based on electronic health records, a multicenter study.

studies.design: Prospective blinded superiority trial
studies.ai_system: Real-time AI for Hill classification during gastroscopy
