studies.finding: Hill classification of the gastroesophageal junction in 131 examinations. AI accuracy was 84.7% (95% CI: 78.6-90.8) versus 62.5% (95% CI: 54.2-71) for physicians (p < 0.01); 85% vs. 56% for inexperienced and 84% vs. 69.6% for experienced physicians (p = 0.07).
studies.limitation: Single study with few physicians and short recruitment period; difference versus experienced physicians not significant.
studies.title: Prospective Evaluation of Real-Time Artificial Intelligence for the Hill Classification of the Gastroesophageal Junction.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-cohort study
studies.finding: In 29,687 patients, AI-derived coronary calcium, left atrial volume and left ventricular mass index significantly improved mortality risk classification compared with identification of abnormalities by a radiologist.
studies.limitation: Compares against radiologist reports rather than a controlled reader study.
studies.title: Predicting mortality from AI cardiac volumes mass and coronary calcium on chest computed tomography.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of automated plans with clinical plans
studies.finding: Across 17 prostate and 13 head & neck VMAT plans, GPT-RadPlan either outperformed or matched clinical plans produced by human experts. It showed superior target coverage and reduced organ-at-risk doses by 5 Gy on average (15% for prostate and 10%-15% for head & neck).
studies.limitation: Small sample of 30 plans; planners and their number not described; dosimetric endpoints only.
studies.title: Automated radiotherapy treatment planning guided by GPT-4Vision.

studies.design: Prospective non-randomized single-centre study
studies.ai_system: Commercial CADx system for polyp characterization
studies.finding: Classifying 262 polyps ≤10 mm as neoplastic or non-neoplastic during live colonoscopy. AI accuracy was 84.35%, versus 83.10% for less experienced and 83.77% for experienced endoscopists; AI sensitivity was 89.70% and specificity 75.26%.
studies.limitation: Single tertiary centre, non-randomized, number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Accuracy of polyp characterization by artificial intelligence and endoscopists: a prospective, non-randomized study in a tertiary endoscopy center.

studies.design: Randomized blinded study of explainable AI interventions in decision support, neurologists vs general population
studies.ai_system: AI decision support system with various xAI explanation methods
studies.humans: 81 neurology society members and 284 general population participants
studies.finding: Participants received DSS recommendations with randomly assigned xAI methods. Performance was not predicted by xAI method but by perceived explainability, and increasing neurology experience and perceived explainability degraded performance (P = 0.0214).
studies.limitation: Compares explanation types rather than AI versus no AI; simulated decision tasks.
studies.title: Effects of explainable artificial intelligence in neurology decision support.
studies.source: Annals of clinical and translational neurology

studies.design: Retrospective registry analysis comparing outcomes of AI-recommended therapies with clinician-prescribed therapies not aligned with AI
studies.humans: Prescribing clinicians in the Hp-EuReg registry
studies.finding: The task was choosing H. pylori eradication therapy, measured by eradication success. AI-recommended therapies achieved a 94.1% success rate (95% CI: 93.2-95.0%) versus 88.1% (95% CI: 87.7-88.4%) for clinician-prescribed therapies not aligned with AI suggestions. Results were replicated in an external validation cohort (n = 7186).
studies.limitation: Retrospective observational comparison open to confounding, with no prospective validation.
studies.title: The Helicobacter pylori AI-clinician harnesses artificial intelligence to personalise H. pylori treatment recommendations.

studies.design: Comparison of manual vs AI-automated mandibular canal segmentation and CBCT-scan registration by 20 clinicians
studies.ai_system: AI tool in implant planning software
studies.humans: 20 clinicians (10 moderate, 10 high experience in computer-assisted implant planning)
studies.finding: Mean time was 4.75 min manual vs 2.03 min AI-automated (p < 0.001). Mandibular canal discrepancy was 0.71 mm vs 0.68 mm RMS and registration discrepancy 0.45 mm vs 0.37 mm (both p > 0.05).
studies.limitation: Single software and limited datasets; generalisability uncertain.
studies.title: Comparison Between Conventional and Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Setup for Digital Implant Planning: Accuracy, Time-Efficiency, and User Experience.

studies.design: Cluster randomized trial in 2 emergency departments
studies.finding: Sepsis bundle compliance: physicians receiving LLM-driven feedback had 82.9% SEP-1 compliance versus 70.1% in control (13.0% absolute improvement; P = .02). There were no differences in ICU admission or 30-day mortality.
studies.limitation: Gains mainly in a documentation-sensitive component; two sites.
studies.title: Medical Record Abstraction for Quality Improvement in Sepsis Care Using Artificial Intelligence: A Cluster Randomized Trial.

studies.design: Parallel-group randomized controlled superiority trial
studies.finding: Clinicians interpreted 50 real spirometry records with or without AI support. AI improved preferred diagnosis performance (mean difference, 9.0; 95% CI, 4.5 to 13.3%) and in COPD cases (15.9; 95% CI, 9.0 to 22.7%), but not pattern interpretation or confidence.
studies.limitation: Only 57% of randomized clinicians completed the assessment; online case-based setting.
studies.title: AI-Assisted Spirometry Interpretation in Primary Care: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Development and validation study with observer study
studies.finding: Diagnosing gastric atrophy and intestinal metaplasia on biopsy whole-slide images. GasMIL achieved an AUC of 0.953 for atrophy, surpassing all ten pathologists. With GasMIL, pathologists improved AUC (p = 0.013), sensitivity (p = 0.014) and weighted kappa (p = 0.016) for IM and specificity (p = 0.007) for atrophy.
studies.limitation: Observer study used only 60 patients.
studies.title: Diagnosing and grading gastric atrophy and intestinal metaplasia using semi-supervised deep learning on pathological images: development and validation study.
studies.source: Gastric cancer : official journal of the International Gastric Cancer Association and the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association

studies.design: Single-center retrospective cohort
studies.ai_system: Queen of Hearts AI ECG algorithm (Powerful Medical)
studies.finding: Prehospital ECGs from 117 patients were assessed for occlusion MI. AI reduced false positives by 34% versus 27% for STEMI criteria and 22% for device software; STEMI criteria missed 6 (5%) OMIs while AI missed none (p = 0.01), and the AI reduced false positives compared to EMS clinician gestalt.
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective study with small sample; comparator largely criteria-based rather than clinician reads.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Driven Prehospital ECG Interpretation for the Reduction of False Positive Emergent Cardiac Catheterization Lab Activations: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

studies.design: Prospective study of students' POCUS with and without AI
studies.ai_system: AI-based automatic LVEF tool on handheld ultrasound
studies.humans: Eight medical students; cardiologists as comparator
studies.finding: LVEF assessment in 88 patients. Correlation with cardiologists was 0.51 for students' visual evaluation and 0.83 for students + AI; students + AI reached moderate/substantial agreement with echocardiographers versus fair agreement for students alone.
studies.limitation: Only eight students and single setting.
studies.title: Empowering Medical Students: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Precision Point-of-Care Echocardiography Assessment of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction.

studies.design: Prospective comparative study on 73 real emergency ophthalmology cases, blinded expert grading
studies.finding: Diagnoses and treatment plans for 73 emergency cases were graded on a 4-point Likert scale. Human experts scored 3.72 (SD = 0.50), GPT-4 3.52 (SD = 0.64), Llama-3-70b 3.48 (SD = 0.48) and GPT-4o 3.20 (SD = 0.81). GPT-4 and Llama-3-70b were not significantly different from ophthalmologists, while GPT-4o scored significantly lower.
studies.limitation: Single-centre, small case set with only two graders; number of comparator ophthalmologists not stated.
studies.title: Using large language models as decision support tools in emergency ophthalmology.

studies.design: Prospective observational cohort with ML models compared against expert judgement
studies.ai_system: ML pipelines (e.g. XGBoost) using morphological features from preoperative photographs
studies.finding: Predicting difficult tracheal intubation in 623 patients. The ML pipelines achieved median AUCs between 0.746 and 0.766, significantly outperforming expert judgement and state-of-the-art methods (highest AUC at 0.716).
studies.limitation: Number of experts and their individual AUC not stated; low prevalence of difficult cases (53/623).
studies.title: Reliable prediction of difficult airway for tracheal intubation from patient preoperative photographs by machine learning methods.
studies.source: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine

studies.design: Retrospective model development with independent test set and radiologist comparison
studies.finding: Detection of visually occult pre-diagnostic pancreatic cancer on CT in an independent test set (n=493). REDMOD had AUC 0.82 and 73.0% sensitivity versus 38.9% for radiologists (p<0.001), and 68.0% vs 23.0% at >24 months lead time.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of radiologists not stated; prospective validation still needed.
studies.title: Next-generation AI for visually occult pancreatic cancer detection in a low-prevalence setting with longitudinal stability and multi-institutional generalisability.

studies.design: Prospective cross-sectional non-inferiority diagnostic comparison
studies.finding: In 52 ulcerative colitis patients, VCE and CADe each detected 9 cases of dysplasia (21.4% and 20.0%; p=0.629). Sensitivity was 90% for both, with diagnostic accuracy of 29.2% for VCE and 22.9% for CADe.
studies.limitation: Small single-centre sample with few dysplasia cases.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence for dysplasia detection during surveillance colonoscopy in patients with ulcerative colitis: A cross-sectional, non-inferiority, diagnostic test comparison study.

studies.design: Prospective study of repeated echocardiograms, one sonographer-cardiologist pair with DL tools vs one without (NCT06310330)
studies.ai_system: Real-time DL guidance and automated measurements
studies.finding: Test-retest reproducibility of LV measurements in 46 patients. GLS minimal detectable change was 2.0 with DL vs. 2.9 manual (P = 0.036), and EDV 32 mL vs. 52 mL. EF reproducibility did not significantly improve.
studies.limitation: Only one operator pair per arm, so operator effects are confounded with DL use; small sample.
studies.title: Real-time guidance and automated measurements using deep learning to improve echocardiographic assessment of left ventricular size and function.
studies.source: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice

studies.design: Prospective observational comparison of a triage system with triage nurses
studies.finding: In outpatient department triage of 306 samples, triage nurses were more accurate (0.9803 vs 0.9153) and precise (0.9213 vs 0.9049) than the system. The system outperformed nurses in recall@3 (0.6230 vs 0.5266) and time consumption (10.11 vs 14.33 seconds).
studies.limitation: The comparison was with nurses rather than physicians, at a single hospital.
studies.title: Evolution of the "Internet Plus Health Care" Mode Enabled by Artificial Intelligence: Development and Application of an Outpatient Triage System.

studies.design: Prospective multicenter validation with radiologist reader assistance analysis
studies.ai_system: MMD-DL deep learning model on thyroid ultrasound videos
studies.finding: Prediction of cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma from US videos. The model achieved AUCs of 0.85 and 0.81 in test and validation cohorts; radiologists improved average accuracy (57% vs. 60%, P = 0.001) and sensitivity (62% vs. 65%, P < 0.001) with AI assistance.
studies.limitation: Small validation cohorts (39 and 70 patients) and modest absolute gains; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Cervical lymph node metastasis prediction from papillary thyroid carcinoma US videos: a prospective multicenter study.

studies.design: Secondary analysis of a prospective registry comparing AI with radiologist readings and biopsy
studies.ai_system: Cascaded deep learning algorithm for biparametric prostate MRI
studies.finding: In 658 participants, the algorithm identified 96% (282 of 294) of participants with clinically significant prostate cancer versus 98% (287 of 294) for the radiologist (P = .23). Lesion-level sensitivity against radiologist ground truth was 55% with PPV 57%.
studies.limitation: Single-registry secondary analysis with comparison to radiologist readings of unstated number.
studies.title: Evaluation of a Cascaded Deep Learning-based Algorithm for Prostate Lesion Detection at Biparametric MRI.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with external DSA-referenced test set
studies.ai_system: Knowledge-augmented deep learning model for CTA
studies.finding: Cerebral aneurysm detection on CTA in 118 external test patients with DSA reference. The model had 85.7% per-vessel sensitivity, and AUC 0.93 vs 0.91 for radiology reports (P = .67).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, single-hospital external test set; compared against clinical reports rather than a controlled reader study.
studies.title: Knowledge-Augmented Deep Learning for Segmenting and Detecting Cerebral Aneurysms With CT Angiography: A Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 43 multiple-choice questions
studies.finding: Answering 43 tracheostomy care questions graded for accuracy. ChatGPT-4.0 had 64.3% correct responses, ChatGPT-3.5 60.5%, and clinical nurses 36.7% (p < .001).
studies.limitation: Nurses rather than physicians, snowball sample, and exam-style multiple-choice questions rather than clinical practice.
studies.title: Comparing ChatGPT and clinical nurses' performances on tracheostomy care: A cross-sectional study.
studies.source: International journal of nursing studies advances

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective reader study, randomized LC-OCT with or without AI
studies.finding: Dermatologists diagnosed 200 equivocal BCC lesions on clinical/dermoscopic images, then with LC-OCT or AI-assisted LC-OCT. AI-assisted LC-OCT improved sensitivity by +25.8 points and specificity by +16.8 points compared to C&D, with most benefit for less experienced readers.
studies.limitation: Retrospective quiz setting; main comparison reported against C&D rather than unaided LC-OCT.
studies.title: AI-assisted basal cell carcinoma diagnosis with LC-OCT: A multicentric retrospective study.
studies.source: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV

studies.design: Prospective observational vignette study comparing nurses with generative AI models
studies.humans: 82 emergency nurses from Italy and Israel
studies.finding: On five standardized emergency cases, generative AI models showed higher overall decision accuracy and stronger alignment with expert recommendations than nurses. Discrepancies appeared in severity and hospitalization decisions, e.g. Case 2 severity AI level 1 vs nurses 1.98 and 2.23.
studies.limitation: Only five vignettes; nurses rather than physicians; accuracy figures not given in abstract.
studies.title: Nursing judgment in the age of generative artificial intelligence: A cross-national study on clinical decision-making performance among emergency nurses.

studies.design: Model development with external validation and reader comparison
studies.finding: Evaluating root-canal filling quality on 500 external periapical radiographs against specialist reference. The network outperformed the inexperienced endodontist in overall performance and all tooth regions, with F1 of 92.05% and 82.93% for correct and incorrect filling, and was 150-220 times faster.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; comparator was an inexperienced endodontist; human figures not reported.
studies.title: Deep-learning network for automated evaluation of root-canal filling radiographic quality.

studies.design: Simulated diagnostic intervention study, baseline then AI-supported
studies.finding: Assessing wound maceration from images, participants were ten times more likely to be correct with a correct AI recommendation (OR = 10.0, p < 0.001), with accuracy decreasing reciprocally when the recommendation was incorrect. The overall effect of introducing AI was equivocal compared to baseline.
studies.limitation: Simulated image task; mixed physicians and nurses; single wound-assessment task.
studies.title: Impact of AI recommendation correctness on diagnostic accuracy in clinical decision-making.

studies.design: Before-after clinical validation of AI feedback
studies.humans: Four radiologists of different experience levels
studies.finding: Acquiring standard first-trimester ultrasound planes. After AI-IQA feedback, the proportion of standard images obtained by junior and mid-level radiologists increased by 7.7% and 5.1%, respectively.
studies.limitation: Non-randomised before-after comparison with only four operators.
studies.title: Effectiveness and clinical impact of using deep learning for first-trimester fetal ultrasound image quality auditing.

studies.design: Single-center cross-sectional survey; patients and rheumatologists rated LLM vs physician responses
studies.humans: Physicians (rheumatology) generating responses; 17 patients and 4 rheumatologists as raters
studies.finding: LLM chatbot and physician responses to rheumatology patient questions were rated. Patients found no significant difference in comprehensiveness (7.12 vs 7.52; P = 0.1962) or readability, but rheumatologists rated AI poorer on comprehensiveness (5.52 vs 8.76), readability (7.85 vs 8.75) and accuracy (6.48 vs 9.08; P < 0.0001).
studies.limitation: Single center with only 17 patients and 4 rheumatologist raters.
studies.title: Doctor Versus Artificial Intelligence: Patient and Physician Evaluation of Large Language Model Responses to Rheumatology Patient Questions in a Cross-Sectional Study.

studies.design: Multicenter deep learning development on cytology images with pathologist comparison and assistance
studies.finding: For tumor origin prediction in cancer of unknown primary, TORCH showed better prediction efficacy than pathologists (1.677 versus 1.265, P < 0.001). It enhanced junior pathologists' diagnostic scores (1.326 versus 1.101, P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of pathologists not stated; randomized validation still needed.
studies.title: Prediction of tumor origin in cancers of unknown primary origin with cytology-based deep learning.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective and prospective development and validation with reader comparison and assistance
studies.finding: LiAIDS achieved F1-scores of 0.940 for benign and 0.692 for malignant focal liver lesions, outperforming junior radiologists (benign: 0.830-0.890, malignant: 0.230-0.360) and on par with seniors (benign: 0.920-0.950, malignant: 0.550-0.650). With assistance, juniors improved to 0.936-0.946 and 0.667-0.680, seniors to 0.950-0.961 and 0.679-0.753.
studies.limitation: Number of reader radiologists not stated; reader study details limited in abstract.
studies.title: A multicenter clinical AI system study for detection and diagnosis of focal liver lesions.

studies.design: Retrospective two-session reader study with high- and low-accuracy AI
studies.ai_system: High- and low-accuracy AI models for lung nodule detection
studies.finding: Readers detected malignant lung nodules on 120 chest radiographs. With the high-accuracy AI, AUC rose from 0.77 to 0.82, whereas with the low-accuracy AI it stayed at 0.75. Susceptibility to changing a diagnosis after the AI suggestion was 67% with the high-accuracy AI versus 59% with the low-accuracy AI.
studies.limitation: Enriched retrospective reader set; benefit depended on the accuracy of the AI.
studies.title: Effect of Human-AI Interaction on Detection of Malignant Lung Nodules on Chest Radiographs.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective and prospective DL development with comparison to clinicians
studies.finding: For identifying benign small renal masses, AUC in the external test set was 0.80 for the algorithm vs 0.84 for radiologists (P = .61), and in the prospective test set 0.87 vs 0.92 (P = .70).
studies.limitation: Only surgically resected masses included, introducing selection bias.
studies.title: Deep Learning Assessment of Small Renal Masses at Contrast-enhanced Multiphase CT.

studies.design: Development and multicenter prospective validation; AI compared with endoscopists on videos
studies.ai_system: ENDOANGEL-CPS deep learning polyp size estimation
studies.finding: Colorectal polyp size estimation from endoscopy videos. Mean CCC of ENDOANGEL-CPS surpassed all endoscopists (0.89 vs. 0.41 [SD 0.29]; P<0.001) and relative accuracy was 89.9% vs. 54.7%. Inappropriate surveillance recommendation error rate was 1.5% vs. 16.6%.
studies.limitation: Endoscopist comparison limited to 69 videos and nine endoscopists rather than live decisions.
studies.title: A real-time deep learning-based system for colorectal polyp size estimation by white-light endoscopy: development and multicenter prospective validation.

studies.design: Retrospective external validation with reader comparison
studies.humans: Three radiologists and one orthopedic surgeon
studies.finding: Kellgren-Lawrence grading of 208 knee radiographs. The model had balanced accuracy 0.693, AUC 0.886 and kappa 0.820; agreement with readers ranged from 0.737 to 0.818, judged comparable to experienced readers.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective dataset; reference was consensus of the same readers.
studies.title: Kellgren-Lawrence grading of knee osteoarthritis using deep learning: Diagnostic performance with external dataset and comparison with four readers.

studies.design: Prospective single-center randomized parallel study using simulated ventilator scenarios
studies.ai_system: AI-estimated inspiratory muscle pressure (Pmus) waveform display (Magnamed)
studies.finding: Participants identified patient-ventilator asynchronies across 49 simulated scenarios with or without the AI-estimated Pmus waveform. Sensitivity per participant was 65.8 ± 16.2 in the Pmus group vs 52.94 ± 8.42 in controls (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Simulated scenarios on a lung simulator at a single center; clinical validation still required.
studies.title: Impact on the ability of healthcare professionals to correctly identify patient-ventilator asynchronies of the simultaneous visualization of estimated muscle pressure curves on the ventilator display: a randomized study (Pmus study).

studies.design: Model development plus prospective pilot deployment in four trauma centres
studies.ai_system: XGBoost model (ShockMatrix) predicting need for hemorrhage resuscitation
studies.finding: In a prospective pilot of 139 trauma patients (22 with need for hemorrhage resuscitation), model predictions were compared with trauma leader gestalt using likelihood ratios. LRs were comparable between the model and the clinicians.
studies.limitation: Small pilot with few outcome events; likelihood ratio values not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Pilot deployment of a machine-learning enhanced prediction of need for hemorrhage resuscitation after trauma - the ShockMatrix pilot study.
studies.source: BMC medical informatics and decision making

studies.design: Single-center RCT
studies.ai_system: Deep learning guidance on a portable ultrasound device
studies.humans: Internal medicine residents without sonography training
studies.finding: Residents acquiring a five-view limited echocardiogram had faster scan times with DL devices (152 s vs 266 s; P < 0.001). Image quality was also higher with DL devices (modified RACE score 15 vs 11; P = 0.034).
studies.limitation: Single center, small sample, and outcomes assessed on a standardized patient.
studies.title: Limited echocardiogram acquisition by novice clinicians aided with deep learning: A randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study
studies.ai_system: Three commercial ICH detection AI services
studies.humans: Radiologists with access to AI results
studies.finding: Detecting intracranial hemorrhage on 3409 brain CTs. AI-assisted radiologists outperformed standalone AI with sensitivity 98.91% vs. 95.91%, specificity 99.83% vs. 87.35% and accuracy 99.53% vs. 90.11% (p < 0.001), with 293 false positives for AI versus 4 for radiologists.
studies.limitation: There was no unassisted radiologist arm, so the comparison is AI-assisted radiologists against AI alone.
studies.title: Standalone AI Versus AI-Assisted Radiologists in Emergency ICH Detection: A Prospective, Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study.

studies.design: Head-to-head cross-sectional mock exam study
studies.finding: On an 87-question ophthalmology mock exam, GPT-4 scored 69%. Expert ophthalmologists scored median 76%, trainees median 59% and unspecialised junior doctors median 43%.
studies.limitation: Exam questions rather than real cases; number of doctors not stated.
studies.title: Large language models approach expert-level clinical knowledge and reasoning in ophthalmology: A head-to-head cross-sectional study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 40 textbook ECG cases
studies.finding: On 40 ECG cases, cardiologists outperformed GPT-4, GPT-4o and Gemini Advanced in all groups. Emergency medicine specialists outperformed GPT-4o on routine and total ECG questions (p = 0.003 and p = 0.042).
studies.limitation: Textbook cases only; small case set and clinician numbers not stated.
studies.title: The accuracy of Gemini, GPT-4, and GPT-4o in ECG analysis: A comparison with cardiologists and emergency medicine specialists.
studies.source: The American journal of emergency medicine

studies.design: Retrospective validation against a surgeon
studies.finding: The algorithm measured knee alignment angles on full-limb radiographs. There was no significant difference between algorithm and surgeon in CPAK angles (n = 140, P = .66-.98, ICC = 0.89-0.91) or phenotype classifications (P = .96).
studies.limitation: Single surgeon as comparator in a retrospective dataset.
studies.title: Deep Learning Phenotype Automation and Cohort Analyses of 1,946 Knees Using the Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee Classification.

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison on 515 radiologic images
studies.humans: One first-year nonradiologist trainee and four board-certified radiologists
studies.finding: In binary abnormality classification, GPT-4V had sensitivities between 56% and 100% and specificities between 8% and 52%. Human readers had pooled sensitivity of 97.2% and pooled specificity of 97.2%.
studies.limitation: Single representative images per case, retrospective design, early model version.
studies.title: Toward Foundation Models in Radiology? Quantitative Assessment of GPT-4V's Multimodal and Multianatomic Region Capabilities.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with before/after AI assistance comparison
studies.finding: The model classified four hip fracture types with external sensitivity/specificity e.g. Displaced (0.83, 0.94). Compared to human diagnosis alone, the model significantly improved accuracy of detecting and classifying hip fractures; reader numbers not given.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, with reader comparison details and numbers not reported.
studies.title: Deep learning for automated hip fracture detection and classification : achieving superior accuracy.

studies.design: Retrospective cohort comparing model with implantologists
studies.humans: One junior and one senior implantologist
studies.finding: Predicting implant success on 42 test implants, the model achieved accuracy 0.943 and AUC 0.943. The junior expert had accuracy 0.857 and AUC 0.850, the senior 0.829 and 0.818.
studies.limitation: Single center, tiny test set (n = 42) and only two experts.
studies.title: Automated Prediction of Dental Implant Success Using a Mask Region-Based Convolutional Neural Network on Preoperative Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Scans.

studies.design: Dual-phase retrospective-prospective comparison of LLM vs radiologists
studies.finding: LI-RADS classification of 426 liver lesions with pathology as gold standard. DSV3 outperformed junior radiologists for LR-3 (17.8% vs. 39.7%), LR-4 (80.4% vs. 46.2%) and LR-5 (86.2% vs. 66.7%) retrospectively, confirmed prospectively, and achieved diagnostic parity with senior radiologists across all categories (P > 0.05).
studies.limitation: Only three radiologists; LLM worked from radiology reports rather than images.
studies.title: DeepSeek-assisted LI-RADS classification: AI-driven precision in hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective study plus prospective feasibility deployment
studies.humans: NHS first, second and consensus readers
studies.finding: Breast cancer screening on 115,973 mammograms. AI achieved superior sensitivity (0.541 versus 0.437 for first reader, P < 0.001) and noninferior specificity (0.943 versus 0.952).
studies.limitation: Primary comparison retrospective; prospective phase showed distribution shift requiring recalibration.
studies.title: Diagnostic accuracy, fairness and clinical implementation of AI for breast cancer screening: results of multicenter retrospective and prospective technical feasibility studies.

studies.design: Prospective diagnostic study with blinded real-time comparison against expert endoscopists
studies.ai_system: CCADS deep learning pCLE computer-aided diagnosis system
studies.finding: In 1254 lesions from 951 patients, CCADS real-time accuracies across Correa cascade categories were 91.71%-97.13%, similar to experts for atrophy, GIM and LGIN with similar sensitivities in all five categories. CCADS had significantly higher sensitivity for gastric neoplasms (96.70% vs. 89.01%, p = 0.044).
studies.limitation: Number of expert endoscopists not stated; specialised pCLE setting.
studies.title: Deep learning-aided optical biopsy achieves whole-chain diagnosis of Correa cascade of gastric cancer: a prospective study.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-reader multi-case study with sequential sessions
studies.ai_system: AI for pelvic radiograph interpretation (alert and visual guidance)
studies.finding: Interpretation of 150 trauma pelvic radiographs without AI, with AI-alert and with AI-visual guidance. AI assistance improved overall accuracy from 0.870 to 0.940 (p < 0.001) and reduced interpretation time from 22.70 to 9.58 s (p < 0.001); trauma surgeons with AI-visual guidance matched unaided radiologists (0.940 vs. 0.920).
studies.limitation: Sequential session design risks order/learning effects; retrospective image set.
studies.title: Comparative analysis of AI support levels in clinical interpretation of traumatic pelvic radiographs.

studies.design: Prospective superiority trial during routine colonoscopy; gold standard frame-by-frame video annotation
studies.ai_system: AI system for colonoscopy withdrawal time measurement
studies.finding: In 126 colonoscopies, the AI had a significantly lower mean absolute error in estimating withdrawal time than physicians (2.2 vs. 4.2 minutes; P < 0.001). The advantage came from examinations with interventions (2.1 vs. 5.2; P < 0.001), while MAE was comparable without interventions (2.3 vs. 2.3; P = 0.52).
studies.limitation: Single study of 126 patients; number of physicians not stated and task is a quality metric rather than diagnosis.
studies.title: A prospective study evaluating an artificial intelligence-based system for withdrawal time measurement.

studies.design: Secondary analysis of a prospective real-world cohort (1,700 colonoscopies)
studies.finding: ADR with CADe was 49.9% in the first 3 procedures of the day but dropped to 39.9% in later procedures, while unassisted ADR stayed stable (39.4% and 40.9%). The CADe gain in adenomas per colonoscopy (+0.27) disappeared later in the day (+0.11, P = 0.51), suggesting alert fatigue.
studies.limitation: Non-randomized single-center secondary analysis; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Computer-Aided Colonoscopy Alert Fatigue and Its Effect on Adenoma Detection.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre comparison on cases built from admitted patients
studies.finding: ChatGPT, residents and attendings gave three likely diagnoses for 126 ophthalmology cases. With history only, ChatGPT accuracy was 54% vs 75% for residents and 71% for attendings (p < 0.01); with examination findings added, 68% vs 94% and 86%. ChatGPT was 4 to 5 times faster.
studies.limitation: Single academic centre and number of participating physicians not stated.
studies.title: Diagnostic capabilities of ChatGPT in ophthalmology.
studies.source: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

studies.design: Retrospective multi-reader study, without then with AI, CT ground truth
studies.finding: Twenty-three radiologists read 296 wrist and hand radiographs without and then with AI, against a CT-based ground truth. AI improved sensitivity (0.658 to 0.703, p < 0.0001) and NPV (0.585 to 0.618, p < 0.0001) without affecting specificity (0.885 vs 0.891, p = 0.91). Stand-alone AI had sensitivity 0.771, specificity 0.898 and AUROC 0.764.
studies.limitation: Retrospective sequential reading design (without then with AI) may introduce order effects.
studies.title: Commercially-available AI algorithm improves radiologists' sensitivity for wrist and hand fracture detection on X-ray, compared to a CT-based ground truth.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter development and validation with comparison to ophthalmologists
studies.ai_system: Deep learning image classifier for fundus photographs
studies.finding: The algorithm differentiated small choroidal melanomas from nevi with an AUC of 0.88 in both test cohorts, outperforming ophthalmologists using MOLES (AUC 0.77) and TFSOM-UHHD (AUC 0.67) risk factors (P < 0.001). It outperformed 12 ophthalmologists in sensitivity (P = 0.006) but not specificity (P = 0.54), and was not more sensitive than ocular oncologists (P > 0.99).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with small test sets (86 and 53 images).
studies.title: Development and Validation of a Deep Learning Algorithm for Differentiation of Choroidal Nevi from Small Melanoma in Fundus Photographs.

studies.design: Multi-center randomized crossover multi-reader study
studies.finding: Readers contoured brain metastases on MRI from 50 patients (203 metastases) with and without BMSS assistance. With assistance, median DSC rose from 0.87 (0.87-0.88) to 0.92 (0.92-0.92) (P < .001), with a median time saving of 42% per lesion; BMSS alone yielded a median DSC of 0.91. Residents improved more than attendings (median DSC gain 0.05 vs 0.03).
studies.limitation: Small reader group (10) and only 50 patients; segmentation accuracy rather than clinical outcomes.
studies.title: Automated segmentation of brain metastases with deep learning: A multi-center, randomized crossover, multi-reader evaluation study.

studies.design: Reader study of 60 retrospective cases read without and with AI, repeated after 4-6 months of use
studies.finding: Diagnosing from PFTs and a short history, AI increased diagnostic accuracy for various lung diseases from 41.8% to 62.3%. Detection of lung fibrosis as the primary diagnosis rose from 42.8% without AI to 72.1% with AI (p<0.0001). In phase 2 it rose from 53.2% to 75.1% (p<0.0001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective enriched cohort of only 60 cases with limited clinical information.
studies.title: AI-powered evaluation of lung function for diagnosis of interstitial lung disease.

studies.design: Multicentre development with retrospective and prospective validation, compared with surgeon predictions
studies.finding: For predicting progression to death within 30 min after extubation in DCD donors, the model had lower futile procurement rates than surgeon predictions (0·195 vs 0·078, respectively, as reported), higher accuracy in cases of poor intersurgeon agreement (0·08 vs 0·29), and similar missed opportunity rates (0·155 vs 0·167). Model AUC was 0·831 in prospective validation.
studies.limitation: Number of surgeons not stated; the order of reported comparison values is ambiguous.
studies.title: Development and validation of a machine-learning model to reduce futile procurements in donations after circulatory death in liver transplantation in the USA: a multicentre study.

studies.design: Multi-reader pilot study with sham AI across four sessions
studies.ai_system: Sham AI with manipulated incorrect results
studies.finding: Follow-up CT decisions on 90 chest radiographs for lung cancer. Relative to no AI (FN = 2.7%, FP = 51.4%), incorrect AI raised errors, e.g. Keep AI (No Box) FN = 33.0%, FP = 86.0%; a bounding box or belief that AI would be deleted mitigated the effect.
studies.limitation: Pilot with only 6 readers and sham AI in an experimental setting.
studies.title: Can incorrect artificial intelligence (AI) results impact radiologists, and if so, what can we do about it? A multi-reader pilot study of lung cancer detection with chest radiography.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 32 published neuroradiology cases
studies.finding: Diagnosis of challenging neuroradiology cases. GPT-4 and GPT-4V achieved 22% and 16% accuracy versus residents 28%-31% and board-certified radiologists 38%-47%; GPT-4V was significantly lower than two board-certified radiologists (p = 0.02 and 0.03).
studies.limitation: Only 32 published cases, possibly in training data; small reader group.
studies.title: Comparing the Diagnostic Performance of GPT-4-based ChatGPT, GPT-4V-based ChatGPT, and Radiologists in Challenging Neuroradiology Cases.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison against on-call resident preliminary reads
studies.ai_system: Faster R-CNN object detection fracture model
studies.finding: For pediatric and young adult upper extremity fracture detection on radiographs, AI accuracy on cases preliminarily interpreted overnight was higher than resident accuracy (AI 89.4% vs. 85.1%, P = 0.01).
studies.limitation: Retrospective comparison against residents' overnight preliminary reads; number of residents not stated.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence to identify fractures on pediatric and young adult upper extremity radiographs.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre model development with reader study, with vs without AI
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model for ACL rupture detection on MRI
studies.humans: Clinicians of varying expertise in sports medicine and radiology from 25 centers
studies.finding: Thirty-eight clinicians diagnosed 3,800 knee MRIs for ACL rupture with and without AI assistance; the model alone achieved AUC 0.987 and sensitivity and specificity of 95.1%. AI assistance significantly improved the accuracy of all clinicians, exceeding 96%, and reduced diagnostic time, with the largest gains in trainees.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; unaided clinician accuracy figures not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: A Deep Learning Model Enhances Clinicians' Diagnostic Accuracy to More Than 96% for Anterior Cruciate Ligament Ruptures on Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
studies.source: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association

studies.design: Model development with internal temporal and external validation
studies.ai_system: Machine learning on clinical variables and exercise ECG
studies.finding: For predicting stress-induced functionally relevant CAD, ML outperformed cardiologists (AUROC: 0.71 vs. 0.64, p = 4.0E-13). Combining clinical judgement with ML gave a mean AUROC of 0.74.
studies.limitation: Cardiologist judgement was taken from records; number of cardiologists not stated.
studies.title: Enhancing the diagnosis of functionally relevant coronary artery disease with machine learning.

studies.design: Multicenter diagnostic study with retrospective development, external validation and prospective real-time cohort
studies.finding: Differentiating GISTs from leiomyomas on endoscopic ultrasonography. In the prospective real-time trial, the AI achieved AUC 0.865 for GISTs and 0.864 for leiomyomas versus endoscopists' AUC 0.698 for GISTs and 0.695 for leiomyomas.
studies.limitation: Prospective comparison cohort small (59 participants); number and experience of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Efficacy of real-time artificial intelligence-aid endoscopic ultrasonography diagnostic system in discriminating gastrointestinal stromal tumors and leiomyomas: a multicenter diagnostic study.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
studies.finding: AI and endodontists assessed endodontic treatment outcomes on periapical radiographs against CBCT. AI had higher sensitivity (tooth 67.3% vs 49.3%) but lower specificity (82.3% vs 92.5%); tooth-level accuracy was comparable (76.3% vs 75.3%) and root-level accuracy slightly lower for AI (78.5% vs 81.6%). AUCs were comparable (0.75 vs 0.71 tooth; 0.71 vs 0.69 root).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, only two clinician readers.
studies.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of a Commercial AI-based Platform in Evaluating Endodontic Treatment Outcomes on Periapical Radiographs Using CBCT as the Reference Standard.

studies.design: Model development with independent test set and comparison to four pathologists
studies.ai_system: Multiple-instance learning classifier on duodenal biopsy WSIs
studies.finding: Coeliac disease diagnosis from duodenal biopsies. The model achieved accuracy, sensitivity and specificity exceeding 95% and AUC exceeding 99% on 644 unseen scans; pathologist-pathologist and pathologist-model inter-observer agreement were statistically indistinguishable (p > 96%).
studies.limitation: Comparison with only four pathologists on a subset of test data; agreement-based rather than head-to-head accuracy.
studies.title: Machine Learning Achieves Pathologist-Level Coeliac Disease Diagnosis.

studies.design: Comparison of ChatGPT with residents' data from five prior bias experiments
studies.finding: ChatGPT was compared with residents on cases designed to induce diagnostic bias, and overall diagnostic accuracy was equivalent. With case-intrinsic bias, residents' accuracy decreased 12%, ChatGPT 4.0's 21% and ChatGPT 3.5's 9%. Situational bias reduced residents' accuracy by 15% but did not affect ChatGPT.
studies.limitation: Resident data came from previously published experiments, not a concurrent comparison.
studies.title: Bias Sensitivity in Diagnostic Decision-Making: Comparing ChatGPT with Residents.

studies.design: Model development with comparison against specialists
studies.ai_system: GoogleNet-based models using TMJ panoramic radiographs and joint noise data
studies.finding: AI models screened for degenerative joint disease of the TMJ using panoramic radiographs with or without joint noise data. The best model achieved an F1-score of 0.72. The AI models outperformed orofacial pain specialists when given imaging alone or imaging combined with all joint noise data.
studies.limitation: Specialists' numbers and their performance figures are not reported in the abstract; single development dataset.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced diagnosis of degenerative joint disease using temporomandibular joint panoramic radiography and joint noise data.

studies.design: Multicentre prospective diagnostic study
studies.ai_system: ResNet 50 deep learning model on greyscale ultrasound
studies.finding: Diagnosis of primary Sjögren's syndrome from salivary and lacrimal gland ultrasound. The model's AUCs were 0.90, 0.88, 0.87 in the validation cohort for SMGs, PGs and LGs, outperforming both radiologists.
studies.limitation: Small sample with only two radiologists; radiologists' figures not given in abstract.
studies.title: Deep learning in the precise assessment of primary Sjögren's syndrome based on ultrasound images.

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective development with prospective clinical cohort of 112 patients
studies.ai_system: Blockchain-based swarm learning YOLOv8n-cls fracture model
studies.finding: Knee fracture recognition and preoperative assessment. Clinically, the SL system achieved 86.8% diagnostic accuracy and assisted treatment decisions in 91.5% of cases, outperforming junior clinicians and rivaling senior specialists in diagnostic efficiency.
studies.limitation: Clinician comparison figures not reported in abstract; small prospective cohort with 6 clinicians.
studies.title: Swarm learning network for privacy-preserving and collaborative deep learning assisted diagnosis of fracture: a multi-center diagnostic study.

studies.design: Retrospective evaluation on trial CT data compared with radiologists
studies.ai_system: CT-based deep learning algorithm for extranodal extension
studies.humans: Four board-certified head and neck radiologists
studies.finding: Predicting pathological extranodal extension on pretreatment CT in 313 nodes from 178 scans. The algorithm achieved an AUC of 0·86 (95% CI 0·82-0·90), outperforming all readers (p<0·0001 for each), whose sensitivity ranged from 45-96% and specificity from 43-86%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with four readers; no prospective validation.
studies.title: Screening for extranodal extension in HPV-associated oropharyngeal carcinoma: evaluation of a CT-based deep learning algorithm in patient data from a multicentre, randomised de-escalation trial.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with reader study (with/without model assistance)
studies.ai_system: MobileNet V3 deep learning model on arterial-phase CT
studies.finding: Differentiating benign from malignant parotid tumors on contrast-enhanced CT. With model assistance, the junior radiologist's AUC improved by 0.128 and 0.102 (p < 0.05) and sensitivity by 0.194 and 0.120 (p < 0.05) in internal and external testing sets, with NRIs of 0.257 and 0.205 and IDIs of 0.316 and 0.252 (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with very few readers; benefit shown mainly for the junior radiologist.
studies.title: Deep learning-assisted diagnosis of benign and malignant parotid tumors based on contrast-enhanced CT: a multicenter study.

studies.design: Model development and validation with multireader benchmarking study (without then with CADe after 6 weeks)
studies.ai_system: Deep learning CADe system for early Barrett's neoplasia (GastroNet-pretrained)
studies.humans: 112 general endoscopists from six countries and 28 international Barrett's oesophagus experts
studies.finding: Endoscopists' sensitivity for Barrett's neoplasia detection increased from 74% to 88% with CADe for images and from 67% to 79% for video, without compromising specificity (89% to 90% images; 96% to 94% video). CADe alone was superior to endoscopists (90% vs 74% images; 91% vs 67% video) and non-inferior to experts (90% vs 87% images; 91% vs 86% video).
studies.limitation: Benchmarking test set enriched with subtle neoplasia cases and read offline, not in live endoscopy; industry funded.
studies.title: A deep learning system for detection of early Barrett's neoplasia: a model development and validation study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional benchmark against human graders
studies.finding: GPT-4 answered 422 JAMA Ophthalmology Clinical Challenges, achieving 48.0% diagnostic and 63.0% next-step accuracy. No significant differences were found between board-certified ophthalmologists and GPT-4, while senior residents outperformed GPT-4 in diagnostic accuracy (p≤0.001 and 0.049) and next-step accuracy (p=0.002 and 0.020).
studies.limitation: Published case challenges rather than real care; number of human graders not stated.
studies.title: Assessing the medical reasoning skills of GPT-4 in complex ophthalmology cases.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with comparison against medical experts
studies.ai_system: Ensemble machine learning interactive AI platform
studies.finding: Predicting postoperative inability to walk in patients with metastatic spinal disease. The AI platform's AUC was significantly higher than the average AUC of medical experts (P <0.001); external validation AUCs were 0.873 and 0.924.
studies.limitation: Expert number and AUC values not reported; retrospective data.
studies.title: Establishment and validation of an interactive artificial intelligence platform to predict postoperative ambulatory status for patients with metastatic spinal disease: a multicenter analysis.

studies.design: Multireader diagnostic accuracy imaging study, baseline then 1 month later with AI assistance
studies.ai_system: i-ROP DL AI-based vascular severity score (Siloam Vision)
studies.finding: Experts diagnosed plus disease on 150 RetCam examinations without and then with AI-based VSS. Agreement with the reference standard improved from κ 0.69 to 0.81, mean AUC from 0.94 to 0.98 and AUPR from 0.86 to 0.95 with AI assistance.
studies.limitation: Small expert reader sample with sequential (not randomised) reading order on a selected retrospective image set.
studies.title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence-Generated Vascular Severity Score Improved Plus Disease Diagnosis in Retinopathy of Prematurity.

studies.design: Blinded expert-panel consensus evaluation of chatbot vs nurse answers to 195 real phone-line questions
studies.finding: On 195 sexual health questions that nurses could correctly answer, overall correctness was 85.2% for Alice, 69.3% for Azure and 64.8% for ChatGPT. Questions were selected as ones nurses answered correctly, and all chatbots generated some incorrect information.
studies.limitation: Questions selected as those nurses answered correctly, biasing the comparison; nurses not physicians; single centre.
studies.title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for providing sexual health information: a consensus study using real-world clinical queries.

studies.design: Three-stage reader study (no AI, AI prediction, AI prediction with explanations)
studies.ai_system: Prototype-based explainable AI model for ultrasound gestational age estimation
studies.finding: Model predictions reduced sonographers' mean absolute error in gestational age estimation from 23.5 to 15.7 days, with explanations giving a further non-significant reduction to 14.3 days. Effects of explanations varied, with some participants performing worse with explanations, and explanations did not significantly affect trust or reliance.
studies.limitation: Small sample of ten sonographers in an offline reader study.
studies.title: The human factor in explainable artificial intelligence: clinician variability in trust, reliance, and performance.

studies.design: Prospective single-center observational study
studies.ai_system: Deep-learning Auto EF algorithm on Philips Lumify hand-held ultrasound
studies.finding: Against Simpson's method on 54 apical 4-chamber clips, bias was similar for Auto EF (-10.17%) and experienced reader-estimated EF (-9.82%). Correlation was lower for Auto EF (r = 0.56) than for the experienced readers (r = 0.80), and Auto EF correlation fell to r = 0.46 on inadequate-quality acquisitions.
studies.limitation: Single-center study with a small sample of 54 clips; the number of readers is not stated.
studies.title: Pragmatic Evaluation of a Deep-Learning Algorithm to Automate Ejection Fraction on Hand-Held, Point-of-Care Echocardiography in a Cardiac Surgical Operating Room.
studies.source: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

studies.design: Retrospective comparative study of chatbot vs original physician responses to real patient messages
studies.humans: 17 oncologists (original responses); rated by 3 oncologists and 20 patients
studies.finding: GPT-4 responses to 4257 asynchronous messages from patients with cancer were compared with oncologists' responses. In patient education, the chatbot was more often fully complete (97.34% vs 93.61%; P=.002) with no differences in accuracy or safety; in medical decision-making it had lower accuracy (96.88% vs 97.99%; P<.001) and trustworthiness (50.71% vs 93.29%; P<.001). 3.12% of chatbot decision-making responses could potentially lead to adverse outcomes vs 2.01% for physicians.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, offline simulation of chatbot replies in a single country; panels gave conflicting empathy ratings.
studies.title: Application of AI Chatbot in Responding to Asynchronous Text-Based Messages From Patients With Cancer: Comparative Study.

studies.design: Multicenter randomized controlled tandem video trial; 96 Barrett's esophagus videos read with and without AI
studies.ai_system: AI system for Barrett's esophagus endoscopic diagnosis
studies.finding: Endoscopists evaluated 96 Barrett's esophagus videos with and without AI assistance. AI assistance significantly increased examiner confidence (p < 0.001) and accuracy; withdrawing AI decreased confidence (p < 0.001) but not accuracy. Correct AI guidance was disregarded in 16% of cases, and 9% of initially correct diagnoses were changed to incorrect ones.
studies.limitation: Video-based study rather than live endoscopy; accuracy effect sizes not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-assisted Endoscopy and Examiner Confidence: A Study on Human-Artificial Intelligence Interaction in Barrett's Esophagus (With Video).

studies.design: Multicenter LLM benchmark with reader study
studies.finding: Generating diagnoses from brain MRI report findings; six radiologists read 500 reports with and without DeepSeek-R1 assistance. Assistance significantly improved diagnostic accuracy (AUPRC: 0.774-0.893) and reduced reading time (from 61 to 53 s), with greater benefit for junior radiologists.
studies.limitation: Small reader sample of six radiologists; retrospective text-based reports.
studies.title: Evaluation of large language models for diagnostic impression generation from brain MRI report findings: a multicenter benchmark and reader study.

studies.design: Model development and validation study including physician survival prediction with and without FaceAge
studies.finding: In patients with incurable cancer receiving palliative treatment, FaceAge improved physicians' survival predictions from AUC 0·74 [95% CI 0·70-0·78] to 0·8 [0·76-0·83] (p<0·0001).
studies.limitation: Primarily a model-development study; physician number and how assistance was delivered not described.
studies.title: FaceAge, a deep learning system to estimate biological age from face photographs to improve prognostication: a model development and validation study.

studies.design: Multicentric retrospective validation vs experts and clinicians
studies.finding: On 350 CTA scans, median absolute diameter difference from ground truth was 1.6 mm for ARVA and 1.6 mm for clinicians. ARVA measurements were within clinically acceptable range in 85.5% vs 86.0% for clinicians.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, two hospitals.
studies.title: Multicentric clinical evaluation of a computed tomography-based fully automated deep neural network for aortic maximum diameter and volumetric measurements.

studies.design: Retrospective before/after implementation study in teleradiology
studies.ai_system: AI clinical decision support for intracranial hemorrhage on head CT
studies.finding: Read times for noncontrast head CT before and after AI ICH detection. Examinations falsely flagged by AI took an average of 9 minutes 40 seconds versus 8 minutes 25 seconds for unremarkable scans before AI (P < .001); AI sensitivity was 75.6% and PPV 21.1%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective before/after design; measures efficiency rather than diagnostic accuracy; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Deep Learning to Detect Intracranial Hemorrhage in a National Teleradiology Program and the Impact on Interpretation Time.

studies.design: Reader study, unaided then aided 2-4 weeks later
studies.finding: Ophthalmologists classified 100 anterior segment images into nine categories. With CorneAI, overall accuracy rose from 79.2 to 88.8% (P < 0.001); specialists 82.8 to 90.0%, residents 75.6 to 86.2%. CorneAI's own accuracy was 86%.
studies.limitation: Single image set reader study with fixed order design (aided read after unaided).
studies.title: Artificial intelligence support improves diagnosis accuracy in anterior segment eye diseases.

studies.design: Validation study comparing manual vs two AI segmentation tools against intraoral scan reference
studies.ai_system: AI segmentation tools in implant planning software (CDX, BSB)
studies.finding: 67 extracted teeth from 14 patients' CBCT scans were segmented manually and by two AI tools, compared to surface scans. Manual segmentation resulted in less RMS deviation than both AI methods (p < 0.05), with AI-manual discrepancy ranging 0.10 to 0.98 mm (mean RMS 0.27 (0.11) mm); both AI methods reduced segmentation time (p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Small sample of 14 patients; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Accuracy and Time Efficiency of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Tooth Segmentation on CBCT Images: A Validation Study Using Two Implant Planning Software Programs.

studies.design: Retrospective training and prospective validation cohort with Turing test by gynecologists
studies.finding: The task was preoperative prediction of cervical cancer stage, histology, grade and LNM, with model accuracies of 75%, 95%, 86% and 76%. Except for LNM, the model's accuracy and F-score were significantly better than doctors and AI-assisted doctors (P < 0.05). Mean time was 581.1s per 20 patients for doctors and 534.8s for doctors with AI.
studies.limitation: Single center with a small validation set (58 cases); doctor accuracy figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.title: A multi-Task Learning based applicable AI model simultaneously predicts stage, histology, grade and LNM for cervical cancer before surgery.

studies.design: Prospective community screening study
studies.ai_system: Cloud-based deep learning AI for vision-threatening disease referral
studies.finding: Retinal image grading for vision-threatening disease referral. AI marked 150/385 (38.9%) eyes ungradable versus 10/385 (2.6%) by human gold standard, with 63.2% sensitivity and 94.5% specificity; AI graded faster (35.6 ± 13.3 s) than the tele-ophthalmology grader (129 ± 41.0) and clinical ophthalmologist (68 ± 21.9).
studies.limitation: Small single-community screening sample; humans served as reference standard so accuracy is only compared against them, with speed the main head-to-head measure.
studies.title: Implementation of deep learning artificial intelligence in vision-threatening disease screenings for an underserved community during COVID-19.

studies.design: Prospective cohort with retrospective AI analysis compared to general endocrinologists and subspecialists
studies.ai_system: Koios DS AI decision support system
studies.humans: General endocrinologists and thyroid nodule clinic subspecialists
studies.finding: In 80 patients, AI-DSS differed from general endocrinologists in features such as solid composition (80% vs. 36%) and led to a higher referral rate (37.3% vs. 30.7%, not significant). Agreement in ACR TI-RADS with general endocrinologists was moderate (r = 0.337), and the AI did not significantly improve risk stratification, tending to overestimate risk.
studies.limitation: Small single-setting sample; AI applied retrospectively rather than used by clinicians; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Preliminary analysis of AI-based thyroid nodule evaluation in a non-subspecialist endocrinology setting.

studies.design: Vignette study comparing ChatGPT with primary care physician recommendations
studies.finding: Treatment recommendations for depression vignettes. For mild depression, ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 recommended psychotherapy in 95.0% and 97.5% of cases versus 4.3% for primary care physicians. ChatGPT aligned with guidelines and showed no gender or socioeconomic bias, unlike the physicians.
studies.limitation: Hypothetical vignettes with physician data from a separate source; the number of physicians is not stated.
studies.title: Identifying depression and its determinants upon initiating treatment: ChatGPT versus primary care physicians.

studies.design: Model development with dermatologist reader study
studies.ai_system: Reinforcement learning skin cancer decision support
studies.finding: Skin cancer diagnosis with AI decision support. The reinforcement learning model increased dermatologists' rate of correct diagnoses by 12.0% and improved optimal management decisions from 57.4% to 65.3%.
studies.limitation: Number of dermatologists and reader-study design not described in the abstract.
studies.title: A reinforcement learning model for AI-based decision support in skin cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter hospital registry study
studies.ai_system: Random forest ML ASA physical status (ML-PS)
studies.finding: ML-PS was compared with anesthesiologist ASA-PS ratings for predicting 30-day mortality, ICU admission and adverse discharge. Agreement was 57.2%; both had excellent predictive values for 30-day mortality, and ML-PS reclassified 1281 (35.6%) of patients who died into a higher risk category. In multiple co-morbidity patients, anesthesiologist ASA-PS had better predictive accuracy.
studies.limitation: Retrospective registry data; number of anesthesiologists not stated.
studies.title: Development and validation of a machine learning ASA-score to identify candidates for comprehensive preoperative screening and risk stratification.

studies.design: Cross-sectional study with 100 text-based BI-RADS multiple-choice questions
studies.ai_system: Ten LLMs, including Claude 3.5 Sonnet and ChatGPT 4o
studies.humans: General radiologists and a breast radiologist
studies.finding: Answering BI-RADS Atlas multiple-choice questions. Claude 3.5 Sonnet (90%) and ChatGPT 4o (89%) outperformed the general radiologists (78% and 76%) but did not differ significantly from the breast radiologist (82%). Lower-performing LLMs scored 60-61%.
studies.limitation: Exam-style questions and very few radiologists; the image task had no human comparison.
studies.title: Evaluating text and visual diagnostic capabilities of large language models on questions related to the Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System Atlas 5th edition.

studies.design: Cross-sectional vignette study
studies.finding: Subspecialty registration and diagnosis on 208 ophthalmology case profiles. Registration accuracy was 63.5% (GPT-3.5), 77.9% (GPT-4.0) and 69.2% (residents), P=.07; top diagnosis accuracy was 59.6% for GPT-4.0 and 60.6% for residents vs 39.4% for GPT-3.5.
studies.limitation: Textbook cases and only three residents.
studies.title: Performance of ChatGPT in Ophthalmic Registration and Clinical Diagnosis: Cross-Sectional Study.

studies.design: Retrospective two-hospital radiomics model development with comparison to radiologists and AI-assisted second reading
studies.ai_system: Multi-modality MRI and mammography radiomics random forest model
studies.finding: The model achieved AUCs of 0.916 internal and 0.892 external validation and surpassed radiologists' ALN diagnosis on MRI and axillary ultrasound. With model assistance, accuracy increased from 70.70 to 78.16% for radiologist A and from 75.42 to 81.38% for radiologist B.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only two radiologists in the assisted reading.
studies.title: Multi-modality radiomics model predicts axillary lymph node metastasis of breast cancer using MRI and mammography.

studies.design: Multiple-reader multiple-case diagnostic study
studies.finding: For ARIA detection on 199 retrospective MRI cases, assisted AUC was 0.87 for ARIA-E (improvement 0.05; P = .001) and 0.83 for ARIA-H (improvement 0.04; P = .001). Sensitivity was 87% vs 71% (ARIA-E) and 79% vs 69% (ARIA-H) assisted vs unassisted.
studies.limitation: Retrospective trial images rather than live clinical use.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Assistive Software Tool for Automated Detection and Quantification of Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities.

studies.design: Retrospective matched case-control study
studies.finding: Ablation cases using AI ECG mapping vs matched controls: time to ablation 133 ± 48 vs. 165 ± 49 min (p = 0.02), procedure duration 233 ± 51 vs. 301 ± 83 min (p < 0.001), fluoroscopy 18.7 ± 13.3 vs. 33.2 ± 18.0 min (p < 0.001). Arrhythmia-free survival at 6 months was 73.5% vs 63.3% (p = 0.56).
studies.limitation: Small retrospective case-control (28 vs 28) with historical controls.
studies.title: Impact of artificial intelligence arrhythmia mapping on time to first ablation, procedure duration, and fluoroscopy use.

studies.design: Blinded observational comparative study scoring GPT-4 and doctor free-text responses to Swedish family medicine specialist examination cases
studies.humans: Doctors taking the Swedish family medicine specialist examination 2017-2022
studies.finding: On complex primary care exam cases scored on a 10-point scale, mean scores were 6.0 for randomly selected doctor responses, 7.2 for top-tier doctor responses and 4.5 for GPT-4. Random doctor responses scored on average 1.6 points higher than GPT-4 (p<0.001) and top-tier responses 2.7 points higher (p<0.001); in a follow-up, random doctor responses scored 0.7 points higher than GPT-4o (p=0.044).
studies.limitation: Exam cases rather than real patient care; GPT-4o follow-up used a single reviewer.
studies.title: ChatGPT (GPT-4) versus doctors on complex cases of the Swedish family medicine specialist examination: an observational comparative study.

studies.design: International AI competition with comparison of algorithms against ophthalmologists on the same test sets
studies.ai_system: Ensemble of deep learning algorithms from the MMAC competition
studies.finding: The tasks were myopic maculopathy classification and lesion segmentation on fundus images. The model ensemble outperformed ophthalmologists in classification sensitivity (0.801 vs 0.727; P = .006) and specificity (0.946 vs 0.933; P = .009). It also outperformed them in LC segmentation (DSC 0.698 vs 0.570) and FS segmentation (DSC 0.863 vs 0.790).
studies.limitation: Public competition dataset and only five ophthalmologists, so generalizability is limited.
studies.title: A Competition for the Diagnosis of Myopic Maculopathy by Artificial Intelligence Algorithms.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with comparison against masked experts
studies.finding: The task was classifying pediatric papilledema versus pseudopapilledema on fundus photographs. AI accuracy was 70.0% (cross-validation) and 73.9% (external test set), significantly higher than human experts on the cross-validation set (P < 0.002). AI sensitivity was significantly higher on the external test set (P = 0.0002), while specificity was similar (56.4%-67.3%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only two human comparators.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence to Differentiate Pediatric Pseudopapilledema and True Papilledema on Fundus Photographs.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on two PERFORMS test sets
studies.ai_system: Commercial breast cancer detection AI algorithm
studies.finding: Mammography interpretation of 60-case enriched test sets. AUC was 0.93 for AI vs 0.88 for humans (P = .15); at developer threshold sensitivity 84% vs 90% (P = .34) and specificity 89% vs 76% (P = .003).
studies.limitation: Enriched challenging test sets too small to demonstrate equivalence.
studies.title: Performance of a Breast Cancer Detection AI Algorithm Using the Personal Performance in Mammographic Screening Scheme.

studies.design: Multicenter international retrospective cohort
studies.finding: In a test cohort of 248 PSC patients, the model detected early-stage perihilar cholangiocarcinoma with sensitivity 87.9% versus 50.0% for radiologists, specificity 84.1% versus 100.0%, and AUC 86.0% versus 75.0% (all p <0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with transplant-registered cancers; radiologists' number not stated.
studies.title: Deep learning analysis of MRI accurately detects early-stage perihilar cholangiocarcinoma in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis.

studies.design: Retrospective study of LLM-enhanced spine MRI request forms and protocoling versus radiologists
studies.finding: On 250 spine MRI requests, the LLM suggested the correct protocol in 78.4% (196/250) of cases, inferior to Rad4 (90.0%) and Rad5 (89.2%). The LLM identified spinal instrumentation in 39/41 (95.1%) cases versus 61.0% and 41.5% for the radiologists.
studies.limitation: Single-institution retrospective study with only two comparison radiologists.
studies.title: MRI spine request form enhancement and auto protocoling using a secure institutional large language model.
studies.source: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of five chatbots and clinicians on 40 true/false orthodontic questions
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-4o, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet
studies.humans: Dental students, general dentists and orthodontists
studies.finding: On 40 true/false orthodontic questions, orthodontists had the highest accuracy rate, while chatbots had higher accuracy than dental students and general dentists. ChatGPT-4o's accuracy was closest to orthodontists; students scored significantly lower than several chatbots and orthodontists.
studies.limitation: True/false knowledge questions only; small clinician sample.
studies.title: Information from digital and human sources: A comparison of chatbot and clinician responses to orthodontic questions.
studies.source: American journal of orthodontics and dentofacial orthopedics : official publication of the American Association of Orthodontists, its constituent societies, and the American Board of Orthodontics

studies.design: Multi-agent LLM system evaluated on benchmarks and four real-world oncology datasets with single-blind physician assessment versus human MDTs
studies.finding: EvoMDT generated oncology MDT treatment recommendations across breast, liver, lung and lymphoma datasets. In single-blind physician review, EvoMDT achieved decision quality comparable to human MDTs while shortening response time by 30-40%.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives no quantitative decision-quality figures for the MDT comparison or the number of reviewing physicians.
studies.title: EvoMDT: a self-evolving multi-agent system for structured clinical decision-making in multi-cancer.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial, 261 orthopedic postoperative patients, AI agent vs doctor-led communication
studies.finding: Postoperative care communication: the AI responded faster (0.5 ± 0.6 vs. 358 ± 47.5 min) but with slightly reduced accuracy (93.9% vs. 98.1%, p < 0.05). The AI group had better IKDC, PCS and satisfaction at 1 and 3 months, with no significant differences by 6 months.
studies.limitation: Lower AI accuracy than physicians; short-term benefits not sustained; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: A randomized controlled trial of a WeChat-based artificial intelligence agent for postoperative care in orthopedic patients.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial, 872 rectal cancer patients, ML-guided vs surgeon discretion
studies.ai_system: RTID machine learning anastomotic leakage model
studies.finding: Ileostomy decision-making: RTID-guided decisions gave a lower diverting ileostomy rate (18.6% vs. 40.5%) and less unnecessary stoma formation (17.7% vs. 41.3%). Anastomotic leakage was comparable (2.4% vs. 2.7%).
studies.limitation: Underpowered for non-inferiority of leakage; number of surgeons not stated.
studies.title: Machine learning model-guided selective use of temporary diverting ileostomy in rectal cancer surgery: a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Prospective double-centre randomized controlled trial
studies.finding: 318 patients were randomized to AI-assisted or conventional nasopharyngolaryngoscopy, with anatomical site coverage as primary outcome. AI-assisted examinations achieved higher mean coverage (93.08% vs. 83.50%, P < 0.0001) without significantly increasing examination time.
studies.limitation: Outcome is procedural coverage, not lesion detection or patient outcomes; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Real-time AI-assisted quality control during nasopharyngolaryngoscopy: a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Comparison on 25 standard uveitis cases
studies.finding: ChatGPT and five ophthalmologists gave likely diagnoses, differentials and management for 25 uveitis cases. Ophthalmologists achieved 60-92% for likely diagnosis versus 60% for AI; counting fully and partially accurate diagnoses, ophthalmologists achieved 76-100% and AI 72%.
studies.limitation: Small set of 25 standardized cases and only five ophthalmologists.
studies.title: Evaluating the Diagnostic Accuracy and Management Recommendations of ChatGPT in Uveitis.

studies.design: Multicenter model development with external test comparison against radiologists
studies.humans: Junior and senior CEUS radiologists and senior MRI radiologists
studies.finding: For six-class classification of focal liver lesions in three external test sets, the model achieved accuracy from 0.85 to 0.86. This was better than junior CEUS radiologists (0.59-0.73) and comparable to senior CEUS radiologists (0.79-0.85) and senior MRI radiologists (0.82-0.86).
studies.limitation: Model-development study by the developers; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound-based AI model for multi-classification of focal liver lesions.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Ensemble deep learning model integrating radiographs and clinical features
studies.finding: The model differentiated primary bone tumors from bone infections on radiographs with AUCs of 0.948 and 0.963 and accuracies of 0.881 and 0.895 on internal and external sets. Its performance surpassed junior and mid-level radiologists and was comparable to senior radiologists (accuracy: 83.6%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; number of radiologists and reader conditions not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Deep learning models in classifying primary bone tumors and bone infections based on radiographs.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on 100 MRI text reports
studies.finding: Assigning PI-RADS categories from 100 prostate MRI text reports. Radiologists reached 95% and 90% accuracy, against 67% for GPT-3.5 and Bard and 83% (GPT-4) and 79% (Gemini) for the updated models.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists and text reports rather than images, with the original report used as reference.
studies.title: Assessing the performance of ChatGPT and Bard/Gemini against radiologists for Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System classification based on prostate multiparametric MRI text reports.

studies.design: Comparison of ChatGPT with pharmacist DDI evaluation in 120 inpatients
studies.finding: Identifying drug-drug interactions for 120 hospitalized patients. ChatGPT showed low true positive rates and minimal agreement with pharmacists (Cohen's kappa 0.077-0.143).
studies.limitation: Pharmacists served as the reference rather than as compared performers, and the clinician number is not stated.
studies.title: Evaluating the capability of ChatGPT in predicting drug-drug interactions: Real-world evidence using hospitalized patient data.

studies.design: Comparison against invasive QCA reference in 208 patients
studies.humans: One level 3 and two level 2 CCTA readers
studies.finding: Detecting obstructive coronary stenosis (≥50%) on CCTA against invasive QCA. Per patient, AI-QCT had an AUC of 0.91 versus 0.77 for the level 3 reader and 0.79 and 0.76 for the level 2 readers. Per vessel, AI-QCT had 0.86, similar to level 3 (0.82; p=0.098) and superior to level 2 readers (both 0.69).
studies.limitation: Only three readers in a single trial cohort.
studies.title: Diagnostic accuracy in coronary CT angiography analysis: artificial intelligence versus human assessment.

studies.design: Model development with retrospective benchmark against clinicians plus prospective cohort
studies.ai_system: 3D CNN explainable model on temporal bone CT
studies.humans: 7 clinical experts (residents, attending otologist, senior clinicians)
studies.finding: For detecting pathological ears and cholesteatoma on temporal bone CT, the model outperformed resident fellows and the attending otologist (P<.05) and rivaled senior clinicians. Prospectively it achieved 81.8% accuracy in preoperative diagnoses for 121 patients.
studies.limitation: Benchmark against only 7 clinicians; human metrics not numerically reported in abstract.
studies.title: A 3D and Explainable Artificial Intelligence Model for Evaluation of Chronic Otitis Media Based on Temporal Bone Computed Tomography: Model Development, Validation, and Clinical Application.

studies.design: Multi-institutional retrospective prognostic reproducibility study with manual and AI-assisted arms
studies.ai_system: Open-source machine learning TIL quantification algorithm
studies.humans: 98 participants: 40 pathologists in manual arm; 11 pathologists and 47 nonpathologists in AI-assisted arm
studies.finding: TIL scoring on 60 H&E melanoma sections. AI-assisted scoring showed ICCs higher than 0.90 for all machine learning TIL variables, outperforming manual assessment (ICC, 0.61 for AI-derived stromal TILs vs Kendall W, 0.44 for manual Clark TIL scoring).
studies.limitation: Retrospective cohorts; arms differed in participant composition (mostly nonpathologists in AI arm); measures reproducibility not accuracy.
studies.title: Pathologist-Read vs AI-Driven Assessment of Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes in Melanoma.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparative reader study with and without AI
studies.humans: Neurosurgeons, anesthetists, OR nurses of varying experience
studies.finding: Detecting cerebral aneurysms in still frames from operative videos. Professionals correctly labeled 70% of frames without AI vs 78% with AI assistance (odds ratio: 1.77, P < 0.001), with neurosurgical attendings improving from 77% to 92%; AI-assisted human performance surpassed both human and AI alone.
studies.limitation: Still frames rather than live surgery; AI-alone accuracy not quantified in abstract.
