studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Surgical Scene Recognition: A Comparative Study Among Health Care Professionals.

studies.design: Multicentre development plus prospective reader study
studies.finding: Ovarian cancer risk assessment on ultrasound in 284 cases. Using UMORSS increased radiologists' average AUC by 10.58% and sensitivity by 22.48%.
studies.limitation: Only six radiologists; absolute unaided/aided values not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A multimodal uncertainty-aware AI system optimizes ovarian cancer risk assessment workflow.

studies.design: Model development with silent prospective validation versus MSBOS and clinician ordering
studies.ai_system: Smart Match XGBoost transfusion prediction model
studies.finding: Predicting perioperative red blood cell transfusion before elective surgery. In silent prospective validation (n=24,003), the model's sensitivity was 0.72 (95% CI, 0.67 to 0.75) and PPV 0.34 (95% CI, 0.31 to 0.37), surpassing both MSBOS and clinician behavior.
studies.limitation: Silent validation at a single center; clinician performance figures not reported in the abstract and model did not influence care.
studies.title: AI-Guided Surgical Blood Readiness: Overcoming Real-World Challenges in Prospective Validation for Safer, More Efficient Blood Preparation.

studies.design: Comparison of GPT-4 vs doctors' reports on cases
studies.humans: Doctors with various levels of experience
studies.finding: GPT-4 generated thyroid cancer ultrasound reports, diagnoses and treatment plans for 109 cases, compared with doctors' reports. GPT-4 was proficient in report structuring, terminology and clarity but showed limitations in diagnostic accuracy.
studies.limitation: No quantitative results reported in the abstract; number of doctors not stated.
studies.title: Assessing the role of GPT-4 in thyroid ultrasound diagnosis and treatment recommendations: enhancing interpretability with a chain of thought approach.
studies.source: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

studies.design: Blinded comparison of ChatGPT vs expert surgeon answers to patient questions
studies.humans: One expert rhinoplasty surgeon; seven expert surgeon raters
studies.finding: Answers to pre- and postoperative septorhinoplasty questions were rated on empathy, accuracy, completeness and overall quality. ChatGPT scored significantly higher in accuracy, completeness and overall quality (p < 0.001) and was preferred in 80.95% of instances.
studies.limitation: Single physician comparator and small rater panel.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Versus Expert Plastic Surgeon: Comparative Study Shows ChatGPT "Wins" Rhinoplasty Consultations: Should We Be Worried?

studies.design: Retrospective cohort simulation of screening scenarios
studies.finding: In 42 236 screening mammograms, double human reading recalled 1244 (2·9%) and single human reading with AI recalled 2112 (5·0%). Single reading with AI improved sensitivity by 8·4% (95% CI 5·7-11·2, p<0·0001) compared with double human reading.
studies.limitation: Retrospective simulation, not live reading with AI; recall rate increased; reader number not stated.
studies.title: AI as an independent second reader in detection of clinically relevant breast cancers within a population-based screening programme in the Netherlands: a retrospective cohort study.

studies.design: Retrospective two-center model development compared against emergency physicians' predictions
studies.ai_system: Machine learning models with NLP (Random Forest selected)
studies.finding: Prediction of ED disposition (death/ICU admission; ward admission/transfer). EPs achieved F1 scores of 0.361 and 0.498 for primary and secondary outcomes, and all machine learning models achieved higher F1 scores than EPs.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; physician predictions taken from routine triage records; model F1 values not given in abstract.
studies.title: Using machine learning and natural language processing in triage for prediction of clinical disposition in the emergency department.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre observer performance study, 225 radiographs
studies.ai_system: Commercial AI tool for KL grading
studies.humans: 11 radiologists and orthopedists, in-training and board-certified
studies.finding: Readers graded knee osteoarthritis with and without AI. Three of six junior readers improved (e.g. AUC 0.81 vs 0.88, P < .001), and interobserver agreement rose from κ = 0.77 to 0.85 (P < .001).
studies.limitation: Benefit limited to some junior readers; retrospective design.
studies.title: Interobserver Agreement and Performance of Concurrent AI Assistance for Radiographic Evaluation of Knee Osteoarthritis.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on 1366 imaging reports
studies.finding: ChatGPT diagnosed benign vs malignant bone tumors from imaging reports. It achieved accuracy 0.73, then 0.87 after few-shot learning, described as much closer to the level of physician diagnostics.
studies.limitation: Physician performance figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Large-Scale assessment of ChatGPT's performance in benign and malignant bone tumors imaging report diagnosis and its potential for clinical applications.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of AI 3D planning vs surgeons' 2D templating
studies.finding: Predicting acetabular cup size for THA in 103 DDH patients. Within ±0 size, AIHIP accuracy was 84.1% vs 64.0% for 2D templates (p < 0.05); within ±1 size, 95.1% vs 81.1% (p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single dataset with only two surgeons; comparison is AI versus a templating method rather than unaided surgeon judgement alone.
studies.title: Application and evaluation of artificial intelligence 3D preoperative planning software in developmental dysplasia of the hip.
studies.source: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on radiology quiz cases
studies.ai_system: OpenAI o1, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.2-90B-Vision
studies.finding: On 95 RSNA 2024 Case of the Day questions, OpenAI o1 scored 59% (56 of 95), comparable to two radiologists at 58% (55 of 95) and 66% (63 of 95) (P = .99).
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists and quiz cases rather than clinical practice.
studies.title: One Year On: Assessing Progress of Multimodal Large Language Model Performance on RSNA 2024 Case of the Day Questions.

studies.design: Simulated clinical reader study with and without AI
studies.finding: With InterpreFFA, residents' FFA diagnostic accuracy improved from 85.55 to 90.34% (p < 0.05) and reporting time fell from 153.93 to 108.08 s (p < 0.001). AI-generated reports scored slightly lower than manual reports (4.12 vs. 4.38, p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Only two residents in a simulated setting.
studies.title: Generative artificial intelligence for fundus fluorescein angiography interpretation and human expert evaluation.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to clinical specialists
studies.ai_system: SLIViT vision transformer pre-trained on 2D scans
studies.humans: Clinical specialists who manually annotated scans
studies.finding: Prediction of disease-risk factors from volumetric CT, MRI, OCT and ultrasound across eight tasks. SLIViT was typically as accurate as clinical specialists; no numbers are given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: No quantitative human comparison reported in abstract; number of specialists not stated.
studies.title: Accurate prediction of disease-risk factors from volumetric medical scans by a deep vision model pre-trained with 2D scans.

studies.design: Retrospective real-world comparison of CXRs within vs outside an AI-integrated alert system
studies.ai_system: FDA-approved pneumothorax detection AI with PACS alerts
studies.humans: Radiologists at an academic medical center
studies.finding: Among 27,397 inpatient chest X-rays, radiologist reporting time for confirmed pneumothorax was compared with and without AI integration. Median reporting time was reduced by 46% with AI integration (100 vs. 186 min, p < .001); the AI tool had AUC .78, sensitivity .60 and specificity .97.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, non-randomised single-institution comparison; diagnostic accuracy of radiologists with vs without AI not reported.
studies.title: Real-World Performance of Pneumothorax-Detecting Artificial Intelligence Algorithm and its Impact on Radiologist Reporting Times.

studies.design: Retrospective before-after study at 2 hospitals
studies.humans: Junior radiologists (senior radiologists' reports as reference)
studies.finding: Lung nodule detection on chest CT in 12,889 patients, compared before and after AI implementation. Detection rates rose from 46.19% to 53.45% (Hospital C) and from 39.29% to 55.22% (Hospital A), and the false negative rate fell from 8.4% to 5.16%. However, the false positive rate increased from 2.36% to 9.77% and accuracy decreased from 93.33% to 92.23% and from 95.27% to 92.77%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective before-after design without concurrent controls; the reference standard was senior radiologists' reports.
studies.title: Enhancing Diagnostic Accuracy of Lung Nodules in Chest Computed Tomography Using Artificial Intelligence: Retrospective Analysis.

studies.design: Model development with human-machine comparison
studies.ai_system: ResNet18 CNN for FFA image classification
studies.finding: CNN classified FFA images of diabetic retinopathy, with accuracy of 63.67%-88.88% for lesion detection. The human-machine comparison showed the CNN had similar accuracy to junior ophthalmologists.
studies.limitation: Human comparison numbers and reader count not reported in abstract; retrospective development study.
studies.title: Automatic interpretation and clinical evaluation for fundus fluorescein angiography images of diabetic retinopathy patients by deep learning.

studies.design: Reader study of residents without then with AI bounding boxes
studies.humans: Two pediatric and two radiology residents
studies.finding: For pediatric wrist fracture detection, AI access improved average resident accuracy from 80 to 93% for any fracture (P < 0.001) and from 69 to 92% for buckle fracture. The model alone had accuracy of 88% and AUC 0.92.
studies.limitation: Four readers, small test set of 125 radiographs, sequential reading design.
studies.title: Detecting pediatric wrist fractures using deep-learning-based object detection.

studies.design: Cross-sectional blinded patient survey comparing ChatGPT and neurologist responses
studies.finding: Among 1133 people with MS rating responses to four questions, ChatGPT responses had significantly higher empathy scores (Coeff = 1.38; 95% CI = 0.65, 2.11). No association was found with mean satisfaction (Coeff = 0.03; p = 0.157).
studies.limitation: Only four questions; outcomes are patient perceptions rather than accuracy.
studies.title: ChatGPT vs. neurologists: a cross-sectional study investigating preference, satisfaction ratings and perceived empathy in responses among people living with multiple sclerosis.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with reader comparison under three assistance scenarios
studies.ai_system: Thyroid US detection, segmentation and classification AI models
studies.humans: Three senior and three junior radiologists
studies.finding: Thyroid nodule cancer diagnosis on US. The AI model (AUC up to 0.98) outperformed all senior and junior radiologists (P < .05 for all comparisons). Diagnostic accuracies of all radiologists improved with rule-based AI assistance (P < .05 for all comparisons).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, Chinese population only, six readers.
studies.title: Generalizability and Diagnostic Performance of AI Models for Thyroid US.

studies.design: Prospective study, 236 patients with 312 thyroid nodules, reader study with and without AI reports
studies.humans: Nine residents and three senior radiologists
studies.finding: Readers diagnosed thyroid nodules as benign or malignant from recorded US images, then again after viewing AI reports. The AI system had sensitivity 0.95, accuracy 0.84 and AUC 0.753, not statistically different from experienced radiologists but superior to residents (all p < 0.01). AI assistance improved residents' accuracy and sensitivity for nodules ≤ 1.5 cm and reduced unnecessary biopsy rate by up to 27.7% for nodules > 1.5 cm (p = 0.034).
studies.limitation: Single experienced operator acquired images; readers interpreted recorded images rather than making live decisions.
studies.title: Clinical value of artificial intelligence in thyroid ultrasound: a prospective study from the real world.

studies.design: Comparison of ChatGPT-4 and nurse answers to post-TKA patient questions graded by surgeons
studies.finding: Surgeons graded 44 of 60 (73.3%) responses appropriate for both nurses and ChatGPT. 136 patients (53.8%) were more comfortable with ChatGPT answers versus 86 (34.0%) preferring nurse answers.
studies.limitation: Nurses rather than physicians; 60 questions at a single institution.
studies.title: Use and Application of Large Language Models for Patient Questions Following Total Knee Arthroplasty.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to human readers
studies.ai_system: Radiomics plus autoencoder machine learning model on breast US
studies.finding: For classifying breast tumors as benign or malignant on US images, the model achieved an AUC of 0.90. No evidence of difference was found between the model and the human readers (AUC 0.83, P = .55, and 0.82, P = .45).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, with a small external validation set (50 patients); the number of readers is not stated.
studies.title: Combining Radiomics and Autoencoders to Distinguish Benign and Malignant Breast Tumors on US Images.

studies.design: Retrospective crossover reader study, cases randomized to LLM-assisted vs conventional internet search
studies.ai_system: LLM-based search engine and hybrid chatbot
studies.finding: Residents gave top-three differential diagnoses for 40 challenging brain MRI cases. LLM-assisted accuracy was 61.4% (70/114) vs 46.5% (53/114) with conventional search (p = 0.033), with no difference in interpretation time or confidence.
studies.limitation: Only six residents and 40 cases at a single setting.
studies.title: Human-AI collaboration in large language model-assisted brain MRI differential diagnosis: a usability study.

studies.design: Multicenter prospective study with reader substudy with and without QCT
studies.ai_system: Deep learning-based texture analysis QCT software
studies.finding: Readers assessed ILD fibrosis stability for 30 samples with and without QCT information. QCT results increased readers' specificity (91.7% vs 94.6%, P = .02).
studies.limitation: Reader substudy on only 30 samples; secondary aim of a measurement-variability study.
studies.title: Measurement Variability of Same-Day CT Quantification of Interstitial Lung Disease: A Multicenter Prospective Study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 188 AAN Question of the Day cases
studies.finding: On 188 neurology questions, the chatbot had a mean success rate of 71.3% versus 69.2% for neurology peers. It achieved a correct diagnosis in 85.0% of cases.
studies.limitation: Question-bank vignettes rather than real patients; peer responses aggregated from an app.
studies.title: Embracing the future-is artificial intelligence already better? A comparative study of artificial intelligence performance in diagnostic accuracy and decision-making.

studies.design: Cross-sectional reader study of 18 complex ECGs against angiography/clinical reference standard
studies.finding: Physicians and QoH AI judged whether 18 STEMI-equivalent/mimic ECGs showed OMI needing cath lab activation. Accuracy was 65.6% for EPs and 65.5% for cardiologists versus 88.9% for QoH AI (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Only 18 curated ECGs read outside clinical context; no prospective validation.
studies.title: Accuracy of cath lab activation decisions for STEMI-equivalent and mimic ECGs: Physicians vs. AI (Queen of Hearts by PMcardio).
studies.source: The American journal of emergency medicine

studies.design: Retrospective development of fine-tuned LLM with reader study with and without LLM
studies.humans: Two radiology residents and two radiologists
studies.finding: On 800 test cases, the LLM had top-1 accuracy of 0.923. With LLM assistance accuracy improved for residents (0.913 vs. 0.936, p = 0.02) and radiologists (0.920 vs. 0.926), and reading times fell by 14% and 12% respectively.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset study with only four readers.
studies.title: Efficacy of Fine-Tuned Large Language Model in CT Protocol Assignment as Clinical Decision-Supporting System.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: User study within model development paper
studies.ai_system: LEADS foundation model for literature mining
studies.finding: Experts performed systematic review study selection and data extraction with and without LEADS. In study selection, recall was 0.81 with LEADS vs 0.78 without, saving 20.8% time. For data extraction, accuracy was 0.85 vs 0.80, with 26.9% time savings.
studies.limitation: Small user study embedded in a model-development paper; participants included non-clinician researchers.
studies.title: A foundation model for human-AI collaboration in medical literature mining.

studies.design: Comparison of LLM responses vs junior doctors on questions from thyroid nodule patients, senior doctors as gold standard
studies.humans: Five junior doctors (five senior doctors as reference)
studies.finding: Questions generated from 145 thyroid nodule patients were answered by two chatbots and five junior doctors. In decision making, New Bing Chat accuracy was 72.41% and ChatGPT-3.5 58.62%, both less accurate than junior doctors (89.66%, P < 0.001). LLMs were comparable to junior doctors only on Q4 and Q6.
studies.limitation: Single condition, small number of doctors, older LLM versions.
studies.title: Clinical application potential of large language model: a study based on thyroid nodules.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic accuracy reader study
studies.ai_system: GPT-4o, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Llama 4 Maverick
studies.finding: Distinguishing synthetic from authentic radiographs. Radiologists had 75% accuracy on the GPT-4o dataset and 70% on the RoentGen dataset; GPT-4o (85%) and GPT-5 (83%) were more accurate on GPT-4o images than Llama 4 Maverick (59%) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (56%).
studies.limitation: No direct statistical comparison between radiologists and LLMs reported; non-clinical task.
studies.title: The Rise of Deepfake Medical Imaging: Radiologists' Diagnostic Accuracy in Detecting ChatGPT-generated Radiographs.

studies.design: Prospective comparison of triage decisions in the emergency department
studies.humans: Triage nurses and emergency medicine doctors
studies.finding: In 500 emergency department patients, triage nurses undertriaged 3.1% of yellow-coded and 3.4% of red-coded patients relative to emergency doctors. ChatGPT, the closest AI, undertriaged 26.5% of yellow-coded and 42.6% of red-coded patients.
studies.limitation: Emergency physicians served as the reference standard, from a single center over one week.
studies.title: Exploring the potential of artificial intelligence models for triage in the emergency department.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of answers to 251 real user cardiology questions rated by cardiologists
studies.humans: Human experts answering on an internet portal
studies.finding: GPT-4 and human expert answers to cardiology questions were compared by three cardiologists. GPT-4 was judged better in 132/251 (52.6%) vs human expert in 119/251 (47.4%); humans had more high-accuracy (21.1% vs 12.6%) but more low-accuracy responses (4.6% vs 0.4%), and outperformed GPT-4 on drug information and preliminary diagnoses.
studies.limitation: Human answers came from an online portal and may not reflect clinical consultation; single specialty.
studies.title: Assessing GPT-4's Performance in Delivering Medical Advice: Comparative Analysis With Human Experts.

studies.design: Single-institution comparison on five scripted clinical scenarios scored with a 50-point rubric
studies.humans: 5 junior residents, 12 senior residents, 5 attending general surgeons
studies.finding: On surgical decision-making across five scenarios scored out of 50, ChatGPT-4 averaged 39.6 points (79.2%), against 33.4 (66.8%) for junior residents, 38.0 (76.0%) for senior residents and 38.8 (77.6%) for attendings. ChatGPT-4 scored significantly better than junior residents (P = .009) and was not significantly different from senior residents or attendings.
studies.limitation: Single institution, only five scenarios, and low response rates (15.9% of residents, 13.8% of attendings).
studies.title: AI Versus MD: Evaluating the surgical decision-making accuracy of ChatGPT-4.

studies.design: Observer study on 72 RSNA 2023 Case of the Day questions, with and without GPT-4V assistance
studies.finding: GPT-4V accuracy was 43% (31 of 72); radiologists and residents did not significantly outperform it on imaging-dependent (59% and 56% vs 39%) or imaging-independent (76% and 63% vs 70%) cases. With access to GPT-4V responses, there was no evidence of improvement in readers' average accuracy.
studies.limitation: Small number of readers (8) and curated quiz cases in an open-book setting rather than clinical practice.
studies.title: Evaluation of GPT Large Language Model Performance on RSNA 2023 Case of the Day Questions.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with reader study
studies.ai_system: Endoscopic multi-site feature fusion AI for autoimmune gastritis
studies.finding: AI sensitivity 91.3% was comparable to experts (87.3%) and outperformed nonexperts (70.0%; P = 0.01). With AI support, endoscopist sensitivity improved to 90.3% vs 78.7% (P = 0.008).
studies.limitation: Retrospective image-based reader study; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: A novel endoscopic artificial intelligence system to assist in the diagnosis of autoimmune gastritis: a multicenter study.

studies.design: Prospective multicentre diagnostic model development with test cohort compared to radiologists
studies.ai_system: Combination SWE-based deep learning radiomics model
studies.finding: For predicting axillary lymph node status after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, radiologists' accuracy ranged from 64.26 to 71.11%. The SWE-based DLR model had accuracy 80.81% and the combination model 88.70% (AUC 0.95).
studies.limitation: Number of radiologists not stated; random split internal test set only.
studies.title: Elastography-based AI model can predict axillary status after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer with nodal involvement: a prospective, multicenter, diagnostic study.

studies.design: Randomized crossover reader study, four rounds with washout
studies.finding: For AMD diagnosis and severity classification on 960 images, AI assistance improved accuracy for 23 of 24 clinicians, with mean F1 rising from 37.71 to 45.52. Manual diagnosis took 39.8 seconds per patient, and AI assistance saved 10.3 seconds.
studies.limitation: Retrospective images from a research dataset (AREDS); combining manual and AI did not always yield the best accuracy.
studies.title: AI Workflow, External Validation, and Development in Eye Disease Diagnosis.

studies.design: Observational cohort with historical/non-CADe controls
studies.finding: Adenoma detection rate with and without CADe. ADR was 42.9% vs 21.5% for trainees, 41.3% vs 36.8% for intermediates and 39.8% vs 33.3% for experts; CADe-assisted trainees did not differ from experts (p = 0.72).
studies.limitation: Non-randomized, small CADe cohort of 335 patients, number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on the adenoma detection rate : Comparison between experienced, intermediate and trainee endoscopists' adenoma detection rate.

studies.design: Model development and validation with retrospective and prospective test sets, compared with spine surgeons
studies.ai_system: Swin-pix2pix cGAN generating virtual X-rays from smartphone photos
studies.finding: For scoliosis severity grading from virtual X-rays, the model's accuracy exceeded that of two spine surgery experts, with accuracy of 0.93 in main curve and 0.89 in secondary curve. Expert accuracy figures are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Only two experts, homogeneous population; human comparator numbers not reported.
studies.title: Conditional generative adversarial network-assisted system for radiation-free evaluation of scoliosis using a single smartphone photograph: a model development and validation study.

studies.design: Retrospective population-based cohort external validation of commercial AI vs radiologists' real-world reads
studies.humans: Screening radiologists who interpreted the screens in practice
studies.finding: On 108,970 consecutive screening mammograms, AI had an AUC of 0.83 compared with 0.93 for radiologists. At a prospective threshold, AI sensitivity (0.67; 95% CI: 0.64-0.70) was comparable to radiologists (0.68; 95% CI: 0.66-0.71) but specificity was lower (0.81 versus 0.97). Simulated AI-radiologist reading had a lower CDR (6.37 versus 6.97 per 1000) and recall (3.14% vs 3.38%), while AI detected interval cancers missed by radiologists (0.72 per 1000).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; AI-radiologist reading was simulated rather than actioned in practice.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) for breast cancer screening: BreastScreen population-based cohort study of cancer detection.

studies.design: Retrospective evaluation against initial clinical diagnosis and blinded experts
studies.ai_system: Previously developed deep learning model for fetal CHD detection
studies.humans: Blinded human experts and initial screening clinicians
studies.finding: The model detected severe congenital heart disease on stored second-trimester ultrasound images of 42 normal fetuses and 66 CHD cases. Model sensitivity and specificity were 91% and 78%, versus 55 ± 10% and 71 ± 13% for three blinded experts; initial clinical screening sensitivity was 53%.
studies.limitation: Small sample and only three blinded experts; experts were limited to stored images.
studies.title: Deep-learning model for prenatal congenital heart disease screening generalizes to community setting and outperforms clinical detection.
studies.source: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology

studies.design: Prospective multi-institutional diagnostic study (832 patients, four centres)
studies.humans: Experienced radiologists using mp-MRI PI-RADS v2.1
studies.finding: Identifying clinically significant prostate cancer. 3D P-Net AUC 0.85-0.89 was similar to mp-MRI PI-RADS v2.1 read by experienced radiologists (AUC 0.83-0.86, P = 0.460-0.732) and superior to the TRUS Likert score (AUC 0.71-0.78). Unnecessary biopsy rate fell from 35.2% (PI-RADS) to 25.8% (3D P-Net).
studies.limitation: Number of radiologists not stated; comparison involves different imaging modalities, and no clinical deployment.
studies.title: Three-dimensional convolutional neural network model to identify clinically significant prostate cancer in transrectal ultrasound videos: a prospective, multi-institutional, diagnostic study.

studies.design: Reader study with three scenarios (no AI, on-demand AI, integrated AI)
studies.ai_system: AI tool integrated in RIS/PACS for COVID-19 lung severity scoring on chest X-ray
studies.finding: Eight residents scored multi-regional lung compromise severity on 150 COVID-19 chest X-rays without AI, with on-demand AI and with integrated AI. AI support significantly reduced severity score errors and increased inter-rater agreement by 22%, and residents were resilient to AI errors above an acceptability threshold. Residents requested AI in 70% of cases when free to choose.
studies.limitation: Very small reader sample (eight residents) on a single COVID-19 scoring task.
studies.title: Upskilling or deskilling? Measurable role of an AI-supported training for radiology residents: a lesson from the pandemic.

studies.design: Survey-based reader experiment with and without CNN assistance
studies.ai_system: CNN with Grad-CAM for scaphoid fracture detection
studies.humans: Residents, hand fellows and attendings in plastic surgery, orthopaedics and emergency medicine
studies.finding: Physicians read 15 scaphoid radiographs with and without CNN assistance. For occult fractures, interobserver agreement was higher with CNN assistance (AC1 0.42 [95% CI 0.17 to 0.68] versus 0.06 [95% CI 0.00 to 0.17]), and sensitivity and specificity improved. Differences in time (18 ± 12 vs 30 ± 27 seconds) and confidence were judged not clinically relevant.
studies.limitation: Only 15 radiographs in a survey setting.
studies.title: Can a Deep Learning Algorithm Improve Detection of Occult Scaphoid Fractures in Plain Radiographs? A Clinical Validation Study.

studies.design: Model development with external prospectively acquired test set compared against human readers
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model estimating fetal weight from abdominal ultrasound video
studies.humans: 6 human readers of varying expertise, including residents
studies.finding: Fetal weight estimation on 100 prospectively acquired scans. The mean absolute percentage error between the 6 human readers and deep learning was 3.75%±2.00%, and 2.59%±1.11% against the 4 experts, with ICCs between 0.9761 and 0.9865. The authors report similar performance for humans and deep learning.
studies.limitation: Agreement-based comparison without a birth-weight ground truth reported in the abstract; small test set.
studies.title: Deep learning for estimation of fetal weight throughout the pregnancy from fetal abdominal ultrasound.
studies.source: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM

studies.design: Model development with comparison against clinicians
studies.ai_system: Explainable machine learning tool on OCT features
studies.finding: Machine learning models diagnosed and staged glaucoma from OCT in 334 normal and 268 glaucomatous eyes, with AUCs of 0.96, 0.98 and 1.00 for early, moderate and advanced glaucoma. The machine outperformed clinicians in early-stage and overall glaucoma diagnosis with 10.4-11.2% higher accuracy.
studies.limitation: Clinician comparison is poorly described in the abstract (number and experience of clinicians not stated).
studies.title: OCT-based diagnosis of glaucoma and glaucoma stages using explainable machine learning.

studies.design: Comparison of chatbots with residents on progress test questions
studies.finding: On diagnostic uncertainty questions, PGY-1 residents scored 61.1% and PGY-2 residents 63.3%, versus 57.7% for Claude-3 and 53.3% for GPT-4o. Both chatbots scored lower than residents (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Only 90 exam questions from one program.
studies.title: The future of AI clinicians: assessing the modern standard of chatbots and their approach to diagnostic uncertainty.

studies.design: Test-retest reproducibility study on MRI of ADPKD patients scanned twice
studies.finding: For total kidney volume measurement on MRI in 19 ADPKD subjects scanned twice, the model averaged across five sequences achieved test-retest reproducibility (percent absolute difference) of 1.3%, which was better than all five expert observers. Observer values are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Small test-retest sample (19 subjects); human comparison numbers not reported.
studies.title: Test Retest Reproducibility of Organ Volume Measurements in ADPKD Using 3D Multimodality Deep Learning.

studies.design: Validation study comparing AI-based automated virtual fracture reduction with manual reduction on 20 CT scans, rated by orthopedic surgeons
studies.ai_system: AI-based preoperative virtual reduction model (deep learning segmentation plus Monte Carlo simulation)
studies.humans: Manual reduction; 20 orthopedic surgeons rated quality
studies.finding: For preoperative virtual reduction of Neer 3- or 4-part proximal humerus fractures, AI-based reduction had better mean DSC (0.78 ± 0.13 vs. 0.69 ± 0.16) and IoU (0.65 ± 0.16 vs. 0.55 ± 0.18) than manual reduction. Reduction quality score was higher with AI (91.47 ± 1.12 vs. 89.30 ± 1.62, p = 0.045), clinical validity agreement was similar (82.25% vs 76.75%, p = 0.06), and AI working time was 1.41% of manual.
studies.limitation: Very small sample of 20 CT scans; unclear who performed manual reduction; Level IV evidence.
studies.title: Clinical validation of artificial intelligence-based preoperative virtual reduction for Neer 3- or 4-part proximal humerus fractures.

studies.design: Retrospective development with prospective external validation and reader comparison with and without AI
studies.ai_system: Multimodal deep learning model (ultrasound, clinical, laboratory data)
studies.finding: For biliary atresia diagnosis, the multimodal model achieved an AUC of 0.9740 in the prospective external test set of 171 cases, comparable to a radiologist with over 10 years of experience (AUC = 0.9766). With AI assistance, the AUC of less experienced radiologists improved from 0.6667 to 0.9006.
studies.limitation: Number of readers not stated; small prospective external set.
studies.title: Development of an artificial intelligence-based multimodal diagnostic system for early detection of biliary atresia.

studies.design: Multicentre development with prospective reader study with and without AI
studies.finding: With HTN-AI assistance in classifying thyroid nodules as benign or malignant, the AUCs of junior radiologists increased from 0.59, 0.59, and 0.57 to 0.68, 0.65, and 0.65.
studies.limitation: Small number of readers; seniors' results not reported.
studies.title: A multicenter diagnostic study of thyroid nodule with Hashimoto's thyroiditis enabled by Hashimoto's thyroiditis nodule-artificial intelligence model.

studies.design: Cross-sectional simulated case study
studies.finding: Diagnosis and decision-making on 4 simulated cases, scored for accuracy, speed and comprehensiveness. Nurses scored higher on average than the shortened GenAI responses. GenAI responses were faster but more verbose, and full-length Gemini and Claude achieved the highest accuracy among the models.
studies.limitation: Only 4 simulated cases, and the clinicians were nurses rather than physicians.
studies.title: Augmenting Community Nursing Practice With Generative AI: A Formative Study of Diagnostic Synergies Using Simulation-Based Clinical Cases.
studies.source: Journal of primary care & community health

studies.design: Prospective video recognition test of AI vs expert and non-expert endoscopists, then non-experts re-read with AI assistance
studies.ai_system: iCLE (inception-ResNet V2-based pCLE computer-aided diagnosis system)
studies.humans: Three expert and three non-expert endoscopists
studies.finding: For diagnosing esophageal squamous neoplasm on 187 pCLE videos from 67 lesions, iCLE achieved accuracy, sensitivity and specificity of 90.9%, 92.0% and 90.2%, with significantly higher sensitivity than experts (92.0% vs 80.4%; P < 0.001) and NPV (94.4% vs 87.7%; P = 0.003). With iCLE assistance, non-expert endoscopists improved in accuracy (from 83.6% to 88.6%) and sensitivity (from 76.0% to 89.8%).
studies.limitation: Small reader group (six endoscopists) and small prospective sample of 54 patients; sequential unaided-then-aided reading.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-aided optical biopsy improves the diagnosis of esophageal squamous neoplasm.

studies.design: Two-phase reader study (unaided then AI-assisted)
studies.finding: Pathologists diagnosed 105 prostate core needle biopsies unaided and then with AI assistance. Accuracy was 95.00% unaided and 93.81% assisted. With AI they requested about 20% fewer IHC studies and about 40% fewer second opinions, and reporting time fell by about 20%.
studies.limitation: Only 4 pathologists, a small cohort and a sequential, non-randomized design.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted cancer diagnosis improves the efficiency of pathologists in prostatic biopsies.
studies.source: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study
studies.ai_system: CAD4TB v6, Lunit INSIGHT v4.9.0, qXR v2
studies.finding: Three CAD systems and two expert radiologists read 2,812 migrant screening chest X-rays for TB. Against the microbiological reference, AUCs were 0.85 (Lunit), 0.75 (qXR) and 0.71 (CAD4TB); the CAD systems performed comparable to the radiologists' sensitivity (98.3%) and, except CAD4TB, specificity (13.7%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective data; microbiological reference not done in low-suspicion individuals.
studies.title: Diagnostic accuracy of three computer-aided detection systems for detecting pulmonary tuberculosis on chest radiography when used for screening: Analysis of an international, multicenter migrants screening study.

studies.design: Comparative diagnostic vignette study
studies.humans: 18 oral medicine/pathology specialists, 23 general dentists, 16 dental students
studies.finding: ChatGPT and humans gave differential diagnoses for 37 oral and maxillofacial lesions. Mean correct diagnoses were 64.86% for ChatGPT-3.5, 80.18% for ChatGPT-4, 86.64% for specialists, 24.32% for general dentists and 16.67% for students. ChatGPT-4 was judged comparable to specialists.
studies.limitation: Dental vignettes; ChatGPT accuracy depended heavily on case description quality.
studies.title: Accuracy and consistency of ChatGPT-3.5 and - 4 in providing differential diagnoses in oral and maxillofacial diseases: a comparative diagnostic performance analysis.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study with biopsy reference
studies.ai_system: Deep learning models on B-mode ultrasound
studies.finding: Grading hepatic steatosis on US against biopsy in a 52-patient test set. For S0 vs S1 or higher, radiologist AUCs ranged 0.49 to 0.84 versus 0.85 for the model; for S0-S1 vs S2-S3, 0.57 to 0.76 versus 0.73; for S2 or lower vs S3, 0.52 to 0.81 versus 0.67.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective test set (n = 52).
studies.title: Comparison of Radiologists and Deep Learning for US Grading of Hepatic Steatosis.

studies.design: Model development with prospective validation and reader assistance comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep Learning Assistant for Retinoblastoma Monitoring (DLA-RB)
studies.finding: Identification of active retinoblastoma on fundus images, prospectively validated on 139 eyes, where DLA-RB reached AUCs of 0.991 and 0.962. Combining ophthalmologists with DLA-RB significantly improved the accuracy of competent ophthalmologists and residents for both binary tasks.
studies.limitation: Reader numbers and accuracy figures with and without AI not reported in the abstract; small prospective sample.
studies.title: Automatic retinoblastoma screening and surveillance using deep learning.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study with and without AI
studies.finding: Residents read 200 radiographs for fractures; sensitivity improved from 58% without AI to 77% with AI (p < 0.001), and specificity went from 77% to 79% (p = 0.0653). AI alone had sensitivity 93% and specificity 77%.
studies.limitation: Only four residents and 200 radiographs, read retrospectively.
studies.title: AI-Assisted X-ray Fracture Detection in Residency Training: Evaluation in Pediatric and Adult Trauma Patients.

studies.design: Single-centre retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
studies.ai_system: Deep learning cervical spine fracture detection algorithm
studies.finding: AI and attending radiologists' original reports were compared for C-spine fracture detection on 2368 CT scans. AI sensitivity was 71.5% vs 88.2% for radiologists (p < 0.001), with specificity 98.6% vs 99.2%. AI detected 22/26 fractures missed by radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-centre study; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Diagnostic accuracy of an artificial intelligence algorithm versus radiologists for fracture detection on cervical spine CT.

studies.design: Reader study with and without AI, crossover with washout
studies.finding: Radiologists read 20 TOF-MRA studies for cerebral aneurysms with and without AI, and half of the cases had a false-positive AI finding. False-positive AI results significantly increased aneurysm suspicion (p = 0.01), and inexperienced readers recommended more intense follow-up (p = 0.005). Reading times were shorter with AI, for example 164.1 vs 228.2 s for inexperienced readers.
studies.limitation: Only 20 cases and 9 readers, with a deliberately enriched false-positive rate.
studies.title: Automation bias in AI-assisted detection of cerebral aneurysms on time-of-flight MR angiography.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-reader study with and without DL aid, one-month washout, plus standalone evaluation
studies.humans: 24 readers: 8 emergency physicians, 8 non-MSK radiologists, 8 MSK radiologists
studies.finding: Fracture detection on extremity radiographs. With DL aid, reader accuracy (AUC) increased by 0.047 (95% CI: 0.034, 0.061; p = 0.004) and sensitivity improved from 0.865 to 0.955, with reading time shortened by 7.1 s (27%) per exam; the model alone achieved accuracy 0.986, sensitivity 0.987, specificity 0.885.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study on 186 cases from a single institution; enriched test set rather than live care.
studies.title: Assessing the Potential of a Deep Learning Tool to Improve Fracture Detection by Radiologists and Emergency Physicians on Extremity Radiographs.

studies.design: Comparison of AI vs radiologist reads within lung cancer screening trial dataset
studies.finding: Negative misclassifications on 3678 baseline LDCTs against an expert panel. AI had 31 (0.8 %) NMs vs 407 (11.1 %) for radiologists; radiologists as first reader would have led to 12/102 (11.8 %) missed referrals vs 3/102 (2.9 %) for AI.
studies.limitation: Only negative misclassifications assessed at baseline; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Feasibility of AI as first reader in the 4-IN-THE-LUNG-RUN lung cancer screening trial: impact on negative-misclassifications and clinical referral rate.

studies.design: Comparative vignette study
studies.finding: LLMs and attending spine surgeons gave surgical plans for five written spine scenarios. LLM surgical decision accuracy was 20% versus 100% for the surgeons. The abstract reports no statistically significant difference between groups.
studies.limitation: Only five scenarios; the difference was not statistically significant.
studies.title: Comparative Analysis of Large Language Models and Spine Surgeons in Surgical Decision-Making and Radiological Assessment for Spine Pathologies.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on published thoracic radiology cases
studies.ai_system: 10 LLMs including Claude 3 Opus, ChatGPT 4, Gemini 1.5 Pro
studies.finding: On 124 Society of Thoracic Radiology cases, Claude 3 Opus had the highest diagnostic accuracy (70.29%), with several LLMs outperforming the radiologists (52.4% and 41.1%). The LLMs received text history and findings, whereas the radiologists assessed the images.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists, on public cases with possible training-data contamination; the inputs differed between the LLMs and the radiologists.
studies.title: The Diagnostic Performance of Large Language Models and General Radiologists in Thoracic Radiology Cases: A Comparative Study.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre NLP model development with physician comparison
studies.finding: ASA Physical Status classification from pre-anesthesia evaluation summaries. ClinicalBigBird achieved an AUROC of 0.915 and outperformed board-certified anesthesiologists with specificity 0.901 vs. 0.897, precision 0.732 vs. 0.715 and F1-score 0.716 vs. 0.713 (all p <0.01).
studies.limitation: Single tertiary hospital, retrospective design, very small absolute differences, and the number of anesthesiologists is not stated.
studies.title: Comparison of NLP machine learning models with human physicians for ASA Physical Status classification.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to and assistance of ophthalmologists
studies.finding: Differentiating uveal melanoma from hemangioma and metastatic carcinoma. The model achieved an F1 score of 0.91, matching senior ophthalmologists, and improved the diagnostic accuracy of less experienced clinicians by 42%.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives no reader numbers or design details; single Asian dataset.
studies.title: A concept-based interpretable model for the diagnosis of choroid neoplasias using multimodal data.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with CBCT reference standard
studies.finding: For detecting periapical radiolucencies on 339 teeth, clinicians had higher tooth-level accuracy than Diagnocat (86.1% vs. 78.5%, p < .001) and greater sensitivity (65.3% vs. 47.9%, p < .001). Specificity was comparable (97.7% vs. 95.4%, p = .3).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only two clinicians.
studies.title: The detection of apical radiolucencies in periapical radiographs: A comparison between an artificial intelligence platform and expert endodontists with CBCT serving as the diagnostic benchmark.

studies.design: Cross-sectional paired diagnostic accuracy study on retrospective anonymized cases
studies.finding: ChatGPT-5 and an oral medicine specialist panel classified 262 cases as OLP, OLL or SCC-over-LP/LLP from histories and intraoral photographs. Overall accuracy was 84.7% for ChatGPT-5 vs 85.5% for OM specialists (McNemar P = .856). Malignant-risk features were identified in 88% vs 92% of SCC cases (P = .41).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset study without histopathology input; number of specialists not stated.
studies.title: A Multimodal Large Language Model Framework for Clinical Subtyping and Malignant Transformation Risk Prediction in Oral Lichen Planus: A Paired Comparison With Expert Clinicians.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre comparison of automated vs clinician CTA measurements
studies.finding: Maximum aortic diameter on pre- and postoperative CTA after FEVAR. ARVA identified the aortic wall accurately in 89% of studies, and among these its measurements were comparable to clinicians', with median absolute difference of 2.4 mm preoperatively and 1.6 mm postoperatively.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-centre study of 50 patients with only 2 clinicians; 11% of studies excluded for failed segmentation.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Sac Diameter Assessment for Complex Endovascular Aortic Repair.
studies.source: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists

studies.design: Model development with prospective test in 202 patients
studies.finding: PAN-VIQ quantified pancreatic cancer vascular invasion on CT. In prospective evaluation it outperformed junior radiologists and matched senior radiologists in accuracy and recall.
studies.limitation: Radiologist numbers and figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A clinically validated 3D deep learning approach for quantifying vascular invasion in pancreatic cancer.

studies.design: Vignette study comparing guideline-augmented LLM with community clinicians against expert gold standard
studies.finding: On 50 bipolar depression vignettes, the guideline-augmented model chose the expert-designated optimal treatment in 50.8% (95% CI 47.7-53.9%). Community clinicians identified the optimal choice for 23.1% (95% CI 15.7-30.5%) of vignettes on average (McNemar's p < 0.001 versus augmented model); the un-augmented model achieved 23.0%.
studies.limitation: Simulated vignettes; number of community clinicians not stated; 12.0% of model outputs included poor or contraindicated choices.
studies.title: Clinical decision support for bipolar depression using large language models.
studies.source: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology

studies.design: Retrospective two-institution model development with external testing compared against thoracic surgeons
studies.finding: Preoperative prediction of spread through air spaces in ground glass-predominant lung adenocarcinoma on CT. In the external testing set STAS-DL achieved an AUC of 0.82 and accuracy of 74%, superior to the physicians with an AUC of 0.68.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with a small external test set (123 patients) from a single external institution and only five surgeons.
studies.title: CT-Based Deep-Learning Model for Spread-Through-Air-Spaces Prediction in Ground Glass-Predominant Lung Adenocarcinoma.

studies.design: Retrospective batch analysis of 3316 consecutive CTPA scans
studies.finding: Detection of acute pulmonary embolism on CTPA in 3316 patients. AI sensitivity was 96.8% vs. 91.6% for the radiology report (p < 0.001) and specificity 99.9% vs. 99.7% (p = 0.035).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset design; reference standard built from discordant cases only.
studies.title: Retrospective batch analysis to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of a clinically deployed AI algorithm for the detection of acute pulmonary embolism on CTPA.

studies.design: Case-based comparison plus survey
studies.finding: Diagnosing six uveitis cases. Uveitis experts accurately diagnosed all cases (100%), compared with 66% for ChatGPT and 33% for Glass 1.0.
studies.limitation: Only six cases; number of experts not stated.
studies.title: Chatbots Vs. Human Experts: Evaluating Diagnostic Performance of Chatbots in Uveitis and the Perspectives on AI Adoption in Ophthalmology.

studies.design: Retrospective two-centre study with internal and external test cohorts
studies.ai_system: X-ray radiomics-based Support Vector Machine classifier
studies.finding: Classification of atypical cartilaginous tumour vs high-grade chondrosarcoma of long bones on X-rays. The classifier had 80%, 83%, 79% accuracy, sensitivity, specificity in the internal test cohort and 80%, 89%, 67% in the external test cohort, with no difference compared to the radiologists (p ≥ 0.617).
studies.limitation: Small retrospective sample (25 and 30 test cases) and only two radiologists.
studies.title: X-rays radiomics-based machine learning classification of atypical cartilaginous tumour and high-grade chondrosarcoma of long bones.

studies.design: Retrospective comparative study on deidentified intake data
studies.finding: Prediction of suicidal ideation with plan from intake chief complaint. At intake clinicians' average precision was 0.7 vs 0.6 for GPT-4, while sensitivity was 0.62 for GPT-4 vs 0.53 for clinicians; with suicide attempt history clinicians reached sensitivity 0.59 and precision 0.77 vs GPT-4 0.59 and 0.54. For future SI with plan with attempt history, clinicians had sensitivity 0.46 and precision 0.69 vs GPT-4 0.74 and 0.48.
studies.limitation: Only six clinicians and limited intake information from a single telehealth platform.
studies.title: Large Language Models Versus Expert Clinicians in Crisis Prediction Among Telemental Health Patients: Comparative Study.

studies.design: Mixed-method study including reader study of 18 dermoscopic images with and without AI
studies.ai_system: AI-based clinical decision support system for melanoma detection
studies.finding: Twenty-five PCPs assessed 18 dermoscopic images with and without AI support. Access to AI decision support increased physicians' diagnostic accuracy; usability SUS score was 84.8.
studies.limitation: Very small image set (18 images) and no accuracy figures reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Exploring the feasibility of an artificial intelligence based clinical decision support system for cutaneous melanoma detection in primary care - a mixed method study.
studies.source: Scandinavian journal of primary health care

studies.design: Model development with external video validation compared against surgeons
studies.finding: Intraoperative parathyroid gland recognition in endoscopic thyroidectomy videos. PTAIR 2.0 achieved AP50 of 92.1% and in the external validation cohort of 54 videos outperformed both junior and senior surgeons in identifying and tracking parathyroid glands (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective video-based evaluation; number of surgeons and their metrics not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Intraoperative AI-assisted early prediction of parathyroid and ischemia alert in endoscopic thyroid surgery.

studies.design: Multicenter development and external reader validation
studies.ai_system: TNVis deep learning 3D ultrasound video tool
studies.finding: For thyroid nodule diagnosis on ultrasound video, radiologists with TNVis reached an AUC of 0.79 compared with 0.66 without TNVis (p < 0.001) and 0.72 with partial assistance (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Number of radiologists and reading design not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: A deep learning based ultrasound diagnostic tool driven by 3D visualization of thyroid nodules.

studies.design: Randomised multimethod clinical vignette experiment
studies.ai_system: AI CDSS for intravenous-to-oral antibiotic switching, with explanations
studies.finding: Decisions on switching from intravenous to oral antibiotics across 12 vignettes. Completion times and many decisions were equivalent between standard care and CDSS, with clinicians able to identify and ignore incorrect advice. Where a difference appeared, the CDSS pushed clinicians towards not switching (odds ratio 0.13 [95% CI 0.03-0.50]; p=0.0031).
studies.limitation: Vignette-based study with a small, network-recruited sample.
studies.title: The impact of artificial intelligence-driven decision support on uncertain antimicrobial prescribing: a randomised, multimethod study.

studies.design: Pilot comparison on 80 real pediatric ED cases scored by two experts
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 1.5 Flash, Llama-3-8B, ChatGPT-4o mini
studies.humans: 23 physicians (10 PED physicians, 6 PED residents, 7 EM residents)
studies.finding: Primary and differential diagnosis for 80 real pediatric emergency cases, scored out of 80. ChatGPT-4o scored 72.5 and Gemini 1.5 Pro 62.75 versus 61.88 for PED physicians, with ChatGPT-4o better (p < 0.05); EM residents scored 43.75, worse than physicians and chatbots (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Pilot single-centre study; written case presentations rather than live care.
studies.title: Diagnostic efficacy of large language models in the pediatric emergency department: a pilot study.

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison against CT-based reference
studies.humans: Two orthopedic surgeons and one resident
studies.finding: Classification of pertrochanteric fractures as AO/OTA A1 or A2 on plain radiographs in 119 patients. Kappa vs CT gold standard: Observer 1 0.494, Observer 2 0.390, Observer 3 0.360, ChatGPT 0.420; ChatGPT accuracy, sensitivity and specificity were comparable to the human observers.
studies.limitation: Single reference rater, three human observers, single-centre retrospective data.
studies.title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Performance in Classifying Pertrochanteric Fractures Based on Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Osteosynthesefragen/Orthopedic Trauma Association (AO/OTA) Standards.

studies.design: Sequential unassisted then assisted reader study on prostate biopsy whole slide images
studies.finding: Eighteen pathologists read 610 prostate needle core biopsy WSIs without and then with Paige Prostate. With assistance, pathologists improved sensitivity and specificity across all histologic grades and tumor sizes, and PaPr correctly classified 100% of WSIs with corrected diagnoses.
studies.limitation: Simulated diagnostic practice with assisted read immediately after unassisted read; no specific sensitivity/specificity figures in abstract.
studies.title: Clinical Validation of Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Pathology Diagnosis Demonstrates Significant Gains in Diagnostic Accuracy in Prostate Cancer Detection.

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison on paediatric trauma radiographs from 878 patients
studies.humans: Pediatric radiologists, emergency physicians, senior and junior residents
studies.finding: The algorithm detected 174 of 182 fractures (sensitivity 95.6%, specificity 91.64%). This was close to pediatric radiologists (sensitivity 98.35%) and senior residents (95.05%) and above emergency physicians (81.87%) and junior residents (90.1%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset study; number of readers not stated.
studies.title: Comparison of diagnostic performance of a deep learning algorithm, emergency physicians, junior radiologists and senior radiologists in the detection of appendicular fractures in children.

studies.design: Experimental comparison of segmentation models vs human participants on laparoscopic images
studies.humans: 28 physicians, medical students and medical laypersons
studies.finding: Pancreas segmentation on laparoscopic images was compared between four ML models and 28 human participants. All four models outperformed at least 26 out of 28 human participants in pancreas segmentation.
studies.limitation: Human comparison limited to a single structure (pancreas) and a mixed cohort including students and laypersons; experimental image-based setting.
studies.title: Anatomy segmentation in laparoscopic surgery: comparison of machine learning and human expertise - an experimental study.

studies.design: Retrospective two-centre model development with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Multimodal AI combining DL suspicion levels and clinical parameters
studies.finding: Detection of clinically significant prostate cancer on biparametric MRI. No significant difference between multimodal AI and radiologist assessments (internal: 0.87 vs 0.88 AUC; external: 0.77 vs 0.75 AUC, both P > 0.05).
studies.limitation: Retrospective; radiologist comparison based on clinical PI-RADS reads, number of radiologists unclear.
studies.title: Multimodal AI Combining Clinical and Imaging Inputs Improves Prostate Cancer Detection.

studies.design: Retrospective validation of pathologists using AI vs original interpretations
studies.finding: Cervical ThinPrep cytology screening in 32,451 cases. Pathologists using AICyte had similar sensitivity to original interpretations (97.89% vs 97.89%) and higher specificity (16.19% vs 6.77%) for CIN2+, with average reading time of 22.23 seconds versus an approximated 180 seconds manually.
studies.limitation: Only two pathologists; comparator was original interpretations and manual time was an approximation.
studies.title: Assessment of Efficacy and Accuracy of Cervical Cytology Screening With Artificial Intelligence Assistive System.
studies.source: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc

studies.design: Model development with external validation and reader comparison
studies.finding: For detecting severe LV hypertrophy or dilated LV on chest X-rays, the model outperformed all 15 individual radiologists for the composite label. It achieved a sensitivity of 71% vs. 66% against the radiologists' consensus at a fixed specificity of 73%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; radiologists do not routinely assess this from CXR.
studies.title: Deep learning to detect left ventricular structural abnormalities in chest X-rays.

studies.design: National cohort model development with comparative testing against doctors
studies.finding: Prediction of postoperative in-hospital mortality in geriatric hip fracture patients. The AI application outperformed doctors in AUC (0.908 vs. 0.682, P <0.001).
studies.limitation: Number and experience of doctors and details of the comparison not described; retrospective data.
studies.title: Establishment and validation of an artificial intelligence web application for predicting postoperative in-hospital mortality in patients with hip fracture: a national cohort study of 52 707 cases.

studies.design: Simulated scenario comparison
studies.humans: Emergency medical technicians and emergency physicians
studies.finding: On 100 simulated triage scenarios, GPT-3.5 with RAG achieved a correct triage rate of 70%, versus 35% and 38% for EMTs and 50% and 47% for emergency physicians (p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Simulated scenarios from exam cases; small, unclear number of human comparators.
studies.title: Emergency Patient Triage Improvement through a Retrieval-Augmented Generation Enhanced Large-Scale Language Model.

studies.design: Cross-sectional vignette assessment
studies.humans: Gastroenterologists and colorectal surgeons with and without a CRC screening mobile app
studies.finding: On 10 CRC screening and surveillance vignette questions, ChatGPT had a mean of 4.5 total correct answers (overall 45%). This was significantly lower than physicians without the app [5.62 (95% CI: 5.32-5.92)] and with the app [7.71 (95% CI: 7.39-8.03); P < 0.001].
studies.limitation: Only 10 multiple-choice vignettes and an older model version.
studies.title: Colorectal Cancer Prevention: Is Chat Generative Pretrained Transformer (Chat GPT) ready to Assist Physicians in Determining Appropriate Screening and Surveillance Recommendations?

studies.design: Multi-center randomized clinical vignette study
studies.humans: Resident and attending physicians in family, internal or emergency medicine
studies.finding: Physicians diagnosed up to six clinical vignettes with GPT-4 plus conventional resources or conventional resources alone. Median diagnostic reasoning score per case was 76.3 percent with GPT-4 vs 73.7 percent with conventional resources (adjusted difference 1.6 percentage points, 95% CI -4.4 to 7.6; p=0.60). GPT-4 alone scored 15.5 percentage points (95% CI 1.5 to 29, p=0.03) higher than the conventional resources group.
studies.limitation: Preprint; small sample of 50 physicians using vignettes rather than real patients.
studies.title: Influence of a Large Language Model on Diagnostic Reasoning: A Randomized Clinical Vignette Study.
studies.source: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

studies.design: Model development with reader comparison and AI-assisted reading
studies.ai_system: Co-plane attention deep learning model for knee MRI
studies.finding: For classifying 12 knee abnormalities on MRI, the model's accuracy of 0.78 outperformed junior radiologists (accuracy 0.65) and was competitive with senior radiologists (accuracy 0.80). With model assistance, radiologists' accuracy improved significantly (p < 0.001) from 0.73 to 0.79 on average.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Learning co-plane attention across MRI sequences for diagnosing twelve types of knee abnormalities.

studies.design: Prospective model development with comparison against ophthalmologists
studies.finding: The system graded corneal fluorescein staining with accuracy 91.2%, recall 78.6% and F1-score 79.2%. It significantly outperformed junior doctors among three ophthalmologists rating the images.
studies.limitation: Only three ophthalmologists; human performance figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: AES-CSFS: an automatic evaluation system for corneal sodium fluorescein staining based on deep learning.

studies.design: Development and validation study on 30 CT scans with timing comparison
studies.finding: Planning patient-specific mandible-angle osteotomy cutting guides. Median planning time was 1 min and 38 s with the automated system vs 19 min and 37 s for an expert and 26 min and 39 s for a novice.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 30 patients; comparison limited to planning time, number of human planners unclear.
studies.title: Innovations in gender affirmation: AI-enhanced surgical guides for mandibular facial feminization surgery.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre model development with external validation
studies.finding: For predicting axillary lymph node metastasis on ultrasound, the DLRN achieved AUCs of 0.914, 0.929 and 0.952 in three external cohorts and outperformed five experienced radiologists in all cohorts.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; radiologist figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Deep learning radiomics based prediction of axillary lymph node metastasis in breast cancer.

studies.design: Two user studies of human-AI collaboration protocols
studies.ai_system: Diagnostic AI with and without explanations (XAI)
studies.finding: Readers evaluated 240 knee MRI and 20 ECG cases under different collaboration configurations. AI support was useful, but XAI had a null or detrimental effect; AI-first protocols gave higher accuracy than human-first protocols and than humans or AI alone.
studies.limitation: Small samples; no numeric results reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Rams, hounds and white boxes: Investigating human-AI collaboration protocols in medical diagnosis.

studies.design: Retrospective two-institution model development with reader comparison
studies.ai_system: Integrated DL, radiomics and clinical/US model
studies.finding: For central lymph node metastasis in PTC, the integrated model (AUC 0.841) reduced the missed CLNM rate from 57.89% and 44.74% (junior and senior radiologists) to 27.63%, and unnecessary CLND from 29.87% and 27.27% to 18.18%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: An integrated model incorporating deep learning, hand-crafted radiomics and clinical and US features to diagnose central lymph node metastasis in patients with papillary thyroid cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to doctors
studies.finding: Risk stratification of invasive lung adenocarcinoma on thin-slice CT. The model achieved 77.6% accuracy for grading and outperformed senior doctors, whose results are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Human performance and the number of doctors are not reported in the abstract; retrospective design.
studies.title: An ensemble deep learning model for risk stratification of invasive lung adenocarcinoma using thin-slice CT.

studies.design: Multicentre reader study of AI-synthesised thin-slice CT
studies.ai_system: Convolutional-Transformer deep learning model generating synthetic thin-slice CT
studies.finding: Radiologists diagnosed community-acquired pneumonia and detected lung nodules. Accuracy with synthetic thin-slice CT surpassed thick-slice CT (p < 0.05) and matched real thin-slice CT (p > 0.99); nodule sensitivity also exceeded thick-slice CT (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Only four radiologists; actual accuracy figures not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Spatial resolution enhancement using deep learning improves chest disease diagnosis based on thick slice CT.

studies.design: Multicentre study with external and prospective testing sets and a reader assistance analysis
studies.ai_system: Fully automated pipeline system (RefineNet + Xception + PPM)
studies.finding: Classification of single-mass breast lesions on contrast-enhanced mammography. The FAPS achieved AUCs of 0.947, 0.940 and 0.891 and classified faster than radiologists (6 s vs 3 min). FAPS assistance improved radiologist performance, with BI-RADS 4 adjusted in 12.4% and 13.3% of patients.
studies.limitation: The size of the improvement in radiologist accuracy is not quantified in the abstract; only six readers took part.
studies.title: Deep learning-enabled fully automated pipeline system for segmentation and classification of single-mass breast lesions using contrast-enhanced mammography: a prospective, multicentre study.

studies.design: Proof-of-concept machine learning study compared with inter-rater accuracy
studies.finding: For dystonia scoring on the Dyskinesia Impairment Scale, model-rater MAEs ranged from 0.21 ± 0.15 for arm dystonia to 0.14 ± 0.10 for leg dystonia. Inter-rater MAEs were 0.21 ± 0.22 and 0.16 ± 0.20, respectively.
studies.limitation: Small dataset (34 individuals) and only three raters.
studies.title: Towards automated video-based assessment of dystonia in dyskinetic cerebral palsy: A novel approach using markerless motion tracking and machine learning.

studies.design: Cross-sectional image evaluation with pathologist comparison
studies.finding: GPT-4 achieved overall accuracy of 0.64 identifying tumour and tissue origin, and 0.88 distinguishing low- from high-grade dysplasia. Its diagnostic accuracy in cancer was comparable to that of pathology residents.
studies.limitation: Small image set; pathologist figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Evaluating ChatGPT's diagnostic potential for pathology images.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader study
studies.finding: Appendicitis prediction in 68 validation patients with acute abdominal pain. ML AUROCs were 0.919 without and 0.923 with laboratory results; ED physicians achieved 0.894, 0.826 and 0.791 without labs and 0.923, 0.892 and 0.859 with labs.
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective data, small validation set and only three physicians.
studies.title: Machine-learning based prediction of appendicitis for patients presenting with acute abdominal pain at the emergency department.
studies.source: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES

studies.design: Prospective multicentre diagnostic study in 4 hospitals
studies.ai_system: Deep multimodal fusion network (clinical close-up + HFUS images)
studies.humans: General practitioners, general dermatologists, HFUS-specialised dermatologists
studies.finding: Classifying skin diseases on 422 prospective cases. In binary classification DMFN AUC 0.876 beat GPs (0.651) and general dermatologists (0.838) and was near HFUS dermatologists (0.891). In 17-class classification DMFN AUC 0.707 beat general dermatologists (0.514) and HFUS dermatologists (0.640).
studies.limitation: Number of human raters not stated; conducted in China only.
studies.title: A deep learning fusion network trained with clinical and high-frequency ultrasound images in the multi-classification of skin diseases in comparison with dermatologists: a prospective and multicenter study.

studies.design: Comparative multiple-choice test study
studies.finding: 20 clinical cases on oral lesion diagnosis in multiple-choice format. Median LLM score was 50.0 vs 65.0 for residents, with no significant difference (p = 0.211).
studies.limitation: Small 20-question MCQ test at a single institution.
studies.title: Comparing Artificial Intelligence and Senior Residents in Oral Lesion Diagnosis: A Comparative Study.

studies.design: Retrospective comparative study
studies.finding: ChatGPT-4o and radiologists evaluated brain MRI of 46 pathologically confirmed tumors. ChatGPT-4o achieved 56.8% and 29.5% for differential and most likely diagnoses versus 93.2-90.9% and 70.5-65.9% for radiologists (p<0.005).
studies.limitation: Small sample of 46 patients and only two radiologists.
studies.title: ChatGPT-4o's Performance in Brain Tumor Diagnosis and MRI Findings: A Comparative Analysis with Radiologists.

studies.design: Multicenter study with reader performance study
studies.ai_system: Deep learning LVO detection software on CTA
studies.finding: AI detected LVO on CTA in 595 stroke patients with sensitivity 0.858 and specificity 0.969. Reading with AI assistance improved residents' sensitivity by 4.0% and AUROC by 0.024 (P<0.001).
studies.limitation: Only four resident readers; retrospective image reading.
studies.title: Automated detection of large vessel occlusion using deep learning: a pivotal multicenter study and reader performance study.

studies.design: Multicenter model development with external validation and interpretation test against cardiologists
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model on single Lead I ECG
studies.finding: Detection of left heart abnormalities from ECG. In interpretation tests the model's accuracy was 78.3% for low EF and 68.3% for LVH; compared with cardiologists reading 12-lead ECGs, the model was superior for LVH and similar for low EF.
studies.limitation: Retrospective data; cardiologists' accuracy figures not reported in the abstract; small reader group.
studies.title: Deep Learning Models for Predicting Left Heart Abnormalities From Single-Lead Electrocardiogram for the Development of Wearable Devices.
studies.source: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society

studies.design: Retrospective model development with external validation
studies.finding: Model predicted post-repair rotator cuff re-tear from 62 preoperative variables with accuracy of 96.93% internally and 79.55% on an external dataset of 518 cases. The abstract states the model outperforms human doctors but reports no doctor figures.
studies.limitation: Doctors' performance and number of doctors are not reported; this is a model-development paper.
studies.title: Re-tear after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair can be predicted using deep learning algorithm.

studies.design: Retrospective comparative study
studies.finding: On 117 knee radiographs, ChatGPT-4o's detailed OA grading accuracy (35%) was substantially lower than surgeons' (89.6%). Surgeon interrater reliability was excellent (ICC 0.78-0.91) versus poor for ChatGPT-4o (ICC 0.16-0.28).
studies.limitation: Small sample, two surgeons only, single dataset.
studies.title: High identification and positive-negative discrimination but limited detailed grading accuracy of ChatGPT-4o in knee osteoarthritis radiographs.
studies.source: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA

studies.design: Survey-based reader comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep learning alveolar crestal height application
studies.finding: Classifying severe vs non-severe periodontal bone loss on 35 ACH measures, dental professionals accurately identified between 35-87% of teeth with severe disease, whereas the AI application achieved 82-87% accuracy.
studies.limitation: Survey-based design with small image set; dental rather than physician readers.
studies.title: Evaluation by dental professionals of an artificial intelligence-based application to measure alveolar bone loss.

studies.design: Vignette study comparing GPT-4 with physician consensus on diagnosis and triage, with race/ethnicity variation
studies.finding: On 45 clinical vignettes, correct diagnosis was 97.8% (44/45) for GPT-4 and 91.1% (41/45) for physicians (P=.38). Triage appropriateness was 66.7% (30/45) for both (P=.99).
studies.limitation: Only 45 typical vignettes and 3 physicians assessed as a consensus; simulated cases.
studies.title: The Accuracy and Potential Racial and Ethnic Biases of GPT-4 in the Diagnosis and Triage of Health Conditions: Evaluation Study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre development/validation with multicase multireader study
studies.ai_system: AI system for cardiac amyloidosis-suggestive uptake on scintigraphy
studies.finding: In a multireader study of 200 scintigraphy cases, five physicians had mean AUC 0·946 (95% CI 0·924-0·967), inferior to AI AUC 0·997 (0·991-1·000), p=0·0040.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; reader study small (5 readers, 200 cases); industry funded.
studies.title: Diagnosis and prognosis of abnormal cardiac scintigraphy uptake suggestive of cardiac amyloidosis using artificial intelligence: a retrospective, international, multicentre, cross-tracer development and validation study.

studies.design: Post hoc analysis of trial biopsies comparing ML pathology with pathologists
studies.finding: For NASH resolution endpoint with semaglutide 0.4 mg vs placebo, pathologists detected 58.5% vs. 22.0% (p < 0.0001) and ML 36.9% vs. 11.9% (p = 0.0015). ML continuous scores detected a fibrosis reduction (p = 0.0099) not detected by pathologists.
studies.limitation: Post hoc analysis of a trial subset; no direct accuracy reference standard.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence scoring of liver biopsies in a phase II trial of semaglutide in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.

studies.design: CADx development with a two-phase benchmark reader study on image and video test sets (without, then with CADx)
studies.ai_system: CADx system for Barrett's neoplasia pretrained on GastroNet
studies.humans: 44 general endoscopists plus 10 international BE experts
studies.finding: The task was characterizing Barrett's neoplasia on NBI images and videos. Stand-alone CADx sensitivity and specificity were 100% and 98% for images and 93% and 96% for videos, and CADx outperformed unassisted general endoscopists in sensitivity (P = .04). With CADx assistance, endoscopists' sensitivity increased from 84% to 96% and specificity from 90% to 98% (P < .001), and CADx performance was similar to that of BE experts.
studies.limitation: Fixed sequential phases (without then with CADx) on an enriched test set of 90 cases, which may introduce learning effects.
studies.title: Computer-aided diagnosis improves characterization of Barrett's neoplasia by general endoscopists (with video).

studies.design: Multicentre blinded multi-case multi-reader study with washout
studies.ai_system: GE Healthcare Critical Care Suite pneumothorax algorithm
studies.humans: Frontline acute care clinicians from six specialties, varying seniority
studies.finding: 18 clinicians read 395 chest X-rays for pneumothorax with and without AI. Sensitivity rose from 66.8% unaided to 78.1% aided (p=0.002), specificity 93.9% to 95.8% (p=0.247); juniors improved from 56.0% to 77.7%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective online reader study on an enriched image set, not live care.
studies.title: Evaluation of the impact of artificial intelligence-assisted image interpretation on the diagnostic performance of clinicians in identifying pneumothoraces on plain chest X-ray: a multi-case multi-reader study.

studies.design: Video-based reader study, endoscopists with and without AI support
studies.ai_system: AI algorithm for intraprocedural submucosal blood vessel detection
studies.finding: Endoscopists detected submucosal blood vessels in 101 video clips (200 vessels) with and without AI. Vessel detection rate increased from 56.4% to 72.4% with AI, and detection time dropped from 6.7 seconds to 5.2 seconds.
studies.limitation: Test on standardized video clips rather than live procedures; authors note clinical trials are needed.
studies.title: Use of artificial intelligence in submucosal vessel detection during third-space endoscopy.

studies.design: Simulated patient study with clinical performance examination and written vignettes
studies.finding: ChatGPT and 12 doctors managed 12 simulated emergency cases. ChatGPT scored higher on history-taking (3.91 vs 2.67, P<.001) and empathy (4.50 vs 1.75, P<.001), with no significant difference in clinical accuracy; simulated patients rated ChatGPT higher for concern reduction (4.33 vs 3.58, P=.04).
studies.limitation: Small simulated study with 12 doctors and a single expert rater.
studies.title: Clinical Performance and Communication Skills of ChatGPT Versus Physicians in Emergency Medicine: Simulated Patient Study.

studies.design: Retrospective multireader multicase study with eye tracking
studies.ai_system: FDA-approved, CE-marked AI decision support system for mammography
