studies.finding: Reading 150 screening mammograms unaided and with AI support. Mean AUC was higher with AI (0.97 vs 0.93 unaided; P < .001), with no evidence of difference in sensitivity (81.7% vs 87.2%; P = .06), specificity (89.0% vs 91.1%; P = .46) or reading time.
studies.limitation: Enriched retrospective reader study setting, not live screening.
studies.title: Influence of AI Decision Support on Radiologists' Performance and Visual Search in Screening Mammography.

studies.design: Cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study with internal and external test sets
studies.ai_system: ResNet50-based multi-instance deep learning model on oral photographs
studies.finding: A deep learning model identified stage II to IV periodontitis from a single frontal oral image with AUROC = 0.93 internally and 0.93 externally. The abstract reports the model showed better sensitivity and specificity than clinicians with different skill levels, without giving clinician figures.
studies.limitation: Clinician comparison figures and number of clinicians not reported in the abstract; single-country population.
studies.title: Deep Learning Photo Processing for Periodontitis Screening.

studies.design: Reader study of 70 suspicious breast masses on ultrasound; experienced and less-experienced radiologist, AI alone, and less-experienced reader with AI
studies.humans: One radiologist with 15 years' experience and one with 1 year
studies.finding: For BI-RADS assessment of 70 breast masses, AUC was 0.888 for the experienced reader, 0.693 for Koios DS alone, and 0.512 for the less-experienced reader without guidance. With Koios alone the less-experienced reader reached an AUC of 0.655, and with Koios plus elasticity 0.679.
studies.limitation: Only two readers and 70 lesions at a single setting.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence in Diagnostic Breast Ultrasound: A Comparative Analysis of Decision Support Among Radiologists With Various Levels of Expertise.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of three LLMs and doctors interpreting 7 CTG images, rated by blinded experts
studies.humans: Five senior and five junior doctors
studies.finding: ChatGPT-4o scored 77.86, outperforming Gemini Advanced (57.14), Copilot (47.29) and junior doctors (61.57). Senior doctors scored 80.43, with no statistically significant difference from ChatGPT-4o (p > 0.05).
studies.limitation: Only seven CTG images and subjective Likert ratings.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-large language models (AI-LLMs) for reliable and accurate cardiotocography (CTG) interpretation in obstetric practice.

studies.design: Comparison of LLM vs local clinician answers to community health worker questions, expert-rated
studies.ai_system: Gemini-2, GPT-4o, o3-mini, Deepseek R1, Meditron-70B
studies.finding: 524 question-answer pairs from Rwandan community health workers were rated on 11 metrics. All LLMs significantly outperformed local clinicians (P < 0.001), with Gemini-2 surpassing local general practitioners by an average of 0.83 points on every metric. Gemini-2 and GPT-4o scored 4.49 and 4.48 out of 5.
studies.limitation: Written answers rated on a rubric rather than patient outcomes; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Large language models for frontline healthcare support in low-resource settings.

studies.design: Prospective shadow evaluation (NCT06779292)
studies.finding: Emergency neurological diagnosis in 433 prospectively enrolled patients. Model diagnostic accuracy was 79.4% versus 65.4% for emergency physicians (p < 0.001), and blinded experts rated model examination and treatment recommendations as more comprehensive, accurate and applicable (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Shadow mode under simulated clinical conditions; model did not affect care; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Development and prospective shadow evaluation of a domain-specific large language model for emergency neurological diagnosis.

studies.design: Randomized 4-arm experiment, 10 clinical vignettes
studies.finding: Physicians diagnosing vignettes with AI under different responsibility structures: dynamic responsibility improved accuracy (mean 0.717 vs 0.592 control; P=.004). Full responsibility gave no improvement (0.596 vs 0.592), and equal responsibility showed lower accuracy (0.496 vs 0.592; P=.07) with poorer calibration.
studies.limitation: Simulated vignettes on an online platform; compares responsibility structures rather than AI vs no AI.
studies.title: Impact of Responsibility Allocation Structures on Diagnostic Quality in AI-Assisted Diagnosis: Randomized Controlled Experiment.

studies.design: Multicenter prospective study (NCT07117266)
studies.finding: Chest radiograph reporting in 296 patients. AI assistance significantly improved report quality scores and reduced interpretation time by 18.3% compared with standard practice.
studies.limitation: Quality score values and reader numbers not reported in abstract; modest sample.
studies.title: A DeepSeek-powered AI system for automated chest radiograph interpretation in clinical practice.

studies.design: Prospective randomized multi-reader multi-case crossover trial (NCT07027605)
studies.ai_system: Machine learning prognostic tool for CRLM
studies.finding: Prediction of 3-year mortality in 166 retrospective colorectal liver metastases cases. Assistance improved AUC (mean difference 0.091; 95% CI 0.001-0.181; P = 0.048) and reduced decision time (2.53 vs. 3.04 minutes), with greatest benefit for junior to mid-level surgeons.
studies.limitation: Retrospective cases in a reader study; effect CI near zero; small reader number; exploratory.
studies.title: Impact of an AI prognostic tool on clinician performance in colorectal liver metastases.

studies.design: Pragmatic diagnostic accuracy study (CTRI/2022/10/046283)
studies.finding: Diabetic retinopathy screening of 600 people. For RDR, the non-ophthalmologist-led model had 95.8% sensitivity and 93.1% specificity, while the offline AI model had 93.3% sensitivity and 85.1% specificity with 38% ungradability versus 8%.
studies.limitation: Different populations/screening arms rather than paired comparison; non-physician screeners; wide CIs.
studies.title: Evaluation of non-ophthalmologist-led and offline AI-assisted models for diabetic retinopathy screening in India: a pragmatic diagnostic accuracy study.

studies.design: Prospective DECIDE-AI stage 1 evaluation comparing two parallel emergency department units
studies.ai_system: SHAKED multi-LLM clinical decision support system
studies.finding: Over 4 weeks with 1,138 patients, one emergency unit used SHAKED and one followed routine rotations. ED length of stay did not differ (4.9 h in both, P = 0.99), and there was a non-significant trend toward shorter consultation cycle time (-9.4 min, P = 0.077); adoption declined from 68% to 30%.
studies.limitation: Non-randomised, single-centre, 4-week early-stage evaluation with declining adoption.
studies.title: Prospective evaluation of a large language model clinical decision support system in the emergency department.

studies.design: Multisite pre/post quality improvement study
studies.ai_system: AI-informed ED triage clinical decision support
studies.finding: Across 174,648 ED visits, high-acuity identification of patients requiring critical care rose from 78.8% to 83.1% (P<0.001) after implementation, with no change in emergency surgery identification (41.2% to 39.2%; P=0.16). Nurses with high agreement with the CDS performed better than the AI alone, whereas low-agreement nurses performed worse.
studies.limitation: Non-randomized pre/post design susceptible to confounding; industry funded; nurses not physicians.
studies.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Based Triage Decision Support on Emergency Department Care.

studies.design: Prospective silent validation comparing algorithm-supported physician decisions with actual clinical decisions
studies.ai_system: Longitudinal ML model predicting delayed cerebral ischemia
studies.humans: 3 independent research physicians vs treating clinicians
studies.finding: Physicians with algorithm support made DCI monitoring and diagnostic decisions for 63 SAH patients (794 assessments), compared with actual clinical decisions. Increased neurologic assessment orders were 466 with algorithm support vs 629 without, false positives were reduced by 164 (P<0.01) with similar true positives and false negatives, and additional diagnostic orders were 128 vs 153.
studies.limitation: Silent validation: research physicians' decisions did not affect care and were compared with different (treating) clinicians; small sample of 3 physicians and 63 patients.
studies.title: Silent Validation of a Longitudinal Model for Predicting Delayed Cerebral Ischemia in Real Time after Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.

studies.design: Blinded comparison of ChatGPT and consultant answers to case-based questions
studies.finding: On 41 case-based ORL questions rated on a 6-point Likert scale, ratings in all categories were significantly higher for ORL consultants (P<.001). Consultants identified ChatGPT as the source correctly in 98.4% (121/123) of cases.
studies.limitation: Textbook and exam questions, rated by the consultants themselves; small question set.
studies.title: ChatGPT Versus Consultants: Blinded Evaluation on Answering Otorhinolaryngology Case-Based Questions.

studies.design: Retrospective simulation of AI-physician collaboration strategies on chest X-rays
studies.ai_system: Deep learning ARDS detection model on chest X-ray
studies.finding: Identification of ARDS findings on chest X-rays. AI-first with deferral to physician achieved accuracy 0.869, physician-first deferring to AI 0.824, physician alone 0.808 and AI alone 0.847.
studies.limitation: Collaboration strategies were simulated rather than tested with physicians interacting with AI live; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Collaborative strategies for deploying artificial intelligence to complement physician diagnoses of acute respiratory distress syndrome.

studies.design: Prospective multi-reader study with and without AI software
studies.humans: Four novice readers, expert reference radiologist
studies.finding: PI-RADS scoring agreement with an expert on 200 prostate mpMRI scans. Kappa without vs with AI changed from 0.673 to 0.736 (Reader 1), 0.628 to 0.483 (Reader 2), 0.603 to 0.292 (Reader 3) and 0.586 to 0.613 (Reader 4).
studies.limitation: Only four novice readers at a single institution with inconsistent effects.
studies.title: Bridging the experience gap in prostate multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging using artificial intelligence: A prospective multi-reader comparison study on inter-reader agreement in PI-RADS v2.1, image quality and reporting time between novice and expert readers.

studies.design: Retrospective cohort with web-based clinician survey on images
studies.ai_system: Neural network for tympanic membrane image classification
studies.finding: Classification of pediatric tympanic membrane images as normal, nonpurulent or purulent effusion. On 22 endoscopic images, 39 clinicians averaged 65.0% accuracy while the model achieved 95.5%.
studies.limitation: Very small 22-image test set for the human comparison; single tertiary center.
studies.title: "Human vs Machine" Validation of a Deep Learning Algorithm for Pediatric Middle Ear Infection Diagnosis.
studies.source: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery

studies.design: Retrospective fully crossed multi-reader multi-case study, with and without AI
studies.finding: Fifteen readers assessed 340 radiographic exams for traumatic fractures. With AI, patient-wise sensitivity increased from 72% to 80% and specificity from 81% to 85% (P < .05), with no significant difference in reading time.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study on a balanced, enriched dataset, not live care.
studies.title: Improving traumatic fracture detection on radiographs with artificial intelligence support: a multi-reader study.

studies.design: Image classification comparison of GPT-4V with blinded experts
studies.humans: CLE experts (two surgeons and one pathologist)
studies.finding: On 139 confocal laser endomicroscopy images classified as SCC or healthy mucosa, GPT-4 accuracy was 71.2%. Human experts achieved an accuracy of 88.5%.
studies.limitation: Images from only 5 patients and a small curated image set.
studies.title: Diagnosis of malignancy in oropharyngeal confocal laser endomicroscopy using GPT 4.0 with vision.
studies.source: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

studies.design: Collective intelligence analysis of physician and LLM differential diagnoses on 2,133 vignettes
studies.finding: Open-ended diagnosis of 2,133 text-based case vignettes. Hybrid collectives of physicians and LLMs outperformed single physicians, physician collectives, single LLMs and LLM ensembles.
studies.limitation: Text vignettes only, with aggregated rather than interactive human-AI collaboration; no numerical results in the abstract.
studies.title: Human-AI collectives most accurately diagnose clinical vignettes.
studies.source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of GPT-4V with clinicians on otoscopic images
studies.finding: Classifying 190 otoscopic images into 4 middle ear diseases, GPT-4V achieved 82.1% accuracy, superior to certified pediatricians at 70.6% but trailing otolaryngologists at more than 95%.
studies.limitation: Web-based questionnaire on images from two Japanese centres, not real clinical workflow.
studies.title: Feasibility of Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Using GPT-4 Vision for the Classification of Middle Ear Disease: Qualitative Study and Validation.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-reader detection accuracy study with and without AI
studies.ai_system: Comprehensive deep learning model for non-contrast brain CT
studies.finding: Across 2848 brain CT scans, assisted vs unassisted radiologists had average AUC 0.79 vs 0.73 across 22 parent findings and 0.72 vs 0.68 across 189 child findings; the model alone had AUC 0.93 across 144 findings. Reading time was significantly reduced with assistance.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study outside live clinical workflow; data from a single private radiology group.
studies.title: Effects of a comprehensive brain computed tomography deep learning model on radiologist detection accuracy.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study on 53 Diagnosis Please cases
studies.finding: Differential diagnosis of complex neuroradiology cases. Radiologists outperformed the models on complete cases (48.0% vs 34.0% and 38.7%), while the models outperformed radiologists on text alone (34.0% and 44.7% vs 16.4%). Radiologists assisted by Gemini improved from 47.2% to 56.0% (P < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Small set of published teaching cases, with only three radiologists in the assisted arm.
studies.title: Comparison between multimodal foundation models and radiologists for the diagnosis of challenging neuroradiology cases with text and images.

studies.design: Reader competition with radiographs randomly split into AI-assisted and unassisted sets
studies.ai_system: Deep learning algorithm detecting normal findings and 13 chest radiograph abnormalities
studies.finding: On 100 chest radiographs, radiologists' average score was 597 (587-605) without AI and 619 (612-626) with AI (P < 0.001), and time fell from 3279 to 1926 s. AI-assisted reading performed better for some findings (e.g., pulmonary fibrosis AUC 0.950) while unaided reading was better for others such as nodule (0.923) and rib fracture (0.987).
studies.limitation: Only 100 radiographs split into different sets for each condition, in a competition setting rather than clinical practice.
studies.title: Deep Learning for Chest X-ray Diagnosis: Competition Between Radiologists with or Without Artificial Intelligence Assistance.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy study
studies.ai_system: Vision Transformer DL model on AS-OCT
studies.humans: Expert clinicians masked to the diagnosis
studies.finding: Differentiating OSSN from pterygium and pinguecula on 566 AS-OCT scans with biopsy-proven OSSN. The DL model had sensitivity of 86.4% and specificity of 93.2% versus 69.8% and 98.5% for expert graders, and an AUROC of 0.945 versus 0.688 (P < .001).
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective study with a small test set (62 eyes), and clinicians had no clinical images or data.
studies.title: Detection of Ocular Surface Squamous Neoplasia Using Artificial Intelligence With Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography.

studies.design: Prospective cross-sectional single-centre study comparing AI biometry software with junior radiologists, using a senior radiologist as reference
studies.finding: Across nine mid-trimester fetal biometric parameters, 90.65-96.11% of CUPID caliper placements needed no adjustment, versus 69.63-92.06% for junior radiologists. ICC with the senior radiologist was 0.843-0.990 for CUPID versus 0.306-0.937 for the juniors. MAE was 0.36-2.53 mm versus 0.64-8.13 mm.
studies.limitation: Single centre, with the senior radiologist used as the reference standard. The number of radiologists is not stated.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence assistance for fetal development: evaluation of an automated software for biometry measurements in the mid-trimester.

studies.design: Observer performance test with three assistance conditions
studies.ai_system: AI-CAD deep learning system for OCT
studies.finding: Subtyping central serous chorioretinopathy on 100 OCT images. The system achieved 99% AUC, outperforming all 66 ophthalmologists; ophthalmologists with probability score plus heatmap achieved the highest mean performance, and nonretina specialists reached expert-level performance.
studies.limitation: Reader study on 100 images from the same test source; reader metrics not given numerically in abstract.
studies.title: Developing and Evaluating an AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis System for Retinal Disease: Diagnostic Study for Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.

studies.design: Model development with test-set comparison against clinical experts
studies.ai_system: Dual AttentionUNet segmentation of bare-back images
studies.humans: Three clinical experts including a deputy chief physician
studies.finding: Classifying scoliosis from bare-back images in a 91-case test set. The model achieved an AUC of 0.93 for identifying scoliosis versus 0.92 for the deputy chief physician, and 0.95 versus 0.96 for severe scoliosis.
studies.limitation: Small single test set of 91 cases with only three expert comparators.
studies.title: Deep learning-assisted screening and diagnosis of scoliosis: segmentation of bare-back images via an attention-enhanced convolutional neural network.
studies.source: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research

studies.design: Diagnostic accuracy study on 50 test radiographs
studies.finding: Detecting supernumerary teeth on periapical radiographs. Faster R-CNN and YOLOv8 had precision of 0.95 and 0.99, and both AI systems outperformed the dental residents.
studies.limitation: Very small test set of 50 images; resident metrics not given in the abstract.
studies.title: Artificial intelligent recognition for multiple supernumerary teeth in periapical radiographs based on faster R-CNN and YOLOv8.
studies.source: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre observational study
studies.humans: Junior radiology residents on night shift
studies.finding: For post-traumatic ICH on head CT, AI sensitivity was 88.8% and specificity 92.1%, comparable to junior residents (sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 99.3%). Combined AI and resident sensitivity improved to 95.2% with overall accuracy 98.8%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-centre design; resident comparison only on a night-shift subset and combination was not a true assisted read.
studies.title: Real-Life Performance of a Commercially Available AI Tool for Post-Traumatic Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection on CT Scans: A Supportive Tool.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic model development with test and external validation
studies.finding: Preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in pancreatic cancer. Test cohort AUC was 0.815 for MTCN+ vs 0.640 for radiologist judgement, external validation AUC 0.854 vs 0.542. Around 40% of patients misdiagnosed by radiologists could be corrected.
studies.limitation: Small single-dataset cohort (363 patients); MTCN+ includes radiologist judgement as input; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: A deep-learning radiomics-based lymph node metastasis predictive model for pancreatic cancer: a diagnostic study.

studies.design: Comparison on 120 FRCR2A-style MCQs
studies.finding: Answering 120 radiology case-vignette exam questions. The residents scored 63.33 and 57.5% versus Bard 44.17%, Bing 53.33% and ChatGPT 45%.
studies.limitation: Only two residents and exam-style questions.
studies.title: Assessing the Capability of ChatGPT, Google Bard, and Microsoft Bing in Solving Radiology Case Vignettes.
studies.source: The Indian journal of radiology & imaging

studies.design: Reader study of physicians unaided vs aided by AI on chest X-rays
studies.ai_system: FDA-cleared deep learning chest X-ray abnormality detection system
studies.finding: Physicians detected abnormalities on chest X-rays with and without AI assistance. Aided physicians showed a difference in AUC of 0.101 (p < 0.001) versus unaided; the AI alone had AUC 0.976. Non-radiologists aided by AI were as accurate as radiologists and faster when aided.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study; number of readers not stated in abstract; vendor-developed system.
studies.title: Deep learning improves physician accuracy in the comprehensive detection of abnormalities on chest X-rays.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to clinician readers
studies.finding: Diagnosis of supraspinatus tears on shoulder MRI. The 2D CNN achieved AUCs of 0.921 and 0.882 on surgery and internal test sets, performing better than junior clinicians and equivalent to senior clinicians.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, small surgery test set (69 MRIs), clinician metrics not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Development and clinical validation of deep learning for auto-diagnosis of supraspinatus tears.
studies.source: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research

studies.design: Reader study of senior surgeons with and without AI against consensus reference
studies.finding: Interpretation of postoperative total knee arthroplasty X-rays. AI angle mean difference was 1.71° vs surgeon average 1.69°; AI assistance let surgeons gain 5% in accuracy and 12% in sensitivity for interface anomalies, with repeatability gain (Light's kappa +0.17).
studies.limitation: Number of surgeons not stated; reference dataset built by consensus of senior surgeons.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Radiographic Analysis Tool for Total Knee Arthroplasty.

studies.design: Reader study with sequential unaided then CADx-aided diagnosis
studies.ai_system: CADx for optical diagnosis of colorectal polyps, with or without confidence score
studies.finding: Endoscopists optically diagnosed 60 colorectal polyps before and after seeing CADx predictions. Diagnostic accuracy rose from 69.3% initial to 76.6% final (P < .001); CADx was used in 36.5% of disagreements and appropriate trust was 48.7%.
studies.limitation: Image-based experimental setting with sequential design, not live colonoscopy.
studies.title: Appropriate trust in artificial intelligence for the optical diagnosis of colorectal polyps: the role of human/artificial intelligence interaction.

studies.design: Randomized pre-post intervention vignette study
studies.finding: Physicians answered triage, risk and treatment questions on a video chest-pain vignette, then reconsidered after receiving GPT-4 advice. AI assistance led to a significant improvement in decision accuracy against guidelines without introducing or worsening race or gender bias; no figures are given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Preprint; single simulated vignette scenario with pre-post design.
studies.title: ChatGPT Influence on Medical Decision-Making, Bias, and Equity: A Randomized Study of Clinicians Evaluating Clinical Vignettes.
studies.source: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

studies.design: Diagnostic cross-sectional model development and validation with comparison to triage nurses
studies.finding: For eye emergency triage, the model achieved an AUC of 0.982 (95% CI, 0.966-0.998) and outperformed the triage nurses (P < .001). Nurse performance figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Comparator is nurses, not physicians; small external test (103 participants); nurse numbers not stated.
studies.title: EE-Explorer: A Multimodal Artificial Intelligence System for Eye Emergency Triage and Primary Diagnosis.

studies.design: Retrospective validation on UKLS trial baseline CT scans against expert panel reference standard and histological outcomes
studies.ai_system: Commercially available AI lung nodule software
studies.humans: Human readers of the UKLS trial
studies.finding: On 1252 UKLS baseline CT scans, AI and human reads were compared with a European expert panel reference standard. AI resulted in less misclassification than human reads, NPV 92·0 %(90·2 %-95·3 %); against histology AI detected all 31 baseline-round lung cancers, classifying one as negative, NPV 99·8 %(99·0 %-99·9 %).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset analysis; number of human readers and their own metrics not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Histological proven AI performance in the UKLS CT lung cancer screening study: Potential for workload reduction.

studies.design: Single-center retrospective reader study; LLMs vs radiologists, and radiologists with vs without LLM assistance
studies.finding: For diagnosing 228 focal liver lesions against histopathology, two-step ChatGPT-4o accuracy (78.9%) was similar to real-world reports (80.0%) and junior radiologists (78.9%-82.0%) but lower than middle-level radiologists (84.6%-85.5%). No incremental diagnostic value of ChatGPT-4o was observed for any radiologist (p-values, 0.63 to > 0.99).
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective design; LLM used report text rather than images.
studies.title: Large Language Models for Diagnosing Focal Liver Lesions From CT/MRI Reports: A Comparative Study With Radiologists.
studies.source: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective development with reader study
studies.finding: Identification of lymph node metastasis in oral squamous cell carcinoma on MRI. The model had AUC 0.81 in external validation and tied or exceeded average performance of general and specialized radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; reader numbers and radiologist metrics not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Diagnosis of lymph node metastasis in oral squamous cell carcinoma by an MRI-based deep learning model.

studies.design: Blinded comparison of GPT and neurologist answers to patient questions rated by neurologists and family members
studies.finding: Answering 14 questions on Alzheimer's disease prevention, treatment and care. Evaluator neurologists rated neurologist responses a mean 3.9 (SD 0.7) versus GPT responses 4.4 (SD 0.6; P<.001). Family members found no significant differences between GPT and neurologists.
studies.limitation: Only 14 questions and 4 respondent neurologists; subjective Likert ratings.
studies.title: Assessing the Role of the Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT) in Alzheimer's Disease Management: Comparative Study of Neurologist- and Artificial Intelligence-Generated Responses.

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective development with prospective cohort reader study
studies.finding: Predicting pathological response to neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy in NSCLC from CT. In the prospective cohort (n=50), NeoPred AUC 0.760 vs experts' mean AUC 0.720; with model assistance pooled expert AUC rose to 0.829 and accuracy to 0.820.
studies.limitation: Small prospective cohort (n=50) with wide confidence intervals; Chinese centres only.
studies.title: NeoPred: dual-phase CT AI forecasts pathologic response to neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy in NSCLC.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of AI, radiologist, and combination on contrast-enhanced liver MRI
studies.ai_system: Deep learning AI software for focal liver lesion detection and measurement
studies.finding: In 395 patients with 1149 focal liver lesions, AI plus radiologist outperformed radiologist alone in detection rate (0.894 vs. 0.825) and sensitivity (0.883 vs. 0.806). AI alone was more sensitive than radiologists for lesions <20 mm (0.848 vs. 0.788), with similar performance for lesions ≥20 mm (0.867 vs. 0.881, P = 0.671).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Based Approach for Identifying and Measuring Focal Liver Lesions on Contrast-Enhanced MRI.
studies.source: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader assistance assessment
studies.finding: Measuring unruptured intracranial aneurysm size on CTA. With model assistance, junior radiologists' ICC improved from 0.88 (95% CI: 0.80, 0.92) to 0.96 (95% CI: 0.92, 0.97), P < .001.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of junior radiologists not stated; measurement agreement only.
studies.title: Integrated Deep Learning Model for the Detection, Segmentation, and Morphologic Analysis of Intracranial Aneurysms Using CT Angiography.

studies.design: Prospective simulation study with vignettes
studies.finding: Diagnosis and classification of seizures and epilepsy in 37 vignettes. ChatGPT had sensitivity ≥96.9% but low specificity (33.3% for acute symptomatic vs unprovoked; 26.7% for epilepsy diagnosis), while human experts consistently outperformed ChatGPT with near-perfect accuracy.
studies.limitation: Small vignette set and only four clinicians; exploratory.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence (ChatGPT 4.0) vs. Human expertise for epileptic seizure and epilepsy diagnosis and classification in Adults: An exploratory study.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of LLM outputs with neurosurgeons on outpatient cases
studies.finding: On 338 CNS tumor outpatient cases, ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 exceeded 90 % accuracy in differential diagnosis with no significant difference from doctors, while Doubao was worse. For treatment advice, all models (ChatGPT-4o: 80.5 %; DeepSeek-R1: 79 %; Doubao: 71.3 %) were significantly lower than doctors.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of neurosurgeons and their accuracy figures not given.
studies.title: Clinical feasibility of AI Doctors: Evaluating the replacement potential of large language models in outpatient settings for central nervous system tumors.

studies.design: Vignette comparison with blinded ratings
studies.humans: Four orthopedic surgeons (two attendings, two trauma fellows)
studies.finding: Responses to 20 questions across five orthopedic ED scenarios were rated on a five-point Likert scale. AI answers were superior in completeness, helpfulness, specificity and overall quality with no difference in accuracy (p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Only 20 questions across five scenarios and four surgeons; simulated text scenarios.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence versus orthopedic surgeons as an orthopedic consultant in the emergency department.

studies.design: Model development with external and prospective validation compared with two clinicians
studies.finding: Classification of fresh versus old vertebral compression fractures on thoracolumbar CT. ResNet18 achieved AUC 0.89 in the external dataset and 0.87 in prospective validation, surpassing the two clinicians in both; clinicians' figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Only two clinicians and small validation sets (34 and 48 vertebrae); single institution.
studies.title: Deep learning model for automated detection of fresh and old vertebral fractures on thoracolumbar CT.
studies.source: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society

studies.design: Multicenter development and validation
studies.finding: Glaucoma screening and diagnosis across hospital tiers. Multi-Glau achieved AUC 0.9254 for screening, 0.8650 for pre-diagnosis and 0.9516 for definitive diagnosis, and improved ophthalmologists' performance.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives no quantitative data or reader count for the clinician comparison.
studies.title: A three-tier AI solution for equitable glaucoma diagnosis across China's hierarchical healthcare system.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with reader comparison and AI-referenced re-evaluation
studies.ai_system: Inception ResNet v2 thyroid FNA model
studies.finding: On 1031 thyroid FNA image patches, AI accuracy was 99.71% vs 88.91% for average expert cytopathologists. After referring to AI results, expert accuracy was 96%, 95%, and 96% and diagnostic agreement rose from 0.64 to 0.84.
studies.limitation: Retrospective patch-level evaluation; number of cytopathologists not clearly stated.
studies.title: Improved Diagnostic Accuracy of Thyroid Fine-Needle Aspiration Cytology with Artificial Intelligence Technology.
studies.source: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to residents
studies.finding: Delineation of laryngeal cancer boundaries on endoscopic images. No significant differences between the model and the two residents on DSC (p = 0.06) and IoU (Senior vs. SegMENT-Plus, p = 0.13; Junior vs. SegMENT-Plus, p = 1.00).
studies.limitation: Only two residents as comparators; retrospective image data.
studies.title: Real-Time Laryngeal Cancer Boundaries Delineation on White Light and Narrow-Band Imaging Laryngoscopy with Deep Learning.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study with simulated AI utilization scenarios
studies.ai_system: Commercial AI computer-aided detection tool for LDCT
studies.finding: LDCT lung cancer screening in 366 individuals. Versus no AI (recall 22.1%, per-nodule sensitivity 64.2%, specificity 88.8%), AI as assistant raised recall to 30.3% and lowered specificity to 81.1% with no sensitivity change (64.8%); AI as prescreener lowered recall (20.8%) and time and raised specificity (90.3%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective with simulated scenarios; five readers.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence for Low-Dose CT Lung Cancer Screening: Comparison of Utilization Scenarios.

studies.design: Model development with reader study of novice dentists with and without assistance
studies.finding: On 800 periapical radiographs, ConvNeXt assistance increased novice dentists' average AUC from 0.88 to 0.94 and ResNet34 to 0.91. ConvNeXt reduced average diagnostic time from 178.8 min to 141.9 min.
studies.limitation: Only three readers, single dataset.
studies.title: A comparative analysis of deep learning models for assisting in the diagnosis of periapical lesions in periapical radiographs.

studies.design: Secondary analysis of knee radiographs read by physicians and ChatGPT
studies.humans: One emergency physician and one radiologist
studies.finding: On 111 knee radiographs (29 CT-confirmed tibial plateau fractures), AUC was 0.72 for the EP, 0.75 for the radiologist, 0.61 for ChatGPT-4 and 0.74 for ChatGPT-4o. Physicians significantly outperformed ChatGPT-4, while ChatGPT-4o showed no significant difference from physicians.
studies.limitation: Only two physician readers and small sample.
studies.title: Diagnostic performance of ChatGPT in tibial plateau fracture in knee X-ray.

studies.design: Retrospective observational model development and validation against expert raters
studies.ai_system: U-Net plus Keypoint R-CNN deep learning measurement system
studies.finding: Automated measurement of sagittal pelvic parameters on 1,011 lumbar radiographs. Interclass CCs comparing the AI model to ground truth ranged from 0.96 to 0.99, outperforming experienced orthopedic surgeons.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset study with ground truth from one specialist and two comparator raters.
studies.title: Automated measurement of pelvic parameters using convolutional neural network in complex spinal deformities: overcoming challenges in coronal deformity cases.
studies.source: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society

studies.design: Multicenter cross-sectional validation study
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model for small bowel capsule endoscopy
studies.finding: Detection of Crohn's ulcers and erosions in 259 capsule exams. Standard-of-care reading had 69.6% sensitivity, 99.4% specificity and 88.8% accuracy, while AI-assisted reading had 90.2% sensitivity, 84.4% specificity and 86.5% accuracy; detection yield was superior (P < .001) with median reporting time of 172 seconds.
studies.limitation: Number of readers not stated; gain in sensitivity came with lower specificity and PPV.
studies.title: AI-Assisted Capsule Endoscopy for Detection of Ulcers and Erosions in Crohn's Disease: A Multicenter Validation Study.
studies.source: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

studies.design: Retrospective model development compared to manual clinician assessment
studies.ai_system: Support vector machine hip classification model
studies.humans: An orthopedic resident and a pediatric orthopedic surgeon
studies.finding: Classification of hip condition by migration percentage on 88 pelvic radiographs in children with cerebral palsy. The model achieved overall accuracy of 92.898 %, and there were no significant differences between the model's MP measurements and those of the clinicians.
studies.limitation: Small dataset and only two clinician comparators.
studies.title: Machine learning-assisted classification of hip conditions in pediatric cerebral palsy patients using migration percentage measurements.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective external validation with reader study (with vs without AI)
studies.ai_system: Upgraded deep learning model for ileocolic intussusception on pediatric abdominal radiographs
studies.finding: Screening for ileocolic intussusception on pediatric abdominal radiographs. The AI model achieved sensitivity 81.7%, specificity 81.7% and AUC 86.2% in external validation, while unassisted radiologists had overall AUC 64%, sensitivity 49.7%, specificity 77.1%. With AI assistance radiologists' specificity improved to 93% (+15.9%; P<.001) and AUC to 79.2% (+15.2%; P=.05).
studies.limitation: Only 3 readers and small external datasets in a retrospective design.
studies.title: External Validation of an Upgraded AI Model for Screening Ileocolic Intussusception Using Pediatric Abdominal Radiographs: Multicenter Retrospective Study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional multiple-choice knowledge test comparing LLMs with neurologists
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-4.0, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3.5, Perplexity, Perplexity Pro
studies.humans: 37 neurology specialists and 79 neurology residents in Turkey
studies.finding: Twenty multiple-choice questions on multiple sclerosis diagnosis, treatment and management were given to neurologists and AI platforms. Specialists scored 12.05 ± 4.01 correct on average, residents 9.08 ± 3.41, and specialists active in MS clinics 17.67 ± 1.75. AI platforms scored between 14 and 19 out of 20, with an average of 17.0 ± 1.79.
studies.limitation: Only 20 multiple-choice questions, which test knowledge rather than real clinical performance.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence versus neurologists: A comparative study on multiple sclerosis expertise.

studies.design: Retrospective paired-design diagnostic yield study
studies.humans: Radiologists at county and township facilities
studies.finding: Detection of pulmonary tuberculosis on chest X-rays of 93,319 patients, including 273 bacteriologically confirmed cases. CAD had a diagnostic yield of 83.9% (229/273) versus 25.6% (70/273) for radiologists, but a lower PPV (1.70% vs 10.31%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design comparing against original clinical reports; very low PPV.
studies.title: AI-Powered Chest X-Ray for Diagnosing Pulmonary Tuberculosis in County and Township Health Care Facilities in Yichang: Retrospective, Real-World Study.

studies.design: Multicenter diagnostic study with human-AI collaboration reading
studies.finding: For classifying acute, chronic and pathological vertebral compression fractures on X-ray, the DL model's AUCs were 0.780, 0.809 and 0.734, versus 0.707, 0.732 and 0.667 for the expert radiologist. With DL assistance, the expert's AUCs were 0.801, 0.825 and 0.751, and the trainee's were 0.722, 0.744 and 0.610.
studies.limitation: Only three readers, one per experience level.
studies.title: Deep learning-based artificial intelligence model for classification of vertebral compression fractures: A multicenter diagnostic study.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of ChatGPT4 vs endoscopists' actual recommendations against expert-panel USMSTF guidance, 505 consecutive colonoscopy patients at 2 academic centers
studies.finding: For postcolonoscopy rescreening/surveillance intervals in 505 patients, ChatGPT4 recommendations agreed with the USMSTF expert panel in 85.7% of cases versus 75.4% for the endoscopists' actual recommendations (P < .001). Inter-rater reliability for ChatGPT4 vs panel was good (Fleiss κ 0.786).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, two academic centers; reference standard is an expert panel applying guidelines rather than patient outcomes; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: ChatGPT4 Outperforms Endoscopists for Determination of Postcolonoscopy Rescreening and Surveillance Recommendations.
studies.source: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

studies.design: Retrospective model development with a randomized blinded clinician evaluation of segmentations
studies.finding: Experts blindly rated AI-generated and expert-generated pediatric low-grade glioma MRI segmentations on 100 scans. AI segmentations received a median Likert score of 9 versus 7 for expert segmentations, and 80.2% versus 65.4% were rated clinically acceptable.
studies.limitation: Only three expert raters, in a retrospective design.
studies.title: Stepwise Transfer Learning for Expert-level Pediatric Brain Tumor MRI Segmentation in a Limited Data Scenario.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study of thyroid ultrasound, six readers before and after AI
studies.finding: Six readers classified thyroid nodules with ACR TI-RADS on ultrasound in 172 patients, before and after using an AI decision support system. AUROC increased from 0.776 to 0.817 with AI (p < 0.001), mean sensitivity from 82.3% to 86.5% and specificity from 38.3% to 54.8%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, single-clinic study with a small number of readers.
studies.title: Clinical Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Decision Support System for the Diagnosis and American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System Classification of Thyroid Nodules.
studies.source: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association

studies.design: Retrospective feasibility study, single institution, LLM vs radiologists and hepatologist on free-text MRI reports
studies.finding: LI-RADS v2018 categorization from free-text MRI report descriptions. The model alone showed moderate agreement with ground truth (κ = 0.54 for LI-RADS category; κ = 0.58 dichotomized), LR-5 sensitivity 0.76 and specificity 0.96. Used as a triage tool, performance (κ = 0.86/0.87 radiologists, 0.76 hepatologist) showed no statistical significance compared to the human readers' individual performance, with workload decreased by 45%.
studies.limitation: Single institution, small test set including fictitious observations; text-based task for research data curation.
studies.title: Utilizing a domain-specific large language model for LI-RADS v2018 categorization of free-text MRI reports: a feasibility study.

studies.design: Agreement study comparing the AI with six doctors' manual measurements
studies.finding: The task was measuring the Cobb angle on spine X-rays in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. The ICCs between the six doctors and the AI were excellent or good, at 0.973 for the major curve in the standing position. The AI tended to measure 1.7°-2.2° smaller than the doctors.
studies.limitation: Measures agreement rather than accuracy against an independent reference standard.
studies.title: Automatic measurement of the Cobb angle for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis using convolutional neural network.

studies.design: Vignette study of 30 neurosurgical scenarios
studies.finding: Participants and ChatGPT determined triage urgency and the most likely diagnosis for 30 neurosurgical scenarios, with attending consensus as the answer key. GPT 4 was 100% accurate in both diagnosis and triage; GPT 3.5 triage accuracy was 92.59%, slightly below a PGY1 (96.3%), and its diagnostic accuracy of 92.59% was higher than the subinterns and similar to residents.
studies.limitation: Small set of vignettes, with attending consensus used as the reference standard.
studies.title: A Quantitative Assessment of ChatGPT as a Neurosurgical Triaging Tool.

studies.design: Model evaluated on an external validation set of 150 MRI studies against a panel of radiologists
studies.finding: The task was detecting and grading lumbar spinal stenosis on MRI. For central canal stenosis, the CNN had sensitivity, specificity and AUROC of (0.971, 0.864, 0.963), against a radiologist average of (0.786, 0.899, 0.842). Results were similarly comparable for lateral recess and foraminal stenosis.
studies.limitation: The reference standard was derived from the same radiologists' majority vote, and the external set was small (150 studies).
studies.title: A neural network model for detection and classification of lumbar spinal stenosis on MRI.
studies.source: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society

studies.design: Retrospective cross-sectional diagnostic comparison with DEXA reference
studies.finding: Detection of low bone density on routine non-contrast chest CT against DEXA. The CNN achieved accuracy 0.75, sensitivity 0.93, specificity 0.61, versus clinical reports accuracy 0.51, sensitivity 0.14, specificity 0.53.
studies.limitation: Small single-period retrospective sample; comparison with routine reports rather than radiologists actively assessing bone density.
studies.title: CNN-based evaluation of bone density improves diagnostic performance to detect osteopenia and osteoporosis in patients with non-contrast chest CT examinations.

studies.design: Comparison on text-based NEJM Image Challenge oral cases against journal readers' answers
studies.finding: The task was diagnosing oral diseases from text-based case descriptions. DeepSeek-R1 achieved 91.6% diagnostic accuracy and ChatGPT-4o 88.9%, against 47.8% for the journal's readers.
studies.limitation: The readers were unselected members of the public whose credentials are unknown, and the AI received text only while readers saw the images.
studies.title: DeepSeek: Another step forward in the diagnosis of oral lesions.

studies.design: Experimental phantom study
studies.ai_system: Robotic system with AI-based lesion detection and needle-path planning
studies.finding: Radiologists performed CT-guided needle insertions into phantom nodules with robotic AI assistance or freehand. Robot-assisted insertions had smaller 3D deviation (3.8 mm ± 1.3 vs 4.7 mm ± 1.6, P = .001) and shorter insertion time (17.3 s ± 7.8 vs 78.6 s ± 38.1, P < .001), with no significant difference in lateral deviation.
studies.limitation: Phantom model rather than patients, with only 8 radiologists.
studies.title: Robot-Assisted CT-Guided Biopsy with an Artificial Intelligence-Based Needle-Path Generator: An Experimental Evaluation Using a Phantom Model.
studies.source: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR

studies.design: Retrospective agreement analysis of 98 oncologic cases
studies.humans: Multidisciplinary tumor board (surgical, medical, radiation oncologists, pathologists, others)
studies.finding: LLM management decisions on four key points (new imaging, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, surgery) were compared with tumor board decisions using Cohen's kappa. Agreement ranged from none to slight for imaging (Gemini κ = 0.100; ChatGPT 4o κ = 0.024) and was higher for radiotherapy (Gemini κ = 0.214; ChatGPT 4o κ = 0.525) and surgery (Gemini κ = 0.194; ChatGPT 4o κ = 0.467).
studies.limitation: Agreement with the tumor board treated as reference rather than patient outcomes; single center, retrospective.
studies.title: Assessment of Challenging Oncologic Cases: A Comparative Analysis Between ChatGPT, Gemini, and a Multidisciplinary Tumor Board.

studies.design: Multireader multicase study comparing AI-enhanced versus traditional OCT software for PCI planning
studies.humans: Interventional cardiologists of varying OCT experience
studies.finding: Thirty interventional cardiologists evaluated 21 pre-PCI OCT pullbacks with AI-enabled Ultreon and traditional AptiVue, with decisions compared to published best practices. Accuracy was higher with Ultreon for calcium severity by 1.77 (95% CI, 1.27-2.50), vessel preparation strategy by 2.00 (95% CI, 1.12-3.4) and stent diameter by 2.83 (95% CI, 1.79-4.50), with less variability and assessments shortened by 0.5 minutes.
studies.limitation: Small case set (21 pullbacks) judged against best-practice standards rather than patient outcomes; vendor software evaluation.
studies.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Optical Coherence Tomography Software on Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Decisions.
studies.source: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions

studies.design: Vignette study of 70 fictional MRI request scenarios
studies.humans: Two radiology residents, two subspecialist attendings, one orthopaedic surgeon
studies.finding: An optimized LLM and five clinicians judged the appropriateness of musculoskeletal MRI requests in 70 fictional cases. The optimized LLM achieved 92.86% accuracy and performed better than all but one radiologist.
studies.limitation: Fictional cases with only five clinician comparators.
studies.title: ChatGPT performance in assessing musculoskeletal MRI scan appropriateness based on ACR appropriateness criteria.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with internal and external test sets compared with radiologist readers
studies.ai_system: 3D U-Net encoder-classifier deep learning model on CT
studies.humans: Two radiology residents and one fellowship-trained radiologist
studies.finding: For differentiating benign from malignant vertebral fractures on CT, the best model achieved AUC 0.85 internal and 0.75 external (0.91 and 0.76 with an uncertainty category). Residents had AUCs of 0.69 and 0.71 internal and 0.70 and 0.71 external, significantly lower only internally (P < .001); the fellowship-trained radiologist had AUC 0.86 internal (P = .39) and 0.71 external (P = .46).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only three readers and modest test sets.
studies.title: Deep Learning to Differentiate Benign and Malignant Vertebral Fractures at Multidetector CT.

studies.design: Retrospective interrupted time series before and after AI deployment
studies.ai_system: AI-based automated non-contrast CT head interpretation device
studies.humans: Non-specialist physicians at a rural Indian hospital
studies.finding: Time from NCCT to significant intervention in stroke patients before versus after AI deployment. Median time to intervention fell from 80 minutes (IQR: 56·8-139·5) to 58·50 (IQR: 30·3-118.2) minutes (location shift: -21·0, 95% CI: -38·0, -7·0).
studies.limitation: Single-site retrospective before-after design with 174 patients, open to secular confounding.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-based automated CT brain interpretation to accelerate treatment for acute stroke in rural India: An interrupted time series study.

studies.design: Analysis of 545 published case reports comparing GPT-4 with physician coding
studies.finding: ChatGPT detected diagnostic errors in 519/545 cases (95%). It coded more contributing factors per case than physicians: DEER median 5 vs 1, RDC 4 vs 2, GDP 4 vs 1 (all p<0.001).
studies.limitation: Published case reports rather than real charts; more factors coded does not establish accuracy.
studies.title: Performance evaluation of ChatGPT in detecting diagnostic errors and their contributing factors: an analysis of 545 case reports of diagnostic errors.

studies.design: Retrospective cohort, 551 chest pain observation unit patients, LLM vs APP HEART scores against blinded emergency physician adjudication
studies.humans: Physician assistants or nurse practitioners (APPs) calculating HEART scores in routine care
studies.finding: For HEART score computation, agreement with adjudicators (Cohen's weighted kappa) was 0.67 for the LLM versus 0.66 for the APPs. The LLM predicted higher mean scores (5.06 vs adjudicators 4.69 and APP 4.23), with no significant difference in diagnostic performance for 60-day MACE (all p > .05).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-institution study; comparators were APPs rather than physicians and adjudication was only for disagreements.
studies.title: Automated computation of the HEART score with the GPT-4 large language model.
studies.source: The American journal of emergency medicine

studies.design: Post-hoc single-center analysis of prospective EUS-nCLE studies; blinded expert video review vs AI
studies.finding: For detecting high-grade dysplasia/invasive cancer in 60 BD-IPMNs, experts had sensitivity 58%, specificity 59% and AUC 0.59, rising to AUC 0.64 with revised Fukuoka criteria; nCLE-AI alone achieved 87% sensitivity, 54% specificity, AUC 0.70. Combined with revised criteria, nCLE-AI reached AUC 0.85, significantly higher than humans with revised criteria (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Small single-center post-hoc sample of 60 lesions.
studies.title: Towards automating risk stratification of intraductal papillary mucinous Neoplasms: Artificial intelligence advances beyond human expertise with confocal laser endomicroscopy.
studies.source: Pancreatology : official journal of the International Association of Pancreatology (IAP) ... [et al.]

studies.design: Retrospective secondary analysis of prospective multicenter cohort
studies.finding: Breast cancer detection among 24 543 screened women with 148 cancers. AI-CAD had sensitivity of 89.9% and specificity of 94.3%; it detected 3.4% (five of 148) of cancers missed by radiologists but missed 8.1% (12 of 148) detected at radiologist recall.
studies.limitation: Secondary analysis; radiologist performance not fully reported; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Breast Cancers Detected and Missed by AI-CAD: Results from the AI-STREAM Trial.

studies.design: Prospective reader study on 180 MRI cases (146 FCD, 34 controls) comparing readers, 3 AI models and reader+AI pairings
studies.ai_system: Three state-of-the-art FCD detection AI models
studies.humans: 28 readers including 20 nonexpert and 5 expert physicians
studies.finding: For detection of focal cortical dysplasia on MRI, nonexpert readers detected 47% and experts 68% of FCDs, while the 3 AI models detected 32%, 51% and 72%, the best model with more than 13 false-positive clusters per subject. All AI models increased expert detection rates by up to 19% (P < 0.001), and nonexpert+AI pairs outperformed single experts by up to 13%.
studies.limitation: Human+AI benefit derived from analysed pairwise combinations of reader and model predictions rather than readers actually using AI; the best AI model had high false positives.
studies.title: A Quantitative Comparison Between Human and Artificial Intelligence in the Detection of Focal Cortical Dysplasia.

studies.design: Prospective multicentre reader study of endoscopists before and after DCNN assistance
studies.ai_system: DCNN real-time diagnosis system for early gastric cancer
studies.finding: For diagnosing early gastric cancer, in the video test novice accuracy improved from 79.36 to 86.41% and expert accuracy from 86.28 to 91.03% with DCNN assistance. With assistance, novices reached accuracy comparable to experts in images (95.22 vs. 96.16%), and image diagnostic time fell from 7.09 ± 0.6 s to 5.05 ± 0.55 s.
studies.limitation: Small reader sample of 12 and before/after design without randomisation.
studies.title: A prospective and comparative study on improving the diagnostic accuracy of early gastric cancer based on deep convolutional neural network real-time diagnosis system (with video).

studies.design: Multicenter validation of AI bone age analyzer vs residents, with expert consensus as reference
studies.ai_system: Commercial AI-powered X-ray bone age analyzer
studies.finding: On 900 radiographs, for TW3-RUS the AI had an MAE of 0.48 ± 0.42, significantly lower than rater 1 (0.54 ± 0.49) and not significantly different from rater 2 (0.48 ± 0.48) or rater 3 (0.49 ± 0.46). For TW3 carpal, the AI MAE of 0.48 ± 0.65 was significantly lower than rater 2 (0.58 ± 0.67) and numerically lower than raters 1 and 3.
studies.limitation: The reference standard was expert readers' estimates, and the AI was compared only with three residents.
studies.title: Validation of an AI-Powered Automated X-ray Bone Age Analyzer in Chinese Children and Adolescents: A Comparison with the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 Method.

studies.design: Retrospective double-blind observational study
studies.ai_system: Commercial AI for bone X-ray fracture, dislocation and effusion detection
studies.humans: Radiology residents (senior radiologist as gold standard)
studies.finding: Detection on 792 emergency bone X-rays. For fractures, residents had Sens = 90.6% and Spec = 98% versus 95.8% and 97.6% for AI; residents achieved higher sensitivity (77.8%) and specificity (100%) for dislocation.
studies.limitation: Single centre, retrospective, single senior radiologist as reference; number of residents not stated.
studies.title: Diagnostic Performance of an Artificial Intelligence Software for the Evaluation of Bone X-Ray Examinations Referred from the Emergency Department.

studies.design: Model development with retrospective and prospective validation plus endoscopist comparison
studies.finding: For invasion depth classification of early ESCC, MUMA-EDx achieved AUC 0.95 retrospectively and 0.80 prospectively. Its performance exceeded novice endoscopists and was comparable to experts.
studies.limitation: Human comparison figures and reader numbers not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Development and validation of a multimodal deep learning model for early esophageal squamous neoplasia detection and invasion depth prediction.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with reader study (70 images)
studies.finding: For tibial plateau fracture detection on knee radiographs, DL assistance improved occult fracture sensitivity of less experienced readers (67.5% to 83.8%). Interreader agreement rose from 0.58 to 0.71 and mean interpretation time fell from 55.8 seconds to 34.3 seconds.
studies.limitation: Small reader study of 70 images from a retrospective external set.
studies.title: Deep learning diagnosis of adult tibial plateau fractures: multicenter study with external validation.

studies.design: Prospective diagnostic accuracy study (STARD) of 97 adolescents
studies.finding: In photographic assessment of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, ChatGPT had specificity 0% and Claude 2 generated 78.3% false positives. Human evaluators showed superior bias control (0.3-2.8° vs. 2.6-10.7°) but suboptimal specificity (21.7-26.1%).
studies.limitation: Only two residents as comparators; photographic assessment not standard practice.
studies.title: Clinical Failure of General-Purpose AI in Photographic Scoliosis Assessment: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study.

studies.design: Experimental reader study manipulating advice source (AI vs radiologist) and annotation
studies.ai_system: Explainable AI diagnostic advice with visual annotations
studies.humans: Physicians, task experts and non-task experts
studies.finding: Physicians diagnosed X-rays given correct advice labelled as from AI or a human radiologist, with or without annotation. Annotated AI advice resulted in the highest diagnostic accuracy, and non-task experts benefited considerably from correct explainable AI advice.
studies.limitation: Only correct advice was given and no numbers or participant counts are reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Non-task expert physicians benefit from correct explainable AI advice when reviewing X-rays.

studies.design: Retrospective image-based development and benchmark study
studies.ai_system: CADe deep learning system for Barrett's neoplasia
studies.finding: On test set 1 (50 neoplastic and 150 NDBE images of subtle lesions), the CADe system had sensitivity of 84% versus 63% for general endoscopists. CADe specificity across test sets was between 64% and 66%.
studies.limitation: Image-based retrospective evaluation, not live endoscopy; endoscopist specificity not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Towards a robust and compact deep learning system for primary detection of early Barrett's neoplasia: Initial image-based results of training on a multi-center retrospectively collected data set.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre development and validation study; AI compared with historic radiologist reports on an expert consensus set
studies.finding: Chest x-ray classification across 37 findings on a consensus set of 1427 exams. X-Raydar outperformed historical reporter balanced accuracy with significance on 27 of 37 findings, was non-inferior on nine and inferior on one, an average improvement of 13·3% (SD 13·1) to 0·763 (0·110). Mean AUC was 0·864 (0·102) on the consensus set.
studies.limitation: Retrospective comparison against historic reports written in routine practice rather than a controlled reader study.
studies.title: Development and validation of open-source deep neural networks for comprehensive chest x-ray reading: a retrospective, multicentre study.

studies.design: Diagnostic accuracy study vs CMR reference, comparing AI with expert reads
studies.finding: For detecting CMR-defined RV dysfunction, AI had sensitivity and NPV of 91% and 96%, versus 91% and 97% for expert physician reads. Specificity and PPV were lower for AI (50% and 32%) than for experts (82% and 56%).
studies.limitation: Number of readers not stated; TTE and CMR not simultaneous.
studies.title: Validation of American Society of Echocardiography Guideline-Recommended Parameters of Right Ventricular Dysfunction Using Artificial Intelligence Compared With Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
studies.source: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective development/test study with reader comparison plus prospective real-world application
studies.finding: For ASPECTS assessment on non-contrast CT in acute ischemic stroke, combining the system with physicians improved AUC from 67.43 to 89.76%. Diagnosis time fell from 130.6 ± 66.3 s to 33.3 ± 8.3 s (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Number of physician readers and reader-study design not stated in the abstract; developer-led evaluation.
studies.title: Deep learning-based automatic ASPECTS calculation can improve diagnosis efficiency in patients with acute ischemic stroke: a multicenter study.

studies.design: Retrospective single-institution study with AI-CAD results provided or withheld by alternating month in clinical screening
studies.finding: In 2061 screening mammograms from 1819 women, radiologists' diagnostic performance did not significantly differ with and without AI-CAD assistance. Radiologists with AI-CAD had the same sensitivity (76.5%) as stand-alone AI-CAD and similar specificity (92.3% vs 93.8%) and AUC (0.844 vs 0.851). Radiologists without AI-CAD showed lower specificity (91.9% vs 94.6%) and accuracy (91.5% vs 94.1%) and higher recall rates (8.6% vs 5.9%) than stand-alone AI-CAD.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-institution study with only 29 cancers; non-randomised monthly alternation.
studies.title: Diagnostic performance with and without artificial intelligence assistance in real-world screening mammography.

studies.design: Model development with independent evaluation set compared against physician consensus
studies.ai_system: Weighted ML/deep learning (Siamese network) model for oART trigger decisions
studies.finding: Deciding whether to trigger online adaptive radiotherapy replanning for cervical cancer fractions. On an independent set of 83 fractions, the weighted model's accuracy significantly outperformed physician consensus (0.855 vs 0.795), with comparable precision (0.917 vs 0.925) and higher recall (0.887 vs 0.790).
studies.limitation: Very small independent test set (83 fractions from 3 patients), and the reference labels are dosimetric.
studies.title: Fully Automated Online Adaptive Radiation Therapy Decision-Making for Cervical Cancer Using Artificial Intelligence.
studies.source: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics

studies.design: Model development compared with a national survey of surgeons in a simulated environment
studies.ai_system: CASL deep learning surgical guidance system
studies.finding: For identifying peritoneal surface metastases on laparoscopy images, the AUC was 0.69 for oncologic surgeons, 0.78 for CASL and 0.79 for the human-computer combination. Surgeons' accuracy in correctly recommending biopsy was only 52%.
studies.limitation: Simulated survey environment; prototype not validated across institutions.
studies.title: Development of a Deep Learning System for Intraoperative Identification of Cancer Metastases.

studies.design: Diagnostic accuracy study comparing software users, microscopic users and hybrid
studies.finding: For diagnosing oral diseases, correct diagnosis rates for software users, microscopic users and hybrid were 87%, 90.6 and 95% respectively. The software's accuracy, sensitivity and specificity were lower than those of oral pathologists, though its correct diagnosis rate was described as comparable.
studies.limitation: Unclear design and number of participants; single-centre archival cases.
studies.title: The innovation of AI-based software in oral diseases: clinical-histopathological correlation diagnostic accuracy primary study.

studies.design: Man-machine comparison on 300 cases
studies.ai_system: CNN-based Cobb angle and Lenke classification system
studies.finding: For Cobb angle measurement and Lenke classification, AI took 0.2 s per patient versus 23.6 min per surgeon. The AI had high reliability compared to senior doctors (ICC 0.962).
studies.limitation: Only four surgeons, and the accuracy comparison is reported mainly as agreement.
studies.title: Validation of Artificial Intelligence in the Classification of Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis and the Compairment to Clinical Manual Handling.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of clinician, ChatGPT-4 and ORAD diagnoses against histopathology
studies.finding: For odontogenic keratocysts and tumours, concordance with histopathology was 43.2% for clinicians, 45.6% for ORAD and 41.4% for Chat-GPT4. ROC-AUC values were similar, e.g. for ameloblastoma Clinician 0.62, ORAD 0.58, Chat-GPT4 0.63.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, based on referral notes; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Concordance of clinician, Chat-GPT4, and ORAD diagnoses against histopathology in Odontogenic Keratocysts and tumours: a 15-Year New Zealand retrospective study.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison against epileptologist diagnoses
studies.finding: In 597 emergency department patients with seizures, neurologists diagnosed epilepsy in 216 (36.2%) versus ChatGPT in 109 (18.2%), with Cohen's kappa of -0.01. Against neurologists' diagnoses, ChatGPT sensitivity was 17.6% and specificity 81.4%, with errors in 41.7% of cases.
studies.limitation: Clinicians served as the reference standard, so their own accuracy was not independently measured; single retrospective dataset.
studies.title: Can ChatGPT 4.0 Diagnose Epilepsy? A Study on Artificial Intelligence's Diagnostic Capabilities.

studies.design: Retrospective pilot study on panoramic radiographs with a held-out test set
studies.finding: For classifying peri-implantitis bone defects, the DL model achieved overall accuracy of 85.33% versus a mean accuracy of 75.6% for the periodontal surgeons. The surgeons showed higher accuracy in severe cases, particularly class II defects.
studies.limitation: Pilot study with only 2 human comparators.
studies.title: Performance of artificial intelligence-based diagnosis and classification of peri-implantitis compared with periodontal surgeon assessment: a pilot study of panoramic radiograph analysis.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter study of AI-radiologist collaboration strategies
studies.finding: HCC ultrasound screening on 21,934 images from 11,960 patients compared four AI-enhanced strategies. Strategy 4 (AI initial detection with radiologist review of negative cases) matched the sensitivity of the original algorithm (0.956 vs. 0.991), improved specificity (0.787 vs. 0.698), and reduced radiologist workload by 54.5%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective simulation of workflow strategies; comparator is the original algorithm rather than clearly reported unaided radiologist performance.
studies.title: AI enhanced diagnostic accuracy and workload reduction in hepatocellular carcinoma screening.

studies.design: Retrospective model development and internal validation
studies.ai_system: Multimodal deep learning model (clinical data + colposcopy images)
studies.finding: Predicting CIN2+ in 6356 conization cases, the combined model achieved AUC-ROC = 95.3 %, accuracy = 90.8 %, and outperformed clinician's colposcopic impressions. Clinician figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Internal validation only, retrospective; clinician performance numbers not reported.
studies.title: A multimodal deep learning model for cervical pre-cancers and cancers prediction: Development and internal validation study.

studies.design: Retrospective cohort comparing endoscopists initially trained with CADe vs conventionally, assessed on later independent colonoscopies
studies.finding: Independent colonoscopy quality of endoscopists trained with CADe was compared with conventionally trained endoscopists across 6000 patients. The AI-trained group had a significantly improved adenoma detection rate by 5.3% (95% CI: 2.9-7.6%) and sessile lesion detection rate by 5.4% (95% CI: 3.8-7.0%), with longer withdrawal time (mean difference 0.8 min). AI-assisted training was a factor of high-quality performance for ADR (OR 1.27) and SDR (OR 1.93).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, non-randomised with only six endoscopists.
studies.title: The implementation of computer-aided detection in an initial endoscopy training improves the quality measures of trainees' future colonoscopies: a retrospective cohort study.

studies.design: Retrospective external validation of three commercial DL algorithms on consecutive UK screening mammograms
studies.ai_system: Three commercial DL algorithms (DL-1, DL-2, DL-3)
studies.humans: Screening mammography readers (single first reader and double reading)
studies.finding: Breast cancer screening on 26 722 cases. Standalone sensitivity was DL-1 64.8%, DL-2 56.7%, DL-3 58.9% vs single first reader 62.8%, and specificity 92.8%, 96.8%, 97.9% vs 96.5%. DL combined with a human reader achieved sensitivity of 67.0%, 65.6%, 65.4% vs double reading 67.4%, with superior specificity (97.4%, 97.6%, 97.6% vs 97.1%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective data from two UK sites in a single year; human reading reflects historical decisions.
studies.title: Deep Learning Algorithms for Breast Cancer Detection in a UK Screening Cohort: As Stand-alone Readers and Combined with Human Readers.

studies.design: Cross-sectional reader study of 30 chronic wound images
studies.finding: 481 healthcare professionals and a CNN classified 30 chronic wound images for maceration. Humans achieved an average accuracy of 79.3% (maximum 85% in the formally qualified group) versus 90% for the CNN, which performed better but not significantly.
studies.limitation: Only 30 images; participants were mixed healthcare professionals rather than physicians specifically.
studies.title: Diagnostic accuracy differences in detecting wound maceration between humans and artificial intelligence: the role of human expertise revisited.
studies.source: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

studies.design: Comparative study of junior physicians with vs without MLLM-preidentified HPO terms, plus standalone MLLMs
studies.finding: Identifying HPO terms from 27 rare-disease patient images. The MLLM-assisted group achieved accuracy of 67.4% (182/270) vs 20.4% (55/270) for manual search (relative risk 3.31, 95% CI 2.58-4.25; P<.001). Standalone ChatGPT-4o achieved 48% (13/27), with high hallucination rates.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 27 images from published literature and 20 physicians; not live clinical care.
studies.title: Enhancing the Accuracy of Human Phenotype Ontology Identification: Comparative Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models.

studies.design: Reader study of 10 colorectal cancer regions with and without CAD assistance
studies.humans: Medical students, pathology residents and practicing pathologists
studies.finding: Tumor cell fraction estimation with and without TCFCAD. SD of scores versus ground truth fell from 9.09 to 4.95 for students, 9.93 to 5.55 for EMMP participants, and 9.98 to 5.69 and 9.9 to 6.13 for pathologists with < 20 and > 20 years of experience. For one image, students and EMMP participants swayed toward an inaccurate tool output, showing automation bias.
studies.limitation: Only 10 regions of interest; automation bias evidence based on a single image.
studies.title: Computer-aided tumor cell fraction (TCF) estimation by medical students, residents, and pathologists improves inter-observer agreement while highlighting the risk of automation bias.
studies.source: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 150 questions
studies.ai_system: Eight LLM chatbots including Claude 2.1, ChatGPT-4, Doctor GPT
studies.humans: Nine oncology physicians (3 residents, 3 fellows, 3 attendings)
studies.finding: Guideline-consistent answers to 150 colorectal cancer questions. Claude 2.1 had the highest accuracy at 82.67% and outperformed residents, fellows and attendings; Doctor GPT (80.45%) outperformed residents and fellows, while weaker models such as Llama-2-70B (61.78%) did not.
studies.limitation: Question-based assessment rather than real patient care; small physician sample.
studies.title: The performance of large language model-powered chatbots compared to oncology physicians on colorectal cancer queries.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to expert PRECISE scoring
studies.ai_system: LSTM time series radiomics model with PSA density
studies.finding: Predicting prostate cancer progression on serial MRI in 76 active surveillance patients, the model achieved an AUC of 0.86 [95% CI: 0.78-0.94]. Expert PRECISE scoring achieved 0.84 [0.76-0.93] (p = 0.710).
studies.limitation: Small single cohort with leave-one-out cross-validation and no external validation.
studies.title: Time series radiomics for the prediction of prostate cancer progression in patients on active surveillance.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study, unassisted then GPT-4-assisted sessions
studies.finding: Diagnosis of 40 imaging studies. Top-3 accuracy improved slightly from 181/240 (75.4%, unassisted) to 188/240 (78.3%, AI-assisted) and confidence was significantly higher; 7.4% of GPT-4 responses were hallucinations.
studies.limitation: Small sample of six radiologists and 40 selected cases; sequential sessions without randomisation.
studies.title: The virtual reference radiologist: comprehensive AI assistance for clinical image reading and interpretation.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study with and without AI assistance
studies.ai_system: Deep learning wrist fracture detection model
studies.finding: An AI model detected distal radius, ulnar styloid and scaphoid fractures on wrist radiographs from 593 subjects, with per-wrist AUCs of 0.903, 0.925 and 0.808. With AI assistance, the scaphoid fracture AUC of two novice radiologists rose from 0.75 to 0.85 and from 0.71 to 0.80.
studies.limitation: Only two novice readers.
studies.title: Clinical Validation of an Artificial Intelligence Model for Detecting Distal Radius, Ulnar Styloid, and Scaphoid Fractures on Conventional Wrist Radiographs.

studies.design: Retrospective cohort study
studies.finding: A model predicted post-DMEK graft detachment from preoperative AS-OCT in a 24-eye test set and was compared with an ophthalmologist. MIL-AI was more sensitive (92% vs. 31%) but less specific (45% vs. 64%).
studies.limitation: Very small test set (24 eyes) and a single comparator.
studies.title: Deep Learning Using Preoperative AS-OCT Predicts Graft Detachment in DMEK.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter analysis
studies.ai_system: Pulmonary nodule malignancy prediction algorithm with an ensemble uncertainty score
studies.finding: Pulmonary nodule malignancy prediction on low-dose CT, with cases split by AI uncertainty. In the certain group AI accuracy was on par with clinicians (80% [95% CI: 76, 85] vs 78% [95% CI: 70, 87]; P = .07). In the uncertain group AI was worse (50% [95% CI: 37, 64] vs 68% [95% CI: 60, 76]; P < .001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective reuse of datasets from earlier studies; the clinician comparison covered only the lung nodule task.
studies.title: Prediction Variability to Identify Reduced AI Performance in Cancer Diagnosis at MRI and CT.

studies.design: Retrospective modelling on clinical trial database
studies.finding: Prediction of fast versus non-fast ALS progression in 5030 PRO-ACT patients. The models achieved AUROC of 0.570-0.748 and were non-inferior to clinician assessments.
