studies.limitation: Clinician comparator and its numbers are not described in the abstract.
studies.title: Predicting amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) progression with machine learning.

studies.design: Model development with temporal and external validation, compared with triage nurses
studies.finding: Identifying ophthalmic emergency attendances on 1269 attendances, DOTS had sensitivity 94.5% and specificity 42.4%, versus triage nurses' sensitivity 96.4% and specificity 25.1%. DOTS had similar sensitivity with a specificity 17.3% higher.
studies.limitation: Retrospective comparison against nurses rather than physicians; not yet prospectively tested.
studies.title: A machine learning system to optimise triage in an adult ophthalmic emergency department: a model development and validation study.

studies.design: Single-center retrospective cohort; blinded expert rating of differential diagnoses
studies.ai_system: Fine-tuned LLaMa-7B and other language models (BioGPT-Large, LLaMa-65B)
studies.humans: Clinicians who wrote PICU admission notes; rated by five critical care experts
studies.finding: Generating differential diagnoses from 130 PICU admission notes, rated on a 5-point Likert scale. Clinician differentials scored a mean 3.43 versus 2.88 for the best model, fine-tuned LLaMa-7B (absolute difference 0.54 units, p < 0.001); clinician and model differentials were ranked highest in 144 (55%) and 74 cases (29%), respectively.
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective design with subjective Likert ratings by five experts.
studies.title: Comparing the Quality of Domain-Specific Versus General Language Models for Artificial Intelligence-Generated Differential Diagnoses in PICU Patients.
studies.source: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

studies.design: Comparison of commercial autocontours with physician-approved manual contours, blinded physician scoring
studies.humans: Treating physicians' approved manual contours; at least three physician raters
studies.finding: CT organ contouring for 16 organs across 47 patients, scored by physicians on a five-point Likert scale. Averaged across structures, physician-approved contours scored 2.02, MIM 2.07, RAD 1.96 and SIE 1.99. Each vendor's AI exhibited capabilities similar to manual contouring.
studies.limitation: Small single-centre sample of ten patients per organ.
studies.title: Evaluation of multiple-vendor AI autocontouring solutions.

studies.design: Within-case comparison of reading with and without AI frame reduction
studies.finding: Small bowel capsule endoscopy reading of 90 cases with versus without AI removal of poorly visualized frames. Diagnostic concordance between the two readings was k = 0.954 (p < 0.001). Reading time was reduced by 35.6% with AI (77.9 min vs 120.9 min).
studies.limitation: Only two readers, and the outcome was concordance rather than accuracy against a reference standard.
studies.title: Reading of small bowel capsule endoscopy after frame reduction using an artificial intelligence algorithm.

studies.design: Retrospective observational study of ED chest X-rays against senior radiologist gold standard
studies.finding: AI and a radiology resident interpreted chest X-rays from 784 ED patients against a senior radiologist's reading. Sensitivity was 100% for both for fractures and pneumothorax, AI = 76% vs resident = 71% for pulmonary opacity, AI = 60% vs resident = 67% for pleural effusion, and AI 33% vs resident 75% for pulmonary nodules.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-center study comparing against a single resident, with a single senior radiologist as gold standard.
studies.title: Diagnostic Performance of Artificial Intelligence in Chest Radiographs Referred from the Emergency Department.

studies.design: Retrospective consecutive cohort comparing AI with initial radiology reports
studies.finding: For incidental acute PE on 3089 portal venous chest CTs, AI sensitivity was 95.5% vs. 62.7% for the initial reports (p < 0.001). Specificity was 99.6% vs 99.9%, and PPV was 85.3% vs. 95.5% (p = 0.047).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, and the reference standard came from adjudicating discordant cases only.
studies.title: Added value of an artificial intelligence algorithm in reducing the number of missed incidental acute pulmonary embolism in routine portal venous phase chest CT.

studies.design: Retrospective accuracy study on consecutive CT scans
studies.finding: Detection of moderate-to-severe vertebral compression fractures on 899 CT scans, with two musculoskeletal specialists as reference. The software had an accuracy of 89.6% (95% CI: 87.4-91.5%), sensitivity of 73.8% and specificity of 92.7%. Among the 145 positive scans it detected, the general radiologist failed to report fractures in 62 (42.8%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, with the radiologist comparison based on original clinical reports.
studies.title: Accuracy of an artificial intelligence algorithm for detecting moderate-to-severe vertebral compression fractures on abdominal and thoracic computed tomography scans.

studies.design: Blinded simulation study with synthetic cases
studies.ai_system: GPT-4 and GPT-5, with and without RAG
studies.humans: A human expert comparator; eight head and neck surgeons as raters
studies.finding: Fourteen synthetic head and neck cancer cases received management recommendations from a human expert and four LLM arms, which eight surgeons rated on Likert scales. RAG-based models achieved the highest mean scores, with some statistically significant differences versus the expert in appropriateness and clarity, though absolute differences were modest.
studies.limitation: Only 14 synthetic cases and a single human expert comparator.
studies.title: Evaluation of large language models as decision support tools for head and neck cancer management: A blinded multidisciplinary simulation study.

studies.design: Vignette comparison of GPT-4 with endocrinologists
studies.finding: On diabetes vignettes, GPT-4 chose metformin in 12% (95% CI 7.9-17%) of responses vs 31% (95% CI 23-39%) for endocrinologists, rising to 25% with a modified prompt. The authors judged GPT-4's responses reasonable but different in clinically important ways.
studies.limitation: Hypothetical vignettes with no single right answer.
studies.title: Large Language Model GPT-4 Compared to Endocrinologist Responses on Initial Choice of Glucose-Lowering Medication Under Conditions of Clinical Uncertainty.

studies.design: Retrospective two-centre model development and validation study
studies.ai_system: MVITV2 and other deep learning models
studies.finding: Deep learning models on sagittal CT were used to distinguish early spinal tuberculosis from acute osteoporotic fracture. MVITV2 achieved accuracy of 98.98% and AUC of 0.997 internally, exceeding the two spine surgeons, who achieved accuracy rates of 77.38% and 93.56%.
studies.limitation: Model-development study with a small external set and only two surgeons.
studies.title: Deep Learning for Discrimination of Early Spinal Tuberculosis from Acute Osteoporotic Vertebral Fracture on CT.

studies.design: Comparative evaluation of LLM-generated vs human researcher-written reports on real clinical queries, rated by physicians
studies.finding: Reports answering 20 real-world clinical dilemmas were compared (20 human reports, 56 LLM reports). Human reports met physicians' expectations more frequently (p = 0.044), were considered more reliable (p = 0.032) and contained no hallucinated or unfaithful citations (p < 0.001), unlike LLM reports. Physician satisfaction did not correlate meaningfully with objective report quality.
studies.limitation: Small number of queries (n = 20) and human comparators were researchers rather than clinicians answering in practice.
studies.title: Evaluating the performance of large language models versus human researchers on real world complex medical queries.

studies.design: Single-center observational before-after implementation study
studies.finding: Detection of incidental pulmonary embolism on chest CT before and after AI implementation. The rate of missed iPEs by radiologists dropped from 50% to 7.1% (P < 0.001); 90-day mortality was unchanged (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.45-1.96; P = 0.88).
studies.limitation: Non-randomised single-center before-after design.
studies.title: Implementation of an AI Algorithm in Clinical Practice to Reduce Missed Incidental Pulmonary Embolisms on Chest CT and Its Impact on Short-Term Survival.

studies.design: Model development plus simulated reader study with and without AI
studies.finding: Detection of torn vs intact rotator cuff on ultrasound. With AI assistance physicians' diagnostic accuracy improved from 80.86% to 88.86% (P = .01) and interobserver reliability from 0.49 to 0.71.
studies.limitation: Simulation data set with unstated number of physicians; balanced single-source dataset.
studies.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Interobserver Reliability of Rotator Cuff Tear Detection With Ultrasonography Are Improved With Attentional Deep Learning.
studies.source: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter diagnostic study
studies.finding: Diagnosis of early osteonecrosis of the femoral head on MRI. The framework had internal test accuracy of 93.83% and external accuracies of 87.76% and 87.60%, comparable to senior orthopedic surgeons and superior to junior surgeons.
studies.limitation: Retrospective with only three surgeons; surgeons' numbers not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Development and evaluation of a 3D ensemble framework for automatic diagnosis of early osteonecrosis of the femoral head based on MRI: a multicenter diagnostic study.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre evaluation against expert consensus and outcomes
studies.finding: On 236 ED triage encounters, MECR-RAG achieved a QWK of 0.902 vs nurse interrater QWK of 0.887. It detected high-risk patients more sensitively than initial nurse triage (124/130, 95.4% vs 117/130, 90.0%; P=.02) and had a lower weighted harm index (13.7 vs 19.5 per 100 patients).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single centre, and the comparators are nurses rather than physicians.
studies.title: Multi-Evidence Clinical Reasoning With Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Emergency Triage: Retrospective Evaluation Study.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison with CT reference standard
studies.finding: For detecting pelvic, hip and extremity fractures on radiographs in 94 patients, the AI had 82 % sensitivity, 69 % specificity and 76 % accuracy. The radiologist had 92 % sensitivity, 88 % specificity and 90 % accuracy, outperforming the AI on all three (P = 0.045, P = 0.016, P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Small single-centre sample with radiologist readings.
studies.title: Comparison between artificial intelligence solution and radiologist for the detection of pelvic, hip and extremity fractures on radiographs in adult using CT as standard of reference.

studies.design: Multi-cohort model development with blinded independent evaluation versus radiologists
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model integrating MedpSeg airway segmentation with convolutional classifier
studies.finding: Detection of radiolucent foreign body aspiration on chest CT. In a blinded independent evaluation cohort, the model outperformed expert radiologists in recall (71.4% vs. 35.7%) and F1 score (74.1% vs. 52.6%).
studies.limitation: Number of radiologists and cohort size not stated in the abstract; retrospective image-based evaluation.
studies.title: Automated detection of radiolucent foreign body aspiration on chest CT using deep learning.

studies.design: Cross-sectional screening study
studies.finding: Fundus images from 120 people with diabetes at a primary care centre were read by an AI programme and an optometrist. The AI detected more glaucoma (17.5% vs 9.2%) and diabetic retinopathy (23.3% vs 15.8%), while the optometrist identified more macula pathology (29.2% vs 19.2%).
studies.limitation: Single optometrist and no reference standard, so detection rates are not accuracy.
studies.title: Screening for diabetic retinopathy at a health centre in South Africa: A cross-sectional study.
studies.source: Journal of public health in Africa

studies.design: Development and validation on consecutive digitized urine cytology slides
studies.ai_system: Fully automated deep learning system for urine cytology
studies.finding: For predicting histological high-grade urothelial carcinoma, AI sensitivity of 63% was superior to pathologists' cytology sensitivity of 46% (p = 0.0037). Specificity (83% vs 89%, p = 0.13) and accuracy (74% vs 68%, p = 0.08) did not differ significantly.
studies.limitation: Single-institution slides with comparison against routine cytology diagnosis; number of pathologists unclear.
studies.title: A Fully Automated Artificial Intelligence System to Assist Pathologists' Diagnosis to Predict Histologically High-grade Urothelial Carcinoma from Digitized Urine Cytology Slides Using Deep Learning.

studies.design: Model development and evaluation against human doctors on exams and clinical vignettes
studies.ai_system: MOPH, a Chinese ophthalmology large language model
studies.finding: On ophthalmic board-style mock exams MOPH's average score closely aligned with trainees (64.7 vs 66.2, p=0.817). For diagnostic accuracy on clinical vignettes ophthalmologists were correct in 96.1% vs 81.1% for MOPH, a difference not statistically significant.
studies.limitation: Simulated exam questions and vignettes with small samples; number of human participants not stated.
studies.title: Development and evaluation of a large language model of ophthalmology in Chinese.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter comparison on CMR reports
studies.humans: 3 radiology residents (1, 2 and 4 years CMR experience)
studies.finding: Diagnosing myocarditis from CMR reports of 396 patients. GPT-4 had accuracy 83%, sensitivity 90%, specificity 78%, comparable to resident 1 (86%, 90%, 84%, p = 0.14) and lower than more experienced residents (R2: 89%, p = 0.007; R3: 91%, p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Only three readers; report-based retrospective task.
studies.title: Generative Pre-trained Transformer 4 analysis of cardiovascular magnetic resonance reports in suspected myocarditis: A multicenter study.
studies.source: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

studies.design: Retrospective single-hospital comparison against initial radiology reports on 191-case test set
studies.ai_system: Optimized deep learning fracture detection model
studies.finding: Detection of extremity fractures referenced to CT. The optimized AI detected more avulsion fractures than radiologists (57.89% vs. 29.82%, P=0.002), with no significant difference for non-avulsion fractures (P=0.853) or case-level accuracy, sensitivity and specificity (P>0.05).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-centre study comparing against routine reports; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence versus radiologist in the accuracy of fracture detection based on computed tomography images: a multi-dimensional, multi-region analysis.
studies.source: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

studies.design: Multicentre model development with test-set comparison against physicians
studies.humans: Three nuclear medicine physicians of varying experience
studies.finding: Whole-body bone scintigraphy classification. Best models reached AUC = 0.72; AI performance was significantly higher than human observers for normal/abnormal classification and comparable for malignant vs non-neoplastic discrimination.
studies.limitation: Only three readers; retrospective data with modest model AUCs.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-based analysis of whole-body bone scintigraphy: The quest for the optimal deep learning algorithm and comparison with human observer performance.

studies.design: Single-centre retrospective diagnostic comparison
studies.finding: In 58 resuscitated OHCA patients, the AI ECG score was compared with experts for detecting coronary occlusion. QCG had an AUC of 0.770 versus 0.676 for the expert group, with 70.8% sensitivity and 79.4% specificity; it was described as non-inferior to expert consensus.
studies.limitation: Very small single-centre sample (58 patients, 24 occlusions).
studies.title: Performance of ECG-Derived Digital Biomarker for Screening Coronary Occlusion in Resuscitated Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Patients: A Comparative Study between Artificial Intelligence and a Group of Experts.

studies.design: Single-centre retrospective observational study using clinical vignettes of 80 TBI patients
studies.finding: Prediction of 6-month functional outcome after moderate-to-severe TBI. AUC-ROC was 0.62 for ChatGPT, 0.70 for the neurointensivist, 0.71 for the non-neurointensivist and 0.81 for IMPACT; ChatGPT had 100% sensitivity but 26% specificity, and was generally less accurate than clinicians for secondary outcomes.
studies.limitation: Only two clinicians and 80 patients from a single centre, with retrospective vignettes.
studies.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT in Predicting 6-Month Outcomes After Traumatic Brain Injury.

studies.design: Model development with multicentre testing and reader comparison with/without AI
studies.ai_system: Modified nnU-Net/U-Net deep learning model for CBCT dentition segmentation
studies.finding: Classification and 3D segmentation of mixed dentition on CBCT. With model aid, junior dentists' performance improved significantly while senior dentists showed no significant improvement; segmentation speed increased by 20.9-22.8 times.
studies.limitation: Only two observers of different seniority; reader results not quantified in abstract.
studies.title: Fully automated method for three-dimensional segmentation and fine classification of mixed dentition in cone-beam computed tomography using deep learning.

studies.design: Retrospective external validation, single centre
studies.ai_system: Commercial CAD system for lung nodule detection on CT
studies.finding: In 263 chest CT scans with 183 true nodules, the radiologist detected 165/183 (90.2%) while CAD achieved a sensitivity of 149/183 (81.4%) with an FP-rate of 49/121 (0.405). CAD detected 12 nodules missed by the radiologist.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-centre study comparing against a single radiologist.
studies.title: Validation of a commercially available CAD-system for lung nodule detection and characterization using CT-scans.

studies.design: Cross-sectional database study with CNN development and doctor assistance assessment
studies.ai_system: U-net segmentation and Inception V3 classification CNN for Pfirrmann grading
studies.finding: CNN classification accuracy for intervertebral disc degeneration grading was .9346 and the network outperformed doctors markedly in accuracy and reliability. With CNN assistance, doctors' success rates increased by 7.9% to 22%.
studies.limitation: Ground truth from the majority of the same four doctors; doctor comparison details and reader numbers unclear in the abstract.
studies.title: An Automatized Deep Segmentation and Classification Model for Lumbar Disk Degeneration and Clarification of Its Impact on Clinical Decisions.

studies.design: Retrospective two-centre model development with reader comparison with and without DL assistance
studies.finding: For predicting extraprostatic extension in prostate cancer, the multimodal DL model had AUC 0.82 (0.78-0.87) internally and 0.81 (0.63-0.97) externally. DL-assisted EPE-grade scoring significantly improved AUC and sensitivity compared with radiologist EPE-grade scoring alone (P < 0.05), with a modest reduction in specificity.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with small external test set (n = 36); number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Multimodal imaging deep learning model for predicting extraprostatic extension in prostate cancer using MpMRI and 18 F-PSMA-PET/CT.
studies.source: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society

studies.design: Retrospective cross-sectional study of consecutive suspected stroke brain MRIs
studies.finding: Detection of acute ischemic, hemorrhagic and space-occupying lesions on stroke MRI in 775 patients, with motion artifacts in 57 (7.4%). Motion artifacts reduced hemorrhage detection accuracy for the AI tool from 88 to 67% and for radiology reports from 100 to 93% (both p < 0.001). Ischemic and space-occupying lesion detection was not significantly affected.
studies.limitation: Single non-comprehensive center, retrospective; few hemorrhages (12); compared against clinical reports rather than a controlled reader study.
studies.title: Motion artifacts and image quality in stroke MRI: associated factors and impact on AI and human diagnostic accuracy.

studies.design: Retrospective study within population-based DBT screening cohort
studies.finding: Comparison of false-positive screening DBT examinations (3183 exams) for AI vs radiologists. The false-positive rate was 10% for both AI (304/3183) and radiologists (308/3183). Only 71 (13%) of false-positive exams were shared, with differing patient and finding characteristics.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, focused on false positives only; sensitivity comparison not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Versus Radiologist False-Positives on Digital Breast Tomosynthesis Examinations in a Population-Based Screening Program.

studies.design: Retrospective validation within UKLS screening trial
studies.ai_system: AI nodule volume doubling time software
studies.finding: Assessing nodule growth (VDT) on 939 follow-up LDCT scans. Against expert panel AI had lowest 3-month negative misclassification rate (1/11, 9.1 %) vs human readers (18.2-63.6 %). AI flagged all 4 panel-positive cancers at 3 months while readers missed or delayed 1-3.
studies.limitation: Very few cancers (9); number of human readers not stated.
studies.title: AI performance for nodule volume doubling time in the follow-up of the UKLS lung cancer screening study compared to expert consensus and histological validation.

studies.design: Multicenter development/validation study with surgeon reader comparison
studies.finding: DeepComp predicted Clavien-Dindo grade ≥II complications after gastrectomy with AUC 0.888 internally and 0.824-0.869 externally. With DeepComp assistance, the mean sensitivity of 10 surgeons increased from 47.1% to 87.9% (P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Reader component is small and details of the assisted reading design are not reported; mainly retrospective data.
studies.title: A multimodal deep learning model for preoperative prediction of post-operative complications in gastric cancer.
studies.source: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology

studies.design: Reader study comparing algorithm with expert readers
studies.ai_system: Deep learning Cobb angle measurement software
studies.finding: Cobb angle measurement on spine radiographs. The algorithm's mean deviation from experts was 4.17 degrees vs the manual average intra-reader discrepancy of 5.16 degrees, with ICC exceeding 0.96.
studies.limitation: Comparison of algorithm deviation with intra-reader variability rather than a direct accuracy reference; dataset size not stated.
studies.title: Deep learning automates Cobb angle measurement compared with multi-expert observers.

studies.design: Multicenter blinded comparison of LLM vs expert answers to 50 real-world clinical questions
studies.humans: 3 senior radiation oncology experts (≥10 years experience)
studies.finding: Fifty real-world radiation oncology questions were answered by 3 senior experts and a local medical LLM, with blinded physician ratings. Quality did not differ significantly (mean 3.38 LLM vs 3.63 experts; P=.26). Answers were deemed potentially harmful in 16% of LLM cases vs 13% of expert cases (P=.63).
studies.limitation: Small sample of 50 questions and only 3 experts; subjective Likert ratings.
studies.title: Comparative Evaluation of a Medical Large Language Model in Answering Real-World Radiation Oncology Questions: Multicenter Observational Study.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of LLMs, ML models and pediatricians
studies.finding: Predicting serious bacterial infection in infants under 90 days in 742 ED patients. ChatGPT-4o had sensitivity 0.65, specificity 0.83, MCC 0.41; Claude 0.60/0.86, MCC 0.42; Gemini 0.43/0.94, MCC 0.43. Pediatricians' majority vote yielded sensitivity 0.69, specificity 0.81, MCC 0.43, comparable to top LLMs.
studies.limitation: Retrospective records; number of pediatricians not stated.
studies.title: Can general purpose large language models assist pediatricians in predicting infants with serious bacterial infection?
studies.source: BMC medical informatics and decision making

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of AI models with ophthalmologists
studies.finding: Differentiation of acute angle closure with or without zonulopathy on ultrasound biomicroscopy across 537 eyes. The best AI model achieved a macro-AUC of 0.9046 at 0.03 s per image, while ophthalmologists' UBM image analysis achieved a mean accuracy of 64.17% at 20.13 s per image.
studies.limitation: The AI and ophthalmologist results use different metrics, and the number of ophthalmologists is not stated.
studies.title: Deep learning-based automatic differentiation of acute angle closure with or without zonulopathy using ultrasound biomicroscopy: a comparison of diagnostic performance with ophthalmologists.

studies.design: Retrospective evaluation of a hybrid AI/radiologist reading strategy
studies.ai_system: AI mammography model with uncertainty quantification
studies.finding: Screening mammography on 41 469 examinations, in which AI made recall decisions only when confident. Hybrid reading gave a recall rate of 23.6‰ and a cancer detection rate of 6.6‰, similar to standard double reading (23.9‰ and 6.6‰), with 61.9% of examinations read by radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective simulation; not prospectively deployed.
studies.title: AI Should Read Mammograms Only When Confident: A Hybrid Breast Cancer Screening Reading Strategy.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on case reports and mock cases
studies.finding: Differential diagnosis for 82 clinical descriptions. Physicians outperformed Bard in top 10 (56.1% vs 82.9%, P < .001), top 5 (53.7% vs 78.0%) and top diagnosis (40.2% vs 64.6%); in mock cases differences were not significant for top 10 and top 5 but were for top diagnosis (60.0% vs 90.0%, P = .02).
studies.limitation: Small case set from published case reports and mock vignettes; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Comparative Evaluation of Diagnostic Accuracy Between Google Bard and Physicians.

studies.design: Retrospective real-world validation
studies.finding: In 527 consecutive non-contrast head CTs, VeriScout detected hemorrhage with sensitivity 0.92 and specificity 0.96, versus general radiologists' sensitivity 0.88 and specificity 0.98. The AI detected 13/14 subarachnoid hemorrhages.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single dataset; number of radiologists not stated; mixed sensitivity/specificity trade-off.
studies.title: Real world validation of an AI-based CT hemorrhage detection tool.

studies.design: Single-center retrospective study comparing ML model antibiotic selection with original ED prescribers
studies.finding: For empirical antibiotic choice in ED patients with UTI, the GBDT model was compared with the original ED prescribers on the use of ineffective antibiotics. The probability of using ineffective antibiotics was significantly lowered by 20% with the model through customization of the decision threshold.
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective comparison against historical prescriptions; not tested prospectively.
studies.title: Machine learning model for predicting ciprofloxacin resistance and presence of ESBL in patients with UTI in the ED.

studies.design: Reader study on 100 test fundus images
studies.ai_system: Deep convolutional ensemble of five InceptionV3 CNNs
studies.finding: Classification of fundus photographs into DR, glaucoma, AMD and normal. Ophthalmologists achieved mean accuracy of 72.7% vs 79.2% for the DCE (p=0.03); DR F1-score 76.8% vs 57.5% (p=0.01), with non-significant differences for other classes.
studies.limitation: Small test set of 100 images from public datasets.
studies.title: Ensemble of deep convolutional neural networks is more accurate and reliable than board-certified ophthalmologists at detecting multiple diseases in retinal fundus photographs.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to clinician annotations
studies.ai_system: CNN for placenta classification and segmentation
studies.finding: The model's image classification accuracy (81%) was lower than experts' and trainees'. For delineating the placenta it outperformed all clinicians, IoU = 0.75 vs 0.69, 0.66, 0.59.
studies.limitation: Retrospective image set; results depend on task (classification vs segmentation).
studies.title: Multi-centre deep learning for placenta segmentation in obstetric ultrasound with multi-observer and cross-country generalization.

studies.design: Reader comparison on wrist radiographs
studies.humans: Board-certified radiologist, hand surgery resident, medical student
studies.finding: Distal radius fracture detection on wrist radiographs. ChatGPT 4 had sensitivity 0.88, specificity 0.98, AUC 0.93, surpassing the medical student (AUC 0.85; p = 0.04) but lagging behind the hand surgery resident (AUC 0.985; p = 0.014).
studies.limitation: Very few human readers (one per level); single-study retrospective image set.
studies.title: Diagnostic power of ChatGPT 4 in distal radius fracture detection through wrist radiographs.
studies.source: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery

studies.design: Retrospective model development with external validation and reader comparison
studies.finding: Differentiating early from late hip avascular necrosis on MRI. The ensemble achieved external AUC of 85.5% with no significant difference from expert MSK radiologists (p = 0.22 and 0.092).
studies.limitation: Small external cohort (49 patients) and only two readers.
studies.title: Deep learning enables the differentiation between early and late stages of hip avascular necrosis.

studies.design: Retrospective two-centre radiomics model development with comparison to radiologist CT reports
studies.ai_system: CT radiomics machine learning models and nomogram
studies.finding: For predicting central lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid microcarcinoma, five machine learning models outperformed radiologists' interpretation with AUCs ranging from 0.606 to 0.730 in the internal test set. The nomogram achieved AUCs of 0.800 and 0.803 in internal and external test sets.
studies.limitation: Retrospective comparison against routine radiology reports; small external test set (n = 27); radiologist AUC not stated in abstract.
studies.title: Development and Validation of a Computed Tomography-Based Radiomics Nomogram for the Preoperative Prediction of Central Lymph Node Metastasis in Papillary Thyroid Microcarcinoma.

studies.design: Retrospective single-ED study
studies.finding: For identifying RV dysfunction from ECGs in 116 acute PE patients, QCG-RVDys achieved an AUC of 0.895 (binarized 0.845). It significantly outperformed all expert clinicians, whose AUCs ranged from 0.628 to 0.683.
studies.limitation: Small single-center retrospective sample; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Screening for RV Dysfunction Using Smartphone ECG Analysis App: Validation Study with Acute Pulmonary Embolism Patients.

studies.design: Model development with reader comparison on test set
studies.humans: Six general dentists and three oral surgery specialists
studies.finding: Classification of 11 classes of oral mucosal lesions on intraoral photographs. The model performed comparable to specialists (p = 0.93) and significantly better than general dentists (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Small test set (n = 282) of photographs; few readers.
studies.title: Machine learning versus clinicians for detection and classification of oral mucosal lesions.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with internal and external testing
studies.finding: For PAS subtype classification, the DRC-2 model performed similarly to radiologists (P = 0.773 and 0.579 internal; P = 0.429 and 0.874 external). DRC-1 achieved AUC 0.850 and 0.841 for PAS diagnosis.
studies.limitation: Retrospective with modest cohorts; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Deep Learning Radiomic Analysis of MRI Combined with Clinical Characteristics Diagnoses Placenta Accreta Spectrum and its Subtypes.
studies.source: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

studies.design: Development and validation study with clinician comparison
studies.finding: Prediction of postoperative complications and mechanical ventilation duration after congenital heart surgery in 256 cases. A poll of the k-most similar patients achieved better prediction than the average of 3 clinicians, and with CHDmap support clinicians substantially improved their predictive capabilities. Best model AUCs were 0.810 and 0.926.
studies.limitation: Only 3 clinicians; clinician performance figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A Patient Similarity Network (CHDmap) to Predict Outcomes After Congenital Heart Surgery: Development and Validation Study.

studies.design: Computerized reader study with and without CADe
studies.humans: Nurses, fellows and experts in colonoscopy
studies.finding: The task was polyp detection in a computerized test module. CADe assistance increased overall detection accuracy from 69.7% to 77.7% (OR 1.88), but accuracy decreased when CADe was wrong (OR 0.72). For SSLs and difficult polyps, assisted sensitivities (66.5%, 71.5%) were below standalone CADe (81.1%, 74.4%).
studies.limitation: Simulated computerized test rather than live colonoscopy; small reader sample.
studies.title: Impact of User's Background Knowledge and Polyp Characteristics in Colonoscopy with Computer-Aided Detection.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison with tumor board decisions
studies.finding: ChatGPT-4 treatment recommendations for 25 laryngeal cancer patients were compared with actual MDT decisions. Responses were totally coherent with MDT decisions in 72% of patients, Grade 2 in 20% and Grade 3 in 8%, with no totally incoherent responses.
studies.limitation: Only 25 patients; MDT decisions used as reference rather than independent outcome.
studies.title: ChatGPT-4 vs. multi-disciplinary tumor board decisions for the therapeutic management of primary laryngeal cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective validation of DNN angle measurement against three surgeons
studies.ai_system: Deep neural network for HVA/IMA measurement
studies.finding: On 92 foot radiographs, the model's MAE versus the surgeons' median was 1.3° for HVA, significantly smaller than the inter-rater difference of 2.0 ± 0.2° among surgeons. For IMA, MAE was 0.8°, not significantly different from the inter-rater difference of 1.0 ± 0.1°.
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective validation with only three surgeons as reference and comparators.
studies.title: Automatic estimation of hallux valgus angle using deep neural network with axis-based annotation.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of chatbot answers with online survey of clinicians
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-4, Claude-3-Opus, Gemini 2.0 Flash Experimental, Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek
studies.humans: General dental practitioners and orthodontic specialists
studies.finding: Answering eight true/false orthodontic FAQs. Chatbot answers differed significantly from those of general dental practitioners and orthodontists for almost all questions (p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Only eight questions; abstract does not state which side was more accurate or how many clinicians responded.
studies.title: Reliability of Large Language Model-Based Chatbots Versus Clinicians as Sources of Information on Orthodontics: A Comparative Analysis.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of chatbots with human experts on real referrals
studies.finding: On 143 real-world brain CT referrals, chatbot agreement with human experts on iGuide justification was limited (κ = 0.3), while the custom prediction model reached κ = 0.853. Chatbots correctly identified alternative imaging modality and region in 83/96 (86.5%) and 81/96 (84.4%) cases.
studies.limitation: Agreement with human raters used as reference rather than head-to-head accuracy; small single-dataset sample.
studies.title: Can ChatGPT and Gemini justify brain CT referrals? A comparative study with human experts and a custom prediction model.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison against surgeons
studies.finding: Detection and grading of fresh rib fractures on chest CT. The model achieved precision 0.963, recall 0.934 and F1 0.948 on the internal test set and outperformed thoracic surgeons of varying experience levels (all p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Small single-centre test set; number of surgeons not stated.
studies.title: Intelligent detection and grading diagnosis of fresh rib fractures based on deep learning.

studies.design: Retrospective single-institution validation
studies.finding: In 28 indeterminate thyroid nodules, radiologist malignancy classification had sensitivity 100%, specificity 33.3%, PPV 33.3%, NPV 100%, versus the AI-adapter's sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 76.2%, PPV 54.5%, NPV 94.1%.
studies.limitation: Very small retrospective single-institution sample (28 nodules).
studies.title: Avoidable biopsies? Validating artificial intelligence-based decision support software in indeterminate thyroid nodules.

studies.design: Deep learning framework development with pathologist reader study with and without AI assistance
studies.ai_system: Deep learning whole-slide image classifier for sebaceous vs squamous cell carcinoma
studies.finding: Distinguishing eyelid sebaceous gland carcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma on whole slide images. Pathologists' accuracy improved with the AI framework (60.0 ± 9.8% vs. 76.8 ± 9.6%). The AI alone had external test accuracy of 22.22% for SGC and 77.78% for SC.
studies.limitation: Small external test set (36 WSIs) with poor external AI accuracy for SGC; number of pathologists not stated.
studies.title: AI assistance enhances histopathologic distinction between sebaceous and squamous cell carcinoma of the eyelid.

studies.design: Retrospective multicohort comparison of AI-generated and radiologist-written chest radiograph reports
studies.ai_system: Generative AI chest radiograph report algorithm
studies.humans: Radiologists who wrote reports; panel of seven thoracic radiologists as evaluators
studies.finding: Acceptability under the standard criterion did not differ between AI-generated and radiologist-written reports (88.4% vs 89.2%; P = .36), but under the stringent criterion AI reports were less acceptable (66.8% vs 75.7%; P < .001). For referable abnormalities, AI reports had higher sensitivity (81.2% vs 59.4%) but lower specificity (81.0% vs 93.6%).
studies.limitation: The design is retrospective, and the number of report-writing radiologists is not stated.
studies.title: Clinical Validation of a Generative Artificial Intelligence Model for Chest Radiograph Reporting: A Multicohort Study.

studies.design: Model development with clinician comparison
studies.finding: For predicting breast cancer molecular subtypes from mammography and ultrasound, MDL-IIA achieved MCC of 0.837 for 4 categories and AUC 0.929 for Luminal vs Non-Luminal. Results significantly outperformed clinicians' predictions based on imaging.
studies.limitation: Clinician numbers and performance figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Predicting breast cancer types on and beyond molecular level in a multi-modal fashion.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Ensemble ResNet-50 DCNN on ultrasound plus clinical variables
studies.finding: For predicting cervical lymph node metastasis in clinically node-negative PTC on the external set, the model vs averaged radiologists had accuracy 0.72 versus 0.59 (p = 0.074), sensitivity 0.75 versus 0.58 (p = 0.039), and specificity 0.69 versus 0.60 (p = 0.078).
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of radiologists not stated and only sensitivity difference significant.
studies.title: Deep learning predicts cervical lymph node metastasis in clinically node-negative papillary thyroid carcinoma.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with cross-validation and physician comparison on a subset
studies.finding: Predicting five-point Deauville scores from PET/CT reports. DA RoBERTa reached 77.4% ± 3.4 five-class accuracy versus 66% for a physician on a subset of the data.
studies.limitation: Single physician on a subset of data; single institution.
studies.title: Domain-adapted Large Language Models for Classifying Nuclear Medicine Reports.

studies.design: Validation study on recordings with comparison against clinicians on a subset
studies.ai_system: FDA-cleared deep learning murmur detection algorithms
studies.finding: Detection of structural heart murmurs from digital stethoscope recordings against echocardiogram gold standard. Algorithm accuracy was 84.7% versus average clinician accuracy of 77.9%.
studies.limitation: Clinician comparison only on a subset of recordings, listening to recordings rather than live auscultation.
studies.title: Deep Learning Algorithms to Detect Murmurs Associated With Structural Heart Disease.
studies.source: Journal of the American Heart Association

studies.design: Retrospective population-wide simulation of AI-integrated screening scenarios
studies.humans: Screening radiologists (standard double reading with arbitration)
studies.finding: Breast cancer screening on 249 402 mammograms compared AI replacing first reader, second reader, or triage against double reading. AI first showed no difference in accuracy except higher arbitration rate (+0.99%); AI second had lower sensitivity (-1.58%); AI triage had higher sensitivity (+1.33%), PPV (+0.36%) and NPV (+0.01%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective simulation of workflows rather than live deployment.
studies.title: AI-integrated Screening to Replace Double Reading of Mammograms: A Population-wide Accuracy and Feasibility Study.

studies.design: Model development with internal and external validation plus reader study of 50 patients
studies.ai_system: HEPNET deep learning model on H&E whole-slide images
studies.finding: Distinguishing intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma from colorectal liver metastasis on whole-slide images. HEPNET surpassed the performance of 6 pathology experts in a reader study of 50 patients (P = .0005) and boosted the performance of resident pathologists to the level of senior pathologists.
studies.limitation: Small reader study (50 patients, 6 pathologists); reader accuracy figures not given in the abstract.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Enabled Diagnosis of Liver Adenocarcinoma.

studies.design: Model development with external validation and reader evaluation
studies.ai_system: AI CAD for CBCT with denoising module
studies.finding: Discrimination of fungal ball, chronic rhinosinusitis and normal maxillary sinus on CBCT. Human diagnosis accuracy improved by 11% (from 71.7 to 83.0%).
studies.limitation: Number of readers and reader-study design unclear from the abstract.
studies.title: Enhanced artificial intelligence-based diagnosis using CBCT with internal denoising: Clinical validation for discrimination of fungal ball, sinusitis, and normal cases in the maxillary sinus.
studies.source: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine

studies.design: Model development with a test set compared against a radiologist
studies.ai_system: Single convolutional network with regression object detection
studies.finding: For TMJ osteoarthritis diagnosis on 350 CBCT images, the AI showed statistically higher agreement with the DC/TMD reference than the radiologist. Cohen's kappa differences were significant for all signs collectively (P = 0.0079) and for subcortical cysts (P = 0.0214).
studies.limitation: Compared against a single radiologist; the reference was set by two evaluators.
studies.title: An artificial intelligence model for the radiographic diagnosis of osteoarthritis of the temporomandibular joint.

studies.design: Prospective observational case comparison
studies.finding: Diagnosis of 26 glaucoma cases. GPT-4o scored 5.500 for primary diagnosis accuracy vs 8.038 for the best ophthalmologist, but for differential diagnosis GPT-4o (7.577) was comparable to Doctor A (7.615) and Doctor C (7.673) with the highest completeness (4.096).
studies.limitation: Only 26 cases and 3 ophthalmologists at a single center.
studies.title: A comparative study of GPT-4o and human ophthalmologists in glaucoma diagnosis.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre model development with human-machine comparison
studies.ai_system: Explainable boosting machine learning model on handcrafted CT features
studies.finding: Classification of benign vs malignant pulmonary nodules on preoperative CT. In human-machine comparison, the AUC of machine learning models was 90.4% (95% CI: 85.5%-94.8%) versus 60% (95% CI: 50%-71.4%) for radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; number of comparison radiologists and comparison test set not stated; model uses features extracted by radiologists.
studies.title: Prediction of benign and malignant pulmonary nodules using preoperative CT features: using PNI-GARS as a predictor.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with held-out test set compared against prospective radiologist assessment
studies.ai_system: Cascaded deep learning and random forest EPE grading workflow
studies.finding: For predicting histologic extraprostatic extension (EPE≥1), the model achieved sensitivity 0.67, specificity 0.73 and accuracy 0.72, versus radiologist sensitivity 0.81, specificity 0.62 and accuracy 0.66.
studies.limitation: Single radiologist comparator; single-centre test set of 127 patients.
studies.title: Automated Detection and Grading of Extraprostatic Extension of Prostate Cancer at MRI via Cascaded Deep Learning and Random Forest Classification.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-reader multi-case study
studies.ai_system: AI second reader for lung nodule detection on chest radiographs
studies.finding: 15 readers read 300 chest radiographs for lung nodules without and then with AI. Mean AFROC was 0.73 without AI and 0.81 with AI. Sensitivity was 72.8% vs 83.5%, and specificity was 71.1% vs 72.0%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study with sequential reads, not done in clinical practice.
studies.title: Effect of Artificial Intelligence as a Second Reader on the Lung Nodule Detection and Localization Accuracy of Radiologists and Non-radiology Physicians in Chest Radiographs: A Multicenter Reader Study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional blinded comparison of chatbot, drug database, and pharmacist answers
studies.finding: Responses to 200 real-world inpatient medication-use questions were rated against pharmacists' answers. The chatbot responded to only 160 (80%) questions, with 85% acceptable for clinical correctness, 65% for completeness, 71% for safety and 68% for usefulness relative to pharmacists.
studies.limitation: Comparators were pharmacists rather than physicians; chatbot version unspecified.
studies.title: Evaluation of inpatient medication guidance from an artificial intelligence chatbot.
studies.source: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists

studies.design: Multicentric model development and validation with surgeon comparison
studies.ai_system: Multi-step deep learning model for leg alignment on long leg radiographs
studies.finding: For alignment analysis on long leg radiographs, the DL model showed accuracy of 0.21 ± 0.18° to 1.06 ± 1.3° vs. 0.21 ± 0.16° to 1.72 ± 1.96° for surgeons, and clinically acceptable accuracy of 53.9%-100% vs 30.8%-100%. Analysis time was 22 ± 0.6 s for DL vs 101.7 ± 7 s for surgeons.
studies.limitation: Only three surgeons compared; retrospective radiograph datasets.
studies.title: Multicentric development and validation of a multi-scale and multi-task deep learning model for comprehensive lower extremity alignment analysis.

studies.design: Retrospective comparative study
studies.finding: GPT-4V interpreted hepatic ultrasound images for MASLD diagnosis. It showed limited interpretive accuracy compared with skilled radiologists. The radiologist comparison is reported without numbers in the abstract.
studies.limitation: The radiologist comparison is secondary and not quantified in the abstract.
studies.title: Exploring the potential of large language models in identifying metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: A comparative study of non-invasive tests and artificial intelligence-generated responses.
studies.source: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

studies.design: Retrospective model development with a radiologic reader study
studies.ai_system: StateViewer FDG-PET ML clinical decision support
studies.finding: In a reader study on differentiating posterior cortical atrophy from Lewy body dementia, readers using the model had 3.3 ± 1.1 times greater odds of a correct diagnosis than readers using the standard-of-care workflow.
studies.limitation: Small, narrow reader study within a model-development paper; number of readers not stated.
studies.title: An FDG-PET-Based Machine Learning Framework to Support Neurologic Decision-Making in Alzheimer Disease and Related Disorders.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with expert comparison
studies.finding: Classifying orbital CT as no TED, mild TED, or severe TED with compressive optic neuropathy. The model had 89.5% accuracy versus 70.0% accuracy for an oculoplastic surgeon in serial image testing.
studies.limitation: Single human comparator, single institution, small cohort of 141 patients.
studies.title: A Deep Learning Model for Screening Computed Tomography Imaging for Thyroid Eye Disease and Compressive Optic Neuropathy.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective diagnostic study; endoscopists read capsule endoscopy videos with SS Plus assistance vs conventional reading
studies.ai_system: SmartScan Plus (SS Plus) deep learning algorithm
studies.finding: In 342 magnetically controlled capsule endoscopy videos, SS Plus-assisted reading reduced images for review to 873.90 versus 44,322.73 with conventional reading, with reading time of 9.54 minutes. SS Plus identified 411 gastric and 422 small-bowel lesions versus 400 gastric and 368 intestinal lesions with conventional reading, and junior endoscopists remarkably improved their reading ability with assistance.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; number of endoscopists and quantitative reader accuracy not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A new artificial intelligence system for both stomach and small-bowel capsule endoscopy.

studies.design: Cross-sectional case-vignette diagnostic comparison
studies.humans: Two clinical experts, two final-year medical students, two general practitioners
studies.finding: GPT4 diagnosed 100 orofacial pain cases, reaching ICOP level 3 accuracy in 38% of cases. In a 24-case subset, its performance was comparable to non-expert human evaluators but was surpassed by clinical experts, who correctly diagnosed 54% of cases at level 3.
studies.limitation: Very small human comparison (six evaluators on 24 cases).
studies.title: Development and Evaluation of a GPT4-Based Orofacial Pain Clinical Decision Support System.

studies.design: Blinded comparison of answers to real-world clinical questions
studies.humans: Human-authored resource (Pearls4Peers); rated by 18 physicians and 21 content experts
studies.finding: Answers to 36 real-world clinical questions from ChatGPT versus a human-authored source were rated for usability and reliability. ChatGPT answers were not useful or accurate in 13.9% and 13.1% of cases, and were inferior to the human source in clarity, accuracy and thoroughness in 38.1%, 34.5% and 31% of cases.
studies.limitation: Small question set, ChatGPT 3.5 only; human comparator is a written resource rather than clinicians answering in real time.
studies.title: Comparison of the Usability and Reliability of Answers to Clinical Questions: AI-Generated ChatGPT versus a Human-Authored Resource.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-reader study comparing reads with and without the tool
studies.ai_system: Deep learning spinal cord lesion segmentation tool
studies.finding: Detection of MS spinal cord lesions on sagittal T2 and STIR MRI in 50 patients. With the tool, mean sensitivity improved from 74.3% to 79.2% (p < 0.0001), while precision did not differ (69.0% vs 70.1%; p = 0.08).
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study on 50 patients.
studies.title: Evaluation of a deep learning segmentation tool to help detect spinal cord lesions from combined T2 and STIR acquisitions in people with multiple sclerosis.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study
studies.humans: Three associate consultants and three senior residents in radiology
studies.finding: Detection of paediatric appendicular fractures on 500 radiographs. The AI alone showed the highest accuracy (AUC 0.97), and the two readers aided with AI had higher AUCs than readers without AI support, reported as statistically significant.
studies.limitation: Only one reader per group used AI; retrospective single-centre design with unclear reported statistics.
studies.title: Accuracy of radiologists and radiology residents in detection of paediatric appendicular fractures with and without artificial intelligence.

studies.design: Model development with multicenter validation
studies.finding: For identifying AEH and EC on hysteroscopy, ECCADx attained 95.2% sensitivity and 91.3% specificity internally and 92.1% sensitivity with 100% specificity externally. It often surpassed experienced endoscopists, being comparable or superior to human experts.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives no endoscopist figures or numbers; retrospective image-based validation.
studies.title: A deep learning-based computer-aided diagnosis system for detecting atypical endometrial hyperplasia and endometrial cancer through hysteroscopy.

studies.design: Model development with reader comparison
studies.finding: For diagnosing scapular fractures on CT, accuracy was 97.78% for CNN combined with orthopedist interpretation, 82.95% for orthopedists alone and 92.05% for CNN alone (P < 0.05). Specificity, PPV and AUC were also higher with the combined approach.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 90 patients; number of orthopedists not stated.
studies.title: Faster R-CNN model for target recognition and diagnosis of scapular fractures.

studies.design: Cross-sectional diagnostic study
studies.finding: For detecting vertical misfit of implant crowns on periapical radiographs, ResNet-50 accuracy was 92.7% vs a dentist mean of 93.3%. Sensitivity/specificity were 90.3%/93.8% for AI vs 90.1%/95.1% for dentists, with no significant difference (p > 0.05).
studies.limitation: Small test set with five dentists, and the reference was set by two experts.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence in Detecting and Segmenting Vertical Misfit of Prosthesis in Radiographic Images of Dental Implants: A Cross-Sectional Analysis.

studies.design: Model development with retrospective evaluation on three clinical datasets
studies.finding: Orthodontic/maxillofacial treatment outcome prediction and cephalometric landmark detection. DeepFuse attained an overall treatment prediction accuracy of 85.6%, reported as significantly outperforming experienced clinicians; clinician figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Clinician comparison mentioned only briefly without numbers or reader details; model-development paper.
studies.title: Multimodal deep learning for cephalometric landmark detection and treatment prediction.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre development of smartphone app with comparison against otolaryngologists
studies.finding: Detection of nasopharyngeal carcinoma on nasal endoscopic images. The app achieved sensitivity of 96.39% and specificity of 99.91% for NPC, outperforming nine experienced otolaryngologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective image-based study; otolaryngologists' figures not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: A deep learning based smartphone application for early detection of nasopharyngeal carcinoma using endoscopic images.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter study with external validation
studies.ai_system: SAM segmentation plus DenseNet-121 multimodal DL classifier
studies.humans: Radiologists using O-RADS MRI and subjective assessment
studies.finding: Benign vs malignant ovarian lesion classification on MRI. The DL model achieved AUC 0.85 internally and 0.79 on external datasets, comparable with radiologists (AUC: 0.84-0.93; all P > .05).
studies.limitation: Retrospective with small external datasets; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: MRI-based Ovarian Lesion Classification via a Foundation Segmentation Model and Multimodal Analysis: A Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Simulated vignette comparison
studies.ai_system: RAG-enhanced LLM grounded in EAU and AUA guidelines
studies.finding: Guideline-concordant PSA testing recommendations for 44 fictional outpatient scenarios. The RAG-LLM was concordant in 95.5% (210/220) versus junior clinicians at 62.3% (137/220) closed-book and 74.1% (163/220) open-book (P<.001 for both).
studies.limitation: Synthetic cases in a controlled simulation with only five junior clinicians.
studies.title: Performance of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Large Language Models in Guideline-Concordant Prostate-Specific Antigen Testing: Comparative Study With Junior Clinicians.

studies.design: Retrospective image reader comparison
studies.finding: On 100 images (50 IH, 50 other vascular anomalies), GPT achieved 75% accuracy, F1 0.742 and AUC 0.80 for identifying infantile hemangioma. Comparison with pediatricians showed comparable results (p = 0.345).
studies.limitation: Small sample of four pediatricians and 100 images; pediatrician accuracy not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Digitizing Diagnoses: Distinguishing Infantile Hemangiomas From Other Vascular Anomalies.

studies.design: Benchmark against pathologists plus a before/after consultation reader study
studies.finding: ChatGPT performed worse than pathologists in reaching the correct diagnosis on histopathology questions. When pathologists consulted ChatGPT on challenging virtual slides, it provided limited help.
studies.limitation: The abstract reports no quantitative numbers or sample size.
studies.title: Bridging bytes and biopsies: A comparative analysis of ChatGPT and histopathologists in pathology diagnosis and collaborative potential.

studies.design: Comparison of GPT-4 differential diagnoses on unpublished challenging cases and 45 common vignettes against previously reported physician accuracy
studies.finding: GPT-4 generated differential diagnoses for challenging and common clinical cases. On unpublished challenging cases GPT-4 had 61.1% correct in its top 6 versus the previously reported 49.1% for physicians; on 45 common vignettes it had the correct diagnosis in its top 3 100% of the time versus 84.3% for physicians.
studies.limitation: Physician performance taken from earlier reports rather than measured head-to-head, and common cases may have been in GPT-4's training data.
studies.title: Diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4 on common clinical scenarios and challenging cases.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre model development with external validation compared against radiologist interpretations
studies.ai_system: Ensemble multi-task deep learning framework on multi-parametric MRI
studies.humans: Three junior and two senior radiologists
studies.finding: For three-category classification of primary bone tumors (benign/intermediate/malignant) on the external validation set, the framework achieved accuracy of 78.3%. This was superior to three junior radiologists (accuracy: 65.2%, 69.6%, and 69.6%) and comparable to two senior radiologists (accuracy: 78.3% and 78.3%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with a small external validation set (N = 53) and only five radiologists.
studies.title: Automatic detection, segmentation, and classification of primary bone tumors and bone infections using an ensemble multi-task deep learning framework on multi-parametric MRIs: a multi-center study.

studies.design: Blinded vignette-based comparison of treatment plans from GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and a clinical rheumatology board, rated by four rheumatologists
studies.finding: For 20 fictional rheumatic disease vignettes (160 ratings), raters preferred the rheumatology board's treatment plans in 68.8% (110/160) of cases versus GPT-4 (16.3%; 26/160) and GPT-3.5 (15.0%; 24/160). Rheumatologists' plans received significantly higher ratings in guideline adherence, medical appropriateness, completeness and overall quality, with no significant safety difference between the board and GPT-4 first-line plans.
studies.limitation: Small set of 20 fictional vignettes with only four raters; not real patient care.
studies.title: Vignette-based comparative analysis of ChatGPT and specialist treatment decisions for rheumatic patients: results of the Rheum2Guide study.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic study comparing AI with manual readers
studies.finding: For leg alignment measurements on long-leg radiographs of 95 patients, the AI showed no significant differences from manual reads. Mean absolute differences were 0.5° or less, and AI intra-observer ICC was 1.0.
studies.limitation: Single cohort; measurement agreement rather than outcomes.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-based analyses of varus leg alignment and after high tibial osteotomy show high accuracy and reproducibility.
studies.source: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA

studies.design: Deep learning model development with test-set comparison against expert and novice readers
studies.ai_system: Convolutional neural network on apical echocardiography videos
studies.finding: The task was detecting regional wall motion abnormalities on transthoracic echocardiography, measured by F1 score. Expert and DL model F1 scores were numerically similar for 6 of 7 regions (e.g., any RWMA 90 vs 94), but lower for the DL model in the anteroseptal region (75 vs 89). The DL model outperformed novices 1 (P = .002) and 2 (P = .02) for any RWMA.
studies.limitation: Ground truth defined by expert readers, and the novice comparison involved only a few readers.
studies.title: Echocardiographic Detection of Regional Wall Motion Abnormalities Using Artificial Intelligence Compared to Human Readers.
studies.source: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of radiologist BI-RADS vs KOIOS AI against pathology in 403 biopsied breast ultrasound cases
studies.finding: In 403 ultrasound-guided biopsies, BI-RADS 4-6 cases were malignant in 54.7%, whereas biopsying only KOIOS suspicious/probably malignant would yield 187 malignant lesions of 312 (60%) but miss 10 cancers. Using KOIOS, 17 BI-RADS 3 biopsies could have been avoided.
studies.limitation: Single-institution retrospective selected cohort of biopsied lesions; images selected by readers.
studies.title: AI: Can It Make a Difference to the Predictive Value of Ultrasound Breast Biopsy?

studies.design: Standardized test comparing the model with dentists
studies.humans: Two radiologists, two periodontists and one general dentist
studies.finding: For periodontal bone loss on 40 panoramic radiographs, the model had weighted sensitivity 0.23 and F1-score 0.29 for light to moderate loss. It could not diagnose severe loss (sensitivity, precision and F1-score = 0); the abstract does not report the dentists' comparative results.
studies.limitation: Tiny test set (40), with radiologists serving as ground truth.
studies.title: "Determining the efficacy of a machine learning model for measuring periodontal bone loss".

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of AI angle measurements with two radiologists on pelvic radiographs
studies.ai_system: Deep learning CNN for hip angle measurement
studies.finding: AI and manual radiologist measurements of Sharp, Tönnis and Center Edge angles showed no significant differences (all p > 0.05), with ICC and r values exceeding 0.75. The AI model measured faster than radiologists (p = 0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single dataset with only two radiologists and a 206-case test set.
studies.title: Deep learning-based automated measurement of hip key angles and auxiliary diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of CNN vs human experts on TMJ MRI
studies.finding: For TMJ effusion detection, the fine-tuning model had higher specificity than experts (87.25% vs. 58.17%) but lower sensitivity (80.00% vs. 57.43% favoring experts). The ensemble model accuracy exceeded experts (74.21% vs. 67.71%, p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Number of experts not stated; retrospective single dataset.
studies.title: Automatic detection and visualization of temporomandibular joint effusion with deep neural network.

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective model development with reader comparison and assisted reading
studies.ai_system: Multimodal ultrasound deep learning model (B-mode + strain elastography)
studies.finding: For malignancy prediction of TI-RADS 4 thyroid nodules, the model achieved AUC 0.937 (test) and 0.927 (external validation) and significantly outperformed three groups of radiologists. With model assistance, all three radiologist groups showed improved diagnostic performance.
studies.limitation: Radiologist numbers and assisted-reading figures not reported in abstract; retrospective design.
studies.title: Deep learning model for malignancy prediction of TI-RADS 4 thyroid nodules with high-risk characteristics using multimodal ultrasound: A multicentre study.
studies.source: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society

studies.design: Retrospective reader study with and without AI assistance
studies.finding: Emergency doctor reviewed 2,000 pediatric radiographs with and without AI. AI assistance improved reading sensitivity from 93.7% to 97.0% and accuracy from 88% to 94.9%.
studies.limitation: Appears to involve a single emergency reader; retrospective image set.
studies.title: Detecting pediatric appendicular fractures using artificial intelligence.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of chatbot vs provider responses to real EHR patient messages
studies.humans: Plastic surgeons and advanced practice providers
studies.finding: Ten breast reconstruction patient questions were answered by ChatGPT and providers. Accuracy did not differ (4.3 ± 0.9 vs 4.5 ± 0.6, P = 0.170), chatbot empathy was higher (2.9 ± 0.8 vs 2.0 ± 0.9, P < 0.001), and provider readability was better (53.3 ± 13.3 vs 36.0 ± 11.6, P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Only ten questions and a small number of graders.
studies.title: Comparing Provider and ChatGPT Responses to Breast Reconstruction Patient Questions in the Electronic Health Record.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic accuracy evaluation with qualitative human factors and productivity analysis
studies.finding: qXR was compared with a human radiologist against a microbiological reference standard for detecting pulmonary TB on chest radiographs. The abstract reports qXR displays near-human performance satisfying the WHO suggested accuracy profile, without giving numeric results.
studies.limitation: No quantitative accuracy figures in the abstract; single-site case study with comparison against a single radiologist.
studies.title: Towards human-AI collaboration in radiology: a multidimensional evaluation of the acceptability of AI for chest radiograph analysis in supporting pulmonary tuberculosis diagnosis.

studies.design: Crossover video study: trainees watched original and AI-enhanced surgical videos more than 4 weeks apart
studies.ai_system: AI anatomical recognition system for robot-assisted esophagectomy
studies.finding: Trainee surgeons identified the recurrent laryngeal nerve in RAMIE videos, measured as time to confidence levels CL1 and CL2. For the right RLN, times with versus without AI were CL1 134 vs. 178 s (p < 0.001) and CL2 233 vs. 325 s (p < 0.001). Average times were reduced with AI in all cases.
studies.limitation: Only five surgical videos and eight trainees were used, and recognition time was measured on recorded videos rather than in live surgery.
studies.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Timing of Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Recognition during Robot-Assisted Minimally Invasive Esophagectomy.

studies.design: Development study comparing CNN grading of facial palsy videos/images against experienced clinicians
studies.ai_system: Convolutional neural network models for each of 13 Sunnybrook Facial Grading System elements
studies.humans: Three clinicians experienced in facial palsy grading
studies.finding: The CNN graded 116 facial palsy patients and 9 healthy subjects on the Sunnybrook Facial Grading System and was compared with three experienced clinicians. Its inter-rater reliability was within the range of human observers, with average ICC of 0.87 for the composite score, 0.45 for resting symmetry, 0.89 for voluntary movement symmetry and 0.77 for synkinesis.
studies.limitation: Small sample with only three human raters; agreement-based comparison rather than accuracy against an independent reference.
studies.title: Automatic grading of patients with a unilateral facial paralysis based on the Sunnybrook Facial Grading System - A deep learning study based on a convolutional neural network.

studies.design: Retrospective analysis of recorded Iriscope videos interpreted by physicians and a deep learning model
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model trained on Iriscope images
studies.finding: Predicting malignancy of small peripheral pulmonary nodules from Iriscope endoscopy in 61 patients. Balanced accuracy was 85.4% for senior physicians, 66.7% for junior physicians and 71.5% for the DL model, which outperformed juniors but was not superior to seniors.
studies.limitation: Small single-series sample (61 patients); number of physician readers not stated.
studies.title: Human and Deep Learning Predictions of Peripheral Lung Cancer Using a 1.3 mm Video Endoscopic Probe.

studies.design: Multicenter development, MRMC reader study, and prospective real-world cohort
studies.finding: Classification of pancreatic cystic neoplasms on contrast-enhanced CT. AI assistance improved radiologists' AUC from 0.786 to 0.845 (p < 0.05) and reduced interpretation time by 23.7% (5.28 vs. 4.03 minutes/case); in a prospective cohort PCN-AI outperformed radiologist double-reading.
studies.limitation: Number of readers not stated; prospective cohort very small (11 patients cited).
studies.title: Deep learning CT model for stratified diagnosis of pancreatic cystic neoplasms: multicenter development, validation, and real-world clinical impact.

studies.design: Retrospective cross-sectional comparison of readability of GPT-4 vs ophthalmologist-written responses to 200 patient questions
studies.finding: Readability of responses to 200 patient questions about ophthalmic surgery was compared with six metrics. GPT-4 responses were at a higher grade level across all metrics (e.g., FK-GL 13.19 vs 10.71; FK-RE 34.39 vs 50.61) and used more complex words (24.42% vs 17.76%). Both required a 12th-grade education, exceeding NIH recommendations, with GPT-4 showing a greater gap.
studies.limitation: Measures readability only, not accuracy or quality; single source of questions and responses.
studies.title: Eyes on the Text: Assessing Readability of Artificial Intelligence and Ophthalmologist Responses to Patient Surgery Queries.
studies.source: Ophthalmologica. Journal international d'ophtalmologie. International journal of ophthalmology. Zeitschrift fur Augenheilkunde

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of AI-CAD vs original radiologist interpretations
studies.finding: In 1534 diagnostic mammograms, AI-CAD at a 50% threshold had higher specificity (95.0% vs 86.2%), accuracy (91.7% vs 87.2%) and PPV (85.1% vs 69.5%) than radiologists. AUCs were comparable (0.886 vs 0.882, p = 0.75). In symptomatic patients AI AUC was higher (0.873 vs 0.815).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single dataset with threshold optimized on the same data.
studies.title: AI-CAD for diagnostic mammography: comparison to radiologists according to different indications.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on outpatient cases
studies.finding: ChatGPT-4o and two otologists diagnosed 15 outpatient vertigo cases. The model's diagnostic accuracy was comparable to a clinician with one year of experience but inferior to a clinician with five years of experience (differences among the three significant, p = 0.04).
studies.limitation: Very small sample: 15 cases and two clinicians.
studies.title: The role of ChatGPT-4o in differential diagnosis and management of vertigo-related disorders.

studies.design: Model development on multicenter pelvic radiographs with test-set comparison against 35 clinicians
studies.ai_system: YOLOv5 detection plus MobileNetV2, Xception, InceptionResNetV2 classifiers
studies.finding: Hip fracture detection on pelvic radiographs was compared. Classifier models achieved accuracies between 94.66% and 97.67% versus a clinician mean accuracy of 84.53%, and DNN models were significantly better in accuracy and speed (p < 0.0005, p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Retrospective test set; clinician specialties and reading conditions not detailed in abstract.
studies.title: An automated hip fracture detection, classification system on pelvic radiographs and comparison with 35 clinicians.

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison
studies.finding: On 112 paediatric elbow radiographs, AI sensitivity was 79.0% vs 64.9% for physicians (P = 0.088) and specificity 81.8% vs 87.3% (P = 0.439). The AI had an AUROC of 0.872.
studies.limitation: Small test set and five physicians; differences not statistically significant.
studies.title: Use of deep learning model for paediatric elbow radiograph binomial classification: initial experience, performance and lessons learnt.

studies.design: Model development with agreement analysis against ophthalmologist graders
studies.finding: Image quality assessment of ultra-widefield fundus photographs. Average agreement between the model and manual graders was 0.731 versus 0.603 average intergrader agreement (Cohen's weighted kappa).
studies.limitation: Agreement-based, not accuracy against independent reference; only three graders.
studies.title: Deep learning-based automatic image quality assessment in ultra-widefield fundus photographs.

studies.design: Comparative reader study on respiratory sound recordings
studies.ai_system: Machine learning model trained on 1162 audio samples
studies.humans: Clinicians experienced in treating COVID-19 or respiratory illness
studies.finding: Predicting COVID-19 from 24 respiratory sound recordings. The ML model achieved sensitivity 0.75 and specificity 0.83, whereas the best clinician achieved 0.67 sensitivity and 0.75 specificity; combining clinician and model predictions reached sensitivity 0.83 and specificity 0.92.
studies.limitation: Very small test set of 24 audio samples.
studies.title: Evaluating Listening Performance for COVID-19 Detection by Clinicians and Machine Learning: Comparative Study.

studies.design: Retrospective reinforcement learning development with off-policy evaluation on MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-III
studies.ai_system: Weighted dueling double deep Q-network reinforcement learning algorithm
studies.finding: For vital-sign management (mean arterial pressure, temperature) in ICU traumatic brain injury, the estimated survival rate was 88.016% under the AI strategy vs 81.094% under clinical doctors. Expected return was 28.978 vs 27.092.
studies.limitation: The AI estimate comes from retrospective off-policy evaluation, not from patients actually treated by the AI.
studies.title: Optimizing Vital Signs in Patients With Traumatic Brain Injury: Reinforcement Learning Algorithm Development and Validation.

studies.design: Mixed-methods randomised crossover experiment
studies.ai_system: Simulated AI advice for intracranial haemorrhage on head CT (basic and explainable)
studies.humans: 50 radiologists and 75 novices (non-radiologist physicians and medical trainees)
studies.finding: Participants read 50 head CTs under no AI, basic AI and explainable AI advice (80% correct advice). Both over-reliance and under-reliance occurred, with under-reliance more detrimental; correct explainable AI advice improved performance (OR=1·84, 95% CI 1·49-2·28) and confidence versus no advice, without reducing reading time (p=0·071).
studies.limitation: Experimental setting with controlled AI advice accuracy rather than live clinical deployment.
studies.title: Examining reliance patterns on AI advice in medical imaging: a mixed-methods, randomised, crossover experiment.

studies.design: Multicenter prospective cohort model development with head-to-head ophthalmologist comparison
studies.finding: Prediction of postoperative BCVA after cataract surgery. The model consistently outperformed both junior and senior ophthalmologists in predictive accuracy across subtypes; OCT-PRO internal MAE 0.128 logMAR.
studies.limitation: Ophthalmologist numbers and results not reported in abstract.
studies.title: OCT-PRO: A Multimodal Model Integrating OCT and Clinical Traits to Predict Postoperative Outcomes in Cataract Patients.

studies.design: Prospective multicenter development and external validation with cardiologist reader substudy
studies.finding: AI auscultation was compared with cardiologists for detecting left ventricular dysfunction (LVEF ≤40%). In a 100-patient reader substudy, AI auscultation outperformed cardiologist consensus in accuracy (82.0% vs. 62.0%; P=0.004).
studies.limitation: Small 100-patient reader substudy with consensus reading; industry-funded.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Auscultation to Identify Left Ventricular Dysfunction - Development and External Validation in Prospective Multicenter Studies.

studies.design: Model development with prospective evaluation of AI assistance
studies.ai_system: Dual cross-attention video deep learning model
