studies.finding: For blepharospasm diagnosis from smartphone videos, in a prospective independent dataset (N = 179), AI assistance improved junior ophthalmologists' diagnostic accuracy by up to 18.5%. Model diagnosis accuracy alone was moderate (0.674).
studies.limitation: Number of ophthalmologists not stated; gains reported as 'up to'.
studies.title: Smartphone video-based early diagnosis of blepharospasm using dual cross-attention modeling enhanced by facial pose estimation.

studies.design: Two-phase diagnostic accuracy study: history-based benchmark plus prospective multicenter evaluation
studies.finding: On 227 structured vertigo histories, Gemini-2.5-pro and o1 achieved the highest Top-1 accuracy (69.6%), and no LLM significantly outperformed the specialist panel majority vote (63.9%). In the prospective phase, the agent matched the reference diagnosis in 140 of 176 (79.55%) patients.
studies.limitation: The head-to-head comparison used static histories, partly simulated, with only 5 specialists.
studies.title: Conversational Large Language Models for Vestibular Diagnosis in Outpatient Clinics: Prospective Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study.

studies.design: Development/validation with prospective physician study, with vs without LLM support
studies.humans: Physicians of varying seniority and specialty
studies.finding: Physicians made acute ischemic stroke treatment decisions with and without LLM support. Accuracy increased from 73.1% to 88.6% (OR 2.86), with the largest gains among junior and nonspecialist physicians. TOAST classification also improved (OR 3.63).
studies.limitation: The number of physicians is not stated, and workflow and clinical outcomes were not assessed.
studies.title: A Multiagent Large Language Model Framework for Emergency Treatment Recommendation in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Development and Validation Study.

studies.design: Single-center randomized controlled trial (1:1), AI-assisted vs standard EUS
studies.ai_system: EUS-GUIDEQ real-time voice-guided AI navigation and quality-control system
studies.finding: In 266 patients randomized to AI-assisted (n=132) or standard EUS (n=134), overall station completeness was higher with EUS-GUIDEQ assistance (median 1.00 [0.94-1.00] vs 0.81 [0.75-0.88]; P<0.001). Procedure time was longer with AI assistance (12.70±3.23 vs 10.55±3.62 min; P<0.001).
studies.limitation: Single-center trial with a process-quality endpoint (station completeness) rather than diagnostic or clinical outcomes; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Real-time Voice-Guided Artificial Intelligence Improves Biliopancreatic Endosonography Quality: A Randomized Trial.
studies.source: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

studies.design: Reader study with washout, pathologists scoring before and after AI results
studies.ai_system: AI digital image analysis for HER2 IHC and ISH
studies.finding: HER2 status scoring of 67 primary and 30 metastatic breast tumors. AI agreement with ground truth was moderate on IHC (Cohen's κ 0.59) and substantial on ISH (κ 0.80); pathologists' agreement with AI scores was 80.6%, and the combined workflow reached κ 0.94.
studies.limitation: Only three pathologists and small cohort; abstract does not clearly report change in pathologist accuracy with AI.
studies.title: Determining HER2 Status by Artificial Intelligence: An Investigation of Primary, Metastatic, and HER2 Low Breast Tumors.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective reader study, readers with and without AI
studies.ai_system: Deep learning AI for digital breast tomosynthesis
studies.finding: Breast cancer detection on DBT in 258 women (65 cancers). Stand-alone AI AUC was 0.93; radiologists' AUC improved from 0.90 to 0.92 with AI (P = .003), and sensitivity rose from 85.44% to 87.69%. AI specificity was 89.64% vs 77.34% for radiologists, and reading time fell from 54.41 to 48.52 seconds.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study on an enriched case set; not live clinical screening.
studies.title: Impact of AI for Digital Breast Tomosynthesis on Breast Cancer Detection and Interpretation Time.

studies.design: Reader study with and without AI assistance
studies.ai_system: Two commercial AI CAD software systems
studies.finding: Pulmonary nodule detection on chest CT in 198 participants with 221 nodules. Residents' mean detection rate increased from 64 to 77% with AI assist, while seniors' remained largely unchanged (85% vs. 86%); neither software significantly affected LungRADS classification.
studies.limitation: Number of readers not stated; single dataset reader study.
studies.title: Impact of artificial intelligence assistance on pulmonary nodule detection and localization in chest CT: a comparative study among radiologists of varying experience levels.

studies.design: Retrospective screening cohort comparing standalone AI with radiologists' final BI-RADS assessments
studies.finding: Screening mammography in 89,855 Korean women. Sensitivity did not differ significantly between radiologists and AI (69.9% vs. 67.1%). AI had better specificity (93.0% vs. 77.6%), recall rate (7.1% vs. 22.5%) and AUC (0.8 vs. 0.74).
studies.limitation: Retrospective comparison against routine clinical reads; only 143 cancers.
studies.title: Screening mammography performance according to breast density: a comparison between radiologists versus standalone intelligence detection.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre development and external validation with radiologist comparison
studies.finding: EDAM detected and subtyped hepatic echinococcosis on plain CT with overall AUC 0·974 internally and 0·953 externally. EDAM outperformed most of the 52 enrolled radiologists in detecting both alveolar and cystic echinococcosis.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; radiologist comparison results not quantified in the abstract.
studies.title: Detection and subtyping of hepatic echinococcosis from plain CT images with deep learning: a retrospective, multicentre study.

studies.design: Randomised crossover reader study
studies.ai_system: SHG/TPEF AI digital pathology platform with qFibrosis
studies.finding: Fibrosis staging of 120 MASH biopsy slides with and without AI. AI assistance significantly improved inter-pathologist kappa, and concordance rose from 45% to 71% for inclusion cases, 38% to 55% for exclusion cases and 49% to 61% for treatment response.
studies.limitation: Only four pathologists; measures agreement rather than accuracy against outcomes.
studies.title: Utility of AI digital pathology as an aid for pathologists scoring fibrosis in MASH.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison against emergency physicians on 30 visits
studies.finding: For predicting critical outcomes (IHCA or ICU admission) from triage data, the model had AUROC 0.874. Compared with emergency physicians on thirty visits, it had better sensitivity (0.95 vs 0.41) and accuracy (0.90 vs 0.67).
studies.limitation: Physician comparison used only thirty randomly selected visits from a single hospital; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Clinical narrative-aware deep neural network for emergency department critical outcome prediction.

studies.design: Reader study of 20 readers reading facial CT with and without AI
studies.humans: 20 readers of varying experience (physicians and radiologists)
studies.finding: For nasal bone fracture detection on CT in 252 patients, the AI alone had 84.78% sensitivity, 86.67% specificity and AUC 0.857. AI-aided reading had higher sensitivity (94.00 ± 3.17% vs 83.52 ± 10.16%), specificity (89.75 ± 6.15% vs 77.55 ± 11.38%) and AUC (0.92 ± 0.04 vs 0.81 ± 0.10) than unaided reading; readers with 11-15 years' experience showed no evidence of improved sensitivity and AUC.
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective dataset; benefit not seen in most experienced readers.
studies.title: Assessment of artificial intelligence-aided reading in the detection of nasal bone fractures.
studies.source: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

studies.design: Diagnostic study with sequential reader study (without then with AI)
studies.finding: Differentiating colon carcinoma from acute diverticulitis on CT. The CNN reached sensitivity 83.3% and specificity 86.6% vs mean reader 77.6% and 81.6%; with AI support readers improved to sensitivity 85.6% and specificity 91.3% (P < .001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective surgical cohort; sequential unaided-then-aided reading may bias results.
studies.title: Development and Validation of a Deep Learning Algorithm to Differentiate Colon Carcinoma From Acute Diverticulitis in Computed Tomography Images.

studies.design: Model development with test set comparison to a blinded radiologist
studies.humans: One radiologist with four years of experience
studies.finding: Detection of active spinal inflammation on STIR MRI in axSpA. The network had sensitivity 0.80 ± 0.03, specificity 0.88 ± 0.02 and AUC 0.87 ± 0.02, reported as comparable to a radiologist with similar sensitivity and specificity.
studies.limitation: Single radiologist comparator and small test set of 60 patients; radiologist figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A deep neural network for MRI spinal inflammation in axial spondyloarthritis.
studies.source: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society

studies.design: Reader study, sequential without then with AI output
studies.finding: Dermatologists classified 50 skin lesions as benign or malignant. Diagnostic sensitivity with the DDI-AI device was 86.1% vs 78.8% with DDI alone, and specificity 80.7% vs 75.9%; management sensitivity was 91.1% vs 84.3%.
studies.limitation: Sequential unblinded reader design on a small enriched image set, not live care.
studies.title: Clinical Utility of a Digital Dermoscopy Image-Based Artificial Intelligence Device in the Diagnosis and Management of Skin Cancer by Dermatologists.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study with two reading rounds, without and with radiomic score
studies.ai_system: Machine-learning radiomic model on PSMA PET/CT
studies.finding: Readers classified 178 PSMA-1007 bone uptakes as unspecific uptake or metastasis. The radiomic model reached accuracy of 84.69% but did not surpass expert readers; less-experienced readers improved significantly with radiomic scores (p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Only 4 readers, single retrospective cohort of 102 patients, and sequential reads 3 months apart.
studies.title: [18F]PSMA-1007 PET/CT-based radiomics may help enhance the interpretation of bone focal uptakes in hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients.
studies.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

studies.design: Physical high-fidelity simulation study of clinician-AI interaction
studies.ai_system: AI recommender system for sepsis drug dosing
studies.finding: Physicians prescribed two drugs for simulated septic patients before and after seeing safe or unsafe AI recommendations. 92% of clinicians rejected unsafe AI recommendations vs 29% of safe ones, and paid +37% gaze fixations to unsafe recommendations.
studies.limitation: Simulation setting; number of physicians not stated in abstract; no outcome comparison against unaided performance accuracy.
studies.title: Safety of human-AI cooperative decision-making within intensive care: A physical simulation study.

studies.design: Retrospective model development compared with manual triage
studies.finding: ED severity and department prediction across 161,198 visits. TextRNN achieved 86.23% for severity and 94.30% for departments, and the method reduced under-triage by 12.06% and over-triage by 17.92% compared to manual triage.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-centre data; comparator is triage nurses, not physicians.
studies.title: Criticality and clinical department prediction of ED patients using machine learning based on heterogeneous medical data.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre model development with reader study
studies.ai_system: Interpretable genetic algorithm-enhanced neural network (MRI radiomics)
studies.finding: Predicting induction chemotherapy response in nasopharyngeal carcinoma, junior doctors' AUC improved from 0.686 to 0.785 and senior doctors' from 0.736 to 0.836 with model assistance (p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; number of doctors not stated.
studies.title: An interpretable machine learning model assists in predicting induction chemotherapy response and survival for locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma using MRI: a multicenter study.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with endoscopist comparison
studies.finding: Detection of laterally spreading tumours on 3636 endoscopic images. The AI achieved accuracy 99.34%, sensitivity 96.88% and specificity 99.8%, significantly better than novice and senior doctors and at the same level as expert endoscopists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective still-image test set; endoscopist numbers and results not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A deep neural network improves endoscopic detection of laterally spreading tumors.

studies.design: Retrospective external validation cohort with a simulated combination of AI and PI-RADS
studies.ai_system: Biparametric MRI AI model for prostate cancer detection
studies.finding: In 144 patients, AI sensitivity was 86.6% for prostate cancer and 88.4% for clinically significant cancer, versus 85.7% (p=0.84) and 89.5% (p=0.80) for radiologists. A simulated combination of radiologist and AI improved csPCa sensitivity by 5.8% (p=0.025).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-clinic cohort. The combined approach was a simulation, not radiologists actually using the AI.
studies.title: External Validation of an Artificial Intelligence Algorithm Using Biparametric MRI and Its Simulated Integration with Conventional PI-RADS for Prostate Cancer Detection.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Multimodal multi-region nomogram (ResNet50 US deep learning + CT fat radiomics + clinical)
studies.finding: Prediction of central lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma. The nomogram had AUCs of 0.829 and 0.818 in internal and external test cohorts; under equal specificity or sensitivity its performance increased by 6.5 % or 2.9 % compared to radiologist assessments, described as comparable to radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; radiologist performance figures not fully reported in abstract.
studies.title: Multi-region nomogram for predicting central lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma using multimodal imaging: A multicenter study.
studies.source: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine

studies.design: Retrospective validation with reader performance study (with/without AI after washout)
studies.finding: Detection of intracranial hemorrhage on CT. The model alone showed 98.7% sensitivity, 88.5% specificity and AUROC 0.936; in the reader study, AUROC with JLK-ICH assistance (0.967) surpassed that without assistance (0.953; P = 0.009).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single tertiary-hospital data with only six non-expert readers in a reader study; no direct AI-vs-reader comparison reported.
studies.title: Deep learning-assisted detection of intracranial hemorrhage: validation and impact on reader performance.

studies.design: Model development with comparison against expert clinicians on 30 unseen cases
studies.finding: Diagnosis of pediatric SLE from clinical and laboratory data in 30 cases. Morgaf was 100% successful in recognizing lupus, the same as clinicians, and gave more precise recommendations for non-lupus cases (93.3%) than clinicians (70%) (p = 0.034).
studies.limitation: Very small single-centre sample of 30 test cases; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Closed circuit artificial ıntelligence model named morgaf for childhood onset systemic lupus erythematosus diagnosis.

studies.design: Deep learning development with hold-out test set compared against clinicians
studies.ai_system: ResNet-18 and other CNN or self-supervised models
studies.humans: An endodontist, an endodontic resident and an oral and maxillofacial radiologist
studies.finding: The task was detecting clinically negotiable MB2 canals on periapical images. ResNet-18 achieved 66.0% accuracy (95% CI, 63.0-68.9) on the test set, versus human accuracy ranging from 53.6% to 61.4%. There was no significant difference between the top AI model and the human experts (p > 0.05).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only three clinicians.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Detection of Clinically Negotiable Second Mesio-Buccal Canals in Periapical Images of Maxillary Molars.

studies.design: Multicenter model development with reader study with and without AI
studies.ai_system: Deep learning VCF detection tool for chest radiographs
studies.humans: Five clinicians of different experience levels
studies.finding: Detection of vertebral compression fractures on chest frontal radiographs. The model's sensitivity outperformed all five clinicians, and AI assistance raised patient-level sensitivity for junior clinicians from 56.1% to 81.6% and for senior clinicians from 65.0% to 85.6%.
studies.limitation: Small reader study of five clinicians; retrospective image-based design.
studies.title: Automatic AI tool for opportunistic screening of vertebral compression fractures on chest frontal radiographs: A multicenter study.

studies.design: Retrospective radiomics ML study compared with clinical reports on follow-up scans
studies.finding: For detecting active giant cell arteritis in 19 follow-up scans, the model had higher PPV (0.83 vs. 0.80), NPV (0.85 vs. 0.79) and accuracy (0.84 vs. 0.79) than the clinical report.
studies.limitation: Very small comparison set (19 scans) with no statistical testing reported.
studies.title: A Machine Learning Model Based on Radiomic Features as a Tool to Identify Active Giant Cell Arteritis on [18F]FDG-PET Images During Follow-Up.

studies.design: Retrospective AI development compared with surgeons' predictions from preoperative CT
studies.ai_system: Automatic 3D liver modelling and AI model for liver resection complexity
studies.humans: Surgeons viewing only the preoperative CT
studies.finding: In a 145-patient HCC cohort, the AI prediction of intraoperative liver resection complexity (accuracy 79.4±3.4%, AUC 85.1±3.2%) outperformed surgeons' individual and combined anticipated complexities.
studies.limitation: Surgeons' own scores and their number are not reported in the abstract. Single cohort.
studies.title: Automatic Generation of Liver Virtual Models With Artificial Intelligence: Application to Liver Resection Complexity Prediction.

studies.design: Retrospective model development compared with physician discharge decisions
studies.finding: Prediction of safe ICU discharge. The model had AUROC 0.85 in 2020 validation; physicians agreed with model predictions in 84.5% of patients, and patients discharged by physicians but not deemed ready by the model had relative risk of 72-h adverse outcomes of 2.32; the model identified readiness 5 to 9 hours earlier.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-centre data; comparison to physician decisions is indirect.
studies.title: Exploring timely and safe discharge from ICU: a comparative study of machine learning predictions and clinical practices.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development
studies.finding: Predicting cage subsidence after lumbar fusion. The combined model had test AUC 0.935 and outperformed predictions by two experienced surgeons.
studies.limitation: Test set of 30 patients and only two surgeons; surgeon figures not reported.
studies.title: Development of a deep learning radiomics model combining lumbar CT, multi-sequence MRI, and clinical data to predict high-risk cage subsidence after lumbar fusion: a retrospective multicenter study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter validation
studies.finding: Detection of incidental vertebral compression fractures on 474 CT scans. CINA-VCF had AUC 0.97, accuracy 93.7%, sensitivity 95.2% and specificity 92.9%, and outperformed clinical reports in a subgroup.
studies.limitation: Comparison with clinical reports only in a subgroup with no figures given.
studies.title: Validation of a Deep Learning Tool for Detection of Incidental Vertebral Compression Fractures.

studies.design: Clinical trial based on retrospective cohort
studies.ai_system: Glandy CAS ML system on facial images
studies.finding: Detection of active thyroid eye disease (CAS ≥3) from 756 facial photos. Glandy CAS had sensitivity 87.9%, specificity 95.8% and F1 0.88 versus ophthalmologists' sensitivity 60.4%, specificity 83.0% and F1 0.57.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, only three junior ophthalmologists, single specialist reference.
studies.title: AI-based assessment of Clinical Activity Score and detection of active thyroid eye disease using facial images: validation of Glandy CAS.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader study
studies.ai_system: Ensemble radiomics + deep learning + clinical CT model
studies.finding: Distinguishing benign from malignant ovarian tumors on CT, the model had higher accuracy (82% vs 66%) and specificity (89% vs 65%) than junior radiologists with comparable sensitivity (68% vs 67%). With model assistance, junior radiologists' accuracy rose to 81% vs 66%, specificity 80% vs 65%, and sensitivity 82% vs 67%.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 149 patients and 5 readers, single retrospective cohort.
studies.title: Machine learning combined with radiomics and deep learning features extracted from CT images: a novel AI model to distinguish benign from malignant ovarian tumors.

studies.design: Randomised-order crossover reader study with washout, 167 WSIs
studies.ai_system: Deep learning algorithm highlighting suspicious metastasis areas
studies.finding: Pathologists reviewed 167 breast sentinel lymph node slides with and without AI. Average reading time per slide was 129 seconds unassisted versus 58 seconds AI-assisted, an efficiency gain of 55% (P <0.001). Two of 3 pathologists improved sensitivity from 74.5% to 93.5% (P ≤0.006).
studies.limitation: Only three pathologists on an enriched dataset of challenging cases.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Helps Pathologists Increase Diagnostic Accuracy and Efficiency in the Detection of Breast Cancer Lymph Node Metastases.
studies.source: The American journal of surgical pathology

studies.design: Retrospective cancer-enriched screening sample
studies.finding: Screening mammography in BreastScreen Norway. AI score 10 captured 92.7% of screen-detected and 40.0% of interval cancers; in the densest breasts, AI sensitivity was 80.9% versus 62.8% for independent double reading.
studies.limitation: Retrospective enriched sample; single threshold; no prospective comparison.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence in BreastScreen Norway: a retrospective analysis of a cancer-enriched sample including 1254 breast cancer cases.

studies.design: Blinded expert evaluation of LLM vs expert answers on vestibular schwannoma questions
studies.finding: GPT and expert neurosurgeon answers to vestibular schwannoma management questions were rated blinded. GPT responses were often rated significantly higher than expert responses and were faster (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Very small number of questions and experts; subjective ratings.
studies.title: neuroGPT-X: toward a clinic-ready large language model.

studies.design: Retrospective simulation of AI integration strategies
studies.finding: Mammography screening across Germany, UK and Sweden. Versus the German programme (CDR 6·32, recall 4·11), standalone AI achieved non-inferior CDR 6·37 at recall 3·80, and programme-level decision referral achieved CDR 6·85 with recall 3·55 and 84% workload reduction.
studies.limitation: Retrospective simulation; no prospective deployment.
studies.title: Strategies for integrating artificial intelligence into mammography screening programmes: a retrospective simulation analysis.

studies.design: External validation cohort of 430 whole-slide images compared with consensus of three pathologists and PFS
studies.finding: PD-L1 TPS scoring in NSCLC to predict immunotherapy response. AI and pathologist TPS correlated (Spearman 0.925); for PFS, AI-based TPS gave HR 1.49 vs 1.36 for the 1%-49% group and HR 2.38 vs 1.62 for the <1% group, with clinical performance described as comparable.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; pathologist consensus of only three readers; concordance low (52.4%) in TPS <1% group.
studies.title: Clinical Validation of Artificial Intelligence-Powered PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score Interpretation for Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Response Prediction in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with radiologist comparison
studies.finding: Preoperative T-staging of rectal cancer on MRI with pathology as reference. The multiparametric DL model had an AUC of 0.854, versus 0.678 for the radiologists' assessment.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, single small test set (N = 52); number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Based Multiparametric MRI Model for Preoperative T-Stage in Rectal Cancer.
studies.source: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

studies.design: Population-wide retrospective screening study, 249,402 screenings
studies.finding: Breast cancer detection in screening mammography. At first-reader sensitivity, AI had lower specificity (97.5% vs 97.7%) and PPV (17.5% vs 18.7%); at first-reader specificity AI was comparable on all accuracy measures. AI detected fewer screen-detected cancers (1166, 1156 vs 1252) but more interval cancers (126, 117 vs 39).
studies.limitation: Retrospective; reference partly defined by radiologist double reading.
studies.title: Population-wide evaluation of artificial intelligence and radiologist assessment of screening mammograms.

studies.design: Blinded physician evaluation of auto-segmented versus manual contours
studies.humans: Six radiation oncologists rating manual delineations
studies.finding: Postprostatectomy CTV and OAR delineation. Contours were deemed acceptable or precise in 87% for DLAS versus 94% for manual delineations; for CTV, 54% for DLAS versus 73% manual.
studies.limitation: Single institution, small test sets, subjective blinded ratings.
studies.title: First Report On Physician Assessment and Clinical Acceptability of Custom-Retrained Artificial Intelligence Models for Clinical Target Volume and Organs-at-Risk Auto-Delineation for Postprostatectomy Patients.

studies.design: Multi-center prospective data collection with head-to-head reader comparison on 200 frames
studies.finding: Detection of nasopharyngeal carcinoma on endoscopic frames. On 200 frames NPC-SDNet achieved accuracy of 94.0% versus 68.9%-88.2% for rhinologists across expertise levels.
studies.limitation: Comparison on only 200 still frames; number of rhinologists not stated.
studies.title: Real-time artificial intelligence-assisted detection and segmentation of nasopharyngeal carcinoma using multimodal endoscopic data: a multi-center, prospective study.

studies.design: International cross-sectional multicenter reader study on 800 retrospectively collected fundus photographs
studies.humans: 30 clinicians: general ophthalmologists, optometrists, neurologists, internists, ED physicians
studies.finding: Classification of optic disc appearance (normal, papilledema, other abnormalities) on fundus photographs. The DLS error rate was 15.3% versus average error rates of 24.4%, 24.8%, 38.2%, 44.8% and 47.9% for general ophthalmologists, optometrists, neurologists, internists and ED physicians. The DLS had higher accuracy than 100% of clinicians for papilledema.
studies.limitation: Retrospective convenience sample of photographs; readers graded images without clinical context.
studies.title: Deep Learning System Outperforms Clinicians in Identifying Optic Disc Abnormalities.
studies.source: Journal of neuro-ophthalmology : the official journal of the North American Neuro-Ophthalmology Society

studies.design: Retrospective model development with radiologist comparison and external validation
studies.ai_system: Automated multitask deep learning system (VGG16 + RC-MTL) on shoulder MRI
studies.finding: For classifying supraspinatus tendon injuries, the system had average AUC of 0.98 and 0.97 in in-group and out-group datasets and outperformed radiologists in classifying groups 0-2.4 (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of radiologists and their metrics not reported in abstract.
studies.title: MRI-based automated multitask deep learning system to evaluate supraspinatus tendon injuries.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with specialist comparison
studies.finding: Diagnosis of prosthetic joint infection on 99mTc-MDP dynamic bone scintigraphy. On the independent test set the framework had accuracy 87.74% and AUC 0.957 for knee infection and 86.36% and AUC 0.906 for hip infection. It was superior to specialists for knee and consistent with them for hip.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; specialist figures and number not given in abstract.
studies.title: An artificial intelligence framework for the diagnosis of prosthetic joint infection based on 99mTc-MDP dynamic bone scintigraphy.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of ChatGPT-4-vision and pathologists staging fibrosis on digitized biopsy images
studies.finding: ChatGPT-4 staged fibrosis on 59 MASH biopsies with 81% accuracy on pathologist-selected fields and 54% on random fields, rising to 88% and 77% with in-context learning. Authors report accuracy overlapping that of expert liver pathologists; pathologists' own figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Small single set of 59 specimens; pathologist accuracy not reported numerically; performance depends on expert field selection.
studies.title: Assessing the diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT-4 in the histopathological evaluation of liver fibrosis in MASH.

studies.design: Retrospective evaluation against human reader and arthroscopy
studies.ai_system: Fine-tuned deep learning algorithm for scapholunate distance
studies.finding: Detection of scapholunate ligament insufficiency on wrist radiographs in 364 patients with arthroscopic reference. For Geissler stages ≤2 versus >2, the algorithm had sensitivity 74% and specificity 78%, compared with 77% and 80% for the human reader.
studies.limitation: Comparison against a single human reader.
studies.title: Evaluation of a newly designed deep learning-based algorithm for automated assessment of scapholunate distance in wrist radiography as a surrogate parameter for scapholunate ligament rupture and the correlation with arthroscopy.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter radiomics model development with comparison to expert radiologists
studies.ai_system: Deep learning 3D super-resolution DWI radiomics models (SVM, RF, LightGBM)
studies.finding: The task was predicting the prognosis of HIFU ablation of uterine fibroids from MRI. Expert radiologists achieved an AUC of 0.706. The SR-DWI models achieved AUCs of 0.868 (SVM), 0.824 (RF) and 0.821 (LightGBM), and the HR-DWI models reached up to 0.805.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; the number of radiologists is not stated.
studies.title: Predicting the Prognosis of HIFU Ablation of Uterine Fibroids Using a Deep Learning-Based 3D Super-Resolution DWI Radiomics Model: A Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Single-centre retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
studies.finding: Per-vessel prediction of invasive FFR ≤ 0.80 in 54 vessels. AUC was 0.91 for AI-QCT ISCHEMIA vs. 0.76 for CT-FFR and 0.62 for physician visual interpretation CAD-RADS ≥ 3.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective single-centre sample (44 patients, 54 vessels).
studies.title: Artificial intelligence coronary computed tomography, coronary computed tomography angiography using fractional flow reserve, and physician visual interpretation in the per-vessel prediction of abnormal invasive adenosine fractional flow reserve.
studies.source: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice

studies.design: Multicenter proof-of-concept model development with pathologist comparison and human-machine fusion
studies.ai_system: LGNet deep learning on frozen-section whole-slide images
studies.finding: Intraoperative discrimination of PCNSL from glioma and other lesions on frozen sections. LGNet achieved external AUROCs of 0.965 and 0.972 (vs glioma), outperformed several pathologists, and significantly improved pathologists' diagnostic performance.
studies.limitation: Proof-of-concept; number of pathologists and their metrics not stated in abstract.
studies.title: A multicenter proof-of-concept study on deep learning-based intraoperative discrimination of primary central nervous system lymphoma.

studies.design: Retrospective radiomics ML study compared with radiologists
studies.finding: For distinguishing ameloblastoma from odontogenic keratocyst on CBCT in 326 patients, XGBoost achieved accuracy 0.843 and AUC 0.872. The ML diagnostics performed better than radiologists; radiologist figures are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Retrospective with cross-validation only; radiologist numbers and results not reported.
studies.title: Application of machine learning in the preoperative radiomic diagnosis of ameloblastoma and odontogenic keratocyst based on cone-beam CT.

studies.design: Reader study, unaided then aided
studies.ai_system: CNN for distal radius fracture detection
studies.humans: 11 physicians (six surgeons in training, five hand surgeons)
studies.finding: Detection of distal radius fracture on 200 wrist radiograph pairs. AI assistance improved sensitivity from 80% to 87% and specificity from 91% to 95%; error rate fell from 14% to 9%.
studies.limitation: Sequential unaided-then-aided reading on selected images; no live care.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence in traumatology.

studies.design: Feasibility study comparing CNN and blinded expert readers on FF-OCT images
studies.finding: On 113 fresh Mohs specimens, readers averaged accuracy 88.1%, sensitivity 93.7%, specificity 58.3%. The AI model achieved accuracy 87.6 ± 5.9%, sensitivity 93.2 ± 2.1%, specificity 81.2 ± 9.2%.
studies.limitation: Small sample, especially for SCCs; only two readers.
studies.title: High-resolution full-field optical coherence tomography microscope for the evaluation of freshly excised skin specimens during Mohs surgery: A feasibility study.

studies.design: Single-centre retrospective reader study: dermatologists, AI, dermatologists + AI
studies.ai_system: Multimodal CNN (RegNetY400MF backbone) using clinical and dermoscopic images and clinical data
studies.finding: Classification of mycosis fungoides versus five inflammatory skin diseases. The AI model had higher accuracy, precision, sensitivity and specificity than dermatologists. With AI, dermatologists' average accuracy, sensitivity and specificity were 82.9%, 86.2% and 96.5% versus 71.5%, 74.6% and 94.1% without AI.
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective design without external validation.
studies.title: Early diagnosis model of mycosis fungoides and five inflammatory skin diseases based on a multimodal data-based convolutional neural network.

studies.design: Experimental study varying levels of AI explanation
studies.ai_system: AI clinical decision support with explanations for breast cancer diagnosis
studies.humans: Clinicians in roles related to breast cancer diagnosis
studies.finding: The experiment assessed how varying levels of AI explanation affected clinicians' trust and diagnostic accuracy in breast cancer. Increasing levels of explanation did not always improve trust or diagnostic performance; no numeric results are given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 28 clinicians and no quantitative results reported in the abstract.
studies.title: The impact of AI explanations on clinicians' trust and diagnostic accuracy in breast cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective data-simulated prospective study of breast ultrasound diagnosis
studies.ai_system: Continuous learning deep learning ensemble system
studies.finding: A continuous learning system was compared with 21 physicians for diagnosing breast masses on ultrasound. By training stage six, the system's diagnostic ability exceeded 20 of the 21 physicians.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; abstract gives no performance figures for either side.
studies.title: Towards precision medicine based on a continuous deep learning optimization and ensemble approach.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to expert reader
studies.ai_system: Deep learning models (e.g. ResNet152V2, InceptionResNetV2) on SPECT-MPI polar maps
studies.finding: Deep learning models diagnosed coronary artery disease from SPECT-MPI with invasive coronary angiography as reference; best per-patient AUC was 0.77 and per-vessel 0.71. The authors report model accuracy close to expert-level analysis, but the expert reader's figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single dataset with 100-patient test set; human comparison numbers not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-powered coronary artery disease diagnosis from SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging: a comprehensive deep learning study.
studies.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

studies.design: Retrospective radiomics machine learning study compared with radiologist assessment
studies.ai_system: Gaussian process classifier on NCCT radiomics features
studies.finding: The task was distinguishing CKD stages 1-3 from healthy kidneys on non-contrast CT. In the testing set, the AUC was 0.790 for the GP model versus 0.575 for radiologist assessments; in training it was 0.849 versus 0.570.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; the number of radiologists is not stated.
studies.title: Radiomics Analysis of Whole-Kidney Non-Contrast CT for Early Identification of Chronic Kidney Disease Stages 1-3.

studies.design: Retrospective cross-sectional study of 79 CBCT images
studies.ai_system: Deep learning tooth guide design pipeline
studies.humans: Senior and junior doctors performing manual design
studies.finding: Reconstructing donor tooth models for autologous transplantation guides. The DL group achieved the lowest RMS (0.335 ± 0.066 mm), not significantly different from a senior doctor (P = .688). DL took 0.017 ± 0.001 minutes versus 19.676 ± 2.386 (senior) and 30.613 ± 6.571 minutes (junior) (P < .001).
studies.limitation: Single center, small sample, few human designers.
studies.title: Autologous Transplantation Tooth Guide Design Based on Deep Learning.
studies.source: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons

studies.design: Cross-over reader study, 68 periapical radiographs with CBCT reference
studies.finding: Radiologists detected apical radiolucencies on 68 periapical radiographs with and without AI predictions. No statistically significant differences were found in AFROC-AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and ROC-AUC. Unaided reading significantly prolonged diagnostic time (β = 12, 95% CI, 11-13, P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Only four readers and 68 radiographs; fixed reading order (unaided first).
studies.title: The influence of a deep learning tool on the performance of oral and maxillofacial radiologists in the detection of apical radiolucencies.

studies.design: Real-world study with blinded AI-assisted re-reading compared to the original double reading
studies.ai_system: AI for rib fracture detection on CT
studies.finding: The task was detecting rib fractures on CT in 243 consecutive chest trauma patients. At patient level, AI-assisted radiologists' sensitivity was 94.2% versus 69.2% for double reading. Specificity was 100% versus 98.2% (noninferior).
studies.limitation: The AI-assisted reading was a retrospective re-read rather than live care; single cohort.
studies.title: AI-assisted radiologists vs. standard double reading for rib fracture detection on CT images: A real-world clinical study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter study with radiologist reader assistance evaluation
studies.humans: Radiologists (six assisted readers; six others rated outputs)
studies.finding: Ternary classification of pure ground-glass nodule invasiveness on chest CT in 848 patients. With GPT-4o assistance, six radiologists achieved an average improvement in pGGN invasiveness diagnosis; the abstract reports no specific accuracy figures for the radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; abstract gives no quantitative reader results; only six radiologists.
studies.title: Predicting Invasiveness of Lung Adenocarcinoma from Chest CT with Few-shot Vision-Language Ternary Classification Model.

studies.design: Retrospective study of 56 children with subperiosteal orbital abscess; AI vs physician CT proptosis measurement for predicting surgery
studies.ai_system: AI software for 3D CT proptosis quantification
studies.finding: AI and physician CT proptosis measurements were compared for predicting surgical drainage. AI volumetric and linear measurements had AUCs of 0.79 and 0.78, while the average physician measurement had an AUC of 0.70. The AI linear measurement was on average 1.2 mm larger and only moderately correlated with physicians (r = 0.53).
studies.limitation: Small retrospective single-centre sample (56 patients) with only two physicians.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Automation of Proptosis Measurement: An Indicator for Pediatric Orbital Abscess Surgery.

studies.design: Multicentre reader study of pathologists scoring IHC slides with and without AI assistance
studies.ai_system: Pretrained AI assistance tool for Ki-67, ER and PR quantification
studies.finding: Pathologists scored 204 breast cancer slides (72 Ki-67, 66 ER, 66 PR) with and without AI assistance. Agreement between scoring with and without AI was 87.6% for Ki-67 and 89.4% for ER/PR, and interobserver agreement rose slightly with AI support (Krippendorff α 0.69 to 0.72).
studies.limitation: Endpoint is agreement rather than accuracy against a reference standard; the improvement in agreement was small.
studies.title: Noninferiority of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Analysis of Ki-67 and Estrogen/Progesterone Receptor in Breast Cancer Routine Diagnostics.
studies.source: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc

studies.design: Two-arm multireader study of 120 HER2 IHC whole-slide images from four sites, pathologists without and with AI
studies.ai_system: Fully automated AI HER2 IHC scoring solution
studies.finding: Pathologists scored HER2 IHC on 120 slides without and with AI. Interobserver agreement increased from 75.0% to 83.7% and scoring accuracy from 85.3% to 88.0% with AI; for HER2 0 vs 1+, accuracy rose from 81.9% to 88.8%. The AI alone showed 92.1% agreement on slides with high-confidence ground truth.
studies.limitation: Small reader study (four pathologists, 120 slides) without live clinical use.
studies.title: Fully Automated Artificial Intelligence Solution for Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 Immunohistochemistry Scoring in Breast Cancer: A Multireader Study.

studies.design: Retrospective randomized crossover reader study with simulated 50% worklist reduction triage
studies.ai_system: Commercial deep learning-based detection algorithm for nine chest radiograph findings
studies.finding: Readers interpreted 1964 outpatient chest radiographs with and without DLD triage. Sensitivity was 82.6% without DLD and 83.5% in the 50% worklist reduction scenario (noninferior), and specificity increased from 86.7% to 90.4% (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-month dataset with simulated triage rather than live deployment.
studies.title: Use of artificial intelligence in triaging of chest radiographs to reduce radiologists' workload.

studies.design: Reader study on crowdsourced whole-slide prostate biopsy images
studies.ai_system: 5 public PANDA challenge algorithms and 2 commercial Gleason grading algorithms
studies.finding: Gleason grading of prostate biopsy whole-slide images. Pairwise quadratic weighted kappa among pathologists ranged from 0.777 to 0.916, while public and commercial algorithms showed agreement with pathologists with quadratic kappa ranging from 0.617 to 0.900. Commercial algorithms performed on par or outperformed top public algorithms.
studies.limitation: Agreement-based comparison without an independent reference standard; mainly compares algorithms with each other.
studies.title: Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence-Based Gleason Grading Algorithms "in the Wild".
studies.source: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc

studies.design: Single-institution study with retrospective and prospective participants, model vs radiologists
studies.ai_system: Radiomic SVM model on T2-weighted MRI, plus radiomic-clinical ensemble
studies.finding: Radiologists had accuracies of 83.7%, 88.1%, and 86.7% (consensus 88.1%) for ileal CD. The bowel-core radiomic model had 89.6% accuracy, significantly better than two of three radiologists, and the ensemble model (93.5%) exceeded radiologist consensus (p = .02).
studies.limitation: Single institution, 135 participants, three readers.
studies.title: Machine Learning Diagnosis of Small-Bowel Crohn Disease Using T2-Weighted MRI Radiomic and Clinical Data.

studies.design: Comparison of AI against an international pathologist panel on digitized biopsies
studies.ai_system: Two-stage deep learning system for BE dysplasia
studies.finding: On 55 digitized Barrett esophagus biopsies, the AI correctly graded 76.4% of whole-slide images, surpassing 53 of the 55 pathologists. For distinguishing nondysplastic from any dysplasia, the AI had an AUC of 0.94.
studies.limitation: Small test set of 55 biopsies.
studies.title: Deep Learning for Histopathological Assessment of Esophageal Adenocarcinoma Precursor Lesions.
studies.source: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective diagnostic study with external validation and radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: XGBoost Model URC (ultrasound features, radiomics, clinical)
studies.finding: Model URC achieved external AUC of 0.899 for distinguishing ≤3 cm HCC. It showed superior ability compared to all radiologists, and its assistance significantly improved diagnostic AUC for all radiologists (all P < 0.0001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective; radiologist numbers and values not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Development and validation of an ultrasound-based interpretable machine learning model for the classification of ≤3 cm hepatocellular carcinoma: a multicentre retrospective diagnostic study.

studies.design: Reader study, 500 CBCT volumes read without and then with AI
studies.finding: Three radiologists scored caries on 500 CBCT volumes without and then with AI. AUCs (unaided/aided) were 0.855/0.920, 0.863/0.917 and 0.747/0.903. Fleiss kappa rose from 0.325 to 0.468 and the best accuracy (0.939) was achieved with aided results.
studies.limitation: Only three readers in a sequential unaided-then-aided design.
studies.title: Evaluation of a Decision Support System Developed with Deep Learning Approach for Detecting Dental Caries with Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Imaging.

studies.design: Cross-sectional study of responses to 20 BPH patient questions in a simulated messaging environment
studies.finding: Responses to 20 BPH patient messages were rated by experts and non-medical volunteers. Expert accuracy was 4.5 (1.1) for chatbots vs 4.6 (1.2) for urologists (not significant), while completeness was 2.4 (0.8) vs 1.6 (0.6) (p < 0.001). Volunteers rated chatbots more empathetic, 3.0 (1.4) vs 2.1 (1.1) (p < 0.001), and preferred them.
studies.limitation: Simulated messages with only 4 urologists, 20 questions and few raters.
studies.title: Physician vs. AI-generated messages in urology: evaluation of accuracy, completeness, and preference by patients and physicians.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with human-machine comparison
studies.ai_system: Convolutional neural network for ONFH classification on MRI
studies.finding: The CNN classified ONFH with 87.8% internal and 83.8% external accuracy. In the human-machine comparison, the CNN outperformed or was comparable to deputy chief orthopaedic surgeons.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; human comparison results not quantified in the abstract.
studies.title: Development and Validation of an Automated Classification System for Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head Using Deep Learning Approach: A Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with reader study on external test set
studies.finding: VUR grading on voiding cystourethrograms. Deep-VCUG achieved AUCs of 0.944 (unilateral) and 0.924 (bilateral) on external testing and outperformed clinicians. With Deep-VCUG assistance, junior and senior clinicians' classification ability significantly improved.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, only four clinicians; clinician figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Development and multi-institutional validation of a deep learning model for grading of vesicoureteral reflux on voiding cystourethrogram: a retrospective multicenter study.

studies.design: Blinded survey evaluation of ChatGPT vs surgeon responses to patient questions
studies.finding: Answers to ten pancreatic cancer surgery questions were rated by patients and surgeons on 1-5 scales. ChatGPT's responses mirrored the surgeons' in empathy from the patient view, and Surgeon 1 was most often ranked first, followed closely by ChatGPT; overall comparable reliability, comprehension and empathy.
studies.limitation: Only ten questions, two surgeons, and small incomplete rater sample (11 patients, 10 surgeons completed).
studies.title: ChatGPT vs. surgeons on pancreatic cancer queries: accuracy & empathy evaluated by patients and experts.
studies.source: HPB : the official journal of the International Hepato Pancreato Biliary Association

studies.design: Post hoc analysis of two prospective cohorts (430 patients) with multidisciplinary multimodal reference diagnosis
studies.ai_system: Openly accessible convolutional neural network for pneumonia on chest x-ray
studies.humans: Senior radiologists and emergency physicians reading CXRs
studies.finding: Diagnosis of pneumonia on chest x-ray against an expert-panel multimodal reference. Accuracy was similar for radiologists and DL (cohort 1: radiologists 75.5% and 71.0%, DL 71.0%; cohort 2: radiologist 70.9%, DL 72.6%; p ≥ 0.269), and both were significantly higher than emergency physicians (cohort 1 64.0%, cohort 2 63.0%; p ≤ 0.022).
studies.limitation: Post hoc retrospective analysis with very few human readers; CXR-only reading without clinical context.
studies.title: Validating the accuracy of deep learning for the diagnosis of pneumonia on chest x-ray against a robust multimodal reference diagnosis: a post hoc analysis of two prospective studies.

studies.design: Reader study on 80 public cardiac cases, radiologists with and without ChatGPT-4o, plus 12 LLMs
studies.humans: One cardiac radiologist and 3 general radiologists
studies.finding: Unassisted accuracy was 72.5% (cardiac radiologist), 53.8% and 51.3% (general radiologists I and II), improving to 78.8%, 70.0% and 63.8% with ChatGPT-4o; radiologist-III improved from 48.8% to 63.8%. Claude 3 Opus and Claude 3.5 Sonnet had the highest LLM accuracy (81.3%).
studies.limitation: Only four radiologists and publicly available teaching cases.
studies.title: Empowering Radiologists With ChatGPT-4o: Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Models and Radiologists in Cardiac Cases.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic study with internal and external test sets compared with radiologists
studies.finding: Detection of SLAP lesions on shoulder MR arthrography against arthroscopy. SLAP-Net had AUC = 0.98 and accuracy = 0.96 in dataset 1, similar to senior radiologists (p = 0.055) but higher than early- and mid-career radiologists (p = 0.025 and 0.011). In dataset 2 (AUC = 0.92, accuracy = 0.85) it was similar to all three radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective with only three radiologists.
studies.title: Preliminary exploration of deep learning-assisted recognition of superior labrum anterior and posterior lesions in shoulder MR arthrography.

studies.design: Comparison of GPT-4 and ophthalmologists on complex ophthalmology cases
studies.finding: On complex ophthalmology cases presented as figures without descriptions, GPT-4 reached 38.4% diagnostic accuracy and 57.8% next-step accuracy. Its diagnostic accuracy was comparable to two ophthalmologists (p = 0.30, p = 0.41) but below the best one (p = 0.0004). For next steps it was similar to one ophthalmologist (p = 0.22) but underperformed the other two.
studies.limitation: Only three ophthalmologists, and published cases rather than live care.
studies.title: Multimodal Performance of GPT-4 in Complex Ophthalmology Cases.

studies.design: Retrospective non-inferiority comparison on real prehospital ECGs
studies.ai_system: QCG analyzer deep learning ECG model (qSTEMI biomarker) from phone photos of printed ECGs
studies.humans: 5 EMS directors (board-certified emergency physicians) and 3 interventional cardiologists
studies.finding: In 53 patients with suspected STEMI (24 STEMI), qSTEMI had an AUC of 0.815 versus 0.736 for the expert consensus score (p=0.081). Sensitivity and specificity were 0.750 and 0.862 for qSTEMI versus 0.708 and 0.793 for the consensus, which met the non-inferiority criterion.
studies.limitation: Very small sample (53 patients) and expert consensus score rather than individual reads.
studies.title: Smartphone AI vs. Medical Experts: A Comparative Study in Prehospital STEMI Diagnosis.

studies.design: Vignette study with blinded expert rating
studies.humans: 100 family and emergency medicine physicians (residents and attendings)
studies.finding: Diagnosis, management and referral in 12 ENT vignettes. Physicians achieved mean diagnostic accuracy of 91.6% and management accuracy of 87.9%, with 30.4% inappropriate referral in non-urgent cases; LLMs demonstrated comparable diagnostic and management accuracy with higher referral appropriateness.
studies.limitation: Only 12 simulated vignettes; LLM figures not quantified in abstract.
studies.title: Empowering front-line physicians with AI: Evaluating large language models in everyday ENT care.
studies.source: The American journal of emergency medicine

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of LLMs and clinicians on imaging selection scenarios
studies.humans: 4 clinicians and 4 radiologists of varying experience
studies.finding: LLMs and clinicians selected imaging modalities for 120 ACR scenarios and 120 practice-oriented scenarios. DeepSeek-R1 chose the appropriate modality in 98.3% of ACR cases. In the realistic scenarios it matched board-certified junior radiologist performance and exceeded clinician and resident performance.
studies.limitation: Small number of human participants and simulated scenarios.
studies.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for imaging modality selection: Potential to reduce unnecessary contrast agent use and radiation exposure.

studies.design: Model development with a model-versus-radiologist comparison and a model-assisted study
studies.ai_system: ResUNet-PSPNet deep learning model on CTA
studies.finding: For carotid plaque detection on CTA, the model's diagnostic results were higher than those of 4 out of 6 radiologists (p < 0.001). In a model-human study the model improved radiologists' sensitivity, and its diagnostic time (6 s) was significantly shorter than that of all radiologists.
studies.limitation: Single centre, retrospective, with a small test set; the size of the assisted-reading improvement is not reported.
studies.title: A deep learning model for carotid plaques detection based on CTA images: a two stepwise early-stage clinical validation study.

studies.design: Comparative analysis of responses to 36 basic and 14 controversial cleft questions
studies.humans: A resident, a general plastic surgeon and craniofacial surgeons
studies.finding: AI and human experts answered 50 cleft lip and palate questions. AI had moderate accuracy (55.6%) on basic questions, lower than experienced craniofacial surgeons, but displayed superior consistency and accuracy compared with residents on controversial topics. DISCERN scores indicated higher-quality treatment information from AI than from less experienced respondents.
studies.limitation: Very small number of human respondents and question-based simulated setting.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence and Human Expertise in Cleft Lip and Palate Care: A Comparative Study of Accuracy, Readability, and Treatment Quality.

studies.design: Vignette-based comparison using 80 published cases
studies.finding: Differential diagnosis of 80 salivary gland cases. ChatGPT outperformed experts at Top-1 (50.0% vs. 37.5%, p = 0.0309), was equal at Top-3 (62.5% vs. 62.5%), while experts surpassed ChatGPT at Top-5 (77.5% vs. 67.5%, p < 0.0001).
studies.limitation: Only three experts and published case reports as vignettes; abstract reports internally inconsistent numbers.
studies.title: Comparative diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT models in salivary gland disease: a multimodal vignette-based evaluation.
studies.source: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of chatbot and physician responses to real online patient inquiries, rated by a blinded expert panel
studies.humans: Physicians answering on a public social media forum; rated by 7 board-certified otorhinolaryngologists
studies.finding: Responses to real online ear, nose and throat inquiries from physicians and from ChatGPT-4 were rated on quality, empathy, consensus alignment, accuracy, comprehension and harm potential. ChatGPT-4 responses were preferred in 70.7% of cases and received higher ratings across all criteria. They were also longer (median 162 words vs 67 words for physicians; P < .0001).
studies.limitation: Physician comparators were forum responses rather than formal consultations, and the length difference may confound ratings; the number of responding physicians is not stated.
studies.title: Comparison of physician and large language model chatbot responses to online ear, nose, and throat inquiries.

studies.design: Retrospective two-centre model development with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Combined radiomics and ResNet18 deep learning MRI model
studies.finding: For preoperative staging of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (I-II vs III-IV) on MRI, the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.877 (95% CI 0.807-0.946) in the external test set. It significantly outperformed the radiologists (both p < 0.050); radiologist AUCs are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Retrospective with a small external test set of 97; radiologist numbers and results not detailed.
studies.title: Multiparameter MRI-based model integrating radiomics and deep learning for preoperative staging of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma.

studies.design: Retrospective validation on EMR data
studies.ai_system: Gradient-boosted tree model with LLM feature extraction
studies.humans: Nurses using a modified Malnutrition Screening Tool
studies.finding: Screening for in-hospital malnutrition in 106,449 patients. The model's AUC was 0.92 on day one and 0.95 using maximum risk, and it outperformed the nurse-administered modified MST used in practice.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, against nurses applying a screening tool rather than physician judgement; nurse performance figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Hospital Malnutrition Screening: Validation of a Novel Machine Learning Model.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre model development with clinician comparison
studies.ai_system: Light gradient boosting model on pure-tone audiometry features
studies.finding: For diagnosing Meniere's disease from pure-tone audiometry, the LGB model achieved accuracy 87%, sensitivity 83%, specificity 90%, and AUC 0.95, which compares favorably with experienced clinicians. Clinician figures are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single tertiary centre; clinician performance and numbers not reported.
studies.title: Applications of Machine Learning in Meniere's Disease Assessment Based on Pure-Tone Audiometry.
studies.source: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery

studies.design: Retrospective institutional database study of 4184 postmastectomy surveillance mammograms
studies.finding: Standalone AI was compared with radiologists for detecting contralateral second breast cancer on surveillance mammograms. AI had higher sensitivity (65.8% vs 55.0%) and cancer detection rate (17.4 vs 14.6 per 1000) but lower specificity (91.5% vs 98.1%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-institution study; radiologist number not reported.
studies.title: Breast Cancer Detection with Standalone AI versus Radiologist Interpretation of Unilateral Surveillance Mammography after Mastectomy.

studies.design: Reader study: pathologists assessed IHC slides without AI, then revisited discordant cases with AI assistance
studies.ai_system: AI-powered HER2 and ER/PR IHC analyzers
studies.finding: Three pathologists scored HER2, ER and PR IHC in 201 breast cancer cases, then revisited cases discordant with AI using AI assistance. Agreement among pathologists increased for HER2 (from 49.3 to 74.1%, p < 0.001), ER (from 93.0 to 96.5%, p = 0.096) and PR (from 84.6 to 91.5%, p = 0.006), and molecular subtype classification concordance improved from 58.2 to 78.6% (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Outcome is interobserver agreement rather than accuracy against a reference, and only three pathologists with sequential non-randomised reading.
studies.title: Augmented interpretation of HER2, ER, and PR in breast cancer by artificial intelligence analyzer: enhancing interobserver agreement through a reader study of 201 cases.

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison on cytology image patches
studies.finding: Classification of 845 pleural effusion cytology patches for metastatic breast carcinoma. The DCNN had higher accuracy, sensitivity and specificity than pathologists (81.1% vs. 68.7%, 95.0% vs. 72.5%, 98.6% vs. 88.9%). After reviewing the DCNN's discordant cases, pathologists' average accuracy, sensitivity and specificity improved to 87.9, 80.2 and 95.7%.
studies.limitation: Only three pathologists reading image patches rather than whole slides or live cases.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Based Computational Cytopathologic Diagnosis of Metastatic Breast Carcinoma in Pleural Fluid.

studies.design: Reader study of knee radiographs graded with and without AI, correlated with clinical scores
studies.finding: Three physicians assigned KL grades to 71 knee X-rays with and without AI, and ratings were correlated with clinical severity scores. AI-aided ratings had a higher association with the overall KL score and the KOOS, though the amount of improvement depended on the individual rater.
studies.limitation: Very small reader sample (three physicians) and no reference-standard accuracy measure; numeric effects not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Artificial-Intelligence-Aided Radiographic Diagnostic of Knee Osteoarthritis Leads to a Higher Association of Clinical Findings with Diagnostic Ratings.

studies.design: Retrospective agreement study of AI digital pathology model vs GI pathologists on esophageal biopsies
studies.ai_system: Supervised AI model on Aiforia cloud platform
studies.humans: Original GI pathologists and a central GI pathologist
studies.finding: On 203 esophageal biopsies plus 10 controls, AI agreement with pathologists for peak eosinophil count (r s = 0.89, ICC = 0.87 vs original; r s = 0.91, ICC = 0.83 vs central) was similar to inter-pathologist agreement (r s = 0.88, ICC = 0.91). AI identified PEC >15 eos/hpf with AUC = 0.98 against both pathologists.
studies.limitation: Agreement study using pathologists as reference; few pathologists and no independent ground truth.
studies.title: Performance of an Artificial Intelligence Model for Recognition and Quantitation of Histologic Features of Eosinophilic Esophagitis on Biopsy Samples.
studies.source: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader comparison on test set
studies.finding: Detection of pulmonary arterial hypertension on chest X-rays (101 test images). The algorithm had AUC 0.988 with sensitivity 0.933 and specificity 0.982, and its AUC was superior to that of experienced doctors.
studies.limitation: Single-centre small test set; doctors' numbers and results not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-based model for predicting pulmonary arterial hypertension on chest x-ray images.

studies.design: Retrospective image and video reader comparison
studies.ai_system: AI system for gastric atrophy identification and Kimura-Takemoto stratification
studies.finding: Identification and stratification of gastric atrophy on endoscopy. Sensitivity was 92.72% vs 76.85% for endoscopists at image level and 94.87% vs 85.90% for experts at video level; stratification accuracy was 81.37% vs 73.04% for experts (p = 0.045).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, small validation set of 102 patients; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: An artificial intelligence system for chronic atrophic gastritis diagnosis and risk stratification under white light endoscopy.
studies.source: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with external test comparison against radiologists
studies.ai_system: 2D U-Net T1 + CE deep learning model
studies.finding: Detection of bone metastases on spine MRI in an external test set. The T1 + CE model achieved per-lesion sensitivity of 0.857 (150/175) in the external test, while radiologists showed a mean per-lesion sensitivity of 0.746 and mean per-lesion positive predictive value of 0.701.
studies.limitation: Small external test set (49 series from 20 patients), and no model positive predictive value is reported alongside the radiologists' figure.
studies.title: Automated Detection and Segmentation of Bone Metastases on Spine MRI Using U-Net: A Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Retrospective two-center multireader study reading prostate MRI with and without AI, 4-week washout
studies.ai_system: AI assistance for prostate MRI csPCa detection
studies.finding: Sixteen radiologists read prostate MRI from 900 patients with and without AI for clinically significant prostate cancer. For less-experienced radiologists AI improved lesion-level sensitivity (0.78 vs. 0.88), sextant-level AUC (0.84 vs. 0.93) and patient-level AUC (0.84 vs. 0.89); for experienced radiologists AI only improved sextant-level AUC (0.82 vs. 0.91). Median reading time fell from 250 s to 130 s.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study; experienced radiologists read only 90 cases each.
studies.title: Assessing the Performance of Artificial Intelligence Assistance for Prostate MRI: A Two-Center Study Involving Radiologists With Different Experience Levels.
studies.source: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

studies.design: Retrospective single-institution cohort comparing commercial AI with clinical radiologist reports
studies.finding: Screening mammography in DM (26,693 exams) and DBT (4824 exams) cohorts. In DM, radiologists had sensitivity 88.6%, specificity 93.3%, recall 7.2%, NPV 99.9% versus AI (elevated risk) 74.4%, 86.3%, 14.0%, 99.8%. AI achieved high NPV but higher recall rates than radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single institution; radiologist number not stated.
studies.title: Commercial Artificial Intelligence Versus Radiologists: NPV and Recall Rate in Large Population-Based Digital Mammography and Tomosynthesis Screening Mammography Cohorts.

studies.design: Retrospective single-center cohort with blinded expert readjudication of discordant reads
studies.finding: The AI-ECG model detected any pediatric ECG abnormality with AUROC 0.94. On readjudication of AI/original cardiologist discordances, blinded experts more often agreed with AI for any abnormality (P = 0.001), WPW (P = 0.01) and prolonged QTc (P = 0.07).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-center data; comparison limited to discordant cases.
studies.title: Expert-Level Automated Diagnosis of the Pediatric ECG Using a Deep Neural Network.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with expert comparison on a 1,000-sample test set
studies.ai_system: Random forest classifier (among five ML approaches)
studies.finding: For detection of M-proteins on serum protein electrophoresis, the random forest classifier achieved F1-Score 93.2 % and accuracy 99.1 %, versus F1-Score 61.2 ± 16.0 % and accuracy 89.2 ± 10.2 % for the 10 experts. Experts had higher sensitivity (94.3 ± 2.8 % vs 89.9 %).
studies.limitation: Retrospective data from a single country; expert group mixed pathologists and technicians.
studies.title: Expert-level detection of M-proteins in serum protein electrophoresis using machine learning.

studies.design: Retrospective multicohort model development and validation with comparison to radiologists
studies.ai_system: Multimodal score (clinical, radiomic and deep features, AutoGluon-Tabular)
studies.finding: Differentiation of benign renal lesions from RCC on CT. The multimodal score had higher AUC than radiologists' interpretations and other scores for overall lesions (AUC: 0.949-0.906 vs 0.926-0.765) and small lesions (AUC: 0.929-0.880 vs 0.901-0.657) in validation and test cohorts.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; radiologist number and reading conditions not stated in the abstract.
studies.title: Integration of radiomic and deep features to reliably differentiate benign renal lesions from renal cell carcinoma.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre comparison against expert consensus
studies.finding: For FRENCH triage level prediction against senior clinician consensus, URGENTIAPARSE achieved an F1-score of 0.900 compared with 0.303 for nurse triage. Composite z scores were 2.514 for URGENTIAPARSE vs. -4.343 for nurse triage.
studies.limitation: Monocentric, 0.90% selected sample, severe overfitting reported; comparator is nurses, not physicians.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Models for Predicting Triage in Emergency Departments: Seven-Month Retrospective Comparative Study of Natural Language Processing, Large Language Model, and Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures.

studies.design: Single-center retrospective cohort; agreement with MDT decisions
studies.finding: GPT-4's spinal cord stimulation candidacy recommendations for 93 patients were compared with expert MDT decisions as the reference standard. The MDT recommended SCS for 91.4% of patients versus 46.2% for GPT-4, and agreement between MDT and GPT-4 was fair (κ = 0.29). GPT-4 approximated but did not replicate MDT decision-making.
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective design with a small sample; the MDT served as the reference standard, so only agreement was measured and clinical outcomes were not assessed.
studies.title: Smart Processing and Intelligent Navigation for Evaluation (SPINE): Comparing Clinicians and AI Language Model (GPT-4) in Spinal Cord Stimulation Candidate Selection.

studies.design: Retrospective validation against expert consensus
studies.finding: Colon-Pilot's colonoscopy surveillance recommendations for 596 colonoscopies were compared with expert consensus and with the original endoscopists' recommendations. For the automated cases, guideline-concordant accuracy was 97.5% (κ = 0.970) for Colon-Pilot versus 69.7% (κ = 0.781) for the original endoscopist recommendations. Colon-Pilot flagged 12.4% of cases for manual review.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-system evaluation in which the AI's accuracy was computed only on cases it did not flag for manual review; the number of endoscopists is not stated.
studies.title: Colon-Pilot: A Generative AI Tool for Automated Colonoscopy Surveillance Recommendations and 2024 ACG/ASGE Quality Benchmarking.

studies.design: Cross-sectional ECG case comparison
studies.finding: GPT-4o and DeepSeek interpreted 40 ECG images from a textbook, and their answers were compared with previously collected answers from cardiologists and emergency medicine specialists. GPT-4o had median correct answers of 27 total versus 22 for DeepSeek. Both models fell short of expert-level performance.
studies.limitation: Small textbook ECG set, with human answers collected previously rather than concurrently.
studies.title: Comparing DeepSeek and GPT-4o in ECG interpretation: Is AI improving over time?
studies.source: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

studies.design: Retrospective concordance analysis of 179 patients' cases
studies.finding: For adjuvant therapy recommendations in 179 patients with stage II colon cancer, agreement between the MDT and ChatGPT-5 was moderate across three categories (70.4%, κ = 0.542) and substantial for adjuvant therapy versus observation (91.1%, κ = 0.719). Discordance mainly reflected AI's tendency to escalate therapy.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset concordance study using MDT decisions as reference, without patient outcomes.
studies.title: Stage II colon cancer: does ChatGPT recommend more intensive adjuvant therapy? A comparison with MDT decisions.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study of 120 chest radiographs read without and with AI
studies.finding: Physicians classified 120 chest radiographs for fibrosing ILD without and with BMAX. Non-expert mean ROC-AUC rose from 0.795 to 0.825 (p=0.005) and sensitivity from 0.744 to 0.802, but expert sensitivity did not change (p=0.285).
studies.limitation: Small enriched reader test set of 120 images.
studies.title: Detection of fibrosing interstitial lung disease-suspected chest radiographs using a deep learning-based computer-aided detection system: a retrospective, observational study.

studies.design: Model development with external test set compared against blinded expert clinicians
studies.ai_system: Machine learning classifiers on video head impulse test data
studies.finding: Distinguishing vestibular neuritis from posterior circulation stroke using VHIT data in a 49-patient external test set. Best ML model accuracy was 87.8% (95% CI 77.6%-95.9%) versus 85.7% (75.5%-93.9%) for expert clinicians (p = 0.56).
studies.limitation: Small external test set; number of clinicians not stated; clinicians limited to VHIT data.
studies.title: Separation of stroke from vestibular neuritis using the video head impulse test: machine learning models versus expert clinicians.

studies.design: Cross-sectional agreement study
studies.ai_system: AI system for panoramic radiograph feature detection
studies.finding: Detection of teeth, caries, implants, restorations and prostheses on 1000 panoramic radiographs. Correlation between AI and two radiologists was 0.691-0.878 for carious teeth, 0.770-0.952 for implants, 0.773-0.834 for restored teeth, 0.972-0.980 for fixed prostheses and 0.956-0.988 for missing teeth. The authors judged the AI comparable to radiologists.
studies.limitation: Only two readers, who also served as the reference; agreement was measured by correlation only.
studies.title: Automatic feature segmentation in dental panoramic radiographs.

studies.design: Retrospective observational study; trainees scored SINS with and without LLM, plus LLM alone
studies.finding: SINS calculation for spinal tumours compared with a consensus reference. LLM-assisted ICC was 0.993 and LLM-predicted ICC 0.990, versus 0.968 for clinicians without LLM (both p < 0.001). Median time was 60.0 s with LLM assistance versus 83.0 s without; LLM alone took approximately 5 s.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-institution study with only eight trainees.
studies.title: Large Language Model (LLM)-Predicted and LLM-Assisted Calculation of the Spinal Instability Neoplastic Score (SINS) Improves Clinician Accuracy and Efficiency.

studies.design: Model development with reader study with and without CNN assistance
studies.finding: The diagnostic performance (ROCAUC) of six oral pathologists improved significantly when CNN results were used as supplementary diagnoses (p-value = 0.031).
studies.limitation: Six readers; effect sizes not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Effectiveness of deep learning classifiers in histopathological diagnosis of oral squamous cell carcinoma by pathologists.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre radiomics study with external test against a radiologist
studies.finding: In the external test cohort, the classifier showed 92% sensitivity and 33% specificity for lipoma versus ALT, with no statistical difference compared to the radiologist (p = 0.474).
studies.limitation: Single reader and a small external cohort of 36 patients.
studies.title: MRI radiomics-based machine learning for classification of deep-seated lipoma and atypical lipomatous tumor of the extremities.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to radiologist visual analysis
studies.finding: For distinguishing the primary origin of brain metastases on MRI, 3D ResNet18 with Grad-CAM and AIC showed better performance than the radiologist for lung vs non-lung cancer, SCLC vs NSCLC, and BC vs GIC. Model AUCs ranged from 0.675 to 0.876 in testing and 0.684 to 0.800 in independent testing; radiologist figures are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Retrospective with small independent test cohort; number of radiologists and their results not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Deep Learning With an Attention Mechanism for Differentiating the Origin of Brain Metastasis Using MR images.
studies.source: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of AI against radiologists' written reports on 499 chest radiographs, with a consensus ground truth
studies.finding: On 499 chest radiographs, the AI showed higher sensitivity than the written reports for lung lesions (0.83 versus 0.52), consolidations (0.88 versus 0.78) and atelectasis (0.54 versus 0.43), but with higher false-detection rates.
