Its sensitivity for pleural effusions was lower (0.74 versus 0.88), and NPVs were comparable.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single dataset; comparison is with routine written reports rather than a controlled reader study; vendor product.
studies.title: Evaluation of the clinical performance of an AI-based application for the automated analysis of chest X-rays.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of AI responses with crowd-sourced surgeon treatment polls
studies.humans: Surgeons responding to OrthoBullets Cases polls
studies.finding: Orthopaedic treatment decisions on 97 case questions, measured by agreement with the most popular surgeon response. ChatGPT 4 matched the most popular response in 68.0%, ChatGPT 3.5 in 40.2% and Bard in 45.4%. AI tools performed poorer on controversial questions.
studies.limitation: Clinicians' poll consensus serves as the reference standard rather than as a scored comparator, and the number of surgeons is not stated.
studies.title: The ability of artificial intelligence tools to formulate orthopaedic clinical decisions in comparison to human clinicians: An analysis of ChatGPT 3.5, ChatGPT 4, and Bard.

studies.design: Retrospective radiomics model development with comparison to two radiologists
studies.ai_system: Random forest radiomics model on 2D-US plus CEUS key frames
studies.humans: One junior and one senior radiologist
studies.finding: For classifying C-TIRADS 4 thyroid nodules, the RF model matched the senior radiologist (AUC: 0.94 vs. 0.92, P = 0.798; ACC: 0.90 vs. 0.92). It outperformed the junior radiologist (AUC: 0.94 vs. 0.80, P = 0.039; ACC: 0.90 vs. 0.81) in the test cohort.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists, a small test cohort from a 9:1 split, and a retrospective single dataset.
studies.title: Applying machine-learning models to differentiate benign and malignant thyroid nodules classified as C-TIRADS 4 based on 2D-ultrasound combined with five contrast-enhanced ultrasound key frames.

studies.design: Cross-sectional vignette comparison
studies.finding: On 120 clinical vignettes with and without images, LLMs outperformed physicians in text-only scenarios (GPT-4o: 70.8 %, Claude Sonnet 3.5: 59.5 %, Physicians: 39.5 %). With images, GPT-4o reached 84.5 %, Claude Sonnet 3.5 67.3 % and physicians 78.8 %, with physicians showing the largest gain.
studies.limitation: Only three physicians as benchmark; vignettes rather than real patients.
studies.title: Visual-textual integration in LLMs for medical diagnosis: A preliminary quantitative analysis.

studies.design: Retrospective model development on 125 patients, compared with expert assessment
studies.ai_system: Integrated radiomics, clinical and deep learning stacking model
studies.finding: For predicting occult lymph node metastasis in early tongue cancer, the model achieved an accuracy of 84% and an AUC-ROC of 0.949. It surpassed younger doctors and was comparable to experienced doctors.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective sample with a 25-patient test set; the doctors' numbers are not reported.
studies.title: A CT-based integrated model for preoperative prediction of occult lymph node metastasis in early tongue cancer.

studies.design: Multi-centre retrospective model development and validation (455 patients)
studies.ai_system: Radiomics machine learning models on chest CT
studies.finding: Distinguishing immune checkpoint inhibitor, radiation and infective pneumonitis on CT. Models outperformed radiologists for RP vs COVID-19 (AUC 0.92 vs 0.8 and 0.8), CIP vs COVID-19 (0.68 vs 0.43 and 0.4) and CIP vs non-COVID-19 IP (0.71 vs 0.55 and 0.63), but were not superior for RP vs non-COVID-19 IP and CIP vs RP.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists; superiority varied by comparison task.
studies.title: Validated machine learning tools to distinguish immune checkpoint inhibitor, radiotherapy, COVID-19 and other infective pneumonitis.
studies.source: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with comparison to radiologists
studies.finding: For discriminating Staphylococcus aureus from Aspergillus pneumonia on CT plus clinical data, the model achieved accuracy of 78% vs 75%, 60% and 40% for high-, mid- and low-ranking radiologists. Its diagnostic performance significantly exceeded that of junior radiologists.
studies.limitation: Very small sample of 60 patients; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: MI-DenseCFNet: deep learning-based multimodal diagnosis models for Aureus and Aspergillus pneumonia.

studies.design: Retrospective deep learning model development with comparison against radiologists
studies.ai_system: VGG19-based combined MRI deep learning model
studies.humans: Two radiologists with different levels of experience
studies.finding: Differentiation of tuberculous from brucellar spondylitis on MRI in 383 patients. The best combined VGG19 model achieved an AUC of 0.973. All combined models performed better than the two radiologists (P<0.05).
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists, a small validation set (n = 76) and no external validation.
studies.title: Differentiation of tuberculous and brucellar spondylitis using conventional MRI-based deep learning algorithms.

studies.design: Retrospective development study of multimodal DL model with test-set comparison against a senior physician
studies.finding: For diagnosing renal artery stenosis against angiography, the ResNeSt model achieved an accuracy of 78.25% ± 1.62%. This was inferior to the senior physician (90.09%).
studies.limitation: Single center, with comparison against only one physician.
studies.title: Deep-learning-based renal artery stenosis diagnosis via multimodal fusion.
studies.source: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to radiation oncologists
studies.humans: Experienced and less experienced radiation oncologists
studies.finding: Autosegmentation of HR CTV and organs at risk for brachytherapy in postoperative endometrial carcinoma. The LP model performed most similarly to the experienced radiation oncologist and outperformed less experienced ones, with mean DSC 0.96 ± 0.02 for HR CTV, 0.91 ± 0.02 for rectum and 0.83 ± 0.07 for urethra.
studies.limitation: Clinician comparison not quantified in the abstract; small single test set.
studies.title: A deep learning-based 3D Prompt-nnUnet model for automatic segmentation in brachytherapy of postoperative endometrial carcinoma.
studies.source: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

studies.design: LLM performance on board examination questions compared with examinees
studies.finding: On 297 JSBE questions, GPT-4o answered 78% (231/297) and GPT-4 55% (163/297) correctly. The LLMs' results were lower than those of the examinees.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; examinee scores not reported numerically in the abstract.
studies.title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Surgical Training by Assessing GPT-4 and GPT-4o on the Japan Surgical Board Examination With Text-Only and Image-Accompanied Questions: Performance Evaluation Study.

studies.design: Model development with reader study on wrist ultrasound images
studies.finding: For classifying carpal tunnel syndrome on ultrasound images from 90 normal and 40 CTS wrists, the system performed comparably to the average of experienced radiologists. It outperformed inexperienced radiologists (accuracy score 3.59% higher and F1 score 5.85% higher).
studies.limitation: Small single dataset (130 wrists); number of readers not stated.
studies.title: One-Stop Automated Diagnostic System for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in Ultrasound Images Using Deep Learning.

studies.design: Retrospective study of 649 thyroid nodules from 347 patients
studies.finding: FNA recommendation for thyroid nodules on ultrasound. Koios with AI-adapter had AUC 0.70, similar to radiologists (AUC 0.70), with higher specificity (0.63 vs 0.43) but lower sensitivity (0.69 vs 0.81). Radiology reports combined with the AI-adapter achieved AUC 0.76, improving specificity from 0.43 to 0.53 with unchanged sensitivity (0.81).
studies.limitation: Retrospective; combination was computed from existing reports rather than radiologists actually using the AI; only 32 malignancies.
studies.title: Assessment of the Diagnostic Performance of a Commercially Available Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Risk Stratification of Thyroid Nodules on Ultrasound.
studies.source: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association

studies.design: Cross-sectional multiple-choice ECG comparison
studies.humans: 100 practitioners (emergency, internal medicine, primary care, cardiology)
studies.finding: On 20 ECG cases with confounders, GPT-4o averaged 3 (±2) in AF cases and 5.40 (±1.34) in non-AF cases. No significant difference was found between GPT-4o and internists or primary care physicians (p = 0.952 and 0.852), while cardiologists outperformed GPT-4o (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Only 20 crafted ECG questions in multiple-choice format.
studies.title: In the face of confounders: Atrial fibrillation detection - Practitioners vs. ChatGPT.

studies.design: Multireader study with washout, unaided then aided reading
studies.ai_system: ResNet-50 deep learning model with Grad-CAM heatmaps for ganglion cell detection
studies.finding: Pathologists assessed 50 frozen whole-slide images for ganglion cells in Hirschsprung disease. Average diagnostic accuracy increased from 77% to 85.8% with the model's heatmap support, and diagnosis time decreased from 139.7 to 70.5 seconds.
studies.limitation: Sequential non-randomized reading design on only 50 slides; possible order/memory effects.
studies.title: The Future of Surgical Diagnostics: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Detection of Ganglion Cells for Hirschsprung Disease.
studies.source: Laboratory investigation; a journal of technical methods and pathology

studies.design: Reader study with endoscopic videos; endoscopists read without then with AI after 4 weeks
studies.ai_system: Video-based AI model for superficial ESCC detection
studies.finding: For detecting superficial ESCC on 115 endoscopic test videos, the AI alone had sensitivity 76.0%, specificity 79.4% and accuracy 77.2%. With AI assistance, endoscopist sensitivity (57.4% vs. 66.5%) and accuracy (68.6% vs. 75.9%) improved significantly, with specificity rising slightly (87.0% vs. 91.6%); both experts and non-experts improved.
studies.limitation: Sequential unaided-then-aided reading design without randomisation; small video test set.
studies.title: Effects of artificial intelligence assistance on endoscopist performance: Comparison of diagnostic performance in superficial esophageal squamous cell carcinoma detection using video-based models.

studies.design: Retrospective evaluation on public PROSTATEx test set (328 cases)
studies.finding: Detection of clinically significant prostate cancer on MRI. At equivalent false-positive rates the model achieved TPRs of 0.93 and 0.79 versus radiologists' 0.87 and 0.68 for PI-RADS ≥ 3 and PI-RADS ≥ 4 lesions (p ≤ 0.05); model AUC was 0.83.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single public dataset; comparator was non-expert radiologists and number not stated.
studies.title: Evaluation of a deep learning prostate cancer detection system on biparametric MRI against radiological reading.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader comparison
studies.ai_system: Random forest classifier on AI segmentation of sagittal T2 MRI
studies.finding: For grading lumbar central canal stenosis on 683 IVD levels, the multiclass model achieved weighted kappa 0.86 versus 0.85 and 0.73 for readers 3 and 4. The binary model had sensitivity 93% and specificity 91%, versus reader sensitivity 74 and 54% and specificity 98 and 99%.
studies.limitation: Cross-validation on a single dataset with only two comparison readers; no external validation.
studies.title: AI-based lumbar central canal stenosis classification on sagittal MR images is comparable to experienced radiologists using axial images.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to orthopedists
studies.ai_system: Deep learning keypoint detection and scoring system
studies.finding: For DDH diagnosis from pelvic radiographs, the system achieved an F1 score of 0.863 (95% CI: 0.851-0.876), significantly outperforming the orthopedist group (0.777, 95% CI: 0.737-0.817).
studies.limitation: Only moderately experienced readers; dataset details limited.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Based Automatic Diagnosis System for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip.
studies.source: IEEE journal of translational engineering in health and medicine

studies.design: Single-center retrospective agreement study of multimodal LLMs vs expert surgeon consensus
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-4.0, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek-R1-0528 Chat
studies.finding: On radiographs of 125 AIS patients, surgeon agreement was high for Lenke classification (92.0%, κ = 0.913) and fusion-level selection (88.8%, κ = 0.879). All LLMs showed very low agreement with expert consensus (Lenke: 1.6-10.2%, κ = 0.001-0.036; fusion: 0.8-12.0%, κ = 0.003-0.053) and chance-level test-retest reproducibility, though they were faster (seconds vs ~11-12 min).
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective study with only two surgeons, whose consensus also served as the reference standard.
studies.title: Reliability of Large Language Model-Based Artificial Intelligence in AIS Assessment: Lenke Classification and Fusion-Level Suggestion.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of machine learning models vs junior residents on test set
studies.finding: For predicting the SMILE nomogram from preoperative data in 1025 eyes, XGBoost provided significantly higher accuracy within 0.05 to 0.25 D than SVR and junior residents (McNemar test, P < 0.001). Model RMSE ranged from 0.075 to 0.110; resident accuracy values are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Only four junior residents compared, no experienced surgeons; retrospective data.
studies.title: Adopting machine learning to predict nomogram for small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE).

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with radiologist comparison
studies.finding: LIDGAX differentiated xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis from gallbladder cancer with AUC 0.94 internally and 0.88 externally. Compared to six radiologists, it improved sensitivity (1.2-8.5%), specificity (0.0-4.6%) and balanced accuracy (1.8-6.6%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only six radiologists.
studies.title: Machine learning model for differentiating xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis and gallbladder cancer in multicenter largescale study.

studies.design: Retrospective radiomics model study with reader comparison
studies.finding: Prediction of pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in rectal cancer on MRI. The radiomic nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.852 (95%CI: 0.774-0.930), higher than the pooled readers (p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Small single dataset (126 patients, validation n = 42) and only two readers.
studies.title: MRI-Based Radiomic Models Outperform Radiologists in Predicting Pathological Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective case-control comparison of smartphone AI ECG analysis vs emergency physicians
studies.ai_system: Smartphone application analysing camera-captured ECG images for hyperkalemia
studies.finding: In 125 ED patients, detection of hyperkalemia (K ≥ 6 mmol/L) from initial ECGs was compared. The application's AUC ranged from 0.898 to 0.904 (median 0.902) with sensitivity 0.797, whereas the physicians' consensus had a significantly lower AUC of 0.662 and sensitivity of 0.203.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective matched case-control sample enriched for hyperkalemia.
studies.title: Hyperkalemia Detection in Emergency Departments Using Initial ECGs: A Smartphone AI ECG Analyzer vs. Board-Certified Physicians.

studies.design: Retrospective two-center model development with comparison to clinicians
studies.finding: Diagnosis of laryngeal cancer on laryngoscopic images. Densenet201 reached 86.3% accuracy in external validation, performing comparably to Clinician A and outperforming Clinician B, particularly in the external validation cohort.
studies.limitation: Only two clinicians compared and clinician metrics not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Computer-Aided Diagnosis of Laryngeal Cancer Based on Deep Learning with Laryngoscopic Images.

studies.design: Reader comparison study
studies.humans: Radiology, emergency medicine and neurosurgery residents
studies.finding: Detection, localization and classification of traumatic intracranial hemorrhage on head CT. The deep learning model achieved an accuracy of 0.89, outperforming the residents with regard to sensitivity (0.82) but still lagging behind in specificity (0.90).
studies.limitation: Comparator limited to residents, and the number of readers is not reported.
studies.title: A comparison of performance between a deep learning model with residents for localization and classification of intracranial hemorrhage.

studies.design: Single-institution retrospective study; radiomics ML model vs radiologist RECIST 1.1 and CT morphologic assessment
studies.ai_system: Machine-learning model using CT radiomic features from tumoral and peritumoral regions
studies.humans: Radiologists using RECIST 1.1 and CT morphologic criteria
studies.finding: The task was estimating pathologic response of colorectal liver metastases to neoadjuvant chemotherapy from post-treatment CT. In the validation cohort, the radiomics model had AUC of 0.87, versus AUC = 0.53 for subjective RECIST assessment (p = 0.01) and AUC = 0.56 for morphologic assessment (p = 0.02).
studies.limitation: Single-institution retrospective cohort (85 patients, 95 tumors) from 2003-2012 with manual segmentation; the number of radiologist readers is not stated.
studies.title: Computed Tomography-Based Radiomics with Machine Learning Outperforms Radiologist Assessment in Estimating Colorectal Liver Metastases Pathologic Response After Chemotherapy.

studies.design: Retrospective single-cohort comparison of two commercial AI systems with standard-of-care double reading
studies.finding: Breast cancer detection on DBT in 419 patients. AUC was 0.86 for Transpara, 0.93 for ProFound AI, and 0.98 for human double-reading. Both AI systems showed lower performance than human double-reading.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, modest sample with 58 cancers; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: AI-enhanced Mammography With Digital Breast Tomosynthesis for Breast Cancer Detection: Clinical Value and Comparison With Human Performance.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
studies.humans: Experienced radiologist and third-year radiology resident
studies.finding: On 600 thyroid ultrasound images verified by cytology, the AI had overall sensitivity of 80% and specificity of 71.4%. The experienced radiologist had sensitivity of 40.0% and specificity of 80.0%; AI significantly outperformed the radiologist in sensitivity (P=0.043) with comparable specificity.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only one radiologist and one resident as comparators.
studies.title: Diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence in interpreting thyroid nodules on ultrasound images: a multicenter retrospective study.
studies.source: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

studies.design: Retrospective radiomics model development with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: T1w MRI radiomics model (WORC automated machine learning) with clinical features
studies.finding: Distinguishing malignant from benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors on MRI in 109 lesions. The T1w radiomics model achieved an AUC of 0.71, and 0.74 when combined with clinical features; experienced radiologists achieved AUCs of 0.75 and 0.66.
studies.limitation: Small single-centre retrospective sample (35 MPNSTs) with cross-validation only and two radiologists.
studies.title: Preoperative Classification of Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumors on MRI Using Radiomics.

studies.design: Retrospective deep learning development with comparison to ENT doctors
studies.finding: Classifying 4549 flexible laryngoscopy images as no vocal fold, normal or abnormal vocal folds; the Xception model's accuracy was 98.90 %, 97.36 %, and 96.26 % respectively. The model produced better results than a junior doctor and was near an expert.
studies.limitation: Few clinician comparators and no quantitative clinician results reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Support of deep learning to classify vocal fold images in flexible laryngoscopy.

studies.design: Reader study, 25 MRI scans read without and with AI prediction and explanation
studies.ai_system: Glioma grading model (88.0% accuracy) with SmoothGrad explanation
studies.finding: Glioma grading on brain MRI. Accuracy rose from 82.5±8.7% alone to 87.7±7.3% with AI prediction (p-value = 0.002), and was 88.5±7.0% (p-value = 0.35) with added AI explanation.
studies.limitation: Only 25 cases; experimental reading setting.
studies.title: Evaluating the clinical utility of artificial intelligence assistance and its explanation on the glioma grading task.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with external validation and comparison against pathologists
studies.ai_system: Logistic regression model on deep learning features from H&E whole-slide images
studies.finding: The model predicted basal vs luminal bladder cancer subtypes from H&E slides, with AUC 0.88 internally and 0.81 and 0.64 in external sets. It outperformed both junior and senior pathologists in differentiating subtypes (AUC: 0.85, accuracy: 74%, sensitivity: 66%, specificity: 82%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; pathologist performance details and number of readers not clearly reported, and external performance fell to 0.64 in one cohort.
studies.title: Pathology-based deep learning features for predicting basal and luminal subtypes in bladder cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader study on balanced test subset
studies.ai_system: Multimodal deep learning model (PET/CT, radiomics, clinical data; MNASNet)
studies.finding: Prediction of lymph node metastasis in prostate cancer from 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT. On the reader-study subset, radiation oncologists had mean accuracy 0.71±0.08 and F1 0.70±0.07 versus the AI model's accuracy 0.79±0.02 and F1 0.76±0.02.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective single dataset (48 test cases, balanced subset) with five readers.
studies.title: Integrating PET/CT, radiomics and clinical data: An advanced multi-modal approach for lymph node metastasis prediction in prostate cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre model development with test cohort comparison against radiologists' interpretation
studies.ai_system: Combined CT radiomics, intratumoral ecological diversity and clinical factor machine learning model
studies.finding: Classification of benign versus malignant renal lesions on arterial-phase CT, with a test cohort of 611 lesions. The combined model outperformed radiologists' interpretation in the whole test cohort (AUC = 0.946 vs 0.823, P < 0.001) and in small renal lesions (AUC = 0.935 vs 0.745, P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with a temporal split, and the number and experience of radiologists are not stated.
studies.title: CT-based conventional radiomics and quantification of intratumoral heterogeneity for predicting benign and malignant renal lesions.
studies.source: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre comparison of AI-assisted ultra-magnifying colonoscopy vs endoscopist Mayo endoscopic score against histology
studies.ai_system: Commercially available AI-assisted ultra-magnifying colonoscopy system
studies.finding: In 52 patients with ulcerative colitis (191 sites), prediction of histological healing (Geboes score < 3.1) was compared. Endoscopist MES0 had sensitivity 79.2%, specificity 90.6% and accuracy 81.2%; the AI system had sensitivity 74.2%, specificity 93.8% and accuracy 77.5%, and histological diagnostic yield was comparable.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective single-centre study with only 3 endoscopists.
studies.title: Comparison of Endoscopic and Artificial Intelligence Diagnoses for Predicting the Histological Healing of Ulcerative Colitis in a Real-World Clinical Setting.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic comparison on shoulder radiographs
studies.finding: Detection and classification of rotator cuff tears on plain radiographs. The CNN had 92% sensitivity, 69% specificity, 86% accuracy and AUC 0.88 for detection, and 60% accuracy for size classification; its accuracy was significantly better than orthopedic surgeons'.
studies.limitation: Surgeon performance figures and number of surgeons not reported in the abstract; retrospective design.
studies.title: Automated detection and classification of the rotator cuff tear on plain shoulder radiograph using deep learning.
studies.source: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery

studies.design: Model development with comparison to residents on X-ray classification
studies.ai_system: CNNs (best ResNet18 with multiangle projection augmentation)
studies.finding: Classifying 3D root canal morphology of fused-rooted mandibular second molars from 2D X-rays, ResNet18 reached an overall accuracy of 79.25%. Endodontic residents averaged 60.38% accuracy (P < .05).
studies.limitation: Small single dataset of 271 extracted teeth; number of residents not stated.
studies.title: Identification of Root Canal Morphology in Fused-rooted Mandibular Second Molars From X-ray Images Based on Deep Learning.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison against experts
studies.ai_system: Deep learning BPD prediction model on chest radiographs
studies.finding: Prediction of bronchopulmonary dysplasia from preterm infant chest radiographs. The model exhibited superior diagnostic performance compared to that of experts; no numeric comparison is given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of experts and comparative metrics not reported.
studies.title: Deep Learning Model for Prediction of Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia in Preterm Infants Using Chest Radiographs.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Cross-sectional study of 60 standardized clinical scenarios in English and Italian, timed and untimed
studies.ai_system: 8 LLMs including ChatGPT-01-preview, GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 3.5
studies.finding: Diagnostic accuracy on 60 standardized obstetrics-gynecology scenarios. AI LLMs had overall accuracy 73.75% vs residents 65.35% (P <.001); resident accuracy declined under time constraints from 73.2% to 56.5%. Integration analysis showed maximum enhancement in early-career residents (+29.7%; P <.001).
studies.limitation: Simulated vignettes at a single residency program; AI models assessed at different times than residents.
studies.title: The PERFORM Study: Artificial Intelligence Versus Human Residents in Cross-Sectional Obstetrics-Gynecology Scenarios Across Languages and Time Constraints.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with reader study
studies.finding: Diagnosing rotational chronic ankle instability on ankle MRI. Model assistance significantly enhanced clinicians' diagnostic accuracy (P = .042), particularly for junior clinicians, and reduced diagnostic variability.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of readers and accuracy values not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Transformer-Based Multilabel Deep Learning Model Is Efficient for Detecting Ankle Lateral and Medial Ligament Injuries on Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Improving Clinicians' Diagnostic Accuracy for Rotational Chronic Ankle Instability.
studies.source: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association

studies.design: Retrospective agreement study
studies.humans: One expert and one non-expert radiologist
studies.finding: Quantifying ILD patterns on HRCT in 48 CTD-ILD patients. AI agreed 81% with the expert (MAE 1.8% to 2.6%) but only 60-70% with the non-expert (MAE 3.9% to 5.2%), aligning more closely with the expert (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Only two readers and agreement-based with no independent ground truth; small retrospective sample.
studies.title: AI-Based HRCT Quantification in Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on published cases
studies.finding: On 50 complex oral and maxillofacial pathology cases, ChatGPT-4o achieved 70% accuracy, ChatGPT-4 66%, ChatGPT-3.5 50% and ChatGPT-4o Mini 46%. Dentists reached 72% accuracy.
studies.limitation: Only two dentists and published multiple-choice cases.
studies.title: Comparative diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT large language models and expert clinicians in complex oral and maxillofacial diseases.

studies.design: Multireader multicase study, readers with and without AI
studies.humans: 4 typical ASPECTS readers and 4 senior neuroradiologists
studies.finding: Eight clinicians scored ASPECTS on 200 NCCT scans with and without the algorithm. With AI, region-based accuracy rose from 72.4% to 76.5% (P < .05) and ROC AUC from 0.749 to 0.788 (P < .05), and reading time fell by 6%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study with only 8 readers.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Based ASPECTS Algorithm Enhances Reader Performance and Reduces Interpretation Time.

studies.design: Cross-sectional blinded comparison
studies.finding: Answers to 6 blepharoplasty FAQs were rated by blinded surgeons on Likert scales. For accuracy, ChatGPT scored 3.8 (SD 0.9) vs 3.6 (SD 1.2) for surgeons (p = .72). For comprehensiveness, ChatGPT scored 3.6 (SD 1.1) vs 3.0 (SD 1.1) (p = .03).
studies.limitation: Very small sample of 6 questions and 3 surgeons.
studies.title: ChatGPT and frequently asked patient questions for upper eyelid blepharoplasty surgery.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with external test set; comparison against radiologist
studies.ai_system: Multimodal machine learning model (LightGBM) using age, IL-6 and two CT radiomics features
studies.finding: The task was differentiating nontuberculous mycobacteria from Mycobacterium tuberculosis using clinical data and CT. The optimal multimodal model reached accuracy = 0.745 and sensitivity = 0.900 on the external test set, and its accuracy was 26% higher than that of the radiologist.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective sample of 175 patients; the number and experience of the radiologists and the details of their assessment are not reported.
studies.title: Multimodal machine learning-based model for differentiating nontuberculous mycobacteria from mycobacterium tuberculosis.

studies.design: Retrospective AI development and reader comparison
studies.ai_system: V-Net/U-Net AI system for lumbar disc CT reconstruction and MSU classification
studies.finding: Diagnosing MSU classification of lumbar disc herniation on CT in spiral and axial data. Accuracy of AI, radiologist, and AI + radiologist differed significantly (P < 0.01); AI-reconstructed image quality did not differ significantly from radiographer reconstructions (P＞0.05).
studies.limitation: Small test sets (40 cases each) and abstract does not report accuracy values or direction of differences.
studies.title: Development and application of AI assisted automatic reconstruction of axial lumbar disc CT images and diagnosis of lumbar disc herniation.

studies.design: Observer study with and without AI assistance
studies.humans: Radiologists, junior radiology residents and other specialists
studies.finding: Detection of skull fractures on emergent CT in a 671-patient test set. AI-assisted diagnosis significantly improved performance for all participants, with sensitivity almost doubling for junior radiology residents and other specialists, and diagnostic durations were significantly reduced (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Number of readers and exact reader metrics not given in the abstract.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Application in Skull Bone Fracture with Segmentation Approach.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Vignette comparison of LLMs with pediatric surgeons
studies.finding: On 13 complex pediatric surgical vignettes, ChatGPT-4 scored 52.1% and Copilot 47.9%. Pediatric surgeons scored 68.8% (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Only 13 vignettes; number of surgeons not stated.
studies.title: Solving Complex Pediatric Surgical Case Studies: A Comparative Analysis of Copilot, ChatGPT-4, and Experienced Pediatric Surgeons' Performance.
studies.source: European journal of pediatric surgery : official journal of Austrian Association of Pediatric Surgery ... [et al] = Zeitschrift fur Kinderchirurgie

studies.design: Model development on panoramic radiograph dataset with radiologist comparison
studies.finding: Determining mandibular third molar–inferior alveolar canal contact on panoramic radiographs with CBCT as gold standard. The ANN surpassed radiologists and DL models in specificity (82%), F1 score (92%), and accuracy (85%), with sensitivity of 86%.
studies.limitation: Radiologist results and number not reported in abstract; development dataset.
studies.title: Panoramic radiographic features for machine learning based detection of mandibular third molar root and inferior alveolar canal contact.

studies.design: Diagnostic test study comparing application with an oral radiologist
studies.ai_system: Web-based CADx application for intraosseous jaw lesions
studies.finding: Differential diagnosis of 95 histopathologically confirmed intraosseous jaw lesions. The application gave a correct differential in 97.89% and top diagnosis in 82.10%, versus 89.47% and 70.52% for an oral radiologist.
studies.limitation: Single human comparator, small sample including literature cases, no statistical test reported.
studies.title: Designing a web-based application for computer-aided diagnosis of intraosseous jaw lesions and assessment of its diagnostic accuracy.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep learning radiomics model (ResNet50 plus clinical variables) on pretreatment ultrasound
studies.finding: For predicting pathologic response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer, the integrated DLR model achieved AUC 0.939 in validation and performed better than two radiologists (all p < 0.05). Radiologists' predictive efficacy improved significantly with DLR assistance.
studies.limitation: Retrospective with only two radiologists; assisted performance numbers not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Pretreatment ultrasound-based deep learning radiomics model for the early prediction of pathologic response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with test-set comparison against radiologists
studies.ai_system: DL-video model (3D ResNet-50) on breast ultrasound video
studies.finding: For classifying breast lesions on ultrasound, the DL-video model had an AUC of 0.969, significantly higher than the DL-image model (0.925) and the six radiologists (0.779-0.912, P < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Single dataset with small test set (10% of 1000 lesions) and no external validation.
studies.title: Deep learning-based classification of breast lesions using dynamic ultrasound video.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study with sequential unaided then DL-aided reading
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model for esophageal cancer detection on CT
studies.humans: One radiologist and three radiology residents
studies.finding: In image-based analysis, reader AUCs improved from 0.96/0.93/0.96/0.93 to 0.97/0.95/0.99/0.96 with the model (p = 0.100/0.006/<0.001/<0.001), significant for the three less-experienced readers. The model alone had AUC 0.95 (image) and 0.98 (patient).
studies.limitation: Small test set of 50 patients, four readers, sequential design.
studies.title: Effects of deep learning on radiologists' and radiology residents' performance in identifying esophageal cancer on CT.

studies.design: Diagnostic accuracy study on MRI of 209 vertebral compression fractures
studies.finding: For differentiating benign from malignant vertebral compression fractures, TSCCN accuracy was 95.2%, 90.4% and 96.2% for T1WI, T2WI-FS and combined images, greater than that achieved by radiologists. Specificity was also higher at 98.4%, 94.3% and 99.2%.
studies.limitation: Radiologists' own accuracy figures and number not reported in abstract; likely retrospective single dataset.
studies.title: Benign vs malignant vertebral compression fractures with MRI: a comparison between automatic deep learning network and radiologist's assessment.

studies.design: Model redevelopment with reader study on prospectively collected sonographic videos in real-world mimic settings
studies.ai_system: Interpretable deep learning smartphone app for biliary atresia
studies.humans: 14 inexperienced radiologists (9 junior, 5 senior) and 4 experienced pediatric radiologists
studies.finding: On 333 sonographic gallbladder videos from 207 infants, the model performed comparably to experienced pediatric radiologists (average AUC 0.860 vs 0.876) and outperformed junior (0.838 vs 0.773) and senior radiologists (0.829 vs 0.749). With AI assistance, average AUC rose from 0.773 to 0.835 for junior and from 0.749 to 0.805 for senior radiologists.
studies.limitation: Simulated (real-world mimic) reading setting rather than live clinical care, with a small number of readers.
studies.title: Interpretable artificial intelligence-based app assists inexperienced radiologists in diagnosing biliary atresia from sonographic gallbladder images.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-reader multi-case study with crossover AI assistance
studies.finding: Diagnosis of CHD and PAH-CHD from chest radiographs. AI achieved higher AUCs than all 5 radiologists for CHD (0.670-0.858) and PAH-CHD (0.610-0.688). With AI assistance radiologists' AUC improved for CHD (ΔAUC + 0.096, P = 0.048) and PAH-CHD (ΔAUC + 0.066, P = 0.031).
studies.limitation: Only 5 readers, retrospective balanced test set from single source.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis of congenital heart disease and associated pulmonary arterial hypertension from chest radiographs: A multi-reader multi-case study.

studies.design: Reader comparison of PD-L1 TPS scoring on 51 NSCLC cases
studies.ai_system: uPath (Roche) and Visiopharm PD-L1 Lung Cancer TME application
studies.finding: PD-L1 tumour proportion scoring on 51 SP263-stained NSCLC cases. Pathologists showed Fleiss' kappa 0.558 for TPS <1% and 0.873 for TPS ≥50%; agreement of AI with median pathologist score at 50% cutoff was fair for uPath (Fleiss' kappa 0.354) and substantial for Visiopharm (Fleiss' kappa 0.672).
studies.limitation: Small sample of 51 cases; agreement rather than accuracy against an independent reference standard.
studies.title: Comparative performance of PD-L1 scoring by pathologists and AI algorithms.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of four LLMs with subspecialty experts on 53 ophthalmology case reports
studies.finding: On 53 case reports, ChatGPT-01 had overall diagnostic accuracy of 84.9% and DeepSeek 79.2%, Qwens 64.2%. Human experts achieved 93.3% in corneal diseases, 51.5% in glaucoma and 90.9% in neuro-ophthalmology; AI models were less accurate than experts in corneal disease but some exceeded experts in glaucoma (e.g. ChatGPT-01 +12.1%).
studies.limitation: Preprint; small sample of 53 published case reports; number of human experts not stated.
studies.title: Performance of DeepSeek, Qwen 2.5 MAX, and ChatGPT Assisting in Diagnosis of Corneal Eye Diseases, Glaucoma, and Neuro-Ophthalmology Diseases Based on Clinical Case Reports.
studies.source: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

studies.design: Single-centre retrospective comparison of DL volumetry with surgeons' manual segmentation against actual graft weight
studies.finding: Liver volume estimation from living donor CT angiography was compared between a DL model and surgeons' manual segmentation. Mean discrepancy versus surgeons was 9.18 ml, and DL estimates correlated more strongly with actual graft weights (R-squared 0.76 vs 0.68 for surgeons).
studies.limitation: Single-centre data over less than one year; number of surgeons not stated and no significance test for the correlation difference.
studies.title: Comprehensive deep learning-based assessment of living liver donor CT angiography: from vascular segmentation to volumetric analysis.

studies.design: Decision analytical modeling study with reader performance testing
studies.ai_system: Deep learning-based synthetic bone-suppressed (DLBS) nodule-detection algorithm
studies.finding: Pulmonary nodule detection on chest radiographs in an external data set (institute 3). Mean radiologist sensitivity was 77.5% unaided vs 92.1% with DLBS assistance (P < .001), and FPPI was reduced with assistance (0.071 vs 0.151; P < .001).
studies.limitation: Only 3 readers and a retrospective external data set.
studies.title: Development and Validation of a Deep Learning-Based Synthetic Bone-Suppressed Model for Pulmonary Nodule Detection in Chest Radiographs.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with cross-validation compared against radiologists' conventional imaging evaluation
studies.ai_system: Neural network model combining CT radiomics and clinicobiochemical features
studies.finding: Subtyping and lateralizing primary aldosteronism in 158 patients who underwent adrenal venous sampling. The proposed model achieved an accuracy and F1 score of 77.5% ± 3.9% and 70.5% ± 7.1% (AUC=0.771 ± 0.046), surpassing the accuracy and F1 score of radiologists' evaluation (p < .05); radiologists' figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset study with cross-validation only and no external test; radiologist comparison based on routine reports.
studies.title: Machine Learning Model with Computed Tomography Radiomics and Clinicobiochemical Characteristics Predict the Subtypes of Patients with Primary Aldosteronism.

studies.design: Reader study on pre-labeled skin lesion images
studies.humans: One expert dermatologist and one non-expert
studies.finding: Classification of malignant skin lesions from images. AI had sensitivity 93.59% and specificity 70.42%, with similar sensitivity and notably higher specificity than the expert dermatologist and non-expert.
studies.limitation: Only one dermatologist and one non-expert; human figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A Comparison of Skin Lesions' Diagnoses Between AI-Based Image Classification, an Expert Dermatologist, and a Non-Expert.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 107 ECG cases
studies.finding: For interpretation of 107 ECGs, cardiologists achieved 92.52% accuracy versus GPT-ECGReader 57.94%, GPT-ECGInterpreter 62.62% and GPT-ECGAnalyzer 62.62% (p < 0.05). Cardiologists outperformed AI across all difficulty levels, with no significant difference for normal ECGs.
studies.limitation: Only two cardiologists and a small case set.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence (ChatGPT) ready to evaluate ECG in real life? Not yet!

studies.design: Comparison on board-style multiple-choice and photo quiz case questions
studies.finding: ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0 answered American Board of Dermatology and Pediatric Dermatology Photoquiz questions compared with pediatric dermatologists. Human clinicians generally outperformed both ChatGPT versions, though ChatGPT-4.0 was comparable in some areas.
studies.limitation: Exam-style questions rather than real cases; abstract reports no numbers or clinician count.
studies.title: Pediatric dermatologists versus AI bots: Evaluating the medical knowledge and diagnostic capabilities of ChatGPT.

studies.design: Model development with reader study with and without AI segmentation masks
studies.finding: Diagnosis of odontogenic cystic lesions on CBCT with and without OCL-Net auto-segmentation masks. Average diagnostic accuracy rose from 53.21% to 55.71%, while average time decreased significantly from 101s to 47s (P<0.05).
studies.limitation: Small reader study of 7 clinicians on retrospective single-hospital images; accuracy gain small with no reported significance.
studies.title: Odontogenic cystic lesion segmentation on cone-beam CT using an auto-adapting multi-scaled UNet.

studies.design: Retrospective development and test of a deep learning model, with agreement compared against radiologists' inter-rater reliability
studies.finding: The task was grading the image quality of axial T2-weighted prostate MRI. The model predicted radiologist IQ scores with Cohen κ = 0.658, similar to human inter-rater reliability (κ = 0.688-0.791). For rescanning necessity, the model κ was 0.537 versus reviewer κ 0.577-0.703.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset study; radiologists served as both reference and comparator.
studies.title: Deep learning for quality assessment of axial T2-weighted prostate MRI: a tool to reduce unnecessary rescanning.

studies.design: Retrospective proof-of-concept on 924 whole-slide images with temporal test set
studies.finding: Distinguishing early-stage mycosis fungoides from benign inflammatory dermatoses on H&E whole-slide images. The best model reached mean balanced accuracy of 76.2 ± 3.9% (AUC 0.827 ± 0.044), nearly matching the 77.7% mean balanced accuracy of 3 expert pathologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, likely single-institution data with only 3 pathologists.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Early-Stage Mycosis Fungoides and Benign Inflammatory Dermatoses on H&E-Stained Whole-Slide Images: A Retrospective, Proof-of-Concept Study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development and validation with radiologist comparison
studies.humans: Vascular interventional radiologists, general radiologists and radiology residents
studies.finding: Detection of aortic dissection on non-contrast CT (1 138 scans). In external validation the model's sensitivity (0.976) was slightly higher than vascular interventional specialists (0.965; p = .18), and its specificity (0.935) was superior to general radiologists (0.835; p < .001). Model inference time was 3.47 seconds vs radiologists' mean 25.32 seconds.
studies.limitation: Retrospective case-control enriched dataset (1:1 dissection to controls); number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Deep Learning Application of YOLOv8 for Aortic Dissection Screening Using Non-contrast Computed Tomography.
studies.source: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

studies.design: Cross-sectional evaluation of ChatGPT-4o on radiology cases with resident comparison and assisted reading
studies.finding: On 129 radiology cases, ChatGPT-4o outperformed residents in text-based configurations (75.45% vs. 42.89%), whereas residents were slightly better on image-based tasks (64.13% vs. 61.24%). When residents used ChatGPT-4o as support, their image-based accuracy increased from 63.04% to 74.16%.
studies.limitation: Curated case set with residents only; not real clinical workflow.
studies.title: Diagnostic accuracy and consistency of ChatGPT-4o in radiology: influence of image, clinical data, and answer options on performance.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of LLMs on structured MRI reports versus neuroradiologists reading the images
studies.ai_system: GPT-4, Claude-3, GPT-3.5, Llama-2, Qwen1.5, Gemini-Pro
studies.finding: LLMs and neuroradiologists differentiated 137 intra-axial primary brain tumors. Radiologists achieved top 1, 3 and 5 accuracies of 85.4%, 94.9% and 94.9%, while the best LLM, GPT-4, achieved 65.7%, 84.7% and 90.5%.
studies.limitation: The LLMs received structured reports rather than images, so inputs differed between arms; single-institution sample.
studies.title: Intra-axial primary brain tumor differentiation: comparing large language models on structured MRI reports vs. radiologists on images.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of definitions of medical terms
studies.humans: General practitioners, resident physicians and specialist physicians
studies.finding: Defining 105 medical terms in patient-understandable language, ChatGPT-4 achieved 100% accuracy versus specialist physicians 98.1%, residents 93.3% and general practitioners 84.8% (p<0.00001).
studies.limitation: Simple binary correctness scoring of term definitions; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Is ChatGPT a Reliable Tool for Explaining Medical Terms?

studies.design: Model development with comparison against ultrasonographers
studies.humans: Mid-level ultrasonographers (4-8 years) and expert sonographers (10+ years)
studies.finding: Joint diagnosis of 8 common systemic diseases on ultrasound. UltraFedFM surpassed the diagnostic accuracy of mid-level ultrasonographers and matched expert-level sonographers; the model achieved an average AUROC of 0.927 for disease diagnosis.
studies.limitation: Human comparison numbers and reader count not reported in the abstract; mainly a model-development paper.
studies.title: From pretraining to privacy: federated ultrasound foundation model with self-supervised learning.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of two LLMs and one general pathologist on textbook histopathology cases
studies.finding: On 459 oral and maxillofacial histopathology cases from textbooks, o3 correctly classified 31.6% and GPT-4o 18.7%. A board-certified general pathologist achieved 28.3% accuracy on the same image set.
studies.limitation: Single non-subspecialist pathologist used only as a difficulty benchmark; textbook cases rather than clinical material.
studies.title: Comparative study of advanced reasoning versus baseline large-language models for histopathological diagnosis in oral and maxillofacial pathology.

studies.design: Retrospective study of chest X-rays for suspected pneumothorax with same-day CT as reference
studies.ai_system: AI system for pneumothorax detection on chest X-ray
studies.finding: Pneumothorax detection on chest radiographs against same-day CT. The AI achieved 74% accuracy, 66% sensitivity and 93% specificity, while radiologists had comparable accuracy (77%, p = 0.355), higher sensitivity (73%, p = 0.040) and lower specificity (85%, p = 0.034).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset study; radiologist performance taken from clinical reports, number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence model for the detection of pneumothorax at chest X-ray.

studies.design: Comparative study of time to prepare digital datasets for virtual implant planning
studies.finding: Dentists and an AI assistant prepared digital datasets for virtual implant planning in 20 cases. Human dentists needed 3.84±2.08 minutes on average, versus 1.88±0.64 minutes for the AI assistant (p<0.01). 71 % of AI cases required no manual adjustments.
studies.limitation: Only time efficiency was measured, not planning accuracy; small case set.
studies.title: Can AI assistants improve time efficiency in digital dataset preparation in virtual implant planning? A comparative study.

studies.design: Retrospective development of a deep learning model with temporal validation against on-screen templating
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model using AP hip radiographs
studies.humans: Surgeons performing on-screen templating (number not stated)
studies.finding: Implant size prediction for hip arthroplasty was compared against the actual implanted size. The DL model was more accurate than on-screen templating for the acetabular cup (88.9% vs. 83.3%) and femoral stem (85.7% vs. 81.6%), whereas on-screen templating was better for the bipolar head (93.2% vs. 72.7%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, single implant system, small validation set of 98 cases.
studies.title: Development of a Deep Learning Model for Hip Arthroplasty Templating Using Anteroposterior Hip Radiograph.

studies.design: Model development and validation with comparison against doctors and ChatGPT
studies.ai_system: H-SYSTEM knowledge graph-enhanced deep learning model
studies.finding: Diagnosis and treatment planning for hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage from electronic medical records. The H-SYSTEM achieved statistically higher accuracy than doctors and ChatGPT (95.26% vs 91.48%, P<.05).
studies.limitation: Number of doctors and the details of the comparison are not described in the abstract; developer-led evaluation.
studies.title: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Deep Learning Model (H-SYSTEM) for Hypertensive Intracerebral Hemorrhage: Model Development and Validation.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic study with reader comparison
studies.ai_system: 3D ResNet101 deep learning model on T2-weighted MRI
studies.finding: Prediction of lymph node metastasis in stage T1-2 rectal cancer from preoperative MRI. In the test set the ResNet101 3D model achieved an AUC of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.70, 0.89), significantly greater than pooled readers' AUC of 0.54 (95% CI: 0.48, 0.60; p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset study with small test set (86 patients) and only three readers.
studies.title: Prediction of lymph node metastasis in stage T1-2 rectal cancers with MRI-based deep learning.

studies.design: Multicenter randomized crossover reader study
studies.finding: Detection of clinically significant prostate cancer on mpMRI. With AI, lesion-level sensitivity rose from 40.1% to 59.0% and patient-level specificity from 57.7 to 71.7%, with sensitivity preserved (88.3% vs. 93.9%, p = 0.06). Median reading time fell from 423 to 185 s.
studies.limitation: Retrospective image reader study; each radiologist read only 30 cases.
studies.title: A multicenter study of artificial intelligence-aided software for detecting visible clinically significant prostate cancer on mpMRI.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study with reader comparison and AI-assisted reading
studies.finding: For identifying echinococcosis on liver ultrasound, the model outperformed senior radiologists from a high-endemicity area (AUC 0·942 vs 0·844; p=0·027). With AI assistance, AUCs improved for junior (0·743 vs 0·850; p<0·0001), attending (0·808 vs 0·886; p<0·0001) and senior radiologists (0·844 vs 0·870; p=0·092).
studies.limitation: Reader comparison on a small random subset of still images; retrospective design.
studies.title: Ultrasound identification of hepatic echinococcosis using a deep convolutional neural network model in China: a retrospective, large-scale, multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre reader study with and without AI
studies.finding: On 3047 low-prevalence screening chest radiographs, AI had AUROC 0.648, sensitivity 35.3% and specificity 94.2%. Readers' AUROCs ranged from 0.534-0.676 without AI and 0.571-0.688 with AI, with reading time 2.96-10.27 s longer with AI.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reading by only four residents; low-prevalence screening population.
studies.title: Multicentre external validation of a commercial artificial intelligence software to analyse chest radiographs in health screening environments with low disease prevalence.

studies.design: Retrospective development with blinded pathologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep learning on H&E whole-slide images
studies.finding: Predicting later brain metastasis from primary NSCLC H&E slides. The DL algorithm achieved an accuracy of 87% (p < 0.0001) compared with an average of 57.3% by the four pathologists.
studies.limitation: Small test set (40 cases) from a retrospective cohort.
studies.title: AI-guided histopathology predicts brain metastasis in lung cancer patients.

studies.design: Reader study, without then with AI after 6-week washout
studies.ai_system: Commercial mammography AI (exam-level read and markers)
studies.finding: On 758 enriched screening mammograms, radiologists' sensitivity without and with AI was 81% and 75% (p < 0.001), and specificity 67% and 86% (p < 0.001). Readers were nudged toward the AI's operating point, sometimes changing positive to negative on erroneous AI information.
studies.limitation: Enriched 1:1 cancer prevalence reader setting, not live screening; number of readers not stated.
studies.title: Reader bias in breast cancer screening related to cancer prevalence and artificial intelligence decision support-a reader study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study
studies.finding: Detection of cervical cord compression on radiography in a 42-patient test set. Correct response rate was 81.0% for the algorithm vs 66.2% for physician consensus (P = 0.034), and the algorithm exceeded each individual physician.
studies.limitation: Very small test set and case-control design.
studies.title: Deep Learning Algorithm for Identifying Cervical Cord Compression Due to Degenerative Canal Stenosis on Radiography.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Ensemble EfficientNet B4 + ResNet 50 on chest X-rays
studies.finding: Distinguishing NTM lung disease from MTB lung disease on chest X-rays. The ensemble model outperformed the radiologist on all evaluation metrics; radiologist figures are not given in the abstract, and the model's accuracy on additional validation was 0.85 for MTB-LD and 0.78 for NTM-LD.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; comparison against an unspecified radiologist with no reported human metrics.
studies.title: Distinguishing nontuberculous mycobacterial lung disease and Mycobacterium tuberculosis lung disease on X-ray images using deep transfer learning.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre model development with surgeon comparison
studies.ai_system: MVITV2 deep learning model on T2 sagittal MRI
studies.humans: Two spine surgeons of differing experience
studies.finding: Differentiating spinal tuberculosis from spinal metastases on MRI. On the external test set MVITV2 reached accuracy 91.9% and AUC 0.95, versus diagnostic accuracy of 73.7% for the less experienced and 88.9% for the more experienced spine surgeon. Authors conclude performance is comparable with experienced surgeons.
studies.limitation: Small sample (121 patients) and only two readers.
studies.title: Accurate Differentiation of Spinal Tuberculosis and Spinal Metastases Using MR-Based Deep Learning Algorithms.

studies.design: Foundation model development with clinician comparison and assisted diagnosis evaluation
studies.finding: MetaGP achieved diagnostic accuracy comparable to experienced clinicians. For emergency conditions it improved diagnostic accuracy for junior and mid-level clinicians by 53% and 46%, respectively.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives few details on study design or number of clinicians.
studies.title: MetaGP: A generative foundation model integrating electronic health records and multimodal imaging for addressing unmet clinical needs.

studies.design: Retrospective two-center radiomics study
studies.ai_system: XGBoost radiomics model on multiparametric MRI
studies.finding: Differentiation of medulloblastoma from ependymoma in children. The T1 + T2 XGBoost model achieved AUC 0.92 on the test set and 0.80 on external validation, while human expert diagnosis had AUC 0.66 and 0.69.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective sample of 135 patients; number of readers not stated.
studies.title: Multiparametric MRI-Based Interpretable Radiomics Machine Learning Model Differentiates Medulloblastoma and Ependymoma in Children: A Two-Center Study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre model development with human-machine comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep convolutional neural network on hip MRI
studies.finding: Detection of early osteonecrosis of the femoral head on hip MRI. The DCNN achieved AUROC 0.97 and accuracy 96.6% internally and AUROC 0.95 and accuracy 95.2% externally, and showed superior diagnostic performance compared with attending orthopaedic surgeons; surgeon figures are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; clinician performance numbers and reader count not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Automatic detection of early osteonecrosis of the femoral head from various hip pathologies using deep convolutional neural network: a multi-centre study.

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison
studies.finding: On 206 hand radiographs, AI had significantly lower MAE than the reader (P < 0.007). Boys: 0.488 vs 0.771 years; girls: 0.494 vs 0.673 years.
studies.limitation: Single human reader who was not a pediatric radiologist.
studies.title: High performance for bone age estimation with an artificial intelligence solution.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study against radiologist consensus
studies.finding: DLSS detected wall motion abnormalities on cine SSFP MRI in 846 segments from 53 patients with ischemic heart disease, with AUC 0.90 and sensitivity, specificity and accuracy of 86%, 85% and 86%. Inter-reader Cohen κ among four cardiothoracic radiologists was 0.60-0.78, and the algorithm was judged comparable with subspecialty radiologists.
studies.limitation: Radiologist consensus served as ground truth, so the AI was not compared head-to-head on an independent reference; the study was retrospective and small.
studies.title: Deep Learning Synthetic Strain: Quantitative Assessment of Regional Myocardial Wall Motion at MRI.

studies.design: Retrospective two-institution model development with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep learning segmentation and classification model
studies.finding: Classification of three types of knee synovitis on MRI. On the internal test set the DL model outperformed the senior radiologist (accuracy 0.86 vs 0.79; AUC 0.83 vs 0.79). On the external test set it performed as well or better than senior and junior radiologists (accuracy 0.79 vs 0.79 vs 0.73; AUC 0.76 vs 0.77 vs 0.70).
studies.limitation: Retrospective with small external test set (n = 50) and few radiologists.
studies.title: Automated Segmentation and Classification of Knee Synovitis Based on MRI Using Deep Learning.

studies.design: Blinded cross-evaluation of physician and ChatGPT answers
studies.finding: On questions about Italian occupational medicine legislation rated on a 5-point Likert scale, occupational physicians outperformed ChatGPT, while ChatGPT with access to legislative texts was comparable to professional doctors. Users tended to prefer human-generated answers.
studies.limitation: No numeric results or participant numbers reported; narrow legislative domain.
studies.title: ChatGPT in Occupational Medicine: A Comparative Study with Human Experts.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with test-set comparison against two readers
studies.ai_system: YOLOv4-based CNN for pediatric distal forearm fractures
studies.finding: On an 88-image test set, the radiologist had the best mean AUC of 0.922, followed by the model (0.892) and the orthopedist (0.830).
studies.limitation: Small test set and only two readers on a public dataset.
studies.title: Multi-Class Deep Learning Model for Detecting Pediatric Distal Forearm Fractures Based on the AO/OTA Classification.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Cross-sectional vignette comparison
studies.finding: On 16 AASM Case Book vignettes, differential diagnosis agreement was 76.7% (ChatGPT-4), 77.7% (Gemini 2.0), 70.7% (DeepSeek) vs physicians' average 72.9% (p = 0.839). For final diagnoses all LLMs scored 87.5%, within the physicians' range of 81.3%-96.9% (p = 0.606).
studies.limitation: Only 16 published vignettes and three physicians; possible training-data contamination.
studies.title: Diagnostic performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) compared with physicians in sleep medicine.

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison
studies.finding: Diagnosis of osteopenia and osteoporosis on knee X-rays. In Cohort #1, FSL models had mean accuracy 0.728 and sensitivity 0.774 vs radiologists 0.512 and 0.448. An FSL-first then radiologist pipeline achieved 0.653 accuracy, 0.582 sensitivity and 0.816 specificity, better than radiologists alone.
studies.limitation: Retrospective with limited samples; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: A few-shot learning framework for the diagnosis of osteopenia and osteoporosis using knee X-ray images.
studies.source: The Journal of international medical research

studies.design: Retrospective model development with internal validation and external testing, compared with radiological interpretation
studies.ai_system: 3-D convolutional block attention module (CBAM) model on noncontrast CT
studies.finding: Detecting hepatocellular carcinoma on noncontrast CT in 2,223 patients. On internal validation the model achieved AUC 0.807 (95% CI 0.772-0.841), comparable to radiological interpretation at 0.851 (95% CI 0.820-0.882); external testing AUC was 0.789.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; radiologist comparison only reported on internal validation and number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Opportunistic Detection of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Using Noncontrast CT and Deep Learning Artificial Intelligence.
studies.source: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR

studies.design: Model development with independent clinical evaluation comparing AI vs manual radiologist post-processing
studies.ai_system: Transfer learning-based 3D attention U-Net for CMRA segmentation
studies.finding: In 70 patients, AI vessel reformation reduced post-processing time from 632.6±17.0 s to 77.4±8.9 s and user interactions from 221±59 to 8±2 versus manual processing by radiologists. Reformatted image quality was comparable (2.7±0.8 vs 2.7±0.6; P = 0.4806).
studies.limitation: Small single cohort; compares workflow efficiency and image quality rather than diagnostic accuracy against radiologists; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Automatic vessel segmentation and reformation of non-contrast coronary magnetic resonance angiography using transfer learning-based three-dimensional U-net with attention mechanism.
studies.source: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

studies.design: Comparative vignette study, 15 standardized emergency scenarios
studies.finding: Across 15 emergency scenarios scored on diagnosis, investigations, treatment, safety and complexity, ChatGPT achieved high concordance (5/5) with the physician in 8 cases (53.3%), moderate in 4 (26.7%) and low in 3 (20.0%). Performance was strongest in protocol-based conditions and weaker in complex cases like stroke and trauma with shock.
studies.limitation: Only 15 simulated cases compared against a single physician; concordance rather than accuracy against a reference.
studies.title: Can AI match emergency physicians in managing common emergency cases? A comparative performance evaluation.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of LLMs with and without RAG against four radiologists
studies.ai_system: GPT-4o and Llama 3.1 405B with retrieval-augmented generation
studies.finding: Assigning neuroradiology MRI protocols for 100 studies. GPT-4o with RAG reached 81% sequence accuracy, comparable to radiologists (81% ± 0.21, P = .43); for contrast media, LLama 3.1 RAG 94% and GPT-4o RAG 92% vs radiologists 91%.
studies.limitation: Single-institution retrospective study of only 100 cases with gold standard set by one neuroradiologist.
studies.title: Automated MRI protocoling in neuroradiology in the era of large language models.

studies.design: Multi-reader study on 65 test radiographs
studies.finding: For spinopelvic measurements on lateral radiographs, AI ICCs were within reader ranges (e.g., TK: 0.92 vs 0.85-0.96). ANOVA confirmed no significant difference between the errors of the AI and any human reader (all p > 0.05).
studies.limitation: Small test set; reference standard derived from the same readers' median.
studies.title: Automated spinopelvic measurements on radiographs with artificial intelligence: a multi-reader study.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison on control set
studies.humans: Two spine surgeons of different experience
studies.finding: For diagnosing fresh vertebral compression fractures on X-ray, the models' accuracies on the control set were 78.1%, 78.1%, and 80.7%. These were all higher than the spine surgeons and significantly higher than the junior surgeon.
studies.limitation: Only two surgeons and a 155-case control set; surgeon figures not reported.
studies.title: Enhancing Diagnostic Accuracy of Fresh Vertebral Compression Fractures With Deep Learning Models.

studies.design: Retrospective planning comparison with blinded physician review
studies.ai_system: Automated contouring and planning scripts (Eclipse Scripting API)
studies.finding: VMAT craniospinal irradiation planning, auto-plans versus manual plans in 20 patients. In blinded review, auto-plans were marked as equivalent or superior to manual plans 88.3% of the time, with auto-contouring and planning taking 1-2 hours versus an estimated 5-6 hours manually.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 20 patients, single institution, manual time only estimated.
studies.title: Automated contouring, treatment planning, and quality assurance for VMAT craniospinal irradiation (VMAT-CSI).

studies.design: Simulated patient experiments
studies.finding: Chronic disease consultations with simulated patients across 384 patient-AI trials. ERNIE Bot reached diagnostic accuracy of 77.3% and correct prescriptions of 94.3% but high unnecessary tests (91.9%) and medications (57.8%); under standardized conditions the chatbots showed higher diagnostic accuracy but greater overprescription than human physicians.
studies.limitation: Simulated patients; physician comparison numbers and sample not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Quality safety and disparity of an AI chatbot in managing chronic diseases: simulated patient experiments.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic comparison of deep learning models vs radiologist manual readings
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model combining thyroid ultrasound and CT
studies.finding: Classifying benign vs malignant TI-RADS 3-5 thyroid nodules in 768 patients. The combined ultrasound+CT deep learning model had AUC 0.930 (95% CI: 0.892, 0.969), higher than radiologists' assessments using ultrasound alone (AUCmean 0.725) or CT alone (AUCmean 0.617).
studies.limitation: Retrospective surgical cohort with no external validation reported; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Diagnostic value of deep learning of multimodal imaging of thyroid for TI-RADS category 3-5 classification.

studies.design: Model development with comparison against ophthalmologists and a reader study of reports
studies.ai_system: RetinaVLM-Specialist; ChatGPT-4o and medical vision-language models
studies.humans: Ophthalmologists, including junior ophthalmologists; two senior ophthalmologists as report raters
studies.finding: On AMD disease staging and referral from retinal images, ChatGPT-4o and two medical VLMs significantly underperformed ophthalmologists. The curriculum-trained RetinaVLM-Specialist reached F1 0.63 for staging and 0.67 for referral, achieving performance comparable to junior ophthalmologists.
studies.limitation: The abstract does not give clinician numbers or clinician scores, and the comparison is with junior ophthalmologists only.
studies.title: Specialized curricula for training vision language models in retinal image analysis.

studies.design: Retrospective data analysis
studies.finding: The task was warfarin dose titration in 127 patients. Modeled potential time in therapeutic range with CURATE.AI was not significantly different from physician-guided dosing.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, modeled outcomes rather than prospective use; no exact figures given and the number of physicians is not stated.
studies.title: AI-assisted warfarin dose optimisation with CURATE.AI for clinical impact: Retrospective data analysis.

studies.design: Retrospective model study comparing DL and ML models with clinician prognosis using Fisher's exact test
studies.ai_system: Deep learning on periapical radiographs combined with logistic regression (DL-LR)
studies.finding: Prediction of non-surgical root canal treatment outcome from 2D periapical radiographs. The DL-LR model showed superior performance to the clinician's prognosis with a statistically significant difference (p-value < 0.05) in sensitivity, NPV and accuracy, and the same trend was seen for DL alone vs clinician prognosis.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective dataset with leave-one-out validation and no external validation; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Integrating Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Predicting Non-Surgical Root Canal Treatment Outcomes Using Two-Dimensional Periapical Radiographs.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with internal and external validation, compared with three clinicians
studies.ai_system: 3D deep learning models on CT nodule regions
studies.finding: Malignancy prediction of incidental sub-centimeter pulmonary nodules on CT. Nodule-box and baseline plus follow-up models had accuracy 86.4% and 90.4% in the testing set, versus 67.0%, 82.5% and 90.0% for resident, junior and senior clinicians; the follow-up model performed comparably to the senior clinician.
studies.limitation: Only three clinicians; retrospective data.
studies.title: Deep learning for malignancy risk estimation of incidental sub-centimeter pulmonary nodules on CT images.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with pathologist comparison
studies.finding: Detection and risk subtyping of basal cell carcinoma on whole-slide images. Models achieved AUCs up to 0.997 for detection and 0.931 for risk stratification internally, and performance was comparable to that of two pathologists who scored 240 BCC positive slides.
studies.limitation: Only two pathologists; human comparison metrics not quantified in the abstract; retrospective.
studies.title: Detection and subtyping of basal cell carcinoma in whole-slide histopathology using weakly-supervised learning.

studies.design: Exam question benchmark against human question-bank users
studies.ai_system: Llama 2, Google Bard, Bing Chat, ChatGPT-3.5
studies.humans: Medical doctors preparing for the MSRA (Qbank users)
studies.finding: Answering 100 MSRA Clinical Problem Solving questions. Bing Chat surpassed human users, Llama 2 was inferior to them, and Google Bard and ChatGPT-3.5 did not differ significantly from human candidates.
studies.limitation: Multiple-choice exam questions only; human comparator is aggregate question-bank data.
studies.title: Evaluation of Large language model performance on the Multi-Specialty Recruitment Assessment (MSRA) exam.

studies.design: Vignette study with synthetic neurological cases
studies.humans: Neurology experts and general medical doctors
studies.finding: Diagnosis of neurological diseases from synthetic anamneses. ChatGPT diagnostic accuracy ranged from 68.5% ± 3.28% to 83.83% ± 2.73%, versus 81.66% ± 2.02% for other experts and 57.15% ± 2.64% for general medical doctors.
studies.limitation: Synthetic expert-generated cases rather than real patients; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: ChatGPT M.D.: Is there any room for generative AI in neurology?

studies.design: Benchmark on board questions compared with historical urologist performance from literature
studies.ai_system: UroBot (GPT-4o with retrieval augmented generation on EAU guidelines)
studies.finding: Answering 200 European Board of Urology in-service assessment questions. UroBot-4o achieved a mean rate of correct answers of 88.4%, versus an average of 68.7% reported in the literature for urologists.
studies.limitation: Human comparison is a historical literature figure, not a concurrent head-to-head on the same questions; exam questions not real care.
studies.title: Superhuman performance on urology board questions using an explainable language model enhanced with European Association of Urology guidelines.
studies.source: ESMO real world data and digital oncology

studies.design: Two-centre retrospective model development with internal and external validation
studies.finding: Differentiating pleomorphic adenoma from Warthin tumour on ultrasound in 203 patients. The USEML model achieved AUC 0.891 and outperformed physicians in internal and external validation (both p < 0.05); sensitivity 89.3% vs 75.0%, specificity 87.5% vs 54.2%.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective sample (203 patients); number and experience of physicians not stated.
studies.title: An ultrasound-based ensemble machine learning model for the preoperative classification of pleomorphic adenoma and Warthin tumor in the parotid gland.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with test-set comparison to specialist interpretation
studies.finding: Classifying AD, FTD or cognitively normal on FDG-PET, the model achieved 89.8 % accuracy in the test set. The physicians' consensus showed 69.5 % accuracy.
studies.limitation: Small test set, retrospective, three readers, no external validation.
studies.title: A 3D convolutional neural network to classify subjects as Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia or healthy controls using brain 18F-FDG PET.

studies.design: Vignette-based agreement study
studies.finding: Judging whether the final diagnosis was in 246 top-10 differential diagnosis lists from 82 vignettes, ChatGPT-4 agreed with physicians in 236 out of 246 (95.9 %), kappa 0.86.
studies.limitation: Agreement only, physicians as reference; single department vignettes.
studies.title: Can ChatGPT-4 evaluate whether a differential diagnosis list contains the correct diagnosis as accurately as a physician?

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader comparison and AI-guided reading
studies.ai_system: Cascaded CNN landmark detection model for angle measurement
studies.humans: An orthopedic surgeon and a general physician
studies.finding: The model showed smaller absolute average angle errors than both human observers for flatfoot diagnosis. With model guidance, average errors decreased from 2.35° ± 3.01° to 1.55° ± 2.09° (orthopedic surgeon) and from 1.99° ± 2.76° to 1.56° ± 2.19° (general physician), both p < 0.001.
studies.limitation: Only two observers; development data from young Korean males.
studies.title: Automated diagnosis of flatfoot using cascaded convolutional neural network for angle measurements in weight-bearing lateral radiographs.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to attending doctors
studies.finding: Children's caries diagnosis on dental panoramic radiographs. The model reached accuracy 0.8557 and AUC 0.9223 and showed higher caries diagnosis accuracy than two attending doctors for the first and second primary molars.
