studies.limitation: Only two comparator doctors; the human accuracy figures are not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Tooth Type Enhanced Transformer for Children Caries Diagnosis on Dental Panoramic Radiographs.

studies.design: Cross-sectional exam evaluation compared with radiologists' average scores
studies.humans: Radiologists taking the European Board of Radiology exam
studies.finding: Performance on the full official EBR exam. In Part 1 GPT-4o scored 70.2% vs 58.4% radiologists' average; in Part 2 (clinically oriented reasoning) it scored 52.9% vs 66.1%.
studies.limitation: Exam setting rather than clinical practice; radiologist comparison uses average scores, number not stated.
studies.title: Evaluating GPT-4o's Performance in the Official European Board of Radiology Exam: A Comprehensive Assessment.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of LLM responses with clinician-derived responses on guideline-based scenarios
studies.finding: Responses to NCCN guideline-based pancreatic adenocarcinoma management scenarios. LLM responses were completely correct in 42% (ChatGPT 52%, Copilot 33%), and clinician responses were more concise (32 ± 13 vs 270 ± 70 words, P < .001); clinician accuracy is not quantified in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Clinician accuracy not reported; clinician reference used mainly as comparator for conciseness; small scenario set.
studies.title: Use of large language models as clinical decision support tools for management pancreatic adenocarcinoma using National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines.

studies.design: Retrospective development and validation with reader comparison
studies.humans: Expert group (orthopedic surgeons, radiologists) and non-expert group (emergency physicians, general practice doctors)
studies.finding: Detection of non-displaced femoral neck fractures on paired AP and lateral hip radiographs. The model had an accuracy of 96.7% (95% CI: 93.9%, 99.5%) versus 90.5% (95% CI: 85.7%, 95.2%) for the expert group.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-centre development; number of human readers not stated.
studies.title: Development and validation of a deep-learning model for the detection of non-displaced femoral neck fractures with anteroposterior and lateral hip radiographs.
studies.source: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

studies.design: Model development with comparison against expert clinicians
studies.finding: Classification of odontogenic lesions on panoramic radiographs. The model outperformed human expert clinicians in classification by 10.7 % and 10.8 % in recall and F1 score, respectively.
studies.limitation: Number and experience of clinicians not stated; model-development paper.
studies.title: Diagnosing oral and maxillofacial diseases using deep learning.

studies.design: Diagnostic accuracy reader comparison
studies.finding: Detection of periapical periodontitis on 30 radiographs. AI accuracy was 89.6%, versus 98.5% for Radiologist 1 and 81.7% for Radiologist 2.
studies.limitation: Only 30 images and two readers.
studies.title: Comparison of the Artificial Intelligence Versus Traditional Radiographic Interpretation in Detecting Periapical Periodontitis: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study.

studies.design: Two-group case-based reader study
studies.ai_system: AI application detecting and localising distal radius fractures
studies.finding: Physicians diagnosed and managed twenty realistic wrist trauma cases with or without AI fracture detection. The AI-supported group diagnosed without additional CT or senior consultation in 75% vs. 52% of cases (p = 0.003), had sensitivity 1.00 vs. 0.96 (p = 0.06) and specificity 0.99 vs. 0.93 (p = 0.17), and used fewer additional CT scans (14% vs. 28%, p = 0.02).
studies.limitation: Simulated cases with only twenty cases; number of physicians not stated; accuracy differences not statistically significant.
studies.title: The potential benefit of artificial intelligence regarding clinical decision-making in the treatment of wrist trauma patients.
studies.source: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison against two blinded readers
studies.finding: Classification of LGE cardiac MRI images into myocardial infarction, myocarditis and healthy. The model achieved 96% accuracy and surpassed the accuracy of Reader 1 by 27% and Reader 2 by 17%.
studies.limitation: Only two readers, experience unclear; single dataset of images.
studies.title: Deep Transfer Learning for Classification of Late Gadolinium Enhancement Cardiac MRI Images into Myocardial Infarction, Myocarditis, and Healthy Classes: Comparison with Subjective Visual Evaluation.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-reader study with and without AI assistance, 1-month washout
studies.ai_system: Transformer-based deep learning model for cervical spine stenosis grading
studies.humans: Ten radiologists (0-7 years of experience), including residents
studies.finding: Ten radiologists graded spinal canal and neural foramina stenosis on 50 degenerative cervical spine MRIs with and without DLM assistance. DLM assistance reduced mean interpretation time from 159-490 s to 90-182 s (p<.001) and improved interobserver agreement, e.g. residents' dichotomous spinal canal grading κ = 0.63 to 0.77 (p<.001). Independent DLM performance alone was equivalent or superior to all readers.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only 50 MRIs from external data and a small reader group.
studies.title: Using deep learning to enhance reporting efficiency and accuracy in degenerative cervical spine MRI.
studies.source: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison against and assistance of junior radiologists
studies.ai_system: Radiomics and deep transfer learning feature fusion model (DeepLabV3 ResNet segmentation)
studies.finding: Quality assessment of fetal nuchal translucency ultrasound images. The feature fusion model achieved AUC 0.978 and accuracy 93.2%; it was reported as more reliable than junior radiologists and significantly improved their capabilities, but radiologist figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Radiologist performance numbers and reader count not reported; retrospective image set.
studies.title: Intelligent quality assessment of ultrasound images for fetal nuchal translucency measurement during the first trimester of pregnancy based on deep learning models.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective development with prospective external validation; reader comparison and AI-assisted reading
studies.ai_system: CTSGrader joint deep learning model (ultrasound plus clinical data)
studies.humans: Two junior and two senior radiologists
studies.finding: For grading carpal tunnel syndrome severity, CTSGrader achieved accuracies of 0.849, 0.833 and 0.827 and outperformed two junior and one senior radiologists (all p<.05), equivalent to 1 senior radiologist. With its assistance, accuracies of two junior and one senior radiologists improved (all p<.05).
studies.limitation: Only four radiologists; largely retrospective data from China.
studies.title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Grading Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: A Multicenter Study in China.

studies.design: Blinded rating study, preprint
studies.finding: Five clinicians rated 36 ChatGPT and 29 human suggestions for improving 7 CDS alerts. Of the 20 highest-scoring suggestions, 9 were generated by ChatGPT; AI suggestions were highly understandable and relevant but had moderate usefulness and low acceptance.
studies.limitation: Preprint; very small sample of alerts and raters.
studies.title: Assessing the Value of ChatGPT for Clinical Decision Support Optimization.
studies.source: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

studies.design: Retrospective algorithm development and validation with pathologist comparison and with/without AI reading
studies.ai_system: Convolutional neural network for tumour detection and regression grading
studies.humans: 12 board-certified pathologists; 3 pathologists in the assisted reading
studies.finding: AI regression grading agreed with 12 pathologists in 63·6% of cases (quadratic kappa 0·749) and triggered reclassification in seven cases, six with small tumour regions missed by pathologists. Use of the AI tool by three pathologists increased interobserver agreement and substantially reduced diagnostic time per case.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, with only three pathologists in the assisted reading and no quantitative assisted accuracy figures in the abstract.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence for tumour tissue detection and histological regression grading in oesophageal adenocarcinomas: a retrospective algorithm development and validation study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre reader study with internal and external test sets
studies.ai_system: CNN-based CAD for prostate MRI (concurrent read and AI-first read)
studies.finding: Prostate cancer diagnosis on MRI: in the internal test, accuracy of AI-based CAD methods was equivalent to radiologists (e.g. 127/150 vs. 130/150 vs. 125/150 for reader 1; all p > 0.05). In the external test, concurrent read was better than or equal to radiologists alone (79/100 vs. 72/100, p = 0.039, reader 1; 87/100 vs. 86/100, p = 1.000, reader 2), and AI-first read was faster (8.54 s/7.66 s vs. 92.72 s/89.54 s).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only two readers and a small external test set.
studies.title: The added value of AI-based computer-aided diagnosis in classification of cancer at prostate MRI.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of deep learning vs radiologists
studies.humans: Three radiologists of varying experience (expert, board-certified, resident)
studies.finding: Distinguishing malignant from benign non-mass enhancement on breast MRI in 86 lesions. The precise-segmentation model (AUC = 0.91) was equivalent to a highly experienced radiologist (AUC = 0.89; p = 0.45); the rough-segmentation model (AUC = 0.80) was equivalent to a board-certified radiologist (AUC = 0.79). Both models exceeded a radiology resident (AUC = 0.64).
studies.limitation: Small single-centre sample with only three readers and manual expert annotation required for the model.
studies.title: Use of a deep learning algorithm for non-mass enhancement on breast MRI: comparison with radiologists' interpretations at various levels.

studies.design: Retrospective development and test of a deep learning ultrasound model compared with radiologists
studies.ai_system: Deep learning ultrasound model combined with clinical data
studies.finding: For differentiating benign from malignant parotid gland tumors on ultrasound, the DL model had a significantly higher AUC than the three doctors with clinical data (AUC =0.9583 vs. 0.6250, 0.7250, and 0.8025; all P<0.05). Its sensitivity was also higher (97.2% vs. 65%, 80%, and 90%).
studies.limitation: Small single-dataset test set of 41 patients after selective exclusion of cases, with only three readers.
studies.title: A deep learning model for the differential diagnosis of benign and malignant salivary gland tumors based on ultrasound imaging and clinical data.
studies.source: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective model development with external test set and reader comparison
studies.finding: Determining myometrial invasion >50% in endometrial cancer on transvaginal ultrasound. In the external testing set EfficientNet-B6 achieved AUC 0.814 and accuracy 0.802, while the 15 radiologists had average accuracy of 0.681 and average AUC of 0.678. The model was significantly better than the radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with a small external test set of 95 patients.
studies.title: A Transvaginal Ultrasound-Based Deep Learning Model for the Noninvasive Diagnosis of Myometrial Invasion in Patients with Endometrial Cancer: Comparison with Radiologists.

studies.design: Retrospective model development compared with physician groups
studies.finding: Detection of distal radius fractures on wrist X-rays. The ensemble model achieved accuracy 97.03%, sensitivity 95.70% and specificity 98.37%, and was superior to both orthopedic and radiology attending physician groups; physician figures not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Physician numbers and results not reported in abstract; balanced retrospective dataset.
studies.title: Deep learning assisted diagnosis system: improving the diagnostic accuracy of distal radius fractures.

studies.design: Reader study, readers assessed MRI scans first without then with AI volumetry
studies.ai_system: Deep learning rapid brain volumetry with lobe segmentation
studies.humans: Two neuroradiologists, two radiologists, three radiology residents
studies.finding: Seven readers differentiated AD, FTD and controls on 55 MRI scans without then with AI. AI improved AD diagnostic accuracy (AUC -AI: 0.800, +AI: 0.926, p < 0.05), and for FTD overall consensus (p < 0.01), BCNR (p < 0.02) and BCR (p < 0.05) recorded significantly more correct diagnoses.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 55 patients; fixed sequential read order (without then with AI) may introduce recall bias.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-based rapid brain volumetry substantially improves differential diagnosis in dementia.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with internal and external testing and radiologist comparison
studies.finding: For classifying moyamoya disease, atherosclerotic disease and normal controls on MRA, DenseNet-121 achieved macro-average AUC of 0.977 internally and 0.880 externally. The abstract reports this as comparable diagnostic capability to that of the human radiologists.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists, small test sets, and radiologist metrics not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Deep learning model for automated diagnosis of moyamoya disease based on magnetic resonance angiography.

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison of radiologists, CNN and synthetic MRI
studies.finding: For differentiating astrocytoma from oligodendroglioma using the T2-FLAIR mismatch sign, mean sensitivity, specificity and AUC of radiologists vs AI were 76.3% vs. 94.7%, 100% vs. 92.9%, and 0.880 vs. 0.938. The AI increased sensitivity and objectivity compared with the radiologists.
studies.limitation: Very small test set of 33 cases, with AI trained on only 50 patients.
studies.title: Comparison of diagnostic performance of radiologist- and AI-based assessments of T2-FLAIR mismatch sign and quantitative assessment using synthetic MRI in the differential diagnosis between astrocytoma, IDH-mutant and oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted.

studies.design: Interrater reliability study on 38 CBCT datasets
studies.finding: Detection of periodontal lesions on 38 CBCT datasets was compared between three dentists and a CNN. The CNN's performance was significantly lower than the human readers, who achieved good to very good interobserver agreement.
studies.limitation: Very small sample of 38 datasets and three readers; quantitative metrics not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Comparison between observer-based and AI-based reading of CBCT datasets: An interrater-reliability study.

studies.design: Model development with comparison against expert clinicians on unseen scans
studies.finding: Differential diagnosis of neuromuscular diseases from muscle MRI, compared on 14 previously unseen scans. Compared to four expert clinicians, the model obtained the highest top-3 accuracy (75.0% ± 4.8%).
studies.limitation: Comparison with clinicians based on only 14 scans and four experts; clinician figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Myo-Guide: A Machine Learning-Based Web Application for Neuromuscular Disease Diagnosis With MRI.
studies.source: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle

studies.design: Model development with comparison against ophthalmologists
studies.finding: Severity-based classification of allergic conjunctival diseases from slit-lamp images. The AI pipeline had a diagnostic accuracy of 86.2%, versus 60.0% for board-certified ophthalmologists.
studies.limitation: Number of ophthalmologists and comparison test set details not stated in abstract.
studies.title: Use of explainable AI on slit-lamp images of anterior surface of eyes to diagnose allergic conjunctival diseases.
studies.source: Allergology international : official journal of the Japanese Society of Allergology

studies.design: Prospective vignette-based diagnostic benchmarking study
studies.humans: Expert panel of a pediatric endocrinologist and a pediatric orthopedic surgeon
studies.finding: Using vignettes of 45 children with genetically confirmed skeletal dysplasias, ChatGPT and DeepSeek achieved top-3 diagnostic accuracy of 62.2% and 64.4%. The expert panel outperformed both models (82.2%).
studies.limitation: Small sample of 45 vignettes compared against only two experts.
studies.title: The Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Diagnosis of Skeletal Dysplasias in Pediatric Patients: A Comparative Benchmark Study of Large Language Models and a Clinical Expert Group.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective reader study with and without DL assistance
studies.ai_system: Deep learning cerebral aneurysm detection model
studies.finding: Detection of cerebral aneurysms in 484 test patients from three institutions. With DL assistance AUC increased from 0.842 to 0.881 (P = 0.008) for junior and from 0.853 to 0.895 (P < 0.001) for senior radiologists, with lesion-level sensitivity rising (JR: 68.9% to 81.6%; SR: 72.4% to 83.5%). Interpretation time fell by 37.2% and post-processing time by 90.8%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study; standalone AI results not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Enhancing Radiologists' Performance in Detecting Cerebral Aneurysms Using a Deep Learning Model: A Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Retrospective two-cohort pediatric study comparing DL model with radiologist TIRADS interpretation
studies.finding: Diagnosis of malignancy in 156 pediatric thyroid nodules was assessed. AI-Thyroid achieved AUROC 0.913-0.929, sensitivity 78.7-89.4% and specificity 79.8-91.7%, and yielded the highest AUROC, followed by ACR-TIRADS and K-TIRADS (p = 0.016 and p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Small retrospective pediatric sample; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: A Deep Learning-Based Artificial Intelligence Model Assisting Thyroid Nodule Diagnosis and Management: Pilot Results for Evaluating Thyroid Malignancy in Pediatric Cohorts.
studies.source: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association

studies.design: Retrospective reproducibility study of automated segmentation on multiphasic abdominal CT versus human readers
studies.ai_system: TotalSegmentator (compared also with an nnU-Net trained on BTCV)
studies.finding: Segmentation volume reproducibility across contrast phases was assessed on 1252 multiphasic abdominal CT scans. TotalSegmentator's absolute volume deviation between contrast phases was superior to the interreader AVD for the same contrast phase (p = 0.036), and its AVD of 6.50% beat the nnU-Net's 10.03%.
studies.limitation: Single-institution retrospective study measuring reproducibility rather than accuracy, with only two human readers.
studies.title: Intra-Individual Reproducibility of Automated Abdominal Organ Segmentation-Performance of TotalSegmentator Compared to Human Readers and an Independent nnU-Net Model.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Retrospective reader study, with/without AI sessions 1 month apart
studies.ai_system: Knee AI assistant (deep learning trained on 23,074 MRIs)
studies.humans: Six radiologists with 2-10 years MSK experience
studies.finding: Six radiologists read 165 knee MRIs for ACL, meniscus, cartilage and MCL lesions with and without AI. AI assistance improved sensitivity from 81% to 86%, accuracy from 86% to 91% and specificity from 88% to 93% (p < 0.001). Fleiss' Kappa rose from 54% to 78%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset reader study with only six readers.
studies.title: Impact of AI assistance on radiologist interpretation of knee MRI.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter reader study, with and without AI in randomized order
studies.humans: Seven ob-gyns and seven maternal-fetal medicine specialists
studies.finding: Readers assessed 200 second-trimester fetal ultrasound exams for findings suspicious for congenital heart defects. AI-aided readers had higher AUROC (0.974 vs 0.825, P=.002), sensitivity (0.935 vs 0.782) and specificity (0.970 vs 0.759). Reading time fell (226 vs 274 seconds) and confidence rose (4.63 vs 3.90).
studies.limitation: Retrospective enriched dataset (50% abnormal) with only interpretable standard views.
studies.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence-Based Software to Aid in the Identification of Ultrasound Findings Associated With Fetal Congenital Heart Defects.

studies.design: Comparative study of LLMs vs urologists on three simulated clinical cases
studies.finding: R1 and o3 were compared with practicing urologists on three real-world prostate cancer cases scored with the CDQAS by blinded senior oncologists. Both models performed comparably with physicians in overall readability and diagnostic appropriateness. Human clinicians maintained strengths in terminology precision and logical reasoning.
studies.limitation: Only three clinical cases; number of urologists not stated.
studies.title: Evaluating the Clinical Competence of Large Language Models in Prostate Cancer Management: A Comparative Study of DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT.

studies.design: Retrospective reader analysis within the PROSA screening trial
studies.humans: One less-experienced radiologist, with expert radiologist as reference
studies.finding: On 499 screening bpMRIs, the AI-assisted less-experienced reader achieved sensitivity 76.5%, specificity 97.2%, AUC 0.969, versus AI alone (sensitivity 58.8%, AUC 0.952) and the unaided reader (sensitivity 67.6%, AUC 0.932). Inter-reader agreement improved with AI from κ = 0.64 to 0.84.
studies.limitation: Single centre, single less-experienced reader, retrospective, with expert reading rather than pathology as reference.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted reading of non-contrast prostate MRI: application and concordance with expert interpretation in a screening population within the PROSA trial.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre comparison of a deep learning detector versus spinal specialists on lumbar MRI
studies.finding: On lumbar MRI from 654 patients (50 in the testing set), the PP-YOLOv2 algorithm reached a mAP of 90.08% and showed higher sensitivity, specificity and accuracy than manual identification by spinal surgeons. Testing time was significantly shorter than manual identification (P < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective study with a 50-case test set and only three readers; human accuracy figures not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: MRI to digital medicine diagnosis: integrating deep learning into clinical decision-making for lumbar degenerative diseases.

studies.design: Preliminary cross-sectional study comparing deep learning quantification with physician visual scoring
studies.finding: In 80 patients with CTD-ILD, the AUC of QILD scores for identifying FVC% <70 was significantly higher with DL-QZIP (0.833) than with the visual method (0.660) (P < 0.01). Correlations between the two methods were 0.75 for QGG, 0.61 for QFIB and 0.75 for QILD.
studies.limitation: Preliminary single-centre study of 80 patients; number of readers not stated.
studies.title: Novel deep-learning analysis for connective tissue disease-related interstitial lung disease extent assessment on CT: a preliminary cross-sectional study.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison against orthopedic residents
studies.ai_system: HigherHRNet-W48-based deep learning model for hip ultrasound
studies.finding: Automated DDH diagnosis on infant hip ultrasound images from 417 infants. The model's AUC for DDH detection on qualifying images was 0.92, exceeding the diagnostic accuracy of the resident; apex point estimation was also more accurate than orthopedic residents.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single dataset; resident comparison numbers and number of readers not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Diagnosis on Ultrasound Images for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip with a Deep Learning-Based Model Focusing on Signal Heterogeneity in the Bone Region.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with external validation compared against two radiologists
studies.ai_system: Deep learning segmentation/classification models for knee MRI meniscal injury
studies.finding: Meniscal injury classification on 206 external knee MRIs was compared between DL models and two radiologists. The binary classification model outperformed the junior radiologist (0.82-0.87 versus 0.74-0.88).
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists; retrospective; comparison with senior radiologist not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Fully and Weakly Supervised Deep Learning for Meniscal Injury Classification, and Location Based on MRI.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Retrospective development study with blinded image-level comparison against endoscopists
studies.ai_system: Vision Transformer-based AI for peroral cholangioscopy
studies.finding: On a balanced 440-image test set of cholangioscopy images of indeterminate biliary strictures, the ViT model had an accuracy of 78.4%. Expert endoscopists reached 82.0% (p = 0.148) and non-experts 73.0% (p = 0.066), with no statistically significant differences.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset study of 125 patients with image-level evaluation; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: Vendor-Agnostic Vision Transformer-Based Artificial Intelligence for Peroral Cholangioscopy: Diagnostic Performance in Biliary Strictures Compared With Convolutional Neural Networks and Endoscopists.
studies.source: Digestive endoscopy : official journal of the Japan Gastroenterological Endoscopy Society

studies.design: Retrospective model development with endoscopist comparison
studies.finding: Differentiating small and micro gastric stromal tumors from leiomyomas on EUS images. Tumor-level ResNet50 AUCs were 0.911 and 0.915 in the two validation sets; endoscopists exhibited notably lower AUC values than the EUS-AI model.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, small dataset; endoscopist numbers and results not reported in abstract.
studies.title: An artificial intelligence model utilizing endoscopic ultrasonography for differentiating small and micro gastric stromal tumors from gastric leiomyomas.

studies.design: Model development plus fully crossed multi-reader multi-case study
studies.ai_system: Knowledge-distilled modality fusion deep learning model using non-contrast MRI
studies.finding: For diagnosing nasopharyngeal carcinoma, readers using non-contrast MRI with AI assistance achieved AUC 0.90, versus 0.93 with contrast-enhanced imaging, reported as not inferior. The abstract compares AI-assisted non-contrast reading with contrast-enhanced reading rather than unaided non-contrast reading.
studies.limitation: The comparator is a different imaging modality, so the effect of AI help on the same images is unclear.
studies.title: Deep learning-based non-contrast MRI model for nasopharyngeal carcinoma diagnosis: an end-to-end gadolinium-free solution.

studies.design: Retrospective study of 50,000 screened women with a reader study of arbitration cases
studies.ai_system: AI tool used as second reader in double-read breast screening
studies.humans: Breast screening readers (22 in the arbitration reader study)
studies.finding: The study tested replacing the second human reader with AI in a double-read breast-screening workflow that includes arbitration. After arbitration, the AI arm was noninferior (5% margin) to two human readers in sensitivity and specificity (P < 0.001), with a workload benefit. Arbitration overruled some correct AI recalls of interval and next-round cancers.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design at two NHS centres, with arbitration simulated in a reader study.
studies.title: Impact of using artificial intelligence as a second reader in breast screening including arbitration.

studies.design: Online clinician diagnostic reader study
studies.finding: Nine ENT physicians diagnosed ear abnormalities from 86 ears using AI composite images, manually selected still frames, or video. SelectStitch and Still images were not statistically different (P > .50), but both differed from Video (P < .01), which performed better at the cost of longer diagnosis time.
studies.limitation: Small number of readers in an online survey setting; comparator is image format rather than unaided reading.
studies.title: Digital Otoscopy With Computer-Aided Composite Image Generation: Impact on the Correct Diagnosis, Confidence, and Time.
studies.source: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery

studies.design: Model development with blinded radiologist report evaluation and prospective user studies
studies.finding: Chest radiograph reports: radiologists judged AI-generated and human-written reports clinically equivalent in 64% of all cases, rising to 91% for normal studies. In user studies, MedVersa use was associated with notable reductions in report writing time and clinically relevant discrepancies compared with standard workflows.
studies.limitation: User-study effect sizes and number of radiologists not reported in the abstract; primarily a model development paper.
studies.title: MedVersa: A Generalist Foundation Model for Diverse Medical Imaging Tasks.

studies.design: Retrospective difference-in-differences analysis
studies.finding: Report-drafting time for chest CT lung nodule reports across 185,044 reports. Pooled analysis showed a modest overall increase of 0.86 minutes (95% CI 0.14 to 1.57); at one hospital a 2.66-minute relative improvement (P<.001) was seen, while the other showed a nonsignificant increase of 0.90 minutes.
studies.limitation: Observational design with nonequivalent comparison groups; heterogeneous results across two sites.
studies.title: Measuring the Impact of AI on Report-Drafting Efficiency in Chest Computed Tomography Interpretation: Retrospective Analysis.

studies.design: Multi-institutional diagnostic reader study, 1117 cases
studies.ai_system: CNN and PanDerm unimodal/multimodal foundation models
studies.finding: Multiclass skin lesion diagnosis: all readers outperformed the CNN (65.9% vs 56.7%). The unimodal model (72.2%) exceeded readers with less than 3 years of experience (68.2%), but experts with more than 10 years of experience (74.2%) outperformed all AI models.
studies.limitation: Readers assessed 100-case samples from image data rather than live patients.
studies.title: Limits of Artificial Intelligence Models for Skin Cancer Diagnosis in Realistic Settings.

studies.design: Comparison of LLM scores with official physician scores on 2022 Israeli board examinations
studies.humans: 849 residents taking the Israeli specialist licence examination
studies.finding: Board residency exam performance across five disciplines. GPT-4 ranked at a median percentile of 74.7% in psychiatry, 44.4% in general surgery and 56.6% in internal medicine, but lower in pediatrics (17.4%) and OB/GYN (23.44%); GPT-3.5 failed all disciplines.
studies.limitation: Multiple-choice exam questions rather than real clinical practice.
studies.title: GPT versus Resident Physicians - A Benchmark Based on Official Board Scores.

studies.design: Benchmark of 750 script concordance test questions compared with human test takers
studies.ai_system: Ten LLMs including o3, GPT-4o, o1-preview, DeepSeek R1, Gemini 2.5 Pro
studies.finding: Clinical reasoning under uncertainty on script concordance tests. o3 scored highest (67.8%±1.2%), followed by GPT-4o (63.9%±1.3%); models matched or exceeded students but did not reach senior residents or attending physicians.
studies.limitation: Written vignette test format, not real patient care.
studies.title: Assessment of Large Language Models in Clinical Reasoning: A Novel Benchmarking Study.

studies.design: Prospective comparative study on clinical images of nail diseases
studies.ai_system: GPT-4o, Grok 3, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Flash
studies.humans: Seventeen dermatologists from residents to nail disease experts
studies.finding: Dermatologists and four multimodal LLMs diagnosed nail diseases from clinical images. Dermatologists were correct in 70.6% (primary diagnosis) and 80.3% (with differentials) of cases, versus 25.0% and 35.0% for AI models (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Exploratory, image-only setting with freely available general-purpose models; larger representative datasets needed.
studies.title: Human expertise or artificial intelligence? A prospective study on nail disorder diagnosis.

studies.design: Proof-of-concept benchmark on simulated psychiatric interviews against expert consensus
studies.finding: LLMs rated transcripts of three simulated psychiatric interviews on 100 AMDP items, and clinicians rated the full audiovisual recordings. The best LLMs reached accuracy 0.72, the 64th percentile of the clinician distribution. GPT-5.1 per-scenario accuracies were 0.81, 0.76 and 0.60, against clinician means of 0.79, 0.68 and 0.58.
studies.limitation: Only three simulated interviews; LLMs received transcripts while clinicians saw recordings.
studies.title: Benchmarking large language models against practicing clinicians on psychopathological assessment.

studies.design: Prospective reader study with eye tracking; three reporting modes (free-text, structured, AI-prefilled structured)
studies.ai_system: AI-prefilled structured reporting for chest radiographs
studies.humans: 4 novice readers (residents and medical students) and 4 non-novice resident radiologists
studies.finding: Eight readers each reported 35 bedside chest radiographs in three modes. Diagnostic accuracy was κ = 0.58 for free-text, κ = 0.60 for SR and κ = 0.71 for AI-SR (both P < .001), with improvements for novice and non-novice readers (Δκ = 0.17 and 0.09). Mean reporting time fell from 88 seconds for free-text to 37 seconds for SR and 25 seconds for AI-SR.
studies.limitation: Very small reader sample (8 readers, mostly trainees) and only 35 radiographs.
studies.title: Effect of Reporting Mode and Clinical Experience on Radiologists' Gaze and Image Analysis Behavior at Chest Radiography.

studies.design: Prospective cohort deployment study at a single quaternary children's hospital
studies.finding: Prediction of critical deterioration events in 1005 PICU patients. P-WIN detected 73% of CDEs 1-24 hours in advance, compared with 39% for the PICU Warning Tool and 23% for the huddle workflow (P < .05), with similar PPV across approaches.
studies.limitation: Single-centre, three-month study; the human comparator is a workflow rather than individual clinicians, and the number of clinicians is not stated.
studies.title: P-WIN deployment: real-time personalized machine learning to predict critical deterioration in a pediatric intensive care unit.

studies.design: Preclinical randomized controlled trial
studies.finding: Surgeons identified bleeding sites in laparoscopic videos with or without AI assistance. Reaction time was 2.53 s with AI vs. 3.23 s without (P < 0.001). The negative emotion score was 1.68 vs. 2.95 (P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Preclinical, video-based setting rather than live surgery.
studies.title: AI enhanced surgeons' faster responses to intraoperative bleeding in laparoscopic surgery: a preclinical randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Model development with multi-institution contouring study with and without auto-segmentation
studies.ai_system: Deep learning auto-segmentation for cervical cancer radiotherapy
studies.finding: Physicians delineated radiotherapy contours with and without auto-segmented contours. Auto-segmentation reduced inter-physician heterogeneity and shortened contouring time by 30 min.
studies.limitation: Number of physicians not stated and heterogeneity results not quantified in the abstract.
studies.title: Comprehensive clinical evaluation of deep learning-based auto-segmentation for radiotherapy in patients with cervical cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective cross-sectional comparison of CNN models with clinicians on eyelid photographs
studies.finding: Classification of eyelid lesions on 4954 clinical photographs. For ternary classification CNN accuracies were 82.1% and 83.0%, inferior to the nine clinicians (87.0-89.5%); for binary malignant vs benign classification CNN accuracies were 87.5% and 92.5%, similar to clinicians (85.8-90.0%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset photograph study without external validation.
studies.title: Differentiating malignant and benign eyelid lesions using deep learning.

studies.design: Retrospective crossover reader study with randomized reading order
studies.finding: Thyroid nodule ultrasound assessment in 650 patients. With Koios DS, average AUC increased by 0.083 and sensitivity and specificity by 8.4% and 14%; time per case decreased by 23.6% and inter-reader correlation rose from r = 0.622 to r = 0.876.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study, not live care.
studies.title: Improving the Efficacy of ACR TI-RADS Through Deep Learning-Based Descriptor Augmentation.

studies.design: Vignette comparison of LLMs vs one internist
studies.finding: On clinical vignettes of DIRA and FMF, GPT-4 did not significantly differ from the internist in correctly identifying patients. The physician had significantly higher accuracy than GPT-3.5 and LLaMa 2.
studies.limitation: Single physician comparator and vignette-based design.
studies.title: Accuracy of generative artificial intelligence models in differential diagnoses of familial Mediterranean fever and deficiency of Interleukin-1 receptor antagonist.

studies.design: Retrospective development and comparison of deep learning model vs endodontists on periapical radiographs
studies.finding: On 402 periapical images (138 dens evaginatus, 264 normal), the AI model exhibited superior AUC compared to endodontists in both full and cropped models. Cohen's kappa showed substantial agreement for AI (0.774 full, 0.684 cropped) and fair agreement for specialists.
studies.limitation: Small single dataset with limited data; number of endodontists not stated.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence in diagnosing dens evaginatus on periapical radiography with limited data availability.

studies.design: Model development with two test cohorts and comparison against 12 radiologists
studies.ai_system: ResNet-based deep learning models on multimodal ultrasound
studies.humans: 12 radiologists with different levels of experience
studies.finding: The deep learning models graded rheumatoid arthritis synovitis on ultrasound with results comparable to experienced radiologists on a per-image basis (ICC 0.239-0.756). The dynamic models, especially the DPD model, were more accurate than most senior radiologists.
studies.limitation: Head-to-head figures for the radiologists are not reported in the abstract. Images only.
studies.title: Deep learning-based automatic scoring models for the disease activity of rheumatoid arthritis based on multimodal ultrasound images.

studies.design: Diagnostic comparison of ML system and ophthalmologists
studies.ai_system: Smartphone-based ML system for clinical activity score
studies.humans: Three residents, three general ophthalmologists, three oculoplastic specialists
studies.finding: Detection of active thyroid-associated orbitopathy in 100 patients. The system averaged sensitivity 71.4%, specificity 81.6%, F1 0.66; residents 69.1%, 55.1%, 0.46; general ophthalmologists 61.9%, 79.6%, 0.55; oculoplastic specialists 73.8%, 90.7%, 0.75.
studies.limitation: Small sample; humans read studio images while AI used smartphone images.
studies.title: A Preliminary Evaluation of the Diagnostic Performance of a Smartphone-Based Machine Learning-Assisted System for Evaluation of Clinical Activity Score in Digital Images of Thyroid-Associated Orbitopathy.
studies.source: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association

studies.design: Retrospective study
studies.humans: Two senior and two junior radiologists
studies.finding: BI-RADS classification and malignancy prediction on breast ultrasound in 671 patients. ChatGPT-4 accuracy 96.87% outperformed junior radiologists (91.95% and 90.01%) and was noninferior to seniors; the image-to-text-LLM workflow significantly increased radiologists' sensitivity and specificity (P<.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-centre with only four radiologists.
studies.title: Using a Large Language Model for Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System Classification and Malignancy Prediction to Enhance Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis: Retrospective Study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparative vignette study
studies.humans: ENT physicians, ENT residents, family medicine specialists, second- and third-year medical students
studies.finding: 32 ENT cases with three differential diagnoses each. ChatGPT accuracy was 70.8%, not significantly different from ENT physicians or residents, but higher than FM specialists (49.8%), Med2 (47.5%) and Med3 (47%). ChatGPT failed to mention the most critical diagnosis in 68.75% of cases.
studies.limitation: Only 32 cases; number of human participants not stated in abstract.
studies.title: A cross-sectional comparative study: ChatGPT 3.5 versus diverse levels of medical experts in the diagnosis of ENT diseases.
studies.source: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

studies.design: Reader study of pathologists with and without AI support on 50 WSIs
studies.ai_system: AI pipeline including CaBeSt-Net for tumor cellularity assessment
studies.finding: Pathologists categorised lung adenocarcinoma samples as adequate or inadequate for molecular testing (TC ≤ 20% cut point). Agreement without AI was moderate in tumor areas (κ = 0.410) and slight in WSIs (κ = 0.132); with AI support it was substantial in WSIs (κ = 0.602) and TAs (κ = 0.704).
studies.limitation: Only three pathologists and 50 slides; outcome is inter-observer consistency rather than accuracy.
studies.title: Tumor Cellularity Assessment Using Artificial Intelligence Trained on Immunohistochemistry-Restained Slides Improves Selection of Lung Adenocarcinoma Samples for Molecular Testing.

studies.design: Reader study with and without AI
studies.ai_system: Deep learning segmentation and classification for ERM grading on OCT
studies.finding: Grading epiretinal membrane severity on OCT. Accuracy of the four ophthalmologists increased with AI from 81.7%, 80.7%, 78.0% and 80.7% to 87.7%, 86.7%, 89.0% and 91.3%, with reduced time.
studies.limitation: Only four readers.
studies.title: Clinical evaluation of deep learning systems for assisting in the diagnosis of the epiretinal membrane grade in general ophthalmologists.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to ophthalmologists on 100 samples
studies.ai_system: DenseNet201-based deep learning model on OCT
studies.finding: Predicting nAMD recurrence from OCT images. The model achieved 53.0% accuracy with a single image and 60.2% with all images, versus ophthalmologists' average accuracy of 52.17% and 53.3%.
studies.limitation: Small comparison set (100 samples) and low absolute accuracy for both sides; no statistical test reported.
studies.title: Prediction of neovascular age-related macular degeneration recurrence using optical coherence tomography images with a deep neural network.

studies.design: Model development with comparison against orthopaedic surgeons on test set
studies.ai_system: Deep learning framework with same-domain transfer learning and feature fusion
studies.finding: Detection of shoulder abnormalities on X-ray images. The framework achieved an accuracy of 99.2%, while three orthopaedic surgeons classifying the test set obtained an average accuracy of 79.1%.
studies.limitation: Only three surgeons compared on a retrospective image test set within a model-development study.
studies.title: Trustworthy deep learning framework for the detection of abnormalities in X-ray shoulder images.

studies.design: Multimodal AI development with a before-and-after reader comparison by pathologists
studies.ai_system: Multimodal AI combining CT and histopathology images
studies.humans: General pathologists and expert pulmonary pathologists
studies.finding: The AI achieved an AUC of 0.92 for distinguishing UIP from non-UIP. With the model, general pathologists' diagnostic agreement rose from κ 0.273 to 0.737. Consensus with experts rose from κ 0.278-0.53 to 0.474-0.602.
studies.limitation: Single test set of 114 samples. The number of pathologists is not stated, and the outcome is agreement rather than accuracy against a reference.
studies.title: Enhancing Interstitial Lung Disease Diagnoses Through Multimodal AI Integration of Histopathological and CT Image Data.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre model development with reader study
studies.ai_system: Habitat-based radiomics SVM model on CT
studies.finding: Thymoma risk classification on CT in 133 patients. With the model, junior radiologists' AUCs increased from 0.747 and 0.775 to 0.932 and 0.972, and experienced radiologists' from 0.932 and 0.859 to 0.977 and 0.972. The combined model alone had AUC 0.960.
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective data with small sample and only four readers.
studies.title: Thymoma habitat segmentation and risk prediction model using CT imaging and K-means clustering.

studies.design: Reader study of pathologists diagnosing laryngeal biopsies with and without AI
studies.ai_system: Previously developed AI tool for laryngeal biopsy grading
studies.finding: Eight pathologists reviewed 115 laryngeal biopsy slides with and without AI. Assisted pathologists had higher accuracy for high-grade dysplasia and invasive carcinoma and improved inter-rater reliability, but over-reliance led to omission of invasive carcinomas that had been correctly diagnosed unassisted.
studies.limitation: Only eight pathologists; no numeric results reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Exploring the risks of over-reliance on AI in diagnostic pathology. What lessons can be learned to support the training of young pathologists?

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparative study on 24 histology slides
studies.humans: Five teams of orthopedic surgery residents (PGY-1 to PGY-5)
studies.finding: For diagnosing musculoskeletal tumours from histology slides, mean resident team accuracy was 55%. ChatGPT-4 scored 25% on its first attempt and 33% on its second (p = 0.0004 and p = 0.0028).
studies.limitation: Only 24 slides, residents worked in teams, and the authors describe the results as exploratory.
studies.title: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT-4 in orthopedic oncology: a comparative study with residents.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with reader study
studies.finding: Distinguishing CVST-related hemorrhage from spontaneous ICH on CT. With model assistance, doctors' accuracy 0·79 vs 0·71, sensitivity 0·88 vs 0·81, specificity 0·75 vs 0·68 (p < 0·05).
studies.limitation: Retrospective; authors state prospective validation needed.
studies.title: Explainable deep learning algorithm for identifying cerebral venous sinus thrombosis-related hemorrhage (CVST-ICH) from spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage using computed tomography.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with human-machine competition and assisted reading
studies.ai_system: EC-NBI computer-aided diagnosis deep learning model
studies.finding: For classifying colorectal lesions on endocytoscopy images, the model surpassed endoscopists' diagnostic accuracy in human-machine competitions. Used as an assistive tool, it enhanced endoscopists' performance; the abstract gives no numbers.
studies.limitation: The design is retrospective, and the abstract reports no quantitative results or number of endoscopists.
studies.title: Development of deep learning-based narrow-band imaging endocytoscopic classification for predicting colorectal lesions from a retrospective study.

studies.design: Reader study of matched cases with and without bone removal
studies.ai_system: Deep learning segmentation-based bone removal for head CT
studies.finding: Trainees detected subdural hematoma on non-contrast head CT. Detection was statistically improved using CT with and without bone removal compared to standard CT alone (P value <0.001); 12/14 (86 %) self-reported improved detection.
studies.limitation: Small number of trainee readers only; accuracy figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Deep learning segmentation-based bone removal from computed tomography of the brain improves subdural hematoma detection.
studies.source: Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader comparison
studies.ai_system: CNN for osteopenia/osteoporosis on cervical radiographs
studies.finding: Detection of osteopenia/osteoporosis from cervical radiographs. The algorithm's correct answer rate was significantly higher than nine spine surgeons (80.0% vs. 60.6%; p = 0.032).
studies.limitation: Very small test set of 30 cases.
studies.title: Deep learning algorithm for identifying osteopenia/osteoporosis using cervical radiography.

studies.design: Model development with comparison against radiologists and assisted-reading evaluation
studies.humans: Junior and senior oral and maxillofacial radiologists
studies.finding: Segmentation of mandibular condyle cortex and marrow on CBCT. The model outperformed radiologists across all segmentation metrics (Dice 0.901 cortex, 0.969 marrow), and with model assistance junior radiologists' diagnostic accuracy significantly improved.
studies.limitation: Number of radiologists and size of improvement not reported in abstract; preliminary study.
studies.title: Automatic segmentation and visualization of cortical and marrow bone in mandibular condyle on CBCT: a preliminary exploration of clinical application.

studies.design: Model development with internal and external validation and comparison against radiologists
studies.ai_system: Deep learning neonatal cranial ultrasound screening system
studies.finding: For detecting severe neonatal cerebral lesions on cranial ultrasound videos, the system achieved AUC 0.982 internally and 0.944 externally. It outperformed junior radiologists, performed on par with mid-level radiologists, and was 55.11% faster.
studies.limitation: The abstract gives no radiologist numbers or radiologist metrics.
studies.title: Deep learning approach for screening neonatal cerebral lesions on ultrasound in China.

studies.design: Model development with a small comparison against ophthalmologists
studies.humans: 2 vitreoretinal/uveitis specialists, 1 glaucoma specialist, 1 comprehensive ophthalmologist
studies.finding: For detecting posterior segment inflammation on 20 additional ultra-widefield fundus photographs, the model was correct in 95%. The specialists, glaucoma specialist and comprehensive ophthalmologist achieved accuracies of 85%, 80%, 70% and 65%.
studies.limitation: The comparison used only 20 images and 4 readers.
studies.title: Detecting Inflammation in Fundus Photographs Using Machine Learning.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with independent validation versus pathologists
studies.finding: Diagnosing invasion depth and histologic grade of bladder cancer on whole slide images. The PAIDM achieved an AUC of 0.847 (95% CI 0.779-0.905), non-inferior to the average diagnostic level of pathologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of pathologists and their results not reported in abstract.
studies.title: An artificial intelligence model for the pathological diagnosis of invasion depth and histologic grade in bladder cancer.

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective development/validation with paired reader comparison
studies.finding: For clinically significant prostate cancer diagnosis on MRI, PI-RADS AI outperformed 5/11 (45.5%) and matched 3/11 (27.3%) general radiologists. AUC internal test 0.801 vs. 0.770 (p < 0.01); external test 0.833 vs. 0.867 (p = 0.309).
studies.limitation: Retrospective image-based comparison; AI did not exceed radiologists in external test.
studies.title: PI-RADSAI: introducing a new human-in-the-loop AI model for prostate cancer diagnosis based on MRI.

studies.design: Multi-reader multi-case study, 374 cases from five sites
studies.ai_system: Deep learning CCTA vessel extraction and stenosis detection system
studies.finding: Diagnosing obstructive coronary disease on CCTA against invasive angiography. Reader AUC improved from 0.81 to 0.82 (p < 0.05) at patient level and 0.79 to 0.81 at vessel level with DL, with gains in inexperienced but not experienced radiologists; post-processing and reporting time fell from 798.60 s to 189.12 s. DL alone had sensitivity 93.55% and specificity 59.57% at patient level.
studies.limitation: Small absolute AUC gain; benefit limited to inexperienced readers.
studies.title: Diagnostic performance of deep learning-based vessel extraction and stenosis detection on coronary computed tomography angiography for coronary artery disease: a multi-reader multi-case study.

studies.design: Retrospective development and test-set reader comparison
studies.finding: Detecting cerebral venous thrombosis on routine brain MRI. The DL algorithm achieved AUC 0.96, sensitivity 96% (48/50) and specificity 88% (44/50) per patient, with higher sensitivity than all 4 radiologists per patient (all P<0.05) and per segment (all P<0.001).
studies.limitation: Small enriched test set of 100 patients from a single registry.
studies.title: Deep Learning Algorithm Enables Cerebral Venous Thrombosis Detection With Routine Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging.

studies.design: Controlled reader study with residents split into CADe-assisted and control groups, followed by a post-intervention phase without CADe
studies.ai_system: Computer-aided detection (CADe) system for chest X-ray
studies.finding: Residents detected five abnormalities on chest X-rays. With CADe, group 1 had higher sensitivity (53% vs 43%), specificity (94% vs 90%) and accuracy (86% vs 81%) than controls (all p < 0.001). After CADe was removed, there were no differences in sensitivity (44% vs 46%), specificity (90% vs 90%) or accuracy (80% vs 80%), so no learning effect was seen.
studies.limitation: Only eight residents in a single reader study; group allocation method not described as randomised.
studies.title: Learning from the machine: AI assistance is not an effective learning tool for resident education in chest x-ray interpretation.

studies.design: Retrospective evaluation of saliency maps against radiologist annotations
studies.ai_system: Gradient-based saliency methods on DCNNs trained on MURA
studies.finding: Localizing abnormalities on upper extremity X-rays. Saliency methods had AUPRCs of 0.438 (SG)-0.590 (XRAI) versus average radiologist AUPRC 0.816; repeatability IoUs 0.427-0.551 versus 0.613.
studies.limitation: Radiologists also defined ground truth; public dataset, explanation methods rather than diagnostic AI.
studies.title: Gradient-Based Saliency Maps Are Not Trustworthy Visual Explanations of Automated AI Musculoskeletal Diagnoses.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Retrospective model development with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model with multiview radiographs and prior zonal segmentation
studies.finding: Kellgren-Lawrence grading of knee osteoarthritis on plain radiographs. Overall accuracy of the DL model was 0.96 compared to 0.86 for an experienced radiologist.
studies.limitation: Single radiologist comparator in a retrospective development study.
studies.title: Deep learning-assisted knee osteoarthritis automatic grading on plain radiographs: the value of multiview X-ray images and prior knowledge.
studies.source: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective model development with reader comparison
studies.finding: Detecting lumbar spondylolisthesis on lateral radiographs. Faster R-CNN F1-score 0.935 vs doctor group 0.910; with DL assistance doctors' precision increased by 4.8%, recall by 8.2%, F1 by 6.4%, and diagnosis time per X-ray shortened by 7.139 s.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number and experience of readers not stated.
studies.title: Deep learning system assisted detection and localization of lumbar spondylolisthesis.

studies.design: Retrospective radiomics model development with reader comparison and assisted reading
studies.finding: The task was differentiating ovarian endometrioma from dermoid cyst on ultrasound. The radiomic model was comparable to senior radiologists and superior to junior radiologists. Junior radiologists' diagnostic performance significantly improved with the model's assistance.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; reader numbers and reader performance figures are not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Ultrasound radiomics-based artificial intelligence model to assist in the differential diagnosis of ovarian endometrioma and ovarian dermoid cyst.

studies.design: Retrospective single-center model development with reader comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep learning CNN for MPI SPECT
studies.finding: Diagnosing coronary artery disease from MPI SPECT. The AI achieved 88% performance, cardiologists with AI 80% and cardiologists alone 65%; diagnosis time was 12 min with AI vs 31 min alone.
studies.limitation: Single-center data; number of cardiologists not stated.
studies.title: A deep learning-based automated diagnosis system for SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging.

studies.design: Cross-sectional pilot with blinded rating of physician vs chatbot answers to 10 clinical questions
studies.finding: Answers to ten gynecologic oncology knowledge and management questions were rated blind. Physician responses were judged best in 76.7% of evaluations vs ChatGPT 10.0% and Bard 13.3%; mean quality 4.2/5.0 vs 3.0/5.0 and 2.8/5.0; accuracy 86.7% vs 60% and 43%.
studies.limitation: Small pilot with only ten questions and five physicians.
studies.title: The doc versus the bot: A pilot study to assess the quality and accuracy of physician and chatbot responses to clinical questions in gynecologic oncology.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of a commercial AI system with radiologists
studies.ai_system: Commercial AI system for BI-RADS categorisation on breast ultrasound
studies.finding: The task was BI-RADS assessment of 715 breast masses on ultrasound. Sensitivity and specificity were 98.51% and 80.72% for radiologist 1, 97.76% and 75.56% for radiologist 2, and 98.51% and 65.40% for AI. Accuracy was 84.06%, 79.72% and 71.61% respectively.
studies.limitation: Retrospective review of images acquired by the performing radiologist, within a single institution.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence in BI-RADS Categorization of Breast Lesions on Ultrasound: Can We Omit Excessive Follow-ups and Biopsies?

studies.design: Model development with comparison against ophthalmologists on 439 additional UBM images
studies.ai_system: Deep learning UBM anterior chamber angle model (UNet++, SVM, LR)
studies.finding: Classification of angle closure, iris curvature and iris root insertion on ultrasound biomicroscopy images. Compared with ophthalmologists, the model achieved an accuracy of 0.765, as high as that of the ophthalmologists (p > 0.05).
studies.limitation: Number of ophthalmologists and their accuracy not reported; single-disease image set.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Based Model for Automatic Assessment of Anterior Angle Chamber in Ultrasound Biomicroscopy.

studies.design: Retrospective model validation with reader study with and without AI
studies.humans: 4 readers including trainees and an attending spine surgeon
studies.finding: Measuring thoracolumbar fracture metrics on lateral radiographs. DL agreement with ground truth was ICC 0.860, 0.944, 0.932 and 0.779 internally, and DL-assisted measurements significantly improved most measurement values, particularly for trainees.
studies.limitation: Only four readers; reader improvement figures not quantified in abstract.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Quantitative Measurement of Thoracolumbar Fracture Features on Lateral Radiographs.

studies.design: Retrospective two-center radiomics study compared with radiologist visual assessment
studies.finding: The task was distinguishing orbital solitary fibrous tumor from schwannoma on MRI. The nomogram outperformed pooled readers in training (AUC 0.986 vs. 0.807) and validation (AUC 0.989 vs. 0.788). In external testing the AUCs were 0.903 vs. 0.792 (p = 0.093), not significant.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with a small sample; the difference was not significant in the external test cohort.
studies.title: MRI-based radiomics nomogram for distinguishing solitary fibrous tumor from schwannoma in the orbit: a two-center study.

studies.design: Comparison of chatbots and a specialist on ophthalmic case scenarios
studies.finding: Diagnosis and management of 11 challenging ophthalmic case scenarios presented stepwise. All three chatbots' individual diagnostic performance was inferior to the ophthalmic specialist, though they gave useful complementary input. ChatGPT's consistency had mean Jaccard similarity 0.58 to 0.76.
studies.limitation: Only 11 cases and a single specialist; qualitative evaluation.
studies.title: Artificial Versus Human Intelligence in the Diagnostic Approach of Ophthalmic Case Scenarios: A Qualitative Evaluation of Performance and Consistency.

studies.design: Comparison of AI and radiologist kidney stone volume measurement on CT-KUB
studies.finding: Measuring kidney stone volume on CT-KUB images. The abstract reports AI had greater accuracy, efficiency and consistency than radiologists, with an average difference of 80% compared with radiologist-calculated volumes.
studies.limitation: Sample size, reference standard and reader numbers not reported; the claim of superiority is weakly supported in the abstract.
studies.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of AI-powered UrologiQ's in accurately measuring kidney stone volume in urolithiasis patients.

studies.design: Cross-sectional three-phase comparison
studies.ai_system: Six LLMs incl. ChatGPT o1-preview, ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet
studies.humans: Five radiologists (two residents, two junior, one senior)
studies.finding: Detecting and correcting MRI artifacts. LLMs outperformed radiologists on text-based questions (ChatGPT o1-preview 3.71±0.60), but on 100 images the senior radiologist achieved 92% and 94% accuracy versus 20% and 18% for the top LLM (ChatGPT-4o).
studies.limitation: Small number of radiologists and questions; single-center cross-sectional design.
studies.title: Textual Proficiency and Visual Deficiency: A Comparative Study of Large Language Models and Radiologists in MRI Artifact Detection and Correction.

studies.design: Retrospective radiomic model development with reader evaluation of lesion-importance guidance
studies.finding: Differentiating NTM-LD from MTB-LD on lung CT. The MLR model achieved an AUC of 90.2%; given the estimated lesion importance, two senior radiologists improved diagnostic accuracy by 8.33% and 8.34%.
studies.limitation: Only two readers, small single test set (72 patients), retrospective design.
studies.title: Lung CT-based multi-lesion radiomic model to differentiate between nontuberculous mycobacteria and Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

studies.design: Blinded rating of ChatGPT versus surgeon answers to patient questions
studies.finding: Answering 10 common TKA patient questions, rated by the same five surgeons. ChatGPT scored higher than combined attendings for empathy (4.4 vs. 3.5), accuracy (4.4 vs. 3.7), completeness (4.4 vs. 3.5) and overall quality (4.4 vs. 3.6) (P < 0.001), though not different from two individual attendings.
studies.limitation: Only 10 questions; raters were the same surgeons who wrote the comparison answers.
studies.title: ChatGPT versus expert arthroplasty surgeons in total knee arthroplasty patient counseling.

studies.design: Reader study on standard and ultra-low dose CT
studies.ai_system: DLADRF deep learning rib fracture detection
studies.finding: Detection of recent rib fractures on SD-CT and ULD-CT in 158 forensic patients. AUC for senior radiologist + DLADRF was significantly better than senior and junior radiologists, junior + DLADRF, and DLADRF alone (all P < 0.05); senior radiologists did not differ from DLADRF on ULD-CT.
studies.limitation: Forensic population and number of readers not stated.
studies.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Ultra-Low Dose CT Compared to Standard Dose CT for Identification of Fresh Rib Fractures by Deep Learning Algorithm.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with reader study with and without model assistance
studies.ai_system: MRI-based deep learning combined model (T1WI, T2WI, CE-T1WI with attention fusion)
studies.finding: Differentiating sinonasal inverted papilloma from SIP-transformed squamous cell carcinoma on MRI in 568 patients. The combined model achieved AUCs of 0.954, 0.897 and 0.859 in training, internal and external validation cohorts. Radiologists' diagnostic performance, especially for less experienced ones, was significantly improved with model assistance.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; reader numbers and assisted performance figures not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Preoperative prediction of malignant transformation in sinonasal inverted papilloma: a novel MRI-based deep learning approach.

studies.design: Model development with multicenter validation and a reader comparison
studies.humans: Ultrasonographers and cardiologists with different working years from three hospitals
studies.finding: Identifying heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF < 40%) from static cardiac ultrasound views. AI classification accuracy was comparable with the best performance of clinicians with more than 3 working years (P = 0.344) but significantly better than the median clinician level (P = 0.0000008).
studies.limitation: Retrospective image-based comparison; clinician accuracy figures are not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: A generalized deep learning model for heart failure diagnosis using dynamic and static ultrasound.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter reader study with and without AI assistance
studies.finding: For diagnosing lung cancer on respiratory cytology image patches, the model had sensitivity, specificity and accuracy of 95.9%, 98.2% and 96.9%, outperforming the average of three pathologists. Pathologist accuracy improved from 82.9% to 95.9% with AI, and Fleiss' kappa rose from 0.553 to 0.908.
studies.limitation: Only three readers, evaluated on image patches.
studies.title: Deep learning-based diagnosis of lung cancer using a nationwide respiratory cytology image set: improving accuracy and inter-observer variability.

studies.design: Reader study on external endoscopic image test set, fellows with optional AI consultation
studies.ai_system: ResNet18 deep learning model for villous atrophy
studies.finding: For detecting villous atrophy on endoscopic still images, AI had sensitivity, specificity and accuracy of 90%, 76% and 84%, fellows 63%, 72% and 67%, and experts 72%, 69% and 71%. AI consultation significantly improved all trainee performance statistics.
studies.limitation: Still images only and a small number of readers.
studies.title: Detection of duodenal villous atrophy on endoscopic images using a deep learning algorithm.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective and prospective model development with radiologist-assisted reading
studies.ai_system: DLAPS deep learning CT pipeline for lateral lymph nodes
studies.finding: DLAPS achieved AUCs of 0.872, 0.910 and 0.822 in the internal, external and prospective test sets for detecting lateral lymph node metastasis. DLAPS assistance improved radiologist performance and inter-observer consistency, and unnecessary dissection decreased from 33.33% to 7.32%.
studies.limitation: The radiologist comparison has no numbers in the abstract, and the number of readers is not stated.
studies.title: Deep learning-based automatic pipeline system for predicting lateral cervical lymph node metastasis in patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma using computed tomography: A multi-center study.
studies.source: Chinese journal of cancer research = Chung-kuo yen cheng yen chiu

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter study with reader assistance
studies.finding: For lymph node staging on rectal cancer MRI, the model had an AUC of 0.81, outperforming junior radiologists (AUC = 0.69) and comparable to senior radiologists (AUC = 0.79). With model assistance, AUCs rose to 0.80 for junior and 0.88 for senior radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design, and the number of readers is not stated.
studies.title: Multicenter Evaluation of a Weakly Supervised Deep Learning Model for Lymph Node Diagnosis in Rectal Cancer at MRI.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to ophthalmologists
studies.finding: Ophthalmic disease diagnosis from fundus images. VisionUnite demonstrated diagnostic capabilities comparable to junior ophthalmologists; no numbers reported in abstract.
studies.limitation: No quantitative results or reader numbers in abstract; developer-led evaluation.
studies.title: VisionUnite: A Vision-Language Foundation Model for Ophthalmology Enhanced With Clinical Knowledge.
studies.source: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence

studies.design: Reader study with four AI-output conditions
studies.humans: 2 consultant fetal cardiologists, 3 pediatric cardiology trainees, 5 fetal cardiac sonographers
studies.finding: Classifying fetal four-chamber ultrasound images as normal or AVSD. AI alone had accuracy 0.798 versus 0.844 for clinicians without AI, and binary AI output improved clinician accuracy to 0.865 (P < 0.001). Incorrect AI advice reduced accuracy from 0.761 to 0.693, worsened by showing confidence (0.649) or grad-CAM (0.644).
studies.limitation: Single-center study with 10 readers using still images rather than live scanning.
studies.title: Interaction between clinicians and artificial intelligence to detect fetal atrioventricular septal defects on ultrasound: how can we optimize collaborative performance?
studies.source: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology

studies.design: Comparative study of manual vs AI-assisted scoring by pathologists
studies.finding: Three pathologists scored PD-L1 on 50 early-stage NSCLC samples manually and with two AI tools. AI-assisted scoring identified significantly more cases with ≥1% tumour proportion score than manual scoring (p=0.00015), and turnaround time differed significantly (p value <0.0001 for all comparisons).
studies.limitation: Small preliminary study of 50 samples and three pathologists without a reference standard for accuracy.
studies.title: Assessment of PD-L1 expression and tumour infiltrating lymphocytes in early-stage non-small cell lung carcinoma with artificial intelligence algorithms.

studies.design: Cross-sectional expert rating of answers
studies.finding: On 7 questions about vaccine and statin hesitancy, expert-rated mean scores were 3.78±0.36 for ChatGPT and 3.65±0.57 for physicians (p=0.33). There was no significant difference for vaccine or statin questions separately.
studies.limitation: Only 7 questions, and the number of physicians is not stated.
studies.title: Is ChatGPT an Accurate and Reliable Source of Information for Patients with Vaccine and Statin Hesitancy?

studies.design: Retrospective model development with two reader tests, with and without AI assistance
studies.ai_system: BikNet (Bilateral Knee Neural Network) deep learning model
studies.finding: Clinicians predicted incident knee osteoarthritis on bilateral knee radiographs from the Osteoarthritis Initiative, with and without BikNet assistance. With assistance, clinicians' sensitivity rose from 28.1-63.2% to 42.1-68.4% and specificity from 57.4-83.4% to 64.1-87.5%, with improved inter-observer reliability. BikNet alone achieved AUC values of 0.761 and 0.745 in testing sets 1 and 2.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader test on a research cohort dataset; the number of readers is not stated in the abstract.
studies.title: Expanding from unilateral to bilateral: A robust deep learning-based approach for predicting radiographic osteoarthritis progression.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study on TOF-MRA, AI vs radiologists and radiologists with vs without AI
studies.humans: Six radiologists (two residents, two attendings, two professors)
studies.finding: For intracranial aneurysm detection in 510 patients, the AI platform achieved AUC 0.96 with SE 91.63% and ACC 91.96%, outperforming the two resident radiologists. With AI assistance, mean SE improved (residents 71.40% vs 88.37%; attendings 82.79% vs 93.26%; professors 90.07% vs 97.44%) and ACC improved (residents 85.29% vs 94.12%; attendings 91.76% vs 97.06%; professors 95.29% vs 98.82%), with no significant change in SP.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only six readers; AI reportedly outperformed only the residents.
studies.title: Deep learning-based platform performs high detection sensitivity of intracranial aneurysms in 3D brain TOF-MRA: An external clinical validation study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter diagnostic study with external test set and reader study
studies.ai_system: Interactive explainable deep learning model on gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI
studies.finding: Classifying LR-5/HCC focal liver lesions on gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI. With AI assistance, sensitivities were higher than without (reader 1, 85.7% vs 72.3%; reader 2, 89.1% vs 74.0%; P < .001), with the same specificities. The AI model alone showed higher sensitivity than LI-RADS category 5 (91.6% vs 74.8%; P < .001) and similar specificity (90.7% vs 96.0%; P = .22).
studies.limitation: Only two readers in a retrospective design.
studies.title: Interactive Explainable Deep Learning Model for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Diagnosis at Gadoxetic Acid-enhanced MRI: A Retrospective, Multicenter, Diagnostic Study.

studies.design: Retrospective development and test of a deep learning model compared with dental residents
studies.finding: Distinguishing nasopalatine duct cysts, radicular cysts and normal anterior maxilla on panoramic radiographs. The deep learning system outperformed the dental residents except for recall of radicular cysts, with significantly higher AUCs for NDCs and radicular cysts.
studies.limitation: Very small comparator group (two residents) and a small single test set.
studies.title: Deep learning system for distinguishing between nasopalatine duct cysts and radicular cysts arising in the midline region of the anterior maxilla on panoramic radiographs.

studies.design: Descriptive laboratory study; AI development plus an assisted-reader analysis
studies.ai_system: Video-based 3D pose reconstruction with an LSTM classifier
studies.finding: Orthopaedic surgeons identified ACL injuries from in-game match video with and without the system's reconstructed 3D poses and derived signals. With system data, their combined F1 score increased by 0.08. The best model alone had an F1 score of 0.63 ± 0.01 and an AUC of 0.88 ± 0.01.
studies.limitation: Only 2 readers and a small set of online video scenes (91 injuries, 38 controls).
studies.title: Identifying Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injuries Through Automated Video Analysis of In-Game Motion Patterns.

studies.design: Retrospective radiomics model development with comparison against physicians on 282 lung ultrasound images
studies.finding: For differentiating NRDS from other neonatal lung disease, the RF model had an AUC of 0.99 vs 0.98 for experienced and 0.85 for junior physicians. The difference from experienced physicians was not significant (P = 0.24) but was significant versus junior physicians (P < 0.0001).
studies.limitation: Small single-center dataset; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Exploring the diagnostic value of ultrasound radiomics for neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to an ophthalmologist
studies.ai_system: Weakly supervised deep learning model on ultra-widefield fundus images
studies.finding: For localizing retinal detachment, the model reached 86.42% precision and 83.27% recall, versus 89.16% precision and 83.38% recall for the ophthalmologist. Four-zone kappa was 0.710 for the model versus 0.753 for the ophthalmologist.
studies.limitation: Comparison against a single ophthalmologist.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted management of retinal detachment from ultra-widefield fundus images based on weakly-supervised approach.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader assistance and training experiments
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model (Faster R-CNN + DenseNet-121) for femoral neck fracture detection and Garden classification
studies.finding: For femoral neck fracture detection on plain radiographs, emergency physicians had average accuracy of 86.33 % unaided and 92.03 % aided, sensitivity 85.94 % vs 91.78 %, specificity 87.88 % vs 93.13 %. The model alone had 94.1 % detection accuracy. Trainees' classification accuracy rose from 81.83 % before to 90.65 % after training with the model.
studies.limitation: Single-hospital retrospective dataset; number of readers not stated in abstract.
studies.title: A deep learning algorithm that aids visualization of femoral neck fractures and improves physician training.

studies.design: Cross-sectional blinded comparison of responses to Reddit questions
studies.finding: For 50 cerebrovascular questions, ChatGPT responses were rated more complete (median 3 (2-3) vs. 2 (1-3)) and more empathetic (4 (3-5) vs. 2 (1-3)) than physician responses (p < 0.001). Accuracy did not differ (4 (3-4) vs. 4 (3-4), p = 0.752), while physician responses were more readable (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Pilot study using physician answers from social media rather than clinical encounters.
studies.title: Comparison of quality, empathy and readability of physician responses versus chatbot responses to common cerebrovascular neurosurgical questions on a social media platform.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison against clinicians
studies.finding: Quantifying the pancreatic necrosis volume ratio (MCTSI) on CT in acute pancreatitis. The model had accuracy 0.854, macro recall 0.850 and macro specificity 0.923, all significantly higher than senior and junior clinicians (P<0.05).
