studies.limitation: Small retrospective dataset; the number of clinicians and their values are not reported.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence models assisting physicians in quantifying pancreatic necrosis in acute pancreatitis.
studies.source: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

studies.design: Cross-sectional vignette comparison
studies.finding: Across five bariatric surgery scenarios, management recommendations were compared with ASMBS guidelines. ChatGPT aligned with guidelines 60% of the time, whereas bariatric surgeons aligned 100% of the time.
studies.limitation: Only five clinical scenarios; number of surgeons not stated.
studies.title: Evaluating the concordance of ChatGPT and physician recommendations for bariatric surgery.
studies.source: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison against ophthalmologists
studies.finding: Classifying 16 fundus conditions on ultra-widefield images. The model's AUCs exceeded 0.975 for common diseases and 0.970 for rare ones, and it achieved significantly higher accuracy than ophthalmologists across all diagnostic tasks.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; the number of ophthalmologists and their accuracy are not reported.
studies.title: Deep learning-based classification of multiple fundus diseases using ultra-widefield images.
studies.source: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

studies.design: Cross-sectional vignette questionnaire with blinded ratings
studies.humans: 7 board-certified spine surgeons; rated by 3 emergency medicine physicians
studies.finding: ChatGPT and spine surgeons answered 7 common emergency department spine consultation vignettes covering examination, diagnosis, management and counseling. AI responses were rated superior across all 5 metrics: clinical accuracy, management appropriateness, completeness, helpfulness and overall quality (p<.05). Inter-rater agreement was substantial (κ=0.76).
studies.limitation: Small number of simulated vignettes, with responses restricted to 3-4 sentences.
studies.title: Performance of ChatGPT versus spine surgeons as an emergency department spine call consultant.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective observer-performance study
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-5 and ChatGPT-5 Thinking (text-only and multimodal)
studies.humans: 2 expert veterinary ophthalmologists and 2 novice veterinary clinicians
studies.finding: In 50 feline fundus cases, multimodal LLMs had Top-1 accuracy of 34% to 46% and Top-3 accuracy of 74-86%. They performed significantly better than novice readers (p < 0.05), with no significant difference from experts. LLM response times were 13.7-84.6 s versus 117-132 s for humans.
studies.limitation: Veterinary setting with only 4 clinicians and 50 cases.
studies.title: Reading systemic disease from the feline fundus: A multicenter comparison of multimodal large language models and veterinary clinicians.

studies.design: Cross-sectional blinded comparison of responses to 30 IBD patient questions
studies.finding: GPT-4o and gastroenterologists answered 30 IBD questions, rated by blinded gastroenterologists and patients. Accuracy and readability were comparable; ChatGPT was rated more complete (4.42 ± 0.67 vs 4.19 ± 0.65). Patients rated gastroenterologists higher for treatment questions (4.54 ± 0.32 vs 4.21 ± 0.38).
studies.limitation: Small question set and only three responding gastroenterologists; no real clinical setting.
studies.title: Revolutionizing inflammatory bowel disease healthcare communication: a head-to-head comparison of gastroenterologist and ChatGPT responses.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with reader study with and without model assistance
studies.ai_system: Ensemble deep learning/radiomics/clinical model on T2W MRI
studies.finding: Readers predicted peritoneal metastasis in epithelial ovarian cancer with and without model assistance. All readers had significantly improved sensitivity with assistance (junior radiologist1 0.639 to 0.820; junior radiologist2 0.689 to 0.803; resident1 0.623 to 0.803; resident2 0.541 to 0.738), and one resident improved specificity from 0.633 to 0.789.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with a small number of readers.
studies.title: Associating Peritoneal Metastasis With T2-Weighted MRI Images in Epithelial Ovarian Cancer Using Deep Learning and Radiomics: A Multicenter Study.
studies.source: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

studies.design: Fully balanced multireader multicase reader study
studies.ai_system: Custom categorical AI system for DBT
studies.finding: Interpretation of 240 screening DBT exams with versus without AI. Average AUC was 0.93 with AI versus 0.87 without (difference 0.06, 95% CI: 0.04, 0.08; P < .001), with improvement for general radiologists (0.08) and breast specialists (0.04).
studies.limitation: Retrospective enriched reader study, not live screening.
studies.title: Impact of a Categorical AI System for Digital Breast Tomosynthesis on Breast Cancer Interpretation by Both General Radiologists and Breast Imaging Specialists.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to endoscopists on endoscopic images
studies.ai_system: DenseNet-121 deep learning model with explainable AI
studies.finding: Five-category Los Angeles grading of GERD on endoscopic images; the model's classification accuracy (86.7%) was significantly higher than junior (71.5%) and experienced (77.4%) endoscopists. Model AUC was 0.968.
studies.limitation: Image-based reader comparison; number of endoscopists and test set details not stated.
studies.title: Using deep learning and explainable artificial intelligence to assess the severity of gastroesophageal reflux disease according to the Los Angeles Classification System.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with external test set compared to radiologists
studies.ai_system: Vision Transformer deep learning model on MRI
studies.humans: Three senior and three junior radiologists using VI-RADS
studies.finding: Diagnosis of muscle-invasive bladder cancer on MRI; the model with manual ROI achieved AUC of 0.872 (95% CI: 0.777, 0.968), comparable to junior radiologists (AUC = 0.862, 0.873, and 0.930). With auto-generated ROI the AUC was 0.815.
studies.limitation: Retrospective with small test set of 53 patients; senior radiologist results not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Development of deep learning model for diagnosing muscle-invasive bladder cancer on MRI with vision transformer.

studies.design: Retrospective two-institution development study with external test comparison against radiologists
studies.ai_system: Multi-task deep learning model (nnU-Net segmentation) on mpMRI
studies.finding: For identifying lymph node metastasis in endometrial cancer on mpMRI, the model achieved an AUC of 0.804 for LNM in the external test cohort. This was better than three radiologists (AUC = 0.770/0.648/0.674).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with a small external test cohort of 54 patients.
studies.title: Fully Automated Identification of Lymph Node Metastases and Lymphovascular Invasion in Endometrial Cancer From Multi-Parametric MRI by Deep Learning.
studies.source: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader agreement substudy on 60 test cases
studies.ai_system: 3D DenseNet121 T2W prostate MRI quality classifier
studies.finding: For T2W prostate MRI quality scoring, AI showed substantial agreement with expert ground truth (κ = 0.704). The three radiologists showed agreement with ground truth of κ = 0.588, κ = 0.649 and κ = 0.487.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, ground truth from a single expert reader, reader comparison on only 60 cases.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Based Interpretable AI for Prostate T2W MRI Quality Evaluation.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with physician comparison
studies.humans: Junior and senior nuclear medicine physicians
studies.finding: For classifying thyroid SPECT images into four disease types, the ResNet-34 model showed higher accuracy than the senior nuclear medicine physician on internal validation (p < 0.001). On the external dataset, model accuracy was 0.931 versus 0.868 for the senior physician (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with few physician comparators.
studies.title: Diagnosis of thyroid disease using deep convolutional neural network models applied to thyroid scintigraphy images: a multicenter study.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with external validation and comparison against human readers
studies.ai_system: Multiparametric deep learning grading model (U-net and ResNet)
studies.finding: For meningioma grading on external validation, the DL model achieved AUC 0.770 and accuracy 72.1%. Human readers had AUCs of 0.675-0.690 and accuracies of 65.6-68.9%.
studies.limitation: Small external set of 61 patients; number of readers and significance testing not reported.
studies.title: Intelligent noninvasive meningioma grading with a fully automatic segmentation using interpretable multiparametric deep learning.

studies.design: Model development with test set compared against endoscopists and external validation
studies.ai_system: AI model on white-light endoscopic images and videos
studies.finding: For predicting pathologic features of early gastric cancer, the model showed significantly higher accuracy than experts for undifferentiated histology (92.7% vs. 71.6%), submucosal invasion (87.3% vs. 72.6%) and LNM (87.7% vs. 72.3%). Model AUCs were lower for LVI (0.706) and LNM (0.680).
studies.limitation: Small test set (260 images, 10 videos); external accuracy dropped to 75.6% and 71.9%.
studies.title: An artificial intelligence system for comprehensive pathologic outcome prediction in early gastric cancer through endoscopic image analysis (with video).
studies.source: Gastric cancer : official journal of the International Gastric Cancer Association and the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association

studies.design: Retrospective agreement study
studies.finding: Measurement of LV volumes and LVEF on echocardiograms of 109 patients; AI correlated strongly with the average of human operators (r = 0.89 for LVEDV and r = 0.92 for LVESV), higher than between operators (r = 0.74 and r = 0.84). AI showed comparable performance to human operators for LVEF, with only moderate correlation for GLS.
studies.limitation: Retrospective agreement study with only two readers and no reference standard.
studies.title: Concordance of left ventricular volumes and function measurements between two human readers, a fully automated AI algorithm, and the 3D heart model.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with independent test cohort compared to surgeons
studies.ai_system: Video-Trans-U-HRNet for parathyroid gland segmentation in intraoperative video
studies.finding: Identification of parathyroid glands in thyroid surgery videos; the model achieved 89.5% precision, 77.3% recall and 70.8% accuracy on the external test. It was comparable to senior surgeons (p = 0.320, p = 0.241) and outperformed both junior surgeons (p = 0.048, p = 0.029).
studies.limitation: Small retrospective sample (15 test videos) and only four surgeons.
studies.title: A novel deep learning method to segment parathyroid glands on intraoperative videos of thyroid surgery.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of AI software with initial radiologist reads against consensus
studies.ai_system: Automatic CMB detection software on SWI
studies.finding: Detection of cerebral microbleeds on SWI in 265 patients. Per-lesion sensitivity was 75.5% for radiologists versus 96.5% for the software (P<0.001), while precision was 92.2% versus 86.0% (P<0.001). Patient-level sensitivity and specificity did not differ significantly.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; reference consensus made by the same radiologists after reviewing AI output.
studies.title: Automatic detection of cerebral microbleeds using susceptibility weighted imaging and artificial intelligence.
studies.source: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

studies.design: Comparison on 100 fictitious thyroid ultrasound reports
studies.humans: Expert team and an inexperienced ultrasound user (medical student)
studies.finding: Applying ACR-TI-RADS 2017 to 100 fictitious thyroid ultrasound reports. ChatGPT agreement with experts ranged from moderate to almost perfect, while the inexperienced user achieved nearly perfect agreement and outperformed ChatGPT.
studies.limitation: Fictitious reports and a single inexperienced human comparator.
studies.title: Comparing ChatGPT 4.0's Performance in Interpreting Thyroid Nodule Ultrasound Reports Using ACR-TI-RADS 2017: Analysis Across Different Levels of Ultrasound User Experience.

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison of 12 CAD products vs 11 radiologists on 774 chest X-rays against microbiological reference
studies.ai_system: 12 CAD software products for TB detection
studies.humans: Radiologists from Nigeria, India, the UK and the US
studies.finding: On 774 chest X-rays for TB detection, radiologist sensitivity ranged from 67.1% (India) to 78.7% (UK) and specificity from 75.8% (Nigeria) to 84.3% (US). The top CAD outperformed all except Indian radiologists when matching specificity, and CE-marked CAD generally matched or surpassed radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective images from a single survey dataset with only 11 radiologists.
studies.title: Comparing the accuracy of computer-aided detection (CAD) software and radiologists from multiple countries for tuberculosis detection in chest X-Rays.

studies.design: Retrospective pilot radiomics study compared with radiologists' assessment
studies.finding: For differentiating leiomyosarcoma from leiomyoma on CECT, the GLM and RF models achieved AUCs ranging from 0.78 to 0.97. Radiologists achieved AUC = 0.73 when blinded to clinical data and AUC = 0.75 with clinical data.
studies.limitation: Small pilot sample (65 patients) without stated external validation.
studies.title: Machine Learning Applied to Pre-Operative Computed-Tomography-Based Radiomic Features Can Accurately Differentiate Uterine Leiomyoma from Leiomyosarcoma: A Pilot Study.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study with and without AI assistance
studies.finding: Detection of nasal bone fractures on 3D CT reconstructions from 82 patients. AI-assisted reading improved accuracy, sensitivity and specificity for junior and senior physicians compared with manual independent review (P <0.05).
studies.limitation: Small retrospective dataset; reader numbers and effect sizes not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Study on the application of deep learning artificial intelligence techniques in the diagnosis of nasal bone fracture.
studies.source: International journal of burns and trauma

studies.design: Model development with comparison against pathologists
studies.finding: For membranous nephropathy pathology, the model achieved 98.97% accuracy for immunofluorescence classification and a Dice of 85.66% for deposit segmentation. It outperformed pathologists in fluorescence image classification and deposit segmentation; pathologists' figures are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Pathologist comparison figures and number not reported.
studies.title: Multimodal deep learning improving the accuracy of pathological diagnoses for membranous nephropathy.

studies.design: Bicentral retrospective model development study with radiologist comparison and assisted reading
studies.ai_system: FADLM (Mask R-CNN segmentation + ResNet34) on ultrasound video keyframes
studies.finding: Prediction of cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma from ultrasound; FADLM AUCs were 0.78, 0.83 and 0.83 across training, internal and external cohorts and the authors report superior performance to radiologists. With FADLM assistance, accuracies of junior and senior radiologists improved by 18% and 15% and sensitivities by 25% and 21% in the external test cohort.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only two radiologists and a small external test cohort (n = 95).
studies.title: Automatic tumor segmentation and lymph node metastasis prediction in papillary thyroid carcinoma using ultrasound keyframes.

studies.design: Cross-sectional reader study of PGMI quality assessment on 520 screening mammograms
studies.humans: Five radiographers from three European countries
studies.finding: Human readers showed poor to moderate agreement on PGMI assessment (κ = -0.018 to κ = 0.41). The software surpassed human inter-reader agreement for glandular tissue cuts, mammilla deviation, pectoral muscle detection and pectoral angle measurement, and was comparable for remaining features and overall quality.
studies.limitation: Readers were radiographers rather than physicians and there was no definitive reference standard.
studies.title: PGMI assessment in mammography: AI software versus human readers.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of AI with two oral radiologists on 1000 periapical radiographs
studies.ai_system: AI system for dental feature detection
studies.finding: Detection of teeth, caries, implants, restorations and prostheses on periapical radiographs. Correlation between AI and the observers was 0.7-0.73 for carious teeth, 0.97-0.98 for implants, 0.85-0.89 for restored teeth, 0.92-0.94 for fixed prosthesis and 0.82-0.85 for missing teeth. The AI was judged comparable to the radiologists.
studies.limitation: Agreement with only two radiologists used as reference; correlation rather than accuracy against ground truth.
studies.title: Clinical Validation of Deep Learning for Segmentation of Multiple Dental Features in Periapical Radiographs.

studies.design: Retrospective radiomics model development compared with junior radiologists
studies.finding: Malignancy prediction in 197 cytologically indeterminate thyroid nodules on ultrasound. The Radunion model achieved 90.5% sensitivity, 56.8% specificity and 76.6% accuracy and outperformed ITS 100, ThyNet and junior radiologists; radiologist figures not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Small single retrospective dataset, only two junior radiologists, and no radiologist numbers reported.
studies.title: Ultrasound radiomics models improve preoperative diagnosis and reduce unnecessary biopsies in indeterminate thyroid nodules.

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison on preoperative spine radiographs
studies.ai_system: Commercial deep learning Cobb angle software
studies.finding: Cobb angle measurement on 151 preoperative radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. AI MAE was 4.57° [95%CI 3.85°, 5.29°], significantly higher than residents' (P=0.0017). For extreme scoliosis AI MAE was 6.53° versus 3.61° for residents (P<0.001), with no significant difference for moderate and severe curves.
studies.limitation: Single retrospective surgical dataset compared only against residents.
studies.title: Performance of a deep learning-based algorithm for automated measurements of Cobb angles on preoperative spine radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.

studies.design: Reader comparison on 25 multimodal musculoskeletal tumor cases
studies.finding: On 25 multimodal imaging cases of musculoskeletal masses, human raters were more accurate than ChatGPT-4.0 for the primary diagnosis (87% vs. 44%). When secondary diagnoses were also considered, accuracy was 94% vs. 71%.
studies.limitation: Only 25 constructed cases; number and expertise of human raters not stated.
studies.title: Evaluating the Diagnostic Accuracy of ChatGPT-4.0 for Classifying Multimodal Musculoskeletal Masses: A Comparative Study with Human Raters.
studies.source: RoFo : Fortschritte auf dem Gebiete der Rontgenstrahlen und der Nuklearmedizin

studies.design: Cross-sectional case comparison
studies.finding: Three LLMs and board-certified dermatologists diagnosed 30 dermatology cases. The abstract reports no significant difference in accuracy rates between the AI models and the dermatologists, with the AI models sometimes exceeding the specialists in rare cases.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 30 cases with potential selection bias; the number of dermatologists and exact accuracy figures are not reported.
studies.title: Evaluation of the Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Models in Dermatological Diagnosis and Comparison With Dermatology Specialists.

studies.design: Experimental reader comparison on quiz cases
studies.finding: Multimodal LLMs and two neuroradiologists answered 401 neuroradiology quizzes derived from RadioGraphics. Top-3 accuracy of the LLMs ranged from 29.9% to 49.4%, versus 80.3% and 68.3% for the two radiologists (P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Quiz cases drawn from published articles, with only two radiologist readers.
studies.title: Evaluating the Accuracy and Diagnostic Reasoning of Multimodal Large Language Models in Interpreting Neuroradiology Cases From RadioGraphics.

studies.design: Comparative agreement study
studies.ai_system: Deep CNN for intestinal metaplasia quantification
studies.finding: A deep learning model's intestinal metaplasia estimates on gastric biopsies were compared with blinded visual estimates by three pathologists. Inter-pathologist agreement (Fleiss' Kappa) ranged from 0.20 to 0.48, while agreement between the pathologists and the best model ranged from 0.12 to 0.35.
studies.limitation: No ground-truth accuracy comparison against the pathologists is reported, only agreement, and only three pathologists took part.
studies.title: Towards deep-learning based detection and quantification of intestinal metaplasia on digitized gastric biopsies: a multi-expert comparative study.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to doctors
studies.ai_system: Deep learning CT classification model for chronic sinusitis
studies.humans: Doctors with low, medium and senior qualifications
studies.finding: Classification of chronic sinusitis on sinus CT images; the model achieved an accuracy of 85.8%, outperforming doctors with low (71.7%), medium (78.4%), and senior (73.4%) qualifications.
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective data; number of doctors and test set not described.
studies.title: Deep learning-based AI model for sinusitis diagnosis.
studies.source: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter study; primary US doctors read before and after AI assistance
studies.ai_system: Ultrasound deep learning model (ResNet-50) combined with large language model
studies.finding: Classification of ovarian tumours on ultrasound as benign, borderline or malignant. With visual and linguistic DL assistance, accuracy of primary US doctors improved in the test set (e.g. doctor A: 76.62% to 90.90%, doctor D: 76.62% to 95.95%). Diagnostic consistency also increased (e.g. doctor A: 0.671 to 0.912).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only five readers and a small external test set of 81 women.
studies.title: Ultrasound-based deep learning model as an assistant improves the diagnosis of ovarian tumors: a multicenter study.

studies.design: Model development with independent test set compared with physicians
studies.humans: Emergency medicine physicians and pediatric radiologists
studies.finding: Detection of subtle pediatric supracondylar fractures on radiographs. The model achieved accuracy 90.5%, 89% sensitivity, 92% specificity, outperforming emergency medicine physicians and approaching pediatric radiologists; physician figures not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Human comparison figures and reader numbers not reported; model-development paper.
studies.title: Deep learning approach based on a patch residual for pediatric supracondylar subtle fracture detection.

studies.design: Model development and validation against clinician assessment
studies.finding: For dental plaque index assessment from intraoral images, the DL model achieved micro-average accuracy of 73.67% and macro-average accuracy of 65.15%. There was no significant difference between the model and the experienced dentist (P > 0.05).
studies.limitation: Small sample of 70 participants and only two human comparators.
studies.title: Deep learning for automated dental plaque index assessment: validation against expert evaluations.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective radiomics model vs subspecialty radiologists
studies.ai_system: FR_RAD LASSO-SVM fusion radiomics model on mpMRI
studies.finding: For distinguishing IgG4-ROD from orbital MALT lymphoma, the model achieved AUC 0.907 on external testing while radiologists achieved AUCs of 0.671-0.740 (all p < 0.001). Model accuracy was 88.6% vs. 66.2% and 71.3% for radiologists (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, 214 cases, only two radiologists.
studies.title: Perilesional dominance: radiomics of multiparametric MRI enhances differentiation of IgG4-Related ophthalmic disease and orbital MALT lymphoma.

studies.design: Reader study, without then with AI support
studies.ai_system: Two-stage AI diagnosis system for private-part skin diseases
studies.finding: Dermatologists classified 115 test images of private-part skin diseases without and then with AI support. The system improved average F1-score of junior, intermediate and senior dermatologists by 16%, 7% and 4%, respectively.
studies.limitation: Sequential without-then-with design and small test set from one institute.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Aided Diagnosis System for the Detection and Classification of Private-Part Skin Diseases: Decision Analytical Modeling Study.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to experts on OCT neointima classification
studies.finding: DeepNeo classified neointimal tissue on OCT with overall accuracy of 75%, comparable to two clinical experts (75% and 71%).
studies.limitation: Only two experts and small dataset.
studies.title: Deep learning model DeepNeo predicts neointimal tissue characterization using optical coherence tomography.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 100 hypothetical cases built from real ophthalmic emergency data
studies.finding: Chatbot and three ophthalmologists graded urgency of 100 hypothetical ophthalmic emergency cases on a four-tier scale. Chatbot agreement with the ophthalmologists gave Cohen's kappa of 0.737, 0.749 and 0.751; Fleiss' kappa among all graders was 0.79. No significant difference in grade distribution (p = 0.967) or kappa values between chatbot and human graders (p = 0.572).
studies.limitation: Hypothetical cases with only three ophthalmologists and agreement, not a ground-truth outcome, as the measure.
studies.title: Performance analysis of an emergency triage system in ophthalmology using a customized CHATBOT.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective AI diagnostic study
studies.finding: The system detected anterior segment diseases on slit-lamp images, e.g. 13-class lesion-level accuracy of 0.972 internally and 0.911 externally, showing comparable performance with ophthalmologists.
studies.limitation: Ophthalmologist numbers and results not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A Generalized and Interpretable Multi-Label Multi-Disease Screening System for Ocular Anterior Segment Disease Detection.

studies.design: Retrospective development and testing of an algorithm on 238 test radiographs, compared with doctors
studies.finding: For detecting chronic fibrosing ILD on chest radiographs, the algorithm achieved an AUC of 0.979, with a sensitivity of 0.896 and a specificity of 1.000 at the chosen cut-off. Its performance was noninferior to that of doctors.
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective study; the doctors' numbers and results are not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Deep-learning algorithm to detect fibrosing interstitial lung disease on chest radiographs.

studies.design: Retrospective two-center study
studies.ai_system: Xception and DenseNet169 deep learning models
studies.finding: Differentiation of benign vs malignant calcified thyroid nodules on ultrasound. Xception achieved AUROC up to 0.970 and DenseNet169 up to 0.959, both outperforming radiologists (P < 0.05); radiologists' performance could be enhanced with DL aid.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; radiologist number and performance figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Deep learning approaches for differentiating thyroid nodules with calcification: a two-center study.

studies.design: Retrospective two-center model development with reader comparison
studies.ai_system: Ultrasound nomogram combining clinical, radiomics and deep transfer learning features
studies.finding: O-RADS risk classification of ovarian masses on ultrasound. The nomogram achieved AUC 0.930 and accuracy 84.9%, with diagnostic indices higher than junior radiologists, whose indices significantly improved with model assistance.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; radiologist numbers and metrics not given in abstract; juniors only.
studies.title: Ultrasound image-based nomogram combining clinical, radiomics, and deep transfer learning features for automatic classification of ovarian masses according to O-RADS.

studies.design: Retrospective single-center study; clinicians with and without model assistance
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model on contrast-enhanced CT
studies.finding: For distinguishing three types of functional adrenal tumors on CT, clinicians reached 92.5% accuracy with the model's help, compared with 80.6% using only their own judgment (P<0.05).
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective design; the number of clinicians is not reported.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence with a deep learning network for the quantification and distinction of functional adrenal tumors based on contrast-enhanced CT images.
studies.source: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery

studies.design: Two retrospective randomized multireader multicase studies
studies.ai_system: AI assistant for lung cancer screening
studies.humans: Experienced thoracic radiologists (six US, six Japan)
studies.finding: Lung cancer screening on 627 low-dose chest CT cases read with and without AI. AUC increased by 0.023 (0.70 to 0.72; P = .02) in the US and by 0.023 (0.93 to 0.96; P = .18) in Japan; specificity increased 5.5% (57% to 63%) and 6.7% (23% to 30%), with no difference in sensitivity.
studies.limitation: Retrospective enriched case set read outside clinical practice.
studies.title: Assistive AI in Lung Cancer Screening: A Retrospective Multinational Study in the United States and Japan.

studies.design: Reader study of 41 PSP patients and 46 controls: three readers using visual, planimetry-supported and volumetry-supported strategies, compared with an automatic SVM classifier
studies.ai_system: Support vector machine on atlas-based volumetry
studies.finding: For detecting PSP on T1 MRI, visual reading supported by automatic volumetry gave the highest accuracy among the visual strategies (75.1% ± 3.5%), no better than midbrain area planimetry (75.9%). Fully automatic SVM classification reached an accuracy of 87.4% and a sensitivity of 70.0% in variant PSP.
studies.limitation: Small sample with only three readers.
studies.title: Brain MRI in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy with Richardson's Syndrome and Variant Phenotypes.
studies.source: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society

studies.design: Reader study: physicians segmented prostate CTV on TRUS with and without U-Net starting boundaries, repeated ≥1 week apart
studies.finding: With versus without U-Net starting points, intra-physician median DSCs were 97.0% and 94.4% (p < 0.0001) and inter-physician median DSCs were 94.8% and 90.2% (p < 0.0001). Median segmentation time was 257.5 s with and 288.0 s without U-Net boundaries (p = 0.1034).
studies.limitation: Very small sample (five physicians, images from five patients); measures variability rather than accuracy against a reference.
studies.title: Deep learning-based ultrasound auto-segmentation of the prostate with brachytherapy implanted needles.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study on cytology patch images
studies.ai_system: Deep convolutional neural network for ascites cytology
studies.finding: Classification of 1041 benign vs metastatic CRC ascites cytology patch images. AI alone had accuracy 93.74%, sensitivity 87.76%, specificity 99.75%; pathologists' accuracy rose from 86.8% to 90.5% and sensitivity from 73.3% to 79.3% with AI assistance.
studies.limitation: Patch-level images rather than whole cases; number of pathologists not stated.
studies.title: Artificial-Intelligence-Assisted Detection of Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Cells in Ascitic Fluid.

studies.design: Model development with comparison against laryngology experts on videostroboscopic frames
studies.finding: A CNN classified videostroboscopic frames of sulcus, benign vocal fold lesions and healthy vocal folds. In multiclassification, the model showed greater accuracy than five laryngologists (%76 versus 72%, 68%, 72%, 63%, and 72%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset frame-level evaluation with only five experts and no statistical testing reported.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence based diagnosis of sulcus: assesment of videostroboscopy via deep learning.
studies.source: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader comparison
studies.finding: Bronchoscopic image diagnosis of normal, benign and malignant lesions. The model achieved 93.10% accuracy and 99.02% AUC for three-class classification, and its accuracy was reported as roughly the same as experienced physicians, with much higher efficiency.
studies.limitation: Only three physicians, single-center data, physician numbers not reported in abstract.
studies.title: An accurate prediction for respiratory diseases using deep learning on bronchoscopy diagnosis images.

studies.design: Multicenter model development and evaluation study with reader comparison
studies.finding: Classification of malignant, premalignant and benign ocular surface tumors from images. OECM achieved AUROCs from 0.891 to 0.993 across test sets, performed comparably to senior ophthalmologists and increased the diagnostic accuracy of junior ophthalmologists.
studies.limitation: Reader comparison results reported without numbers in the abstract; model-development focus.
studies.title: A Domain-Specific Pretrained Model for Detecting Malignant and Premalignant Ocular Surface Tumors: A Multicenter Model Development and Evaluation Study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter study; external test set of 350 patients also read by 2 radiologists
studies.humans: 2 musculoskeletal radiologists (7 and 15 years of experience)
studies.finding: For differentiating lateral malleolar avulsion fractures from subfibular ossicles on CT, the radiologists reached accuracies of 75.6% and 69.1%, sensitivities of 75.0% and 65.2% and specificities of 76.0% and 71.1%. YOLOv12 reached an accuracy of 92.0%, sensitivity of 86.7% and specificity of 82.2%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only two readers.
studies.title: YOLOv12 Algorithm-Aided Detection and Classification of Lateral Malleolar Avulsion Fracture and Subfibular Ossicle Based on CT Images: Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
studies.ai_system: YOLOv4 deep learning model on MRI
studies.finding: Detection and diagnosis of spinal schwannomas and meningiomas on sagittal MRI in 50 schwannoma, 45 meningioma and 100 control cases. Detection accuracy of the model was 84.8% (T1W), 90.3% (T2W) and 93.8% (T1W + T2W) versus 88.9% and 90.1% for the two surgeons; diagnostic accuracy was 76.4%, 83.3% and 84.1% for the model versus 77.4% and 76.1% for the surgeons.
studies.limitation: Small single-dataset retrospective study with only two human readers and no statistical comparison reported.
studies.title: Automated Detection and Diagnosis of Spinal Schwannomas and Meningiomas Using Deep Learning and Magnetic Resonance Imaging.

studies.design: Retrospective CNN development with reader comparison on 30-lesion test set
studies.humans: Two radiologists (one senior head/neck, one junior)
studies.finding: Diagnosis of skull-base invasion by nasopharyngeal malignancies on CT. CNN accuracy was 0.973 vs 0.838 (senior reader) and 0.595 (junior reader); AUC 0.953 for CNN versus 0.832 and 0.617 (both p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Very small test set (30 lesions) and only two readers from a single dataset.
studies.title: Diagnosis of skull-base invasion by nasopharyngeal tumors on CT with a deep-learning approach.

studies.design: Retrospective model evaluation on chest X-ray dataset
studies.finding: Detection of pneumothorax and oedema on chest X-rays. DenseNet121 achieved an AUC of 94% and its performance surpassed that of expert radiologists; radiologist figures are not reported.
studies.limitation: Radiologist comparison not quantified or described in abstract.
studies.title: AI-Driven Thoracic X-ray Diagnostics: Transformative Transfer Learning for Clinical Validation in Pulmonary Radiography.

studies.design: Retrospective DL model development compared with CCTA readers against QCA reference
studies.ai_system: Modified Inception V3 deep learning model
studies.finding: Binary classification of coronary stenosis (≥50%) on CCTA against QCA. AI agreement exceeded readers (Cohen kappa .79 vs. .39 patient level and .77 vs. .40 vessel level, p < .0001).
studies.limitation: Number of readers not stated; retrospective design.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence evaluation of coronary computed tomography angiography for coronary stenosis classification and diagnosis.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-institutional model development with external test sets and radiologist comparison
studies.finding: Detection of early-stage osteonecrosis of the femoral head on hip radiographs. On external test set 1 the model's AUC was 0.93 (95% CI 0.88-0.97) versus an average radiologist AUC of 0.83 (range 0.78-0.88). On external test set 2 it was 0.94 (95% CI 0.90-0.98) versus 0.79 (range 0.74-0.85).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design, and the number of radiologists is not stated.
studies.title: Automated detection of early-stage osteonecrosis of the femoral head in adult using YOLOv10: Multi-institutional validation.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre diagnostic study comparing an object detection framework with dermatologists on dermoscopic images
studies.ai_system: Multi-network fusion object detection framework (Faster R-CNN with CLAHE image enhancement)
studies.finding: Diagnosis of scalp psoriasis versus scalp seborrheic dermatitis from 1876 dermoscopic images. The framework achieved test accuracy, specificity, sensitivity and Youden index of 91.0%, 89.5%, 91.0% and 0.805 for scalp psoriasis diagnosis. The abstract states the framework performed better than the five dermatologists but gives no dermatologist figures.
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective data with only five dermatologists and no reported dermatologist performance figures in the abstract.
studies.title: Enhancing assisted diagnostic accuracy in scalp psoriasis: A Multi-Network Fusion Object Detection Framework for dermoscopic pattern diagnosis.
studies.source: Skin research and technology : official journal of International Society for Bioengineering and the Skin (ISBS) [and] International Society for Digital Imaging of Skin (ISDIS) [and] International Society for Skin Imaging (ISSI)

studies.design: Reliability study comparing FDA-cleared AI with three manual readers on 320 legs
studies.ai_system: FDA 510(k) AI software for lower extremity radiographic measurements
studies.finding: Measurement of leg length and alignment on full-leg radiographs. Reader vs AI ICCs were excellent for 12/13, 12/13 and 9/13 variables for readers 1-3; median reading times were 250, 282, 236 s for readers and 38 s for AI.
studies.limitation: Agreement study without independent reference standard; AI failed to produce output for 48 of 320 legs.
studies.title: Reliability assessment of leg length and angular alignment on manual reads versus artificial intelligence-generated lower extremity radiographic measurements.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study on 116 cytology images
studies.finding: Six-category classification of Diff-Quik respiratory cytology images. The AI model demonstrated proficiency comparable to the cytopathologists, and all combinations of AI assistance and human cytopathologist increased diagnostic efficiency to varying degrees. No numerical results are given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Only 3 readers and 116 images; no quantitative results reported in abstract.
studies.title: Evaluation of an enhanced ResNet-18 classification model for rapid On-site diagnosis in respiratory cytology.

studies.design: Monocentre retrospective study with reader evaluation
studies.ai_system: CT radiomic and combined logistic regression models
studies.finding: Diagnosis of acute versus chronic thoracolumbar vertebral compression fractures on CT. Models achieved external validation AUCs of 0.883 and 0.875; the less experienced reader achieved higher accuracy with the models (p = 0.027).
studies.limitation: Single centre, small sample, few readers; reader accuracy values not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Diagnosis of Acute Versus Chronic Thoracolumbar Vertebral Compression Fractures Using CT Radiomics Based on Machine Learning: a Preliminary Study.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Retrospective reader study, 800 radiographs, readers without and with AI reports
studies.finding: Detection of tuberculosis-related abnormalities on chest radiographs. Accuracy was 90.8% for AI reports versus 93.4% and 91.3% for readers alone (significantly lower for AI, p < .001); with AI reports accuracy was 94.1% (reader 1, p = .47) and 93.5% (reader 2, p = .03). Localization was 63.3% for AI versus 79.8% and 77.9% for readers, unchanged with AI.
studies.limitation: Only two readers; retrospective public datasets.
studies.title: Multimodal Generative Artificial Intelligence Model for Creating Radiology Reports for Chest Radiographs in Patients Undergoing Tuberculosis Screening.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader comparison on one test fold
studies.ai_system: Multidimensional CNN imaging model (fundus photographs + RNFL/GCIPL maps)
studies.humans: Two attending ophthalmologists and one resident ophthalmologist
studies.finding: Detection of primary open-angle glaucoma from fundus and OCT images. The model achieved an AUC of 0.969 (95% CI 0.934 to 0.988) in one fold of the test dataset versus AUCs of 0.847 and 0.842 for two attending ophthalmologists and 0.755 for a resident (p<0.001).
studies.limitation: Comparison with only three readers on a single test fold from a single dataset of 546 patients.
studies.title: Multidimensional imaging model for diagnosing primary open-angle glaucoma using fundus photographs and optical coherence tomography images.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with a reader study
studies.ai_system: Deep learning and radiomics fusion model on contrast-enhanced CT
studies.finding: Detection of cervical lymph node metastasis in oral squamous cell carcinoma on CECT. The fusion model had higher sensitivity than the clinicians (92.0 vs. 72.0% and 60.0%) but lower specificity (88.9 vs. 97.5% and 98.8%).
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective study with only two readers and a 24-patient test set.
studies.title: A deep learning and radiomics fusion model based on contrast-enhanced computer tomography improves preoperative identification of cervical lymph node metastasis of oral squamous cell carcinoma.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to physician segmentations
studies.ai_system: CNN model for PET/CT skeletal tumor burden (PET index)
studies.finding: Skeletal lesion detection on [18F]fluoride PET/CT in 26 test patients. Lesion detection sensitivity was 65-76% for AI and 68-91% for physicians, depending on which physician was the reference; AI PET index correlated with physician PET index at mean r = 0.69.
studies.limitation: Small test set of 26 patients; the number of physicians is not stated.
studies.title: Automated quantification of PET/CT skeletal tumor burden in prostate cancer using artificial intelligence: The PET index.
studies.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

studies.design: Retrospective algorithm development benchmarked against expert endoscopists
studies.ai_system: CNN on endoscopic images, GBDT on clinical parameters, and a hybrid of both
studies.finding: Differential diagnosis of IBD versus infectious and ischemic colitis. Global accuracy did not differ between the image-based CNN (.709) and the endoscopists (.721), while the clinical-parameter GBDT (.792) outperformed both the CNN and the experts.
studies.limitation: Retrospective study with only three endoscopists.
studies.title: Artificial-intelligence-based decision support tools for the differential diagnosis of colitis.

studies.design: Retrospective single-cohort model development with independent test set compared against ultrasound physicians
studies.ai_system: ResNet-152 CNN (also DenseNet-161, EfficientNet-B7) on ultrasound images
studies.finding: Differentiating tubal-ovarian abscess from ovarian endometriosis cyst on ultrasound images in an independent test set of 31 patients. ResNet-152 achieved an AUROC of 0.986 (0.954-1), versus 0.781 (0.620-0.942), 0.738 (0.629-848) and 0.683 (0.501-0.865) for the three physicians.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with a very small independent test set (31 patients) and only three physician readers.
studies.title: Ultrasound image-based deep learning to differentiate tubal-ovarian abscess from ovarian endometriosis cyst.

studies.design: External validation reader study on still endoscopy images
studies.finding: Classification of 300 gastroscopy still images as neoplastic or non-neoplastic. Endoscopists had mean accuracy 0.847, sensitivity 0.525 and specificity 0.872, versus 0.777, 0.591 and 0.791 for AI. For high-grade dysplasia, AI classified 80% as neoplastic against 29.1% picked up by endoscopists.
studies.limitation: Static still images from a single center rather than live endoscopy.
studies.title: Comparing artificial intelligence to humans for endoscopic diagnosis of gastric neoplasia: An external validation study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional online survey comparing ChatGPT and physician answers to 20 FAQs, rated by a 7-expert panel
studies.humans: Five mammography physicians and five gynaecology physicians
studies.finding: Answers to 20 frequently asked questions about cervical and breast cancer were rated by experts on a 7-point Likert scale. ChatGPT had an accuracy score of 7.0 (range: 6.6-7.0), surpassing the highest-scoring physicians (P < 0.05), with readability comparable to physicians and longer responses.
studies.limitation: Only 20 questions and 10 physicians, with subjective Likert ratings; consistency and reliability of ChatGPT were judged inadequate.
studies.title: An assessment of ChatGPT's responses to frequently asked questions about cervical and breast cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with comparison to radiologists
studies.ai_system: Radiomics plus deep transfer learning fusion model (LASSO-SVM) on DCE-MRI
studies.finding: Benign versus malignant breast lesion classification on DCE-MRI. The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.950 internally and 0.921 externally and showed superior diagnostic accuracy compared with two experienced radiologists; the radiologists' figures are not given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only two radiologists and a small external test set (60 patients).
studies.title: Integrating intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics with deep transfer learning for DCE-MRI breast lesion differentiation: A multicenter study comparing performance with radiologists.

studies.design: Multi-centre model development with test-set comparison against ophthalmologists
studies.ai_system: End-to-end deep learning segmentation and classification system
studies.finding: The task was classifying orbital tumors as benign or malignant on non-contrast CT. The DL model had accuracy 86.96%, sensitivity 80.00% and specificity 94.12%. There was no significant difference in diagnostic performance between the system and three ophthalmologists (p > 0.05).
studies.limitation: Only three ophthalmologists and a small test set; ophthalmologists' own metrics not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: End-to-End Deep-Learning-Based Diagnosis of Benign and Malignant Orbital Tumors on Computed Tomography Images.

studies.design: Retrospective multireader multicenter study with balanced incomplete block design
studies.ai_system: Deep learning AI model for prostate bpMRI
studies.finding: Detection of csPCa on prostate bpMRI in 180 patients. With AI, lesion-level PPV improved (77.2% vs 67.2%) but sensitivity fell (44.4% vs 48.0%), and patient-level AUC did not differ (0.822 vs 0.832). Interreader agreement for lesion-level PI-RADS improved (κ = 0.748 vs 0.336).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only six readers.
studies.title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Prostate Biparametric MRI Interpretation: An International Multireader Study.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study of 262 histopathologically verified ABUS-detected breast lesions
studies.ai_system: AI-based computer-aided detection software for automated breast ultrasound
studies.finding: Radiologists assigned BI-RADS categories to 262 breast lesions, which were then readjusted with AI-CAD results in four ways. Radiologists' AUC of 0.870 significantly improved to 0.919 (P = 0.001) when radiologists modified BI-RADS using AI results (AI-aided 1), while the other strategies gave non-significant gains (0.884, 0.890, 0.890).
studies.limitation: Retrospective study with only two radiologists; benefit significant for only one of four integration strategies.
studies.title: Diagnostic Performance of Artificial Intelligence-Based Computer-Aided Detection Software for Automated Breast Ultrasound.

studies.design: Multicenter model development with a reader study with and without model assistance
studies.humans: One junior and one senior radiologist
studies.finding: Assessment of axillary lymph node metastasis on breast ultrasound. With model assistance, AUC increased from 0.71 to 0.82 for the junior radiologist and from 0.75 to 0.85 for the senior radiologist.
studies.limitation: Only two readers took part in the assisted-reading comparison.
studies.title: Ultrasound-based deep learning radiomics for enhanced axillary lymph node metastasis assessment: a multicenter study.

studies.design: Retrospective two-center model development with reader comparison with and without AI aid
studies.ai_system: Deep learning radiomics (MobileNet-V3-large + radiomics) model on multiparametric MRI
studies.finding: Predicting lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer on MRI. With the model's aid, AUC values for junior and senior radiologists increased by 0.162 and 0.232 on the Training set and by 0.096 and 0.113 on the External test set. The model alone achieved an AUC of 0.752 on the External test set.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with a small external test set (66 patients); number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Development and Validation of Multiparametric MRI-based Interpretable Deep Learning Radiomics Fusion Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis and Prognosis in Rectal Cancer: A Two-center Study.

studies.design: Comparison of LLM responses to case vignettes against reported GP responses
studies.finding: Identifying childhood anxiety disorder in complex cases, comparing LLMs with GP reports. AI tools exhibited significantly higher rates of identifying anxiety than GPs; Claude.AI and Gemini identified at least four cases, ChatGPT-3 three, and ChatGPT-4 one or two. 40% of GPs preferred to manage cases within their practice, whereas AI tools generally recommended referral.
studies.limitation: Small number of vignette cases with GP comparison drawn from reports; number of GPs not stated and findings described as preliminary.
studies.title: Large language models outperform general practitioners in identifying complex cases of childhood anxiety.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study of breast whole slide images with and without AI support
studies.ai_system: AI solution for classification of breast lesion whole slide images
studies.finding: Pathologists classified 104 breast lesion cases with and without AI support. Diagnostic accuracy improved from 97.1% to 100% with AI support (303 vs. 312 accurate case reads per arm), review time fell by an average of 16.5%, and immunohistochemistry usage fell by 33%.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 104 cases and only 3 pathologists; no statistical significance reported for the accuracy gain.
studies.title: A Comprehensive AI-Based Approach in Classifying Breast Lesions: Focusing on Improving Pathologists' Accuracy and Efficiency.

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective reader study; radiologists read nonenhanced CT alone, then with deep-learning synthetic contrast-enhanced CT
studies.ai_system: DL-SynCCT (weakly supervised deep-learning synthetic contrast-enhanced CT)
studies.finding: Three radiologists detected lesions on nonenhanced CT in 398 patients, first with NECT alone and then with DL-SynCCT added. With DL-SynCCT, pooled sensitivity for lesion detection increased from 72.0% to 76.4% (P < 0.001). Diagnostic confidence increased from 3.0 to 3.6 (P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Only three readers, and a sequential reading design in which the AI session always came second, so order and recall effects cannot be excluded.
studies.title: Clinical feasibility of deep learning based synthetic contrast enhanced abdominal CT in patients undergoing non enhanced CT scans.

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective model development with external validation, compared against radiologists
studies.ai_system: Hybrid radiomics ensemble (SVM_RBF and SVM_lin) using hand-crafted and deep features including the peritumoral region
studies.humans: Two radiologists (senior and junior) using ATA and TI-RADS guidelines
studies.finding: The task was to differentiate benign from malignant thyroid nodules on ultrasound, using 1602 nodules from four centres. The ensemble model achieved AUC of 0.954, 0.949, 0.932 and 0.921 across internal and external validations. It outperformed both radiologists using ATA and TI-RADS, but the radiologists' values are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists, and their performance figures are not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Diagnosis of Thyroid Nodule Malignancy Using Peritumoral Region and Artificial Intelligence: Results of Hand-Crafted, Deep Radiomics Features and Radiologists' Assessment in Multicenter Cohorts.
studies.source: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine

studies.design: Retrospective model development on 77 patients with operator performance compared with and without automated support
studies.ai_system: Radiomic-based Inception-V3 CNN model for myometrial invasion on ultrasound
studies.finding: Prediction of depth of myometrial invasion in endometrial cancer on ultrasound. With the radiomic decision support, the operator's overall accuracy rose to 82.82% from 71.88% and recall of the intermediate class rose to 71.88% from 56.25%, both statistically superior; precision increased by 10% points.
studies.limitation: Small single dataset (77 patients) with cross-validation only and apparently a single operator.
studies.title: A Radiomic-based model to predict the depth of myometrial invasion in endometrial cancer on ultrasound images.

studies.design: Simulation study with 50 pediatric clinical scenarios derived from ACR guideline variants
studies.ai_system: ped-Llama (RAG-enabled locally deployed Llama-3.1-8B); also generic Llama-3.1-8B, GPT-4o, Claude Opus
studies.humans: Three radiologists: junior resident, senior resident, specialist pediatric radiologist
studies.finding: Imaging modality recommendations for 50 pediatric scenarios were graded against ACR Appropriateness Criteria. ped-Llama achieved 80% (40/50) 'Usually appropriate' recommendations, versus 46% for Llama-3.1-8B, 54% for GPT-4o and 46% for Claude Opus, matching the specialist pediatric radiologist (76%). Accepting 'May be appropriate' as well, ped-Llama reached 90% accuracy.
studies.limitation: Simulated vignettes (50 scenarios) with only three radiologists; resident results not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Locally deployed context-aware chatbot outperforms generic large language models for guideline-concordant pediatric imaging recommendations.

studies.design: Model development with 10-fold cross-validation, compared with ophthalmologists
studies.finding: The task was differential diagnosis among high myopia, glaucoma, highly myopic glaucoma and normal eyes from fundus photographs. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 97.7% (AUC 98.6%), versus accuracies of 64.7% and 69.9% for two attending ophthalmologists.
studies.limitation: Only two ophthalmologist comparators; cross-validation without external validation.
studies.title: Detecting Glaucoma in Highly Myopic Eyes From Fundus Photographs Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre cohort with reader study
studies.finding: For discriminating early breast cancer among ultrasound-benign findings, EDL-BC had AUC 0.945 and radiologists with AI assistance had AUC 0.899, both significantly higher than radiologists without AI (0.716; p < 0.0001). There was no significant difference between the model alone and AI-assisted radiologists (p = 0.099).
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study on Chinese centres only.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted ultrasound image analysis to discriminate early breast cancer in Chinese population: a retrospective, multicentre, cohort study.

studies.design: Model development with man-machine contest, reader study and video validation
studies.finding: CCIC predicted cancer invasion in large sessile colorectal polyps with accuracy of 90.4% on images and 89.7% on video. It was comparable with expert endoscopists and superior to senior and junior endoscopists. With CCIC assistance, the accuracy of junior endoscopists improved from 75.4% to 85.3% (P = 0.002).
studies.limitation: Small test set (198 lesions) and a retrospective reader study rather than live care.
studies.title: Development and validation of an artificial intelligence-based system for predicting colorectal cancer invasion depth using multi-modal data.
studies.source: Digestive endoscopy : official journal of the Japan Gastroenterological Endoscopy Society

studies.design: Multicentre agreement study on NSCLC whole-slide images against six readers
studies.ai_system: Deep learning PD-L1 cell detection algorithm
studies.finding: Cell-level PD-L1 detection and TPS quantification in NSCLC slides. At cell level, mean reader-reader F1 was 0.68 vs mean reader-AI F1 of 0.55. For TPS, mean reader-reader kappa was 0.54 (95% CI 0.26-0.81) vs mean reader-AI kappa of 0.49 (95% CI 0.27-0.72).
studies.limitation: Agreement-based reference standard without ground truth; AI performance dropped on cases from the centre not in training.
studies.title: Comparing deep learning and pathologist quantification of cell-level PD-L1 expression in non-small cell lung cancer whole-slide images.

studies.design: Model development with radiologist-assisted reading
studies.finding: Breast cancer diagnosis on photoacoustic ultrasound images. The model achieved a testing AUC of 0.870, and it improved radiologists' diagnostic specificity without reducing sensitivity.
studies.limitation: Single centre, small cohort; reader numbers and assisted metrics not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Deep learning combined with attention mechanisms to assist radiologists in enhancing breast cancer diagnosis: a study on photoacoustic imaging.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to expert radiologist
studies.ai_system: MFFC-Net multi-modal MRI deep learning classifier
studies.finding: Classification of glioblastoma, solitary brain metastases and primary CNS lymphoma on multi-modal MRI. MFFC-Net accuracy was 0.920 versus 0.924 for the expert radiologist, with no significant difference (p = 0.774).
studies.limitation: Retrospective model-development study; number of radiologists not stated and comparison is secondary.
studies.title: Aided Diagnosis Model Based on Deep Learning for Glioblastoma, Solitary Brain Metastases, and Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma with Multi-Modal MRI.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with pathologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model on whole slide images
studies.humans: Junior, senior GI and senior non-GI pathologists
studies.finding: Distinguishing Crohn's disease from intestinal tuberculosis on resection WSIs. In training the model AUC 0.886 was better than junior pathologists (0.701, 0.861) and inferior to senior GI pathologists (0.910, 0.946); in the test cohort the model (AUC 0.893) outperformed senior non-GI pathologists (0.782, 0.821), with all P values non-significant.
studies.limitation: Small sample (85 cases) and few pathologists; differences were not statistically significant.
studies.title: Deep learning model to differentiate Crohn's disease from intestinal tuberculosis using histopathological whole slide images from intestinal specimens.
studies.source: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology

studies.design: Retrospective development and validation of a segmentation model on 40 bone marrow biopsy whole-slide images, compared with pathologists
studies.ai_system: AI semantic segmentation model for bone marrow cellularity
studies.humans: Five expert hematopathologists and three trainees
studies.finding: Cellularity assessment in 40 bone marrow biopsies from Ph-negative MPN was compared between the AI model and five expert hematopathologists and three trainees. The model showed optimal concordance with the expert pathologists' evaluation, with poorer concordance for trainees. No numeric concordance values are reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Small single-centre sample (40 test slides) with concordance reported only qualitatively.
studies.title: Development of an Artificial-Intelligence-Based Tool for Automated Assessment of Cellularity in Bone Marrow Biopsies in Ph-Negative Myeloproliferative Neoplasms.

studies.design: Vignette study comparing o1 with historical clinician results
studies.finding: Susceptibility to cognitive bias across ten paired clinical vignettes. o1 showed no measurable bias in seven of ten vignettes; in two it showed significant bias of lower magnitude than reported for human clinicians, and in one (Occam's razor) consistent bias.
studies.limitation: Comparison against historical human data rather than concurrent clinicians; vignettes only.
studies.title: Evaluating the o1 reasoning large language model for cognitive bias: a vignette study.

studies.design: Model development with interobserver comparison against expert reader
studies.finding: Coronary plaque segmentation on CCTA. In the interobserver study, PlaqueViT performed as well as the expert reader (Dice coefficient = 0.51 and 0.50, average surface distance = 1.31 and 1.15 mm, ICC = 0.97 and 0.98, respectively).
studies.limitation: Small interobserver set (n = 65) with apparently a single expert reader comparison; retrospective.
studies.title: PlaqueViT: a vision transformer model for fully automatic vessel and plaque segmentation in coronary computed tomography angiography.

studies.design: Model development on 3046 whole slide images with comparison to a chief pathologist on a 100-slide subset
studies.finding: Classification of salivary gland neoplasm subtypes on whole slide images. On a subset of 100 WSIs, SGN-ViT demonstrated comparable diagnostic performance to that of the chief pathologist while significantly reducing diagnosis time; overall the model achieved an accuracy of 0.9966.
studies.limitation: Comparison against a single pathologist on a small 100-slide subset, with no human performance numbers reported.
studies.title: A Recognition System for Diagnosing Salivary Gland Neoplasms Based on Vision Transformer.

studies.design: Retrospective two-centre radiomics model study with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: DBT radiomics nomogram (Ki67 + RadScore, logistic regression)
studies.finding: For predicting axillary lymph node metastasis from digital breast tomosynthesis, the Signature tumor+10 mm model reached AUC 0.806 and the nomogram reached AUC 0.813. The nomogram outperformed radiologists' assessments in predictive accuracy, but the abstract does not report figures for the radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design, and the radiologists' performance and number are not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Preoperative DBT-based radiomics for predicting axillary lymph node metastasis in breast cancer: a multi-center study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre radiomics model study with physician comparison
studies.ai_system: CCH-NET random forest ultrasound radiomics model
studies.finding: For predicting seronegative Hashimoto's thyroiditis on ultrasound, CCH-NET achieved sensitivity 0.762, specificity 0.714 and AUC 0.8248. This outperformed senior ultrasound physicians (AUC = 0.681).
studies.limitation: Small retrospective sample (164 patients) with an 80:20 split.
studies.title: Prediction of Seronegative Hashimoto's thyroiditis using machine learning models based on ultrasound radiomics: a multicenter study.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on panoramic radiographs
studies.humans: Experienced dentomaxillofacial radiologist using London Atlas
studies.finding: Dental age estimation from 620 panoramic radiographs. ChatGPT had higher MAE and RMSE than the radiologist using the London Atlas, and lower reproducibility (ICC = 0.703 vs ICC = 0.960).
studies.limitation: Single expert rater; dental rather than physician task; single-population retrospective sample.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence versus human expertise: reliability of ChatGPT and the London atlas for dental age estimation using panoramic radiographs.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on radiograph-based vignettes
studies.finding: Diagnosis and management of complex endodontic anomalies across 19 radiograph cases with six questions each. The expert achieved 100% accuracy while all LLMs performed significantly lower (P < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Only one expert and 19 cases; expert also likely close to reference key.
studies.title: Dens invaginatus as a diagnostic challenge: evaluating large language models against expert endodontic reasoning.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre diagnostic accuracy reader comparison
studies.ai_system: Google Cloud Vertex AI AutoML deep learning model
studies.humans: 15 physicians from general practice, emergency medicine, thoracic surgery and radiology
studies.finding: On 152 CT-confirmed chest radiographs, the AI had accuracy 0.95, sensitivity 1.00 and specificity 0.89 for pneumothorax detection. It outperformed junior clinicians and matched or exceeded senior physicians. For minimal pneumothoraces, AI sensitivity was 0.93 versus 0.55-0.84 among human readers.
studies.limitation: Small single-centre balanced dataset (76/76), which may not reflect clinical prevalence.
studies.title: Multidisciplinary Evaluation of an AI-Based Pneumothorax Detection Model: Clinical Comparison with Physicians in Edge and Cloud Environments.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with reader comparison and assisted reading
studies.finding: Meniscal injury detection on knee MRI in 259 knees. The model outperformed two clinicians, with accuracy 0.980 for medial and 0.920 for lateral menisci. With model assistance and saliency maps, both clinicians improved their diagnostic performance.
studies.limitation: Only two clinicians, single retrospective dataset; clinician figures not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Multitask learning for automatic detection of meniscal injury on 3D knee MRI.
studies.source: Journal of orthopaedic research : official publication of the Orthopaedic Research Society

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of LLM-selected and human-selected protocols against a reference standard
studies.humans: Radiologists, fellows and residents in practice
studies.finding: GPT-4o and radiologists in practice assigned protocols for abdominal and pelvic CT scans. GPT-4o with prompting only selected optimal protocols more often than humans (96.2% [527 of 548] vs 88.3% [484 of 548]; P < .001). Inappropriate protocols did not differ (1.3% vs 2.4%; P = .21).
studies.limitation: Single-institution retrospective study; the reference standard was set by the same institution's radiologists and guidelines.
studies.title: Optimizing Large Language Models for Automated Protocoling of Abdominal and Pelvic CT Scans: The Power of Context.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective development and external validation study
studies.ai_system: XGBoost model integrating PET MPI parameters and CAC
studies.finding: Diagnosis of obstructive coronary artery disease from PET/CT myocardial perfusion imaging in a testing cohort (n = 1278). The AI model achieved an AUC of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.81-0.85), outperforming experienced physicians (0.80, p = 0.02).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with patients selected for invasive angiography; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Multicenter evaluation of interpretable AI for coronary artery disease diagnosis from PET biomarkers.

studies.design: Model development with physician-AI collaboration comparison
studies.finding: Diagnostic workflows on real-world cases. Collaboration between physicians and ClinDiag-GPT yielded higher diagnostic accuracy and efficiency compared to either working alone; no numbers reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: No quantitative results or physician numbers reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Grounding large language models in clinical diagnostics.

studies.design: Retrospective user study with vs without AI
studies.ai_system: GenVF generative vision transformer visual field forecasts
studies.finding: Residents rated glaucoma progression from visual fields with and without AI forecasts, measured by MAE. Global MAE showed minor differences; residents made more conservative decisions and reported higher confidence with AI, with comparable reaction times.
studies.limitation: Only 8 residents at a single center; no quantitative effect sizes reported.
studies.title: Toward Long-Term Visual Field Appearance Forecasting Using Artificial Intelligence for Ophthalmic Education and Diagnosis.

studies.design: AI-human collaboration reader study within model development
studies.finding: Insulin titration in type 2 diabetes with and without STII-DIL assistance. Accuracy significantly improved for junior clinicians, while senior clinicians showed minimal change; both reported increased confidence.
studies.limitation: No numbers or clinician count reported; retrospective EHR cases.
studies.title: Explainable deep learning framework incorporating medical knowledge for insulin titration in diabetes.

studies.design: Retrospective EHR benchmark with silent deployment and small ICU pilot
studies.ai_system: Random Forest (length of stay); BioClinical-BERT retrieval
studies.finding: Prediction of length of stay in paediatric cardiology. The Random Forest model achieved accuracy of 0.88 ± 0.02, outperforming clinicians. In a 25-case ICU pilot, clinician-rated utility of retrieval improved from 4.23 ± 2.42 to 4.41 ± 2.16.
studies.limitation: Clinician performance figures and number of clinicians not reported; single centre.
studies.title: Clinically-applicable prediction of hospital stay and patient similarity retrieval in paediatric cardiology using machine learning.

studies.design: Retrospective multireader study, 212 patients, unassisted vs AI-assisted vs expert-assisted reading
studies.ai_system: AI lesion measurement system for RECIST 1.1
studies.finding: For RECIST measurement on follow-up CT, AI assistance reduced per-patient reading time (-36.0 s) and increased RECIST outcome agreement by 7.7% versus unassisted reading. It slightly increased lesion-level variability (1.32 mm), and expert-assisted reading gave higher agreement (13.3%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study; readers were told all support was AI-derived.
studies.title: Multicenter AI- versus expert-assisted RECIST target lesion measurements in follow-up body CT of patients with cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective multireader multicase study, 150 non-contrast CT heads, unaided then aided after washout
studies.finding: Detecting critical abnormalities on non-contrast CT head: with AI, pooled reader sensitivity rose from 82.8% to 89.7% while specificity fell from 84.5% to 78.9%. Stand-alone AI AUC was 0.821-0.976, and ED clinicians with AI matched the sensitivity of unaided radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective enriched dataset; not in clinical practice.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted reader evaluation in acute CT head interpretation (AI-REACT): a multireader multicase study.

studies.design: Retrospective EHR model development with comparison to clinician discharge predictions
studies.finding: Length of stay prediction. Best XGB models matched clinician LoS prediction accuracy in elective admissions and significantly outperformed clinicians in emergency admissions (p <0.001).
studies.limitation: Clinicians gave predictions for only 3%-5% of admissions, mostly near discharge; single region.
studies.title: Concurrent prediction of in-hospital mortality and length of stay using single-task, multiclass and multitask machine learning.

studies.design: Retrospective study using PLCO trial chest radiographs plus reader study
studies.ai_system: Commercially available AI lung cancer detection software
studies.humans: PLCO radiologists and 3 experienced radiologists in reader study
studies.finding: Detection of unsuspected lung cancer on chest radiographs. Versus PLCO radiologists, AI had higher specificity (0.910 vs 0.803) but lower sensitivity (0.326 vs 0.412); in the reader study differences with 3 radiologists were not significant. Authors conclude comparable performance.
studies.limitation: Retrospective use of historical 1993-2001 radiographs; reader study with only 3 radiologists on an enriched subset.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence software for detecting unsuspected lung cancer on chest radiographs in an asymptomatic population.

studies.design: Dual-center retrospective study with two phases: model vs routine report diagnoses, then generalist readers without and with AI assistance
studies.humans: Subspecialist and generalist radiologists (routine reports); seven generalists in reader phase
studies.finding: GPT-5-Thinking interpreted narrative MRI reports of orbital and head-and-neck tumors; top-1 accuracy was similar to subspecialists (76.7% vs 78.3% orbital; 67.5% vs 68.0% head-and-neck) and higher than routine generalists (74.0% vs 68.7%; 64.0% vs 27.0%). With GPT-5-Thinking assistance, generalist top-1 accuracy rose from 61.4% to 70.3% (orbital) and from 47.0% to 61.0% (head-and-neck), both P < .001.
studies.limitation: Retrospective convenience series using text reports rather than images; only seven generalists in the assistance phase.
studies.title: Bridging the Generalist-Subspecialist Gap with GPT-5-Thinking: Dual-Center Evaluation in Orbital and Head-and-Neck Tumor MRI Reports.

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective model development with clinical reader study
studies.ai_system: MPSUR (graph convolutional and recurrent neural network multimodal system)
studies.finding: MPSUR predicted causes of unplanned reoperations from multimodal EMRs. In the clinical reader study it outperformed surgeons across all departments (mean accuracy=60.27%, 95% CI 58.27% to 62.26%); surgeon accuracy is not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Retrospective data; surgeon numbers and their accuracy figures not reported; modest absolute accuracy.
studies.title: Predicting the causes of unplanned reoperations using an AI-based multimodal system: a multicentre, multidepartmental study based on EMRs.

studies.design: Retrospective two-institution study comparing LLMs given radiology findings plus clinical information against radiologists
studies.finding: LLMs generated diagnoses from radiology reports for histopathologically confirmed liver, lung and breast disease. In the liver cohort DeepSeek-R1 reached 76.2% vs radiologists 81.2% (adjusted P >.99); in the lung cohort Gemini 2.5 Pro reached 78.3% vs radiologists 87.0% (adjusted P =.25), with no statistically significant differences.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, small cohorts (301 patients) and text-based input; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Incremental Diagnostic Value of Clinical Information for Large Language Models Across Multiple Organs: Retrospective Study.

studies.design: Model development with reader study and collaborative workflow evaluation
studies.humans: 32 readers: junior, intermediate general practitioners and senior specialists
studies.finding: Across dental imaging diagnosis tasks, DentVLM surpassed junior readers, matched intermediate general practitioners and approached senior specialists. With AI collaboration, junior and intermediate readers moved toward specialist-level performance, and diagnostic time fell by 15.0-37.0% for all readers.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives few quantitative accuracy figures for the reader comparison; study design details are limited.
studies.title: A multimodal vision-language model for comprehensive dental diagnosis and enhanced clinical practice.

studies.design: Model development with multicenter evaluation and reader study
studies.humans: Physicians using ECG and clinically acquired CMR images
studies.finding: In a reader study, CardioNets was compared with physicians using ECG and clinically acquired CMR for cardiac disease detection. CardioNets achieved an accuracy of 0.874 (95% CI, 0.800 to 0.923), outperforming participating readers; reader numbers are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Reader study details and reader accuracy not reported; retrospective data.
studies.title: Generating Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Images from Electrocardiograms - A Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Model development with blinded review comparing AI and cardiologist reports
studies.finding: In a blinded review of 365 evaluations across 288 angiograms, DeepCORO-CLIP reports were clinically usable in 76% of evaluations versus 88% for cardiologists. False positives were comparable (17% versus 14%, P = 0.38).
