studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of cardiologists not stated.
studies.title: A multiview video-text model detects obstructive coronary stenosis and predicts 1-year cardiovascular events from angiography.

studies.design: Retrospective multinational external validation
studies.finding: AI detection of Gleason grade group ≥2 prostate cancer on MRI was compared with standard-of-care radiology diagnoses. Agreement was 83.0%, 87.9% and 87.7% across three external datasets, meeting prespecified interchangeability criteria relative to an average radiologist.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; comparison against routine readings rather than a controlled reader study; performance varied across sites.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence for Prostate Cancer Detection and Screening on MRI in Global Populations: The SCARLET-1 Study.

studies.design: Model development with reader study
studies.finding: In a reader study on abdominal CT diagnosis, RADAR assistance increased the diagnostic sensitivity of 26 radiologists by ~10%. Other reader metrics are not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives only an approximate sensitivity gain and no specificity or reader-study design details.
studies.title: An expert-level generalist AI for abdominal CT diagnosis.

studies.design: Multicenter ex vivo video-clip reader study, unaided vs CADx-assisted
studies.ai_system: CADx system for optical polyp diagnosis
studies.finding: 35 endoscopists assessed 100 polyps on NBI video clips. High-confidence diagnostic accuracy improved from 78.3% to 89.8% with CADx assistance (p<0.001), and novices improved from 74.1% to 88.8%.
studies.limitation: Ex vivo video-based assessment rather than live colonoscopy.
studies.title: Structured Integration of an Artificial Intelligence-Based System for the Optical Diagnosis of Colorectal Polyps.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-institution comparison of radiomics model vs radiologist
studies.ai_system: Bayesian additive regression trees radiomics model
studies.finding: Classifying atypical lipomatous tumors vs lipomas on MRI in 423 patients, BART had accuracy 77.07%, sensitivity 77.67% and specificity 76.50%, versus the radiologist's 78.72%, 76.21% and 81.11%. AUC was 84.72% for BART and 84.74% for the reader.
studies.limitation: Single human reader as comparator; retrospective design.
studies.title: Bayesian additive regression trees for machine learning to classify benign vs atypical lipomatous tumors on MRI.

studies.design: Cross-sectional analysis of population-based cohort
studies.ai_system: ML model estimating vertical cup-disc ratio
studies.finding: VCDR from fundus images was estimated by ML and by trained human graders to predict specialist-ascertained glaucoma in 6304 participants. For left eyes, AUROC was 88% for ML-VCDR vs 79% for H-VCDR; for right eyes, 90% vs 81%.
studies.limitation: Human comparators were trained graders, not clinicians, and the task was limited to VCDR estimation.
studies.title: A Comparison of Machine Learning and Human Graders for Glaucoma Diagnosis from Fundus Images for Population Screening.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter study
studies.finding: LLMs interpreted 1063 thyroid ultrasound text reports. For benign-malignant differentiation, DeepSeek-R1 accuracy was 0.729 and ChatGPT-4o 0.644, while senior radiologists achieved AUC 0.865 and accuracy 0.804.
studies.limitation: Radiologists had access to images and clinical context that the LLMs did not; the number of radiologists is not stated.
studies.title: The Performance of ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 in Interpreting Thyroid Nodule Ultrasound Text Reports: Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Two-stage before-after reader study
studies.ai_system: Claude Sonnet 4.5, ChatGPT-5.0, Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek-V3.2
studies.finding: On 40 orthopedic rare disease cases, three LLMs achieved 90% (36/40) primary-diagnosis accuracy. Physician accuracy rose with LLM assistance from 42.22% to 68.80% (intermediate) and from 58.67% to 83.33% (senior).
studies.limitation: Same-day repeated-case design with possible recall bias; only 40 cases.
studies.title: Diagnostic Performance of Large Language Models for Orthopedic-Related Rare Diseases and Their Impact on Physicians' Diagnostic Accuracy: 2-Stage Comparative Evaluation Study Based on the Chinese Rare Disease Catalog.

studies.design: Retrospective study
studies.ai_system: Privately hosted Claude 3.5 secure LLM with EMR data
studies.finding: MRI protocol selection for 608 outpatient examinations against a consensus reference. Overall protocol accuracy was 93.1% for the sLLM vs 91.4% (Rad 3) and 92.1% (Rad 4) (P=.23, P=.40); contrast decisions were 94.4% vs 92.1% (P=.027) and 92.9% (P=.16).
studies.limitation: Single-institution retrospective study with only two comparator radiologists; EMR data manually retrieved.
studies.title: Initial Insights Into an Institutional Secure Large Language Model for Magnetic Resonance Imaging Examination Requests: Retrospective Study.

studies.design: Multicentre model development with reader comparison and pilot training study
studies.ai_system: AI system for detecting fetal orofacial clefts on ultrasound
studies.humans: Senior and junior radiologists; 24 radiologists and trainees in the pilot
studies.finding: The task was detecting fetal orofacial clefts on ultrasound. The AI reached sensitivity and specificity exceeding 93% and 95%, matching senior radiologists and substantially outperforming junior radiologists. As a copilot, it raised junior radiologists' sensitivity by more than 6%.
studies.limitation: The abstract reports few reader numbers, and the training effect comes from a small pilot.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence for detecting fetal orofacial clefts and advancing medical education.

studies.design: Retrospective model development plus prospective multi-reader multi-case crossover reader study
studies.ai_system: Random Forest model predicting 3-month CGRP-mAb response
studies.finding: Physicians predicted ≥50% migraine-day reduction at 3 months in 46 test cases. Without the model, median physician accuracy was 65.2% and kappa 0.30; with the model, accuracy was 73.9% and kappa 0.48, with accuracy, sensitivity, F1-score and kappa statistically improved. The model alone had accuracy of 76.1%.
studies.limitation: Small single-center test set (46 patients) and only 8 physicians, without external validation.
studies.title: Development of a machine learning (ML) model to predict 3-month response to CGRP monoclonal antibodies in migraine: A pilot evaluation of physician-ML model interaction.

studies.design: Preprint; comparison of ChatGPT versions and neuro-ophthalmologists on published case reports
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT v3.5 and ChatGPT Plus v4.0
studies.finding: On 22 neuro-ophthalmic case reports, ChatGPT v3.5 was correct in 13 (59%) and ChatGPT Plus v4.0 in 18 (82%). Each neuro-ophthalmologist was correct in 19 (86%) cases.
studies.limitation: Preprint; only 22 public cases and 2 clinicians; no statistical testing.
studies.title: ChatGPT Assisting Diagnosis of Neuro-ophthalmology Diseases Based on Case Reports.
studies.source: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

studies.design: Proof-of-concept platform compared with a pathologist panel
studies.ai_system: Hyperspectral autofluorescence virtual staining with deep learning NASH scoring
studies.finding: The task was NASH CRN scoring of liver tissue. The automated platform was comparable to an independent pathologist panel when evaluated against expert consensus; no numbers are reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Proof-of-concept study with no quantitative results in the abstract.
studies.title: An End-to-End Platform for Digital Pathology Using Hyperspectral Autofluorescence Microscopy and Deep Learning-Based Virtual Histology.
studies.source: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc

studies.design: Foundation model development and validation, with a comparative diagnostic accuracy study against ophthalmologists
studies.finding: VisionFM and ophthalmologists of varying experience diagnosed 12 ocular diseases from fundus photographs. VisionFM's diagnostic accuracy was close to that of intermediate-level ophthalmologists. Separately, it achieved an average AUROC of 0.950 across eight disease categories in internal validation.
studies.limitation: The abstract gives no numbers for the human comparison and does not state the number of readers.
studies.title: Development and Validation of a Multimodal Multitask Vision Foundation Model for Generalist Ophthalmic Artificial Intelligence.

studies.design: Multicentre development and validation study with a reader study of AI-assisted interpretation
studies.finding: BL4AS was evaluated for classifying BI-RADS 4 breast MRI lesions. It significantly outperformed radiologists in specificity (0.889 versus 0.491). BL4AS-assisted interpretation improved diagnostic accuracy for senior and junior radiologists, reducing inter-reader variability by 24.5% and false-positive rates by 27.3%.
studies.limitation: The number of readers and the study design (retrospective reader study) are not described in detail in the abstract.
studies.title: An interpretable AI system reduces false-positive MRI diagnoses by stratifying high-risk breast lesions.

studies.design: Cross-sectional vignette benchmark with blinded physician rating
studies.finding: Open-ended responses to 507 primary healthcare vignettes were rated on an 11-domain rubric. Clinician mean ratings were lower than LLMs in 9/11 domains, e.g. guideline alignment 2.86 vs 4.25-4.72 and low likelihood of harm 3.68 vs 4.54-4.81. Performance was similar for irrelevant content (4.28 vs 4.25-4.35) and demographic bias (4.86 vs 4.91-4.94).
studies.limitation: Vignette-based tasks rather than real patient encounters; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Benchmarking large language models and clinicians using locally generated primary healthcare vignettes in Kenya.

studies.design: Agent development with simulated practice study, external validation and silent trial
studies.finding: Treatment decisions in hematological malignancies measured as concordance with tumor board decisions. In a simulated practice study, agent-assisted resident physicians achieved near-senior concordance and partially outperformed senior physicians in their subspecialty.
studies.limitation: Human comparison was a simulated study with no numbers or participant counts reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Clinical decision support in hematological malignancies using a case-grounded AI agent.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on FRCOphth part 2 textbook MCQs
studies.ai_system: GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama-3.2, DeepSeek V3, Qwen2.5
studies.humans: Expert ophthalmologists, ophthalmology trainees, junior physicians
studies.finding: On textual questions, Claude 3.5 Sonnet (accuracy, 77.7%) outperformed trainees (difference, 9.0%) and junior physicians (difference, 35.2%) and was comparable to experts (difference, 1.3%; P = .72). On multimodal questions, GPT-4o (accuracy, 57.5%) was weaker than experts (70.0%-85.0%) and trainees (62.5%-80%).
studies.limitation: Textbook exam questions rather than clinical cases; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Performance of Foundation Models vs Physicians in Textual and Multimodal Ophthalmological Questions.

studies.design: Multicenter model development with reader study
studies.finding: Detection and diagnosis of gliomas and brain metastases on MRI. With BTSC-CAD assistance, junior radiologists achieved mean AUC improvements of 4.8% (P < 0.05) for detection and 17.3% (P < 0.001) for diagnosis, with an average reduction of 64.75 s in reading time.
studies.limitation: Reader study details (number of readers, design) not reported in abstract; junior radiologists only.
studies.title: Multi-task deep learning assists detection and diagnosis of gliomas and brain metastases.

studies.design: Reader comparison study with external validation
studies.finding: Prediction of IDH mutation status from MRI. On BraTS, GliomaVista-IDH had AUC 0.97, significantly outperforming all physician groups; on an external Japanese cohort AI fell to AUC 0.75 and 0.82, while high-performing physicians achieved AUC 0.88 with better calibration (Brier 0.19 vs 0.32).
studies.limitation: Result depends on dataset; AI degraded on external validation; small reader group.
studies.title: Comparing artificial intelligence and physician performance in predicting IDH mutation status in glioma.

studies.design: Model development and benchmark with pathologist comparison
studies.finding: Lymph node metastasis detection on whole-slide images. PRET, using only eight slide examples, delivered clinical-grade performance outperforming 11 pathologists.
studies.limitation: Pathologist comparison metrics not reported in abstract; benchmark datasets.
studies.title: PRET is a few-shot system for pan-cancer recognition without example training.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with reader comparison
studies.finding: Differentiating follicular thyroid carcinoma from adenoma on ultrasound. The model achieved AUCs of 0.816-0.847 on external test sets, consistently outperformed radiologists, and improved diagnostic accuracy as an assistive tool.
studies.limitation: Radiologist figures and numbers not reported in abstract; retrospective.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled ultrasound diagnosis and stratification of follicular thyroid neoplasms: a multi-center study.

studies.design: Retrospective multireader paired eye-tracking study, 60 screening mammograms
studies.finding: Reading screening mammograms with AI prompts: median sensitivity for cases with false-negative AI suggestions fell from 71% unassisted to 39% with AI. Specificity for cases with false-positive AI suggestions was 39% vs 21%, and more prompts lengthened read times from 25 to 34 seconds.
studies.limitation: Small enriched test set and 10 readers.
studies.title: Automation Bias in Action: Eye Tracking of Humans Reading Screening Mammograms with and without AI Prompts.

studies.design: Model development with reader study
studies.finding: Predicting retinal vein occlusion treatment response: the AI system achieved higher predictive accuracy than retinal specialists and reduced interpretation time. Clinicians' predictive performance improved with AI assistance; no reader numbers are reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Reader study details and numbers not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Treatment effects prediction and clinical decision-making system for retinal vein occlusion by artificial intelligence.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter diagnostic study with reader comparison
studies.humans: Five board-certified head and neck cancer specialists
studies.finding: Detection of extranodal extension on preoperative CT in laryngeal/hypopharyngeal cancer. DeepENE outperformed the experts, e.g. AUC 0.87 vs mean reader AUC 0.66 in external test set 2 (P < .001); sensitivity 97% vs experts' mean 77% in external set 1, and 78% and 80% vs 36% and 46% in sets 2 and 3.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only five readers.
studies.title: Pretreatment CT Identification of Extranodal Extension in Laryngeal and Hypopharyngeal Cancers Using Deep Learning.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study, unaided then LLM-assisted session randomized at reader-case level
studies.finding: 10 readers interpreted 100 chest imaging cases unaided and then with LLM suggestions; primary outcome was adequate interaction (accepting correct or rejecting incorrect suggestions). Model confidence (OR 3.82) and reader expertise (OR 2.06) were independently associated with adequate interaction. Higher rationale quality increased acceptance of incorrect suggestions (OR 1.71), while expertise (OR 0.54) and reader confidence (OR 0.80) were protective.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, small reader sample, teaching-platform cases.
studies.title: Determinants of Reader-LLM Interaction in Thoracic Radiology: Impact of Model Confidence and Reader Expertise.

studies.design: Comparative structured question-answer study with expert rating
studies.finding: LLMs and 12 clinicians answered 25 guideline-based questions on CVD management in people living with HIV, rated on a 4-point scale. AI mean scores ranged from 3.44 to 3.68, versus 1.78-2.05 for clinicians (P<.001 across all dimensions).
studies.limitation: Small clinician sample, with clinicians answering in interviews rather than in practice; 25 questions only.
studies.title: Comparative Performance of AI Models and Clinicians in Evidence-Based Cardiovascular Disease Management for People Living With HIV: Comparative Study.

studies.design: Source-masked multirater comparative evaluation
studies.finding: The agent and clinicians answered CGM counseling questions, and responses were rated on 6 quality dimensions. The agent scored 4.37 (SD 0.57) versus 3.58 (SD 0.90) for clinicians, a mean difference of 0.782 points on a 5-point scale. Safety flags were similar between the two (0.7% each).
studies.limitation: Vignette-based design with a small clinician panel.
studies.title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Counseling for Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Diabetes: Source-Masked Multirater Comparative Evaluation.

studies.design: Prospective multicentre survey; patients blindly compared paired radiologist-written and AI-simplified breast imaging reports
studies.finding: Patients compared radiologist-written and ChatGPT-4 simplifications of 10 breast imaging reports across 2965 evaluations. AI-generated reports were preferred in 63.3% (1876/2965) of evaluations. High simplicity and comprehensibility scores were more frequent for AI than radiologist reports (70.0% vs 43.4% and 68.1% vs 40.4%).
studies.limitation: Only 10 reports simplified; outcome is patient perception rather than accuracy or clinical impact.
studies.title: Large language model-based simplification of breast imaging reports: a prospective multicentre study with 2965 patient-based evaluations.

studies.design: Vignette-based comparison with specialist evaluation
studies.ai_system: AMIE with web search and self-critique
studies.humans: Internal medicine trainees, oncology fellows and general oncology attendings
studies.finding: Management plans for 60 synthetic breast oncology vignettes. AMIE outperformed trainees and fellows but was overall inferior to attending oncologists.
studies.limitation: Synthetic vignettes and evaluation limited to a few physicians.
studies.title: Exploring Large Language Models for Specialist-Level Oncology Care.

studies.design: Deep learning model development with comparison to ophthalmologists
studies.finding: Pixel-level grading of reticular pseudodrusen on NIR images. ReticularNet mean DSC 0.36 vs ophthalmologists 0.03, 0.13, 0.19 and 0.23 (P ≤ 0.02 each); ICCs also higher.
studies.limitation: Small dataset (117 eyes) and only 4 ophthalmologists.
studies.title: ReticularNet: Automated Pixel-Level Segmentation of Reticular Pseudodrusen on Near-Infrared Reflectance Images by Deep Learning.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development and reader study with and without AI assistance
studies.humans: Five musculoskeletal radiologists and five emergency medicine physicians
studies.finding: For femoral-neck fracture detection on radiographs, model sensitivity for radiograph-negative or indeterminate fractures (94.7%) exceeded radiologists (86.2%) and emergency physicians (68.8%). With AI assistance, sensitivity rose from 93.7% to 97.2% (radiologists) and 84.3% to 95.6% (emergency physicians), and reading times shortened by 14.9% and 18.9%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only 10 readers.
studies.title: Improving Recognition Performance and Reader Efficiency for Femoral-Neck Fracture Detection on Pelvic or Hip Radiographs Using Artificial Intelligence.

studies.design: Retrospective multireader multicase crossover study across three European hospitals
studies.finding: For appendicular fracture detection on radiographs, AI assistance improved overall reader sensitivity by 11 percentage points (95% CI: 6.8, 14.4; P < .001) while maintaining specificity (0.6 percentage points; P = .34). Standalone AI sensitivity ranged from 80% to 86% across hospitals.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study; number and type of readers not stated in abstract.
studies.title: Multinational Validation of a Radiography-Based AI Tool for Appendicular Fracture Detection and Corresponding Reader Performance.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study with simulated reading strategies
studies.finding: TB screening on 1466 chest X-rays compared human-only, CAD-only and CAD-assisted reading. Human-only reading had sensitivity 79.0% and specificity 84.8%; CAD-only had 91.4% and 81.9%; CAD-assisted human reading had non-significant sensitivity gains (82.9%, p=0.057) and reduced specificity (82.2%, p<0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective test library with simulated workflows; single setting.
studies.title: Accuracy and operational performance of computer-aided detection software use cases for TB screening: a retrospective comparative evaluation in Ho Chi Minh City, Viet Nam.

studies.design: Multicohort retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with blinded reader comparison
studies.finding: Predicting brain tumour enhancement from non-contrast MRI, nnU-Net reached a balanced accuracy of 83·0% (sensitivity 91·5%, specificity 74·4%). In 564 matched cases, radiologists' majority-vote balanced accuracy was 71·7% (sensitivity 77·6%, specificity 65·8%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective; novel task radiologists do not normally perform, read blinded to clinical context.
studies.title: Predicting brain tumour enhancement from non-contrast MRI with artificial intelligence: a multicohort, retrospective, diagnostic accuracy study.

studies.design: Two-stage retrospective reader study, AI-assisted vs unaided
studies.finding: Six radiologists reviewed 200 CT scans for kidney cancer detection with and without BMVision. The tool reduced reporting time by an average of 33%, up to 52%, and improved sensitivity for detecting benign renal lesions from 79.9 to 86.3%, with a significant increase in inter-radiologist agreement.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study with only six radiologists; commercial tool developed by authors.
studies.title: A clinically validated AI framework for kidney cancer detection and characterization.

studies.design: Pilot retrospective study on public datasets with dentist reader comparison
studies.finding: For oral mucosal disease classification, the ensemble model reached 94.32% accuracy. When used by general dentists, diagnostic time fell from 241 s to 112.4 s, with an accuracy rate of 93%.
studies.limitation: Pilot study on public datasets; reader numbers and unaided accuracy not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Performance evaluation and clinical application exploration of a ViT-CNN ensemble model for multiclass oral mucosal disease classification: a pilot retrospective analysis based on public datasets.

studies.design: Model development with retrospective workflow audit and 120-WSI reader study
studies.finding: In a 120-WSI reader study, AI assistance was associated with higher inter-observer agreement (kappa 0.847 to 0.967). A workflow audit estimated a 72.7% reduction in turnaround time (72.4 hours to 19.8 hours).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, single-institution, hypothesis-generating estimates; reader count not stated.
studies.title: Explainable hybrid vision transformer-convolutional neural network with cross-attention fusion for multi-institutional breast cancer receptor status prediction from H&E histopathology images.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective development with prospective test set and reader study
studies.finding: For bone tumor risk stratification on radiographs, the model achieved AUC 0.96 in the external set versus 0.68-0.82 for radiologists. With AI assistance, mean reader AUC increased by 0.07 and median reading time decreased by 3 seconds.
studies.limitation: Only 9 readers; the reader study was largely retrospective.
studies.title: Radiograph-based Deep Learning Algorithm for Assisting Bone Tumor Risk Assessment: A Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Model development and evaluation on multicentric dataset
studies.finding: For EGD diagnosis of nineteen GI diseases, MLLM-EDR achieved average accuracy of 0.882, compared with 0.784 for junior endoscopists. Report completeness and facticity matched those of senior endoscopists.
studies.limitation: Model-development paper; the number of endoscopists and the comparison design are not described.
studies.title: Bootstrapping multimodal large language model with medical knowledge for automatic esophagogastroduodenoscopy diagnosis and reporting.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study of endoscopic images with and without AI assistance
studies.ai_system: Deep learning model for ampullary lesion classification
studies.humans: Endoscopy fellows, gastrointestinal endoscopists and pancreatobiliary endoscopists
studies.finding: Endoscopists identified ampullary lesions on endoscopic images with and without AI; the stand-alone AI achieved 84.2% accuracy. With AI assistance mean accuracy improved for fellows (63.5%-75.8%, P < 0.001) and gastrointestinal endoscopists (68.4%-76.5%, P = 0.012), but not for pancreatobiliary endoscopists (70.8%-73.1%, P = 1.000).
studies.limitation: Retrospective proof-of-concept on still images; prospective and video-based validation needed; reader number not stated.
studies.title: AI-assisted improvement of endoscopic diagnosis of ampullary lesions.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre model development with reader studies
studies.ai_system: CRVIA, clinician-centric AI for CT vascular invasion assessment
studies.finding: For CT assessment of pancreatic cancer vascular invasion, CRVIA achieved AUCs of 0.946 internally and 0.943 externally. In reader studies, CRVIA exceeded senior radiologists' accuracy, elevated junior radiologists to expert-level performance, and substantially improved inter-reader agreement.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only eight readers; reader-study numbers not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: A clinician-centric intelligent method towards reliable pancreatic cancer vascular invasion assessment: a retrospective, multi-centre study.
studies.source: The Lancet regional health. Western Pacific

studies.design: Model development with two reader studies and real-world screening deployment
studies.ai_system: BIRD breast ultrasound intelligent recognition device
studies.finding: BIRD classified breast ultrasound lesions with accuracy 0.837 in the internal test set and significantly improved radiologists' accuracy in 2 reader studies (P < 0.05). In screening of 6,817 individuals it showed Cohen's kappa 0.702 with clinical assessments.
studies.limitation: Reader study details, including radiologist numbers and accuracy values, not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: A non-invasive end-to-end intelligent assistance system for breast ultrasound.

studies.design: Multicentre model development with comparison to radiologists
studies.ai_system: MPANet multimodal deep learning on multiphase CT and clinical data
studies.humans: Four radiologists using CT and two using MRI ccLS
studies.finding: For four-class renal tumor classification, MPANet achieved 73.3% accuracy on the internal test set versus 43.6-62.4% for four radiologists on CT and 52.5% and 49.5% for two radiologists using MRI ccLS. Net improvement over radiologists ranged from 10.9% to 29.7%.
studies.limitation: Radiologist comparison only on the internal test set with six readers.
studies.title: Multimodal deep learning model for multiclass classification of renal tumors.

studies.design: Multireader multicase clinical trial (registered ChiCTR2400084624)
studies.finding: Junior radiologists classified benign vs malignant pulmonary nodules on 400 CT cases from three institutions with and without DeepFAN. DeepFAN alone achieved AUC 0.954 (95% CI 0.934-0.973) on the trial dataset; with assistance, reader AUC improved by 10.9% (95% CI 8.3-13.5%), accuracy by 10.0%, sensitivity by 7.6% and specificity by 12.6% (all P < 0.001). Interreader consistency improved (κ 0.313 versus 0.421; P = 0.019).
studies.limitation: Reader study on retrospective images with junior radiologists only; not live clinical care.
studies.title: DeepFAN, a transformer-based model for human-artificial intelligence collaborative assessment of incidental pulmonary nodules in CT scans: a multireader, multicase trial.

studies.design: Model development with multicenter validation and pathologist reader comparison
studies.finding: Histological classification of early pregnancy loss subtypes including hydatidiform moles on whole-slide images. The model reached accuracy 0.801 with AUROC 0.930 in independent testing, and AI-assisted diagnosis significantly improved pathologist performance (p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Abstract gives no reader numbers or effect sizes for the assisted comparison; retrospective slides.
studies.title: Patch-to-slide fusion deep learning model for histological diagnosis of early pregnancy loss including hydatidiform mole.

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective model development and validation
studies.finding: The task was distinguishing primary from metastatic bone lesions on CT. BoneCoT achieved a 40% AUROC improvement and significantly surpassed experienced radiologists.
studies.limitation: The abstract gives few details on the reader comparison, including the number of radiologists and their absolute metrics.
studies.title: BoneCoT: multicentre validation of a whole-body skeleton foundation model for bone metastases guided by clinician-derived chain of thought.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-institution development with external test sets and reader comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep learning models for CECT and NCCT
studies.finding: The task was diagnosing pancreatic cancer on CT. The DL models performed similarly to or better than the reader mean (CECT AUC 0.99 vs 0.99, P = .84; NCCT AUC 0.93 vs 0.91, P = .03). For cancers 20 mm or smaller, model sensitivity was higher (CECT 98% vs 82.6%; NCCT 86% vs 41.1%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only six readers.
studies.title: Deep Learning Detection of Direct and Indirect Imaging Findings Associated with Pancreatic Cancer at Contrast-enhanced and Noncontrast CT.

studies.design: Prospective eye-tracking study, before/with/after AI
studies.finding: Readers interpreted 50 chest radiographs before, with and after AI while gaze was recorded. Viewing patterns were significantly less systematic with and after AI; novices showed increased gaze dissimilarity persisting after AI, whereas experts showed no significant change.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 12 readers; measures gaze behaviour, not diagnostic accuracy.
studies.title: The Impact of AI on Eye Gaze Patterns in Chest X-Ray Interpretation: An Eye Tracking Study of Novice and Expert Radiologists.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective model development with prospective reader study with and without model assistance
studies.finding: Six radiologists classified O-RADS 4 adnexal masses in a prospective validation set with and without hybrid model assistance. Model assistance significantly improved accuracy and specificity across all readers (p < 0.05), with inter-reader agreement improving from kappa 0.49 to 0.73. The model alone had an AUC of 0.88 in the prospective set.
studies.limitation: Small reader study (six radiologists) with prospective set from a single center; reader accuracy numbers not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Development and Multicenter Validation of a Hybrid Radiomics-Deep Learning Model for Risk Stratification of O-RADS 4 Adnexal Masses.

studies.design: Prospective intra-individual reader study with eye tracking; residents read chest radiographs before and after a night shift, post-shift with and without AI
studies.ai_system: AI model for chest radiograph interpretation (not named in abstract)
studies.finding: Ten radiology residents interpreted sets of 33 chest radiographs before and after a night shift; fatigued readers' accuracy fell from κ = 0.71 ± 0.05 to κ = 0.61 ± 0.10 (p < 0.001). AI assistance did not significantly improve diagnostic accuracy (Δκ = 0.03-0.04; p ≥ 0.525), though reporting times were significantly shorter with AI in non-fatigued readers (Δ9.9 s; p = 0.031).
studies.limitation: Very small sample of ten residents reading 33-radiograph sets, single AI model, experimental reading sessions rather than live practice.
studies.title: From dusk till dawn?-Night shift-induced fatigue, diagnostic performance, and AI assistance in chest radiography.

studies.design: Retrospective development with prospective test set
studies.ai_system: Multimodal deep learning fusion model (Model-UT: ResNet50, BERT, ViT)
studies.finding: For differentiating benign from malignant renal tumors on ultrasound, Model-UT yielded an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86-0.97) in the prospective test set, outperforming high-level, mid-level, and low-level radiologists (all p-values < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Single tertiary hospital with a small prospective test set (82 patients); radiologist numbers and results not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Deep learning multimodal fusion model based on ultrasound images and clinical-ultrasound texts for differentiating benign and malignant renal tumors.

studies.design: In vitro study on a colonoscopy training model
studies.finding: Colonoscope insertion on a training model: full automated (Level 4) insertion took 2.92 ± 1.20 minutes versus 1.43 ± 0.32 for the expert and 2.97 ± 1.32 for trainees. The success rate was 86.1%.
studies.limitation: Simplified in vitro model; few operators.
studies.title: In vitro development of the Autonomous Colonoscope Robot System (ACRS) for fully automated colonoscope insertion.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter reader study of compensated missed-fracture claims plus controls; unassisted vs AI-assisted reads after washout, and standalone AI
studies.finding: In 156 patients (26 claimants with missed fractures, 130 controls), standalone AI sensitivity was 80.8% for claimants and 96.3% for the control cohort. AI assistance did not significantly improve sensitivity, with expert reader sensitivity increasing from 81.1% to 92.5% (p = 0.10).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, small claimant sample (26) and only three readers; financial savings are theoretical.
studies.title: AI for reducing claims and compensation payments from missed fractures on radiographs.

studies.design: Multicenter development and external validation of ML model with comparison against clinicians
studies.finding: The model predicted suboptimal clinical response after sleeve gastrectomy with internal AUC 0.821 and external AUC 0.761. The XGB model significantly outperformed 10 clinicians across experience levels and remained superior in challenging cases.
studies.limitation: Clinician performance figures are not reported in the abstract; model-development study with modest external cohorts.
studies.title: Development and Validation of an Interpretable Machine-Learning Model for Predicting Suboptimal Clinical Response After Sleeve Gastrectomy: A Multicenter Study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development with external validation and comparison against radiologists
studies.ai_system: Two-level AI system (EfficientNet-B3 screening, 3D nnU-Net segmentation, fusion network)
studies.finding: For identifying ischemic pneumatosis intestinalis on the internal test set, the model achieved AUC 0.947 (sensitivity 91.3%, specificity 93.6%), significantly outperforming senior radiologists (AUC = 0.876). External validation AUC was 0.931.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; number of radiologists and reader conditions not described; model used clinical metadata.
studies.title: Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study, with vs without multi-LLM assistance
studies.ai_system: Ensemble of GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.6, Llama 4 Maverick on structured reports
studies.finding: Radiologists diagnosed primary bone tumors in 217 test patients with and without multi-LLM suggestions. LLM assistance improved Top-1 accuracy from 57.1% to 72.0% and Top-3 from 81.1% to 90.9% (both adjusted P < 0.001), with larger gains for less experienced readers. Standalone ensemble Top-1 accuracy ranged 56.7% to 62.2%.
studies.limitation: Only three readers, single retrospective dataset; less-experienced readers accepted incorrect suggestions more often.
studies.title: Enhancing Radiologists' Diagnostic Performance for Primary Bone Tumors Using Structured Report-Driven Assistance From Multiple Large Language Models.

studies.design: Reader comparison on test sets of screening mammograms
studies.finding: AI was compared with readers on 540 screening mammograms (179 cancer). AI case-level AUC was 0.974 versus 0.82 ± 0.06 for radiologists and 0.74 ± 0.05 for trainees. At lesion level, sensitivity was 66.3% (AI), 67.0% (radiologists) and 55.0% (trainees).
studies.limitation: Enriched test-set cases rather than real screening workflow.
studies.title: From shadows to signals: exploring the strengths and limitations of artificial intelligence in breast cancer lesion detection on screening mammograms compared to radiologists and radiology trainees.

studies.design: Paired video-based reader study with and without AI plus feasibility deployment
studies.ai_system: U-Net-derived semantic segmentation model for tracheoesophageal fistula identification
studies.finding: In identifying the tracheoesophageal fistula in thoracoscopic video, AI identified it faster than experts and novices (1.05 versus 2.87 and 6.92 s) and achieved higher Dice (0.881) than experts (0.803) and novices (0.780). With AI, novices' median identification time was 263 vs. 390 frames (P < 0.001) and confidence rose, while experts showed no significant time change (186 vs. 172 frames, P = 0.22).
studies.limitation: Small video test set (five cases) from limited cases; real-time deployment only in two operations.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted detection of tracheoesophageal fistula during thoracoscopic esophageal atresia repair: Comparison with pediatric surgeons and real-time clinical deployment.

studies.design: Single-centre retrospective observational study with cross-sectional AI evaluation
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT, ChatGPT Plus, DeepSeek, ESC guideline-based RAG model
studies.finding: Four AI systems assessed consecutive acute heart failure cases and recommendations were compared with physician decisions on diagnosis, treatment, timing and prognosis. ChatGPT Plus achieved the highest HF accuracy (86.5%), followed by RAG (77.5%), ChatGPT (77.0%) and DeepSeek (69.0%); agreement with physicians was highest for guideline-directed therapies and more variable for prognosis and escalation of care.
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective design using physician decisions as reference rather than a head-to-head accuracy comparison; physician numbers not stated.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence versus physician decision-making in acute heart failure: a comparative evaluation of four contemporary AI systems.

studies.design: Cross-sectional exploratory blinded web rating study of five matched plan pairs
studies.ai_system: Constrained AI-assisted meal plan generation pipeline
studies.finding: Dietitians rated, blinded, AI pipeline-generated versus dietitian-designed meal plans. Pipeline-generated plans received a mean rating of 3.67 (SD 0.57) versus 3.11 (SD 0.73) for dietitian-designed plans (d = 0.86), and 32 of 42 eligible pairwise choices selected the pipeline-generated plan.
studies.limitation: Only five plan pairs, anonymous self-selected evaluators with overlapping records, and quality ratings rather than patient outcomes.
studies.title: Blinded professional ratings of artificial intelligence-generated and dietitian-designed meal plans.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-institution report-based reader study with and without LLM assistance, plus standalone model evaluation
studies.ai_system: Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-R1 large language models
studies.finding: Radiologists inferred modified AHA carotid plaque class from free-text MRI reports with and without LLM assistance. Vessel-level agreement improved for junior radiologists from 61.75% to 83.12% (Qwen3-8B) and 87.75% (DeepSeek-R1), and for senior radiologists from 77.00% to 87.50% and 92.25% (all Holm-corrected p < 0.001). Patient-level agreement rose from 41.0% to 78.8% (junior) and 59.8% to 87.8% (senior) with DeepSeek-R1.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, only four radiologists, and reference standard was text-based expert consensus rather than histology or imaging.
studies.title: Large language model assistance for report-based carotid plaque AHA classification: a multi-reader study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional two-level reader study on 100 histologically validated face and scalp lesions
studies.finding: Differentiation of melanocytic from non-melanocytic face and scalp lesions. The CNN reached an accuracy of 79.0% (69.7%-86.5%) and ROC-AUC 0.847; dermatologists reached 66.7% with dermoscopy only and 73.6% with expanded case information, significantly below the CNN (79.0% vs. 73.6%; p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Reader study on curated images rather than live clinical care; dermatologists were not tested with AI support.
studies.title: When to refuse cosmetic treatment - AI-decision support for differentiating melanocytic and non-melanocytic facial lesions.
studies.source: Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft = Journal of the German Society of Dermatology : JDDG

studies.design: Retrospective model development with independent prostatectomy validation cohort compared with radiologist MRI interpretation
studies.ai_system: MRUSuNet (multimodal MRI + TRUS deep learning model)
studies.finding: Detection and localisation of clinically significant prostate cancer on TRUS, validated against whole-mount prostatectomy pathology in 110 patients. Compared with radiologists, MRUSuNet showed higher specificity (0.88 vs 0.78; P = 0.004) and lesion Dice score (0.32 vs 0.27; P = 0.048), with no statistical difference in sensitivity (0.79; P = 1.000).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with a small comparison cohort of 110 patients; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: An artificial intelligence model combining MRI and ultrasound images (MRUSuNet) for prostate cancer detection outperforms radiologist MRI interpretation.

studies.design: Single-centre diagnostic study comparing fully automated, hybrid (expert-reviewed AI) and conventional interpretation
studies.humans: Two expert panels of three EEG readers each
studies.finding: Interpretation of 78 adult long-term EEG recordings. The hybrid approach had higher sensitivity than conventional reading (.88 vs .69; adjusted p = .006), similar accuracy (.75 vs .68, nonsignificant), and markedly shorter review time (median 2.2 vs 52.4 min). Fully automated accuracy was .55, lower than the hybrid approach.
studies.limitation: Small single-centre dataset of 78 recordings, with different reader panels for the hybrid and conventional arms.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted categorization of interictal abnormalities in adult long-term electroencephalographic monitoring: Comparable diagnostic accuracy with marked efficiency gain.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter model development study with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: DR-DLR dual-region deep learning radiomics model
studies.finding: Preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in gastric cancer on CT. The model achieved AUCs of 0.898, 0.834 and 0.848 in the internal and two external test cohorts, and the abstract reports that it outperformed junior and senior radiologists; radiologist figures are not given.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; radiologist performance numbers and reader count are not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Incorporating visceral adipose tissue into dual-region deep learning radiomics on CT improves preoperative lymph node metastasis prediction in gastric cancer: A multicenter study.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on 33 challenging ECGs, angiography as gold standard
studies.finding: Detection of occlusion MI on diagnostically challenging ECGs against coronary angiography. Cardiologists had sensitivities of 62%, 85%, and 62%, specificities of 70%, 50%, and 55%, and misclassification rates of 33%, 36%, and 42%. The AI had sensitivity and NPV of 100%, specificity of 60%, PPV of 62%, and a misclassification rate of 24%.
studies.limitation: Very small retrospective sample (33 ECGs, 3 readers).
studies.title: Human vs Artificial Intelligence in Detecting Coronary Occlusions in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Retrospective Study.

studies.design: Retrospective records with 5x5 Latin square crossover
studies.finding: Junior physicians made preoperative arthroplasty risk-assessment decisions with and without model assistance. DeepSeek-R1 + KB assistance significantly improved decisions over independent decision-making (OR = 1.58, p = 0.004).
studies.limitation: Retrospective records, and the number of physicians is not stated.
studies.title: Evaluation of DeepSeek with a RAG-based knowledge base in preoperative assessment for arthroplasty to improve the decision-making accuracy of junior physicians.

studies.design: Retrospective two-centre development and validation study with comparison against senior radiologists
studies.finding: Task was automated phenotyping of HCC pathological gross classification from gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI in 551 patients. The model achieved a micro-averaged AUC of 0.932, significantly outperforming senior radiologists (AUC 0.825), with about 40-fold improved efficiency.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with a small external test set (n=68); number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Preoperative 3D morphological phenotyping of hepatocellular carcinoma via a foundation model: a non-invasive biomarker for recurrence risk stratification.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre development with external test set against DSA, compared with radiologists of varying experience
studies.ai_system: SAM-guided multi-view decoding network for TOF-MRA aneurysm segmentation
studies.finding: Task was intracranial aneurysm detection on TOF-MRA. The model achieved an overall detection F1-score of 86.7, significantly outperforming junior radiologists (P <.001) and comparable to mid-level radiologists (P >.05). External sensitivity was 83.4%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design; number of radiologists and their scores not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Automatic 3D TOF-MRA Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation using SAM-Guided Multi-View Decoding Network.
studies.source: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of vision-language models vs radiologist consensus pairs on axillary lymph node ultrasound images
studies.ai_system: GPT-5.2, Gemini 3.0 Pro, Claude Opus 4.5 (image-only input)
studies.humans: 2 inexperienced radiologists and 2 experienced breast imaging radiologists (consensus per pair)
studies.finding: In 718 biopsied axillary nodes, accuracy was 76% for inexperienced radiologists, 83% for experienced radiologists, 78% for GPT-5.2, 73% for Gemini 3.0 Pro and 67% for Claude Opus 4.5. Experienced radiologists had significantly higher accuracy than all three models; GPT-5.2 did not differ significantly in accuracy from inexperienced radiologists.
studies.limitation: Single biopsied node image per patient, consensus reads by only four radiologists, retrospective design.
studies.title: Vision-Language Models for Ultrasound Assessment of Suspicious Axillary Lymph Nodes in Breast Cancer.

studies.design: Single-centre retrospective reader study
studies.finding: Readers scored 50 calf carpal radiographs for septic arthritis against expert consensus. Novice 1 had mean κw 0.68 and exact agreement 55.6%; best model ChatGPT-5 had κw 0.58 and exact agreement 53.0%, while Claude and Gemini showed slight agreement. The best novice remained more reliable than the models.
studies.limitation: Veterinary setting, only two novice readers and 50 cases at a single centre.
studies.title: Agreement of Multimodal Large Language Models and Novice Readers With Expert-Based Radiographic Scoring of Presumptive Septic Carpal Arthritis in Calves.
studies.source: Veterinary radiology & ultrasound : the official journal of the American College of Veterinary Radiology and the International Veterinary Radiology Association

studies.design: Retrospective reader study with and without AI
studies.humans: 3 otology professors, 5 senior residents, 5 junior residents
studies.finding: Clinicians diagnosed middle ear disease on 100 otoendoscopic images with and without AI. Accuracy rose from 78.7% to 89.7% for professors, 65.0% to 93.8% for senior residents and 54.4% to 86.6% for junior residents (P <.001). Stand-alone AI accuracy was 94.0% to 99.0%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, 100 images, small reader groups under time-constrained simulated conditions.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Diagnosis of Middle Ear Diseases in Otoendoscopy Across Clinician Experience Levels: Retrospective Reader Study.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with external validation compared against radiologists
studies.ai_system: T1-weighted MRI radiomics support vector machine
studies.finding: For differentiating myxoid liposarcoma from myxoma in a 32-patient external cohort, the T1-weighted SVM achieved accuracy 0.84 and AUC 0.91. Its performance did not differ significantly from radiologists (AUC, 0.88-0.94; p > 0.05), though fluid-sensitive SVM was weak (AUC, 0.60).
studies.limitation: Small external cohort (32 patients), only two radiologists, and not powered for equivalence.
studies.title: Externally validated MRI radiomics machine learning models for differentiating between myxoid liposarcoma and myxoma.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre model development with external reader comparison and AI-assisted reading
studies.humans: Radiologists, junior orthopaedists and expert orthopaedists
studies.finding: For staging osteonecrosis of the femoral head on hip x-rays (external set I), the model's accuracy was 96·60%, higher than radiologists (74·96%) and junior orthopaedists (83·98%) and similar to expert orthopaedists (96·54%; p=0·20). Model assistance improved accuracy of junior orthopaedists by 12·70% and radiologists by 21·47%, with a non-significant 0·74% gain for experts and reduced diagnostic time across groups.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader comparison on Chinese hospital datasets; number of clinicians not stated in abstract.
studies.title: A deep learning model for detection and staging of osteonecrosis of the femoral head on x-ray images: a retrospective, large-scale, multicentre study in China.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to human raters on test set
studies.finding: Classifying breast reconstruction aesthetics from photographs, the algorithm achieved overall accuracy of 60.6%. Mean accuracy was 78.9% for plastic surgeons, 60.2% for nurses, and 59.3% for laypersons.
studies.limitation: Small single test set (99 images) with subjective reference labels; rater numbers not stated.
studies.title: Automated Aesthetic Evaluation After Breast Reconstruction Using Routine Postoperative Photographs: A No-Code AutoML Approach.

studies.design: Multicenter model development with retrospective, external and prospective validation plus a pathologist user study
studies.ai_system: DeepLNM multimodal foundation model (WSI, CT, text)
studies.finding: Prediction of lymph node metastasis in colorectal cancer. In a user study, DeepLNM improved pathologists' diagnostic accuracy, especially for junior pathologists (95.0%-97.3%), while reducing diagnostic time and increasing confidence.
studies.limitation: User study is a minor component of a model-development paper; number of pathologists and unaided baseline figures not clearly reported in the abstract.
studies.title: DeepLNM: A Multimodal Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Colorectal Cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre multi-reader study with sequential unaided and aided sessions separated by a 4-week washout
studies.ai_system: Deep-learning computer-aided diagnostic tool for contrast-enhanced mammography
studies.finding: Five radiologists read 150 contrast-enhanced mammography examinations without and then with the tool. The mean area under the free-response curve increased by 0.030 ± 0.018 at lesion level, and false positives at 89% sensitivity decreased by an average of 11.4% ± 24%. No improvement was observed at breast level.
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective design with only five readers and a fixed reading order (unaided first).
studies.title: Retrospective multi-reader evaluation of a Deep-Learning-based cancer detection model in Contrast-Enhanced Mammography.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentric development and validation study
studies.ai_system: Deep learning system for automated medial open wedge high tibial osteotomy planning
studies.finding: Osteotomy planning on long-leg radiographs. Clinically acceptable accuracy was 72% to 100% for humans versus 91% to 100% for the DL model on alignment parameters. The model outperformed surgeons in intrarater reliability (0.88 vs. 1.0) and processing time (25.3 ± 0.8 s vs. 148.7 ± 10.1 s, p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only three surgeon comparators.
studies.title: Multicentric development and validation of a fully automated artificial intelligence system for planning medial open wedge high tibial osteotomy on weight-bearing anterior-posterior long leg radiographs: The ISAKOS John Joyce Award 2025.
studies.source: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA

studies.design: Validation study comparing automated plaque coverage with clinical plaque scoring
studies.finding: Plaque grading of 438 teeth in 20 adults against the T-QHPI. After calibration, weighted κ for the model was 0.812 (0.766 to 0.844), compared with 0.791 (0.710 to 0.853) between two examiners.
studies.limitation: Very small sample of 20 participants with no external validation.
studies.title: A deep-learning system for dental plaque quantification from disclosed intraoral photographs, validation against clinical plaque scoring.

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic study comparing dermatologists with and without AI guidance across two sessions
studies.ai_system: AI-assisted 3D reconstruction and segmentation system for facial vitiligo
studies.finding: Quantification of facial vitiligo lesions in photographs from 329 patients. AI assistance reduced mean absolute error in lesion quantification (3.13 vs. 6.71) compared with manual assessment alone, and raised correlation with reference lesion areas (r = 0.92 vs. 0.84).
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective study; number of dermatologists not stated.
studies.title: Objective and quantitative assessment of facial vitiligo via artificial intelligence-powered three-dimensional analysis for diagnostic support.

studies.design: Retrospective multireader multicase study
studies.finding: Readers detected large-vessel occlusion on source images alone versus source images plus RescueCTA-generated vascular images. MRMC AUC improved from 0.850 to 0.933 (ΔAUC = 0.083, p = 0.007). Strict AUC improved from 0.756 to 0.880 (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: The primary cohort used simulated underopacification, and only four readers took part.
studies.title: Generative enhancement of suboptimally opacified cerebral CT angiography for large-vessel occlusion detection: a multireader study.

studies.design: Retrospective two-center study with exploratory reader analysis
studies.finding: Junior radiologists differentiated endometrial stromal sarcoma from cellular leiomyoma on MRI with and without model assistance. With assistance, specificity increased from 46.4 to 82.1% and accuracy from 52.3 to 77.3%.
studies.limitation: Exploratory reader analysis on a small cohort, with the number of readers not stated.
studies.title: Development and External Testing of an Interpretable MRI-Based Machine Learning Model for Differentiating Endometrial Stromal Sarcoma from Cellular Leiomyoma.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Multi-reader multi-case study in 3 phases
studies.ai_system: Deep learning GBM survival model with XAI heatmaps
studies.finding: Experts predicted glioblastoma survival from MRI with and without AI assistance. AI assistance significantly improved expert accuracy (OR 1.598, p < 0.01) without boosting confidence (p = 0.561). Heatmaps changed how experts used the AI score.
studies.limitation: Only 37 patients and 4 readers.
studies.title: Explainability and Clinical Trust of Deep Learning in Glioblastoma Treatment Efficacy Prediction: A Comprehensive Framework.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter reader study
studies.finding: Radiologists interpreted screening mammograms unaided, AI-assisted, and under several AI-integration scenarios. Aggregated reader AUC improved from 83.04% unaided to 88.40% in the union scenario (p < 0.001). Sensitivity rose from 54.8% to 83.9% and specificity from 83.6% to 91.1%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design, and the number of readers is not stated.
studies.title: Optimizing AI-assisted decision-making in mammography screening: focusing on uncertainties.

studies.design: Comparative reader study on 160 radiographs
studies.finding: Readers judged whether chest radiographs were real or AI-generated. Gemini 3.5 Flash had a balanced accuracy of 77.9% and the best radiologist 75.8%, a paired difference of -2.1 percentage points (95% CI, -5.8 to 1.2). Nonradiologists performed near chance.
studies.limitation: Only 4 human readers, and LLM judgments were not reproducible.
studies.title: Complementary Error Profiles of Human Readers and Large Language Models in Detecting AI-Generated Chest Radiographs: A Comparative Reader Study.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Retrospective two-centre model development with reader study with and without AI assistance
studies.ai_system: Multimodal Swin Transformer model combining carotid ultrasound deep learning, radiomic and clinical features
studies.finding: Task was predicting acute ischemic stroke risk in T2DM patients from carotid ultrasound. With AI assistance reader AUCs increased from 0.760 to 0.857 and from 0.868 to 0.929 for senior readers, and from 0.450 to 0.700 and from 0.548 to 0.659 for junior readers. Diagnostic correctness improved significantly for senior (P=0.00235) and junior (P=0.000343) readers.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with small external cohort (n=86) and apparently only a few readers.
studies.title: Multimodal Carotid Ultrasound-based Artificial Intelligence Model for Predicting Acute Ischemic Stroke Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

studies.design: In vitro study comparing AI-based vs manual surgical guide planning
studies.humans: Manual planning by clinician(s); single experienced clinician performed surgeries
studies.finding: Mean absolute deviation from ideal resection length was 0.031 ± 0.030 mm with AI vs 0.341 ± 0.234 mm manual, and from ideal angle 4.06 ± 2.27° vs 9.95 ± 4.24° (p < 0.001). Planning time was 98.48 ± 33.91 s vs 157.8 ± 22.45 s.
studies.limitation: In vitro model study on 24 teeth with a single clinician; number of manual planners unclear.
studies.title: An In vitro study on the application of artificial intelligence in trephination pathway planning for endodontic microsurgery: a key step in digital guide design.

studies.design: Quality improvement pilot with before-after surveys and EHR metrics
studies.humans: Clinicians in primary care and specialties
studies.finding: The study compared clinicians' time in notes and workload before and after implementing ambient AI. Mean time in notes per appointment fell from 6.2 to 5.3 minutes (P < .001), NASA-TLX mental demand fell from 12.2 to 6.3, and burnout fell from 42.1% to 35.1% (P = .12, not significant).
studies.limitation: Uncontrolled before-after pilot with a purposive sample and survey-based outcomes.
studies.title: Evaluation of an Ambient Artificial Intelligence Documentation Platform for Clinicians.

studies.design: Randomized waiting-list quality improvement study
studies.ai_system: GenAI-drafted patient message replies in EHR
studies.finding: GenAI drafts were associated with a 21.8% increase in read time (95% CI, 5.2% to 41.0%), a -5.9% change in reply time (95% CI, -16.6% to 6.2%; P = .33), and a 17.9% increase in reply length. The hypothesized time savings were not observed.
studies.limitation: Single academic health system, short follow-up, QI design measuring efficiency not quality.
studies.title: AI-Generated Draft Replies Integrated Into Health Records and Physicians' Electronic Communication.

studies.design: Prospective quality improvement before-after study
studies.finding: The study measured documentation time from EHR use data after physicians began using an ambient AI scribe. Median time per note fell by 0.57 minutes, and daily documentation, after-hours and total EHR time fell by 6.89, 5.17 and 19.95 minutes/day respectively.
studies.limitation: Uncontrolled pilot at a single centre measuring time only, not documentation quality.
studies.title: Ambient artificial intelligence scribes: utilization and impact on documentation time.
studies.source: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial, three arms (PreA-only, PreA-human, No-PreA)
studies.ai_system: PreA LLM chatbot for pre-consultation history-taking and referral reports
studies.finding: Patients were randomised to use an LLM pre-assessment chatbot or not before specialist consultation. Consultation duration was 3.14 ± 2.25 min with PreA-only vs 4.41 ± 2.77 min without (28.7% reduction; P < 0.001), and physician-perceived care coordination scored 3.69 ± 0.90 versus 1.73 ± 0.95 (P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Outcomes are efficiency and perceived coordination rather than diagnostic accuracy or patient health outcomes; resource-limited setting in two centres.
studies.title: An LLM chatbot to facilitate primary-to-specialist care transitions: a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Randomized quality improvement study at a single tertiary academic center
studies.ai_system: LLM-generated plain language summaries added to ophthalmology notes
studies.humans: Nonophthalmology clinicians and professionals; ophthalmologists reviewing summaries
studies.finding: Nonophthalmology clinicians reading notes with an LLM plain language summary reported enhanced diagnostic understanding (percentage point increase, 9.0; 95% CI, 0.3-18.2), note detail satisfaction (21.5) and explanation clarity (23.0) versus standard notes. PLS error rate on ophthalmologist review was 26% (126 of 489), mostly low risk.
studies.limitation: Outcomes are self-reported survey responses with a 33.0% response rate, single centre.
studies.title: Evaluation of AI Summaries on Interdisciplinary Understanding of Ophthalmology Notes.

studies.design: Single-center RCT of nurse-LLM collaboration vs nurses alone at outpatient reception
studies.finding: In an RCT of 2,164 participants, nurse-SSPEC collaboration achieved higher patient satisfaction (3.91 ± 0.90 vs 3.39 ± 1.15, P < 0.001) and fewer repeated Q&R (3.2% vs 14.4%). Response empathy was 4.14 ± 0.98 vs 3.27 ± 1.22.
studies.limitation: Single center; nurses performing reception rather than physicians.
studies.title: Outpatient reception via collaboration between nurses and a large language model: a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Cross-sectional blinded evaluation
studies.humans: Physicians who wrote discharge summaries; 22 attending reviewers
studies.finding: Across 100 inpatient encounters, LLM and physician discharge narratives had comparable overall quality (mean 3.67 vs 3.77; P = .21). LLM narratives were more concise and coherent but less comprehensive (3.72 vs 4.13), had more errors per summary (2.91 vs 1.82) and higher overall harm scores (0.84 vs 0.36; P < .001).
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective records; no evaluation of real-world use after review.
studies.title: Physician- and Large Language Model-Generated Hospital Discharge Summaries.

studies.design: Model adaptation study with blinded clinical reader study
studies.humans: Medical experts writing summaries; 10 physician readers
studies.finding: Physicians compared LLM summaries with medical experts' summaries across four clinical summarization tasks for completeness, correctness and conciseness. Summaries from the best-adapted LLMs were deemed equivalent (45%) or superior (36%) to the experts' summaries.
studies.limitation: Small reader study of 10 physicians, embedded in a model-development paper.
studies.title: Adapted large language models can outperform medical experts in clinical text summarization.

studies.design: Prospective cohort study in a tertiary academic health system
studies.ai_system: Workflow-integrated generative model drafting radiograph reports
studies.finding: For 23 960 radiographs, model-assisted interpretations were faster (mean 159.8 s) than without the model (189.2 s) (P = .02), a 15.5% efficiency increase. Peer review of 800 studies showed no difference in clinical accuracy (P = .41) or textual quality (P = .06).
studies.limitation: Non-randomised, single health system, matched baseline comparison; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Efficiency and Quality of Generative AI-Assisted Radiograph Reporting.

studies.design: Single-blind randomised controlled pilot trial
studies.finding: Informed consent for total knee arthroplasty with physicians using ChatGPT versus traditional surgeon-led consent in 60 patients (55 completed). Anxiety after consent was lower in the ChatGPT group (HADS-A: 10.48 ± 3.84 vs 12.75 ± 4.12, P = .04) and satisfaction with preoperative education was higher (4.22 ± 0.51 vs 3.43 ± 0.84, P <.001). No differences in depression, knee function or pain.
studies.limitation: Small single-centre pilot; patient-reported outcomes; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: ChatGPT's role in alleviating anxiety in total knee arthroplasty consent process: a randomized controlled trial pilot study.

studies.design: Randomized crossover trial
studies.finding: For preoperative consultation documentation, PEACH did not significantly reduce overall documentation time. Subgroups showed time savings for moderate-complexity patients (5.77 min, p = 0.010) and experienced physicians (4.6 min, p = 0.040). Evaluators preferred PEACH-assisted documentation in 57.1% of cases.
studies.limitation: Single-center trial; number of residents not stated in the abstract.
studies.title: Clinical and economic impact of a large language model in perioperative medicine: a randomized crossover trial.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study with inserted errors
studies.finding: GPT-4 detected 82.7% of 150 inserted report errors vs 89.3% for senior radiologists, 80.0% for attendings and 80.0% for residents (P .522-.99). GPT-4 took 3.5 seconds per report vs 25.1 seconds for the fastest reader.
studies.limitation: Artificially inserted errors, single institution, six readers.
studies.title: Potential of GPT-4 for Detecting Errors in Radiology Reports: Implications for Reporting Accuracy.

studies.design: Randomized quality improvement trial with difference-in-differences
studies.finding: KLAS Net EHR Experience improved from 52.6 to 75.2 among intervention providers but dropped from 37.3 to 30 in controls; burnout dropped from 8 (89%) to 5 (56%). There was no significant change in pajama time (-9.4 minutes per scheduled day) or time in notes per encounter.
studies.limitation: Very small sample with incomplete survey response.
studies.title: The Influence of Artificial Intelligence Scribes on Clinician Experience and Efficiency among Pediatric Subspecialists: A Rapid, Randomized Quality Improvement Trial.

studies.design: Blinded randomized controlled study comparing typing, dictation and ChatGPT for documenting HPI of standardized patients
studies.humans: Medical students, orthopaedic surgery residents and attending surgeons
studies.finding: Participants documented history of present illness for standardized patients using typing, dictation or ChatGPT. ChatGPT was intermediate for speed (dictation fastest) but produced markedly longer and higher quality histories by Physician Documentation Quality Instrument score than dictation and typing. However, ChatGPT included erroneous information in 36% of the documents.
studies.limitation: Very small sample (11 participants) with standardized patients and poor inter-reviewer agreement on quality.
studies.title: ChatGPT's Ability to Assist with Clinical Documentation: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
studies.source: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons

studies.design: Randomized sequential prospective validation; comparative effectiveness study
studies.ai_system: Fine-tuned LLM assistant for ED discharge notes
studies.finding: Six emergency physicians wrote discharge notes manually and then by editing LLM drafts. LLM-assisted notes scored higher on completeness (4.23 vs 4.03), correctness (4.38 vs 4.20), conciseness (4.23 vs 4.11) and clinical utility (4.17 vs 3.85). Median documentation time dropped from 69.5 to 32.0 seconds.
studies.limitation: Single centre with only 6 physicians; fixed session order with a 1-hour washout.
studies.title: Large Language Model Assistant for Emergency Department Discharge Documentation.

studies.design: Randomised stepped-wedge trial of ambient clinical intelligence
studies.finding: Providers were randomised to start using ambient clinical intelligence early or late, and documentation time was measured from medical records metadata alongside monthly burden and burnout measures. ACI significantly reduced documentation burden, frustration and burnout, with 2.5 h less per week of off-hours documentation.
studies.limitation: Outcomes were documentation time and burnout rather than note quality or patient outcomes; the number of providers is not stated in the abstract.
studies.title: Deploying ambient clinical intelligence to improve care: A research article assessing the impact of nuance DAX on documentation burden and burnout.

studies.design: Retrospective cohort comparing LLM vs physician-written handoff notes
studies.humans: EM physicians' written notes; 3 board-certified EM physician raters
studies.finding: EM-to-inpatient handoff notes. LLM notes scored higher on automated metrics (ROUGE 0.322 vs 0.088) but in a 50-summary subsample rated by physicians, usefulness was 4.04 vs 4.36 and patient safety 4.06 vs 4.50 for physician-written notes.
studies.limitation: Single centre; physician rating on only 50 summaries by 3 reviewers.
studies.title: Developing and Evaluating Large Language Model-Generated Emergency Medicine Handoff Notes.

studies.design: Prospective observational cohort of LLM draft replies to patient messages
studies.ai_system: LLM-generated draft replies in the EHR
studies.finding: Across 919 patient messages, physicians used the LLM draft in 58% of replies. Total response time did not differ significantly between blank replies and drafted replies with ≥10% match (157 vs. 153 s, p = 0.69).
studies.limitation: Observational design with self-selected use; outcome is time, not reply quality.
studies.title: AI-generated draft replies to patient messages: exploring effects of implementation.

studies.design: Single-blinded randomized online assessment
studies.humans: 32 Young Academic Urologists rating materials vs original expert-written PEMs
studies.finding: GPT-4-generated patient education materials were compared with original guideline PEMs. Readability was better for GPT-4 (Mean FKRE: 43.5 vs. 70.8; p < .001), with no significant difference in accuracy, completeness and clarity.
studies.limitation: Small set of 8 materials; comparator is existing materials, not clinicians writing in-study.
studies.title: GPT-4 generates accurate and readable patient education materials aligned with current oncological guidelines: A randomized assessment.

studies.design: Crossover randomized controlled trial, web-based
studies.humans: Clinical coders (junior doctors or medical secretaries)
studies.finding: ICD clinical coding of notes with vs without the tool. Median coding time for longer notes fell by 123 seconds (46% reduction, P<.001) but not for shorter notes; accuracy improved (62% vs 67%; 60% vs 70%) without statistical significance.
studies.limitation: Very small sample (15 analysed participants), web-based not in real workflow.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence to Improve Clinical Coding Practice in Scandinavia: Crossover Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Retrospective study of 180 CT reports; surgeons reviewed original and AI-generated reports
studies.finding: Categorising pancreatic cancer resectability from CT reports. Surgeons were more accurate using AI-generated reports than original reports (83% vs 76%, P = .03), while spending less time on each report (58%; 95% CI: 0.53, 0.62).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-centre study; the number of surgeons is not stated.
studies.title: Large Language Models for Automated Synoptic Reports and Resectability Categorization in Pancreatic Cancer.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of LLM-generated vs original physician requisition histories with radiologist pairwise review
studies.humans: Ordering physicians' original requisition histories; rated by 10 radiologists
studies.finding: For 200 patients, LLM-generated histories more often included primary oncologic diagnosis (99.5% vs 89%), acute or worsening symptoms (15% vs 4%) and relevant surgery (61% vs 12%) than original requisitions. Radiologists preferred LLM histories (89% vs 5%, 7% equal) and rated lower likelihood of harm (3% vs 55%).
studies.limitation: Single cancer centre, retrospective; original requisitions not written for comparison; subjective radiologist preference.
studies.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Generate Clinical Histories for Oncologic Imaging Requisitions.

studies.design: Randomized multireader multicase crossover study
studies.finding: EGD report generation with versus without AI-EARS across 44 procedures. With AI, completeness of textual description was 79.03% vs 51.86% and accuracy was 64.47% vs 42.81% (P < .001), and landmark photo-documentation completeness was 92.23% vs 73.69%. Reporting time per lesion was 80.13 ± 16.12 seconds vs 46.47 ± 11.68 seconds after AI assistance.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 12 endoscopists and 44 procedures, all in China.
studies.title: Effect of a deep learning-based automatic upper GI endoscopic reporting system: a randomized crossover study (with video).

studies.design: Prospective observational study with masked comparison of encounters with and without DAX
studies.ai_system: DAX ambient voice recognition with NLP/AI
studies.finding: In 304 primary care patients in the masked phase, total PDRQ-9 score did not differ between encounters using DAX (median 45, IQR 8) and those without (median 45, IQR 3.5; p = 0.31). The adjusted odds ratio for complete satisfaction with clinician listening was 0.8 (95% CI 0.48-1.34).
studies.limitation: Observational, non-randomized design; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Effect of Ambient Voice Technology, Natural Language Processing, and Artificial Intelligence on the Patient-Physician Relationship.

studies.design: Quality improvement study with blinded editing and A/B evaluation
studies.humans: 10 internal medicine residents (editors), 8 hospitalists (evaluators); physician-written hospital courses
studies.finding: Residents edited LLM- and physician-written hospital course summaries for 100 admissions. Residents edited a smaller percentage of LLM summaries (31.5% vs 44.8%; P < .001), and LLM summaries were rated more complete but contained more confabulations (-0.98; P = .002). Composite scores were similar (1.70; P = .46).
studies.limitation: Single-center convenience sample with artificial time constraints.
studies.title: Evaluating Hospital Course Summarization by an Electronic Health Record-Based Large Language Model.

studies.design: Prospective randomised comparison of chatbot vs physician pre-CT consultation
studies.finding: In 86 patients before CT, information clarity (PIA 8.64 ± 1.69 vs control 8.86 ± 1.28; p = 0.82) and comprehension (8.81 ± 1.40 vs 8.93 ± 1.61; p = 0.35) were similar. Doctors were better at alleviating concerns (8.30 ± 2.63 versus 6.46 ± 3.29; p = 0.003).
studies.limitation: Small single-setting sample with patient-reported outcomes only.
studies.title: Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation-Powered Chatbot for Pre-CT Informed Consent: a Prospective Comparative Study.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Retrospective reader comparison on public dataset reports with applied errors
studies.finding: For detecting errors in head CT reports, human readers had worse factual error detection sensitivity than GPT-4 (0.33-0.69 vs 0.89) and took longer to review (82-121 seconds vs 16 seconds). GPT-4 had low positive predictive value of 0.05 on 10 000 unaltered reports.
studies.limitation: Errors artificially inserted; single public dataset; number of readers not stated in abstract.
studies.title: Large-Scale Validation of the Feasibility of GPT-4 as a Proofreading Tool for Head CT Reports.

studies.design: Single-center randomized controlled trial, 200 patients
studies.finding: For EDX/EMG report quality measured by the AIGERS score, physician-AI interpretation was compared with physician-only interpretation. AIGERS scores were nearly the same in both arms and did not reach statistical significance (p > 0.05 for all comparisons).
studies.limitation: Single center with only three physicians; outcome uses a newly developed, unvalidated score.
studies.title: AI-Based EMG Reporting: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Retrospective matched case-control cohort of primary care notes
studies.finding: Primary care annual visit notes (20 302) with AI ambient scribes were compared with human-scribed, unscribed and pre-deployment notes. AI-scribed notes had significantly greater documented neuropsychiatric symptom levels in all 6 RDoC domains, but lower likelihood of psychiatric intervention vs contemporaneous unscribed visits (adjusted odds ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.72-0.95).
studies.limitation: Retrospective observational design; associations may be confounded and patient outcomes were not assessed.
