studies.title: Psychiatric Documentation and Management in Primary Care With Artificial Intelligence Scribe Use.

studies.design: Three-arm pragmatic randomised clinical trial
studies.ai_system: Ambient AI scribes Microsoft DAX and Nabla
studies.finding: Outpatient documentation. Nabla users had a 9.5% decrease in time-in-note versus control (p=.02), while DAX showed no significant change (-1.7%; p=.66). Any scribe improved Mini-Z (+2.76), task load (-35.8) and work exhaustion (-0.27).
studies.limitation: Preprint, not peer reviewed; single health system, two-month exposure, low usage rates.
studies.title: A Randomized-Clinical Trial of Two Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribes: Measuring Documentation Efficiency and Physician Burnout.
studies.source: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

studies.design: Prospective within-clinician time-motion study
studies.finding: Documentation time and engagement in 169 outpatient consultations with vs without ambient scribe. Documentation time fell 15.0% (mean 5.3 to 4.5 minutes; P=.04) and eye contact proportion rose from 69.6% to 77.1% (P=.009), with no significant change in consultation duration.
studies.limitation: Only nine clinicians at a single centre, non-randomised.
studies.title: Impact of an Ambient AI Scribe Among Clinicians and Patients: Real-World Prospective Observational Time-Motion Study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional blinded survey comparing GPT-generated and real provider portal message responses
studies.humans: Primary care physicians and advanced practice providers (49 raters)
studies.finding: Providers rated GPT-generated versus real doctor responses to patient portal messages for empathy, relevance, accuracy and readability (0-5). GPT responses scored significantly higher for empathy (p < 0.05) and readability (p < 0.05), with no significant difference in relevance and accuracy (p > 0.05).
studies.limitation: Survey of ratings with 59% completion rate; not in real workflows and no patient evaluation.
studies.title: Automating Responses to Patient Portal Messages Using Generative AI.

studies.design: Blinded paired comparison of 97 encounters rated with modified PDQI-9
studies.finding: Gold physician notes scored higher overall (4.25/5 vs. 4.20/5, p = 0.04) and on accuracy, succinctness and internal consistency, while ambient notes were more thorough and organized. Hallucinations were found in 20% of gold vs 31% of ambient notes (p = 0.01).
studies.limitation: Notes generated from audio recordings rather than live care; physician number not stated.
studies.title: Assessing the quality of AI-generated clinical notes: validated evaluation of a large language model ambient scribe.

studies.design: Retrospective study with staggered rollout, GEE analysis
studies.ai_system: Hybrid ambient clinical documentation (LLM draft notes plus virtual scribe)
studies.humans: 181 primary care attending physicians and advanced practice clinicians (66 enrolled)
studies.finding: Work outside of work, documentation delay and wRVUs over 50 days after adopting hybrid ambient documentation versus baseline. WOW initially increased by 32.1% on day 10 but decreased by 41.7% by day 50; odds of delayed note closure fell by 66.0% at day 50; financial productivity increased 12.1% by day 50.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, voluntary enrolment (selection bias), single health system, short follow-up.
studies.title: Hybrid Ambient Clinical Documentation and Physician Performance: Work Outside of Work, Documentation Delay, and Financial Productivity.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of responses to patient questions
studies.finding: Responses to IBD patient questions were compared. ChatGPT was preferred in 48.4% of 1578 binary assessments; overall quality was 3.98 for ChatGPT vs 3.95 for specialists (P=.34), with ChatGPT more complete but inferior in one section (P=.006).
studies.limitation: Subjective ratings; number of specialists and evaluators not stated.
studies.title: Ability of ChatGPT to Replace Doctors in Patient Education: Cross-Sectional Comparative Analysis of Inflammatory Bowel Disease.

studies.design: Model development with retrospective internal/external and prospective man-machine comparison
studies.ai_system: EUS-AIRS deep learning image report system
studies.finding: Completeness of capturing biliopancreatic standard stations during EUS photodocumentation. EUS-AIRS exceeded endoscopists in internal testing (90.8% vs 70.5%; P < .001) and external testing (91.4% vs 68.2%; P < .001), and outperformed manual reports prospectively (91.4% vs 78.1%; P < .001).
studies.limitation: Single-centre prospective test with 114 patients; number of endoscopists not stated.
studies.title: A deep learning-based, real-time image report system for linear EUS.

studies.design: Feasibility randomised controlled noninferiority trial
studies.ai_system: AI chatbot integrated with a digital avatar ("digital clinician")
studies.humans: Nursing staff delivering conventional semaglutide education
studies.finding: Patient education for semaglutide self-injection, comparing the AI avatar with conventional education from nursing staff in 43 patients (27 intervention, 16 control). Post-consultation knowledge was higher with the digital clinician (median 10, IQR 10-11 vs median 8, IQR 7-9.3; P<.001). The nurse-educated group was more satisfied (median 7, IQR 6-7 vs median 7, IQR 7-7; P<.001) and had more trust (median 7, IQR 4.8-7 vs median 7, IQR 7-7; P<.001), with no difference in self-efficacy (P=.57).
studies.limitation: Small, unbalanced feasibility trial at a single national centre, and the comparators are nurses rather than physicians.
studies.title: "Digital Clinicians" Performing Obesity Medication Self-Injection Education: Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Model development and evaluation on 120 questions comparing EyeGPT, unassisted ophthalmologists, and EyeGPT+human
studies.finding: Answering patient inquiries and educational questions in ophthalmology, rated for accuracy, understandability, trustworthiness and empathy. EyeGPT showed competitive understandability and empathy compared with human ophthalmologists, and ophthalmologist performance was notably enhanced with EyeGPT assistance; no numbers are reported for the human comparisons.
studies.limitation: Human comparison results are not quantified in the abstract; small question set and few evaluators.
studies.title: EyeGPT for Patient Inquiries and Medical Education: Development and Validation of an Ophthalmology Large Language Model.

studies.design: Single-blinded comparison of GPT-4 vs junior clinician discharge letters for simulated urology cases
studies.finding: For 5 simulated urology outpatient cases, blinded primary care physicians rated GPT-4 letters higher for information provision (mean 4.32 vs 3.70; P=.03). Overall satisfaction did not differ significantly (3.96 vs 3.62; P=.36), and GPT-4 had no hallucinations.
studies.limitation: Only 5 fictional cases; small sample; numbers of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Comparison of the Quality of Discharge Letters Written by Large Language Models and Junior Clinicians: Single-Blinded Study.

studies.design: Retrospective sequential multireader multicase study of 758 chest radiographs read without and with AI-generated preliminary reports
studies.ai_system: Domain-specific multimodal generative AI report tool
studies.finding: AI-generated preliminary reports reduced average reading times from 34.2 seconds to 19.8 seconds (P < .001), and report quality scores changed from 4.5 (IQR 4.0-5.0) to 4.5 (IQR 4.5-5.0) (P < .001). Sensitivity increased for widened mediastinal silhouettes (84.3% to 90.8%) and pleural lesions (77.7% to 87.4%).
studies.limitation: Sequential design (without-then-with AI) on a public dataset with only five radiologists; variability among individual radiologists.
studies.title: Value of Using a Generative AI Model in Chest Radiography Reporting: A Reader Study.

studies.design: Comparative evaluation by blinded expert raters
studies.humans: First-year oral surgery resident (authors); 18 surgeons as raters
studies.finding: Quality of informed consent documents for oral surgery procedures rated by 18 surgeons. ChatGPT-4 had median accuracy 4 [IQR 4-4] vs human 4 [IQR 3-4] and completeness 4 [IQR 4-5] vs 4 [IQR 3-4], and received the highest overall quality ratings.
studies.limitation: Human comparator was a single first-year resident.
studies.title: Evaluating AI-Generated informed consent documents in oral surgery: A comparative study of ChatGPT-4, Bard gemini advanced, and human-written consents.
studies.source: Journal of cranio-maxillo-facial surgery : official publication of the European Association for Cranio-Maxillo-Facial Surgery

studies.design: Retrospective observational study using EHR audit logs
studies.finding: Documentation time in ED encounters with vs without an ambient AI scribe. Median on-shift documentation time was 2:45 min for ambient vs 3:50 min for standard encounters (-28%), and total EHR time 8:39 vs 10:21 min (-16%).
studies.limitation: Observational single-centre design with optional, skewed adoption toward lower-acuity encounters, introducing selection bias.
studies.title: Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribe Adoption and Documentation Time in the Emergency Department.

studies.design: Prospective comparative study of AI vs physician discharge summaries
studies.finding: For discharge summaries of 100 renal insufficiency patients, accuracy was comparable (AKI 90 vs. 92 points; CKD 88 vs. 90, p > 0.05) and quality was similar (26 vs. 27; 25 vs. 26). AI needed about 30 s versus over 15 min for physicians (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Single department; number of physicians and rater blinding not stated.
studies.title: Comparative study of Claude 3.5-Sonnet and human physicians in generating discharge summaries for patients with renal insufficiency: assessment of efficiency, accuracy, and quality.

studies.design: Single-center mixed-methods study; supervisory notes written with and without ChatGPT
studies.finding: Physicians wrote supervisory notes for clinical scenarios with and without ChatGPT assistance. ChatGPT yielded a 40% reduction in time and a 33% decrease in effort for intricate cases, with no discernible effect on simpler notes.
studies.limitation: Very small single-center sample using simulated scenarios and self-reported effort.
studies.title: Harnessing the Power of Generative AI for Clinical Summaries: Perspectives From Emergency Physicians.

studies.design: Retrospective evaluation with blinded radiologist rating of reports from AI, radiologists and GPT-4V
studies.ai_system: Domain-specific multimodal generative AI chest radiograph report model
studies.finding: Chest radiograph reports were rated for acceptability. Acceptance was 70.5% for model-generated, 73.3% for radiologist and 29.6% for GPT-4Vision reports; model reports had highest agreement and quality scores (median = 4) and were most often ranked highest (60.0%).
studies.limitation: Subjective ratings by only four radiologists on retrospective data; no live clinical use.
studies.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Clinical Value of a Domain-specific Multimodal Generative AI Model for Chest Radiograph Report Generation.

studies.design: Comparison of AI video-based operative reports with surgeon-written reports against expert video review
studies.ai_system: Computer vision surgical step detection generating operative reports
studies.finding: Across 158 cases, overall accuracy was 87.3% for AI reports versus 72.8% for surgeon reports (p = 0.001). Clinically significant discrepancies occurred in 12.7% of AI reports versus 27.2% of surgeon reports.
studies.limitation: Single tertiary center, single procedure; number of surgeons not stated.
studies.title: Enhancing Accuracy of Operative Reports with Automated Artificial Intelligence Analysis of Surgical Video.
studies.source: Journal of the American College of Surgeons

studies.design: Cross-sectional non-inferiority validation study with blinded physician evaluators
studies.humans: 42 physician summary writers from 8 specialties (10 evaluators)
studies.finding: Writing medical summaries of 50 patient records, rated for completeness, correctness and conciseness. Completeness and correctness did not differ significantly, LLM summaries were less concise (3.0 vs 3.5, p=0.001), and overall scores were similar (3.4 vs 3.3, p=0.373). Physicians took an average of 7 min per summary versus 15.7 s for the LLM.
studies.limitation: Single Dutch academic hospital with only 50 records.
studies.title: Quality and efficiency of integrating customised large language model-generated summaries versus physician-written summaries: a validation study.

studies.design: Retrospective evaluation of data extraction from reports against physicians
studies.ai_system: Neuro-symbolic AI (GPT-4 plus rule-based expert system)
studies.finding: Extracting data from 206 prostate cancer PET/CT reports, physicians reached F1 scores of 1.00 and 0.99 with 98.1% PSA accuracy, while the neuro-symbolic AI scored 1.00 twice with 100% PSA accuracy. GPT-4 alone achieved F1 0.63 and 0.95 with 96.6% correct PSA values.
studies.limitation: Single report type and institution; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Neuro-symbolic AI for auditable cognitive information extraction from medical reports.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with cardiologist qualitative review
studies.finding: EchoGPT summarized echo findings into impressions, compared to cardiologist-generated impressions. In qualitative review, its reports were comparable to cardiologists, significantly preferred for conciseness (P < 0.001) with no significant preference in completeness, correctness and clinical utility.
studies.limitation: Single health system data; number of reviewing cardiologists not stated.
studies.title: Evaluating large language models in echocardiography reporting: opportunities and challenges.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre comparison
studies.finding: Error detection in 400 Chinese ultrasound reports. In few-shot settings Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed senior and resident radiologists, and LLMs were faster (Claude 3.5 Sonnet: 13.2 s, GPT-4o: 15.0 s, radiologist: 42.0 s per report).
studies.limitation: Retrospective with seeded/collected errors; radiologist accuracy figures not reported in the abstract; advantage only in certain aspects.
studies.title: The use of large language models in detecting Chinese ultrasound report errors.

studies.design: Feasibility study with mock vignettes and blinded GP evaluation
studies.humans: Five junior doctors who completed the UK Foundation Programme
studies.finding: Discharge summaries for 25 mock vignettes were written by ChatGPT and by junior doctors. GPs rated 100% of AI summaries acceptable vs 92% of junior doctor summaries; both had mean 97% compliance with the minimum dataset.
studies.limitation: Small feasibility study using mock vignettes, not real patient data.
studies.title: Transforming healthcare documentation: harnessing the potential of AI to generate discharge summaries.

studies.design: Pilot study of 6 fictional cases with blinded expert panel rating
studies.humans: Junior attending orthopedic surgeon and advanced orthopedic resident
studies.finding: Discharge documents for 6 fictional orthopedic cases were written by physicians and ChatGPT-4 and rated blind by 15 experts. Quality was comparable, ChatGPT-4 was 10 times faster, and 4 hallucination events were found in ChatGPT-4 content versus 6 in physician notes.
studies.limitation: Pilot of only 6 fictional cases with two physician authors.
studies.title: ChatGPT-4 generates orthopedic discharge documents faster than humans maintaining comparable quality: a pilot study of 6 cases.

studies.design: Comparison of LLMs vs specialists extracting comorbidities from 250 clinical reports
studies.finding: Extraction and classification of comorbidities from oncology EHR reports. GPT-4 achieved sensitivity of 96.8% vs 88.8% for physicians (McNemar P<.001), while physicians marginally outperformed GPT-4 in precision (97.7% vs 96.8%); GPT-3.5 was slightly lower than physicians without significant difference (P=.79).
studies.limitation: Single task and 250 reports from one setting; small number of specialists.
studies.title: The Transformative Potential of Large Language Models in Mining Electronic Health Records Data: Content Analysis.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of LLM vs clinical team in-basket responses graded by clinicians and nurses
studies.humans: Clinical care teams; 5 clinicians and 4 nurses as graders
studies.finding: On 158 in-basket messages, RadOnc-GPT slightly outperformed the clinical care team in empathy and was comparable in completeness, correctness and clarity. Estimated time saved was 5.2 minutes per message for nurses and 2.4 minutes for clinicians.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-institution study; graders identified hallucinations and context gaps.
studies.title: Retrospective Comparative Analysis of Prostate Cancer In-Basket Messages: Responses From Closed-Domain Large Language Models Versus Clinical Teams.

studies.design: Preprint; LLM adaptation study with a clinical reader study
studies.humans: Human experts writing summaries; ten physician readers
studies.finding: In a reader study with ten physicians, summaries of clinical text from the best-adapted LLMs were compared with human expert summaries across four summarization tasks. The LLM summaries were preferred to human summaries for completeness and correctness.
studies.limitation: Preprint; preference ratings only, and no numerical results are given in the abstract.
studies.title: Clinical Text Summarization: Adapting Large Language Models Can Outperform Human Experts.

studies.design: Retrospective study; fine-tuned model compared with two radiologists on a test set
studies.finding: Brain MRI reports were classified into nontumor, posttreatment tumor and pretreatment tumor groups. The fine-tuned LLM reached an overall accuracy of 0.970 (95% CI: 0.930-0.990), with no statistically significant differences from the radiologists in accuracy, sensitivity or specificity (p ≥ 0.371). The LLM was approximately 20-26-fold faster than the radiologists.
studies.limitation: Single retrospective dataset, small test set of 164 reports, and only two comparator radiologists.
studies.title: Automated classification of brain MRI reports using fine-tuned large language models.

studies.design: Benchmark of LLMs plus a reader study comparing clinician-written and LLM-generated summaries on 30 samples
studies.ai_system: GPT-4 with in-context learning; Llama2-13B fine-tuned
studies.humans: Clinician-written brief hospital course summaries, rated by 5 clinicians
studies.finding: Brief hospital course summaries generated by LLMs were compared with the original clinician-written summaries. Readers showed a significant preference for GPT-4 in-context learning summaries over both the Llama2-13B fine-tuned summaries and the original summaries (P<.001).
studies.limitation: Small reader study (5 clinicians, 30 samples), preference ratings only, MIMIC data.
studies.title: A dataset and benchmark for hospital course summarization with adapted large language models.
studies.source: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of data extraction on 103 records
studies.finding: ChatGPT-4 and trained human collectors extracted data and assigned appendicitis grade from ultrasound and operative reports, adjudicated by a pediatric surgeon. Grade was erroneously assigned manually in 29 patients (28.2%) and by ChatGPT-4 in 3 (2.9%), and 98% of errors were in manual extraction.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 103 records; human collectors were not necessarily clinicians.
studies.title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Label Free-Text Operative and Ultrasound Reports for Grading Pediatric Appendicitis.

studies.design: Blinded expert rating of AI vs physician summaries
studies.humans: 2 physicians writing summaries; 5 CDS expert raters
studies.finding: Summarising user comments on CDS alerts for 8 alerts. AI summaries were rated similar on clarity and accuracy and significantly higher on completeness and usefulness (AI: 3.4 ± 1.2, human: 2.7 ± 1.2, P = .001).
studies.limitation: Very small sample of 8 alerts and 2 physician summarisers at a single center.
studies.title: Why do users override alerts? Utilizing large language model to summarize comments and optimize clinical decision support.
studies.source: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

studies.design: Retrospective multi-institution comparison
studies.humans: Six readers: two fellowship-trained radiologists, two fellows, two residents
studies.finding: Lung cancer staging from 700 free-text CT and PET/CT reports. GPT-4o accuracy was 74.1%, worse than fellowship-trained radiologists (82.3%, 85.4%), not different from fellows (77.7%, 75.6%) and resident 1 (72.3%), and better than resident 2 (65.7%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, Korean institutions, zero-shot prompting only.
studies.title: Lung Cancer Staging Using Chest CT and FDG PET/CT Free-Text Reports: Comparison Among Three ChatGPT Large Language Models and Six Human Readers of Varying Experience.

studies.design: Blinded comparison of AI vs clinician-written discharge summaries rated by attendings
studies.finding: Four blinded attending physicians rated psychiatric discharge summaries written by clinical staff versus ChatGPT 4.0 for consistency, completeness and comprehensibility. AI summaries were reported as more efficient and particularly better in coherence and information structure.
studies.limitation: No numeric results or sample sizes reported in abstract.
studies.title: Application of artificial intelligence (AI) in the creation of discharge summaries in psychiatric clinics.
studies.source: International journal of psychiatry in medicine

studies.design: Retrospective quality-improvement pre-post study
studies.humans: Orthopaedic surgeons, advanced practice providers and podiatrists
studies.finding: EHR efficiency metrics for 19 providers were compared pre- vs post-utilization of the AI tool. Time in notes per appointment fell (-3.1 minutes, 41%), notes per day (-16.9 minutes, 31%), and time outside 7 am to 7 pm (-23.6 minutes, 61%).
studies.limitation: Uncontrolled retrospective pre-post pilot with low utilization (24.0% to 31.4%).
studies.title: Utilization of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Documentation System Improves Provider Efficiency in Outpatient Orthopaedic Clinics: Reducing the Afterhours Burden of the Electronic Health Record-A Pilot Study.
studies.source: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons

studies.design: Before-after quality improvement project
studies.finding: Ward round documentation time was compared between conventional documentation and use of the Heidi AI tool over two 4-day periods. AI implementation led to a statistically significant reduction in documentation time; no numbers reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Single-department before-after QI project over 4-day periods with no reported numbers.
studies.title: Improving ward round documentation using the Heidi Health application.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study comparing LLM vs radiologist impressions
studies.finding: Readers rated LLM-generated versus radiologist-written CT chest impressions. Model scored 3.56/4 clinical accuracy, 3.92/4 grammar, 3.37/4 style versus 3.75/4, 3.87/4, 3.54/4 for radiologists.
studies.limitation: Single institution; no statistical tests reported in abstract.
studies.title: An open-source fine-tuned large language model for radiological impression generation: a multi-reader performance study.

studies.design: Comparison of chatbots and human readers coding AO classification from created reports
studies.finding: On 100 created radiology reports, chatbots reached a maximum of 86% correct full AO codes vs 95% in human readers. Chatbots were faster (mean 3.2 s vs 50 s per case, p < .001).
studies.limitation: Synthetic reports; number of human readers not stated.
studies.title: Performance of ChatGPT, human radiologists, and context-aware ChatGPT in identifying AO codes from radiology reports.

studies.design: Blinded multicentric comparison of operative notes rated by 10 otolaryngologists
studies.humans: Surgical resident and attending surgeon authors
studies.finding: Operative notes for five otolaryngologic procedures were written by a resident, an attending, GPT alone and an attending using GPT, then rated blindly by 10 otolaryngologists. Hybrid notes had the highest "as is" approval rate (79%), while GPT-only notes had the lowest (23%), and writing time was significantly reduced in both AI-assisted groups.
studies.limitation: Very small dataset of five procedures with one author per arm.
studies.title: Surgeon, Trainee, or GPT? A Blinded Multicentric Study of AI-Augmented Operative Notes.

studies.design: Virtual endoscopy comparison on recorded EGD videos
studies.finding: Capturing 11 anatomical landmarks from 37 EGD videos. APT showed similar completeness to endoscopists (87.72% vs. 85.75%, P = .0.258), and combined endoscopist plus APT photodocumentation reached higher completeness (91.89% vs. 85.75%, P < .0.001). APT images had higher mean opinion scores (3.88 vs. 3.41, P < .0.001).
studies.limitation: Single-centre study using 37 recorded videos in virtual endoscopy rather than live procedures.
studies.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based system for real-time high-quality photodocumentation during esophagogastroduodenoscopy.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on 200 discharge summaries
studies.finding: Classifying GI bleeding episodes from 200 discharge summaries. GPT-4 accuracy was 94.4% vs Reviewer 1 98.5% (P < 0.001) and Reviewer 2 90.8% (P = 0.170), outperforming ICD codes (63.5%). GPT-4 took 12.7 min versus 8-9 h per reviewer.
studies.limitation: Only two human reviewers and 200 summaries from a single source; ground truth set by physician reviewers.
studies.title: Validation of GPT-4 for clinical event classification: A comparative analysis with ICD codes and human reviewers.

studies.design: Two-session reporting study: control vs GPT-4-assisted structured reporting of abdominopelvic CT
studies.finding: Mean case reporting time for RAD-1 decreased from 00:20:08 to 00:16:30 and for RAD-2 from 00:12:04 to 00:10:04 with AI assistance, not statistically significant (p > 0.05). Quality scores of finalized reports were comparable with no significant differences.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists and 30 scans.
studies.title: Cutting Edge to Cutting Time: Can ChatGPT Improve the Radiologist's Reporting?
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Validation of NLP adjudication against physician clinical events committee
studies.ai_system: Heart Failure Natural Language Processing model
studies.finding: Adjudication of heart failure hospitalizations in the DELIVER trial. AI-based adjudication agreed with the clinical events committee in 83% of events; human review of uncertain events (16%) would have achieved 91% agreement. Estimated treatment effect was HR 0.76 with AI vs 0.77 with the committee.
studies.limitation: Committee used as reference standard, so agreement rather than independent accuracy is measured.
studies.title: Natural Language Processing to Adjudicate Heart Failure Hospitalizations in Global Clinical Trials.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of LLM-generated vs physician-written patient education materials rated by experts and patients
studies.humans: One experienced physician (author of comparator material); 7 expert raters and 50 patients
studies.finding: Patient education materials on early diabetic kidney disease were rated on accuracy, completeness, safety and comprehensibility. ERNIE Bot 4.0's non-guideline PEM and the physician-sourced PEM were the top two, and patients rated the ERNIE material as well as, if not slightly better than, the physician material.
studies.limitation: Single physician-written comparator and small rater panel; Likert ratings without numeric results reported.
studies.title: Comparison of artificial intelligence-generated and physician-generated patient education materials on early diabetic kidney disease.

studies.design: Development and validation study comparing NLP pipeline with human reviewers on EHR data extraction
studies.finding: Extraction of clinical concepts from EHRs of total hip arthroplasty patients, against a gold standard of 100 randomly selected EHRs. The algorithm was as accurate as human reviewers (0.95 vs 0.94; P=.01), with a database-wide average F1-score of 0.92.
studies.limitation: Single-surgeon practice and small 100-record gold standard limit generalisability.
studies.title: Assessing Total Hip Arthroplasty Outcomes and Generating an Orthopedic Research Outcome Database via a Natural Language Processing Pipeline: Development and Validation Study.

studies.design: Retrospective crossover of conventional vs summary+LLM reporting
studies.finding: Reporting of 100 oncology CT scans using conventional reports vs radiologist summaries expanded by LLMs. Average reporting time was 6.76 min for summary method vs 8.95 min conventional (p < 0.005); only one LLM-generated report received a worse RADPEER score than its summary.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists and 100 scans; LLM reports still contained errors requiring oversight.
studies.title: Integrating Large language models into radiology workflow: Impact of generating personalized report templates from summary.

studies.design: Retrospective reporting workflow comparison on 80 imaging studies
studies.ai_system: GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 3.5 with audio input
studies.finding: LLM-based workflows reduced reporting time (38.9 s vs. 88.0 s, p < 0.01) and corrections (GPT-4o: 1.0, Sonnet 3.5: 0.9 vs. 2.4) versus conventional speech recognition. Sonnet 3.5 reports were rated highest in quality, while GPT-4o and conventional reports showed no difference.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists on 80 retrospective studies.
studies.title: From dictation to diagnosis: enhancing radiology reporting with integrated speech recognition in multimodal large language models.

studies.design: Comparative evaluation of patient education materials written by a physician and five LLMs
studies.ai_system: Bing Copilot, Claude 3 Opus, Gemini Pro, ChatGPT-4, ERNIE Bot 4.0
studies.humans: Physician author; rated by five gastroenterologists and 50 patients
studies.finding: For writing H. pylori patient education materials, the physician-sourced material had the highest accuracy mean score of 5.60, while LLM-generated English materials ranged from 4.00 to 5.40. Completeness was comparable between physician and LLM materials in English, and no material met the sixth-grade reading level.
studies.limitation: Single physician-authored comparator and a single topic; subjective Likert ratings.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Patient Education Materials for Helicobacter pylori Infection: A Comparative Analysis.

studies.design: Cross-sectional expert panel comparison
studies.humans: Professional society-authored answers rated by pediatric spine surgeons
studies.finding: Answers to 15 pediatric scoliosis FAQs from LLMs were compared with professional society-authored answers. The expert panel favored professional society responses for 40% of questions, AI for 40%, rated them equally good for 13%, and saw a tie for 7%.
studies.limitation: Only 15 questions; comparator is society-written text rather than individual clinicians; panel size not stated.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Large Language Models Can Facilitate Patient Education.
studies.source: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America

studies.design: Blinded comparison of AI-authored and clinician-authored summaries
studies.finding: Summarising 70 simulated primary care EHRs. Clinicians rated clinician-authored summaries higher overall (7.39 vs 7.00 out of 10; P = .02). Accuracy was similar, and AI summaries were less likely to omit important information.
studies.limitation: Simulated records; the number of summarising clinicians is not stated.
studies.title: Comparing artificial intelligence- vs clinician-authored summaries of simulated primary care electronic health records.

studies.design: Blinded comparison of one physician-written and one AI-generated manuscript
studies.finding: Writing a scientific manuscript from identical inputs, rated by two human and one AI reviewer. The AI manuscript scored higher in clarity and readability (mean 9.0 vs 7.2) but lower in technical accuracy (mean 6.3 vs 9.3) and depth (mean 5.5 vs 7.5).
studies.limitation: Single manuscript per side and only three reviewers; simulated analysis.
studies.title: Can artificial intelligence write science? A comparative analysis of human-written and artificial intelligence-generated scientific writings.

studies.design: Blinded survey comparison (quality improvement project)
studies.humans: Two ENT doctors (letter authors); rated by 47 parents
studies.finding: Parents of paediatric tonsillectomy patients blindly rated two ChatGPT discharge letters for hypothetical patients against two real letters by ENT doctors. AI letters were rated as containing significantly better medical information (p = 0.0059) and significantly easier to read (p < 0.0001); respondents had 50% sensitivity identifying AI letters.
studies.limitation: Only four letters, hypothetical AI cases, and lay-perceived quality rather than clinical accuracy.
studies.title: A quality improvement project of patient perception of AI-generated discharge summaries: a comparison with doctor-written summaries.
studies.source: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England

studies.design: Blinded comparison of LLM vs expert responses rated by physicians
studies.ai_system: Le Chat Pixtral Large, DeepSeek-R1, ChatGPT-4.5
studies.finding: Three LLMs and three experts answered 3 patient education and 3 clinical decision-making VTE queries, rated by 37 physicians. LLMs scored higher on patient education (mean differences +1.6, +1.7, +1.9). In decision-making DeepSeek-R1 outperformed experts (+1.4) while the other two were comparable (-0.3, +0.5).
studies.limitation: Only six queries and three experts.
studies.title: Large language models vs thrombosis experts: a comparative study on patient education and clinical decision-making in venous thromboembolism.
studies.source: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH

studies.design: Retrospective multireader study
studies.humans: Referring clinicians' indications; rated by 20 radiologists
studies.finding: 20 radiologists compared imaging indications written by referring clinicians, radiologists and LLMs for 241 examinations. LLM indications were rated more comprehensive (Likert 5: 37.14% and 28.42%) and more factual (68.05% and 59.75%) than referring clinician indications. The proprietary LLM ranked most useful in protocoling (rank 1: 40.87%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, single institution, with subjective ratings.
studies.title: Radiologically Relevant Clinical History Summarization with Large Language Models: A Multireader Performance Study.

studies.design: Multisite observational within-physician EHR audit-log analysis across 20 EDs
studies.finding: Among 275 attending physicians, AI-scribed notes took less active time (median 10.0 versus 12.5 min; 2.4 minutes less after adjustment) and were about 14% longer (median 5,220 versus 4,468 characters). Note completion was not delayed (-6 minutes) and 72-hour ED return was not increased (-0.8 percentage point; 95% CI -1.5 to -0.1).
studies.limitation: Observational non-randomized design; physicians chose which encounters to scribe, so residual confounding is possible.
studies.title: Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribe Use and Objective Documentation Effort Among Emergency Physicians.

studies.design: Single-centre pilot PROBE randomized controlled trial
studies.ai_system: LLM-generated draft discharge summaries and referrals
studies.humans: Ophthalmology physicians at Kyoto University Hospital (21 randomized, 17 completed)
studies.finding: Physicians wrote discharge summaries and referrals for six simulated records with or without LLM drafts. Clinician-in-the-loop time differences were non-significant (summaries β = -59.4 seconds, P = .18; referrals β = 52.9 seconds, P = .08), but quality outperformed clinician-only drafting in most expert-rated domains. LLM-only drafts were fastest but had the lowest quality.
studies.limitation: Small pilot trial in one department using simulated patient records.
studies.title: Evaluating an LLM-assisted workflow for clinical documentation: A pilot randomized controlled trial on time and quality.

studies.design: Quasi-experimental interrupted time-series study comparing 150 days before and after AI scribe access
studies.humans: 220 primary care clinicians (physicians and advanced practice providers)
studies.finding: Effect of ambient AI scribe use on documentation in 314 845 encounters. Note writing time decreased 7% at day 0 (IRR 0.93), increasing to a 16% decrease by day 150 (IRR 0.84). At day 150 pajama time decreased 19% and wRVU increased 2%, with no change in note length.
studies.limitation: Non-randomised pre-post design; includes advanced practice providers alongside physicians.
studies.title: Longitudinal effects of ambient artificial intelligence scribe use on documentation burden and financial productivity in primary care: a quasi-experimental study.
studies.source: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter study of 78,336 EGDs
studies.finding: The study assessed landmark photodocumentation during EGD with and without real-time AI suggestions. AI suggestions reduced zero-landmark procedures by 42.6% (15.8 vs. 27.5%; P < 0.001), with improvements across all seven anatomical sites.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, non-randomised comparison.
studies.title: A Video-Based Artificial Intelligence Platform for Measuring Esophagogastroduodenoscopy Duration and Suggesting Real-Time Landmark Documentation.

studies.design: Pilot simulated study comparing clinic letters from AI platforms vs clinician dictation-secretary transcription, rated by two senior dermatologists
studies.humans: Clinicians using traditional dictation with secretarial transcription
studies.finding: Dermatology clinic letters from four scripted cases were rated for accuracy, satisfaction, readability and time. ChatGPT achieved average accuracy 92.6% and satisfaction 4.59/5, Heidi 85% and 4.34/5, versus 58.81% and 3.52/5 for the traditional method. Time per letter was 27 s (Heidi), 54 s (ChatGPT) and 10 min 54 s (traditional), though traditional letters were easiest to read.
studies.limitation: Pilot with only four scripted simulated cases, two doctor-patient pairs and two raters.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence compared with traditional methods of generating dermatology consultation letters: a pilot study comparing accuracy, readability and efficiency.

studies.design: Non-inferiority comparison on identical case materials
studies.finding: Medical history documentation was rated by two attending physicians. ChatGPT-4o scored 88.9 versus 89.6 for residents (p = 0.25), within the non-inferiority margin. Average documentation time was 40.1 s for ChatGPT-4o versus 14.9 min for residents.
studies.limitation: Very small sample of five residents from a single department.
studies.title: Comparison of medical history documentation efficiency and quality based on GPT-4o: a study on the comparison between residents and artificial intelligence.

studies.design: Comparative evaluation of error auditing in resident-drafted reports, plus a pilot real-world validation
studies.humans: Retinal specialists, general ophthalmologists and ophthalmic technicians
studies.finding: GPT-4o audited 180 FFA and B-scan reports for laterality and anatomical errors. It detected 79.0% (158 of 200) of errors, comparable to general ophthalmologists at 78.0% (155 of 200; P ≥ 0.09), and reviewed the reports in about 0.27 h versus 2.17-3.19 h for humans. In a real-world pilot it detected 18 of 20 errors, versus 95-100% by human reviewers.
studies.limitation: Single-centre study with a small real-world pilot of 20 reports; the number of human reviewers is not stated.
studies.title: Leveraging ChatGPT for Report Error Audit: An Accuracy-Driven and Cost-Efficient Solution for Ophthalmic Imaging Reports.

studies.design: Simulated consultation study; notes rated blind by GPs using a modified PDQI-9
studies.humans: Human note writers in simulated general practice consultations; three GP raters
studies.finding: Notes from four commercial AI scribes and human-written notes for four standardised RACGP exam scenarios were rated blind by three GPs on a modified PDQI-9. Top AI scribes scored a mean of 44.08/50 (SD = 3.32) vs. 37.42 (SD = 9.78) for humans. AI scribes excelled in thoroughness (M = 4.92), accuracy (M = 4.67) and freedom from bias (M = 4.92).
studies.limitation: Simulated consultations with only four scenarios and three raters; the number of human note writers is not stated.
studies.title: The Great Scribe-Off: A Comparative Analysis of AI Scribes Versus Human Documentation in Simulated General Practice Consultations.
studies.source: Studies in health technology and informatics

studies.design: Model development with blind grading of reports against ophthalmologists
studies.ai_system: MORG deep learning OCT report generation model
studies.finding: Generating reports from retinal OCT image pairs, assessed by blind grading. MORG scored 4.55 compared to ophthalmologists' 4.63 out of a maximum of 5.
studies.limitation: Number of ophthalmologists and graders not stated; no statistical comparison reported in the abstract.
studies.title: A deep learning based automatic report generator for retinal optical coherence tomography images.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of NLP phenotyping against human annotation
studies.finding: Sub-phenotyping Crohn's disease patients from clinical notes. GPT-4 achieved note-level F1 of at least 0.90 for disease behavior and 0.82 for age at diagnosis; there was no statistical evidence for a difference to the performance of human experts.
studies.limitation: Single disease, small test set of 280 texts; human comparison based on prior inter-annotator agreement with no reported clinician numbers.
studies.title: Automating clinical phenotyping using natural language processing.

studies.design: Retrospective study of 500 ED visits with masked physician review
studies.finding: Primary diagnosis ICD-10 coding for ED visits. Reviewers favoured RAG-enhanced GPT-4 for accuracy in 447 instances vs 277 for provider-assigned codes (P<0.001), and for specificity in 509 vs 181 (P<0.001).
studies.limitation: Single health system, retrospective, preference-based judgement rather than gold standard.
studies.title: Assessing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Medical Coding.

studies.design: Observational within-subject comparison of human-only vs GPT-aided responses
studies.humans: Frontline health workers (doctors, nurses, community health workers) in Nigeria
studies.finding: 36 frontline health workers answered 15 patient questions with and without ChatGPT-3.5. GPT-aided responses significantly outperformed human-only responses on all clinician-rated metrics (P<.001), with largest gains in completeness, empathy and overall preference.
studies.limitation: Observational design with written patient questions, not live care.
studies.title: Evaluating Frontline Health Workers' Responses to Patient Inquiries With and Without Large Language Model Support in Nigeria: Observational Study.

studies.design: Retrospective cross-sectional blinded comparison of 256 cases
studies.humans: Physicians who wrote the original records; rated by 3 senior emergency physicians
studies.finding: The task was generating initial senior ward round records for acute poisoning. DeepSeek scored a mean total of 24.14, higher than ChatGPT (23.30) and physicians (23.86; P=.02). High-harm records were significantly more frequent in both LLM groups than in the physician group (P=.02).
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective study in which the LLM records were not used in care.
studies.title: Quality Evaluation of Large Language Model-Assisted Generation of Initial Senior Physician Ward Round Records for Patients With Acute Poisoning: Cross-Sectional Study.

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter evaluation with blinded head-to-head reader comparison on an error-enriched challenge set
studies.finding: LLM detection of text errors in radiology reports was compared with radiologists on an error-enriched challenge set. The model's error instance exact category recall exceeded that of the radiologists (0.96 vs 0.45-0.67; P<.001), with shorter mean task completion time (5.80 vs 55.80-67.80 seconds per report).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, error-enriched challenge set with only 3 radiologists; text-only task.
studies.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Radiology Report Quality Assurance: Real-World Multicenter Evaluation.

studies.design: Multistage evaluation study with reader comparison
studies.finding: Detection of errors in Chinese emergency radiology reports. DeepSeek-R1 detected 84.4% of errors vs 51.6% and 53.1% for residents (both P<.05), with no significant difference from senior and attending radiologists (84.4% vs 68.8%-93.8%, P=.26 to ≥.99).
studies.limitation: Small stress-test set (n=100) with inserted errors; comparison depends on reader seniority.
studies.title: Error Detection in Emergency Radiology Reports Using a Large Language Model: Multistage Evaluation Study.

studies.design: Comparative study extracting data from 100 ILD clinic notes
studies.ai_system: 12 LLMs incl. Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, o1, gpt-oss
studies.finding: The task was extracting binary answers to ILD questions from clinic notes. Seven LLMs performed at human-level accuracy, similar to the 3 ILD clinicians (96.2%). Five LLMs performed significantly worse than humans (Holm-adjusted P≤.003).
studies.limitation: Single-centre study with 100 notes and only 3 clinician comparators.
studies.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models for Structured Data Extraction From Interstitial Lung Disease Clinical Notes: Comparative Study.

studies.design: Retrospective cohort of 500 ED visits with blinded physician review of LLM vs provider codes
studies.ai_system: RAG-enhanced LLMs (nine models incl. GPT-4, Llama-3.1-70B)
studies.finding: ICD-10-CM coding from emergency department records. In 200 discrepant cases, reviewers favored GPT-4 for accuracy in 447 instances vs 277 for providers (p<0.001), and for specificity in 509 vs 181 (p<0.001).
studies.limitation: Preprint, not peer reviewed; single health system and reviewer panel included LLMs.
studies.title: Assessing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Performance in Emergency Department ICD-10-CM Coding Compared to Human Coders.
studies.source: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

studies.design: Retrospective quality-improvement study comparing AI-assisted and manual encounters
studies.humans: 16 clinicians (12 physicians, 4 APPs) in pediatric otolaryngology
studies.finding: Documentation efficiency in pediatric otolaryngology encounters. Median note-editing time was lower with AI assistance (∼4.0 vs 11.8 min), with similar median note length (∼4000 characters).
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective study with a small number of clinicians and possible self-selection into AI use.
studies.title: Implementation and early outcomes of AI-powered ambient documentation in pediatric otolaryngology practice.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial
studies.finding: Students using ChatGPT as a learning tool scored higher on an orthopedics test than controls (mean 141.20 vs 130.80; P=.04). They also did better in final surgery (76.54 vs 72.54) and obstetrics and gynecology exams.
studies.limitation: Single-site trial with 19 withdrawals and exam-based outcomes.
studies.title: Integrating ChatGPT in Orthopedic Education for Medical Undergraduates: Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial
studies.finding: Dental students learning clinical operative skills were randomised to ChatGPT plus videos or videos alone, with skills tested in desktop virtual reality. Performance was superior in the ChatGPT group (mean 73.12, SD 10.06) than control (mean 65.54, SD 12.48; P<.001), with lower eye-tracked cognitive load (0.137 vs 0.312). Benefit was largest among students with low spatial ability (70.20 vs 55.41; P<.001).
studies.limitation: Single university, 1-week intervention, students rather than practising clinicians, skills assessed in simulation only.
studies.title: Exploring the Application Capability of ChatGPT as an Instructor in Skills Education for Dental Medical Students: Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Single-center RCT of ChatGPT versus expert feedback
studies.finding: Students received ChatGPT-generated (n = 64) or expert-written (n = 65) feedback on UTI clinical reasoning tests. Key-Features Question scores were not significantly different immediately (control 78.5 vs experiment 74.7, P = .26) or after 10 days (78.0 vs 76.0, P = .57). The control group outperformed the ChatGPT group in complicated UTI cases (P < .001).
studies.limitation: Single school, first-year students, single topic.
studies.title: ChatGPT versus expert feedback on clinical reasoning questions and their effect on learning: a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial
studies.finding: Over 12 weeks, students with LearnGuide had higher Self-Directed Learning Scale scores (4.15 [95% CI, 0.82 to 7.48]; p = 0.01) and Cornell Critical Thinking scores (7.11 [95% CI, 4.50 to 9.72]; p < 0.001) than controls, sustained at 14 weeks.
studies.limitation: Outcomes are learning scales rather than clinical performance; single trial.
studies.title: Enhancing self-directed learning with custom GPT AI facilitation among medical students: A randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Double-blind RCT of AI feedback on AI-simulated history taking
studies.finding: After four sessions, CRI-HTI clinical decision-making scores were 3.60 ± 0.13 in the AI feedback group versus 3.02 ± 0.12 in the control group, F (1,18) = 4.44, p = .049.
studies.limitation: Very small sample of 21 students; simulated training outcome.
studies.title: Large language models improve clinical decision making of medical students through patient simulation and structured feedback: a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Randomised comparison of ChatGPT-based blended teaching vs traditional teaching
studies.finding: Hepatobiliary surgery training. The ChatGPT group scored higher on theoretical exams (86.44 ± 5.59 vs. 77.86 ± 4.16, p < .001) and clinical skills (83.84 ± 6.13 vs. 79.12 ± 4.27, p = .001).
studies.limitation: Small single-centre trial; unblinded educational outcomes.
studies.title: Application of ChatGPT-based blended medical teaching in clinical education of hepatobiliary surgery.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial of AI warning disclaimer on advice-taking with vignettes
studies.finding: Students given disagreeing ChatGPT-attributed advice on ambiguous vignettes changed diagnosis at similar rates with or without a warning (15.3% no-warning vs. 15.9% warning; OR = 1.09, p = 0.84). Weight of advice was 0.15, lower than the 0.30 prior meta-analytic average, indicating underweighting of AI advice.
studies.limitation: Students, three simulated vignettes and scripted AI advice; measures advice-taking, not accuracy.
studies.title: 'ChatGPT can make mistakes' warnings fail: A randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Randomized group allocation of surgical clerkship students to ChatGPT-supported vs traditional teaching
studies.humans: 64 medical students in general surgery clerkship
studies.finding: Students using ChatGPT as a supplementary tool showed significantly higher compliance in pre-class preparation and post-class review (P < 0.05) and higher overall satisfaction (P < 0.0001) than controls using traditional multimedia learning.
studies.limitation: Small single-centre study with outcomes based mainly on questionnaires; test-score results not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Implementation and evaluation of an optimized surgical clerkship teaching model utilizing ChatGPT.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial (cluster sampling)
studies.finding: Students received standard learning or added 3 sessions with ChatGPT as simulated patient, assessed by blinded OSCE history-taking. Scores significantly increased in the intervention group alone (p < 0.001, 0.37v0.19 Cohen D effect size).
studies.limitation: Single surgery module; students not practicing clinicians; modest sample.
studies.title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of a Deep Language Learning Model-Based Simulation Tool for Undergraduate Medical Students in Surgery.

studies.design: Comparative cross-sectional study on exam questions
studies.finding: On 1312 AAP in-service exam questions, ChatGPT-4 (total average 79.57%) outperformed all resident groups. Gemini (72.86%) surpassed first- (63.48%) and second-year residents (66.25%) but not third-year residents (69.06%).
studies.limitation: Exam questions only, image-based items poorly handled, and residents' scores are historical aggregates.
studies.title: Performance of three artificial intelligence (AI)-based large language models in standardized testing; implications for AI-assisted dental education.

studies.design: Cross-sectional exam question comparison
studies.finding: On 180 orthopaedic assessment questions, ChatGPT-3.5, GPT-4 and residents scored 29.4%, 47.2% and 74.2% respectively, with residents scoring higher than both (P < 0.001). Models were not given images.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; images not provided to AI; resident data aggregated from question bank.
studies.title: Comparison of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, and Orthopaedic Resident Performance on Orthopaedic Assessment Examinations.
studies.source: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of ChatGPT on Orthopaedic In-Training Examination questions against historical resident scores
studies.finding: ChatGPT answered 47% (97 of 207) of Orthopaedic In-Training Examination questions correctly. This placed it in the 40th percentile for PGY1s, eighth percentile for PGY2s and first percentile for PGY3-PGY5s, so it was judged unlikely to pass the board examination.
studies.limitation: Text-only exam questions excluding figures; comparison to historical resident norms rather than a head-to-head study.
studies.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Pass the American Board of Orthopaedic Surgery Examination? Orthopaedic Residents Versus ChatGPT.

studies.design: Cross-sectional evaluation of ChatGPT on Plastic Surgery In-Service Examinations compared with national resident performance
studies.finding: ChatGPT answered 57% of questions correctly on the 2022 Plastic Surgery In-Service Examination. This ranked in the 49th percentile for first-year residents, 13th for second-year, 5th for third- and fourth-year, and 0th percentile for fifth- and sixth-year residents.
studies.limitation: Comparison against national score norms on multiple-choice questions only.
studies.title: ChatGPT Is Equivalent to First-Year Plastic Surgery Residents: Evaluation of ChatGPT on the Plastic Surgery In-Service Examination.

studies.design: Observational comparison of LLMs with medical students on German licensing exams
studies.humans: Medical students taking the German licensing exams
studies.finding: On 937 questions from 3 written German medical licensing examinations, GPT-4 averaged 85%. This ranked in the 92.8th, 99.5th and 92.6th percentiles among the medical students who took the same exams, while GPT-3.5 passed only 1 of 3 exams.
studies.limitation: Multiple-choice exam questions only; comparison against student norms.
studies.title: Comparison of the Performance of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 With That of Medical Students on the Written German Medical Licensing Examination: Observational Study.

studies.design: Single-center randomized controlled trial
studies.finding: Initial quiz scores were higher with ChatGPT (mean = 9.60 ± 0.52) and external resources (9.08 ± 0.79) than with institutional resources (6.64 ± 1.57) (p < 0.001). Retention scores one week later did not differ: 6.20, 5.58 and 4.36 (p = 0.118).
studies.limitation: Very small sample (33) at a single centre with short follow-up.
studies.title: ChatGPT as a Learning Tool for Medical Students: Results From a Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Prospective exam-based study of LLMs and physicians with and without ChatGPT-4.0
studies.finding: On the Chinese NCE-CPDC diabetes examination, ChatGPT-4.0 scored 84.82% and surpassed all PCPs. With ChatGPT-4.0 assistance most PCPs improved by 1 %-6.13%.
studies.limitation: Exam questions rather than clinical practice; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Large language models for diabetes training: a prospective study.

studies.design: Comparative cross-sectional study on course MCQ exams
studies.ai_system: OpenAI o1, GPT-4o, DeepSeek R1, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini 1.5 Flash
studies.finding: On final MCQ exams in four clinical courses with negative marking, mean LLM course scores ranged 7.46-9.88 versus student means 4.28-7.32. Aggregated, LLMs averaged 8.75 compared with 5.76 for students.
studies.limitation: Single institution, Spanish-language exams, descriptive student-LLM contrasts only.
studies.title: When AI models take the exam: large language models vs medical students on multiple-choice course exams.

studies.design: Randomised multireader study of simulation training
studies.ai_system: GAN generating synthetic mammograms for training
studies.finding: Residents were randomised to practice with an AI-generated mammography simulation tool (27) or no practice (23). After training there was significant improvement in sensitivity (7.43 percent, p = 0.03), negative predictive value (5.05 percent, p = 0.008) and accuracy (6.49 percent, p = 0.01) in cancer detection.
studies.limitation: Small sample of residents and short-term outcomes on test images only.
studies.title: Simulation training in mammography with AI-generated images: a multireader study.

studies.design: Observational study on exam questions
studies.finding: On 674 MRCGP Applied Knowledge Test questions, ChatGPT averaged 60.17%, below the mean passing mark in the last 2 years (70.42%).
studies.limitation: Comparison is to a pass mark rather than measured clinician performance; exam questions only.
studies.title: Trialling a Large Language Model (ChatGPT) in General Practice With the Applied Knowledge Test: Observational Study Demonstrating Opportunities and Limitations in Primary Care.

studies.design: Comparison of ChatGPT with medical students on progress test MCQs
studies.finding: ChatGPT answered 400 German Progress Test Medicine MCQs, getting 65.5% of 395 evaluated responses correct. It outperformed almost all medical students in years 1-3 and was comparable to students in the second half of their studies.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; student comparison not quantified in detail in abstract.
studies.title: ChatGPT in medical school: how successful is AI in progress testing?

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on course MCQs
studies.ai_system: Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-3.5, GPT-4-1106, Copilot, Gemini 1.5 Flash
studies.finding: On 200 USMLE-style neuroscience MCQs, chatbots averaged 67.2% correct, 7.4% below the students' average. Claude (83%) and GPT-4 (81.7%) exceeded the average student, while Copilot (59.5%), GPT-3.5 (58.3%) and Gemini (53.6%) were lower.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; number of students not stated.
studies.title: Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini performance versus students in different topics of neuroscience.

studies.design: Randomized comparison of dental students mounting radiographs with vs without AI
studies.finding: Students mounted full-mouth radiograph series with or without AI pre-mounting. The AI group was significantly faster (p < 0.05) but accuracy was lower with AI assistance (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Small student sample on an educational task; effect sizes not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted full-mouth radiograph mounting in dental education.

studies.design: Cohort follow-up of RCT comparing AI-tutored students with no-feedback controls
studies.ai_system: Intelligent tutor feedback in neurosurgical simulation
studies.finding: AI-enhanced curriculum improved safety metrics such as healthy tissue removal rate (mean difference -7.05 × 10-5 mm3 per 20 ms) versus control. It reduced dominant hand velocity and tumor removal rate (mean difference -4.85 × 10-5 mm3 per 20 ms), moving efficiency away from expert benchmarks.
studies.limitation: Secondary analysis in simulation with small medical student sample.
studies.title: AI in Surgical Curriculum Design and Unintended Outcomes for Technical Competencies in Simulation Training.

studies.design: Cross-sectional exam question comparison
studies.humans: Medical students, neurosurgery residents, SANS users
studies.finding: GPT-4 achieved 76.6% accuracy on SANS questions, exceeding medical students (26.3%), neurosurgery residents (61.5%) and the national average of SANS users (69.3%).
studies.limitation: Human scores taken from previous findings; exam questions only.
studies.title: GPT-4 Artificial Intelligence Model Outperforms ChatGPT, Medical Students, and Neurosurgery Residents on Neurosurgery Written Board-Like Questions.

studies.design: Observational study of ChatGPT on national specialty exam with candidate ranking
studies.finding: ChatGPT answered 1177 questions from 5 medical specialty exams, scoring 54.3% to 70.9% correct. It ranked 1787th of 22,214 in its best exam and 4428th of 21,476 in its worst.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; GPT-3.5 version; comparison to candidates by ranking only.
studies.title: ChatGPT performance in the medical specialty exam: An observational study.

studies.design: Comparison of ChatGPT versions on 750 USMLE-style vignette questions against medical student average
studies.finding: On 750 clinical vignette multiple-choice questions, GPT-4o achieved 90.4% accuracy, GPT-4 81.1% and GPT-3.5 60.0%. Both GPT-4o and GPT-4 significantly outperformed the medical student average accuracy of 59.3% (95% CI 58.3-60.3).
studies.limitation: Exam-question benchmark against aggregate student averages, not real clinical tasks.
studies.title: ChatGPT-4 Omni Performance in USMLE Disciplines and Clinical Skills: Comparative Analysis.

studies.design: Benchmark of LLMs on critical care MCQs compared with physicians on a practice test
studies.ai_system: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-3.5-turbo, Mistral Large 2407, Llama 3.1 70B
studies.humans: Human physicians taking a European Diploma in Intensive Care-level practice test
studies.finding: On a 77-MCQ critical care practice test, the models scored 89.0%, 80.9%, 84.4%, 80.3% and 66.5%, compared with 61.9% for 350 human physicians. Only GPT-3.5-turbo did not significantly outperform physicians (p = 0.196).
studies.limitation: Exam-style multiple-choice questions rather than real clinical decisions.
studies.title: Comparative evaluation and performance of large language models on expert level critical care questions: a benchmark study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional exam benchmark against physician norms
studies.humans: 322 physicians who completed the 2019 ASSH self-assessment
studies.finding: On 192 questions from the 2019 ASSH hand surgery self-assessment exam, ChatGPT-4 scored 61.98%, below the average physician's performance. It outperformed physicians in the 'vascular' section with 81.82%.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only, with comparison against published aggregate physician scores rather than a direct study.
studies.title: ChatGPT Earns American Board Certification in Hand Surgery.

studies.design: Comparison of ChatGPT and medical students on three years of the Chinese NMLE
studies.finding: ChatGPT took three years of the Chinese National Medical Licensing Examination and was compared with medical students. Its performance was lower than that of the medical students; no numbers were given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; the abstract reports no figures.
studies.title: ChatGPT Performs on the Chinese National Medical Licensing Examination.

studies.design: Preregistered single-centre blinded within-subject observational comparison
studies.humans: Medical students (n = 82) and physicians (n = 46); expert item authors
studies.finding: Comparison of 24 GPT-4o-generated vs 24 human-authored MCQs across imaging specialties. Item difficulty (human 0.65 vs LLM 0.67) and discrimination (0.27 vs 0.29) did not differ significantly, and participants did not identify item origin above chance (0.50).
studies.limitation: Single centre, human-in-the-loop expert review of AI items, and small item set.
studies.title: Psychometric properties and detectability of GPT-4o-generated multiple-choice questions compared with human-authored items across imaging specialties.

studies.design: Prospective non-randomized parallel-group interventional study
studies.ai_system: Fully automated AI system generating MCQs and personalized feedback
studies.humans: Preclinical medical students (38 Year-1 intervention, 33 Year-2 control)
studies.finding: Diagnostic reasoning for 5 abdominal pain conditions was assessed by OSVE. Students trained with the AI system outperformed the control group immediately after the intervention (p < 0.001) and at 2-week follow-up (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Non-randomized control from a different year group; single institution, small sample.
studies.title: AI Teaches Surgical Diagnostic Reasoning to Medical Students: Evidence from an Experiment Using a Fully Automated, Low-Cost Feedback System.

studies.design: Exam benchmark compared with student averages
studies.humans: Medical students taking the Polish Medical Final Examination
studies.finding: Three editions of the Polish MFE. GPT-4 achieved mean accuracies of 79.7% and GPT-3.5 54.8% (Polish) and 60.3% (English); GPT-4 score was mostly lower than the average medical student score.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; student comparison uses aggregate averages.
studies.title: Evaluation of the performance of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on the Polish Medical Final Examination.

studies.design: Controlled comparison of students trained with vs without AI quality indicator
studies.ai_system: AI-based real-time quality indicator for cardiac POCUS
studies.finding: Students using the AI quality indicator had higher median overall scores (P = 0.002) and a relative risk of 2.3 (95% CI: 1.10, 4.93, P = 0.03) for obtaining correct cardiac views, with better image quality.
studies.limitation: Small single-course study; tool also used during test, so skill gain without AI unclear; allocation method not stated.
studies.title: The effect of real-time EF automatic tool on cardiac ultrasound performance among medical students.

studies.design: Exam benchmark compared with student performance
studies.humans: Medical students taking German State Examinations
studies.finding: 630 questions from 2022 German Medical State Examinations. GPT-4 scored 88.1%, Bing 86.0% and GPT-3.5-Turbo 65.7% versus a student average of 74.6%; GPT-4 and Bing significantly outperformed students.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; student comparison uses aggregate averages.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence in Medical Education: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT, Bing, and Medical Students in Germany.

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial with rheumatology vignettes
studies.finding: Students using ChatGPT-4o plus traditional resources identified the correct top diagnosis more often than controls (77.5% vs. 32.4%; adjusted OR 7.0), and exceeded LLM-only performance (77.5% vs. 71.6%). Completion time increased with the LLM (505 vs. 287 s).
studies.limitation: Small sample of students solving three vignettes.
studies.title: Large language models enhance diagnostic reasoning of medical students in rheumatology: a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Single-blind randomised controlled pilot trial, three arms
studies.humans: Medical students with no prior FCU experience
studies.finding: 66 medical students were randomised to AI-enabled, VR-based or traditional instructor-led focused cardiac ultrasound training, assessed by RACE score. Traditional scored highest (15.77) versus AI (13.39) and VR (13.23), but AI was non-inferior (95% CI -∞ to 3.60; p < 0.001). Time to optimal A4C view was 158 ± 99.1 s for AI versus 199 ± 115.1 s traditional (p = 0.591).
studies.limitation: Small pilot trial in novice students; non-inferiority despite lower mean scores.
studies.title: Effectiveness of traditional, artificial intelligence-assisted, and virtual reality training modalities for focused cardiac ultrasound skill acquisition: a randomised controlled study.

studies.design: Mixed methods blinded web survey comparing ChatGPT- vs expert-generated script concordance tests
studies.humans: Psychiatry clinical experts (SCT authors); 102 clinician-educator and resident raters
studies.finding: Three ChatGPT-generated SCTs were compared with three expert-created SCTs by 102 respondents. There were no significant differences in scenario (P=.84), clinical questions (P=.99) and expert opinion (P=.07), and respondents struggled to tell them apart.
studies.limitation: Only 3 SCTs per group, subjective ratings, single specialty and region.
studies.title: Using ChatGPT in Psychiatry to Design Script Concordance Tests in Undergraduate Medical Education: Mixed Methods Study.

studies.design: Masked survey study rating MCQ quality
studies.humans: Committee of expert examination writers (rated by 10 ophthalmologists)
studies.finding: Generation of ophthalmology board-style MCQs. GPT-4 and expert-committee questions received median scores of 9 and 9 for combined scores, appropriateness, clarity and relevance (P > .99), 8 and 9 for discriminative power (P = .52), and 8 and 8 for suitability for trainees (P > .99).
studies.limitation: Subjective Likert ratings with moderate interrater reliability; question performance in real exams not assessed.
studies.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Generate Multiple-Choice Questions for Ophthalmology Education.

studies.design: Non-randomised controlled trial
studies.ai_system: DeepSeek V3 and R1 LLM-assisted problem-based learning
studies.finding: Hematology residency PBL training with versus without DeepSeek assistance, assessed by five standardized examinations and a survey. The DeepSeek-assisted group outperformed in four of five competency domains (Exams I, III, IV, V) and achieved higher total examination scores, with no significant difference in clinical skills (Exam II).
studies.limitation: Non-randomised design at a single programme with small groups; numeric exam scores not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Application of DeepSeek-assisted problem-based learning in hematology residency training.

studies.design: Comparison of LLM scores with student scores on course assessments
studies.finding: Answering multiple-choice and final exam questions in an introductory biomedical and health informatics course. All LLMs scored between the 50th and 75th percentiles of students.
studies.limitation: Informatics course knowledge exam rather than a clinical task; mostly non-medical students.
studies.title: Results and implications for generative AI in a large introductory biomedical and health informatics course.

studies.design: Prospective mixed-methods study, intervention vs control groups
studies.humans: Radiology residents and fellows (28 intervention, 29 control)
studies.finding: Trainees did simulated PACS-based reporting with or without the RADHawk recommender over a month's rotation. The intervention group reduced case report time by -162 s per case and increased accuracy scores by 14% compared with controls. They also reported lower mental demand (P=0.030).
studies.limitation: Single-department study with simulated reporting; allocation not described as randomised.
studies.title: RADHawk-an AI-based knowledge recommender to support precision education, improve reporting productivity, and reduce cognitive load.

studies.design: Two-site single-blind randomized controlled trial
studies.finding: 247 students were randomized to 2.5 months of AI-standardized OSCE training or standard training. ASCE users scored higher on the faculty OSCE (median 11.4 vs. 10.7; P = 0.02).
studies.limitation: Small absolute score difference; students rather than practising clinicians.
studies.title: AI-Standardized Clinical Examination Training on OSCE Performance.

studies.design: Exam question benchmark against resident normative data
studies.finding: GPT-4 answered 251 of 396 OITE questions correctly (63.4%) versus 46.3% for GPT-3.5. GPT-4's performance was most comparable to an average third-year orthopedic resident, while GPT-3.5 performed below an average orthopedic intern.
studies.limitation: Comparison to historical resident averages on exam questions, not clinical tasks.
studies.title: The Rapid Development of Artificial Intelligence: GPT-4's Performance on Orthopedic Surgery Board Questions.

studies.design: Exam question benchmark against historical human performance
studies.finding: Models answered part 1 FRCOphth MCQ practice questions. ChatGPT surpassed historical human pass marks and examination performance, while Bard underperformed.
studies.limitation: Comparison with historical exam statistics only; no numbers reported in abstract.
studies.title: Performance of ChatGPT and Bard on the official part 1 FRCOphth practice questions.

studies.design: Prospective comparative study of mock national selection interview
studies.humans: 8 UK doctors applying for neurosurgical training
studies.finding: ChatGPT and eight applicants answered neurosurgical selection interview questions scored by consultants. For overall score, ChatGPT fell behind six human competitors and did not exceed any individual who achieved training positions.
studies.limitation: Very small sample; ChatGPT answers delivered via virtual template, limiting blinding.
studies.title: Can ChatGPT outperform a neurosurgical trainee? A prospective comparative study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional exam comparison
studies.finding: Ophthalmology resident training exam questions. ChatGPT answered 37 of 69 correctly (53.62%) versus overall resident accuracy of 50.37% (43.49% to 60.05% by year), ranking 292nd among residents and below the average 3rd-year resident.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only, single ChatGPT version, small question set.
studies.title: Performance of Chatgpt in ophthalmology exam; human versus AI.

studies.design: Mixed-methods study including LLM vs human comparison on exam questions
studies.humans: Undergraduates, master's students and ophthalmology residents
studies.finding: On 130 ophthalmology examination questions, ChatGPT o1-preview achieved the highest accuracy rate of 73%, outperforming other LLMs and professional groups such as undergraduates and master's students.
studies.limitation: Comparison with residents is not clearly reported; exam questions only.
studies.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Large Language Models in Providing Patient Education for Chinese Patients With Ocular Myasthenia Gravis: Mixed Methods Study.

studies.design: Cluster quasi-randomized controlled trial
studies.ai_system: AI-based real-time intraoperative anatomy visualization system
studies.finding: Students annotated pancreatic regions on 6 laparoscopic/robotic images before and after observation training with or without AI visualization. Recall improved more with AI (ΔRecall: 0.112 vs 0.013, P = .020); the primary outcome Dice improved more with AI (ΔDice: 0.087 vs 0.028) but not significantly (P = .097); precision did not differ (P = .746).
studies.limitation: Quasi-randomized design; primary outcome not significant; number of students not stated in abstract.
studies.title: Effectiveness of artificial intelligence-based visualization for surgical anatomy education: A cluster quasirandomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of ChatGPT scoring with faculty grades
studies.finding: Grading of 111 pre-clinical students' critical appraisal assignments. Overall agreement between ChatGPT and faculty was 67% (OR = 2.53, P < 0.001), mean AUCPR 0.69, with ChatGPT internal-consistency reliability of 0.64 and a fivefold reduction in faculty time.
studies.limitation: Single institution, faculty grade treated as reference; number of faculty not stated.
studies.title: Comparing Scoring Consistency of Large Language Models with Faculty for Formative Assessments in Medical Education.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of ChatGPT with exam candidates on 400 board exam questions
studies.finding: ChatGPT answered 400 questions from four years of the Turkish Orthopedics and Traumatology Board written exam. It scored higher than 619 (98.7%) of 627 candidates and significantly above the mean in all exams (p=0.012, p=0.012, p=0.002, p=0.005).
studies.limitation: Written theoretical exam questions only; compared with candidate mean scores rather than practice performance.
studies.title: Can ChatGPT pass the Turkish Orthopedics and Traumatology Board Examination? Turkish orthopedic surgeons versus artificial intelligence.
studies.source: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES

studies.design: Comparison on in-training exam questions
studies.finding: On 137 General Medicine In-Training Examination questions in Japanese, GPT-4 scored 70.1% versus residents' mean of 55.8% (P<.001). GPT-4 scored 17.2 points lower on easy problems (P=.007) but higher on normal and difficult ones.
studies.limitation: Text-only exam questions; number of residents not stated.
studies.title: Performance Comparison of ChatGPT-4 and Japanese Medical Residents in the General Medicine In-Training Examination: Comparison Study.

studies.design: Exam benchmark against resident norms
studies.finding: ChatGPT-3.5 answered 360 Orthopedic In-Service Training Exam questions, scoring 55.8%, 47.7% and 54% for 2020-2022. Against the annual technical reports for resident physicians, it performed around the PGY-1 level.
studies.limitation: Comparison is with published resident norms rather than a direct head-to-head test; outdated model.
studies.title: Assessing ChatGPT's orthopedic in-service training exam performance and applicability in the field.
studies.source: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research

studies.design: Cross-sectional MCQ comparison
studies.finding: Answering 304 MCQs from medical courses. ChatGPT-4 achieved a higher overall score (73.7%) than students (66.7%).
