studies.limitation: MCQ exam questions from a single institution; number of students not stated.
studies.title: Comparing the Performance of ChatGPT-4 and Medical Students on MCQs at Varied Levels of Bloom's Taxonomy.
studies.source: Advances in medical education and practice

studies.design: Blinded rating of GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and a pathologist's answers to 15 board-style questions
studies.humans: One staff pathologist who recently passed licensing exams
studies.finding: On 15 pathology board-level questions scored by 15 pathologists, GPT-3.5 performed at a similar level to the staff pathologist while GPT-4 outperformed both. Reviewers could identify GPT-3.5 answers in all but one question.
studies.limitation: Only 15 questions and a single human comparator; no numeric scores reported in abstract.
studies.title: Assessment of Pathology Domain-Specific Knowledge of ChatGPT and Comparison to Human Performance.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of ChatGPT on a pulmonology exam vs students' past results
studies.finding: On a French pulmonology examination, ChatGPT without contextualization failed to pass, while the contextualized version passed, outperforming 139 (62.1%) medical students. ChatGPT performed worse on multiple choice questions, better on low and intermediate difficulty questions, while students did better on highly challenging questions.
studies.limitation: Single institution exam, ChatGPT-3.5 only, non-English questions.
studies.title: Appraisal of ChatGPT's Aptitude for Medical Education: Comparative Analysis With Third-Year Medical Students in a Pulmonology Examination.

studies.design: Cross-sectional evaluation of LLMs on 99 nephrology board renewal self-assessment questions, compared with nephrology residents
studies.finding: On 99 nephrology board renewal self-assessment questions, overall correct answer rates were 31.3% for GPT-3.5, 54.5% for GPT-4 and 32.3% for Bard. GPT-4's performance was between third- and fourth-year nephrology residents.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; small question set; resident numbers and scores not reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Performance of ChatGPT and Bard in self-assessment questions for nephrology board renewal.

studies.design: Comparative study; trainees completed manual and AI-assisted reading tests
studies.finding: 104 trainees interpreted digital cervical cytology with and without AI assistance. Mean interpretation scores were higher with AI (81.97 ± 16.670 vs. 67.98 ± 21.469, p < 0.001), and averaged pairwise κ improved from 0.535 to 0.731.
studies.limitation: Single training programme with test-based assessment rather than clinical practice; reading order and design not clearly controlled.
studies.title: Integration of AI-Assisted in Digital Cervical Cytology Training: A Comparative Study.
studies.source: Cytopathology : official journal of the British Society for Clinical Cytology

studies.design: Benchmark of LLMs on 450 single-choice questions compared with human students
studies.finding: LLMs answered 450 expert-validated TCM questions on knowledge, classical texts and clinical decision-making. Models achieved comparable overall accuracy to human students (p > 0.05). Humans were significantly more robust in TCM Diagnostics and Syndrome Differentiation.
studies.limitation: Exam-style questions only; number of students and exact scores not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A triaxial benchmark for assessing responses from large language models in traditional Chinese medicine.

studies.design: Questionnaire-based comparison on exam questions
studies.finding: 228 BCSC refractive surgery self-assessment questions. OpenAI-o1 scored 91.2% and ChatGPT-4o 86.4%, versus an average of 77% for 1983 human users; both models significantly outperformed humans.
studies.limitation: Exam questions, text-only; human data are historical aggregate averages.
studies.title: ChatGPT-4o and OpenAI-o1: A Comparative Analysis of Its Accuracy in Refractive Surgery.

studies.design: Comparison of LLMs with average surgeon performance on a maintenance of certification exam
studies.humans: Fellowship-trained shoulder and elbow surgeons (average exam performance)
studies.finding: On the 2023 ASES MOC exam, humans outperformed GPT-4 overall (75.3% vs. 60.2%, P = .012) and on image-based questions (73.9% vs. 53.2%). On text-only questions, humans outperformed ChatGPT 3.5 (76.4% vs. 60.8%), with no significant difference versus GPT-4 (76.4% vs. 66.7%).
studies.limitation: Exam questions rather than clinical care; human performance taken as aggregate averages.
studies.title: ChatGPT performance on the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons maintenance of certification exam.
studies.source: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on a medical biochemistry exam
studies.finding: On a 79-question biochemistry term exam, ChatGPT scored 140 out of 200, outperforming almost all students and ranking fifth in the class. It scored 92% on information-based MCQs but 52% on clinical scenario-based questions.
studies.limitation: Single exam at one institution with students, not physicians; basic science content.
studies.title: Is ChatGPT's Knowledge and Interpretative Ability Comparable to First Professional MBBS (Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery) Students of India in Taking a Medical Biochemistry Examination?

studies.design: Reader comparison on CBCT test images
studies.humans: 23 residency students and two experienced implantologists
studies.finding: Lekholm and Zarb bone quality classification on 100 CBCT test slices. The DL model (accuracy 86.00%) outperformed human assessors across all parameters; residency students and one implantologist had low recall for bone type 2 (48.15% and 40.74%).
studies.limitation: Small test set of 100 images; single-source dataset.
studies.title: A Comparison of Deep Learning vs. Dental Implantologists in Cone-Beam Computed Tomography-Based Bone Quality Classification.
studies.source: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

studies.design: Comparison of LLMs and residents on a multiple-choice progress test
studies.humans: Family Medicine residents at University of Toronto
studies.finding: On a 108-question Family Medicine progress test, GPT-4 answered 82.4% correctly and GPT-3.5 57.4%. Average resident performance was 56.9% (95% CI 56.2%-57.6%); GPT-3.5 was similar to the average resident (P=.16) and GPT-4 exceeded the top-performing resident (P<.001).
studies.limitation: Multiple-choice knowledge test only, not clinical performance; number of residents not stated.
studies.title: Assessment of Resident and AI Chatbot Performance on the University of Toronto Family Medicine Residency Progress Test: Comparative Study.

studies.design: LLM performance on in-service exam compared with national resident norm tables
studies.finding: GPT-4 scored 63% overall on the 2022 Plastic Surgery In-service Examination, and 68% with MC-with-explanation prompting. This placed it in the 93rd percentile for first-year but only the 15th percentile for sixth-year residents; GPT-3.5 scored 58%.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; comparison to aggregate norm tables rather than concurrent residents.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Augmentation: Performance of GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 on the Plastic Surgery In-service Examination.
studies.source: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on questions and clinical cases
studies.finding: Answering validated paediatric surgery questions and clinical cases. ChatGPT-4.0 had a median score of 13.75 and ChatGPT-3.5 a median of 8.75, against 8.13 for residents. ChatGPT's accuracy declined on more complex questions.
studies.limitation: Small single cross-sectional sample using exam-style questions.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence in clinical practice: a cross-sectional survey of paediatric surgery residents' perspectives.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 15 MCI triage scenarios
studies.finding: Using START triage across 15 scenarios, Google Bard had accuracy of 60% and ChatGPT 26.67%. Medical students had accuracy of 64.3% in a previous study, with no significant difference from Google Bard (p = 0.211).
studies.limitation: Student data came from a historical study, and only 15 scenarios were used.
studies.title: Performance of Google bard and ChatGPT in mass casualty incidents triage.
studies.source: The American journal of emergency medicine

studies.design: Single-institution retrospective study scoring 168 first-year students' free-text H&P notes against an 85-element rubric
studies.finding: ChatGPT and standardized patients scored medical students' free-text history and physical notes against an 85-element rubric (14,280 scores). The ChatGPT incorrect scoring rate was 1.0% versus 7.2% for standardized patients, and the mean incorrect scoring rate was 12 (SD 11) versus 85 (SD 74; P=.002).
studies.limitation: Single-institution retrospective study; the comparators were standardized patients rather than physicians.
studies.title: Assessing the Ability of a Large Language Model to Score Free-Text Medical Student Clinical Notes: Quantitative Study.

studies.design: Comparison of AI-generated and expert-created exam questions administered to 103 students
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Advanced Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet
studies.finding: AI-generated and expert-created case-based pharmacology questions were given to 103 medical students in a real exam. No statistically significant differences were found in correct response rate or discrimination index, although 19 out of 60 AI-generated questions were deemed unusable.
studies.limitation: Small number of questions; the number of expert educators is not stated in the abstract.
studies.title: Generative AI vs. human expertise: a comparative analysis of case-based rational pharmacotherapy question generation.

studies.design: Questionnaire study of 100 BCSC self-assessment questions; LLMs compared with resident user data
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-4o, Gemini, Gemini Advanced, Copilot
studies.finding: On 100 cataract and refractive surgery questions, ChatGPT-4o scored 84% (simple prompt) and 86% (contextualized prompt), Gemini Advanced 82%, Copilot 78%, ChatGPT-4 77% and Gemini 62%. The mean resident score was 77% (95% CI 75%-79%); only ChatGPT-4o significantly outperformed residents (P = .04).
studies.limitation: Exam multiple-choice questions only, not clinical practice; human comparison from aggregate question-bank data.
studies.title: Evaluating large language models vs residents in cataract and refractive surgery: comparative analysis using the American Academy of Ophthalmology Self-Assessment Program.
studies.source: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

studies.design: Pre-post study of students answering clinical cases independently, after viewing ChatGPT answers, and after group discussion
studies.finding: Forty medical students answered clinical cases independently, after reviewing ChatGPT answers, and after group discussion. Their responses shifted significantly to match ChatGPT's answers whether or not these were correct, and group discussion did not correct AI-induced misinformation.
studies.limitation: Small single-group study of students; no quantitative results reported in the abstract.
studies.title: Exploring Medical Student Trust in Generative Artificial Intelligence (ChatGPT) Versus Peers in Team-Based Learning.

studies.design: Comparative study of student ratings of AI versus tutor feedback
studies.finding: Second-year medical students (85 of 108 responding) rated feedback on a written assignment from their tutor and from ChatGPT. Tutor feedback was rated significantly higher in clarity (p < 0.001), relevance (p < 0.001), accuracy (p = 0.003) and overall usefulness (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Outcome is student perception; single institution; number of tutors not stated.
studies.title: Bytes versus brains: A comparative study of AI-generated feedback and human tutor feedback in medical education.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on national exam questions
studies.humans: Physicians from Italy, France, Spain and Portugal
studies.finding: Answering 600 national medical exam questions, with 17,144 physicians providing 221,574 answers. The assistant outperformed physicians in all countries (72-96% vs. 46-62%; p < 0.001) and across most domains. The exception was paediatrics (45% vs. 52%; p = 0.60).
studies.limitation: Exam-style questions answered on a voluntary digital platform, which does not reflect clinical performance.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Outperforms Physicians in General Medical Knowledge, Except in the Paediatrics Domain: A Cross-Sectional Study.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of feedback on written surgical scenarios, rated by residents and experts
studies.finding: Identifying errors and giving feedback on written surgical scenarios. Residents rated ChatGPT outputs useful 96.43% of times, comparable to surgeons B and C; an education expert gave ChatGPT a higher feedback quality median score of 8 vs. 7 and 7.5 for surgeons A and B, with no difference vs. surgeon C (8).
studies.limitation: Only three surgeons and text-based scenarios rather than live surgery.
studies.title: Surgeons vs ChatGPT: Assessment and Feedback Performance Based on Real Surgical Scenarios.

studies.design: Cross-sectional exam comparison
studies.finding: On a medical physiology university exam, ChatGPT scored a median (IQR) of 75% (66-84%) versus 56% (43-65%) for students (P < 0.001). ChatGPT passed (100% success) whereas 29% (n = 7) of students failed.
studies.limitation: Single small exam with 24 students; exam questions rather than clinical tasks.
studies.title: The conversational AI "ChatGPT" outperforms medical students on a physiology university examination.

studies.design: Cross-sectional blinded comparison of AI- vs attending-written questions
studies.humans: Attending radiologists (question writers); 21 radiology residents as raters
studies.finding: ChatGPT-generated board-style MCQs were compared with attending-written MCQs. Perceived quality did not differ (M=6.93 vs M=7.08; p=0.15), nor did correct answer percentages (57% vs 59%; p=0.78); ChatGPT questions were less often thought to be attending-written (57% vs 71%; p=0.04).
studies.limitation: Small single-institution study with 17 vs 11 questions and 21 residents.
studies.title: Leveraging ChatGPT for Enhancing Learning in Radiology Resident Education.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to an inexperienced observer
studies.finding: Classifying third molar–mandibular canal relationship on panoramic radiographs. ResNet-152 accuracy was 88.86% and VGG-19 85.28% versus 62.53% for the dental student.
studies.limitation: Single student comparator and small image set (142 images).
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence for Classifying the Relationship between Impacted Third Molar and Mandibular Canal on Panoramic Radiographs.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on board exam question bank
studies.finding: On 93 text-based rhinology board questions, ChatGPT 3.5 scored 45.2% (8th percentile) and GPT-4 86.0% (66th percentile) relative to question bank users, primarily otolaryngology residents. GPT-4 answered image-based questions correctly 64.7% of the time.
studies.limitation: Comparison against aggregate question bank averages of unspecified users rather than a defined clinician sample.
studies.title: Comparative Performance of ChatGPT 3.5 and GPT4 on Rhinology Standardized Board Examination Questions.

studies.design: Exam comparison of ChatGPT and residents
studies.finding: On a 100-question exam modelled after EDAIC Part I, ChatGPT answered 71 correctly versus a median resident score of 70 (IQR 67-73). ChatGPT ranked eighth in Group J (median 67) and 47th in Group S (median 73).
studies.limitation: Single centre; multiple-choice exam questions only.
studies.title: Can Artificial Intelligence be Successful as an Anaesthesiology and Reanimation Resident?
studies.source: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation

studies.design: Comparison of ChatGPT-4 answers on 1292 Plastic Surgery In-Service Examination questions (2018-2023) against national resident percentiles
studies.finding: ChatGPT-4 answered 961 (74.4%) of 1292 text-based in-service exam questions correctly, ranking between the 61st and 97th percentiles of all residents. It outperformed 80.7% of residents on average and scored above the 97th percentile among first-year residents, while being comparable with sixth-year integrated residents (55.7th percentile on average).
studies.limitation: Multiple-choice exam questions with image-based items excluded; comparison against aggregate resident percentiles rather than clinical performance.
studies.title: ChatGPT-4 Surpasses Residents: A Study of Artificial Intelligence Competency in Plastic Surgery In-service Examinations and Its Advancements from ChatGPT-3.5.
studies.source: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open

studies.design: Cross-sectional exam comparison
studies.finding: 30 otolaryngology board-style questions. ChatGPT outperformed MS1, MS2 and MS3 (p = <0.001, 0.003, 0.019), PGY4 and PGY5 residents outperformed ChatGPT (p = 0.033 and 0.002), and there was no statistical difference for MS4 and PGY1-3.
studies.limitation: Only 30 questions and a small single-sample of trainees; tests rote knowledge.
studies.title: Is ChatGPT 3.5 smarter than Otolaryngology trainees? A comparison study of board style exam questions.

studies.design: Comparison of LLM exam scores with medical student scores
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-4 Omni, Gemini Advanced, Le Chat, DeepSeek R1
studies.finding: LLMs were scored on clinical pharmacology and therapeutics exams and the European Prescribing Exam against medical students. LLMs outperformed M1 students and matched L3 and M2 students on local exams, and significantly outperformed students in both knowledge and prescribing sections of EuroPE+.
studies.limitation: Exam questions rather than clinical practice; student numbers not stated.
studies.title: Evaluating and leveraging large language models in clinical pharmacology and therapeutics assessment: From exam takers to exam shapers.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of graded short-answer responses
studies.finding: Short-answer assessment problems graded by six tutors. ChatGPT scored a mean 3.29 out of 5 vs 2.38 for minimally passing students (P = .008), but was outperformed by historical class averages (mean 3.67, P = .018).
studies.limitation: Small number of problems from a single program; student numbers not stated.
studies.title: Examining the Threat of ChatGPT to the Validity of Short Answer Assessments in an Undergraduate Medical Program.
studies.source: Journal of medical education and curricular development

studies.design: Comparative study of AI- vs faculty-written physiology MCQs administered to medical students
studies.finding: Psychometric quality of physiology MCQs was compared. Chatbot MCQs had a higher difficulty index (0.64 ± 0.22) than faculty MCQs (0.47 ± 0.19; P < 0.0001), with no significant difference in discrimination index (P = 0.17); faculty MCQs had fewer nonfunctional distractors (median 0 vs 1; P = 0.0063).
studies.limitation: Single discipline and institution; 50 items per group; number of faculty not stated.
studies.title: Faculty versus artificial intelligence chatbot: a comparative analysis of multiple-choice question quality in physiology.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of ChatGPT with medical doctors' exam scores
studies.humans: Medical doctors who took the 2022 Italian residency exam
studies.finding: ChatGPT answered 136 Italian Medical Residency Exam questions with 90.44% overall accuracy (92.45% clinical cases, 89.15% notional questions). Its performance was higher than 99.6% of the doctors who took the test.
studies.limitation: Exam questions rather than real clinical decisions; single exam.
studies.title: Exploring the potential of ChatGPT for clinical reasoning and decision-making: a cross-sectional study on the Italian Medical Residency Exam.

studies.design: Benchmark on 240 internal medicine board-style questions compared with human MKSAP users
studies.finding: LLMs answered 240 MKSAP internal medicine board-style questions. GPT-4.0 scored 77.5-80.7%, outperforming GPT-3.5, human respondents, LaMDA and Llama 2 in that order. GPT-4.0 outperformed human MKSAP users on every tested IM subject.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; human comparison uses aggregate MKSAP user data rather than a controlled cohort.
studies.title: Performance of Publicly Available Large Language Models on Internal Medicine Board-style Questions.

studies.design: Observational study comparing ChatGPT answers on Progress Test questions 2021-2023 with student scores
studies.humans: First- to sixth-year medical students from over 120 Brazilian universities
studies.finding: ChatGPT answered Brazilian Progress Test questions with average accuracy of 69.7%, 68.3%, and 67.2% in 2021, 2022, and 2023. It surpassed students from all medical years in the three tests.
studies.limitation: Exam multiple-choice questions only; student numbers and scores not detailed in the abstract.
studies.title: Performance of ChatGPT in Solving Questions From the Progress Test (Brazilian National Medical Exam): A Potential Artificial Intelligence Tool in Medical Practice.

studies.design: Comparison of LLMs and residents on in-service training exam questions
studies.finding: On 316 otorhinolaryngology in-service exam questions, GPT-4 scored 54.75%, Gemini 40.50% and Bing 37.00%. Senior residents outperformed all LLMs at 75.5%, while GPT-4 and Gemini performed similarly to junior residents (46.90%).
studies.limitation: Exam questions rather than clinical care; number of residents not stated.
studies.title: Evaluating the Performance of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Bing Compared with Resident Surgeons in the Otorhinolaryngology In-service Training Examination.

studies.design: Comparison of AI chatbots against resident percentiles on an in-service exam
studies.finding: On the 2019-2023 Plastic Surgery In-service Training Examination, ChatGPT-4.0 reached accuracy rates up to 79%. On the 2023 exam it ranked in the 95th percentile of first-year residents but the 12th percentile of sixth-year residents.
studies.limitation: Comparison is against normative percentiles on exam questions only.
studies.title: Unveiling the Potential of AI in Plastic Surgery Education: A Comparative Study of Leading AI Platforms' Performance on In-training Examinations.
studies.source: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of ChatGPT and residents on national exam questions
studies.finding: On 250 questions from the French orthopaedic and trauma surgery DES exams, ChatGPT-4o scored 74.8% versus 70.8% for residents (p = 0.32). ChatGPT-4 scored 58.8%.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; number of residents not stated.
studies.title: Comparing performances of french orthopaedic surgery residents with the artificial intelligence ChatGPT-4/4o in the French diploma exams of orthopaedic and trauma surgery.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of GPT-4 with chain-of-thought on a bilingual nuclear medicine specialty exam versus human examinees
studies.humans: Human doctors taking the Taiwanese Nuclear Medicine Specialty Exam
studies.finding: GPT-4 with chain-of-thought answered Taiwanese Nuclear Medicine Specialty Exam questions and was compared with human doctors. It often surpassed or matched human doctor performance in theoretical knowledge, clinical medicine and integrated questions but struggled with medical regulations questions. No numeric scores are reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only, with no quantitative results or human sample size given in the abstract.
studies.title: Performance of ChatGPT incorporated chain-of-thought method in bilingual nuclear medicine physician board examinations.

studies.design: Comparative cross-sectional exam study
studies.humans: Medical doctors taking Polish nephrology specialty exams
studies.finding: 1560 nephrology specialty exam questions. ChatGPT-4.0 achieved 69.84% accuracy versus 45.70% for ChatGPT-3.5 and the top results of medical doctors (85.73%, P = .0001); ChatGPT-4.0 scored higher than the average of human exam results.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; human comparator from historical exam results.
studies.title: The potential of ChatGPT in medicine: an example analysis of nephrology specialty exams in Poland.

studies.design: Cross-sectional benchmark of LLMs on Orthopedic In-Training Examination questions compared against resident percentile data
studies.finding: ChatGPT and BARD answered 390 text-only OITE multiple choice questions; BARD answered more correctly than ChatGPT (58% vs 54%). Compared with prior resident data, the AI ranked in the 42nd-96th percentile for PGY1s, 27th-58th for PGY2s, 3rd-29th for PGY3s, 1st-21st for PGY4s and 1st-17th for PGY5s, reaching about a second-year resident level.
studies.limitation: Image questions excluded and residents compared via historical exam data rather than a head-to-head study.
studies.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Performs at a Second-Year Orthopedic Resident Level.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on multiple-choice exams
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT, Bing AI, Bard AI, Perplexity AI, ChatSonic
studies.finding: Chatbots and first-year medical students answered histology and embryology multiple-choice questions. All five chatbots showed better results than the students on both tests.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; no numeric results reported in abstract; chatbot answers inconsistent on retest.
studies.title: Comparing the performance of artificial intelligence learning models to medical students in solving histology and embryology multiple choice questions.
studies.source: Annals of anatomy = Anatomischer Anzeiger : official organ of the Anatomische Gesellschaft

studies.design: Cross-sectional benchmark against historical student performance
studies.finding: Surgical text and image questions from GMLE and USMLE. GPT-4 outperformed students on text (83.7% vs. 67.8%; p < 0.001) and image questions (78% vs. 67.4%; p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Comparison against historical average student scores, not a concurrent human cohort; exam questions only.
studies.title: Benchmarking Vision Capabilities of Large Language Models in Surgical Examination Questions.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of human vs GPT-3.5 discrimination of real and synthetic resident feedback
studies.finding: Faculty raters and GPT-3.5 judged whether 220 feedback comments were human-written or GPT-generated. Human raters were more accurate (80.5 %) than GPT-3.5 (50 %), and agreement between them was low (k=-0.237).
studies.limitation: Only two human raters, a single program, and an older model.
studies.title: Differentiating between GPT-generated and human-written feedback for radiology residents.

studies.design: Comparison of residents learning with a custom GPT versus traditional resources, plus accuracy and satisfaction evaluation
studies.ai_system: Custom GPT built on teaching resources
studies.finding: Residents using the custom GPT achieved better test scores than those using traditional resources (p < 0.05), though fewer perfect scores were obtained. The custom GPT itself had 83.6% accuracy on clinical questions.
studies.limitation: Abstract gives no sample sizes, randomisation details or effect sizes for the learning comparison.
studies.title: Accuracy, satisfaction, and impact of custom GPT in acquiring clinical knowledge: Potential for AI-assisted medical education.

studies.design: Cross-sectional evaluation on 151 radiology exam multiple-choice questions
studies.finding: On 151 radiology exam questions for medical students, GPT-4 achieved 88.1% overall accuracy and GPT-3.5 67.6%. GPT-4 outperformed medical students on both lower-order and higher-order questions.
studies.limitation: Text-only exam questions; student performance figures and numbers not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Large language models (LLMs) in radiology exams for medical students: Performance and consequences.
studies.source: RoFo : Fortschritte auf dem Gebiete der Rontgenstrahlen und der Nuklearmedizin

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 299 self-assessment questions
studies.humans: One adult reconstruction fellow and one senior attending arthroplasty surgeon
studies.finding: On 299 OrthoBullets adult reconstruction questions, ChatGPT achieved 66.9% accuracy compared to 84.3% for the Fellow and 85.3% for the Attending. ChatGPT did better on text-only than image-based questions.
studies.limitation: Exam questions with only two human comparators.
studies.title: Exploring ChatGPT's Efficacy in Orthopaedic Arthroplasty Questions Compared to Adult Reconstruction Surgeons.

studies.design: Descriptive comparison on simulated board exam items
studies.humans: A medical student, a resident, a consultant and an EBIR holder
studies.finding: GPT-4o correctly answered 248 of 370 CIRSE Prep items (67.0%). On 50 items, the medical student answered 46.0%, the resident 42.0%, the consultant 50.0% and the EBIR holder 74.0% correctly.
studies.limitation: Only four human participants answering a 50-item subset.
studies.title: GPT-4o’s competency in answering the simulated written European Board of Interventional Radiology exam compared to a medical student and experts in Germany and its ability to generate exam items on interventional radiology: a descriptive study.
studies.source: Journal of educational evaluation for health professions

studies.design: Cross-sectional exam benchmark against trainees
studies.finding: On 294 EPSITE questions, DeepSeek scored 85.0%, Copilot 55.4% and Bard 48.0%, versus a trainee average of 60.1%. DeepSeek significantly outperformed trainees (p < 0.0001), while Bard was outperformed by trainees across all training levels (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Exam questions rather than clinical care; models assessed at different times.
studies.title: Pediatric surgical trainees and artificial intelligence: a comparative analysis of DeepSeek, Copilot, Google Bard and pediatric surgeons' performance on the European Pediatric Surgical In-Training Examinations (EPSITE).

studies.design: Benchmark of 15 LLMs on radiation oncology in-training exam questions compared with resident averages
studies.ai_system: 15 LLMs (GPT, Claude-3, Gemini-2.0, Llama, DeepSeek-R1) with and without RAG
studies.finding: LLMs answered 298 questions from the 2021 ACR radiation oncology in-training exam. Six models outscored graduating residents (P < .01); top reasoning models (GPT-4o1, DeepSeek-R1 91.6%, o3-mini 86.6%) surpassed graduating resident averages by 17.7%-20% (P < .01).
studies.limitation: Exam-question benchmark using historical resident averages rather than clinical tasks.
studies.title: RadOncRAG: A Novel Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework Improves Large Language Model Benchmark Performance in Radiation Oncology.

studies.design: Cross-sectional evaluation on neurosurgery board question bank against human performance
studies.finding: On 2,120 non-imaging SANS questions, ChatGPT had an accuracy of 50.4% (1,068/2,120). It performed worse than humans overall and in no subject did it perform better than humans, and its accuracy was below that required to pass.
studies.limitation: Human comparator is aggregate question-bank performance with no number reported; imaging questions were excluded.
studies.title: Educational Limitations of ChatGPT in Neurosurgery Board Preparation.

studies.design: Single-blind parallel-group randomised controlled trial, AI virtual patient training vs reading module
studies.ai_system: SOPHIE, generative AI virtual patient with automated feedback
studies.humans: Medical, nursing and physician assistant students and practicing clinicians
studies.finding: Fifty-one students and clinicians were randomised to 30 minutes of SOPHIE training or a reading module, with serious illness communication skills rated by blinded SPs and raters. SOPHIE participants showed greater improvement in overall communication score (β=.09, 95% CI .04-.14; P=.001), and in Empower (β=.11), Be Explicit (β=.08) and Empathize (β=.07). They also reported higher confidence (4.31 vs 3.83; P=.009).
studies.limitation: Small sample of mixed professions and training levels, short intervention with immediate post-test only, outcomes assessed in simulated encounters.
studies.title: Effects of a Generative AI Virtual Patient on Serious Illness Communication Skills: Randomized Controlled Trial.

studies.design: Crossover randomized pilot study
studies.finding: Students prepared for pathology small-group sessions with the custom GPT or with conventional resources. SDL rubric scores were 10.3 vs. 9.4 out of 12 and discussion scores were 14.9 vs. 13.7 out of 16 (both P<.001). Delayed retention did not differ (P=.052).
studies.limitation: Single-site, unregistered pilot with voluntary participants.
studies.title: Curriculum-Aligned Conversational AI to Support Pathology Self-Directed Learning in Preclinical Medical Students: A Crossover Randomized Pilot Study.

studies.design: Prospective study: LLM exam benchmark plus resident crossover with and without LLM assistance, 1-month washout
studies.ai_system: ERNIE Bot 4.5 Turbo and 10 other LLMs
studies.finding: ERNIE Bot 4.5 Turbo scored 98.00% on the Chinese ophthalmology exam and significantly outperformed all residents (P = 0.001). With LLM assistance, residents' mean accuracy on the text exam rose from 60.75% to 79.00% (P = 0.001). On keratitis image classification, assistance did not improve accuracy (41.25% vs. 40.56%, P = 0.662).
studies.limitation: Only 10 residents at a single centre, using exam questions rather than real patients.
studies.title: Large Language Models for Ophthalmology Training in China: A Prospective Evaluation.

studies.design: Randomized assessor-blinded wait-list-controlled trial
studies.ai_system: AI-driven virtual patient platform for colposcopy training
studies.finding: Residents trained with traditional teaching plus an AI platform versus traditional teaching only. At 1 month the AI group scored higher in Case Analysis (78.57 ± 3.72 vs 71.03 ± 5.82, p < 0.001), Diagnostic Justification (81.63 ± 6.21 vs 74.13 ± 6.77) and Communication Performance (80.97 ± 3.90 vs 75.77 ± 6.08); operative competence did not differ (p = 0.113).
studies.limitation: Small sample from two affiliated hospitals with short-term outcomes; both groups converged by 3 months.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced colposcopy training improves diagnostic reasoning and communication competencies: A randomized controlled study.
studies.source: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction

studies.design: Exploratory observational comparison of ChatGPT against published trainee scores on validated instruments
studies.humans: Medical students, internal medicine residents, geriatric medicine fellows (literature-reported results)
studies.finding: On the UCLA geriatrics knowledge test ChatGPT outperformed medical students, residents and geriatric fellows (14.7 vs 11.3). On geriatrics attitude, ChatGPT's mean total score was lower than trainees' (2.7 vs 3.7).
studies.limitation: Human comparators taken from historical literature rather than tested concurrently; single model evaluated.
studies.title: ChatGPT's Attitude, Knowledge, and Clinical Application in Geriatrics Practice and Education: Exploratory Observational Study.

studies.design: Blinded expert rating of multiple-choice questions written by LLMs versus physicians
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT, GPT4o, Google Gemini and Gemini Advanced
studies.humans: Physicians drafting questions; experts validating them
studies.finding: Four experts rated 90 head and neck ultrasound MCQs. LLM questions were broadly comparable to physician drafts, with Gemini differing significantly on relevance, suitability and rationale, and ChatGPT only on suitability. LLM questions scored significantly lower than expert-validated questions on all criteria.
studies.limitation: Small question set and only four raters.
studies.title: Evaluation of Multiple-Choice Tests in Head and Neck Ultrasound Created by Physicians and Large Language Models.

studies.design: Cross-sectional exam benchmark against resident national averages
studies.finding: Answering the 193-question 2022 Family Medicine In-Training Exam. ChatGPT 4.0 scored 86.5%, above the PGY-3 residents' mean of 68.4%, while ChatGPT 3.5 (66.3%) and Bard (64.2%) scored below it.
studies.limitation: Multiple-choice exam questions compared with historical national averages rather than a direct clinical task.
studies.title: Performance of Language Models on the Family Medicine In-Training Exam.

studies.design: Cross-sectional benchmark of LLMs against nationwide resident exam performance
studies.finding: Korean Society of Radiology in-training exam (776 questions). On image-based questions GPT-4 Turbo and GPT-4o (41.8% and 48.2%) were comparable to 1st-year residents (43.3%) but lower than 2nd- to 4th-year residents (56.0%-63.9%). On text-only questions the models (69.0% and 77.9%) outperformed residents of all years (44.7%-57.5%).
studies.limitation: Multiple-choice exam questions rather than clinical practice; resident numbers not stated.
studies.title: Performance of GPT-4 Turbo and GPT-4o in Korean Society of Radiology In-Training Examinations.

studies.design: GPT-5 answered 2024 OITE; compared with published resident scores
studies.finding: On the 203-question 2024 OITE, GPT-5 achieved 78.3% accuracy, exceeding the mean PGY-5 resident score (73%). However, hallucinated or misrepresented references occurred in 33% of 88 audited responses.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only; comparison against published aggregate resident scores without statistical testing.
studies.title: Accuracy Is Not Enough: Reasoning and Reference Reliability in Orthopaedic Large Language Model (LLM) Applications.

studies.design: Exam question benchmark compared with national resident averages
studies.finding: GPT-4v and GPT-4o answered 1,136 DXIT radiology in-training exam questions. GPT-4o and GPT-4v achieved accuracies of 73.5% and 69.3%, exceeding the PGY-3 resident national average of 61.9%. On image-based questions they scored 55.6% and 50.3%, below radiology trainees.
studies.limitation: Comparison against historical national averages rather than a direct head-to-head study, using publicly available questions.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence in Radiology: Performance of ChatGPT-4v and GPT-4o on Diagnostic Radiology in-Training (DXIT) Examination Questions.
studies.source: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of LLMs and residents on 282 institutional in-training exam questions
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, Claude 4 Opus, Claude 4.1 Opus, Gemini 2.5 Pro
studies.finding: On 282 radiology in-training multiple-choice questions, Gemini 2.5 Pro achieved the highest overall accuracy (83.0%), followed by ChatGPT-5 (82.3%), versus 78.2% for radiology residents. For image-based questions, residents achieved the highest accuracy (80.4%), followed by ChatGPT-5 (73.6%).
studies.limitation: Exam questions from a single institution; number of residents not stated and no statistical test of LLM versus resident reported.
studies.title: Performance of Large Language Models on Radiology Residency In-Training Examination Questions.

studies.design: Exam comparison
studies.humans: Dermatology residents across four seniority levels
studies.finding: ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0 were compared with dermatology residents on a 100-question residency exam. Second, third and fourth-year residents scored significantly higher than ChatGPT 3.5 (p = 0.038, 0.041, 0.020). ChatGPT 4.0 was similar to first- and third-year residents but worse than second (p = 0.037) and fourth-year residents (p = 0.029).
studies.limitation: Small 100-question multiple-choice exam; the number of residents is not reported.
studies.title: The Performance of AI in Dermatology Exams: The Exam Success and Limits of ChatGPT.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison of LLM- vs clinician-generated MCQs rated by experts and tested on practitioners
studies.humans: Clinicians writing MCQs; 12 expert raters; 312 practitioners tested
studies.finding: For cervical cancer control MCQ generation, LLM questions were similar to clinician ones in most dimensions, but clinician MCQs had higher cognitive level (4.00±1.08) than GPT-4o (3.68±1.07) and Baichuan4 (3.7±1.13). Difficulty and discrimination did not differ significantly among clinicians (59.51±24.50, 0.38±0.14), GPT-4o (61.89±25.36, 0.30±0.19) and Baichuan4 (59.79±26.25, 0.33±0.15).
studies.limitation: Only 40 MCQs per source in one topic; number of clinician authors not stated.
studies.title: Advancing medical education in cervical cancer control with large language models for multiple-choice question generation.

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 98 MKSAP cardiology multiple-choice questions
studies.humans: Internal medicine intern, senior resident, internal medicine attending, cardiology attending
studies.finding: ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4 and physicians at several levels answered 98 MKSAP cardiovascular medicine multiple-choice questions. ChatGPT-4 scored 74.5%, comparable to the IM intern (63.3%), senior resident (63.3%), IM attending (62.2%) and ChatGPT-3.5 (64.3%). It was significantly lower than the cardiology attending (85.7%).
studies.limitation: Exam questions rather than clinical tasks, with very few physician participants.
studies.title: Evaluating Performance of ChatGPT on MKSAP Cardiology Board Review Questions.

studies.design: Performance study on authentic national residency exam questions compared with actual resident scores
studies.humans: OBGYN residents who sat the 2021-2022 Shlav-Alef exam
studies.finding: Answering 150 Hebrew OBGYN 'Shlav-Alef' examination multiple choice questions. ChatGPT correctly answered 58 questions (38.7%), versus a mean resident score of 68.4 (38.7% vs. 68.4%, p < .001).
studies.limitation: Single exam, text-only multiple choice questions, an older ChatGPT version, and number of residents not stated.
studies.title: Performance of ChatGPT in Israeli Hebrew OBGYN national residency examinations.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of LLM scoring with historical faculty grades
studies.finding: GPT-4o mini scored 433 OSCE post-encounter notes and was compared with historical faculty grades. LLM scores were significantly lower than faculty scores (mean differences -1.12 GPT-NE and -0.65 GPT-E, both P < .001), with Spearman correlations r = 0.43-0.53.
studies.limitation: Single institution; faculty grades used as reference rather than an independent gold standard; number of faculty not stated.
studies.title: Comparative analysis of large language model and faculty rater scoring of medical student documentation in objective structured clinical examinations.
studies.source: Academic medicine : journal of the Association of American Medical Colleges

studies.design: Cross-sectional blinded test of AI-generated vs expert-written questions
studies.finding: Generating in-training MCQs for radiology residents. There were no significant differences in overall correct response rates or source attribution accuracy, but residents had lower correct rates for DeepSeek A3/A4 questions and rated DeepSeek A2 clinical realism lower.
studies.limitation: Only 28 questions at a single program; the number of expert question writers was not stated.
studies.title: Performance of DeepSeek in the generation of in-training examination questions in radiology resident education.

studies.design: Randomized quality improvement project
studies.ai_system: Deep learning algorithm for incidental coronary artery calcium on nongated chest CT
studies.finding: Notification of clinicians and patients of AI-detected, radiologist-confirmed incidental CAC versus usual care. Statin prescription at 6 months was 51.2% (44/86) with notification versus 6.9% (6/87) with usual care (P <0.001).
studies.limitation: Single health system; intervention combined AI detection with notification, outcome is prescribing not clinical events.
studies.title: Incidental Coronary Artery Calcium: Opportunistic Screening of Previous Nongated Chest Computed Tomography Scans to Improve Statin Rates (NOTIFY-1 Project).

studies.design: Multicenter randomized controlled trial, 6 centers, 3059 subjects
studies.finding: In screening colonoscopy, AI-assisted colonoscopy raised overall adenoma detection rate versus conventional colonoscopy (39.9% vs 32.4%; P < .001), with higher advanced ADR (6.6% vs 4.9%) and higher ADR for both expert (42.3% vs 32.8%) and nonexpert endoscopists (37.5% vs 32.1%). Median withdrawal time was slightly longer with AI (8.3 vs 7.8 minutes).
studies.limitation: Conducted only in Chinese centers; endoscopists not blinded to AI use.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Colonoscopy for Colorectal Cancer Screening: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
studies.source: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

studies.design: Prospective multicenter pivotal trial
studies.humans: General ophthalmologists and retina specialists performing dilated ophthalmoscopy
studies.finding: For detecting more than mild diabetic retinopathy against reading-center grading, retina specialists had sensitivity 59.5% and specificity 98.9% versus EyeArt 97% and 88%. General ophthalmologists had sensitivity 20.6% and specificity 99.8% versus EyeArt 96.5% and 86%.
studies.limitation: AI used fundus photographs while clinicians used ophthalmoscopy; number of clinicians not stated; subgroup analysis.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy: Subgroup Comparison of the EyeArt System with Ophthalmologists' Dilated Examinations.

studies.design: Prospective observational study in one academic ED
studies.ai_system: LASSO logistic regression machine learning model
studies.finding: Physician gestalt at 15 minutes was compared with screening tools including a LASSO ML model for identifying sepsis in critically ill ED patients. Physician VAS had AUC 0.90 (95% CI 0.88, 0.92) versus LASSO 0.84 (95% CI 0.82 to 0.87).
studies.limitation: Single-center study; outcome based on discharge diagnosis.
studies.title: Early Physician Gestalt Versus Usual Screening Tools for the Prediction of Sepsis in Critically Ill Emergency Patients.
studies.excluded: compares physician judgment with standard sepsis screening scores, not with AI (editor, 2026-11-06)

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial of CADe-assisted vs standard colonoscopy in 370 patients
studies.finding: ADR was 55.1% with CADe vs 43.8% in controls (P = .029). Polyp detection rate was 67.1% vs 51% (P = .004); after stratification by endoscopist and bowel cleansing ADR differences were not significant.
studies.limitation: Short recruitment period; endoscopists not blinded; stratified analyses not significant.
studies.title: Usefulness of a novel computer-aided detection system for colorectal neoplasia: a randomized controlled trial.

studies.design: Retrospective development and validation, sensitivity compared with original radiologist reports
studies.ai_system: CNN-based CAD tool for pancreatic cancer on CT
studies.finding: Detection of pancreatic cancer on contrast-enhanced CT. In the internal test set the DL tool had 89.9% sensitivity versus 96.1% for the original radiologist report, without significant difference (P = .11).
studies.limitation: Retrospective comparison against routine reports in a single country; no prospective reader study.
studies.title: Pancreatic Cancer Detection on CT Scans with Deep Learning: A Nationwide Population-based Study.

studies.design: Retrospective model development and validation with radiologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Automated deep learning model for tumor and lymph node segmentation on CT
studies.finding: For predicting lymph node metastasis in PDAC on CT, the AI model had AUC 0.92 in validation versus 0.65 for radiologists (P < .001). In training, AI AUC was 0.91 vs 0.58 for radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset study; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence to Predict Lymph Node Metastasis at CT in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.

studies.design: Prospective single-institution cohort with before-after comparison
studies.finding: Adenoma detection in colonoscopy. Post-intervention median ADR with AI was 30.4%, higher than the median baseline polypectomy rate of 24.3% (p = 0.02); 13 of 18 endoscopists improved.
studies.limitation: Non-randomised before-after design comparing ADR against baseline polypectomy rate; single institution, short 3-month period.
studies.title: Real-time artificial intelligence (AI)-aided endoscopy improves adenoma detection rates even in experienced endoscopists: a cohort study in Singapore.

studies.design: Prospective comparative cohort study of on-call ophthalmology referrals, with the ophthalmologist's assessment as reference
studies.ai_system: Cloud-based decision tree clinical decision support system
studies.humans: Referring providers: medical doctors, optometrists, nurse practitioners
studies.finding: Across 96 on-call ophthalmology referrals, the CDSS and the referring providers were each compared with the ophthalmologist on diagnostic category, provisional diagnosis and urgency. Category agreement was similar (CDSS κ = 0.5898 vs providers κ = 0.5880). The CDSS did better on diagnosis (agreement = 53.1%, κ = 0.4999 vs 43.8%, κ = 0.4191) and on urgency (ρ = 0.5014 vs ρ = 0.4035).
studies.limitation: Single community clinic with only 96 referrals, and the comparator group mixed physicians with optometrists and nurse practitioners.
studies.title: Development of a Cloud-Based Clinical Decision Support System for Ophthalmology Triage Using Decision Tree Artificial Intelligence.

studies.design: Retrospective study of 637 patients (1917 radiographs)
studies.ai_system: Deep neural network fracture detection software
studies.finding: Detection of wrist fractures on radiographs. AI sensitivity was 83% versus 76% for the initial radiology reports (p < 0.001), with similar specificity (96% vs 96%). AI combined with the reports reached 88% sensitivity but lower specificity (92%).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, single-centre comparison against routine reports; the number of radiologists is not stated.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence vs. radiologist: accuracy of wrist fracture detection on radiographs.

studies.design: Retrospective development and multi-country test with reader comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep learning system for active TB on chest radiographs
studies.finding: In the four-country test set the DLS had AUC 0.89, higher than all nine India-based radiologists. At the prespecified operating point DLS sensitivity was higher (88% vs 75%, P < .001) and specificity noninferior (79% vs 84%, P = .004).
studies.limitation: Retrospective data; comparison mainly with India-based radiologists.
studies.title: Deep Learning Detection of Active Pulmonary Tuberculosis at Chest Radiography Matched the Clinical Performance of Radiologists.

studies.design: Machine learning model compared with clinician predictions
studies.finding: For predicting headache surgery outcome from pain drawings, the algorithm was consistently more accurate (94%) than trained clinical evaluators.
studies.limitation: Small dataset (131 drawings); clinician accuracy not reported.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Evaluation of Pain Sketches to Predict Outcomes in Headache Surgery.

studies.design: Retrospective development and validation study with two independent test sets
studies.finding: The task was detecting solid and cystic pancreatic neoplasms on contrast-enhanced CT. The DL approach had an AUC of 0.91 in test set 1 and 0.87 in test set 2. Its sensitivity was 98%-100% for solid lesions and 92%-93% for cystic lesions of 1.0 cm or larger, comparable with radiologists at 95%-100% and 93%-98% respectively.
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only two comparator radiologists.
studies.title: Deep Learning-based Detection of Solid and Cystic Pancreatic Neoplasms at Contrast-enhanced CT.

studies.design: Prospective study with comparison to an external grader panel
studies.finding: For identifying abnormal urinary flows, Audioflow had 83.8% (95% CI, 77.5-90.1%) agreement with the reference standard and was comparable with the panel of six residents/general practitioners. Its AUC was 0.892.
studies.limitation: Single centre, male patients only; panel results not given numerically.
studies.title: Development and Validation of a Deep Learning System for Sound-based Prediction of Urinary Flow.

studies.design: Model development with reader comparison on 100 images
studies.humans: Six ophthalmologists (3 with 2 years, 3 with >5 years)
studies.finding: Multi-disease classification on ultra-widefield fundus images. On 100 images the model's accuracy was 93.00% vs 88.00% for ophthalmologists with 2 years and 94.00% for those with more than 5 years.
studies.limitation: Small 100-image reader comparison at a single tertiary hospital.
studies.title: Deep Learning for the Detection of Multiple Fundus Diseases Using Ultra-widefield Images.

studies.design: Multiple-reader multiple-case study, aided vs unaided
studies.ai_system: FDA-cleared deep learning fracture detection system
studies.humans: 24 clinicians: radiologists, orthopaedic surgeons, PAs, primary care and emergency physicians
studies.finding: Clinicians read 175 musculoskeletal radiographs with and without AI. AUC rose from 0.90 unaided to 0.94 aided (p < 0.01); sensitivity 82% to 90% and specificity 89% to 92%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective enriched reader study, not live care.
studies.title: Deep Learning Assistance Closes the Accuracy Gap in Fracture Detection Across Clinician Types.

studies.design: Multicenter nonrandomized video-based external validation
studies.finding: Detection of Barrett's neoplasia on 75 real-time endoscopic videos. CAD sensitivity, specificity, NPV and accuracy were 93.8%, 90.7%, 95.1% and 92.0% vs endoscopists' 63.5%, 77.9%, 74.2% and 71.8% (P < .05 in all).
studies.limitation: Recorded videos rather than live endoscopy; compared only with nonexpert endoscopists.
studies.title: Development and validation of artificial neural networks model for detection of Barrett's neoplasia: a multicenter pragmatic nonrandomized trial (with video).

studies.design: Retrospective development study with observer study comparing AI against radiologists and radiologists with vs without AI
studies.finding: Detecting scaphoid fractures on multi-view radiographs, the algorithm achieved AUC 0.88 versus radiologists' mean 0.87 (p ≥ .05). AI assistance improved five of ten inter-observer kappa pairs and reduced reading time in four radiologists (p < .001), but did not improve other metrics in most radiologists.
studies.limitation: Retrospective data from two hospitals with only five readers.
studies.title: Musculoskeletal radiologist-level performance by using deep learning for detection of scaphoid fractures on conventional multi-view radiographs of hand and wrist.

studies.design: Retrospective radiomics model development with radiologist comparison
studies.finding: For distinguishing T1/2 from T3/4 rectal cancer, model SRT2 achieved AUC 0.869 and model HRT2 0.810. Both radiomics models achieved higher AUCs than expert radiologists (0.685, p < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Retrospective single-dataset chronological validation; radiologist number not stated.
studies.title: Deep-learning-based 3D super-resolution MRI radiomics model: superior predictive performance in preoperative T-staging of rectal cancer.

studies.design: Multicentre prospective cohort; random forest models tested on external centre versus radiologists
studies.ai_system: Random forest classifier on MRI and PET/MRI features
studies.finding: Axillary nodal status determination in newly diagnosed breast cancer on 18F-FDG PET/MRI. Diagnostic accuracy for MRI features was 87.5% for both radiologists and the algorithm; for PET/MRI 89.3% for radiologists and 91.2% for the algorithm, with no significant differences (P = 0.671 MRI; P = 0.683 PET/MRI).
studies.limitation: Single external test centre with modest sample; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Clinical Decision Support for Axillary Lymph Node Staging in Newly Diagnosed Breast Cancer Patients Based on 18F-FDG PET/MRI and Machine Learning.
studies.source: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter comparison
studies.finding: Rib fracture detection on chest CT in ER trauma patients. On the external dataset the model had sensitivity 86.2% vs 70.5% for attending radiologists (p < .0001), with specificity 98.8% vs 98.8% (p = 0.175).
studies.limitation: Retrospective; radiologist readings likely from clinical reports; number of radiologists not stated.
studies.title: Assessment of automatic rib fracture detection on chest CT using a deep learning algorithm.

studies.design: Deep learning model development with ophthalmologist survey comparison
studies.ai_system: Ensemble neural network on external photographs
studies.finding: On a 50-image survey set for detecting thyroid eye disease, the model achieved accuracy 86%, specificity 84%, recall 89%, precision 77% and F1 82%. The 27 ophthalmologists achieved mean 75%, 82%, 63%, 72% and 66%, respectively.
studies.limitation: Comparison based on only 50 images from a single clinical database.
studies.title: Ensemble neural network model for detecting thyroid eye disease using external photographs.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with external test and specialist comparison
studies.ai_system: Deep learning myopic maculopathy classifier on fundus photographs
studies.finding: Classification of myopic maculopathy into four categories. External-test AUCs were 0.99, 0.96, 0.98 and 1.00; the model achieved high sensitivities, specificities and reliable kappa compared with attending ophthalmologists.
studies.limitation: Ophthalmologist results not quantified in abstract.
studies.title: Efficacy of a Deep Learning System for Screening Myopic Maculopathy Based on Color Fundus Photographs.

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective model development with external validation versus expert radiologist PI-RADS
studies.ai_system: Deep learning bpMRI models (DL-BM, DL-CS) and integrated PIDL-CS
studies.finding: Detection of clinically significant prostate cancer in 645 external validation patients. AUCs of DL-BM and DL-CS were not significantly different from PI-RADS by expert radiologists (P > 0.05); the combined PIDL-CS model had higher AUC than PI-RADS in most cohorts (P < 0.05) and much higher specificity.
studies.limitation: Retrospective; radiologist number not stated; comparison against routine PI-RADS reads.
studies.title: Predicting clinically significant prostate cancer with a deep learning approach: a multicentre retrospective study.
studies.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

studies.design: Model development with comparison against oral surgeons on internal and external panoramic radiograph sets
studies.finding: The model and oral surgeons assessed contact between the lower third molar and inferior alveolar nerve on panoramic radiographs, with CBCT as reference. The model's accuracy was 0.894 and 0.927 in the original and external datasets, versus 0.628 and 0.615 for oral surgeons.
studies.limitation: Small test sets; the number of surgeons is not stated in the abstract.
studies.title: Deep learning model for the automated evaluation of contact between the lower third molar and inferior alveolar nerve on panoramic radiography.

studies.design: Model development with comparison against otolaryngologists on a standardized test set of voice recordings
studies.ai_system: Artificial neural network on mel-spectrograms of voice recordings
studies.finding: On a standardized test set of voice recordings for vocal cord pathology, the AI outperformed otolaryngologists (83% compared to 55% ± 15%).
studies.limitation: Small proof-of-concept dataset with variable smartphone recordings; number of otolaryngologists not stated.
studies.title: Developing an Artificial Intelligence Tool to Predict Vocal Cord Pathology in Primary Care Settings.

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre model development with comparison to radiologist scores
studies.ai_system: Deep learning plus machine learning surveillance model on bpMRI
studies.finding: For detecting csPCa on serial prostate bpMRI in 73 patients, the AI model reached an AUC of 0.86 with clinical variables (0.81 without). Radiologists reached an AUC of 0.69 (p = 0.02).
studies.limitation: Small longitudinal subset of 73 patients with cross-validation only.
studies.title: AI-assisted biparametric MRI surveillance of prostate cancer: feasibility study.

studies.design: Retrospective single-center reader study on a 100-radiograph test set, with aided versus unaided reads
studies.ai_system: Neural network trained on structured bedside chest radiograph reports
studies.humans: Six radiologists and two nonradiologist ICU physicians
studies.finding: Readers interpreted bedside ICU chest radiographs, with agreement against the expert panel majority vote measured by weighted κ. The neural network had κ = 0.86 versus κ = 0.81 to ≤0.84 for individual radiologists. Nonradiologist physicians improved with AI preliminary readings (aided vs unaided, κ = 0.87 vs 0.79, P < .001).
studies.limitation: Single-center retrospective study with only two nonradiologist readers and 100 test images.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Interpretation of Bedside Chest Radiographs.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre model development with comparison to human observers
studies.ai_system: Mask R-CNN transfer learning model on contrast-enhanced CT
studies.finding: For positive lymph node identification, model accuracy was 0.7042 vs. 0.7647 for the radiologist (p = 0.243), 0.4216 for surgeons and 0.3629 for students (p < 0.001). Clinical accuracy was highest for the model (0.8509 vs. 0.8000, 0.5500, 0.4500, and 0.6658 of the Radiology Department).
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective study; number of human observers not stated.
studies.title: Deep learning assisted contrast-enhanced CT-based diagnosis of cervical lymph node metastasis of oral cancer: a retrospective study of 1466 cases.

studies.design: Model development with comparison to radiologists
studies.finding: Benign vs malignant parotid neoplasm classification on MRI from 266 patients. The best model achieved accuracy 0.85, AUC 0.96, sensitivity 0.90, specificity 0.84, and potentially outperformed experienced radiologists; radiologist figures not reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Small single dataset; radiologist results and number not reported in abstract.
studies.title: A Deep Learning Model for Classification of Parotid Neoplasms Based on Multimodal Magnetic Resonance Image Sequences.

studies.design: Retrospective model development and comparison
studies.finding: For scaphoid fracture detection on wrist radiographs, the CNN achieved sensitivity 82% and specificity 94% (AUC 92%). The majority decision of four hand surgeons achieved sensitivity 76% and specificity 96%. Performance was judged similar.
studies.limitation: Single referral centre with comparison against only four surgeons' majority vote.
studies.title: Evaluation of a convolutional neural network to identify scaphoid fractures on radiographs.
studies.source: The Journal of hand surgery, European volume

studies.design: Retrospective validation comparing deep learning with human readers
studies.ai_system: Deep learning automatic CAD-RADS reporting system
studies.finding: CAD-RADS grading on coronary CT angiography in 346 patients. DL accuracy was 82.08% against invasive angiography, with no significant difference from reader grading (kappa 0.775-0.802). Time fell from 14.97 ± 1.80 min to 5.02 ± 0.8 min.
studies.limitation: Retrospective single cohort; reader numbers are unclear.
studies.title: Clinical Evaluation of the Automatic Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) in Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography Using Convolutional Neural Networks.

studies.design: Retrospective multi-reader multi-case study
studies.ai_system: Deep learning CAD for prostate mpMRI
studies.humans: Two experienced and two less-experienced radiologists
studies.finding: With DL-CAD, less-experienced radiologists' AUC rose from 0.66 to 0.80 (p = 0.001) and experienced radiologists' from 0.81 to 0.86 (p = 0.146). Median reading time fell from 157 to 150 s (p = 0.023).
studies.limitation: Only four readers, single-centre retrospective dataset.
studies.title: A concurrent, deep learning-based computer-aided detection system for prostate multiparametric MRI: a performance study involving experienced and less-experienced radiologists.

studies.design: Reader study of knee X-rays read unaided and aided by AI computer-assisted detection reports
studies.ai_system: AI-based computer-aided knee osteoarthritis assessment system
studies.humans: Three board-certified orthopaedic surgeons, compared with senior residents from a previous study
studies.finding: On 115 knee X-rays from the OAI study, aided senior reader agreement rates improved significantly for KL grade (2.0-fold), sclerosis (1.42-fold), JSN (1.37-fold) and osteophyte OARSI grades (3.33-fold), and specificity and accuracy increased significantly for all features. Sensitivity increased only for OA diagnosis and decreased (without statistical significance) for other features; aided senior readers reached similar accuracy to junior readers, both surpassing AI performance.
studies.limitation: Only three senior readers on a single public dataset; junior reader comparison drawn from a previous study.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence-based computer-aided system for knee osteoarthritis assessment increases experienced orthopaedic surgeons' agreement rate and accuracy.
studies.source: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective study of 4351 COVID-19 inpatient records comparing delirium detection methods
studies.finding: Delirium detection in 4351 hospitalized COVID-19 patient records was compared across methods, with detection by any method as reference. NLP-CAM captured 80% of overall delirium, clinician diagnosis 55%, and nursing flowsheet documentation 43%.
studies.limitation: Retrospective with no independent reference standard; composite of the methods themselves used as comparison.
studies.title: Natural Language Processing CAM Algorithm Improves Delirium Detection Compared With Conventional Methods.
studies.source: American journal of medical quality : the official journal of the American College of Medical Quality

studies.design: Retrospective two-centre development and validation study comparing a deep learning model on T2-weighted MRI with radiologists using VI-RADS
studies.ai_system: Deep convolutional neural network on T2-weighted MRI
studies.humans: Two groups of radiologists (readers 1 and readers 2) scoring VI-RADS
studies.finding: For predicting muscle invasion in bladder cancer, AUCs of the DL model, readers 1 and readers 2 were 0.963, 0.843 and 0.852 in internal validation, and 0.861, 0.808 and 0.876 in external validation. In VI-RADS 2 or 3 tumours in the external set, DL accuracy was higher than radiologists (0.886 vs. 0.600 and 0.879 vs. 0.636).
studies.limitation: Small external validation set (55 tumours) and retrospective design. In external validation one reader group had a higher AUC than the model.
studies.title: Predicting muscle invasion in bladder cancer by deep learning analysis of MRI: comparison with vesical imaging-reporting and data system.

studies.design: Retrospective deep learning model development compared with a radiologist-evaluation-based prediction model
studies.ai_system: ResNet50+SE deep learning model on contrast-enhanced ultrasound
studies.finding: The task was predicting microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma from contrast-enhanced ultrasound. The DL model achieved an ROC of 0.856 with accuracy of 77.2, whereas the radiologist-based model had a C-index of 0.729 with accuracy of 69.4. Sensitivity was 52.4% for the DL model versus 62% for the radiologist-based model.
studies.limitation: The comparator is a regression model built on radiologist evaluations rather than direct reader diagnoses; small test set of 54.
studies.title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound with Deep Learning with Attention Mechanisms for Predicting Microvascular Invasion in Single Hepatocellular Carcinoma.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with radiologist comparison
studies.finding: Diagnosing cleft palate on panoramic radiographs, AUCs were 0.95 for Model A, 0.93 for Model B, and 0.70 and 0.63 for the radiologists; model AUCs were significantly higher.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists and a single-dataset retrospective test set.
studies.title: Deep-learning systems for diagnosing cleft palate on panoramic radiographs in patients with cleft alveolus.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study
studies.finding: Benign vs malignant thyroid nodules on ultrasound in 139 patients aged 21 or younger. Radiologists' overall impression had mean sensitivity 58.3% and specificity 79.9%; the DL algorithm had sensitivity 87.5% and specificity 36.1%.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective sample; only three readers.
studies.title: Thyroid Nodules on Ultrasound in Children and Young Adults: Comparison of Diagnostic Performance of Radiologists' Impressions, ACR TI-RADS, and a Deep Learning Algorithm.

studies.design: Retrospective model development with internal and external test cohorts and reader assistance
studies.finding: For preoperative identification of axillary lymph node metastasis, RCNet-tumor+ALN achieved an AUC of 0.852 in the external test cohort. With its assistance, the radiologists' performance was improved (external test cohort, P < 0.05).
studies.limitation: Retrospective with only three readers; reader results without assistance not numerically reported in abstract.
studies.title: Attention-based Deep Learning for the Preoperative Differentiation of Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis in Breast Cancer on DCE-MRI.
studies.source: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

studies.design: Bicentric retrospective study with radiologist comparison
studies.finding: The model detected meniscus tears on knee MRI with accuracies of 95.4%, 95.8% and 78.8% across internal testing, internal validation and external validation sets. One radiologist had significantly lower performance than the model (accuracy 0.9025 ± 0.093 vs 0.9580 ± 0.025).
studies.limitation: Retrospective with only three radiologists; only one differed significantly, and external accuracy dropped.
studies.title: Automatic Detection of Meniscus Tears Using Backbone Convolutional Neural Networks on Knee MRI.
studies.source: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

studies.design: Model development with comparison against endoscopists and AI-assisted diagnostic study
studies.finding: For diagnosing gastric neoplasms, the models outperformed endoscopists on WM data (85.00 vs 71.67%, P = 0.002) and multi-modal data (90.00 vs 76.17%, P = 0.002). With ENDOANGEL-MM assistance, non-expert accuracy improved (85.75 vs 70.75%, P = 0.020), with no significant difference from experts (85.75 vs 89.00%, P = 0.159).
studies.limitation: Number of endoscopists not stated; reader comparisons largely on images/videos.
studies.title: A deep-learning based system using multi-modal data for diagnosing gastric neoplasms in real-time (with video).
studies.source: Gastric cancer : official journal of the International Gastric Cancer Association and the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic comparison on internal and external test sets against 24 radiologists
studies.ai_system: Closed-loop AI system (U-Net segmentation + TrumpetNet detection) for prostate MRI
studies.finding: Diagnosing clinically significant prostate cancer on MRI. Internally, AI AUC was lower than subspecialists (0.85 vs. 0.92) and comparable to junior (0.84) and general (0.86) groups; externally AI (0.86) equalled subspecialists (0.86) and exceeded junior (0.80) and general (0.83). AI outperformed 54.2% (13/24) of readers.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader comparison; result depends on reader experience level.
studies.title: Performance of Artificial Intelligence-Aided Diagnosis System for Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer with MRI: A Diagnostic Comparison Study.
studies.source: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

studies.design: Retrospective analysis of multi-center phase 3 trial data
studies.ai_system: Deep learning-based attenuation correction (DLAC) with total perfusion deficit quantification
studies.finding: Detection of obstructive CAD on SPECT MPI in 722 patients against invasive coronary angiography. DLAC achieved AUC 0.752 (95% CI: 0.711-0.792) versus consensus of expert readers AUC 0.743 (0.701-0.784), with no significant difference (p = 0.913).
studies.limitation: Only three expert readers compared, using consensus reading; patients were referred for angiography, so selection bias is possible.
studies.title: Multi-center, multi-vendor validation of deep learning-based attenuation correction in SPECT MPI: data from the international flurpiridaz-301 trial.
studies.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

studies.design: Retrospective model development compared with original physician protocol assignments
studies.finding: The task was brain MRI protocol selection across 19,721 exams, scored against physician consensus labels. The model achieved 90.5% accuracy versus 85.9% for the original protocol assignments (κ = 0.84 versus 0.72, P < .001).
studies.limitation: Single academic center, retrospective; the reference standard was physician consensus and the number of physicians is not stated.
studies.title: An Artificial Intelligence Tool for Clinical Decision Support and Protocol Selection for Brain MRI.

studies.design: Retrospective deep learning validation with clinician annotator comparison
studies.finding: Detection of iRORA and cRORA on OCT B-scans in AMD. On an enriched set the model achieved AUROC iRORA 0.68 and cRORA 0.84. The model can achieve similar sensitivity compared with human graders.
studies.limitation: Clinician comparison figures not reported in the abstract and number of graders not stated.
studies.title: Automated Identification of Incomplete and Complete Retinal Epithelial Pigment and Outer Retinal Atrophy Using Machine Learning.

studies.design: Retrospective reader study of breast DCE MRI MIP images with CAD comparison
studies.finding: In 198 lactating patients, readers achieved mean sensitivity 93.3%, specificity 80.3% and diagnostic accuracy 84.6% on MIP-DCE images. CAD's derived diagnostic accuracy was similar (p = 0.41).
studies.limitation: Retrospective, single MIP image reading; CAD comparison is secondary and minimally described.
studies.title: MRI can accurately diagnose breast cancer during lactation.

studies.design: Multi-reader multi-case study with and without CAD
studies.ai_system: SYNAPSE SAI Viewer V1.4 deep learning CAD
studies.humans: Radiologists of low, medium and high experience
studies.finding: The task was characterising and diagnosing 101 pulmonary nodules/masses on CT. With CAD, AUCs for several characteristics and for malignancy improved significantly across all 15 radiologists, with no significant improvement in the most experienced group. Intraclass correlation coefficients improved and assessment time was not prolonged.
studies.limitation: Single-center study with 101 nodules.
studies.title: Radiologists with and without deep learning-based computer-aided diagnosis: comparison of performance and interobserver agreement for characterizing and diagnosing pulmonary nodules/masses.

studies.design: Multicenter deep learning development study with reader study on 324 patients
studies.finding: Classification of breast lesions on ultrasound (benign/malignant and BI-RADS). Versus the consensus of three radiologists, DL BI-RADS had similar AUC (0.901 vs. 0.933, p = 0.0632), sensitivity (90.98% vs. 95.90%) and accuracy (83.33% vs. 79.01%), but higher specificity (78.71% vs. 68.81%, p = 0.0012).
studies.limitation: Only three radiologists in reader study; subset of 324 patients.
studies.title: Ultrasound-based deep learning in the establishment of a breast lesion risk stratification system: a multicenter study.

studies.design: Retrospective multireader study
studies.finding: Breast cancer reading with AI CAD synthesized mammograms versus digital mammograms, alone and with DBT. Mean AUC was 0.895 for AI CAD SM versus 0.863 for DM (P < 0.0001), and 0.902 for AI CAD SM + DBT versus 0.886 for DM + DBT (P = 0.094), with reduced reading time (P < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Retrospective design with only four readers in an enriched virtual screening set.
studies.title: Comparisons between artificial intelligence computer-aided detection synthesized mammograms and digital mammograms when used alone and in combination with tomosynthesis images in a virtual screening setting.

studies.design: Retrospective ultrasound radiomics study comparing models with a radiologist
studies.ai_system: Radiomics machine learning models (random forest, SVM, logistic)
studies.finding: For diagnosing carpal tunnel syndrome on ultrasound, random forest models achieved test AUCs of 0.830 and 0.872. Model performance was significantly better than the inexperienced radiologist (AUC 0.702).
studies.limitation: Comparison against a single inexperienced radiologist in a small retrospective dataset.
studies.title: Ultrasound-based radiomics in the diagnosis of carpal tunnel syndrome: The influence of regions of interest delineation method on mode.

studies.design: Multicentre model development with image test comparison to endoscopists and prospective evaluation
studies.ai_system: AI system for detecting and delineating superficial ESCC under NBI
studies.finding: Delineation of superficial esophageal squamous cell carcinoma extent under NBI; system delineation accuracy was 88.9% (internal) and 87.0% (external). Its delineation performance was superior to junior endoscopists and similar to senior endoscopists; endoscopist figures not reported in abstract.
studies.limitation: Human comparison was on still images only; endoscopist numbers and results not given in abstract.
studies.title: Artificial intelligence for detecting and delineating the extent of superficial esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions under narrow-band imaging (with video).

studies.design: Multicentre retrospective model development with comparison to and assistance of radiologists
studies.ai_system: CBAM-based Xception attention deep learning model on CESM
studies.humans: Two radiologists with specialised breast imaging experience
studies.finding: For benign vs malignant breast lesions on CESM, the model achieved AUC 0.970, sensitivity 0.848, specificity 1.000 and accuracy 0.891 on the external test set, higher than the radiologists. The diagnostic performance of the two radiologists improved with deep learning assistance.
studies.limitation: Only two radiologists; radiologist figures not reported in abstract.
studies.title: Attention-based deep learning for breast lesions classification on contrast enhanced spectral mammography: a multicentre study.

studies.design: Retrospective radiomics model compared with 3 radiologists on 148 renal masses
studies.ai_system: Random forest model on CT radiomics features
studies.finding: For distinguishing benign from malignant solid renal masses, the model had an accuracy of 0.82 (AUC 0.80). The three radiologists had significantly lower accuracies (p = 0.02), ranging from 0.67 to 0.75.
studies.limitation: Small single-institution retrospective cohort.
studies.title: Differentiation of benign from malignant solid renal lesions using CT-based radiomics and machine learning: comparison with radiologist interpretation.

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective reader study
studies.ai_system: AI algorithm differentiating COVID-19 from community-acquired pneumonia on CT
studies.finding: Differentiation of COVID-19 from CAP on chest CT. AI alone accuracy was 76.5%; radiologists' accuracy was 79.1% without AI and 81.5% with AI, with significantly shorter decision times and higher confidence.
studies.limitation: Assisted reading evaluated on a 180-scan subset; small accuracy gain.
studies.title: AI support for accurate and fast radiological diagnosis of COVID-19: an international multicenter, multivendor CT study.

studies.design: Retrospective observational model development with agreement against clinician grading
studies.humans: Clinicians grading disc damage likelihood scale
studies.finding: Grading optic disc photographs on the disc damage likelihood scale. DDLSNet achieved an average weighted kappa of 0.54 (95% CI: 0.40, 0.68) compared to clinicians, versus average interclinician agreement of 0.52 (95% CI: 0.49, 0.56).
studies.limitation: Small test set of 120 photographs and clinician average used as ground truth; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: DDLSNet: A Novel Deep Learning-Based System for Grading Funduscopic Images for Glaucomatous Damage.

studies.design: Lab experiment; trainees performed surgical task with and without adaptive automation
studies.ai_system: Mental workload-based adaptive automation semi-autonomous suction tool
studies.finding: Robotic-assisted surgical hemorrhage task performed with and without the MWL-AA. Trainees showed lower self-reported workload and better task performance with MWL-AA; abstract gives no numeric performance values beyond 77.9% workload detection accuracy.
studies.limitation: Very small sample of nine novice trainees in a simulated lab task.
studies.title: An Adaptive Human-Robotic Interaction Architecture for Augmenting Surgery Performance Using Real-Time Workload Sensing-Demonstration of a Semi-autonomous Suction Tool.
